# The heart / the inner self — a discovery document (developing)

> **Mode: DISCOVERY, not summary.** The heart is the master-term of the inner being, and the most colour-rich; it also raises the corpus's hardest structural question — how the four **seats** (heart, soul, spirit, flesh) differ. Gather widely, trace the colours, hold the boundaries open. Registry: `ib_characteristic.code = the-heart`.

## Working sense (held open)
The centre of the inner being — but the corpus will not let "heart" settle into one meaning. It is at once an *organ/seat*, the *true self*, a thing to be *guarded, given, weighed, searched, ruled, inclined, cleansed*, and the *place where every other operation happens*. Proverbs is intensely heart-centred; the Psalms distribute the interior across heart/soul/spirit/flesh. The central discovery task: is "the heart" **one characteristic**, or the **whole interior named from its centre** — and how does it differ from the other seats?

## The evidence, gathered by colour

**Colour 1 — the heart is the TRUE self.** "As in water face reflects face, so **the heart of man reflects the man**" (Pro 27:19). Not a faculty the self *has* but the self it *is*. Here "heart" = identity.

**Colour 2 — the heart is the SOURCE of the life, to be GUARDED.** "**Keep your heart with all vigilance, for from it flow the springs of life**" (Pro 4:23). The heart is the *origin* from which everything issues; hence the object of the most vigilant guarding.

**Colour 3 — the heart is the self's OFFERING, to be GIVEN.** "**My son, give me your heart**" (Pro 23:26); "apply your heart… direct your heart" (Pro 23:12,19). The deepest appeal asks not for behaviour but for *the heart itself*.

**Colour 4 — the heart is WEIGHED and SEARCHED by God.** "The LORD **weighs the heart**" (Pro 21:2; 16:2 "weighs the spirit"); "you who **test the hearts**" (Ps 7:9); "he **knows the secrets of the heart**" (Ps 44:21); "he **fashions the hearts** of them all" (Ps 33:15); "search me… **know my heart**" (Ps 139:23). The heart lies open to God — and can invite that opening.

**Colour 5 — the heart can be HARDENED.** "Whoever **hardens his heart** will fall into calamity" (Pro 28:14); the "**stiffened neck**" broken beyond healing (Pro 29:1); "do not **harden your hearts**" (Ps 95:8). A self-inflicted callousing.

**Colour 6 — the heart cannot self-CLEANSE.** "**Who can say, 'I have made my heart pure'?**" (Pro 20:9); therefore "**create** in me a clean heart, O God" (Ps 51:10) — it must be *made*, not self-washed.

**Colour 7 — the heart DIVIDED vs UNITED / WHOLE / STEADFAST.** "They speak with a **double heart**" (Ps 12:2); against it, "**unite my heart** to fear your name" (Ps 86:11); "with my **whole heart** I seek you" (Ps 9:1; 119:10; 138:1); "my heart is **steadfast/fixed**" (Ps 57:7; 108:1; 112:7 "his heart is firm"). The heart can be split, or gathered and made firm.

**Colour 8 — the heart BROKEN / contrite.** "The LORD is near to the **brokenhearted**" (Ps 34:18); "a **broken and contrite heart** you will not despise" (Ps 51:17); "he **heals the brokenhearted**" (Ps 147:3). Here brokenness is not failure but the acceptable condition.

**Colour 9 — the FELT heart.** "**The heart knows its own bitterness**, and no stranger shares its joy" (Pro 14:10); "a **glad heart** makes a cheerful face, but by sorrow of heart the **spirit is crushed**" (Pro 15:13); "**anxiety in a man's heart weighs him down**" (Pro 12:25). (Fuller treatment: `the-felt-interior`.)

**Colour 10 — the DEEP / opaque-yet-drawable heart.** "**The purpose in a man's heart is like deep water**, but a man of understanding will draw it out" (Pro 20:5); "the heart of kings is **unsearchable**" (Pro 25:3); "the inward mind and heart… are **deep**" (Ps 64:6). Hidden, yet reachable by the discerning (though never by self, Colour 6).

**Colour 11 — the heart INCLINED / directed.** The heart's *direction* can be set: by the self — "**incline your heart** to understanding" (Pro 2:2); by God — "**incline my heart** to your testimonies" (Ps 119:36); guarded against evil — "**let not my heart incline** to any evil" (Ps 141:4). The heart is steerable — but by whom?

**Colour 12 — the heart as WRITING-SURFACE / the place wisdom ENTERS.** "**Write them on the tablet of your heart**" (Pro 3:3; 7:3); "**wisdom will come into your heart**" (Pro 2:10); "your law is **within my heart**" (Ps 40:8). The interior as an inscribable, in-fillable space.

## Where it changes colour — the developing picture
The heart is **simultaneously the most active and the most passive** thing in the inner being. It *guards, gives, inclines, seeks* (the self acting from its centre) — and it is *weighed, searched, fashioned, hardened, broken, cleansed, inscribed* (the self acted upon). The live discovery is this **double agency**:
- The heart can be **inclined by the self** (Pro 2:2 — I incline my own heart) **and by God** (Ps 119:36 — you incline my heart) **and is turned by God even against its grain** (Pro 21:1 — the king's heart a stream in the LORD's hand).
- The heart can be **hardened by the self** (Pro 28:14) but **cannot be cleansed by the self** (Pro 20:9) — the self can *damage* its heart but not *purify* it.

So the heart is the arena where the self's agency and God's meet — the self can steer, harden, offer, and guard it, but only God can weigh, fashion, and cleanse it. **The heart is the one thing the self both owns and cannot control.**

## The seats — the hard structural question
Heart (*leb/lebab*), soul (*nephesh*), spirit (*ruach*), flesh (*basar*) are all tagged as *seats*, and the operations distribute across them unevenly and overlappingly:
- **soul** carries longing/thirst, the self-addressed "O my soul", the fainting/poured-out self (Ps 42, 62, 103, 116);
- **spirit** carries the crushed/faint spirit, the committed spirit, ruling/holding-back the spirit, the lamp searching the innermost (Ps 31:5, 51:10, Pro 16:32, 18:14, 20:27);
- **heart** carries nearly everything above;
- **flesh** carries frailty/dust and the body's register of inner states (Ps 16:9, 63:1, 73:26, 103:14).
**Open:** are these four *different faculties*, or one inner being named from four angles (its centre = heart, its life/appetite = soul, its breath/animating force = spirit, its frailty = flesh)? The data show heavy overlap (the crushed *spirit* 18:14 vs the crushed *heart*-sorrow 15:13) — suggesting angles more than parts. But *ruach* (spirit) clusters distinctly around *ruling/holding* and *committing* — a hint that it is the self's *governing/animating* aspect. Unresolved and central.

## Junctions (boundaries blurring — nearly all of them)
Because the heart is *where the operations happen*, it junctions with almost every characteristic: **being-known** (weighed/searched, Colour 4); **self-mastery** (guarding/ruling/inclining, Colours 2,11); **the-felt-interior** (Colour 9); **forgiveness-confession** (cleansing, Colour 6); **integrity-legibility** (divided vs whole, Colour 7); **self-address** (the heart addressed and exhorted); **teachability** (the hardened heart, Colour 5); **wisdom-formation** (the heart as the place wisdom enters, Colour 12).

## Thin / uncertain evidence (noted, not yet weighed)
- **The ENLARGED heart.** "I will run… when you **enlarge my heart**" (Ps 119:32) — the heart can be *made bigger* (capacity expanded by God). One clear witness; a distinct colour (dilation) worth watching.
- **The heart that ENVIES / rages.** "his heart **rages against the LORD**" (Pro 19:3); envy "makes the bones rot" (Pro 14:30) — the heart as the seat of resentment; thin, junctions with self-toward-others.
- **The heart that MEDITATES / muses.** "the **meditation of my heart**" (Ps 19:14); "I commune with my own heart" (Ps 77:6) — the heart as the organ of inner speech/reflection; under-gathered here.

## Open questions (the debate, left open)
1. Is "the heart" **one characteristic** or the **whole interior named from its centre** — and is it even the right unit, given the four seats?
2. How do **heart / soul / spirit / flesh** differ in *operation* — distinct faculties, or four angles on one self? (Is *ruach* the governing aspect?)
3. Given the **double agency** — the self can incline/harden/offer/guard the heart, but only God can weigh/fashion/cleanse/enlarge it — where exactly is the line between what the self does *to* its heart and what only God does?
4. If Proverbs makes the heart the *source* of the springs of life (4:23) and the *true self* (27:19), is "the heart" the master-characteristic under which the others are *facets* — or a genuine peer among them?

---
*Status: developing — the richest and least-bounded of the characteristics. Gathers heart-evidence (Psalms + Proverbs) and foregrounds the double-agency and the seats-question as the live edges. Not a summary. The seats-question especially should drive whether soul/spirit/flesh get their own discovery docs or fold in here.*

*Section id 617 · status `approved` · v1 · 1136 words · author `claude_code` · source `verse-analysis/characteristics/wa-ibchar-trust-refuge-discovery-20260703.md`*

# Trust / taking refuge — a discovery document (developing)

> **Mode: DISCOVERY, not summary.** Gather the trust/refuge evidence across Psalms + Proverbs, trace the colours, and hold open the two hardest edges: whether *refuge* (spatial hiding) and *trust* (leaning/valuing) are one operation, and whether the **formation-law** ("you become what you trust") is a property of trust or a law over the whole inner being. Registry: `ib_characteristic.code = trust-refuge`.

## Working sense (held open)
The inner being leaning its security on God — and, crucially, being *re-formed* by what it leans on. Trust is not only a posture but a *forming* relation.

## The evidence, gathered by colour

**Colour 1 — refuge / shelter / running-to (spatial).** "In you, O LORD, do I **take refuge**" (Ps 31:1; 7:1; 11:1; 16:1; 71:1); "**the name of the LORD is a strong tower**; the righteous **runs into it** and is safe" (Pro 18:10); "he is a **shield** to those who take refuge in him" (Pro 30:5); "under his wings you will **find refuge**" (Ps 91:4); "my **rock** and my **fortress**" (Ps 18:2; 62:2). Trust as a *place fled into* — spatial, protective.

**Colour 2 — trust as leaning / reliance (postural).** "**Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding**" (Pro 3:5); "**commit your way** to the LORD; **trust** in him" (Ps 37:5); "those who **trust** in the LORD are like Mount Zion" (Ps 125:1). Trust as *leaning weight* onto God.

**Colour 3 — trust as valuation / deliberate choice.** "**It is better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in man**" (Ps 118:8–9); trust argued *from mortality* — "put not your trust in princes… his plans perish" (Ps 146:3–4). Here trust is a *reasoned ranking*, not a mood.

**Colour 4 — trust as self-DISTRUST.** "Do **not lean on your own understanding**" (Pro 3:5); "whoever **trusts in his own mind** is a fool" (Pro 28:26); "not in my bow do I trust" (Ps 44:6). Trust is constituted *negatively* — to trust God is to *stop* trusting the self.

**Colour 5 — mis-placed trust (the object corrupts it).** In **riches** (Ps 52:7; 49:6; 62:10; Pro 11:28); in **princes / man** (Ps 118:8; 146:3); in **idols** — "those who make them **become like them**; so do all who **trust** in them" (Ps 115:8; 135:18); in the self (Colour 4). Trust aimed wrong *topples* the self.

**Colour 6 — trust yielding IMMOVABLE stability (the effect on the self).** "Those who trust in the LORD are like **Mount Zion, which cannot be moved**" (Ps 125:1); "his heart is **firm**, trusting in the LORD… he will **not be afraid**" (Ps 112:7); "I shall **not be moved**" (Ps 16:8). Trust *stabilises* — the truster takes on the fixity of what he leans on.

**Colour 7 — trust CONSTITUTED from the womb.** "On you was I cast **from my birth**, and from my mother's womb you have been my God" (Ps 22:10); "you are my **hope**, my trust, **from my youth**" (Ps 71:5). Trust as *original*, not first chosen — the self trusting before it could decide to.

**Colour 8 — human trust (between people).** "The **heart of her husband trusts in her**" (Pro 31:11); "he who is **trustworthy in spirit** keeps a thing covered" (Pro 11:13). Trust *given to a person* — and its mirror, *being* trustworthy.

## Where it changes colour — the developing picture
The most important shift: **what you trust, you become.** "You become what you trust" (Ps 115:8) is stated of idols but reads as a *law*: dead idols deaden their trusters, and by the same logic the living God enlivens. Colour 6 (trust→immovable-stability) is this law working God-ward — the truster takes on the *fixity of Zion* because he leans on the unmovable. Trust is therefore not a neutral posture but a **conforming** one: it *re-shapes* the self toward its object.

The live edge: **is the formation-law trust's own property, or a law over the whole inner being?** It has its own registry entry (`formation-by-relation`) because it seems to run through *love* (you become what you love) and *company* (you become your company) as well. Trust may be the clearest *instance* of a deeper law rather than its owner.

A second edge: **refuge (Colour 1) and trust (Colours 2–4) may be two operations.** Refuge is *spatial* — fleeing into a tower/rock/wings; trust is *postural/evaluative* — leaning, ranking, self-distrusting. They co-occur but are not obviously the same act. And Colour 7 (trust from the womb) is *neither* chosen nor spatial — it is *constitutional*, a trust the self was *born into*.

## Junctions (boundaries blurring)
- **fear-of-the-lord** — fear-of-man (a snare) is dissolved *by trust* (Pro 29:25; Ps 56:11); trust and the fear of God are near-inseparable in the confidence-pole. Can one *both* fear and trust the same God — and how do they combine?
- **entrustment** — committing the self/plans/grievance to God (Ps 31:5; Pro 16:3; 20:22) looks like trust's *resolving act*. Is entrustment a colour of trust or its own operation?
- **fearlessness** — trust → "I will not be afraid" (Ps 112:7; 56:11). Fruit or facet?
- **rest-stillness** — the trusting heart sleeps (Ps 4:8); trust and rest interlock.
- **formation-by-relation** — see above; the formation-law is the deepest junction.

## Thin / uncertain evidence (noted, not yet weighed)
- **Trust as *casting*.** "**Cast your burden** on the LORD, and he will sustain you" (Ps 55:22) — trust as a *throwing-off* of weight onto God. Junctions with entrustment; a distinct motion (unloading) worth watching.
- **Being trustWORTHY** (Colour 8) as the *reciprocal* inner quality — the self that *can be trusted* (Pro 11:13; 31:11). Thin as inner-being data but a real mirror of the operation.
- **Trust that "waits" / "hopes"** — trust shades into waiting/hope so smoothly (Ps 33:20–22) that the boundary may be artificial.

## Open questions (the debate, left open)
1. Are **refuge** (spatial fleeing-into) and **trust** (leaning/valuing) one operation or two?
2. Is the **formation-law** ("you become what you trust") a property of trust, or a law governing the whole inner being (running also through love and company)? — a candidate *organising principle* for the study.
3. How do **trust from the womb** (constituted, Ps 22:10) and **trust as valuation** (chosen, Ps 118:8) relate — is trust originally given and later ratified?
4. How do **trust and fear** coexist toward the same God — do they combine into one settled orientation, or remain two postures held together?
5. What exactly does trust *do to* the self (Colour 6 — stabilisation)? Is being-formed-by-trust the whole point, making trust the master-operation?

---
*Status: developing. Gathers trust/refuge across Psalms + Proverbs; foregrounds the formation-law and the refuge-vs-trust boundary as the live edges. Not a summary. The formation-law question should be worked in the `formation-by-relation` doc, which this feeds.*

*Section id 618 · status `approved` · v1 · 1106 words · author `claude_code` · source `verse-analysis/characteristics/wa-ibchar-desire-appetite-discovery-20260703.md`*

# Desire / longing / appetite — a discovery document (developing)

> **Mode: DISCOVERY, not summary.** Gather the desire evidence across Psalms + Proverbs; trace the colours from God-ward thirst to the insatiable eye; hold open the hardest questions — whether desire is good/neutral/fallen by default, and whether contentment is *fulfilment* or *renunciation*. Registry: `ib_characteristic.code = desire-appetite`.

## Working sense (held open)
The inner being's *wanting*. Its two live variables are **direction** (toward God or elsewhere) and **satisfiability** (can it be filled?). Nearly every colour turns on one of these.

## The evidence, gathered by colour

**Colour 1 — thirst / longing for God (aching, bodily).** "As a deer **pants**… so my soul **thirsts for God**" (Ps 42:1–2); "my soul thirsts for you… in a **dry and weary land**" (Ps 63:1; 143:6); "my soul **longs, yea faints** for the courts of the LORD" (Ps 84:2); "my soul is **consumed with longing**" (Ps 119:20); "my soul **longs for your salvation**" (Ps 119:81). Desire at the pitch of *bodily need* — pants, thirsts, faints, consumed.

**Colour 2 — desire MET / satisfied by God.** "He **satisfies the longing soul**, and the hungry soul he fills with good" (Ps 107:9); "you **open your hand**; you **satisfy the desire** of every living thing" (Ps 145:16); "he **fulfills the desire** of those who fear him" (Ps 145:19); "who **satisfies you with good**" (Ps 103:5); "those who seek the LORD **lack no good thing**" (Ps 34:10). The appetite *answered* — and answered at *God's* hand.

**Colour 3 — the INSATIABLE eye (structurally unfillable).** "**Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied, and never satisfied are the eyes of man**" (Pro 27:20); "the leech has two daughters: Give and Give… three things **never say, 'Enough'**" (Pro 30:15–16). Desire with *no natural floor* — a want that cannot be filled by its objects.

**Colour 4 — disordered craving (that tests God, or kills).** "They had a **wanton craving**… and put God to the test… he gave them what they asked, but sent a **wasting**" (Ps 106:14–15; 78:29–30); "**the desire of the sluggard kills him**… all day long he **craves and craves**" (Pro 21:25–26). Craving that *devours its owner* — answered to ruin, or lethal because it never acts.

**Colour 5 — hope deferred (wounds) / fulfilled (heals).** "**Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but a desire fulfilled is a tree of life**" (Pro 13:12); "a desire fulfilled is **sweet to the soul**" (Pro 13:19). Desire has a *temporal* register: its *deferral* sickens, its *fulfilment* is life.

**Colour 6 — WEANED desire (past craving).** "I have calmed and quieted my soul, **like a weaned child**… like a weaned child is my soul within me" (Ps 131:2). Desire *transcended* — the soul content past the fretful demand, wanting nothing but presence.

**Colour 7 — CONSOLIDATED desire (the "one thing").** "**One thing** have I asked… to gaze upon the beauty of the LORD" (Ps 27:4); "**there is nothing on earth I desire besides you**" (Ps 73:25). The scattered wants *gathered onto one object*.

**Colour 8 — DELIGHT (settled desire, given its object).** "**Delight yourself in the LORD**, and he will give you the **desires of your heart**" (Ps 37:4); "his **delight is in the law**" (Ps 1:2; 112:1; 119). Desire in its *fulfilled, restful* mode — and, strikingly, delighting seems to *reshape* the desires (37:4) so that they are then granted.

## Where it changes colour — the developing picture
Desire runs from **aching thirst → met/satisfied → weaned/transcended**, with a shadow-track of **insatiable → disordered/craving → self-killing**. The decisive discovery is a paradox the corpus holds without resolving:
- The eye is **structurally insatiable** (27:20) — nothing fills it; yet God **satisfies the desire of every living thing** (145:16). The resolution seems to be that an *infinite* appetite can be filled only by an *infinite* good — the insatiability is not a defect to be cured but a *capacity that points to God* (nothing less than God says "Enough").
- Contentment appears in **two forms** that may be one or two: desire **fulfilled** (the satisfied soul, 107:9, 145:16) and desire **weaned** (the soul past craving, 131:2). Is the weaned child *satisfied* or *renouncing*? The text gives both as *ends* — and this is the live edge.

And a second: **does delighting reshape desire, or grant it?** "Delight in the LORD and he will give you the desires of your heart" (37:4) — either God *grants* the desires, or delighting in him *re-forms* the desires so that what the heart now wants is what God gives. The syntax allows both; the inner-being stakes are high.

## Junctions (boundaries blurring)
- **love-aheb** — the deepest junction. Love = *settled attachment*, desire = *reaching want*? Or the same operation (both object-set, both God-ward or ruinous)? "Delight" sits exactly on the seam.
- **waiting-hope** — hope *is* desire projected forward under delay; "hope deferred" (13:12) is desire-in-time. The boundary may be artificial.
- **the-felt-interior** — the *hope-sick heart* (13:12) is desire registering as feeling/soma.
- **self-mastery** — appetite-*restraint* (Pro 23:2 "knife to your throat"); desire governed.
- **the-compulsive-will** — craving that *captures* the will (21:25; the drunkard's "another drink", 23:35).

## Thin / uncertain evidence (noted, not yet weighed)
- **Desire for the WORD.** "More to be **desired** than gold… sweeter than honey" (Ps 19:10); "I **long** for your precepts" (Ps 119:40,131,174). Desire aimed at God's word specifically — junctions with wisdom-formation.
- **The directional couplets.** "The **desire of the righteous** will be granted, but what the wicked **dreads** will come" (Pro 10:24; 11:23) — desire and dread as two futures the self already lives toward. Thin but suggestive of desire as *anticipation*.
- **Being "satisfied with your likeness."** "I shall be **satisfied** with your likeness when I awake" (Ps 17:15) — a desire whose satisfaction is *deferred past this life*. One witness; a distinct eschatological colour.

## Open questions (the debate, left open)
1. Is desire **good, neutral, or fallen** by default? The corpus has holy thirst *and* deadly craving as the *same* faculty aimed differently — like love/aheb.
2. Is the **insatiable eye** a defect or a *capacity* — an infinite appetite that only God can fill?
3. Is **contentment** *fulfilment* (satisfied soul) or *renunciation* (weaned child) — or a passage from one to the other?
4. Does **delighting reshape** the desires or merely earn their granting (Ps 37:4)?
5. What finally distinguishes **desire from love** — reaching vs resting, want vs attachment — or nothing?

---
*Status: developing. Gathers desire across Psalms + Proverbs; foregrounds the insatiable-vs-satisfied paradox and the desire/love seam. Not a summary. Watch Ecclesiastes (the insatiable) and the Song (desire as love) for the next colours.*

*Section id 619 · status `approved` · v1 · 932 words · author `claude_code` · source `verse-analysis/characteristics/wa-ibchar-self-mastery-discovery-20260703.md`*

# Self-mastery / ruling one's spirit — a discovery document (developing)

> **Mode: DISCOVERY, not summary.** Gather the self-government evidence; trace the colours; hold open whether self-mastery (the ACT), self-address (the MODE), and stillness (the STATE) are three faces of one operation — and where the *governing* self sits relative to the *governed* spirit. Registry: `ib_characteristic.code = self-mastery`.

## Working sense (held open)
The self governing the self. In Proverbs it is the **supreme strength** (16:32) and the **wall** that makes a self defensible (25:28); in the Psalms it appears mostly as the *stilling* of one's own soul. A self that can hold, quiet, restrain, and steer itself.

## The evidence, gathered by colour

**Colour 1 — ruling / holding the spirit (the governing act).** "**Whoever rules his spirit** is better than **he who takes a city**" (Pro 16:32); "a fool gives **full vent** to his spirit, but a wise man **quietly holds it back**" (Pro 29:11). The conquest of the *self* set above the conquest of a city.

**Colour 2 — the WALL / city (self-control as defensibility).** "**A man without self-control is like a city broken into and left without walls**" (Pro 25:28). The un-governed self is *defenceless*; self-control is the perimeter that makes an interior holdable.

**Colour 3 — slow-to-anger / governing temper.** "Whoever is **slow to anger** has great understanding, but a **hasty temper** exalts folly" (Pro 14:29); "a **soft answer** turns away wrath" (Pro 15:1); "it is his **glory to overlook** an offense" (Pro 19:11). Temper governed — the overlooking a *chosen* honour.

**Colour 4 — appetite-restraint.** "Put a **knife to your throat** if you are given to appetite" (Pro 23:2); "eat only **enough** for you, lest you… vomit it" (Pro 25:16). The self checking its own hunger.

**Colour 5 — tongue-restraint / guarding the mouth.** "Whoever **restrains his lips** is prudent" (Pro 10:19); "whoever **guards his mouth** preserves his life" (Pro 13:3; 21:23); "a **cool spirit**" restrains words (Pro 17:27); "I will **guard my ways**… I will **muzzle my mouth**" (Ps 39:1); "**set a guard**, O LORD, over my mouth" (Ps 141:3). Speech governed — sometimes by the self, sometimes *asked of God* (141:3).

**Colour 6 — self-QUIETING / stilling the soul (the Psalter's mode).** "For God alone, O my soul, **wait in silence**" (Ps 62:1,5); "I have **calmed and quieted** my soul" (Ps 131:2); "**be angry, and do not sin**… **be silent**" (Ps 4:4); "**Be still**, and know that I am God" (Ps 46:10). The self *hushing itself*.

**Colour 7 — guarding the heart's INCLINATION.** "**Let not my heart incline** to any evil" (Ps 141:4); "keep your heart with all vigilance" (Pro 4:23). Governing not just act and word but the heart's *leaning* — and again, sometimes *asked of God* (141:4).

## Where it changes colour — the developing picture
Self-mastery spans **holding, quieting, restraining, cooling, steering** — from the fierce "rule his spirit / knife to the throat" to the tender "calmed and quieted… like a weaned child." The live discoveries:
- **The governed thing is usually the *spirit* (ruach)** — "rules his spirit" (16:32), "holds back his spirit" (29:11), "a cool spirit" (17:27), "the spirit of man is the lamp of the LORD" (20:27). This clusters with the seats-question (see `the-heart`): *ruach* may be the self's *governing/animating* aspect, the thing both ruled and doing the ruling.
- **Sometimes the self masters itself; sometimes it asks God to.** "I will muzzle my mouth" (Ps 39:1, self) vs "set a guard over my mouth" (Ps 141:3, asked of God); "let not my heart incline to evil" (141:4, asked of God). Self-mastery shades into *petition for keeping* — the self that does not trust its own governing asks God to govern it. **Where is the line between self-control and dependence for control?**

## Junctions (boundaries blurring)
- **self-address** — the *mode* of self-mastery: the self commanding its own soul ("O my soul…"). Is self-address how self-mastery is *performed*?
- **rest-stillness** — the *state* self-quieting produces (sweet sleep, the stilled soul). Act → state.
- **the-felt-interior** — self-mastery governs the *felt* states (the tranquil vs raging heart, Pro 14:30).
- **speech-outflow** — tongue-restraint is a large slice of self-mastery.
- **the-compulsive-will** — its *failure*: the un-governed self venting, the captured will unable to hold back.
- **the-heart** — ruling/inclining the heart (Colours 1,7).

## Thin / uncertain evidence (noted, not yet weighed)
- **Overlooking as *glory*.** "It is his **glory** to overlook an offense" (Pro 19:11) — restraint framed as *honour*, not mere suppression. A positive colour worth developing.
- **The "cool spirit."** "He who has a **cool spirit**" (Pro 17:27) — a *temperature* metaphor for self-command, against the "hot-tempered" (15:18). Physiological/temperamental register, lightly attested.
- **Bridling.** "I will **bridle** my tongue" imagery (Ps 39; cf. the horse/mule "without understanding" needing bit and bridle, Ps 32:9) — the self as an animal needing restraint. Suggestive of self-mastery as *self-bridling*.

## Open questions (the debate, left open)
1. Are **self-mastery (act), self-address (mode), and stillness (state)** three faces of one operation, or three operations?
2. Where does the **governing "I"** sit relative to the **governed spirit** — is the ruach both ruler and ruled?
3. Where is the line between **self-control** and **asking God for control** (Ps 141:3–4)? Is mature self-mastery actually *dependence*?
4. Is self-control a **strength the self has** (16:32 — a might greater than a warrior's) or a **gift/fruit** it receives? The corpus leans "strength," but the petitions (141) lean "gift."

---
*Status: developing. Gathers self-government across Psalms + Proverbs; foregrounds the ruach-clustering and the self-control-vs-dependence edge. Not a summary. Feeds `the-heart` (seats) and `self-address`.*

*Section id 620 · status `approved` · v1 · 1037 words · author `claude_code` · source `verse-analysis/characteristics/wa-ibchar-being-known-discovery-20260703.md`*

# Being known / searched / weighed / tested by God — a discovery document (developing)

> **Mode: DISCOVERY, not summary.** Gather the being-known evidence; trace the colours from threat to comfort to invitation; hold open what turns being-known from dread to welcome, and whether "testing" is inspection or a *refining that changes the self*. Registry: `ib_characteristic.code = being-known`.

## Working sense (held open)
The inner being's transparency to God — its thoughts, ways, depths lie open — and, at its height, the self that stops hiding and *asks* to be searched.

## The evidence, gathered by colour

**Colour 1 — exhaustively KNOWN.** "You have **searched me and known me**… you **discern my thoughts from afar**… acquainted with all my ways" (Ps 139:1–3); "he **knows the secrets of the heart**" (Ps 44:21); "the LORD **knows the thoughts of man**" (Ps 94:11); "he **fashions the hearts** of them all and **observes** all their deeds" (Ps 33:15). Not behaviour only but *thoughts* — known before the self is aware of them.

**Colour 2 — the INVITED search.** "**Search me**, O God, and **know my heart**! Try me and know my thoughts!" (Ps 139:23); "**Prove me**, O LORD, and **try me**; **test** my heart and my mind" (Ps 26:2). The self that *offers* its inmost — transparency embraced, even requested.

**Colour 3 — TESTED / refined (the assay that purifies).** "The crucible is for silver… and **the LORD tests hearts**" (Pro 17:3); "you have **tried us as silver is tried**" (Ps 66:10); "you have **tried my heart**… you have **tested** me and will find nothing" (Ps 17:3). Testing as *smelting* — refining, not merely inspecting.

**Colour 4 — WEIGHED / the excuse seen through.** "The LORD **weighs the heart**" (Pro 21:2; 16:2 "weighs the spirit"); "does not **he who weighs the heart perceive it**?" — the plea of ignorance exposed (Pro 24:12). Being-known as *moral assessment* the self cannot evade.

**Colour 5 — the LAMP within.** "**The spirit of man is the lamp of the LORD, searching all his innermost parts**" (Pro 20:27). God's searching is a light *inside* the person — the conscience as divine illumination of the self's depths.

**Colour 6 — INESCAPABLE presence.** "Where shall I **flee from your presence**? If I ascend to heaven, you are there; if I make my bed in Sheol, you are there… even the **darkness is not dark to you**" (Ps 139:7–12). Being-known as *unavoidable accompaniment* — nowhere is outside the gaze.

**Colour 7 — known-in-distress as COMFORT.** "You have **known the distress of my soul**" (Ps 31:7); "you **know my way**" (Ps 142:3); "you have kept count of my **tossings**; put my tears in your bottle" (Ps 56:8). Here being-known is *tender* — the self *glad* to be seen in its straits.

**Colour 8 — known before BIRTH.** "You **formed my inward parts**… your eyes saw my **unformed substance**; in your book were written… the days **formed for me**" (Ps 139:13–16). Known *before it existed* — foreknown, not merely observed.

## Where it changes colour — the developing picture
The decisive movement is **from being-known-as-threat to being-known-as-comfort to being-known-as-invitation.** The same fact — "you know my heart" — is *dread* to the guilty (the excuse seen through, Pro 24:12), *comfort* to the afflicted (you know my distress, Ps 31:7), and finally *welcomed* by the trusting self ("search me," Ps 139:23). **What accomplishes the passage?** Ps 139 itself models it: the self that begins overwhelmed by being known (v.6 "too wonderful") ends *asking* for it (v.23) — the difference is *trust in the searcher*. Being-known becomes bearable, then desirable, when the One who knows is loved and trusted.

A second edge: **is "testing" inspection or transformation?** Colour 3 (the crucible, Pro 17:3; Ps 66:10) is *refining* — the fire that *purifies* the metal, not just reveals its content. If God's testing *changes* the self (burns off dross), then being-known is not passive exposure but an active *forming* — junctioning with restoration and forgiveness.

And a third: **the lamp within (20:27).** If the human *spirit* is "the lamp of the LORD searching the innermost," then God's searching is not only external gaze but *interior light* — the conscience *is* God's searching operating inside the person. Being-known and self-examination may meet in the conscience.

## Junctions (boundaries blurring)
- **the-heart** — the heart is what is weighed/searched/fashioned (Colours 1,4,5,8).
- **self-examination** — the human counterpart; and the lamp-within (20:27) makes them nearly one.
- **integrity-legibility** — testing as *assay* of the true inner condition.
- **forgiveness-confession** — the un-self-cleansable heart (Pro 20:9) is *exposed* by being-known and can only be *made* clean.
- **self-address** — "search me" (139:23) is a self-offering that follows self-address.
- **restoration** — if testing *refines* (Colour 3), being-known makes the self new.

## Thin / uncertain evidence (noted, not yet weighed)
- **Being-known and being-COUNTED/kept.** "You keep **count** of my tossings; my tears in your bottle, in your **book**" (Ps 56:8); "in your book were written… the days" (Ps 139:16) — being-known as being *recorded/treasured*, not just seen. A tender colour, lightly attested.
- **Tested at NIGHT.** "You have **tried my heart**, you have **visited me by night**" (Ps 17:3) — testing in the dark/solitude, when no one watches. Junctions with the purposed heart (17:3). One-two witnesses.
- **The excuse pre-empted.** Pro 24:12's "we did not know" seen through — being-known specifically *defeats self-exculpation*. A moral edge worth developing.

## Open questions (the debate, left open)
1. What turns being-known from **threat → comfort → welcome** (Ps 139's own arc)? Is it simply *trust in the searcher*?
2. Is "**testing**" inspection or a **refining that changes the self** (the crucible, 17:3; 66:10)? — i.e. does being-known *form* the self?
3. Does the **lamp within** (Pro 20:27) mean the conscience **is** God's searching operating inside the person — collapsing being-known and self-examination?
4. Are being-known-as-**judge** (weighs the excuse, 24:12) and being-known-as-**comforter** (knows my distress, 31:7) the same operation felt differently, or two?
5. Why is the **summit of the inner being** its *asking to be searched* (139:23) — is total transparency-before-God the study's endpoint?

---
*Status: developing. Gathers being-known across Psalms + Proverbs; foregrounds the threat→welcome arc, the testing-as-refining question, and the lamp-within collapse of being-known/self-examination. Not a summary.*

*Section id 621 · status `approved` · v1 · 1037 words · author `claude_code` · source `verse-analysis/characteristics/wa-ibchar-formation-by-relation-discovery-20260703.md`*

# Formation by trust and company — a discovery document (developing)

> **Mode: DISCOVERY, not summary.** This may not be a *characteristic* at all but a **law over the whole inner being** — the candidate organising principle of the study. Gather its evidence, test its reach (trust, company, love, beholding), and hold open whether it is one operation or the physics under all of them. Registry: `ib_characteristic.code = formation-by-relation`.

## Working sense (held open)
The self **takes the shape of what it leans on and whom it keeps near.** Not a mood or an act but a *forming relation* — the inner being is *conformed* to its objects. If this is a law rather than a characteristic, it reframes the whole map: every other operation (trust, love, teachability, company) would be a *channel* of this one forming.

## The evidence, gathered by colour

**Colour 1 — you become what you TRUST.** "Their idols are silver and gold… **those who make them become like them; so do all who trust in them**" (Ps 115:8; 135:18). Dead idols *deaden* their trusters — blind, deaf, breathless things make blind, deaf, breathless worshippers. By the same law, trusting the *living* God enlivens (implied, not stated). This is the sharpest statement: *the object of trust re-forms the truster into its own likeness.*

**Colour 2 — you become like your COMPANY.** "**Whoever walks with the wise becomes wise, but the companion of fools will suffer harm**" (Pro 13:20); "make no friendship with a man given to anger, **lest you learn his ways** and entangle yourself" (Pro 22:24–25) — dispositions are *caught*. The self is shaped by its associations.

**Colour 3 — sharpened by ANOTHER (mutual).** "**Iron sharpens iron, and one man sharpens another**" (Pro 27:17). Formation as *mutual* honing — two selves shaping each other by contact.

**Colour 4 — the refused company (choosing NOT to be formed).** "Blessed is the man who **walks not** in the counsel of the wicked, **nor stands**… **nor sits** in the seat of scoffers" (Ps 1:1); "**I do not sit** with men of falsehood… I will not sit with the wicked" (Ps 26:4–5). The self *guarding its formation* by refusing certain company — a negative exercise of the same law.

**Colour 5 — wisdom acquired reshapes from WITHIN.** "Wisdom will **come into your heart**, and knowledge will be **pleasant to your soul**" (Pro 2:10); discretion "will **watch over you**" (Pro 2:11). What is internalised *becomes* an inward agent — the self re-formed by what it took in.

**Colour 6 — TRANSMISSION across generations.** "When I was a son with my father… **he taught me** and said, 'Let your heart hold fast my words'" (Pro 4:3–4). Formation *handed down* — the inner life inherited, not self-generated.

## Where it changes colour — the developing picture
The colours are all one motion seen through different relations: **trust** (Colour 1), **company** (2,3,4), **internalised wisdom** (5), **inheritance** (6). In each, the self is *conformed* to what it relates to. The live discovery is the **reach** of the law:
- It clearly runs through **trust** (115:8) and **company** (13:20).
- It plausibly runs through **love** — the aheb doc's darkest datum, "all who hate me **love death**" (Pro 8:36), reads as *you become what you love* (love death → die; love wisdom → live). Not yet stated as a law, but the structure matches.
- It may run through **beholding/attention** — the fixed gaze (Ps 25:15; 123), the meditation that dwells (Ps 1:2; 119) — *you become what you behold* (a structure the NT will make explicit, 2 Cor 3:18; here only implicit).

If the law reaches trust *and* love *and* company *and* attention, then it is **not one characteristic among the others but the physics beneath them** — the reason trust stabilises (you take the fixity of the Rock, Ps 125:1), the reason company corrupts, the reason the word revives. **This is the candidate organising principle for the whole inner being.**

## Junctions (boundaries blurring — it may *contain* several)
- **trust-refuge** — Colour 1 is trust's forming face; trust may be the clearest *instance* of the law.
- **love-aheb** — "you become what you love" (implied, 8:36).
- **teachability / wisdom-formation** — the internalised word reshaping the self (Colour 5).
- **self-toward-others** — company as a forming relation (Colours 2–4).
- **the-heart** — the heart as the surface *inscribed/entered* and so re-formed.

## Thin / uncertain evidence (noted, not yet weighed)
- **The mechanism is unnamed.** The texts *state* the outcome (you become like them) but never *explain* the mechanism — imitation? attachment? attention? an ontological conformation? All the data are outcome-data; the *how* is dark.
- **The self can CHOOSE its formation.** Because the law works through *chosen* relations (whom you trust, whom you sit with, what you meditate on), the self holds a *lever*: refuse the wicked's seat (Ps 1:1), choose the wise's company (13:20), fix the gaze on God (25:15). If so, formation-by-relation is the **master-lever of self-formation** — the one law the self can *use*. Suggestive; needs testing.
- **Directionality.** Does the object *always* win (you always become like what you trust), or can a strong self resist a bad company? The corpus leans "the object wins" (13:20 "the companion of fools *will* suffer harm"), but the refused-company texts (Ps 1, 26) imply the self can *pre-empt* by choice, not resist mid-relation.

## Open questions (the debate, left open)
1. Is this a **characteristic** or the **law/physics** under the whole inner being? (Strongly leans *law*.)
2. What is the **mechanism** — imitation, attachment, attention, ontological conformation?
3. Does the law reach **love** and **beholding** as it reaches trust and company — i.e. *you become what you trust AND love AND behold*?
4. Is formation-by-relation the **master-lever of self-formation** — the one law the self can *use* by choosing its relations?
5. If it is the organising principle, does the whole study reduce to a single question: **to what is the inner being joined?**

---
*Status: developing — and possibly foundational. Gathers the formation-law across Psalms + Proverbs; argues it may be the organising principle, not a peer characteristic. Not a summary. This doc should be revisited as every other characteristic's forming-face is traced back to it.*

*Section id 622 · status `approved` · v1 · 1040 words · author `claude_code` · source `verse-analysis/characteristics/wa-ibchar-the-felt-interior-discovery-20260703.md`*

# The felt interior / the heart's states — a discovery document (developing)

> **Mode: DISCOVERY, not summary.** Gather the *felt* states of the inner being; trace the colours; hold open whether the felt interior is a distinct characteristic or the *experiential face* of all of them, and why Proverbs — terse and impersonal — maps it more finely than expected. Registry: `ib_characteristic.code = the-felt-interior`.

## Working sense (held open)
The inner being as a *felt* thing — its states (glad, crushed, heavy, tranquil, anxious, bitter), their register on the body, and their privacy. This is where the inner being is most obviously *experienced* rather than *acted*.

## The evidence, gathered by colour

**Colour 1 — the incommunicable / private heart.** "**The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger shares its joy**" (Pro 14:10) — the deepest word in the corpus on the *privacy* of the interior: its grief and gladness are *not fully shareable*.

**Colour 2 — glad vs crushed (with somatic register).** "A **glad heart** makes a **cheerful face**, but by sorrow of heart the **spirit is crushed**" (Pro 15:13); "a **joyful heart is good medicine**, but a **crushed spirit dries up the bones**" (Pro 17:22); and the floor — "a man's spirit will endure sickness, but a **crushed spirit who can bear?**" (Pro 18:14). The state *shows on the face* and *works on the bones*.

**Colour 3 — the cheerful heart's "continual feast."** "The **cheerful of heart has a continual feast**" (Pro 15:15). The inner disposition, not the outer event, *sets the taste of existence* — a self that feasts on ordinary days because its heart is cheerful.

**Colour 4 — anxiety as a WEIGHT.** "**Anxiety in a man's heart weighs him down**, but a good word makes him glad" (Pro 12:25); "when the **cares of my heart are many**, your consolations **cheer my soul**" (Ps 94:19). Worry as a *downward pull*, lifted from outside.

**Colour 5 — the TRANQUIL heart (peace as bodily life; envy as bodily decay).** "A **tranquil heart gives life to the flesh, but envy makes the bones rot**" (Pro 14:30). Inner peace is *somatic health*; corrosive feeling is *somatic rot*.

**Colour 6 — the HEAVY heart (that cannot be jollied).** "Whoever **sings songs to a heavy heart** is like vinegar on soda" (Pro 25:20) — ill-timed cheer *aggravates* the heavy heart; the felt state must be *matched*, not overridden.

**Colour 7 — the self UNDONE / dissolved (extremity).** "My **heart melts like wax**" (Ps 22:14); "I am weary with my **moaning**… my eye **wastes** away from grief" (Ps 6:6–7); "my **bones wasted away**" (Ps 32:3); "my heart is struck down like grass and has **withered**" (Ps 102:4); "my **heart and flesh may fail**" (Ps 73:26). The felt interior at its limit — the whole self coming apart.

**Colour 8 — the MASK (outward belies inward).** "**Even in laughter the heart may ache**, and the end of joy may be grief" (Pro 14:13). The face can *contradict* the state — laughter over an inward ache.

## Where it changes colour — the developing picture
Two discoveries stand out:
- **The felt interior is intensely SOMATIC.** Almost every state writes itself on the body — cheerful face, crushed/dried bones, rotting bones, withered heart, wasting eye, melting-wax heart, failing flesh. The inner and the outer are *not sealed off*: the heart's state is *legible on the body* and *affects* it (good medicine / dries the bones). This is a real anthropology, not decoration — the inner being is *embodied*, its feeling and its flesh interpenetrating.
- **Proverbs maps this more finely than the Psalms** — which is surprising, since Proverbs is terse, impersonal, third-person, and Psalms is first-person prayer. Yet Proverbs gives the *incommunicable heart* (14:10), the *continual feast* (15:15), the *mask* (14:13), the *mistimed comfort* (25:20) — sharper *general* observations of felt states than the Psalms' *particular* cries. **The Psalms feel it; Proverbs anatomises it.** The two modes may be complementary evidence-channels on one thing.

## Junctions (boundaries blurring)
- **the-heart** — Colour 9 there = Colours here; the felt heart is the heart in its experiential mode.
- **grief-lament** — Colour 7 (the undone self) is grief felt; the boundary with grief-as-*handled* is where feeling becomes operation.
- **joy-gladness** — the glad/cheerful heart is joy felt.
- **rest-stillness** — the tranquil heart (Colour 5).
- **self-mastery** — the tranquil vs raging heart (14:30); governing the felt states.
- **self-toward-others** — envy (Colour 5) as a corrosive relational feeling.

## Thin / uncertain evidence (noted, not yet weighed)
- **Comfort from OUTSIDE.** The heavy heart is lifted by "a **good word**" (12:25), by God's "**consolations**" (94:19), aggravated by mistimed song (25:20). The felt interior is *permeable* — reachable (or wounded) from outside. A distinct sub-theme (the economy of comfort) worth gathering.
- **The felt interior entered only by God.** If "no stranger shares its joy" (14:10), yet "you have **known the distress of my soul**" (Ps 31:7) — then God enters where no *stranger* can. The privacy of the heart is total *toward humans* and open *toward God*. A profound junction (being-known) on thin but pointed data.
- **The PANG / being pierced.** "My soul was **embittered**, I was **pricked** in heart" (Ps 73:21) — feeling as a *wound/sting*. Lightly attested; a distinct texture.

## Open questions (the debate, left open)
1. Is the felt interior a **distinct characteristic** or the **experiential face** of all of them (trust felt as security, being-heard felt as relief, etc.)?
2. Why does **Proverbs anatomise** the felt heart more finely than the **Psalms** *feel* it — and what does that say about how the inner being is best studied (cry vs observation)?
3. Is the **somatic register** (heart → bones/face/flesh) metaphor, or a real anthropology in which the inner *writes on* the outer?
4. Is the inner being finally **solitary** (14:10 — no stranger shares it), entered only by God (31:7)? Is privacy-toward-humans + openness-toward-God its basic condition?
5. What is the **economy of comfort** — the felt heart reached, lifted, or wounded from outside (a good word, God's consolations, mistimed song)?

---
*Status: developing. Gathers the felt interior across Psalms + Proverbs; foregrounds the somatic anthropology, the Proverbs-anatomises/Psalms-feels complementarity, and the privacy-toward-humans/openness-toward-God condition. Not a summary.*

*Section id 623 · status `approved` · v1 · 1091 words · author `claude_code` · source `verse-analysis/characteristics/wa-ibchar-speech-outflow-discovery-20260703.md`*

# Speech as the outflow of the heart — a discovery document (developing)

> **Mode: DISCOVERY, not summary.** Gather the speech evidence; trace the colours; hold open whether speech is a *characteristic* or the primary *evidence-channel* for the others — and whether speech only reveals the heart or also *forms* it (and the hearer's). Registry: `ib_characteristic.code = speech-outflow`.

## Working sense (held open)
Speech as the heart *surfacing* — what is within comes out the mouth, so the lips *diagnose* the heart. But speech is also an *actor*: it kills, heals, and penetrates others. It is at once symptom and agent.

## The evidence, gathered by colour

**Colour 1 — legibility (the mouth reveals the heart).** "The **mouth of the righteous** is a fountain of life, but the **mouth of the wicked conceals violence**" (Pro 10:11); "the **tongue of the righteous** is choice silver; the **heart of the wicked** is of little worth" (Pro 10:20); "the **heart of fools proclaims folly**" (Pro 12:23); "the heart of the wise makes his speech **judicious**" (Pro 16:23); "there is **no truth in their mouth**… their throat is an open grave" (Ps 5:9). Speech as the heart made audible — the reliable *symptom* of the interior.

**Colour 2 — restraint (governing the outflow).** "When words are many, transgression is not lacking, but whoever **restrains his lips** is prudent" (Pro 10:19); "whoever **guards his mouth** preserves his life" (Pro 13:3; 21:23); "**I will muzzle my mouth**" (Ps 39:1); "**set a guard** over my mouth" (Ps 141:3). The self *holding* its outflow. (Junctions self-mastery.)

**Colour 3 — concealment / masking (the mouth HIDES the heart).** "**Fervent lips with an evil heart** are like the glaze covering an earthen vessel… when he speaks graciously, **believe him not**, for there are **seven abominations in his heart**" (Pro 26:23–25); "whoever **conceals hatred** has lying lips" (Pro 10:18); "'Eat and drink!' he says, but **his heart is not with you**" (Pro 23:7); "his **speech was smooth… but war was in his heart**" (Ps 55:21; 28:3; 62:4). Here speech *breaks* legibility — deliberately masking the heart with fair words.

**Colour 4 — the power of LIFE and DEATH.** "**Death and life are in the power of the tongue**" (Pro 18:21); "the words of a man's mouth are **deep waters**" (Pro 18:4); "a fool's mouth is **his ruin**, and his lips a **snare to his soul**" (Pro 18:7). Speech as an *agent* of the gravest outcomes.

**Colour 5 — healing / gracious words (the tongue as medicine).** "The **tongue of the wise brings healing**" (Pro 12:18); "**gracious words** are like a honeycomb, **sweetness to the soul** and health to the body" (Pro 16:24); "a **gentle tongue is a tree of life**" (Pro 15:4); "a **word in season**, how good it is!" (Pro 15:23; 25:11). Speech that *heals and sweetens* the hearer's interior.

**Colour 6 — PENETRATION (words go into the inner parts).** "The words of a **whisperer** are like delicious morsels; they **go down into the inner parts** of the body" (Pro 18:8; 26:22). Speech does not stay on the surface — it *enters* the hearer and lodges within.

**Colour 7 — the God-ward tongue.** "**Open my lips**, and my mouth will declare your praise" (Ps 51:15); "his praise shall **continually be in my mouth**" (Ps 34:1); confession — "**I acknowledged my sin**… and you forgave" (Ps 32:5). Speech turned *toward God* — praise, confession, the release of the concealed self.

## Where it changes colour — the developing picture
Speech is **both symptom and agent**, and this doubling is the discovery:
- As *symptom* (Colours 1,3) it *reveals* the heart — reliably, unless deliberately *masked*. The masking (Colour 3) is the interesting break: the wicked can *coat* an evil heart with gracious speech (the glaze over cheap clay), so the mouth *lies about* the heart. Yet the corpus insists the mask *fails* — "his wickedness will be **exposed** in the assembly" (Pro 26:26). So legibility is the *default and the end*, masking a *temporary success*.
- As *agent* (Colours 4,5,6) speech *acts on* the hearer's interior — killing, healing, penetrating "into the inner parts." This raises the deepest question: **does speech only reveal the heart, or also form it?** If a whisperer's words "go down into the inner parts" (18:8), then speech *enters and shapes* the hearer — a channel of formation-by-relation (you become what you are told). And "gracious words… health to the body" (16:24) *heal* the interior. Speech is not only the heart's exhaust but a *tool that works on other hearts*.

## Junctions (boundaries blurring)
- **integrity-legibility** — the largest junction; the masking heart (Colour 3) is where speech and integrity meet. Are they one operation seen from two sides (the condition, and its readability)?
- **the-heart** — speech is the heart surfacing (Colours 1,3).
- **self-mastery** — tongue-restraint (Colour 2) is a slice of self-government.
- **formation-by-relation** — words penetrating/forming the hearer (Colour 6) — speech as a forming channel.
- **forgiveness-confession** — confession (Colour 7) as the speech that releases.

## Thin / uncertain evidence (noted, not yet weighed)
- **Speech as DEEP WATERS.** "The words of a man's mouth are **deep waters**; the fountain of wisdom a bubbling brook" (Pro 18:4) — speech as coming *from the depths* of the self, not the surface. A colour that ties speech to the deep/opaque heart (20:5).
- **The word IN SEASON.** "A **word fitly spoken**… a word **in season**" (Pro 25:11; 15:23) — the *timing* of speech as an inner-being skill (reading the moment). Lightly gathered; junctions discernment.
- **Rash words as sword-thrusts.** "**Rash words** are like sword thrusts" (Pro 12:18) — the *unconsidered* tongue as a weapon; the failure of the pondering heart (15:28). A junction with self-mastery/the pondering heart.

## Open questions (the debate, left open)
1. Is speech a **characteristic** or the primary **evidence-channel** for the heart (the way we *read* the other operations)?
2. Does speech only **reveal** the heart, or also **form** it — and form the *hearer* (words that penetrate the inner parts, 18:8)?
3. How does **masking** (Colour 3) coexist with **legibility** (Colour 1) — is the mask always a temporary success that finally fails (26:26)?
4. Are **speech** and **integrity** one operation (the inner condition and its readability) or two?
5. Is the **God-ward tongue** (praise/confession, Colour 7) a distinct operation (speech toward God) or the same outflow turned upward?

---
*Status: developing. Gathers speech across Psalms + Proverbs; foregrounds the symptom/agent doubling and the does-speech-form-the-heart question. Not a summary. Closely paired with `integrity-legibility`, which it should be read against.*

# Ruthlessness — the story from the refined lexicals (5 passages, 2026-07-02)

- **Source:** the sanity-checked `lexical-model-2026` ve-records (roles assigned: characteristic / process-qualifier / standalone). **Lexicals only** — no old fanout, no old findings, no cohabitation. Cited; grounded in the DB.
- **The one characteristic** these passages turn on is **ruthlessness** (perek / "harshness") — role=characteristic in every occurrence (Exo 1:13-14; Lev 25:43,46,53; Eze 34:4). It is never a standalone act: it **welds to** a verb of dominion. Everything else is process (the actions/drivers it works through) or standalone background.

## The story
**I. Egypt — dread schemes into ruthless enslavement (Exo 1:7-14).**
A king who *did not know* Joseph (Exo 1:8) plots — *"deal shrewdly"* (1:10) — against a people he casts as **enemies**; out of **dread** (1:12) he **afflicts** and **oppresses** them (1:11-12); and he makes them serve — **ruthlessly** (1:13; the characteristic welds to *enslave*, source = dread) — **embittering** their lives (1:14; effect = *bitter*).

**II. The servant-law — ruthlessness forbidden, the fear of God its restraint (Lev 25:34-53).**
The law **forbids** ruling a brother **ruthlessly** (1:43; characteristic, prohibition) and sets against it the **fear of God** (restrained-by fear-of-God @25:36/43). The poor brother is to be **supported** (25:35), **lent to** without gain (25:37), **not made a slave** (25:39). Ruthlessness recurs as the forbidden **manner of rule** (25:46; 25:53).

**III. The shepherds — ruthlessness as the failure of care (Eze 34:4-6).**
The shepherds do **not strengthen, heal, or seek** (34:4, all under prohibition) but **rule** with **force** and **harshness** (34:4; the characteristic welds to *rule*); and the flock is **scattered** (34:5).

**Across the three:** ruthlessness is the **harsh manner of dominion** (welds to *enslave* and *rule*), **driven** by dread, **restrained** only by the fear of God, **condemned** wherever it appears — its impact the **embittering of life** and the **scattering of the weak**.

## Honest notes (from the refined-but-not-perfect lexicals)
- The **spine is clean** now: role=characteristic isolates ruthlessness (6 spans); source=dread, restraint=fear-of-God, prohibition, and the enslave/rule welds all hold.
- **Residual process-qualifier noise** remains (next refinement circle): `manner`/`coupling` still over-attach to any preposition-marked noun — e.g. *heavy* "welds afflict", *Pharaoh* "welds built", *of* "welds dread", *mortar* "welds bitter". These are qualifier-level mis-welds; they don't touch the characteristic spine but should be tightened.
- **Bearer** is flagged unreliable in D11 on every bearer span (nearest-agent heuristic; subject-agreement not yet parsed) — so the story does not lean on bearer.

*Section id 549 · status `approved` · v2 · 847 words · author `claude_code` · source `verse-analysis/psalms/readings/wa-psalm1-inner-being-reading-20260702.md`*

# Psalm 1 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 1:1–6 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Lexicals only; cited; grounded in the verses. Every inference tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). *Part B of the re-alignment sweep — process-lens re-frame + Lens bullet added; findings unchanged (this reading was already operation-focused).*
- **The chapter is multi-characteristic** (as expected for a poem): it works by **two ways** set in antithesis, and reads the inner being from several perspectives at once — **desire, cognition, moral condition, rootedness, and destiny**.

## The reading
Psalm 1 does not describe a deed so much as an **orientation of the inner being** — which way the whole person is turned — and it contrasts two.

**I. The blessed man — a desire that becomes meditation (vv.1–2).**
The blessed man is first defined by a **refusal**: he does *not* walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand in the way of sinners, nor sit in the seat of scoffers (v.1). The three verbs *walk → stand → sit*, paired with *counsel → way → seat*, read as a **deepening of association** *(inferred from the progression)* — from taking advice, to taking the road, to taking a seat among mockers. What he refuses is a settling-in with evil. Positively, his inner life is a **desire**: his *delight* (H2656, characteristic — M04) is in the law of the LORD (v.2). *Delight* is affection, not duty *(stated: the term is pleasure/delight)* — the law is what he *wants*. And that desire does not stay still: it becomes **meditation** (H1897, characteristic — M42), a low continual muttering *day and night* (v.2). So the inner sequence is **desire → rumination**: what the inner being loves, it dwells on *(inferred)*.

**II. The impact — rootedness, fruit, permanence (v.3).**
The effect of that inner orientation is given as a simile: he is *like a tree planted by streams of water.* Its lexical operations — it **yields** its fruit in season, its leaf does **not wither**, and *in all he does he prospers* — read as the **stability and fruitfulness** the delighting-meditating inner life produces *(inferred: the tree is the vehicle; the tenor is the man of vv.1–2)*. The inner being that is rooted in what it loves does not run dry; it bears in season and endures out of season.

**III. The other way — the wicked, rootless and driven (vv.4–5).**
*Not so the wicked* (v.4). Where the righteous is planted, the wicked (H7563, characteristic — M10) is *like chaff that the wind drives away* — the exact negation of rootedness: no soil, no water, no permanence, carried off by a breath *(stated: chaff/wind/drives)*. The consequence is inability to **stand**: the wicked will not stand in the judgment, nor sinners (H2400, characteristic — M10) in the congregation of the righteous (v.5). The inner condition that took its seat among scoffers has no standing when it counts *(inferred: the v.1 progression closes here)*.

**IV. The two destinies — knowing and perishing (v.6).**
The psalm resolves the two ways into two ends held by the LORD: he *knows* the way of the righteous (H6662, characteristic — M26), but the way of the wicked will *perish* (v.6). The righteous's way is **relationally known** — held, acknowledged *(stated: "the LORD knows")*; the wicked's way simply ends.

## What Psalm 1 says about the inner being
- The inner being is fundamentally **oriented** — turned one of two ways — and the psalm reads that orientation from several angles at once: **desire** (delight), **cognition** (meditation), **moral condition** (righteous / wicked–sinner–scoffer), **rootedness** (planted tree vs driven chaff), and **destiny** (endure/known vs perish).
- The generative core is **desire that becomes meditation**: the blessed inner life *loves* the law and therefore *dwells* on it continually — and that inner orientation, not any single act, is what roots the person into stability and fruitfulness.
- The wicked is drawn as the **privation** of this: not a rival root but *no* root — rootless, transient, unable to stand.
- **Blessedness** is thus presented as an inner state (a rooted, God-delighting, meditating orientation), not a reward for deeds.

## Honest notes
- **Characteristics** the chapter surfaces (sanity-checked roles): *delight* (M04), *meditation* (M42) — the righteous inner life; *wicked / sinners* (M10) and *righteous* (M26) — the two moral poles; the tree-simile operations *yields / does-not-wither* carried as the **fruitfulness/stability** expression of the righteous (kept as characteristic; read as the simile's tenor).
- **counsel** (v.1) and **judgment** (v.5) were sanity-checked to **process-qualifier** (they function adverbially — the *sphere* of the wrong walk, the *scene* of non-standing — not inner dispositions).
- **bearer** is unreliable across vv.2 and 6 (the nearest-proper heuristic attaches "LORD" to spans it does not govern) — flagged in D11; this reading does not lean on bearer (e.g. it is the *man*, not the LORD, who meditates in v.2).
- Residual mechanical noise (prohibition over-firing, manner/coupling over-welding) does not touch the reading's spine.

# Psalm 2 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 2:1–12 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). **Complete chapter** — verses 3–4 were absent from the corpus and were **backfilled** (measure-layer ingest) before this reading. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). §II (the LORD's derision/wrath) is the *arena* — the drama's counter-voice — not itself a human inner-being finding; the findings are the human movements (defiant desire, glad awe, sheltering refuge). *Part B re-alignment sweep; findings unchanged.*
- **Multi-characteristic**, and structured as a **four-voice drama** — the nations, the LORD, the Anointed, and the psalmist's closing counsel — each disclosing a different movement of the inner being: **defiant desire, holy wrath, derision, and the fear/refuge that is the only safety.**

## The reading
Psalm 2 stages the inner being through **who speaks**, and reads it as a collision between human self-will and divine sovereignty.

**I. The nations — defiant desire that schemes (vv.1–3).**
The peoples **rage** and **plot** (H1897, characteristic — M42) "in vain" (v.1) — an inner scheming, the same lexical operation that is godly *meditation* in Psa 1:2, here turned to **conspiracy** *(inferred: valence from context; the operation is identical, the object opposite)*. The kings **set themselves** and take **counsel together** against the LORD and his Anointed (v.2). Their inner posture is then spoken aloud (v.3, backfilled): "let us **burst** their bonds and **cast** away their cords" — the desire underneath the plotting is **the throwing-off of restraint** *(stated: burst/cast the bonds/cords)*. The inner being here is **autonomy as appetite** — rule experienced as bondage, freedom imagined as revolt.

**II. The LORD — derision, then holy wrath (vv.4–6).**
The answer is first **laughter**: the One enthroned in the heavens **laughs**, holds them in **derision** (v.4, backfilled) — the rebellion is not met with alarm but with **contempt for its futility** *(inferred: derision as the measure of the threat)*. Then the mood turns: he will **speak** to them in his wrath and **terrify** them (H0926, characteristic — M01) in his **fury** (H2740, qualifier — M02) (v.5) — dread deliberately induced. And he asserts the settled fact they revolted against: "I have **set** my King on Zion, my **holy** hill" (v.6). *(holy here qualifies the place, not a human inner state — sanity-checked to standalone.)*

**III. The Anointed — sonship and the asking (vv.7–9).**
The King recites the **decree**: "You are my Son; today I have begotten you" (v.7) — an identity **received, not seized** *(inferred, against the nations' seizing)*. And the mode of his rule is **petition**: "**Ask** of me (H7592, characteristic — M21), and I will make the nations your heritage" (v.8) — dominion comes by **asking the Father**, the exact inverse of the kings who take counsel to grasp it. The rule itself is unbreakable (v.9, the iron rod).

**IV. The counsel — be wise; serve with fear; take refuge (vv.10–12).**
The psalmist turns to the rebels with an inner-being summons: "be **wise** (H7919, characteristic — M15), be warned" (v.10) *(rulers/judges here = a vocative address, sanity-checked to standalone).* The prescribed inner posture is **Serve the LORD** (H5647, characteristic — M36) **with fear** (H3374, qualifier — M01), and **rejoice** (H1523, characteristic — M04) **with trembling** (H7461, qualifier — M01) (v.11) — a striking weld: joy and dread held together, worship that is glad *and* awed. The alternative is his **anger** (H0599, characteristic — M02) kindled (v.12). The psalm closes where Psalm 1 began: "**Blessed** are all who **take refuge** (H2620, characteristic — M19) in him" — the inner being's only safety is **sheltering trust**, the opposite of the opening revolt.

## What Psalm 2 says about the inner being
- The chapter reads the inner being as a **contest of wills**, disclosed through four voices: **defiant desire** (the nations — autonomy felt as the throwing-off of restraint), **holy wrath and derision** (the LORD — the rebellion is contemptible, then dreadful), **received sonship that asks rather than seizes** (the Anointed), and the counselled posture of **fear-filled worship and sheltering refuge** (the close).
- Its sharpest disclosure is the **weld of opposites** in v.11: *serve with fear*, *rejoice with trembling* — the right inner orientation to God is **glad awe**, joy and dread inseparable.
- **Refuge/trust** (v.12) is named as the inner being's safety — and it stands as the exact inverse of the opening **revolt** (v.3): the whole psalm moves from "burst his bonds" to "take refuge in him."
- The **same operation carries opposite value by context**: *hagah* is *meditation* (Psa 1:2) and *plotting* (Psa 2:1) — the inner being's activity is morally weighted by its object, not its mechanism.

## Honest notes
- **Corpus completeness:** vv.3–4 were **backfilled** (they held no study term, so were absent) — without them the psalm would have lost the rebels' cry *and* the divine derision, its two hinges. Both are gate-2 content (no IB-cluster term tags them), read here as operations.
- **Characteristics** (sanity-checked): *plot* (M42), *terrify* (M01), *ask* (M21), *wise* (M15), *serve* (M36), *rejoice* (M04), *angry* (M02), *take-refuge* (M19); qualifiers *fury/fear/trembling* (M02/M01).
- **Reclassified** by sanity-check: *holy* (v.6, attribute of a place → standalone), *rulers/judges* (v.10, vocative address → standalone).
- **bearer** unreliable in vv.4,7,11 (nearest-proper "LORD" bleed) — flagged D11; the reading does not lean on it (the bearers of *serve/rejoice* are the kings, not the LORD).

# Psalm 3 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 3:1–8 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (no backfill needed). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens (re-framed 2026-07-03):** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`). *Part B re-alignment sweep; §II re-headed to lead with the inner-being effect (dignity restored) rather than God-as-actor; findings unchanged.*
- **The movement** is a single arc from **encirclement to rest**: from an assault that targets not just the body but *hope* itself, to a settled confidence in God that shows itself as a **lifted head, peaceful sleep, and fearlessness**.

## The reading
Psalm 3 (David fleeing Absalom, per the superscription in v.1) reads the inner being under siege — and its distinctive disclosure is what **trust does to a threatened person**.

**I. The assault reaches the soul (vv.1–2).**
The opening is pressure: "how **many** are my **foes** (H6862, M44 Relational), many are **rising** against me" (v.1) — the intensity marker *many* is stamped on nearly every span, the felt weight of being outnumbered *(inferred from the repetition)*. But the sharpest blow is not physical: "many are **saying** of my **soul** (H5315, M47 Constitution — the seat), 'There is no **salvation** for him in God'" (v.2). The attack is aimed **at the inner being** — at hope — trying to sever the sufferer from his God *(stated: they speak against the soul)*.

**II. The turn — dignity restored from outside the self; the lifted head (v.3).**
The operation here is the inner being's **dignity being restored from beyond itself** (God the arena of that restoration). Against the assault, a threefold confession: "But you, O LORD, are a shield about me, my **glory** (H3519, M22 Praise), and the **lifter of my head**." The inner being's dignity is **restored from outside itself** — where the foes said *no salvation*, God is named as the very **honour and raised head** of the one they mock *(inferred: the lifted head answers the assault on hope)*.

**III. Crying and being answered (v.4).**
"I **cried** aloud (H7121, M37 Calling) to the LORD, and he **answered** me from his holy hill." The inner posture is **appeal** — the calling-out that expects response *(holy here qualifies the hill, a place → sanity-checked standalone)*.

**IV. The jewel — sleep in the middle of danger (vv.5–6).**
"I **lay** down and **slept**; I **woke** again, for the LORD **sustained** me" (v.5). This is the psalm's inner-being centre: trust that produces **rest** — the confidence that can *sleep* while surrounded *(inferred: sleep amid threat is the bodily proof of an inner security)*. From it flows fearlessness: "I will **not be afraid** (H3372, M01 Fear) of many **thousands** set against me" (v.6). The negated fear is the point — trust has **displaced** dread, not merely balanced it.

**V. Appeal and confession (vv.7–8).**
"**Arise**, O LORD! **Save** me" (v.7) — confidence does not make the appeal unnecessary; it makes it bold. And the close names the ground of the whole: "**Salvation** belongs to the LORD; your **blessing** (H1293, M22 Praise) be on your people" (v.8) — the deliverance the foes denied (v.2) is precisely what the psalm ends by confessing as God's own.

## What Psalm 3 says about the inner being
- The inner being can be **assaulted at the level of hope** — the cruelest attack (v.2) is the whisper that there is *no salvation for you*, aimed at the soul, not the body.
- Its answer is **confidence received from God**: dignity restored (the lifted head, v.3), rest granted (sleep amid enemies, v.5), and fear displaced (v.6). Trust is shown not as a feeling but as an **effect** — you can sleep, you are not afraid.
- **Calling-out** (v.4) and **bold appeal** (v.7) coexist with that confidence — trust makes the cry more urgent, not less.
- The arc closes the wound it opened: the "no salvation" of v.2 becomes "**salvation belongs to the LORD**" of v.8.

## Honest notes
- **New noise type — superscription metadata:** *Psalm* (H4210, mizmor — the genre label) was mechanically marked a characteristic (M22); it is superscription metadata → **standalone** (a stop-list for genre-label/superscription lemmas is a candidate refinement). Proper names (*David*, *Absalom*) sit as gate-2 standalone, correctly.
- **External vs inner:** *foes* (H6862) and *enemies* (H0341), M44 Relational, are **external adversaries**, not inner states → read as the pressure the inner being faces, not characteristics ([[feedback_external_pole_not_inner_state]]).
- **Characteristics** (sanity-checked): *cried* (M37 Calling), *not-afraid* (M01 Fear); with *glory* / *blessing* (M22 Praise) read as God-given dignity/bestowal, and *soul* (M47) as the seat the assault targets.
- **Residuals:** bearer=LORD bleed (nearest-proper) across most verses — flagged D11, not leaned on; *many/all* intensity over-stamping; manner/coupling over-weld.
