# Proverbs 25 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 25, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-25-heart-unsearchable · 25:2,3 · [S] — the unsearchable depth of the heart.** "As the **heavens for height and the earth for depth, so the heart of kings is unsearchable**" (v.3). Finding: the heart's depth is likened to the *unsearchable* heights and depths of creation *(stated; the opaque-heart thread, cross-book w/ 20:5, Ps 64:6 "the inward mind and heart… are deep")*. *Surfaced:* the unsearchable-deep heart (shared w/ 20:5).

**PRO-25-heavy-heart · 25:20 · [S] — comfort mistimed wounds the heavy heart.** "**Whoever sings songs to a heavy heart is like vinegar on soda**" (v.20). Finding: the **heavy heart** is a real felt state that *ill-timed cheer* only aggravates *(stated)*. Operation: **the felt heaviness that cannot be jollied out of** — comfort must match the heart's state or it *stings* *(inferred; the felt-interior thread, cross-book w/ Ps 137:2–4 refusing to sing in grief)*. *Surfaced:* the heavy heart / mistimed comfort (shared felt-interior).

**PRO-25-enemy-bread · 25:21,22 · [S, multi] — good done to the enemy.** "**If your enemy is hungry, give him bread… you will heap burning coals on his head, and the LORD will reward you**" (vv.21–22). Finding — a cornerstone: the disposition toward the enemy is **active good**, not merely restrained revenge *(stated)*. Operation: **love of enemy expressed as provision** — the self *feeds* the one who wronged it, leaving the outcome to God *(inferred; the fullest positive form of the not-repaying thread, cross-book w/ Ps 35:13, Rom 12:20)*. *Surfaced:* good-done-to-the-enemy / love-of-enemy (★ cornerstone, w/ Ps 35).

**PRO-25-thirsty-soul · 25:25 · [S] — the thirsting soul refreshed by good news.** "**Like cold water to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country**" (v.25). Finding: the soul **thirsts**, and good news is *cold water* to it *(stated; the thirsting-soul thread, cross-book w/ Ps 42:1–2, 63:1, 143:6)*. *Surfaced:* the thirsting soul (★ shared cross-book w/ Ps 42/63).

**PRO-25-self-control · 25:28 · [S] — self-control as the wall of the self.** "**A man without self-control is like a city broken into and left without walls**" (v.28). Finding — a cornerstone: the un-governed self is **defenceless**, a breached city *(stated)*. Operation: **self-control as the *wall* that makes a self defensible** — without it the interior lies open to every incursion *(inferred; the self-mastery cornerstone, cross-book w/ 16:32, 29:11, and the Psalter's self-governing self)*. *Surfaced:* self-control as the wall of the self (★ cornerstone).

---
**Chapter notes.** **Cornerstones:** love-of-enemy/good-done (★ 25:21, w/ Ps 35); the thirsting soul (★ 25:25, w/ Ps 42/63); self-control-as-wall (★ 25:28). **Shared:** the unsearchable heart; the heavy heart / mistimed comfort.

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-25-humility-before-great · Prov 25:5, 6, 7 · [D] — self-lowering before the great.** "Take away the **wicked from the presence of the king**, and his throne will be established in righteousness" (v.5); "**do not put yourself forward** in the king's presence or stand in the place of the great, for it is **better to be told, 'Come up here,'** than to be put lower" (vv.6–7). Finding: the wise self **does not exalt itself** before the great — it is better to be *raised* than to be *lowered* *(stated)*. Operation: **the humility that declines self-promotion** — taking the low place and being invited up, rather than grasping honour and being demoted *(inferred; self-lowering as wisdom, w/ Luke 14:8–10; the un-self-promoting interior)*. *Surfaced:* the humility that declines self-promotion (new — w/ Luke 14:8).

**PRO-25-prudent-dispute · Prov 25:8, 9, 10 · [D, multi] — restraint in conflict.** "Do **not hastily bring** a matter into court… what will you do when your neighbour puts you to shame?" (v.8); "**argue your case with your neighbour himself, and do not reveal another's secret**, lest… your **ill repute have no end**" (vv.9–10). Finding: the prudent self **handles disputes directly and discreetly** — not rushing to court, not betraying confidences *(stated)*. Operation: **the self-restraint that keeps conflict contained and confidences kept** — haste and secret-telling both recoil into lasting shame *(inferred; discretion in dispute)*. *Surfaced:* restraint in conflict; keeping a confidence even in a quarrel (new).

**PRO-25-listening-faithful · Prov 25:12, 13 · [S, multi] — the listening ear and the refreshing faithful.** "Like a **gold ring… is a wise reprover to a listening ear**" (v.12); "like the **cold of snow in harvest is a faithful messenger** to those who send him; he **refreshes the soul** of his masters" (v.13). Finding: wise reproof meeting a **listening ear** is an ornament; a **faithful messenger refreshes the soul** *(stated)*. Operation: **the receptive interior that adorns reproof, and faithfulness as refreshment** — the reproof is beautiful only where there is an ear to receive it; the faithful one cools like snow *(inferred; receptivity as what makes correction golden, w/ the teachability thread)*. *Surfaced:* the listening ear that makes reproof golden (thread); faithfulness that refreshes the soul (new).

**PRO-25-empty-betrayal · Prov 25:14, 18, 19 · [D, multi] — empty words and unreliable trust.** "Like **clouds and wind without rain is a man who boasts of a gift he does not give**" (v.14); "a man who **bears false witness** against his neighbour is like a **war club, a sword, a sharp arrow**" (v.18); "**trusting in a treacherous man in time of trouble is like a bad tooth or a foot that slips**" (v.19). Finding: the **empty boaster** promises rain and gives none; false witness is a weapon; and **misplaced trust fails exactly when needed** *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior that promises and does not deliver, and the pain of trust betrayed in crisis** — the treacherous man is a tooth that breaks on the very bite that needs it *(inferred; the felt failure of false trust, w/ Job 6:15 the dry-wadi friends)*. *Surfaced:* the empty boaster (new); trust that fails in the crisis (w/ Job 6:15).

**PRO-25-restraint · Prov 25:17, 23, 27 · [D, multi] — restraint of presence, tongue, and self-glory.** "Let your **foot be seldom in your neighbour's house**, lest he have his fill of you and **hate** you" (v.17); "the north wind brings rain, and a **backbiting tongue, angry looks**" (v.23); "it is not good to eat much honey, **nor is it glorious to seek one's own glory**" (v.27). Finding: the self exercises **restraint** — of its presence (don't wear out welcome), its tongue (backbiting breeds anger), and its self-seeking (glory-hunting is not glorious) *(stated)*. Operation: **the self-limiting interior** — knowing when enough is enough, in company, in speech, and in appetite for honour *(inferred; self-restraint across domains; the glory-seeking self checked, w/ Ecc 1's vanity of self-exalting)*. *Surfaced:* restraint of presence/tongue/self-glory (new); glory-seeking as not glorious.

**PRO-25-compromised-righteous · Prov 25:26 · [S] — the righteous who gives way.** "Like a **muddied spring or a polluted fountain is a righteous man who gives way before the wicked**" (v.26). Finding: a righteous man who **caves before the wicked** becomes a *fouled source* — his compromise pollutes what should be pure *(stated)*. Operation: **integrity's failure imaged as a polluted spring** — the righteous is meant to be a clean fountain; yielding to evil muddies it *(inferred; a sharp image of compromised integrity)*. *Surfaced:* the compromised righteous as a fouled spring (new — a gem).

**PRO-25-quarrelsome · Prov 25:24 · [S] — the strife-filled home (again).** "It is **better to live in a corner of the housetop than in a house shared with a quarrelsome wife**" (v.24). Finding: chronic strife makes the home unlivable *(stated; repeated from 21:9)*. Operation: strife driving the self to solitude (thread w/ 21:9, 17:1) *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* the strife-filled home (thread w/ 21:9).

# Proverbs 26 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 26, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-26-wise-own-eyes · 26:12 · [S] — self-conceit worse than folly.** "**Do you see a man who is wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him**" (v.12). Finding: **self-conceit is more hopeless than folly** — the self certain of its own wisdom cannot be helped *(stated; the self-certainty thread, cross-book w/ 3:7, 12:15, Ps 36:2)*. *Surfaced:* self-conceit as the most hopeless closure (★ shared thread, sharpened).

**PRO-26-sluggard · 26:13,14,15,16 · [T, multi] — the self-justifying sloth.** "The sluggard says, '**There is a lion in the road!**'… As a **door turns on its hinges, so the sluggard on his bed**… The sluggard is **wiser in his own eyes than seven men** who can answer sensibly" (vv.13,14,16). Finding: sloth **manufactures excuses** (a lion!), turns endlessly without progress, and is *self-certain* about its own sense *(stated)*. Operation: **the self-justifying inertia** — the slothful interior *rationalises* its inaction and cannot see itself *(inferred; sloth + self-conceit joined)*. *Hidden:* **sloth's self-justification** (excuse-making as an inner operation). *Surfaced:* self-justifying sloth (new — sloth wedded to self-conceit).

**PRO-26-concealing-heart · 26:23,24,25,26 · [T, multi] — the masking self exposed.** "**Fervent lips with an evil heart** are like the **glaze covering an earthen vessel**… whoever **hates disguises himself with his lips and harbors deceit in his heart**; when he **speaks graciously, believe him not, for there are seven abominations in his heart**; though his hatred be **covered with deception**, his wickedness will be **exposed**" (vv.23–26). Finding — a cornerstone of the masking self: the wicked **coats an evil heart with gracious speech** (glaze over cheap clay), *disguising hatred with the lips* — but the concealment *fails*, the heart is exposed *(stated)*. Operation: **the split between mouth and heart made into a strategy** — the self deliberately *masks* its interior with fair speech, and the reading's warning is *not to believe the surface*; yet the hidden heart is finally *uncoverable to God/the assembly* *(inferred; the masking-self thread at its fullest, cross-book w/ Ps 28:3 "who speak peace… while evil is in their hearts", 55:21, 62:4)*. *Hidden:* **concealment as a *deliberate craft*** (the glaze) — and its ultimate failure. *Surfaced:* the masking/concealing heart (★ cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps 28/55); "believe not the fair surface."

---
**Chapter notes.** **Cornerstone:** the masking/concealing heart (★ 26:24–26, w/ Ps 28/55). **New:** self-justifying sloth. **Shared:** self-conceit ("wise in his own eyes").

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-26-fool-honor · Prov 26:1, 8, 11 · [D, multi] — honour misplaced on a fool; folly's return.** "Like snow in summer… **honour is not fitting for a fool**" (v.1); "like one who **binds the stone in the sling is one who gives honour to a fool**" (v.8); "like a **dog that returns to his vomit is a fool who repeats his folly**" (v.11). Finding: honour on a fool is **as absurd and dangerous as arming a sling with the stone still bound**; and the fool **cannot leave his folly** — he returns to it like a dog to its vomit *(stated)*. Operation: **the fixity of folly** — it is not a passing mistake but a *returning*, a compulsion the fool circles back to *(inferred; folly as compulsive repetition, the un-teachable self at its most fixed)*. *Surfaced:* folly as compulsive return (new); honour absurd on a fool.

**PRO-26-answer-fool · Prov 26:4, 5 · [S, multi] — the discernment of when to engage folly.** "**Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest you be like him**" (v.4); "**answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own eyes**" (v.5). Finding: the paired paradox — **whether to engage folly depends on the moment**: silence to avoid becoming a fool, engagement to puncture his self-conceit *(stated)*. Operation: **the discerning interior that reads which folly needs silence and which needs answer** — no rule fits both; wisdom is knowing which risk (imitation vs his self-conceit) is live *(inferred; a gem on situational discernment — the same act right or wrong by the moment)*. *Surfaced:* situational discernment in engaging folly (new — a gem); the two risks (becoming like him / confirming his conceit).

**PRO-26-meddle-strife · Prov 26:17, 21 · [S, multi] — meddling and the kindling of strife.** "Whoever **meddles in a quarrel not his own** is like one who takes a **passing dog by the ears**" (v.17); "as charcoal to embers… so is a **quarrelsome man for kindling strife**" (v.21). Finding: **meddling in others' quarrels invites needless injury**, and the contentious self **feeds strife** as fuel feeds fire *(stated)*. Operation: **the strife-kindling interior, and the folly of grabbing another's quarrel** — some conflicts the self should not seize; the quarrelsome man is the fuel that keeps them burning *(inferred; the strife-thread)*. *Surfaced:* meddling as self-injury (new); the quarrelsome man as strife's fuel (thread).

**PRO-26-deceit · Prov 26:19, 28 · [S, multi] — the deceiver's "joke" and the flattering, hating mouth.** "So is the man who **deceives his neighbour and says, 'I am only joking!'**" (v.19); "a **lying tongue hates its victims, and a flattering mouth works ruin**" (v.28). Finding: deceit **hides behind 'just joking,'** and beneath the flattering mouth is **hatred** — flattery ruins *(stated)*. Operation: **the malice masked as jest or flattery** — the lying tongue *hates* the very ones it addresses; the smooth mouth is a weapon *(inferred; flattery as concealed hatred, a sharp inner-being diagnosis)*. *Surfaced:* deceit masked as joking (new); flattery as concealed hatred (new).

# Proverbs 27 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 27, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-27-boast-tomorrow · 27:1,2 · [S, multi] — presumption and self-praise.** "**Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring**"; "**let another praise you, and not your own mouth**" (vv.1–2). Finding: the self is to refuse **presumption over the future** and **self-praise** — two forms of over-reaching *(stated; cross-book w/ Ps 30:6 "I said in my prosperity, I shall never be moved")*. *Surfaced:* presumption / self-praise refused (shared w/ Ps 30).

**PRO-27-passions · 27:4 · [S] — the ranking of the passions.** "**Wrath is cruel, anger is overwhelming, but who can stand before jealousy?**" (v.4). Finding: the passions are **weighed against each other** — jealousy the most irresistible *(stated)*. Operation: **a taxonomy of the overwhelming passions** (wrath < anger < jealousy) *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps's fierce affections)*. *Surfaced:* the ranked passions / jealousy strongest (new).

**PRO-27-friend-wounds · 27:5,6,9 · [T, multi] — the honest friend; the gladdened heart.** "**Better is open rebuke than hidden love**. **Faithful are the wounds of a friend**; profuse the kisses of an enemy"; "**oil and perfume make the heart glad**, and the sweetness of a friend comes from his earnest counsel" (vv.5–6,9). Finding: love is **better shown in honest wounding** than in hidden fondness or flattering kisses; and a friend's *earnest counsel* **gladdens the heart** *(stated)*. Operation: **love as honest correction** (the friend's wounds are *faithful*) and **the heart gladdened by true counsel** *(inferred; teachability + the felt heart; cross-book w/ Ps 141:5 "let a righteous man strike me")*. *Hidden:* **love that *wounds faithfully* over love that *hides***. *Surfaced:* the honest-wounding friend (★ cross-book w/ Ps 141:5); the heart gladdened by counsel.

**PRO-27-iron-sharpens · 27:17 · [S] — formation by another.** "**Iron sharpens iron, and one man sharpens another**" (v.17). Finding — a cornerstone: the self is **honed by another self** *(stated)*. Operation: **mutual formation — the self shaped sharper by contact with another** *(inferred; the formation-by-company thread, cross-book w/ 13:20, and the trust-formation law of Ps 115:8)*. *Surfaced:* formation-by-another / iron-sharpens-iron (★ cornerstone — mutual formation).

**PRO-27-heart-mirror · 27:19 · [S] — the heart is the true self.** "**As in water face reflects face, so the heart of man reflects the man**" (v.19). Finding — a cornerstone: the **heart *is* the true self** — what a person really is shows in the heart as a face in water *(stated)*. Operation: **the heart as the mirror/identity of the person** — the deepest Proverbs statement that the self *is* its heart *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 7:9 "the minds and hearts", the heart as the self's core)*. *Surfaced:* the heart as the true self (★ cornerstone — the heart = the person).

**PRO-27-insatiable · 27:20 · [S] — the never-satisfied eye.** "**Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied, and never satisfied are the eyes of man**" (v.20). Finding — a cornerstone: human desire (the *eyes*) is **structurally insatiable**, like the grave *(stated)*. Operation: **the unfillable appetite** — the self's wanting has no natural floor; it is *never satisfied* *(inferred; the shadow-side of the desire thread, cross-book w/ Ps 106:14–15, and the only-God-satisfies datum of Ps 107:9, 145:16)*. *Surfaced:* the insatiable eye/desire (★ cornerstone — the unfillable appetite).

**PRO-27-tested-praise · 27:21 · [S] — a man is tested by his praise.** "The crucible for silver… **and a man is tested by his praise**" (v.21). Finding: how one **handles praise** assays the self — praise is a furnace *(stated)*. *Surfaced:* praise as a test of the self (new).

---
**Chapter notes.** **Cornerstones:** iron-sharpens-iron / formation-by-another (★ 27:17); the heart as the true self (★ 27:19); the insatiable eye (★ 27:20). **New:** the ranked passions; praise-as-test. **Shared:** presumption/self-praise (w/ Ps 30); the honest-wounding friend (w/ Ps 141:5).

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-27-fool-weight · Prov 27:3, 22 · [S, multi] — the weight and fixity of a fool's folly.** "A stone is heavy… but a **fool's provocation is heavier than both**" (v.3); "**crush a fool in a mortar** with a pestle… yet his **folly will not depart** from him" (v.22). Finding: a fool's vexation is a **crushing weight**, and his folly is so **fixed** that even pulverising will not remove it *(stated)*. Operation: **folly as an ineradicable interior set** — not a surface fault correction can grind out, but the grain of the self *(inferred; folly's fixity, w/ 26:11 the returning dog)*. *Surfaced:* the crushing weight of a fool's provocation (new); folly as ineradicable (thread w/ 26:11).

**PRO-27-appetite · Prov 27:7 · [S] — appetite conditioned by fullness and hunger.** "One who is **full loathes honey**, but to one who is **hungry everything bitter is sweet**" (v.7). Finding: **satisfaction and need re-colour the same thing** — honey cloys the full, and bitterness sweetens for the hungry *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior's valuation set by its own state of fullness** — desire is not fixed to the object but to the appetite's condition *(inferred; the never-satisfied thread's mirror — fullness dulls, hunger sweetens, w/ Ecc 6:7)*. *Surfaced:* appetite conditioned by fullness/hunger (new — w/ Ecc 6:7); the state of the self colouring the object.

**PRO-27-strayer-friend · Prov 27:8, 10 · [S, multi] — the strayer, and the near friend.** "Like a **bird that strays from its nest is a man who strays from his home**" (v.8); "**do not forsake your friend**… better is a **neighbour who is near than a brother who is far away**" (v.10). Finding: to wander from one's place is a **displacement** like a bird from its nest; and a **near friend outvalues a distant brother** *(stated)*. Operation: **rootedness and proximate loyalty** — the self belongs somewhere, and the friend who is *near in calamity* is worth more than kin who are far *(inferred; the value of the present friend, w/ 18:24)*. *Surfaced:* the strayer displaced from his place (new); the near friend over the distant brother (w/ 18:24).

**PRO-27-child-glad · Prov 27:11 · [S] — the child's wisdom that gladdens and vindicates.** "Be **wise, my son, and make my heart glad**, that I may answer him who reproaches me" (v.11). Finding: a child's wisdom **gladdens the parent's heart** and even **vindicates** him before critics *(stated)*. Operation: **the child's character as the parent's joy and defence** (the glad pole, w/ 10:1, 23:24) *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* the child's wisdom gladdening and vindicating the parent (thread w/ 10:1).

**PRO-27-prudence-service · Prov 27:12, 18 · [S, multi] — foresight, and faithful service rewarded.** "The **prudent sees danger and hides himself**, but the simple go on and suffer" (v.12); "whoever **tends a fig tree will eat its fruit**, and he who **guards his master will be honoured**" (v.18). Finding: prudence **foresees and takes cover**; faithful tending is **rewarded** — the fruit to the keeper, honour to the guard *(stated)*. Operation: **the anticipating self and the fidelity that reaps** — foresight spares suffering; steady service earns its fruit and honour *(inferred; prudence w/ 22:3; faithful service)*. *Surfaced:* foresight that takes cover (thread w/ 22:3); faithful service rewarded (new).

**PRO-27-praise-contention · Prov 27:14, 16 · [S, multi] — excessive praise as curse; the un-restrainable contentious.** "Whoever **blesses his neighbour with a loud voice, rising early**… will be counted as **cursing**" (v.14); "to **restrain her** [the contentious woman] is to **restrain the wind** or grasp oil in the hand" (v.16). Finding: **over-loud praise curdles into a curse**, and the chronically contentious is **as un-restrainable as the wind** *(stated)*. Operation: **the excess that inverts its intent, and the ungovernable contentious interior** — praise too loud reads as mockery; the quarrelsome cannot be gripped any more than wind or oil *(inferred; the un-restrainable contentious, w/ 21:9,19)*. *Surfaced:* over-loud praise as curse (new); the ungovernable contentious (thread w/ 21:9).

**PRO-27-stewardship · Prov 27:23, 24, 27 · [D, multi] — diligent stewardship against impermanent riches.** "**Know well the condition of your flocks**… for **riches do not last forever**; does a crown endure to all generations?" (vv.23–24); "there will be **enough goats' milk** for your food… and maintenance for your girls" (v.27). Finding: attentive **stewardship** sustains the household, because **riches are impermanent** — the diligent care, not the hoard, provides *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior that tends rather than trusts wealth** — knowing the flock's condition, aware that riches and crowns pass, so care is ongoing *(inferred; diligence over hoarding, w/ the impermanence-of-riches thread, Ecc)*. *Surfaced:* attentive stewardship (new); the impermanence of riches (w/ Ecc).

**PRO-27-surety · Prov 27:13 · [S] — the senseless surety (again).** "**Take a man's garment when he has put up security for a stranger**" (v.13). Finding: standing surety for a stranger is folly to be guarded against *(stated; thread w/ 6:1–5, 17:18, 22:26)*. Operation: the imprudent self-binding *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* the surety-snare (thread w/ 6:1).

# Proverbs 28 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 28, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-28-bold-lion · 28:1 · [S] — the guilty flee, the righteous are bold.** "**The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are bold as a lion**" (v.1). Finding: the inner state of **guilt manufactures pursuers** where none exist, while a clear conscience is **fearless** *(stated)*. Operation: **conscience as the source of dread or boldness** — the wicked's fear is *self-generated* (no one pursues), the righteous's courage is *conscience-born* *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 53:5 "there they are in great terror, where there was no terror", 27:1)*. *Hidden:* **fear conjured by a guilty conscience** (dread with no external cause). *Surfaced:* conscience → dread-or-boldness (★ new — the self-generated fear of guilt).

**PRO-28-confess · 28:13 · [S, multi] — concealment vs confession of sin.** "**Whoever conceals his transgressions will not prosper, but he who confesses and forsakes them will obtain mercy**" (v.13). Finding — a cornerstone: **hiding sin fails; confessing-and-forsaking obtains mercy** *(stated)*. Operation: **confession as the release of the concealed self** — the interior that *hides* its sin stays bound; the one that *owns and forsakes* is freed to mercy *(inferred; the exact Proverbs parallel to Ps 32:3–5 "when I kept silent, my bones wasted… I acknowledged my sin… and you forgave")*. *Surfaced:* confession-vs-concealment (★ cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps 32).

**PRO-28-fear-harden · 28:14 · [S, multi] — fearing always vs the hardened heart.** "**Blessed is the one who fears the LORD always, but whoever hardens his heart will fall into calamity**" (v.14). Finding: continual reverent fear vs the **hardened heart** — the self that *hardens* falls *(stated)*. Operation: **the hardening of the heart as the opposite of the fear of the LORD** *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 95:8 "do not harden your hearts")*. *Hidden:* **the heart-hardening operation** (a self-inflicted callousing). *Surfaced:* the hardened heart vs continual fear (★ new — the hardening operation, cross-book w/ Ps 95).

**PRO-28-trust · 28:25,26 · [T, multi] — trust in the LORD vs greed vs self-reliance.** "A **greedy man stirs up strife, but the one who trusts in the LORD will be enriched**"; "**whoever trusts in his own mind is a fool**, but he who walks in wisdom will be delivered" (vv.25–26). Finding: trust is set against **greed** and against **self-reliance** ("trusts in his own mind") *(stated)*. Operation: **trust as the alternative to grasping and to self-confidence** — the two great rivals to trusting God are *greed* and *the self's own mind* *(inferred; cross-book w/ 3:5 "lean not on your own understanding", Ps 62:8–10)*. *Surfaced:* trust vs greed vs self-reliance (shared, sharpened w/ 3:5).

---
**Chapter notes.** **Cornerstones:** confession-vs-concealment (★ 28:13, w/ Ps 32); the hardened heart (★ 28:14, w/ Ps 95). **New:** conscience→dread-or-boldness (28:1). **Shared:** trust vs greed/self-reliance (w/ 3:5, Ps 62).

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-28-rule-public · Prov 28:2, 12, 28 · [D, multi] — the public weather of righteous vs wicked ascendancy.** "When a land transgresses, it has **many rulers**, but with a **man of understanding… stability** continues" (v.2); "when the **righteous triumph, great glory**, but when the wicked rise, **people hide themselves**" (vv.12,28). Finding: the ascendancy of righteousness or wickedness **changes the public atmosphere** — glory and stability, or a people in hiding *(stated)*. Operation: **the collective interior shaped by who rules** — the same people flourish or hide depending on the moral character in power *(inferred; the corporate mood, w/ 29:2)*. *Surfaced:* the public atmosphere set by righteous/wicked rule (thread w/ 29:2).

**PRO-28-law-ear · Prov 28:4, 7, 9 · [D, multi] — the law and the hearing (or turned-away) ear.** "Those who **forsake the law praise the wicked**, but those who keep it strive against them" (v.4); "the one who **keeps the law is a son with understanding**" (v.7); "if one **turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer is an abomination**" (v.9). Finding: keeping the law forms an understanding self; **turning the ear from it corrupts even prayer** *(stated)*. Operation: **the ear's orientation determining the whole interior** — refuse to hear instruction, and even worship sours; the receptive ear is the root of understanding *(inferred; the hearing ear, w/ the teachability thread; unheard-law makes prayer abomination — a striking link of receptivity and worship)*. *Surfaced:* the turned-away ear corrupting even prayer (new); law-keeping as understanding.

**PRO-28-seek-understand · Prov 28:5 · [S] — seeking the LORD as the key to understanding justice.** "**Evil men do not understand justice, but those who seek the LORD understand it completely**" (v.5). Finding: moral understanding is **unlocked by seeking God** — the evil are blind to justice; the God-seeker sees it fully *(stated)*. Operation: **the God-ward orientation that opens moral perception** (w/ the fear-of-the-LORD-as-wisdom thread, Job 28:28) *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* seeking-God as the key to understanding justice (w/ Job 28:28).

**PRO-28-integrity-way · Prov 28:6, 10, 18 · [D, multi] — the two ways; the pit-digger.** "**Better a poor man who walks in his integrity** than a rich man crooked in his ways" (v.6); "whoever **misleads the upright into an evil way will fall into his own pit**" (v.10); "whoever **walks in integrity will be delivered**, but he who is crooked will **suddenly fall**" (v.18). Finding: **integrity delivers and outranks crooked wealth**; the one who lays a trap for the upright **falls into it himself** *(stated)*. Operation: **the self-recoiling crooked way** — the pit dug for another swallows the digger; the straight walk is preserved *(inferred; the pit-digger, w/ Ps 7:15; integrity over status, w/ 19:1)*. *Surfaced:* the pit-digger self-trapped (w/ Ps 7:15); integrity delivering (thread).

**PRO-28-wealth-greed · Prov 28:8, 11, 19, 20, 22, 27 · [D, multi] — wealth, self-conceit, greed, and generosity.** "Whoever **multiplies wealth by interest… gathers it for him who is generous to the poor**" (v.8); "a **rich man is wise in his own eyes**, but a poor man of understanding **finds him out**" (v.11); "**works his land → plenty of bread**; follows worthless pursuits → poverty" (v.19); "a **faithful man abounds with blessings**, but whoever **hastens to be rich** will not go unpunished" (v.20); "a **stingy man hastens after wealth** and does not know that poverty will come" (v.22); "whoever **gives to the poor will not want**, but he who **hides his eyes** gets many a curse" (v.27). Finding: **greedy haste for wealth self-defeats** (unpunished it is not, and poverty overtakes it), the rich are **self-deceived**, and **generosity to the poor** is the blessed path *(stated)*. Operation: **the grasping vs the open interior** — the hastening, stingy, self-conceited self toward poverty and curse; the faithful, generous, land-working self toward plenty and blessing *(inferred; the never-satisfied greed, w/ Ecc 5:10; generosity as un-wanting, w/ 11:24)*. *Surfaced:* greedy haste self-defeating (w/ Ecc 5:10); the rich self-deceived; generosity as the un-wanting path.

**PRO-28-oppressor · Prov 28:15, 16 · [S, multi] — the oppressive ruler.** "Like a **roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a poor people**" (v.15); "a **ruler who lacks understanding is a cruel oppressor**, but he who **hates unjust gain will prolong his days**" (v.16). Finding: the understanding-lacking ruler becomes a **predatory oppressor**; the one who **hates unjust gain** endures *(stated)*. Operation: **power without understanding turning predatory** — the interior that hates ill-gotten gain is what makes rule bearable and lasting *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* the predatory ruler (new); hating unjust gain as what preserves.

**PRO-28-guilt-theft · Prov 28:17, 21, 24 · [D, multi] — guilt's flight, cheap corruption, the self-justified thief.** "One **burdened with the blood of another** will be a **fugitive until death**" (v.17); "to show **partiality is not good**, but for a **piece of bread a man will do wrong**" (v.21); "whoever **robs his father or mother and says, 'That is no transgression,'** is a companion to a destroyer" (v.24). Finding: bloodguilt makes a lifelong **fugitive**; corruption comes **cheap** (a piece of bread); and the thief who **denies his sin** is kin to a destroyer *(stated)*. Operation: **the fleeing conscience, and the self that renames its theft as innocence** — guilt cannot rest; the self-justified robber calls his sin "no transgression" *(inferred; guilt's flight, w/ Gen 4:12; self-justified sin, the un-owned wrong)*. *Surfaced:* guilt's lifelong flight (w/ Gen 4:12); corruption bought cheap; the self-justified thief (new).

**PRO-28-rebuke · Prov 28:23 · [S] — honest rebuke over flattery.** "Whoever **rebukes a man will afterward find more favour** than he who **flatters** with his tongue" (v.23). Finding: **honest rebuke earns deeper favour** than flattery — the truth-teller is finally more loved than the flatterer *(stated)*. Operation: **the reproof that is valued over time** (w/ 27:5–6 "faithful are the wounds of a friend") *(inferred)*. *Surfaced:* honest rebuke outlasting flattery (thread w/ 27:5).

# Proverbs 29 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 29, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-29-stiff-neck · 29:1 · [S] — the hardened, unteachable self broken.** "**He who is often reproved, yet stiffens his neck, will suddenly be broken beyond healing**" (v.1). Finding: repeated reproof *refused* — the **stiffened neck** — ends in sudden, unhealable breaking *(stated)*. Operation: **the un-teachable self hardening past repair** — each refused reproof calcifies until nothing can bend it *(inferred; the terminal form of the closed heart, cross-book w/ Ps 95:8, and the teachability thread)*. *Surfaced:* the hardened/unteachable self (★ shared — the terminal closed heart).

**PRO-29-vent-spirit · 29:11 · [S] — venting vs holding back the spirit.** "**A fool gives full vent to his spirit, but a wise man quietly holds it back**" (v.11). Finding — a cornerstone: the fool **discharges** his whole spirit; the wise **restrains** it *(stated)*. Operation: **self-restraint as the holding-back of the spirit** — the mastered self does not spill its every impulse; it *quietly holds it back* *(inferred; the self-mastery thread, cross-book w/ 16:32, 25:28, and the Psalter's self-quieting, Ps 62:1, 131:2)*. *Surfaced:* self-restraint / holding-back-the-spirit (★ cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps 131).

**PRO-29-pride-lowly · 29:23 · [S, multi] — pride brings low; the lowly are lifted.** "**One's pride will bring him low, but he who is lowly in spirit will obtain honour**" (v.23). Finding: pride **lowers**, lowliness **lifts** — the inversion *(stated; pride/humility cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps 138:6, 18:27)*. *Surfaced:* pride/humility (★ shared cornerstone).

**PRO-29-fear-man · 29:25 · [S, multi] — the fear of man vs trust in the LORD.** "**The fear of man lays a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is safe**" (v.25). Finding — a cornerstone: **fear of man is a *snare*** to the self; trust in the LORD is safety *(stated)*. Operation: **the fear of man as an inner trap, dissolved by trust** — the dread of people *ensnares* the self, and only Godward trust frees it *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 56:11, 118:6 "the LORD is on my side; I will not fear. What can man do to me?")*. *Surfaced:* fear-of-man-vs-trust (★ cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps 56/118).

**PRO-29-anger · 29:22 · [S] — the wrathful stir strife.** "**A man of wrath stirs up strife, and one given to anger causes much transgression**" (v.22). *Surfaced:* anger (shared thread).

---
**Chapter notes.** **Cornerstones:** self-restraint/holding-back-the-spirit (★ 29:11, w/ Ps 131); fear-of-man-vs-trust (★ 29:25, w/ Ps 56/118). **Shared:** pride/humility (★); the hardened/unteachable self; anger.

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-29-rule-public · Prov 29:2, 4, 14, 16 · [D, multi] — just rule and the people's mood.** "When the **righteous increase, the people rejoice**, but when the **wicked rule, the people groan**" (v.2); "by **justice a king builds up the land**" (v.4); "if a **king faithfully judges the poor, his throne** will be established forever" (v.14); "when the wicked increase, transgression increases, but the **righteous will look upon their downfall**" (v.16). Finding: righteousness in power **makes a people rejoice and a throne endure**; wickedness makes them **groan** *(stated)*. Operation: **the corporate interior rising or sinking with the justice of its rulers** — the king who judges the poor faithfully secures his throne *(inferred; the public mood, w/ 28:12,28)*. *Surfaced:* the people's joy/groaning under just/unjust rule (thread w/ 28:12); faithful judgment of the poor as what establishes.

**PRO-29-snare-song · Prov 29:6, 27 · [S, multi] — the snare and the song; the mutual abomination of the two ways.** "An **evil man is ensnared in his transgression, but a righteous man sings and rejoices**" (v.6); "an **unjust man is an abomination to the righteous, but one whose way is straight is an abomination to the wicked**" (v.27). Finding: the two ways issue in **a snare and a song** — the evil trapped in his own sin, the righteous free enough to *sing* — and each way is **abhorrent to the other** *(stated)*. Operation: **the self ensnared by its own transgression vs the self at liberty to rejoice** — sin is a net that closes on its doer; righteousness opens into song *(inferred; sin as self-snaring, w/ 5:22; the incompatible interiors)*. *Surfaced:* the snare of one's own sin vs the freed song (new gem — w/ 5:22); the mutual abomination of the two ways.

**PRO-29-child-discipline · Prov 29:3, 15, 17, 19 · [D, multi] — the child, the rod, and what mere words cannot do.** "He who **loves wisdom makes his father glad**, but a companion of prostitutes squanders" (v.3); "the **rod and reproof give wisdom**, but a child left to himself shames his mother" (v.15); "**discipline your son, and he will give you rest**… delight to your heart" (v.17); "by **mere words a servant is not disciplined**, for though he understands, he will not respond" (v.19). Finding: **loving wisdom gladdens; discipline gives wisdom and rest**; and some are not moved by words alone *(stated)*. Operation: **formation through loving correction, and the limit of words** — the child left to himself drifts to shame; discipline returns *rest and delight*; but understanding without will does not respond *(inferred; discipline-as-rest, w/ 19:18; the gap between understanding and responding)*. *Surfaced:* discipline yielding rest and delight (new); the will that words alone cannot move.

**PRO-29-poor-justice · Prov 29:7, 26 · [S, multi] — the righteous knowing the poor's cause; justice from the LORD.** "A **righteous man knows the rights of the poor**; a wicked man does not understand such knowledge" (v.7); "**many seek the face of a ruler, but it is from the LORD** that a man gets justice" (v.26). Finding: righteousness includes **knowing the poor's cause** (which the wicked cannot grasp), and true justice comes **from God**, not the ruler's favour *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior attuned to the poor, and the eye that looks past power to God for justice** *(inferred; the poor's cause, w/ 28:5; justice from the LORD)*. *Surfaced:* knowing the poor's rights as righteousness (thread w/ 28:5); justice from God over the ruler's face.

**PRO-29-inflaming-speech · Prov 29:8, 9, 20 · [D, multi] — the inflaming scoffer, the raging fool, the hasty tongue.** "**Scoffers set a city aflame, but the wise turn away wrath**" (v.8); "if a wise man argues with a fool, the **fool only rages and laughs, and there is no quiet**" (v.9); "do you see a man **hasty in his words**? There is **more hope for a fool** than for him" (v.20). Finding: scoffers **inflame**, the wise **defuse**; arguing with a fool yields **no quiet**; and the **hasty tongue** is worse than folly *(stated)*. Operation: **speech that ignites vs speech that cools; the futility of reasoning with rage** — the scoffer is a fire-setter, the fool un-quietable, the hasty-worded beyond hope *(inferred; the peacemaker vs the inflamer, w/ 15:1; hasty speech, w/ Ecc 5:2)*. *Surfaced:* the scoffer as fire-setter / the wise as wrath-turner (new); the futility of arguing with a raging fool; the hasty tongue below folly.

**PRO-29-hatred-complicity · Prov 29:10, 12, 24 · [S, multi] — hatred of the blameless; complicity from the top and bottom.** "**Bloodthirsty men hate one who is blameless** and seek the life of the upright" (v.10); "if a **ruler listens to falsehood, all his officials will be wicked**" (v.12); "the **partner of a thief hates his own life**; he hears the curse but discloses nothing" (v.24). Finding: the violent **hate the blameless**; a ruler's ear for lies **corrupts his whole court**; and the thief's silent partner **hates his own life** *(stated)*. Operation: **corruption spread from the ruler's ear down, and complicity as self-hatred** — heeding falsehood makes wicked officials; the accomplice who will not disclose destroys himself *(inferred; the ruler's ear shaping the court; complicity as self-harm)*. *Surfaced:* the ruler's ear corrupting the court (new); complicity as self-hatred; hatred of the blameless.

**PRO-29-restraint · Prov 29:18 · [S] — vision and the restraint it gives.** "Where there is **no prophetic vision the people cast off restraint**, but blessed is he who **keeps the law**" (v.18). Finding: without revelatory **vision the people run unrestrained**; the law-keeper is blessed *(stated)*. Operation: **restraint as a gift of vision/law** — the interior needs a revealed word to hold it in bounds; without it, it unravels *(inferred; the restraining word, w/ the law-ear thread 28:9)*. *Surfaced:* vision/law as what restrains the self (thread w/ 28:9).

# Proverbs 30 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 30 (Agur), per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-30-humility · 30:1–4 · [D, multi] — the seeker's self-emptying before the unknowable God.** "I am **weary**, O God… **Surely I am too stupid to be a man**. I have **not the understanding of a man**. I have **not learned wisdom**, nor have knowledge of the Holy One… **Who has ascended to heaven?**" (vv.1–4). Finding — a cornerstone: the wisdom-seeker begins in **exhausted self-emptying** — confessing his own stupidity before the God he cannot comprehend *(stated)*. Operation: **intellectual humility as the floor of wisdom** — the truest sage *unknows* himself before God's unsearchable greatness; the confession of ignorance *is* the beginning of insight *(inferred; the deepest form of the fear-of-the-LORD-as-beginning; cross-book w/ Ps 73:22 "I was brutish and ignorant… like a beast toward you", 131:1)*. *Surfaced:* intellectual humility / self-emptying before God (★ cornerstone — the sage's un-knowing).

**PRO-30-middle · 30:7–9 · [D, multi] — the prayer for the middle; self-knowledge of the heart's dangers.** "**Give me neither poverty nor riches**; feed me with the food that is needful, **lest I be full and deny you** and say, 'Who is the LORD?' **or lest I be poor and steal** and profane the name of my God" (vv.8–9). Finding — a cornerstone: the self prays for the *mean* out of a sober **knowledge of its own heart** — knowing that *fullness* tempts to *forget God* and *want* tempts to *steal* *(stated)*. Operation: **self-knowledge as the ground of a prayer for limits** — the inner being, aware that *both excess and lack* imperil its fidelity, asks God to guard it from *its own* likely failures *(inferred; a rare, honest self-diagnosis; cross-book w/ Ps 19:13 "keep back your servant from presumptuous sins", 131:1–2's contentment)*. *Hidden:* **the two opposite dangers to fidelity** (fullness→forgetting, want→theft) — a mapped self-knowledge. *Surfaced:* self-knowledge / the prayer-for-the-middle (★ cornerstone — contentment grounded in self-diagnosis).

**PRO-30-self-clean · 30:12,13 · [S, multi] — clean in one's own eyes.** "There are those who are **clean in their own eyes but are not washed of their filth**… how **lofty are their eyes**" (vv.12–13). *Surfaced:* self-deception + pride (shared w/ 20:9, 16:2).

**PRO-30-insatiable · 30:15,16,20 · [S, multi] — the never-satisfied; the seared conscience.** "The **leech has two daughters: Give and Give**. Three things are **never satisfied**… the adulteress **eats and wipes her mouth and says, 'I have done no wrong'**" (vv.15–16,20). Finding: the **insatiable** appetite (never says "Enough"), and the **seared conscience** that feels no guilt after wrong *(stated)*. Operation: **the unfillable want + the conscience that registers no sin** *(inferred; the insatiable-eye thread of 27:20, and the numbed conscience; cross-book w/ the hardened heart, Ps 36:1–2)*. *Hidden:* **the seared conscience** ("I have done no wrong" — no inner registration of guilt). *Surfaced:* the insatiable (shared w/ 27:20); the seared conscience (★ new — guilt un-registered).

**PRO-30-restraint · 30:32,33 · [S] — checking the self before it spills.** "If you have been **foolish, exalting yourself**… **put your hand on your mouth**. For… **pressing anger produces strife**" (vv.32–33). *Surfaced:* self-restraint (shared w/ 29:11).

---
**Chapter notes.** **Cornerstones:** intellectual humility / self-emptying (★ 30:1–4); the prayer-for-the-middle / self-knowledge (★ 30:7–9). **New:** the seared conscience (30:20). **Shared:** self-deception/pride; the insatiable; self-restraint.

---

## Catch-up units (2026-07-04) — loose study-term verses bound to units

**PRO-30-refuge · Prov 30:5 · [S] — God's word proven, a shield to those who take refuge.** "**Every word of God proves true; he is a shield to those who take refuge in him**" (v.5). Finding: God's word is **tested and true**, and he is a **shield** to the one who **takes refuge** in him *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior that shelters in the tried word of God** — refuge-taking as the trusting movement toward a proven shield *(inferred; take-refuge/shield, cross-book w/ Ps 18:30 which this quotes, Ps 2:12)*. *Surfaced:* taking refuge in the proven word (thread w/ Ps 18:30 — the trust/refuge cluster).

**PRO-30-parent-honour · Prov 30:10, 11, 17 · [D, multi] — the dishonoured parent and the mocking eye.** "Do **not slander a servant** to his master" (v.10); "there are those who **curse their fathers and do not bless their mothers**" (v.11); "the **eye that mocks a father and scorns to obey a mother** will be picked out by the ravens" (v.17). Finding: **contempt for parents** — cursing, refusing blessing, the **mocking eye** — is marked for a dishonourable end *(stated)*. Operation: **the scorn legible in the eye, and the dishonouring interior** — the mocking eye betrays a heart that scorns its origin, and meets a fitting ruin *(inferred; the contemptuous eye, w/ 6:17 haughty eyes; dishonour of parents inverting the honour-thread)*. *Surfaced:* the mocking eye that scorns a parent (new — w/ 6:17); the dishonoured parent (inverting the honour thread).

**PRO-30-wonder · Prov 30:18, 19, 21, 23 · [D, multi] — wonder at the unsearchable, and the destabilising reversals.** "**Three things are too wonderful for me; four I do not understand**: the way of an eagle… a serpent… a ship… and the **way of a man with a virgin**" (vv.18–19); "under three things the earth **trembles**… an **unloved woman when she gets a husband**, and a **maidservant who displaces her mistress**" (vv.21,23). Finding: some things exceed understanding — the mysterious **way of love** among them — and certain **reversals unsettle the world** (the long-unloved suddenly powerful, the servant supplanting the mistress) *(stated)*. Operation: **the interior that owns the limits of its understanding, and reads which reversals destabilise** — wonder ("too wonderful… I do not understand") as an honest posture; the note on reversals that the human order cannot bear *(inferred; owned not-knowing, w/ Job 42:3, Ecc 3:11; the way of a man and a maid as the unsearchable inner mystery of love)*. *Surfaced:* owned wonder at the unsearchable (w/ Job 42:3); the way of love as too-wonderful; the destabilising reversal.

**PRO-30-small-wise · Prov 30:24, 25, 26, 29 · [D, multi] — the wisdom of the small.** "**Four things on earth are small, but they are exceedingly wise**": the **ants**, "a people not strong, yet they **provide their food in summer**"; the **rock badgers**, "not mighty, yet they **make their homes in the cliffs**" (vv.24–26); and "**three things are stately in their tread**" (v.29). Finding: **wisdom is not a function of strength** — the small creatures are "exceedingly wise" in *provision* (the ant's foresight) and *security* (the badger's cliff-home) *(stated)*. Operation: **prudent foresight and shelter-seeking as wisdom available to the weak** — strength is not required; the ant stores against winter, the badger builds beyond reach *(inferred; the ant's foresight, w/ 6:6–8; wisdom in the small, not the mighty)*. *Surfaced:* wisdom-in-the-small (foresight and security without strength, w/ 6:6); provision-in-season / shelter-in-the-cliff as the weak's wisdom.

# Psalm 32 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 32:1–11 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, with the God-relation as its arena (memory `feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The anatomy of confession as an inner-being process.** Psalm 32 maps a **mechanism**: how *concealed* guilt actively corrodes the inner being (silence → somatic wasting, vv.3–4), and how the *operation of uncovering* reverses it (acknowledgment → release, v.5). Its signature move: **you must uncover what you want covered** — self-concealment is the block. Around this runs a second operation: the mode by which an inner being can be guided (by understanding, or only by force) depends on its own **understanding** (vv.8–9).

## The reading

**I. The blessed state: an inner being without cover to keep (vv.1–2).**
"Blessed is the one whose transgression is **forgiven**, whose sin is **covered** (H3680)… in whose **spirit** (H7307, the seat) there is **no deceit** (H7423, M14, *remiyah*)" (vv.1–2). The state named at the outset is defined *inwardly*: a spirit with **no guile / self-deception** *(stated)*. The operation to watch is already implied — the blessed inner being is one that has **stopped concealing** (there is nothing left to hide, "no deceit in the spirit") *(inferred: the beatitude pairs "sin covered" with "no deceit in the spirit" — the outward pardon and the inward transparency go together)*.

**II. The mechanism of concealment — silence corrodes the inner being (vv.3–4).**
"For when I **kept silent** (H2790, M33), my bones **wasted away** (H1086) through my **groaning** (H7581, M42) all day long. For day and night your hand was **heavy** (H3513) upon me; my strength was **dried up**" (vv.3–4). The core discovery, stated as a *process*: **concealed guilt is not inert — it actively consumes the inner being.** The refusal to confess ("kept silent") produces a chain of interior effects — bones wasting, ceaseless groaning, strength dried up *(stated)*. **The inner being cannot hold unacknowledged guilt without being eroded by it**; silence is an inner act with a somatic output *(inferred: the "for" makes the wasting the consequence of the silence)*. The "heavy hand" is the pressure the concealment generates from within, felt as from God *(inferred)*.

**III. The reversal — uncover to be covered (v.5).**
"I **acknowledged** (H3045) my sin to you, and I did **not cover** (H3680) my iniquity; I said, 'I will **confess** (H3034, M22) my transgressions'… and you forgave" (v.5). The reversing operation: the inner being **stops covering and names the sin** — and the wasting stops *(stated)*. Note the exact mechanism in the verb: the sin that is "**covered**" in v.1 (by God) is what the psalmist would **not "cover"** in v.5 (himself) — **the inner being must *un*cover what it wants God to cover.** Self-concealment is precisely the block to being covered; acknowledgment removes it *(inferred: the same root *kasah* is refused by the self in v.5 and granted by God in v.1)*. The operation is **human uncovering → divine covering → release**.

**IV. The environment inverts — from heavy hand to encircling deliverance (vv.6–7, 10).**
What *surrounds* the inner being changes with the operation. Under concealment, "your hand was **heavy** upon me" (v.4); after acknowledgment, "you **surround** (H5437) me with shouts of **deliverance** (H7438, M42)" (v.7), and "**steadfast love** (H2617, M05) **surrounds** the one who **trusts** (H0982, M19)" (v.10). The inner being's **encompassing environment flips** — from being *pressed by a heavy weight* (guilt) to being *encircled by deliverance and chesed* (release) *(stated: heavy hand → surrounded by deliverance/steadfast love)*. What surrounds the self is a function of whether it conceals or trusts *(inferred)*.

**V. The mode of guidance depends on the inner being's understanding (vv.8–9).**
"I will **instruct** (H7919, M15) you… I will **counsel** (H3289, M15) you with my eye upon you. Be not like a **horse** or a **mule**, without **understanding** (H0995, M15), which must be **curbed with bit and bridle**" (vv.8–9). A second operation, in contrast form: an inner being *with understanding* can be guided **relationally — by counsel, by an eye upon it**; an inner being *without understanding* can only be moved **by force — bit and bridle** *(stated)*. The gem: **the mode by which the inner being is led is keyed to its own capacity to understand** — the teachable are guided by counsel, the brutish only by compulsion *(inferred: the "be not like" sets understanding-led guidance against force-led control)*. To have understanding is to be led *without* the bridle.

**VI. The two inner climates (vv.10–11).**
"**Many** are the **sorrows** (H4341, M03) of the wicked, but steadfast love surrounds the one who trusts… Be **glad** (H8055, M04)… **rejoice** (H1523, M04), O righteous, and **shout for joy** (H7442, M42), all you **upright in heart** (H3820, the seat — M47)" (vv.10–11). The end-state of the confessed/trusting inner being is **gladness located in the heart** ("upright in heart"), set against the "many sorrows" that attend the concealing/wicked self *(stated)*. The two operations (conceal vs uncover-and-trust) issue in two interior climates — sorrow-ridden or glad-hearted *(inferred)*.

## What Psalm 32 says about the inner being
- **Concealed guilt actively corrodes the inner being (vv.3–4).** Silence is not neutral — the unacknowledged sin wastes the bones, drives ceaseless groaning, dries up strength. The self cannot hold unconfessed guilt without erosion.
- **The releasing operation is *uncovering* (v.5).** Acknowledgment reverses the corrosion — and the mechanism is exact: the inner being must *un*cover what it wants God to cover. Self-concealment is the block to being covered.
- **Transparency is the blessed inner state (v.2).** "No deceit in the spirit" — an inner being with nothing left to hide is the one at rest; outward pardon and inward transparency go together.
- **What surrounds the inner being flips with the operation (vv.4, 7, 10).** Concealment → a heavy weight pressing; acknowledgment/trust → being encircled by deliverance and steadfast love. The self's environment tracks its inner act.
- **The mode of guidance is keyed to understanding (vv.8–9).** An understanding inner being is led relationally (counsel, an eye upon it); a brutish one only by force (bit and bridle). Understanding is what makes guidance possible without compulsion.
- **The two operations issue in two inner climates (vv.10–11).** Concealment breeds "many sorrows"; the uncovered, trusting self is glad *in the heart*.

## Honest notes
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at vv.2, 5, 6, 9 — negation/petition, not prohibition; bearer=LORD bleed pervasive; intensity *all/many*) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **The *kasah* ("cover", H3680) wordplay (vv.1, 5)** is the psalm's hinge — the same verb refused by the self and granted by God; the two occurrences are correctly the same lemma, read here as the operation's mechanism.
- **"silent" (H2790, M33, v.3)** is tagged in the peace/stillness cluster but here is the *guilty* silence of non-confession — a per-occurrence sense (negative), distinct from restful stillness. Sanity note.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *transgression/sin/iniquity* (H6588/H2401/H2403/H5771, M10, vv.1,2,5); *deceit* (H7423, M14, v.2 — the spirit); *silent* (H2790, M33, v.3); *groaning/shouts* (H7581/H7438, M42, vv.3,7); *counts* (H2803, M15, v.2); *confess* (H3034, M22, v.5); *godly* (H2623, M05, v.6); *instruct/counsel/understanding* (H7919/H3289/H0995, M15, vv.8,9); *sorrows* (H4341, M03, v.10); *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05, v.10); *trusts* (H0982, M19, v.10); *glad/rejoice/joy* (H8055/H1523/H7442, M04/M42, v.11); *upright/heart* (H3477/H3820, M13/M47, v.11).

# Psalm 33 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 33:1–22 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (vv.13–14 backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **A praise hymn — honestly scoped.** Much of it (the word, creation, God's counsel, the all-seeing eye, vv.4–14) is about God; that is the **arena**. The genuine inner-being findings cluster at the human end and share one through-line: **where the inner being *locates* its confidence, and what that produces.** Three operations: the heart as a **fashioned, observed** thing (v.15); **misplaced confidence** as a "false hope" in external strength (vv.16–17); and the **mechanism of gladness** — a soul that *waits* and a heart made *glad because it trusts* the name (vv.20–22).

## The reading

**I. The heart is a *fashioned*, legible thing (vv.13–15).**
Out of the seeing-God arena (vv.13–14, "he sees all the children of man") comes a specific inner-being disclosure: "he who **fashions** (H3320-family, *yatsar* — forms as a potter) the **hearts** (H3820, the seat — M47) of them all and **observes** (H0995, M15, *bin* — discerns) all their deeds" (v.15). The operation: the inner being (the heart) is **not self-made — it is *formed*, and formed *individually* ("of them all")**, by a Fashioner who then **reads what he shaped** *(stated: he fashions the hearts and observes)*. Two facts about the inner being at once — its **origin** (made, not self-originating) and its **transparency** (legible to its Maker) *(inferred)*.

**II. Misplaced confidence — the "false hope" in external strength (vv.16–17).**
"The king is **not saved** by his great **army** (H2428, M23); a warrior is **not delivered** by his great **strength** (H3581, M23). The war **horse** is a **false hope** (H8267, M14, *sheqer* — a *lie*) for salvation; by its great **might** (H2428, M23) it cannot rescue" (vv.16–17). The operation mapped here is the inner being's **temptation to locate its security in the tangible** — army, strength, horse — and the verdict is that this confidence is **founded on a lie** (*sheqer*) *(stated: the horse is a false hope)*. The finding is not about horses but about **the placement of hope**: confidence resting on visible power is confidence resting on a falsehood *(inferred; cf. the chariots-vs-name of Ps 20:7)*.

**III. The inner posture that meets the gaze (v.18).**
"Behold, the **eye of the LORD** is on those who **fear** (H3373, M01) him, on those who **hope** (H3176, M18, *yachal*) in his **steadfast love** (H2617, M05)" (v.18). Against the general seeing of vv.13–15, this narrows: the eye **rests on** a particular inner posture — **fear paired with hope-in-chesed** *(stated)*. The finding is the **correlation**: the inner being's disposition (fearing, hoping in steadfast love) is what the sustaining gaze settles on — the self's posture and the divine attention meet *(inferred: the eye is "on those who… hope")*.

**IV. The mechanism of gladness — relocated confidence (vv.20–22).**
The response gathers the whole into a compact inner sequence: "Our **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47) **waits** (H2442, M18, *chakah*) for the LORD… For our **heart** (H3820, the seat — M47) is **glad** (H8055, M04) in him, **because** we **trust** (H0982, M19) in his holy **name**… even as we **hope** (H3176, M18) in you" (vv.20–22). The operation, stated with its causal joint: **the heart is glad *because* it trusts** — gladness is not primary but **produced by trust in the name** *(stated: "our heart is glad… because we trust")*. And the object of that trust is the **name** (God's revealed character), **not the might** that vv.16–17 called a lie — so the inner being has **relocated its confidence** from external strength to the name, and *that relocation* is what yields gladness *(inferred: the same faculty that vv.16–17 warned against misplacing is here rightly placed on the name)*. Two seats work in concert — the **soul waits** (posture toward the future), the **heart is glad** (present state) — held by trust and sustained by hope *(inferred)*.

## What Psalm 33 says about the inner being
- **The heart is a *fashioned*, legible thing (v.15).** The inner being is *formed* — individually shaped by a Maker who then reads it. Its origin is not itself, and it is fully transparent to the one who made it.
- **Confidence misplaced in external strength is a *lie* (vv.16–17).** The operation the psalm exposes is *where the inner being locates security*; resting it on visible power (army, strength, horse) is a "false hope" — founded on a falsehood.
- **A particular inner posture meets the sustaining gaze (v.18).** Fear paired with hope-in-steadfast-love is what the eye of the LORD rests on — the self's disposition and the divine attention correlate.
- **Gladness is *produced* by relocated trust (vv.20–22).** The mechanism is explicit: the heart is glad *because* it trusts — and it trusts the *name*, not the might it was tempted to lean on. Confidence moved from strength to the name is what yields gladness; soul (waiting) and heart (glad) operate together.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** vv.4–14 (word, creation, God's counsel that stands, the all-seeing eye) are the God-ward arena; read as the setting that frames the human operations (vv.15–22), not mined for inner content they do not carry.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at vv.16–17 — the "not saved / not delivered" negations that *make the point*; bearer=LORD bleed; intensity *all/great*) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Two wait/hope words:** *chakah* (H2442, waits, v.20) and *yachal* (H3176, hope, vv.18,22), both M18 — the inner being's forward-postures; consistent with the *qavah*/*yachal* waiting thread (Ps 25, 27, 31).
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *fear/awe* (H3372/H1481, M01, v.8); *counsel* (H6098, M17, vv.10,11); *plans* (H4284, M14, vv.10,11 — God's); *hearts* (H3820, M47, vv.11,15,21); *observes* (H0995, M15, v.15); *army/strength/might* (H2428/H3581, M23, vv.16,17 — the false hope); *false-hope* (H8267, M14, v.17); *fear/hope* (H3373/H3176, M01/M18, v.18); *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05, vv.5,18,22); *soul* (H5315, M47, vv.19,20); *waits* (H2442, M18, v.20); *glad* (H8055, M04, v.21); *trust* (H0982, M19, v.21).

# Psalm 34 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 34:1–22 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **An acrostic** — a circling gathering (not a linear argument). Its inner-being findings cluster around two kinds of operation: **experiential knowing** (the inner being verifies God's goodness by *tasting*, and its very *looking* re-forms the face), and **responsive transformation** (seeking dissolves fear; the *shattered* inner being is the locus of nearness). Plus the self-governance of speech and the desire that drives a learnable fear.

## The reading

**I. The soul's boasting-faculty, redirected (vv.1–3).**
"My **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47) makes its **boast** (H1984, M08, *halal*) in the LORD; let the **humble** (H6035, M24) hear and be **glad** (H8055, M04)" (v.2). The operation: the inner being's **boasting/glorying faculty** — the very capacity that is *pride* when aimed at the self (M08) — is **redirected onto the LORD** *(inferred: halal sits in the pride cluster but its object here is the LORD, not the self)*. And the redirection has a **social output**: the soul's boasting *gladdens the humble* who hear it — one inner being's rightly-aimed glorying feeds another's gladness *(stated)*.

**II. Seeking dissolves the inner being's fears (v.4).**
"I **sought** (H1875, M41, *darash*) the LORD, and he answered me and delivered me from all my **fears** (H4034, M01, *megurah*)" (v.4). The operation is a resolution: the *seeking* act meets an answer that **dissolves the inner dread itself** — not merely the external danger but "my *fears*," the interior state *(stated)*. Seeking is the inner being's move that discharges its own fear *(inferred: the object delivered-from is the internal *megurah*)*.

**III. Looking re-forms the face (v.5).**
"Those who **look** to him are **radiant** (H5102, *nahar* — shine), and their **faces** shall never be **ashamed** (H2659, M07)" (v.5). A striking operation: the inner being's *direction of attention* produces a **visible facial change** — those who *look* toward God become **radiant**, their faces un-shamed *(stated)*. The gaze is not passive; **it lights the countenance** — the inner orientation is legible on the face, and looking outward-and-upward is what removes shame from it *(inferred: radiance and no-shame follow from the looking)*.

**IV. Tasting — the inner being knows by participation (v.8).**
"Oh, **taste** (H2938, M15, *ta'am*) and **see** that the LORD is **good** (H2896, M04)!" (v.8). The gem-operation: the inner being verifies God's goodness **not by abstract report but by *tasting*** — a first-hand, participatory knowing *(stated: taste *and* see)*. Knowing-by-tasting precedes and grounds knowing-about; the inner being is invited to **test the claim on its own palate** *(inferred: ta'am makes the knowing sensory/experiential, and it is paired with — and precedes — "see")*.

**V. The learnable fear, driven by the inner being's own desire (vv.9–12).**
"those who **fear** (H3373, M01) him have **no lack**… those who **seek** (H1875, M41) the LORD lack no good thing" (vv.9–10). The fearing/seeking inner being's state is **fullness** (no lack), set against the *want and hunger* of the young lions who trust their own strength *(stated)*. Then: "Come, O children… I will **teach** you the **fear** (H3374, M01) of the LORD. What man **desires** (H2655, M04, *chaphets*) **life** (H2416, M25) and loves many days, that he may see good?" (vv.11–12). Two findings: the fear of the LORD is **learnable** (taught, not innate), and the appeal is lodged in **the inner being's own native desire** — "what man *desires life* and loves good days" *(stated)*. The operation harnesses the self's existing longing for life/good and **directs it** through the fear of the LORD *(inferred: the teaching is motivated by the pre-existing chaphets for life)*.

**VI. The inner being governs its own speech-organs (vv.13–14).**
"**Keep** (H5341) your **tongue** from evil and your **lips** from speaking **deceit** (H4820, M14). **Turn away** (H5493, M30) from evil and do good; **seek** (H1245, M41) **peace** (H7965, M33) and **pursue** it" (vv.13–14). The operation is **self-governance**: the inner being *guards* its own tongue and lips — the speech-organs are placed under inner discipline *(stated)*. And peace is not merely received but **actively hunted** — "seek peace *and pursue* it," a directed inner exertion *(stated)*.

**VII. The shattered inner being is the locus of nearness (v.18).**
"The LORD is **near** to the **brokenhearted** (*nishbere-leb* — the shattered of heart) and saves the **crushed** (H1793, *dakka*) **in spirit** (H7307, the seat)" (v.18). The gem-finding: the inner being **in its most broken state** — heart shattered, spirit crushed — is **precisely where nearness comes** *(stated)*. Brokenness of the inner being is *not* distance from God; it is the very condition that **draws** his nearness *(inferred: nearness is predicated *of* the brokenhearted, not despite them)*. The crushed spirit is met, not abandoned — a reversal of the intuition that shattering means being cast off.

## What Psalm 34 says about the inner being
- **The boasting-faculty can be redirected (v.2).** What is *pride* aimed at the self becomes *praise* aimed at the LORD — and one soul's rightly-aimed glorying gladdens the humble who hear it.
- **Seeking dissolves the inner being's *fears* (v.4).** The seeking act meets an answer that discharges the interior dread itself, not just the outward threat.
- **Looking re-forms the face (v.5).** The inner being's direction of attention has a visible output — looking toward God makes the face radiant and un-shamed. Orientation is legible on the countenance.
- **The inner being knows God's goodness by *tasting* (v.8).** Verification is participatory and first-hand — knowing-by-tasting grounds knowing-about.
- **The fear of the LORD is learnable and desire-driven (vv.11–12).** It is *taught*, and it works by harnessing the inner being's own native longing for life and good and directing it.
- **The inner being governs its own speech-organs (vv.13–14).** Tongue and lips are placed under inner discipline; peace is actively pursued, not merely awaited.
- **The shattered inner being is the locus of nearness (v.18).** A broken heart and crushed spirit draw God's nearness rather than repelling it — brokenness is the condition met, not the condition abandoned.

## Honest notes
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at vv.5, 10, 20, 22 — negation/descriptive; bearer=LORD bleed pervasive incl. superscription; intensity *all/many*) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **v.18 "brokenhearted"/"crushed in spirit"** captured via gate-2 spans (*shabar* + *leb*; *dakka* + *ruach*, seat=spirit) rather than a single tagged characteristic; the inner-being state is read from the span pair. Candidate to promote *broken-of-heart / crushed-of-spirit* to a stored characteristic (a recurring inner-state).
- **`aheb` ("loves", v.12)** again gate-2 standalone (as at Ps 26:8, 31:23) — here "loves many days"; the aheb-reclassification candidate holds, though this object is *days*, not God.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *soul/boast* (H5315/H1984, M47/M08, v.2); *humble/glad* (H6035/H8055, M24/M04, v.2); *sought/seek* (H1875/H1245, M41, vv.4,10,14); *fears* (H4034, M01, v.4); *ashamed* (H2659, M07, v.5); *taste* (H2938, M15, v.8); *good* (H2896, M04, v.8); *fear* (H3373/H3374, M01, vv.7,9,11); *desires/life* (H2655/H2416, M04/M25, v.12); *deceit* (H4820, M14, v.13); *turn-away/keeps* (H5493/H8104, M30, vv.14,20); *peace* (H7965, M33, v.14); *righteous* (H6662, M26, vv.15,19,21); *afflictions* (H7451, M03, vv.19,21); *wicked/hate/condemned* (H7563/H8130/H0816, M10/M06, v.21); *redeems/refuge* (H6299/H2620, M38/M19, vv.8,22).
