# Psalm 46 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 46:1–11 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (vv.9 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Fearlessness and stillness grounded in an indwelling.** Psalm 46's inner-being findings are two operations: a **fearlessness decoupled from the world's stability** — the self unafraid *even when the world is unmade* (vv.1–3), *not moved* while the mountains move (v.5); and the command to **cease striving** — "be still" (*raphah*, let go / drop the hands) — as the **precondition of knowing God** (v.10). (Much of the psalm — the river-city, the raging nations, the ending of wars — is the *arena* in which these operate.)

## The reading

**I. Fearlessness decoupled from the world's stability (vv.1–3).**
"God is our **refuge** (H4268, M19) and **strength** (H5797, M23)… **Therefore we will not fear** (H3372, M01) though the earth give way, though the mountains be **moved** (H4131) into the heart of the sea, though its waters roar" (vv.1–3). The operation: the inner being's fearlessness is a **consequence** — "*therefore* we will not fear" — grounded in God-as-refuge *(stated)*. The finding: the not-fearing extends **even to total cosmic collapse** — the earth dissolving, the mountains falling into the sea — because the self's **ground is God, not the world** *(inferred: the fear is refused precisely at the point where every solid thing gives way, so the stability cannot be the world's)*. The inner being's steadiness is **decoupled from the stability of its surroundings**: even if everything solid is unmade, it does not fear *(inferred)*.

**II. The God-indwelt self is *not moved* while the mountains move (v.5).**
"God is **in the midst** of her; she shall **not be moved** (H4131, *mot*); God will help her when morning dawns" (v.5). The finding, in exact contrast to v.2: the mountains **are moved** (*mot*, v.2), but the God-indwelt self is **not moved** (*mot*, v.5) *(stated: the same verb, opposite outcome)*. The operation: stability comes **from an indwelling presence** ("God is in the midst"), not from external solidity — what steadies the inner being is *who is within it*, while the world outside shakes *(inferred: the not-moved is predicated on "God is in the midst")*.

**III. "Be still" — cease striving as the precondition of knowing (v.10).**
"**Be still** (H7503, M24, *raphah* — let go, drop the hands, cease), and **know** (H3045) that I am God" (v.10). The gem-operation: *raphah* is not merely "be quiet" but **let go / stop striving** — the same verb as Ps 37:8's "*refrain* from anger" — a **dropping of the self's own frantic effort** *(stated)*. And it is joined to *knowing*: "be still, **and** know." The finding: **the cessation is the *condition* of the knowledge** — the inner being must **stop its own struggling** for the knowledge of God to arrive *(inferred: the imperative pairs the ceasing and the knowing — one enables the other; striving must drop for knowing to happen)*. That *raphah* sits in the humility cluster (M24) fits: the ceasing is a **self-lowering**, a release of one's own grip *(inferred)*.

## What Psalm 46 says about the inner being
- **Fearlessness can be *decoupled from the world's stability* (vv.1–3).** The self does not fear *even when the world is unmade*, because its ground is God, not its surroundings. The not-fearing holds precisely where every solid thing gives way.
- **Stability comes from an *indwelling*, not from external solidity (v.5).** The mountains are moved; the God-indwelt self is *not* moved. What steadies the inner being is who is within it, while the world outside shakes.
- **Ceasing is the precondition of knowing (v.10).** "Be still" is *raphah* — let go, drop the hands, stop striving — and it is the condition of knowing God. The inner being must stop its own struggling for the knowledge of God to arrive; the ceasing is a self-lowering release of its grip.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** vv.4, 6–9 (the glad river-city, the raging nations, the ending of wars, God's uttered voice) are the arena; read as the setting for the two inner-being operations (vv.1–3, 5, 10), not mined verse-by-verse.
- **"be still" (H7503, *raphah*, v.10)** correctly tagged M24 (humility/self-lowering) — the reading foregrounds the *let-go/cease-striving* sense (same lemma as Ps 37:8's "refrain"), a good convergence.
- **The *mot* ("moved") contrast** (v.2 mountains moved / v.5 she not moved) is captured across gate-2 spans; the inner-being finding (stability from indwelling) read from the deliberate repetition. Ties to the "not moved" thread (Ps 16:8, 21:7 gift; 30:6 presumption) — here, *indwelling-grounded*.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at v.2 "not fear"; bearer=Korah/LORD bleed via superscription; intensity *very*; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *refuge/strength* (H4268/H5797, M19/M23, v.1); *trouble* (H6869, M03, v.1); *fear* (H3372, M01, v.2); *still* (H7503, M24, v.10). Note the cosmic-upheaval verbs (give way / roar / totter / melt) are gate-2 standalone (the arena), correctly not inner-being characteristics.

# Psalm 47 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 47:1–9 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **A brief enthronement hymn — honestly scoped.** Its body (God reigns, is exalted, sits on his throne) is the *arena* of praise. Its two genuine inner-being findings are modest: **joy expressed bodily and vocally** (clap, shout, sing — vv.1, 6), and a **God-conferred exaltation** ("the pride of Jacob") grounded in being *loved* (v.4).

## The reading

**I. Joy overflows into the body and voice (vv.1, 6).**
"**Clap your hands**, all peoples! **Shout** to God with loud songs of **joy**!… **Sing praises** (H2167, M42) to God, **sing praises**!" — the imperative repeated five times (v.6) (vv.1, 6). The operation: the inner being's gladness **does not stay interior — it moves out through the body (clapping) and the voice (shouting, singing)** *(stated)*. The finding: joy here is **enacted, not merely felt** — the whole person, hands and voice, is the medium of the inner being's praise *(inferred: the fivefold "sing" and the clapping/shouting make the joy bodily-vocal, an overflow into action)*.

**II. A God-conferred exaltation, grounded in being loved (v.4).**
"He **chose** (H0977, M37) our **heritage** for us, the **pride** (H1347, M08, *gaon*) of Jacob whom he **loves** (H0157, *aheb*)" (v.4). The finding: the "**pride**" of Jacob — *gaon*, the exaltation/glory — is here **not the sinful self-exaltation of the M08 cluster but a *conferred* dignity**: God *chose* it, and it rests on being *loved* *(stated: God chose the heritage, the pride of Jacob whom he loves)*. The operation: the inner being's legitimate exaltation is **received, not self-generated** — dignity grounded in election and love, the opposite of the self-inflating pride the same cluster elsewhere warns against *(inferred: gaon here is God-chosen and love-grounded, so the exaltation is a gift, not a claim)*.

## What Psalm 47 says about the inner being
- **Joy is enacted through body and voice (vv.1, 6).** The inner being's gladness overflows into clapping, shouting, and repeated singing — praise as bodily-vocal action, not merely interior feeling.
- **Legitimate exaltation is *conferred* and *love-grounded* (v.4).** The "pride of Jacob" is a dignity *chosen* by God and resting on being loved — received, not self-generated; the opposite of self-inflating pride.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** this is a short hymn largely about God's reign (vv.2–3, 5, 7–9 — the arena); the inner-being content is limited to the bodily-vocal joy and the conferred exaltation. Noted plainly rather than inflated (memory `feedback_no_stats_trends_review_fabricated_data`).
- **SANITY-CHECK CATCH (recurring) — "loves" (H0157, *aheb*, v.4) gate-2 standalone** — the sixth occurrence of the pattern (Ps 26:8, 31:23, 34:12, 45:7, and here). *aheb* toward/of persons keeps being under-tagged; the **aheb-reclassification is a firmly established pattern** for the Phase-1 rules.
- **"pride" (H1347, *gaon*, M08)** correctly a characteristic but read here in its *positive* (conferred-exaltation) sense — a per-occurrence note: the M08 cluster holds both sinful self-exaltation and God-given dignity.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *feared* (H3372, M01, v.2); *chose* (H0977, M37, v.4); *pride/gaon* (H1347, M08, v.4 — conferred sense); *loves* (H0157, v.4 — see catch); *sing* (H2167, M42, vv.6–7).

# Psalm 48 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 48:1–14 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.7 backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **A Zion hymn — honestly scoped.** Its body (the city's beauty, the routed kings, God as her fortress) is the *arena*. Three inner-being operations surface: **contemplation** of God's steadfast love in the temple (v.9), the maturing of knowledge from **heard to seen** (v.8), and **considered observation for transmission** (vv.12–14).

## The reading

**I. Knowledge matures from heard to seen (v.8).**
"As we have **heard**, so have we **seen** in the city of the LORD of hosts" (v.8). The operation: the inner being's inherited **report** ("heard" — cf. Ps 44:1's "we have heard with our ears") is now **confirmed by first-hand experience** ("seen") *(stated)*. The finding: the inner being's knowledge **matures from received testimony to verified sight** — the passed-down word becomes the self's own seeing *(inferred: "as we heard, so we have seen" is the movement from report to first-hand confirmation)*.

**II. Contemplation of steadfast love in the temple (v.9).**
"We have **thought on** (H1819, *damah* — pondered, dwelt upon) your **steadfast love** (H2617, M05), O God, in the midst of your temple" (v.9). The operation: a **deliberate meditation** — the inner being *dwells upon* God's chesed, and it does so in a **place set apart** (the temple) *(stated)*. The finding: the inner being **contemplates God's steadfast love as a practice**, an inward pondering located in the sanctuary — not a passing thought but a considered dwelling-upon *(inferred: damah "in the midst of the temple" makes it a sustained, sited contemplation)*.

**III. Considered observation, oriented to transmission (vv.12–14).**
"Walk about Zion… number her towers, **consider well** (H7896, M15) her ramparts… **that you may tell the next generation** that this is God… He will **guide** us forever" (vv.12–14). The operation: careful, deliberate **observation** (walk, number, consider) undertaken **for the sake of passing it on** *(stated)*. The finding: the inner being's **considered perception is oriented outward and forward** — one observes *well* so as to *tell* the next generation; attention serves transmission *(inferred: the "consider well… that you may tell" makes the careful looking instrumental to teaching)*.

## What Psalm 48 says about the inner being
- **Knowledge matures from *heard* to *seen* (v.8).** Inherited testimony becomes the inner being's own first-hand sight — the passed-down word verified in experience.
- **Contemplation of steadfast love is a *practice* (v.9).** The inner being deliberately *dwells upon* God's chesed, sited in the sanctuary — a sustained pondering, not a passing thought.
- **Considered perception serves *transmission* (vv.12–14).** The inner being observes *well* in order to *tell* the next generation — attention oriented outward and forward, to teaching.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** vv.1–7, 10–11 (Zion's beauty, the panicked kings, praise) are the arena; the inner-being content is the three operations above. Noted plainly, not inflated.
- **"thought on" (H1819, *damah*, v.9)** captured gate-2 standalone; the *contemplation/meditation* operation read from the verb (a pondering sense distinct from *hagah* of Ps 1/39). Candidate for a contemplation characteristic.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Zion/Judah/LORD bleed via the personifications; backfilled v.7 now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05, v.9); *glad/rejoice* (H8055/H1523, M04, v.11); *consider* (H7896, M15, v.13). The kings' *trembling/anguish/panic* (vv.5–6) are the external pole (the routed enemy), read as arena.

# Psalm 49 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 49:1–20 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.4 backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **A wisdom meditation on the soul and wealth.** Psalm 49's findings turn on what wealth *cannot* do to the inner being and what *understanding* does for it: the heart's **meditation producing understanding** (vv.3–4); the **un-ransomable soul** — wealth has no purchase on the inner being's ultimate fate (vv.7–9); the fool's **self-deceiving inner conviction of permanence** (v.11); **understanding as the beast/man divider** (the refrain, vv.12, 20); and the soul **ransomed by God** where wealth failed (v.15).

## The reading

**I. The heart's meditation produces understanding (vv.3–4).**
"My mouth shall speak **wisdom** (H2451); the **meditation** (H1900, M15, *hagut*, seat=heart) of my **heart** (H3820, the seat — M47) shall be **understanding** (H8394, M15, *tevunah*). I will **incline my ear** to a **proverb** (H4912); I will solve my riddle" (vv.3–4). The operation: **understanding is the *output* of the heart's meditation** — the inner being *ponders* (hagut) and thereby *understands* *(stated: the heart's meditation *shall be* understanding)*. The finding: wisdom is **worked inwardly** — the inner being inclines its ear, dwells on a riddle, and the heart's meditation *becomes* insight *(inferred: the meditation and the understanding are equated — the process yields the faculty)*.

**II. The un-ransomable soul — wealth's impotence over the inner being's fate (vv.5–9).**
"Why should I **fear** (H3372, M01)… when the iniquity of those who cheat me surrounds me — those who **trust** (H0982, M19) in their **wealth** (H2428, M23) and **boast** (H1984, M08) of their riches? Truly no man can **ransom** (H6299, M38, *padah*) another… for the **ransom** (H6306, *pidyon*, seat=soul) of their **life/soul** (H5315, M47) is **costly and can never suffice**, that he should live on forever" (vv.5–9). The gem-finding: **the soul cannot be bought back** — the ransom-price of a life is beyond any payment *(stated: the ransom of the soul is costly and can never suffice)*. The operation: the misplaced **trust in wealth is exposed by its total impotence over the soul's ultimate fate** — the very thing the fool leans on **has no purchase on death** *(inferred: those who *trust in wealth* are answered by wealth's inability to ransom a soul)*. And so the inner being need not *fear* the wealthy cheat — his riches cannot secure even his own life *(inferred: the "why should I fear" of v.5 is answered by vv.7–9's un-ransomable soul)*.

**III. The self-deceiving inner conviction of permanence (v.11).**
"Their **inward thought** (*qereb* — inner part) is that their houses **endure forever**… they called lands by their own names" (v.11). The operation: the fool harbours a **false inner conviction of his own permanence** — the self *telling itself* it will last *(stated: their inward thought is that their houses endure forever)*. The finding: the inner being can **deceive itself about its mortality** — an interior belief in permanence held *against* the reality of death *(inferred: the "inward thought" is a self-generated conviction contradicted by v.12)*. This is the exact inverse of Ps 39's *grasping* of finitude — here the inner being *refuses* to grasp it.

**IV. Understanding as the beast/man divider (vv.12, 20).**
The refrain, twice: "Man in his **pomp** (H3366) will not remain; he is like the **beasts** (H0929) that perish" (v.12), sharpened at the close: "Man in his pomp **yet without understanding** (H0995, M15, *bin*) is like the beasts that perish" (v.20). The gem-finding: what distinguishes man from beast is **understanding** — the man who has pomp *but lacks understanding* is **reduced to the animal level** *(stated: pomp *without understanding* = like the beasts)*. The operation: **understanding is the inner faculty that raises the inner being above the perishing beasts** — and wealth/pomp cannot substitute for it *(inferred: the added "without understanding" in v.20 names the missing faculty as the difference between man and beast)*.

**V. God ransoms the soul that wealth could not (v.15).**
"**But God will ransom** (H6299, M38, *padah*) **my soul** (H5315, M47) from the power of Sheol, for he will **receive** (H3947, *laqach* — take) me" (v.15). The gem-contrast: what **no wealth could do** (ransom a soul, vv.7–9), **God does** — "God will ransom *my* soul" *(stated)*. The finding: the inner being's redemption from death, **impossible by any payment it could make**, is **accomplished by God as gift** — "he will *receive/take* me" *(inferred: the same *padah* that "can never suffice" from man is done by God)*. The whole psalm turns here: the un-ransomable-by-wealth soul is *ransomed-by-God*.

**VI. The self not intimidated by wealth (vv.16–17).**
"**Be not afraid** (H3372, M01) when a man becomes rich… For when he dies he will carry **nothing** away; his glory will not go down after him" (vv.16–17). The operation, echoing Ps 37's "fret not": the inner being is **commanded not to be intimidated or envious of wealth** — grounded in the truth that riches **do not follow into death** *(stated)*. The finding: the self-management of not-fearing-the-rich rests on the same insight as the whole psalm — wealth has no power past the grave *(inferred)*.

## What Psalm 49 says about the inner being
- **Understanding is the *output* of the heart's meditation (vv.3–4).** Wisdom is worked inwardly — the inner being ponders a riddle and the heart's meditation *becomes* insight.
- **The soul is un-ransomable by wealth (vv.7–9).** No payment can buy back a life; the very thing the fool trusts (wealth) has no purchase on the inner being's ultimate fate — so the self need not fear the rich cheat.
- **The inner being can deceive itself about its mortality (v.11).** A false inner conviction of permanence, self-generated and held against the reality of death — the inverse of grasping one's finitude (Ps 39).
- **Understanding is the beast/man divider (vv.12, 20).** What raises the inner being above the perishing beasts is *understanding*, not pomp; wealth cannot substitute for the missing faculty.
- **God ransoms the soul that wealth could not (v.15).** The redemption impossible by any payment the self could make is accomplished by God as gift — the psalm's turn.
- **The self need not be intimidated by wealth (vv.16–17).** Not-fearing-the-rich rests on wealth's impotence past the grave — the same insight as the whole psalm.

## Honest notes
- **The two *ransom* words** (*padah* H6299, the act; *pidyon* H6306, the price, seat=soul) frame the finding — man's *pidyon* "can never suffice" (v.8), God's *padah* does (v.15). The lexical captured both; the contrast is the psalm's spine.
- **"inward thought" (v.11, *qereb*)** captured via gate-2; the self-deception-about-permanence operation read from the phrase. Candidate for a self-deception inner mechanism (cf. Ps 36:2's self-flattery).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at vv.7, 16, 20; bearer=Korah/LORD bleed via superscription; backfilled v.4 now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *meditation/understanding* (H1900/H8394/H0995, M15, vv.3,20); *heart* (H3820, M47, v.3); *fear/afraid* (H3372, M01, vv.5,16); *trust* (H0982, M19, v.6); *wealth* (H2428, M23, vv.6,10); *boast* (H1984, M08, v.6); *ransom* (H6299, M38, vv.7,15); *soul/life* (H5315, M47, vv.8,15,18–19).

# Psalm 50 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 50:1–23 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (vv.12 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **True worship and the projected God.** Psalm 50 (God's own speech) discloses two inner-being findings: what God desires from the inner being is **thanksgiving and dependence**, not the provision of ritual goods (vv.14–15, 23); and the wicked inner being's defining error — it **likens God to itself**, projecting its own nature onto him (v.21), which shows itself in a **discarded word** and **corrupt speech** (vv.16–20).

## The reading

**I. True offering — thanksgiving and calling, not provision (vv.7–15, 23).**
God's critique of ritual is not that sacrifice is offered but that it is **misunderstood as *provisioning* God**: "I will **not accept a bull** from your house… every beast of the forest is mine… If I were hungry, I would not tell you… **Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving** (H8426, M22, *todah*)… and **call** (H7121, M37) upon me in the day of trouble" (vv.9–15). The finding: what God desires from the inner being is **gratitude and dependence** — *thanksgiving* and *calling-upon-in-trouble* — not goods it imagines God needs *(stated: the sacrifice desired is thanksgiving + calling, not the bull)*. The operation: true worship is a **posture of the inner being** (grateful, dependent), and the closing line makes it explicit — "the one who offers **thanksgiving**… glorifies me; to one who **orders his way** rightly I will show salvation" (v.23) *(stated)*. Worship is re-located from the altar's goods to the heart's gratitude *(inferred: the whole speech displaces provision with thanksgiving/calling)*.

**II. The wicked *likens God to himself* — the projection (v.21).**
The gem-finding: "These things you have done, and I have been **silent**; you **thought** (H1819, *damah* — *likened*, deemed *similar*) that I was **one like yourself**. But now I rebuke you" (v.21). The verb is *damah* — literally *to liken / make similar* — so the charge is exact: the wicked inner being **remade God in its own image**, projecting its own moral indifference onto him *(stated: you *likened* me to yourself)*. The operation: **God's silence is misread as God's *likeness*** — because God did not immediately react, the self concluded he shares its own indifference to evil *(inferred: the "I have been silent; you likened me to yourself" ties the misreading of silence to the projection)*. The finding is a deep tendency of the inner being: **to construct God after its own nature**, a self-serving theological distortion.

**III. The discarded word and the rejected discipline (vv.16–17).**
"What right have you to recite my statutes… For you **hate** (H8130, M06) **discipline** (H4148, *musar*), and you **cast my words behind you**" (vv.16–17). The operation: the inner being **actively discards instruction** — it *casts the word behind*, out of sight, and *hates* the correction *(stated)*. The finding: the projection of a like-me God (v.21) is enabled by first **putting God's actual word where it cannot be seen** — the discarded word clears the space for the invented God *(inferred: casting the words behind precedes and permits the liken-God-to-self)*.

**IV. The corrupt speech that follows (vv.19–20).**
"You give your **mouth** free rein for evil, and your **tongue** frames **deceit** (H4820, M14). You sit and speak against your brother; you **slander** your own mother's son" (vv.19–20). The finding: with the word discarded and God re-imagined, the inner being's **speech runs to evil** — mouth and tongue framing deceit and slander *(stated)*. Speech is the outflow of the projected-God inner being: having remade God, it speaks as if unaccountable *(inferred: the corrupt speech follows from the discarded word and projected God)*.

## What Psalm 50 says about the inner being
- **True worship is a posture of the inner being, not provision (vv.14–15, 23).** God desires *thanksgiving* and *calling-upon-in-trouble* — gratitude and dependence — not goods it imagines he needs. Worship is re-located from the altar to the heart.
- **The inner being tends to *liken God to itself* (v.21).** *Damah* — it remakes God in its own image, projecting its own moral indifference; God's silence is misread as God's *likeness*. A deep, self-serving distortion.
- **The projection is enabled by *discarding the word* (vv.16–17).** Casting God's actual word behind, out of sight, and hating discipline clears the space for the invented God.
- **Corrupt speech follows the projected God (vv.19–20).** With the word discarded and God re-imagined, mouth and tongue run to deceit and slander — the inner being speaks as if unaccountable.

## Honest notes
- **"thought"/"likened" (H1819, *damah*, v.21)** captured gate-2 standalone; the *projection* operation (liken-God-to-self) is the psalm's key finding, read from the verb's *make-similar* sense. Candidate for a projection inner mechanism (cf. Ps 36:2 self-flattery, 49:11 self-deceived permanence — a family of self-serving distortions).
- **Scope honesty:** vv.1–6 (theophany, God summons to judgement) are the arena; the inner-being findings are in God's speech to worshippers (vv.7–15) and to the wicked (vv.16–23).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at vv.8–9, 12; bearer=Asaph/LORD bleed; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *call* (H7121, M37, vv.4,15); *thanksgiving* (H8426, M22, vv.14,23); *hate* (H8130, M06, v.17); *deceit* (H4820, M14, v.19). *discipline/musar* (H4148), *slander*, *forget* (H7911, v.22) captured gate-2 — the discarding/projection operations read from these.

# Psalm 51 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 51:1–19 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The re-creation of the inner being's core — a cornerstone psalm.** Psalm 51's findings run deeper into the inner being than any so far: sin **owned to its origin** (vv.3–5); God's concern for **truth in the *hidden* parts** (v.6); the plea to **CREATE** (*bara*) a clean heart — the core **cannot be self-repaired, only re-made** (v.10); the **spirit** renewed, sustained, and offered (vv.10–12, 17); and the **broken and contrite heart** as the offering God *receives* (vv.16–17). The whole is the mechanics of an inner being that cannot cleanse itself and is re-created from outside.

## The reading

**I. Sin owned to its depths — before the self, against God, from birth (vv.3–5).**
"For I **know** (H3045) my transgressions, and my **sin** (H2403, M10) is **ever before me**. **Against you, you only**, have I **sinned** (H2398, M10)… I was brought forth in **iniquity** (H5771, M10), and in **sin** did my mother conceive me" (vv.3–5). Three moves of full acknowledgment: the sin held **constantly in view** ("ever before me"); referred to its **ultimate object** ("against you only"); and traced to its **origin** ("brought forth in iniquity") *(stated)*. The finding: true owning is not admitting an act but **keeping the sin before one's own eyes, referring it to God as the one wronged, and recognising it as a condition reaching to the beginning** — the inner being's corruption is *constitutional*, not merely occasional *(inferred: the "ever before me… against you only… from conception" deepens sin from deed to condition-from-origin)*.

**II. God delights in truth in the *hidden* parts (v.6).**
"Behold, you **delight in truth** (H0571, M13, *emet*) in the **inward being** (*tuchot* — the hidden interior), and you **teach me wisdom** in the **secret heart** (H5640, *satum* — the sealed/hidden place)" (v.6). The gem-finding: God's concern is **not the surface but the innermost** — *truth in the hidden parts* — and he **teaches wisdom *there*, in the sealed interior** *(stated)*. The operation: God **works at the level of the secret heart**, the place hidden even from others; what he wants is integrity in the depths the self barely sees, and that is where his instruction lands *(inferred: the locus of both the delight (truth) and the teaching (wisdom) is the *hidden/sealed* interior)*.

**III. CREATE a clean heart — the core requires divine creation, not self-repair (v.10).**
"**Create** (H1254, *bara* — the verb reserved for God's making-from-nothing) in me a **clean heart** (H3820), O God, and **renew** (H2318, *chadash*) a right **spirit** (H7307, the seat) within me" (v.10). The central finding: the clean heart **cannot be self-generated — it must be *created*** *(stated: the verb is *bara*, used elsewhere only of divine creation)*. The operation: the inner being asks God to **create, not clean** — implying the old heart is **beyond mere washing; it needs a new making** *(inferred: choosing *bara* over a repair-verb signals the heart is un-reformable by the self and requires a creative act)*. The self **cannot manufacture its own clean heart**; the transformation of its core is a work only God can do *(inferred)*. Paired with it: *renew* (*chadash*) a steadfast **spirit** — the spirit's re-establishment *(stated)*.

**IV. The spirit in its states — holy, willing, broken (vv.11–12, 17).**
The *ruach* (spirit) recurs across the psalm in distinct states: "take not your **Holy Spirit** (H6944, M22, seat=spirit) from me" (v.11) — the sustaining divine spirit; "uphold me with a **willing spirit** (H5081, M09, *nadib* — free, generous, consenting)" (v.12) — the inner being's **freely-consenting disposition** that holds it upright; and "a **broken spirit** (H7665, *shabar*)" (v.17) — the shattered offering *(stated)*. The finding: the inner being's **spirit is worked on multiple registers at once** — it needs God's holy spirit to *remain*, a willing spirit to *uphold*, and is accepted as a *broken* spirit *(inferred: the three ruach-states name what the spirit receives, becomes, and offers)*. The *willing/nadib* spirit is notable — restoration includes a **freely-consenting** inner disposition, not mere compliance *(inferred: nadib is the free/generous will, so the upheld self *consents*)*.

**V. The broken and contrite heart as the offering God receives (vv.16–17).**
"For you will **not delight in sacrifice**… The sacrifices of God are a **broken spirit** (H7665); a **broken and contrite** (H1794, M24, *dakah* — crushed) **heart** (H3820), O God, you will **not despise**" (vv.16–17). The gem-finding: the acceptable offering is **not ritual but a *shattered inner being*** — a broken spirit, a crushed heart *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **offers its own brokenness**, and *that* is what God wants — the crushed heart is **not rejected but welcomed** ("you will not despise") *(inferred: the sacrifices "of God" are redefined as the broken spirit — brokenness is the offering, not a disqualification)*. This joins Ps 34:18 (the crushed spirit *drawn near*): the shattered inner being is precisely the acceptable thing *(inferred)*.

**VI. The restored joy overflows into teaching and praise (vv.8, 12–15).**
"Let me hear **joy** (H8342, M04) and gladness; let the **bones** that you have **broken** (H1794, *dakah*) **rejoice**… Restore to me the **joy** of your salvation… **Then I will teach** (H3925) transgressors your ways… my **tongue** will **sing aloud** (H7442, M42); open my **lips**, and my mouth will declare your praise" (vv.8, 12–15). The finding: the re-created inner being's joy **does not terminate in itself — it overflows into teaching others and praise** *(stated: "then I will teach transgressors… my tongue will sing")*. The restoration is **generative**: the cleansed self becomes an instructor of sinners and a voice of praise (cf. Ps 40's un-concealing, 32's confession issuing in teaching) *(inferred: the "then" makes the ministry-to-others the fruit of the restoration)*. And even the *broken bones* are made to **rejoice** — the very parts God broke are the parts restored to gladness *(stated)*.

## What Psalm 51 says about the inner being
- **Sin is owned to its origin, not just its act (vv.3–5).** True acknowledgment keeps the sin before one's own eyes, refers it to God as the one wronged, and recognises it as a condition reaching to conception — corruption constitutional, not occasional.
- **God's concern is *truth in the hidden parts* (v.6).** Not the surface but the sealed interior — and he teaches wisdom *there*, in the depths the self barely sees.
- **The clean heart must be *created*, not self-repaired (v.10).** *Bara* — the inner being asks God to *make*, not clean; the old heart is beyond washing, and the self cannot manufacture its own clean core. The transformation is a divine creative act.
- **The spirit is worked on several registers (vv.11–12, 17).** It needs God's holy spirit to *remain*, a *willing* (freely-consenting) spirit to *uphold*, and is accepted as a *broken* spirit. Restoration includes a consenting will, not mere compliance.
- **The broken and contrite heart is the offering God *receives* (vv.16–17).** Not ritual but a shattered inner being — the crushed heart is welcomed, not despised (with Ps 34:18). Brokenness offered *is* the sacrifice.
- **The re-created joy overflows into teaching and praise (vv.12–15).** The cleansed self becomes generative — an instructor of sinners, a voice of praise; even the broken bones are made to rejoice.

## Honest notes
- **"Create" (H1254, *bara*, v.10)** captured gate-2 standalone; the reading foregrounds it as *the* finding (the divine-creation verb applied to the heart — the core is re-made, not repaired). Strong candidate to promote as a characteristic-bearing item (the heart's re-creation).
- **"inward being" (*tuchot*, v.6)** not surfaced as its own span; read from the text alongside *secret heart* (H5640) — the hidden-interior locus. Candidate for an inner-depth characteristic.
- **The three *ruach* states** (Holy H6944-seat=spirit v.11; willing H5081/*nadib* M09 v.12; broken H7665 v.17) are the spirit-cluster of the psalm; the *nadib* (willing/free) spirit is a notable M09 datum — restoration as consenting will.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at vv.11, 17; bearer=David/Nathan/LORD bleed via superscription; *create/renew/restore* gate-2 verbs — the re-creation operation read from *bara*) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *sin/iniquity* (H2403/H2399/H2398/H5771, M10, vv.1–5,9,13); *truth* (H0571, M13, v.6); *joy* (H8342, M04, vv.8,12); *broken/contrite* (H1794, M24, *dakah*, vv.8,17); *heart* (H3820, M47, vv.10,17); *spirit* (H7307, seat=spirit, vv.10,11,12,17); *Holy* (H6944, M22, v.11); *willing* (H5081, M09, v.12); *sing-aloud* (H7442, M42, v.14).

# Psalm 52 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 52:1–9 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Mis-ordered love versus flourishing trust.** Psalm 52 sets the **evildoer whose love is aimed at evil** (vv.1–4) against the **one who trusts God's steadfast love and flourishes** (vv.7–8). The through-line: **what the inner being *loves* and where it places its *refuge* determine whether it is uprooted or flourishes** — the negative pole of Ps 45:7's ordered love.

## The reading

**I. Love aimed at evil — character as the direction of the love-faculty (vv.1–4).**
"Why do you **boast** (H1984, M08, *halal*) of **evil** (H7451, M27), O mighty man?… Your **tongue** plots **destruction** (H1942, M28)… You **love** (H0157, *aheb*) evil more than **good** (H2896), and lying more than speaking what is right. You **love** all words that **devour**, O **deceitful** (H4820, M14) **tongue**" (vv.1–4). The finding: the evildoer's character is defined by **where its love is aimed** — *loving evil more than good, lying more than truth* — the **exact inverse of Ps 45:7** ("loved righteousness, hated wickedness") *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's **love-faculty is set on the wrong objects**, and that mis-direction *is* the corruption — not the absence of love but its perverse aim *(inferred: character is the *direction* of aheb, here toward evil/lying/devouring)*. And the aimed love **arms the tongue**: the boasting and the razor-tongue are the outflow of the evil-loving inner being *(inferred: the plotting tongue expresses the loved evil)*.

**II. Two refuges — riches uprooted, steadfast love flourishing (vv.5–8).**
"God will **uproot** you from the land of the living… 'See the man who would **not make God his refuge**, but **trusted** (H0982, M19) in the abundance of his **riches**'… But I am like a **green olive tree** in the house of God. I **trust** (H0982, M19) in the **steadfast love** (H2617, M05) of God forever" (vv.5–8). The gem-finding: the two placements of trust produce **two opposite states** — the riches-truster **uprooted** (torn from his tent, v.5), the chesed-truster a **green olive tree** flourishing in God's house *(stated)*. The operation: **where the inner being lodges its refuge determines rootedness or uprooting** — trust in riches ends in being torn up; trust in God's steadfast love makes the self a *rooted, green, fruit-bearing tree* (the Ps 1 tree-image) *(inferred: the "uproot… but I am like a green olive tree" opposes the two trusts by their outcomes)*.

## What Psalm 52 says about the inner being
- **Character is the *direction* of the love-faculty (vv.3–4).** The evildoer *loves* evil, lying, devouring words — the corruption is not the absence of love but its perverse aim (the inverse of Ps 45:7). What the inner being loves *is* its character.
- **The aimed love arms the tongue (vv.1–4).** Boasting and the razor-tongue are the outflow of the evil-loving inner being — speech as the weapon of the disordered love.
- **Where refuge is placed determines rootedness or uprooting (vv.5–8).** Trust in riches ends uprooted; trust in God's steadfast love makes the inner being a flourishing green olive tree (the Ps 1 tree). The object of trust decides the state.

## Honest notes
- **SANITY-CHECK CATCH (recurring, now central) — "love" (H0157, *aheb*, vv.3–4) gate-2 standalone.** Seventh occurrence of the pattern (Ps 26:8, 31:23, 34:12, 45:7, 47:4, and here — twice). Here *aheb* is the **psalm's core inner-being finding** (loving evil), yet still under-tagged. The **aheb-reclassification is overdue** — *aheb* toward any object should be a characteristic (its *object* sets the valence). Strongly recommend acting on it in the Phase-1 rules.
- **Scope honesty:** the pronouncement of the evildoer's downfall (v.5) and the righteous' response (v.6) frame the two inner dispositions; the inner-being weight is the mis-aimed love (vv.3–4) and the two trusts (vv.7–8).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Ahimelech/LORD bleed via the long superscription; prohibition at v.7) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *boast* (H1984, M08, v.1); *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05, vv.1,8); *destruction* (H1942, M28, vv.2,7); *deceit/deceitful* (H7423/H4820, M14, vv.2,4); *love* (H0157, vv.3,4 — see catch); *trusted/trust* (H0982, M19, vv.7,8).

# Psalm 53 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 53:1–6 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. **A near-twin of Psalm 14** (id 412; 53 uses *Elohim* throughout and differs at v.5) — read here on 53's own terms, cross-referenced to 14. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Practical atheism as a heart-posture — and the divine scan for the inner faculties.** Two findings, as in Ps 14: the "no God" is a **disposition of the *heart*** that corrupts conduct (v.1), and God **scans mankind for the inner operations of *understanding* and *seeking*** (v.2).

## The reading

**I. "No God" as a heart-posture that corrupts conduct (v.1).**
"The **fool** (H5036, *nabal*) says **in his heart** (H3820, the seat — M47), 'There is no God.' They are **corrupt** (H7843, M27, *shachath*), doing **abominable** (H8581, M06) iniquity; there is none who does **good**" (v.1). The finding: the denial is **not an intellectual conclusion but a *heart-disposition*** — "says *in his heart*" — a practical **living-as-if-no-God** *(stated)*. The operation: this inner posture **corrupts the conduct** that flows from it — the "no God" in the heart issues directly in corrupt, abominable action *(inferred: the "says in his heart… they are corrupt" chains the inner denial to the outward corruption)*. The inner conviction is the **root**; the corrupt life is its fruit *(inferred)*.

**II. The divine scan for understanding and seeking (v.2).**
"God **looks down** from heaven on the children of man to see if there are any who **understand** (H7919, M15, *sakal*), who **seek** (H1875, M41, *darash*) after God" (v.2). The operation: God searches mankind specifically for **two inner faculties directed toward himself — *understanding* and *seeking*** *(stated)*. The finding: what God scans for is not deeds first but the **inner operations** — a mind that *understands* and a will that *seeks* God; these are the marks he looks for *(inferred: the object of the divine looking is "any who understand, who seek after God" — inner faculties, not acts)*. And the verdict is **universal turning-aside**: "they have **all fallen away**… none who does good, not even one" (v.3) — the scan finds the understanding/seeking absent across the board *(stated)*.

**III. The terror where there is no terror (v.5).**
"There they are, in **great terror**, where there is **no terror**!" (v.5, distinct from Ps 14). The finding: the "no God" heart, having lived as if unaccountable, is seized by a **groundless dread** — terror *where there is no terror* *(stated)*. The operation: the practical-atheist inner being, cut off from God, is subject to a **fear that has no external cause** — the interior instability of the self that denied God, dread arising from within rather than from a real threat *(inferred: "in great terror where there is no terror" locates the dread in the self, not the situation)*.

## What Psalm 53 says about the inner being
- **Practical atheism is a *heart-posture*, not a conclusion (v.1).** The "no God" is said *in the heart* — a disposition of living-as-if-no-God — and it is the root from which corrupt conduct flows.
- **God scans for the inner faculties of understanding and seeking (v.2).** What he looks for is a mind that *understands* and a will that *seeks* him — inner operations, not deeds first — and finds them universally absent.
- **The God-denying heart is seized by groundless terror (v.5).** Having lived as if unaccountable, it dreads "where there is no terror" — an interior instability, fear arising from the self rather than from a real threat.

## Honest notes
- **Near-duplicate of Ps 14** (id 412, slant "fool's 'no God' as heart posture corrupting conduct; God scans for seekers; universal turning-aside"). The shared findings are 14's; the distinctive datum here is **v.5's "terror where there is no terror"** (the groundless dread), which Ps 14 lacks. The pair should be noted together in any cross-chapter reading.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed via superscription; the wicked's *heart* mis-assigned in v.1; intensity *all*) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *corrupt* (H7843, M27, vv.1,3); *abominable* (H8581, M06, v.1); *heart* (H3820, M47, v.1); *understand* (H7919, M15, v.2); *seek* (H1875, M41, v.2).

# Psalm 54 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 54:1–7 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Setting God before oneself; the upheld soul; the freewill offering.** Psalm 54's inner-being findings: the wicked's root failure is **not *setting* God before themselves** (v.3, the inverse of Ps 16:8); God is the **upholder of the soul** (v.4); and gratitude is a **freewill** (spontaneous, un-compelled) offering (v.6).

## The reading

**I. The governing disposition — setting (or not) God before oneself (v.3).**
"For strangers have risen against me; ruthless men seek my **life** (H5315, the soul — M25/M47); **they do not set** (H7760, *sim*) **God before themselves**" (v.3). The finding: the ruthless assault is traced to a **prior inner failure — not keeping God in view** *(stated)*. The operation: **"setting God before oneself"** is a *disposition of the inner being* — a deliberate keeping of God in the field of vision — and its **absence is the root of the ruthlessness** *(inferred: the "they seek my life; they do *not set* God before themselves" makes the un-set God the source of the cruelty)*. This is the exact inverse of Ps 16:8 ("I have *set* the LORD always before me"): the same operation, refused *(inferred)*.

**II. God as the upholder of the soul (v.4).**
"Behold, God is my **helper** (H5826); the Lord is the **upholder** (H5564, *samak* — props up, sustains) of my **life/soul** (H5315, M47)" (v.4). The finding: the inner being (the *nephesh*) is **held up from outside** — *samak*, propped/sustained *(stated)*. The operation: the soul does not stand by its own strength but is **upheld**, leaned against a sustaining hand *(inferred: samak is the propping of something that would otherwise fall)*.

**III. The freewill offering — spontaneous gratitude (v.6).**
"With a **freewill offering** (*nedabah* — freely, un-compelled) I will sacrifice to you; I will **give thanks** (H3034, M22) to your name… for it is **good** (H2896, M04)" (v.6). The finding: the inner being's gratitude is **freely given, not extracted** — a *freewill* offering *(stated)*. The operation: thanksgiving here is **spontaneous, arising from the self's own willing** (the *nadib*/*nedabah* free-will family, cf. Ps 51:12's willing spirit) — the self gives because it *will*, not because it must *(inferred: nedabah names the un-compelled, self-moved offering)*.

## What Psalm 54 says about the inner being
- **"Setting God before oneself" is a governing disposition (v.3).** Keeping God in view is an inner operation; its *absence* is the root of ruthlessness. The inverse of Ps 16:8 — the same operation, refused.
- **The soul is *upheld* from outside (v.4).** The inner being does not stand by its own strength but is propped/sustained (*samak*) — leaned against a sustaining hand.
- **Gratitude is a *freewill* offering (v.6).** Thanksgiving is spontaneous, self-moved, un-compelled — the inner being gives because it *will* (the *nadib*/*nedabah* free-will family, with Ps 51:12).

## Honest notes
- **"set God before themselves" (H7760, *sim*, v.3)** captured gate-2 standalone; the *keeping-God-in-view* operation read from the phrase — a direct inverse of Ps 16:8's *shivviti* ("I have set"). Candidate to note a *set-God-before-self* inner operation (a recurring disposition, positive and negative poles).
- **Scope honesty:** short psalm; the appeal (vv.1–2), the enemy note (v.3), and the confidence (vv.4–7) frame the three inner-being findings.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed via the long superscription; prohibition at v.3 "do not set"; *nedabah* gate-2) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *vindicate* (H1777, M26, v.1); *might* (H1369, M23, v.1); *life/soul* (H5315, M47, vv.3,4); *give-thanks* (H3034, M22, v.6); *good* (H2896, M04, v.6).

# Psalm 55 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 55:1–23 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.8 backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The overwhelmed inner being — between *flight* and *casting*.** Psalm 55's findings: under a flood of dread the inner being's impulse is **escape** — "wings like a dove… I would fly away" (vv.4–8); the deepest wound is **betrayal by the intimate** who shared its confidential counsel (vv.12–14); the betrayer's **heart is at war behind smooth speech** (v.21); and the resolution is to **cast the burden** on God rather than flee ("he will sustain you," v.22). Two responses to being overwhelmed — *fly away* or *cast-and-be-held*.

## The reading

**I. The overwhelming, and the impulse to flee (vv.4–8).**
"My **heart** (H3820, the seat — M47) is in **anguish** (H2342, *chul*) within me; the **terrors** (H0367, M01, *emah*) of death have fallen upon me. **Fear** (H3374, M01) and **trembling** (H7461, M01, *raad*) come upon me, and **horror** (H6427, M01, *pallatsuth*) overwhelms me. And I say, 'Oh, that I had **wings like a dove**! I would **fly away** (H5774) and be at **rest** (H7931); I would **wander** (H5074, M18) far away… find a **shelter** from the raging wind'" (vv.4–8). The finding: a **fourfold flood of dread** (terrors, fear, trembling, horror — a dense M01 cluster) overwhelms the inner being *(stated)*, and its immediate impulse is **escape** — the wish for wings, to *fly away*, to *be elsewhere and at rest* *(stated)*. The operation: under extreme anguish the inner being **longs to flee its situation entirely** — an honest escape-fantasy, the desire to *not be here* *(inferred: the "oh, that I had wings… I would fly away" is the overwhelmed self's reflex toward flight)*.

**II. The deepest wound — betrayal by the intimate who shared the *sod* (vv.12–14).**
"For it is **not an enemy** who taunts me — then I could bear it… **But it is you**, a man **my equal**, **my companion** (H0441, *alluph*), my familiar friend. We used to take **sweet counsel** (H5475, M17, *sod*) together; within God's house we walked in the throng" (vv.12–14). The finding: the wound's depth is **the intimacy betrayed** — "an enemy I could bear, but *you*" *(stated)*. The gem: what was shared was the **sod** — the *confidential counsel*, the very word Ps 25:14 uses for the **friendship of the LORD** given to those who fear him *(stated)*. So the betrayal violated the **innermost circle of shared confidence** *(inferred: the sod is the intimate-confidence bond, here turned)*. The operation: **the depth of trust shared sets the depth of the wound when it turns** — betrayal by an *equal/companion* who held one's confidence cuts as an enemy's assault cannot (cf. Ps 41:9's bread-sharing friend) *(inferred)*.

**III. The war-heart behind smooth speech (v.21).**
"His speech was **smooth** (H2505, *chalaq* — the flatterer's verb, as in Ps 36:2) as butter, yet **war** (H7128) was in his **heart** (H3820, M47); his words were softer than oil, yet they were drawn swords" (v.21). The finding: the betrayer's **heart is at war while the mouth speaks peace** — smooth words masking the heart's true content *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being can be **divided against its own speech** — war within, butter without; the heart's real state (hostility) concealed by the tongue's oil (the concealing-speech mechanism of Ps 28:3, 50:19) *(inferred: the "smooth speech… yet war in his heart" names the split)*.

**IV. Casting the burden — the alternative to flight (v.22).**
"**Cast your burden** (H3053, *yehav* — your lot, what is given you) on the LORD, and **he will sustain** (H3557, *kul*) you; he will never permit the righteous to be **moved**" (v.22). The gem-resolution: against the earlier wish to **fly away** (vv.6–8), the inner being is told to **cast its burden on God**, who *sustains* *(stated)*. The finding — the psalm's key contrast: **the two responses to being overwhelmed are *escape* (fly away, vv.6–8) and *transfer* (cast the burden, be held, v.22)** — and the psalm moves from the flight-wish to the burden-casting *(inferred: v.22's "cast your burden… he will sustain" answers vv.6–8's "I would fly away")*. What the self cannot carry it **hands over** rather than **runs from** — and is *sustained* and *not moved* *(inferred)*. The close confirms the settled posture: "But I will **trust** in you" (v.23).

## What Psalm 55 says about the inner being
- **Under a flood of dread, the inner being's impulse is *flight* (vv.4–8).** A fourfold overwhelming (terrors, fear, trembling, horror) drives the honest wish to fly away, to be elsewhere and at rest — the reflex to *not be here*.
- **Betrayal by the intimate is the deepest wound (vv.12–14).** The depth of shared confidence — the *sod*, the same word for God's own friendship — sets the depth of the injury when it turns. An enemy could be borne; the equal-companion cannot.
- **The heart can be at war behind smooth speech (v.21).** The inner being divided against its own tongue — war within, butter without; the heart's true hostility concealed by the mouth's oil.
- **Casting the burden is the alternative to flight (v.22).** The two responses to being overwhelmed are *escape* and *transfer*; the inner being moves from the wish to fly away to casting its burden on God — what it cannot carry it hands over rather than runs from, and is sustained and not moved.

## Honest notes
- **"sweet counsel" (H5475, *sod*, v.14)** correctly M17 — and notably the **same word as Ps 25:14's "friendship of the LORD"**; the reading foregrounds that the betrayed bond was the *sod* (innermost confidence). A strong cross-psalm datum for the *sod* thread.
- **The M01 dread-cluster (vv.4–5)** — *emah*/*yirah*/*raad*/*pallatsuth* all M01 — is a good convergence for the fear cluster (the fourfold overwhelming as one operation).
- **"Cast your burden" (H3053, *yehav*) / "sustain" (H3557, *kul*)** captured gate-2; the transfer-vs-flight operation read from the pairing against vv.6–8. Candidate to note a *burden-casting* inner operation.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at vv.1, 22; bearer=David/LORD bleed via superscription incl. the enemies' *strife* mis-assigned in vv.9–11; backfilled v.8 now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *give-ear* (H0238, M41, v.1); *hide* (H5956, M14, v.1); *heart* (H3820, M47, vv.4,21); *terrors/fear/trembling/horror* (H0367/H3374/H7461/H6427, M01, vv.4–5); *wander* (H5074, M18, v.7); *strife* (H7379, M02, v.9); *counsel/sod* (H5475, M17, v.14); *trust* (implied v.23).

# Psalm 56 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 56:1–13 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Trusting *while* afraid, and the tenderly-recorded grief.** Psalm 56's findings: the inner being **trusts *in* the fear, not after it** — "when I am afraid, I put my trust in you" (vv.3–4); its grief is **precisely counted and treasured** by God — tossings numbered, tears bottled, all booked (v.8); trust **re-sizes the threat** ("what can flesh do to me?", vv.4, 11); and the delivered soul's end is to **walk before God in the light of life** (v.13).

## The reading

**I. Trust performed *in* the fear (vv.3–4, 10–11).**
"When I am **afraid** (H3372, M01), I put my **trust** (H0982, M19) in you. In God… I **trust**; I shall **not be afraid**. What can **flesh** (H1320, seat=flesh — mortal weakness) do to me?" (vv.3–4; repeated vv.10–11). The gem-finding: the inner being **does not wait for the fear to pass before trusting — it trusts *when* afraid** *(stated: "when I am afraid, I put my trust in you")*. The operation, with its mechanism: **afraid → trust → not afraid** — trust is what the self *does with* the fear, and the doing dissolves the fear's grip *(inferred: the sequence runs from "when I am afraid, I trust" to "I shall not be afraid")*. Fear is the **occasion** for trust, not its obstacle; the two coexist and the trusting is the resolving act *(inferred)*.

**II. Trust re-sizes the threat (vv.4, 11).**
"What can **flesh** (H1320) do to me?… What can **man** do to me?" (vv.4, 11). The finding: the trusting inner being **re-measures its attackers** — they are mere *flesh* (basar, the word of mortal frailty) *(stated)*. The operation: trust **shrinks the threat to its true size** — what looked overwhelming (v.1, "man tramples on me all day long") is re-seen as *flesh*, unable to reach the self that trusts God *(inferred: the rhetorical "what can flesh do?" follows the trusting, re-sizing the same attackers of v.1)*.

**III. The tenderly-recorded grief — tossings counted, tears bottled (v.8).**
"You have kept **count** of my **tossings** (H5112, *nod* — restless turnings/wanderings); put my **tears** (H1832, M03, *dimah*) in your **bottle** (*nod* — a wordplay). Are they not in your **book** (H5612)?" (v.8). The gem-finding: the inner being's suffering is **not ignored but preciously recorded** — every sleepless *tossing* numbered, every *tear* stored in a bottle, all written in a book *(stated)*. The operation: the self's grief is **seen and treasured** by God with tender precision — the restless nights counted, the tears kept as something of value *(inferred: counting the tossings and bottling the tears makes the grief precious data, not overlooked pain)*. The Hebrew wordplay (*nod* = wandering / *nod* = skin-bottle) binds the two: **the wanderings counted, the tears kept in the wanderer's flask** *(inferred)*.

**IV. The delivered soul walks in the light of life (v.13).**
"For you have delivered my **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47) from **death**… my feet from falling, that I may **walk** before God in the **light of life** (H0216 + H2416)" (v.13). The finding: the deliverance's **end is not mere survival but a *walk before God in the light of life*** — the restored soul lives *in God's presence and light* *(stated)*. The operation: rescue is **for** relationship — the soul brought out of death to *walk before God*, in the light (the light-of-life, cf. Ps 36:9) *(inferred: the "delivered… that I may walk before God" makes the presence-walk the purpose of the rescue)*.

## What Psalm 56 says about the inner being
- **Trust is performed *in* the fear, not after it (vv.3–4).** "When I am afraid, I put my trust in you" — the inner being trusts *while* afraid; the trusting is what it does with the fear, and the doing dissolves the fear's grip. Fear is the occasion for trust, not its obstacle.
- **Trust re-sizes the threat (vv.4, 11).** The attackers who "trample all day long" are re-seen as mere *flesh* — trust shrinks the threat to its true size, unable to reach the God-trusting self.
- **Grief is precisely counted and treasured (v.8).** Every restless tossing numbered, every tear bottled, all booked — the inner being's suffering is seen and kept as something of value, not overlooked.
- **Rescue is *for* the presence-walk (v.13).** The soul delivered from death is delivered *to* walk before God in the light of life — survival's end is relationship, life in God's presence and light.

## Honest notes
- **The *nod* wordplay (v.8)** — *tossings/wandering* (H5112) and *bottle/skin* (H4997) — captured across gate-2 spans; the reading foregrounds the tender-recording operation (grief treasured) read from the counting/bottling/booking. A candidate for a "grief-seen-and-kept" inner-being datum.
- **"flesh" (H1320, *basar*, seat=flesh, vv.4)** correctly captured — read here as *mortal frailty* (the threat re-sized), the object trust shrinks; the same basar was the assaulted body in Ps 27:2.
- **The afraid/trust refrain** (vv.3–4, 10–11) is the psalm's spine — *yare* (M01) and *batach* (M19) paired twice; a clean datum for the fear→trust→not-afraid mechanism.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (heavy prohibition over-stamp across the "not afraid" refrain and v.8's questions; bearer=David/LORD bleed via the long superscription; "life" H2416 tagged M44 where M25 fits) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *afraid* (H3372, M01, vv.3,4,11); *trust* (H0982, M19, vv.3,4,11); *flesh* (H1320, M47, v.4); *tears* (H1832, M03, v.8); *soul/life* (H5315, M47, vv.6,13); *praise* (implied, "whose word I praise", vv.4,10).

# Psalm 57 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 57:1–11 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **From the bowed soul to the steadfast heart, and the self that rouses itself.** Psalm 57's findings: refuge as a **temporary sheltering "till the storm passes"** (v.1); the movement from a **soul bowed down** to a **heart *fixed* / steadfast** (vv.6–7); and the inner being **rousing *itself* to praise** — "awake, my glory!" (v.8), the positive mode of self-address.

## The reading

**I. Refuge as a sheltering *until* the storm passes (v.1).**
"For in you my **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47) **takes refuge** (H2620, M19, *chasah*); in the shadow of your **wings** I will take refuge, **till the storms of destruction pass by**" (v.1). The operation: the inner being **takes cover under the wings for the *duration* of the danger** — refuge here is explicitly **temporal**, a sheltering *until* the storm passes *(stated)*. The finding: refuge is not a permanent hiding but an **active waiting-out** — the soul lodges under the wings *through* the danger, expecting it to pass *(inferred: the "till the storms pass by" makes the refuge a bounded, waited-out shelter)*.

**II. From the bowed soul to the fixed heart (vv.6–7).**
"They set a net for my steps; my **soul** (H5315, M47) was **bowed down** (H3721, *kaphaph* — pressed low). They dug a pit… But now: **My heart** (H3820, the seat — M47) is **steadfast** (H3559, *kun*/*nakon* — fixed, established), O God, my heart is steadfast!" (vv.6–7). The gem-finding: the inner being moves from a **soul *pressed low*** (v.6) to a **heart *fixed and established*** (v.7) — and the affirmation is **doubled** for emphasis *(stated: "my heart is steadfast… my heart is steadfast")*. The operation: the same inner being **shifts from bowed to settled** — *nakon* names a heart that no longer wavers, a **fixed core** *(inferred: the bowed soul of v.6 and the fixed heart of v.7 are the one self, moved from pressed to established)*. And the fixity is the **ground of praise**: "my heart is steadfast… **I will sing and make melody**" — the settled heart *issues in* song *(stated)*.

**III. "Awake, my glory!" — the inner being rousing itself (v.8).**
"**Awake** (H5782, M25, *ur*), my **glory** (H3519, M22, *kabod* — here the inner self/soul, as Ps 30:12)! Awake, O harp and lyre! **I will awake the dawn**!" (v.8). The gem-operation: the inner being **commands *itself* to wake** — "awake, my glory" is self-address in the **positive mode**, the self *rousing* its own inner being to praise *(stated)*. The finding: where Ps 42's self-address *interrogated* a downcast soul, here the inner being **stirs itself to action** — waking its "glory" (the God-facing inner self) and even, in eagerness, **waking the dawn itself** rather than being woken by it *(inferred: "I will awake the dawn" reverses the usual order — the roused self outruns the morning)*. The steadfast heart (v.7) does not wait to feel like praising; it **rouses itself** *(inferred)*.

## What Psalm 57 says about the inner being
- **Refuge is a sheltering *until* the storm passes (v.1).** The inner being takes cover under the wings for the duration of the danger — an active waiting-out, not a permanent hiding; it expects the storm to pass.
- **The inner being can move from *bowed* to *fixed* (vv.6–7).** From a soul pressed low to a heart *steadfast* (*nakon*) — doubled — the same self shifting from pressed to settled; and the fixed heart is the ground from which song issues.
- **The inner being can rouse *itself* to praise (v.8).** "Awake, my glory!" — self-address in the positive mode; the steadfast heart stirs its own inner self to action rather than waiting to feel like it, outrunning even the dawn.

## Honest notes
- **Self-address, positive mode:** "awake, my glory" (v.8) pairs with Ps 42's "why are you cast down, O my soul" — the same dialogical structure (an "I" addressing its own inner being), here *rousing* rather than *interrogating*. A strong datum for the self-address/self-government operation (cf. Ps 42–43, 103's "bless the LORD, O my soul").
- **"steadfast" (H3559, *kun*, vv.7)** captured gate-2 standalone; the *fixed-heart* operation read from the doubled affirmation. The heart's *fixity* (nakon) is a recurring inner-state worth a characteristic (cf. Ps 51:10 "renew a *nakon* spirit", 112:7 "his heart is *nakon*, trusting").
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Saul/LORD bleed via the long superscription; intensity *all*; the enemies' *lions/teeth/swords* v.4 are the external arena) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *soul* (H5315, M47, vv.1,4,6); *take-refuge* (H2620, M19, v.1); *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05, vv.3,10); *glory* (H3519, M22, vv.5,8,11 — v.8 = the inner self); *heart* (H3820, M47, v.7); *make-melody* (H2167, M42, v.7); *awake* (H5782, M25, v.8).

# Psalm 58 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 58:1–11 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.8 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The wicked inner being — manufactured from origin, self-sealed against correction.** Psalm 58's findings: injustice is **devised in the *heart*** before the hands execute it (v.2); the wicked's disorder reaches to **origin** — estranged from the womb (v.3); and the inner being **makes itself *deaf*** — the adder stopping its own ear against the charmer (vv.4–5), the inverse of Ps 40's opened ear.

## The reading

**I. The heart is the workshop of injustice (v.2).**
"No, in your **hearts** (H3820, the seat — M47) you **devise** (H6466, *pa'al* — work, fabricate) **wrongs** (H5766, M10, *avel*); your hands deal out **violence** on earth" (v.2). The operation: injustice is **manufactured in the heart *first*** — the heart *works* the wrong, and only then do the hands *deal it out* *(stated: in the heart wrongs are devised; the hands dispense them)*. The finding: the **heart is the workshop** — the inner being fabricates the wrong inwardly before it becomes outward violence; the deed is the heart's output *(inferred: the "hearts devise… hands deal out" sequence makes the heart the origin, the hands the delivery)*.

**II. Disorder from the womb — corruption at origin (v.3).**
"The wicked are **estranged** (H2114, *zur* — made strange, alienated) from the **womb**; they **go astray** (H8582, *ta'ah*) from **birth**, speaking **lies**" (v.3). The finding: the wicked's disorder reaches **all the way to origin** — *estranged from the womb, astray from birth* *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's corruption is presented as **congenital, not merely acquired** — a strangeness present from the beginning *(inferred: "from the womb… from birth" locates the estrangement at origin)*. (The same depth Ps 51:5 owns of *itself* — "in sin conceived" — here diagnosed of the *wicked* from outside; the penitent's confession and the diagnosis meet at the origin-point.)

**III. The willful self-deafness — the adder that stops its own ear (vv.4–5).**
"They have **venom** (H2534, M02, *chemah* — the same word as *wrath*) like the venom of a serpent, like the **deaf** (H2795) **adder** that **stops its ear** (H0241), so that it does **not hear** the voice of **charmers**" (vv.4–5). Two findings. First, the venom is *chemah* — **the serpent's poison is *stored wrath*** (the M02 anger word): the inner being's malice is a treasured heat *(inferred: chemah names the venom as wrath, so the poison is the heart's stored anger)*. Second, the gem: the wicked inner being **makes itself deaf** — like an adder **stopping its own ear** against the charmer's voice *(stated)*. The operation: a **willful, self-induced deafness** — the inner being **actively closes the faculty of hearing** against what would correct or charm it *(inferred: the adder "stops its ear so that it does not hear" — a deliberate self-sealing)*. This is the exact inverse of Ps 40's **"dug/opened ear"** (God-given receptivity): here the ear is **self-stopped** — the refusal of instruction as an active operation *(inferred)*.

## What Psalm 58 says about the inner being
- **The heart is the workshop of injustice (v.2).** Wrongs are *devised* in the heart before the hands deal them out — the deed is the heart's manufactured output, not a first cause.
- **The wicked's disorder reaches to origin (v.3).** Estranged from the womb, astray from birth — corruption presented as congenital, not merely acquired. (The penitent owns this of himself in Ps 51:5; here it is diagnosed of the wicked.)
- **The inner being can make itself *deaf* (vv.4–5).** Like an adder stopping its own ear against the charmer, the wicked self *actively closes* the faculty of hearing against correction — a willful self-deafening, the inverse of Ps 40's opened ear.
- **Malice is *stored wrath* (v.4).** The venom is *chemah* — the poison the inner being carries is treasured heat/anger.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the imprecation (vv.6–9) and the righteous' response to vindication (vv.10–11) are the arena; the inner-being weight is the wicked's *manufacture* and *self-sealing* (vv.2–5).
- **"venom" = *chemah* (H2534, M02)** correctly a characteristic in the *anger* cluster — the reading foregrounds the venom-as-stored-wrath link (a good M02 datum: malice as treasured heat, cf. Ps 37's self-kindling fire).
- **"stops its ear" (H0241, v.4)** captured via gate-2 *deaf/ear* spans; the self-deafening operation read from the adder image — a clean inverse of Ps 40:6's dug ear. Candidate to note a *self-stopped ear* inner mechanism.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed via superscription; *estranged/astray/devise* gate-2 verbs; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *right/judge* (H6664/H8199, M26, v.1); *hearts* (H3820, M47, v.2); *wrongs* (H5766, M10, v.2); *venom* (H2534, M02, v.4). *estranged/astray/lies* (H2114/H8582/H3577) captured gate-2 — the origin-corruption read from these.

# Psalm 59 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 59:1–17 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked). Complete chapter (v.15 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **God as the self's *own* strength — watched-for and sung-to.** A deliverance psalm (the howling-dog enemies are the arena); its inner-being findings: the self **watches for God** as its fortress (v.9); it names God as **"my Strength"** — its strength located outside itself (vv.9, 17); and its **morning-song** stands against the enemies' never-filled **evening-prowl** (vv.6, 14–16).

## The reading

**I. "I will watch for you" — vigilant Godward expectancy (v.9).**
"O my **Strength** (H5797, M23, *oz*), I will **watch** (H8104, M30, *shamar* — keep watch, guard) for you, for you, O God, are my **fortress**" (v.9). The operation: the inner being **keeps watch *for* God** — a vigilant, expectant waiting *(stated)*. The finding is sharpened by the superscription's inversion: Saul's men *watch* (*shamar*) the house *to kill* (v.1), while the psalmist *watches* (*shamar*) *for God* to deliver — **the same watching-faculty turned Godward** *(inferred: the enemy's lethal watching and the psalmist's expectant watching are the same verb, oppositely aimed)*.

**II. "O my Strength" — the self's strength located in God (vv.9, 17).**
The refrain names God as the inner being's **own strength** — "*my* Strength" — twice (vv.9, 17) *(stated)*. The finding: the self's strength is **not intrinsic but relocated** — its *oz* is God, its fortress is God *(inferred: "*my* Strength… *my* fortress" places the self's power outside itself, in God)*. The inner being draws its stability from a source it does not generate (cf. Ps 46:1's "refuge and strength").

**III. The morning-song against the evening-prowl (vv.6, 14–16).**
Twice: "Each **evening** they come back, **howling like dogs** and prowling about the city… They **wander about** for food and **growl if they do not get their fill**" (vv.6, 14–15). Against this: "But I will **sing** of your **strength**; I will **sing aloud** (H7442, M42) of your **steadfast love** (H2617, M05) **in the morning**" (v.16). The gem-finding: two **temporal rhythms of the inner being** — the wicked's **restless, never-satisfied *evening* prowling** (they *growl* when not filled), versus the psalmist's **satisfied *morning* song** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's disposition **shows in its rhythm** — the God-strengthened self *sings at dawn* (settled, satisfied), while the God-less self *prowls at dusk* (restless, unfilled) *(inferred: the evening-howl and the morning-song mark the two inner states by their hour)*.

## What Psalm 59 says about the inner being
- **The self *watches for* God with vigilant expectancy (v.9).** The same watching-faculty the enemies aim lethally, the psalmist turns Godward — expectant waiting for the fortress.
- **The self's strength is located in God (vv.9, 17).** "O my Strength" — the inner being's power is not intrinsic but relocated; it draws stability from a source it does not generate.
- **Disposition shows in the inner being's *rhythm* (vv.6, 14–16).** The wicked prowl and growl at evening, never filled; the God-strengthened self sings at morning, satisfied. The hour reveals the state.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the howling-dog enemies (vv.6–7, 14–15), the imprecation (vv.11–13), and God's derision (v.8) are the arena; the inner-being weight is the watching, the located strength, and the morning-song (vv.9, 16–17).
- **"watch" (H8104, *shamar*, v.9)** correctly M30 — the reading foregrounds the *watching-for-God* sense and its inversion of the enemies' lethal watching (superscription). A clean datum for the watch/wait family.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Saul/LORD bleed via the long superscription; intensity *all*; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *watch* (H8104, M30, v.9); *strength* (H5797, M23, vv.9,16,17); *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05, vv.10,16,17); *sing-aloud* (H7442, M42, v.16); *distress* (H6887, M24, v.16).
