# Psalm 94 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 94:1–23 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (vv.6 + others backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The "God doesn't see" self-deception refuted, and the anxious soul consoled.** Psalm 94's findings: the wicked's inner license **"the LORD does not see,"** refuted by the *Maker of eye and ear* (vv.7–9); God's **discipline received as blessing** (v.12); and the **multiplied cares of the heart answered by God's consolations** (vv.17–19).

## The reading

**I. "God doesn't see" — self-deception refuted by the Maker of eye and ear (vv.7–9).**
"And they say, '**The LORD does not see**; the God of Jacob does not **perceive** (H0995, M15, *bin*).' Understand, O dullest of the people!… **He who planted the ear, does he not hear? He who formed the eye, does he not see?**" (vv.7–9). The gem-finding: the wicked inner being grants itself license by telling itself **God is blind and deaf** to its evil — "the LORD does not see" *(stated)*. The refutation strikes at the root: **the One who *formed* the faculties of perception cannot lack them** — the Maker of the eye *sees*, the Maker of the ear *hears* *(stated)*. The operation: the wicked's **self-deception about God's perception** (the license "he doesn't see") is exposed by God-as-Maker-of-perception *(inferred: "he who formed the eye, does he not see?" turns the very existence of the self's faculties into evidence that their Maker perceives; cf. Ps 10:11, 50:21's projected/like-me God)*.

**II. Discipline received as blessing (vv.11–13).**
"The LORD knows the **thoughts** of man, that they are but a **breath**… **Blessed** is the man whom you **discipline** (H3256, *yasar*), O LORD, and whom you **teach** (H3925) out of your law" (vv.11–13). Two findings. God **knows the inner thoughts**, and they are *breath* (transient, fully seen) *(stated)*. And, counter-intuitively, God's **discipline is a *blessing*** — "*blessed* is the man whom you discipline" *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **counts God's correction as a good** — the disciplined-and-taught self is *blessed*, not merely chastened *(inferred: "blessed… whom you discipline… teach" makes correction a benefit; the opposite of the flight-from-discipline, Ps 39:13)*.

**III. The anxious soul consoled — cares answered (vv.17–19).**
"If the LORD had not been my help, my **soul** (H5315, the seat — M47) would soon have lived in the land of **silence**. When I thought, '**My foot slips**,' your **steadfast love** (H2617, M05) **held me up**. When the **cares** (*sarappim* — anxious, divided thoughts) of my **heart** (H3820, M47) are **many**, your **consolations** (*tanchumim*) **cheer** my **soul**" (vv.17–19). The gem-finding: when the inner being's **anxious cares *multiply*** — the heart full of divided, worrying thoughts — God's **consolations *cheer* the soul** *(stated)*. The operation: the **many inner cares** are met and **answered by God's comforts** — the anxious, care-crowded heart is *cheered/delighted* by consolation *(inferred: "the cares of my heart are many → your consolations cheer my soul" pairs the multiplication of anxiety with the consolation that lifts it)*. And at the point of *slipping* ("my foot slips"), it is **steadfast love that *holds up*** the self — catching the inner being precisely as it gives way *(stated)*.

## What Psalm 94 says about the inner being
- **The wicked license themselves by "God doesn't see" — refuted by the Maker of the faculties (vv.7–9).** The self-deception that God is blind to its evil is exposed: the One who *formed* the eye and ear surely perceives. The existence of the self's own faculties is evidence their Maker sees.
- **God's discipline is received as *blessing* (vv.12–13).** The inner being counts correction as a good — "blessed is the man whom you discipline" — the taught, corrected self, not merely chastened.
- **Multiplied cares are answered by God's *consolations* (vv.18–19).** When the heart's anxious thoughts multiply, God's comforts *cheer* the soul; and at the point of slipping, steadfast love *holds up* the self — catching it as it gives way.

## Honest notes
- **The Maker-of-the-eye refutation (v.9)** is a strong datum against the "God doesn't see" self-deception (the projected/like-me God of Ps 50:21, the wicked's "he will never see" of Ps 10:11) — captured via gate-2 *see/hear/eye/ear*; the operation read from the argument.
- **"cares of my heart / consolations cheer my soul" (vv.18–19)** captured via *heart* (H3820) + *soul* (H5315) with gate-2 *sarappim/tanchumim*; the anxious-soul-consoled read from the pair — a tender datum (with Ps 42's downcast soul, 55's overwhelmed self).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp across the "does not see/hear/discipline" negations vv.7–10; bearer=LORD bleed; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *perceive* (H0995, M15, v.9); *afflict* (H6031, M24, v.5); *wicked* (H7563, M10); *steadfast-love* (H2617, M05, v.18); *soul/heart* (H5315/H3820, M47, vv.17,19). *see/hear/discipline/consolations/cheer* captured gate-2 — the refutation, discipline-blessing, and consolation read from these.

# Psalm 95 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 95:1–11 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (v.3 backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The fork at hearing God's voice.** A call to worship that turns to warning. Its inner-being findings: the response to hearing God's voice can be a **hardening of the heart** (vv.7–8); and the **erring heart that does not know God's ways** forfeits rest (vv.10–11).

## The reading

**I. The fork at hearing God's voice — heed or harden (vv.7–8).**
"**Today, if you hear** (H8085) his voice, **do not harden** (*qashah*) your **hearts** (H3824, the seat — M47), as at Meribah… when your fathers put me to the **test**" (vv.7–8). The gem-finding: hearing God's voice presents the inner being with a **fork** — to *heed* or to *harden* *(stated)*. The operation: the heart can **stiffen itself against the very word it hears** — hardening is the heart's *refusal to be moved* by what it has just heard *(inferred: "if you hear his voice, do *not harden* your hearts" makes the hardening a response *to* the hearing — the heart setting itself against the word; contrast Ps 85's listening posture, 81's given-over refusal)*. And the **"today"** presses the urgency — the fork is *now*, at *this* hearing *(stated)*.

**II. The erring heart that does not know God's ways (vv.10–11).**
"They are a people who **go astray** (*taah*) **in their heart** (H3820, M47), and they **have not known** my ways… I swore in my wrath, 'They shall **not enter my rest**'" (vv.10–11). The finding: the inner root of straying is a **heart that *errs*** — those who "go astray *in their heart*" do **not know** God's ways *(stated)*. The operation: the **heart's inner wandering → ignorance of God's ways → exclusion from rest** *(inferred: "go astray in their heart… have not known my ways… shall not enter my rest" chains the erring heart to the lost knowledge and the forfeited rest — the hardening/wandering heart cannot enter the rest)*.

## What Psalm 95 says about the inner being
- **Hearing God's voice presents a *fork* — heed or harden (vv.7–8).** The heart can stiffen itself against the very word it hears; hardening is the refusal to be moved by what it has just heard. The "today" presses the fork into the present.
- **The *erring heart* forfeits the knowledge of God's ways and his rest (vv.10–11).** Inner wandering — "going astray in the heart" — issues in not knowing God's ways and in exclusion from rest. The heart that wanders cannot enter.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the worship-call (vv.1–7a — sing, bow down, the sheep of his hand) is the arena; the inner-being weight is the fork-at-hearing (vv.7b–8) and the erring heart (vv.10–11).
- **Cross-psalm:** the hearing/hardening fork ties to Ps 81 (refusal → given over to the stubborn heart), 85 (the listening posture), 95's own "today" — a coherent hearing-response thread.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at v.8; bearer=LORD/Meribah bleed; backfilled v.3 now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *hearts* (H3824/H3820, M47, vv.8,10). *hear/harden/go-astray/known/rest* captured gate-2 — the fork-at-hearing and the erring heart read from these.

"**Ascribe** (H3051, *yahav* — give, render) to the LORD, O families of the peoples, ascribe to the LORD **glory** (H3519, M22) and **strength** (H5797, M23)! The finding: the inner being's worship is **ascription** — *rendering* to God the glory that is *due his name*, not adding to him *(stated)*. The operation: to *ascribe* (*yahav*) is to **acknowledge and give back** what is already God's — worship as **recognition and self-abasement** (the *trembling* before him), not contribution *(inferred: "ascribe… the glory *due* his name… tremble before him" makes worship the rendering of what is owed, with awe, not an increase of God; the same finding as Ps 29:1–2, and worship "in the splendour of holiness" bows before beauty as well as majesty)*.

## What Psalm 96 says about the inner being
- **Worship is *ascription* — rendering, not augmenting (vv.7–9).** The inner being *gives back* to God the glory *due his name*, with trembling awe — worship as recognition and self-abasement before God's splendour and holiness, not a contribution to him. (The Ps 29:1–2 finding, restated.)

- **Creation-wide joy (vv.11–13):** the heavens/earth/sea/field rejoicing at God's righteous coming is read as the arena's response, not the inner being's operation (external creation, not the self).

## The reading

**I. To love the LORD is to hate evil (v.10).**

Ps 45:7's loved-righteousness/hated-wickedness)*.

The gem-finding: the inner being's light and joy are **sown** — *planted like seed* — for the upright *(stated)*. The operation: the upright-in-heart's gladness is a **seed awaiting harvest** — *sown* now, to spring up later; light and joy are **planted for** the upright, a deferred but certain gladness growing toward them *(inferred: "light is sown… joy for the upright in heart" makes the gladness a seed sown for a future harvest, not an immediate possession — the upright's joy is *coming up*)*.

## What Psalm 97 says about the inner being
- **Loving the LORD *entails* hating evil (v.10).** Right affection is a paired love-and-hate — the inner being that loves God must hate evil; the two are one ordered disposition, not love alone.
- **Light and joy are *sown* for the upright in heart (v.11).** The gladness of the upright is a seed planted for a future harvest — sown now, springing up later; a deferred but certain joy growing toward them.

# Psalm 99 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 99:1–9 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (v. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **A holiness hymn — honestly scoped, thin.** The declaration of God's reign and threefold "Holy is he" (vv.3, 5, 9) is the arena. Two inner-being resonances: **trembling worship/self-abasement before God's holiness** (vv.1, 5, 9); and the pattern of **calling and being answered** (vv.6, 8).

## The reading

**I. Trembling worship before God's holiness (vv.1, 5, 9).**
"The LORD reigns; **let the peoples tremble**!… **Worship at his footstool**! **Holy is he**!… Exalt the LORD our God, and worship at his holy mountain; for the LORD our God is **holy**!" (vv.1, 5, 9). The finding: the fitting inner response to God's holiness is **trembling worship** — bowing *at his footstool*, the lowest place *(stated)*. The operation (resonance): God's holiness draws the inner being to **awe and self-abasement** — the threefold "Holy is he" frames a worship that *trembles* and bows low *(inferred: "let the peoples tremble… worship at his footstool… holy is he" makes the holiness evoke trembling self-abasement; cf. Ps 96:9's worship in the splendour of holiness, 5:7's bowing in fear)*.

**II. Calling and being answered (vv.6, 8).**
"They **called** to the LORD, and **he answered** them… you were a **forgiving** God to them, but an **avenger** of their wrongdoings" (vv.6, 8). The finding: the pattern of the intercessors (Moses, Aaron, Samuel) — **they called, and God answered** *(stated)*. The resonance: the inner being that *calls* is *answered* — and the God who answers is both **forgiving** and **holding to account** (forgiving yet avenging wrongdoing) *(inferred: "they called… he answered… forgiving… but an avenger" pairs the answered call with a God who both pardons and holds accountable — the answer is not indulgence)*.

## What Psalm 99 says about the inner being
- **God's holiness draws the inner being to *trembling worship* (vv.1, 5, 9).** Awe and self-abasement — bowing at the footstool, the lowest place — is the fitting response to the thrice-holy God.
- **The one who *calls* is *answered* — by a God who both forgives and holds to account (vv.6, 8).** The intercessors called and were answered; the answering God is forgiving yet an avenger of wrongdoing — the answer is not indulgence.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the psalm is largely a declaration of God's holy reign and might (vv.1–4, 7); the inner-being weight is the trembling worship (vv.1, 5, 9) and the call-and-answer (vv.6, 8). Thin hymn, noted plainly.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed; "loves justice" v.4 is God's, not the inner being's; backfilled v. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** the terms are largely God-attributes and worship-calls captured gate-2 (the arena); the inner-being resonances (trembling worship, call-and-answer) read from vv.1, 5, 6, 8, 9. Noted plainly.

# Psalm 100 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 100:1–5 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (v. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Serving with gladness; the self as God's own.** A short thanksgiving. Two inner-being findings: **service rendered in gladness** (v.2); and the foundational knowledge that the self is **made by God and belongs to him — not its own** (v.3).

## The reading

**I. Service in gladness (v.2).**
"**Serve** the LORD **with gladness** (H8057, M04)! Come into his presence with singing!" (v.2). The finding: the inner being's service is to be **rendered *in gladness*** — joyful, not grudging *(stated)*. The operation: gladness is the **mode** of the self's service — worship and obedience done *with joy*, the inner disposition of the servant *(inferred: "serve… with gladness" makes joy the manner of the service, not a separate act — the self serves *gladly*)*.

**II. "We are his, not our own" — the self as God's (v.3).**
"**Know** that the LORD, he is God! **It is he who made us, and we are his**; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture" (v.3). The gem-finding: the inner being's foundational knowledge is that it is **made by God and *belongs* to him** — "we are *his*" *(stated)*. The operation: the self **knows itself as God's *possession*** — made-by, and belonging-to, God, **not self-owned** *(inferred: "he made us, and we are his" locates the self's origin and ownership in God — the inner being is not its own but God's; a foundational orientation, cf. Ps 95:7 "the sheep of his hand", 24:1 the earth is the LORD's)*.

## What Psalm 100 says about the inner being
- **Service is rendered *in gladness* (v.2).** Joy is the mode of the self's service — worship and obedience done gladly, not grudgingly; the servant's inner disposition.
- **The self is *made by God and belongs to him* — not its own (v.3).** The inner being's foundational knowledge is that God made it and it is *his*; the self is not self-owned but God's possession — origin and ownership located in God.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** short thanksgiving; the calls to praise (joyful noise, singing, thanksgiving, vv.1, 4) and God's goodness (v.5) are the arena; the inner-being weight is the gladness-in-service (v.2) and the self-as-God's (v.3).
- **"we are his, not our own" (v.3)** captured via gate-2 *made/people*; the self-as-God's-possession read from it — a foundational datum (with Ps 24:1, 95:7, 139:13–16).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed; backfilled v. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *gladness* (H8057, M04, v.2); *thanksgiving* (H8426, M22, v.4); *good* (H2896, M04, v.5). *serve/know/made* captured gate-2 — the glad service and the self-as-God's read from these.

# Psalm 101 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 101:1–8 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The inner being's active self-governance for integrity.** Psalm 101 is a set of *resolutions*. Its findings are operations of **self-governance**: integrity of heart **in the private sphere** (v.2); **governing what enters through the eyes** (v.3); **distancing the perverse heart** and refusing intimacy with evil (v.4); and **curating one's company** (vv.5–7).

## The reading

**I. Integrity of heart *within the house* — the private self (v.2).**
"I will **ponder** (H7919, M15, *sakal*) the way that is **blameless** (H8549, M12)… I will **walk with integrity** (H8537, M13, *tom*) **of heart** (H3824, the seat — M47) **within my house**" (v.2). The finding: the inner being resolves on **integrity of heart in the *private* sphere** — "within my house," where no one watches *(stated)*. The operation: integrity is maintained **unwatched** — the self is as integrous in private as in public *(inferred: "integrity of heart *within my house*" locates the integrity in the unobserved, domestic sphere — the private self held to the same standard; the *tom*-heart of Ps 26:1, here specifically *at home*)*.

**II. Governing the eye-gate (v.3).**
"I will **not set before my eyes** anything that is **worthless** (*beliyaal*). I **hate** (H8130, M06) the work of those who fall away; **it shall not cling to me**" (v.3). The finding: the inner being **governs its own *gaze*** — refusing to *set* anything worthless before its eyes *(stated)*. The operation: the self **controls its *intake through sight*** — guarding the eye-gate against the worthless, and refusing to let corruption *cling* *(inferred: "I will not set before my eyes… it shall not cling to me" makes the self the gatekeeper of what it looks at and what attaches to it; cf. Ps 119:37 "turn my eyes from worthless things")*.

**III. Distancing the perverse heart; refusing to *know* evil (v.4).**
"A **perverse heart** (H6141, *iqqesh* — twisted + H3824, M47) shall be **far from me**; I will **know nothing of evil**" (v.4). The finding: the inner being actively **puts the crooked disposition at a distance** and **refuses *intimacy* with evil** *(stated)*. The operation: two moves — **distancing the perverse heart** (holding the twisted disposition away) and **declining to *know* evil** (refusing the *intimate acquaintance* that "know" implies) *(inferred: "a perverse heart shall be far… I will know nothing of evil" makes the self actively separate from crookedness and refuse familiarity with evil — the opposite of the wicked who *cherish* iniquity, Ps 66:18)*.

**IV. Curating the company (vv.5–7).**
"Whoever **slanders** his neighbour secretly I will destroy… the **haughty look** and **arrogant heart** I will not endure. I will look with **favour on the faithful** (H0539, M13, *aman*)… he who walks **blamelessly** shall minister to me. No one who practices **deceit** (H7423, M14) shall **dwell in my house**" (vv.5–7). The finding: the inner being's integrity is **worked out in whom it keeps near** — the faithful/blameless *welcomed*, the slanderer/haughty/deceitful *excluded from the house* *(stated)*. The operation: **curating one's company** as the externalising of the heart's integrity — the self chooses its associates by their inner condition (faithful vs deceitful) *(inferred: "favour on the faithful… no deceit shall dwell in my house" makes the chosen company the outward form of the inner integrity; cf. Ps 26:4–5, 1:1's refused seat)*.

## What Psalm 101 says about the inner being
- **Integrity is held in the *private* sphere (v.2).** "Integrity of heart within my house" — the unwatched self is as integrous as the public; integrity is not for show.
- **The inner being governs its own *gaze* (v.3).** It refuses to set the worthless before its eyes and refuses to let corruption cling — the self as gatekeeper of what it looks at.
- **It *distances* the perverse heart and refuses to *know* evil (v.4).** Two active moves: holding the crooked disposition away, and declining intimacy with evil — the opposite of cherishing iniquity.
- **It *curates its company* as the outward form of its integrity (vv.5–7).** The faithful welcomed, the deceitful excluded from the house — the heart's integrity externalised in whom it keeps near.

## Honest notes
- **A strong self-governance datum:** integrity worked across three gates — the *heart* (private), the *eyes* (intake), and the *company* (association). A coherent inner-being process (with Ps 26's integrity, 119:37's guarded eyes, 1:1's refused company).
- **"perverse heart far / know nothing of evil" (v.4)** captured via *heart* (H3824) + gate-2 *perverse/know*; the distancing and refused-intimacy read from these.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp across the "I will not…" resolutions vv.3–7; bearer=David/LORD bleed) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *ponder* (H7919, M15, v.2); *blameless* (H8549, M12, vv.2,6); *integrity* (H8537, M13, v.2); *heart* (H3824, M47, vv.2,4,5); *hate* (H8130, M06, v.3); *faithful* (H0539, M13, v.6); *deceit* (H7423, M14, v.7). *eyes/worthless/perverse/know* captured gate-2 — the eye-governance and distanced-evil read from these.

# Psalm 102 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 102:1–28 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The afflicted, withering, lonely self anchoring on God's eternity.** Psalm 102's findings: affliction **saturating the whole life** — the heart withered, food ashes, days smoke (vv.3–11); the **isolation** figured as a lonely bird (vv.6–7); and the **fleeting self anchoring on God's unchanging eternity** (vv.11–12, 27).

## The reading

**I. Affliction saturating the whole life (vv.3–11).**
"My **days** pass away like **smoke**… My **heart** (H3820, the seat — M47) is **struck down** like grass and has **withered**; I forget to eat my bread… I eat **ashes** like bread and mingle **tears** (H1065, M03) with my drink… My days are like an evening **shadow**; I **wither** like grass" (vv.3–11). The finding: the affliction **pervades every dimension** of the inner being's life — the *heart* withers, the *food* becomes ashes, the *drink* becomes tears, the *days* become smoke and shadow *(stated)*. The operation: the affliction is not localised but **total** — it saturates the heart, the appetite, and the very texture of the days *(inferred: heart-withered, ashes-for-bread, tears-for-drink, days-as-smoke pile up to make the affliction pervade the whole life, not one faculty)*.

**II. The isolation — a lonely bird in waste places (vv.6–7).**
"I am like a **desert owl** of the wilderness, like an owl of the **waste places**; I lie **awake**; I am like a **lonely sparrow** on the housetop" (vv.6–7). The gem-finding: the afflicted inner being's **loneliness** is figured as a **solitary bird** — the owl in the desolate wilderness, the sleepless *lonely sparrow* alone on the roof *(stated)*. The operation: the self's **isolation and sleeplessness** — a creature alone in waste places, awake through the night *(inferred: the owl/sparrow images name a self cut off and unable to rest, the solitude of affliction; cf. Ps 88's darkness-companion)*.

**III. The fleeting self anchored on God's unchanging eternity (vv.11–12, 27).**
"My days are like an evening shadow; I wither like grass. **But you**, O LORD, are enthroned **forever**… you are the **same**, and your years have **no end**" (vv.11–12, 27). The gem-finding: the **withering, fleeting** inner being is set against God's **unchanging eternity** — "you are the *same*" *(stated)*. The operation: the transient self **anchors on the permanent God** — where the self is grass/shadow/smoke (soon gone), God *endures unchanged*, and *that* is the ground the fleeting self stands on *(inferred: the "but you… are the same… your years have no end" turns from the self's brevity to God's permanence as the counter and the hope — the withering self leans on the One who does not wither; cf. Ps 90:1–4)*. The self's very transience drives it to the eternal God *(inferred)*.

## What Psalm 102 says about the inner being
- **Affliction can *saturate the whole life* (vv.3–11).** The heart withers, food becomes ashes, drink becomes tears, days become smoke — the affliction pervades every dimension, not one faculty.
- **Isolation is figured as a *lonely bird* (vv.6–7).** The afflicted self is a solitary owl in waste places, a sleepless sparrow alone on the roof — cut off, unable to rest.
- **The fleeting self *anchors on God's unchanging eternity* (vv.11–12, 27).** Where the inner being is grass, shadow, smoke — soon gone — God *is the same*, his years without end; the transient self leans on the permanent God, and its very brevity drives it there.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** the psalm's middle (God's compassion on Zion, the nations fearing his name, the generations to come, vv.13–22) is the community/God arena; the inner-being weight is the affliction-imagery (vv.3–11), the isolation (vv.6–7), and the fleeting-self/eternal-God contrast (vv.11–12, 27).
- **The imagery** (smoke, grass, owl, sparrow, ashes, shadow) is captured largely gate-2; the affliction-saturation and isolation are read from the image-cascade, with *heart* (H3820, M47) and *tears* (H1065, M03) as the tagged inner terms.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *heart* (H3820, M47, v.4); *tears* (H1065, M03, v.9). The affliction/isolation/eternity images captured gate-2 — the saturated affliction, the lonely bird, and the anchoring-on-eternity read from these.

# Psalm 103 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 103:1–22 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The self rousing its whole inner being to bless; God's dust-frame compassion. A cornerstone.** Psalm 103's findings: the **self commanding *itself* to bless God** — enlisting the whole inner being and its *memory* (vv.1–2, 22); the **renewal of the self** (v.5); and God's **fatherly compassion grounded in knowing our frailty — that we are dust** (vv.13–14).

## The reading

**I. "Bless the LORD, O my soul" — the self rousing its whole inner being (vv.1–2, 22).**
"**Bless the LORD, O my soul** (H5315, the seat — M47), and **all that is within me**, bless his holy name! Bless the LORD, O my soul, and **forget not** all his benefits" (vv.1–2; refrain at v.22). The gem-finding: the inner being **commands *itself* to bless God** — an "**I**" rousing "**my soul**" (and "all that is *within me*") to worship *(stated)*. The operation: self-address in the **mode of *stirring to praise*** — the self **enlists its *whole* inner being**, "all that is within me," every faculty gathered into the blessing *(inferred: "O my soul… all that is within me" musters the entire interior, cf. Ps 57:8 "awake, my glory", 42's self-interrogation — here the positive rousing)*. And it commands its own **memory**: "**forget not** all his benefits" — the self governs its *remembering*, guarding against the ingratitude of forgetting *(stated; the self directs its own memory, cf. Ps 77's willed remembering)*.

**II. The renewal of the self (vv.3–5).**
"who **forgives** (H5545, M11) all your iniquity, who **heals** all your diseases, who **redeems** your life from the pit… who **satisfies** (H7646, *saba*) you with good so that your **youth** is **renewed** (H2318, *chadash*) like the eagle's" (vv.3–5). The finding: the inner being, satisfied with good, is **re-youthed** — its *youth renewed* like the eagle (which molts and renews) *(stated)*. The operation: the self is **renewed/rejuvenated** by God's benefits — not merely maintained but *made young again*, its vitality restored *(inferred: "satisfies you with good so that your youth is renewed" makes the satisfaction issue in a renewal of the self's very youth; cf. the revived-again of Ps 71:20)*.

**III. God's fatherly compassion grounded in knowing our dust-frame (vv.11–14).**
"As high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is his **steadfast love**… as far as the east is from the west, so far does he **remove our transgressions**… As a **father** shows **compassion** (H7355, M05, *racham*) to his children, so the LORD shows compassion to those who **fear** (H3373, M01) him. **For he knows our frame; he remembers that we are dust**" (vv.11–14). Two gem-findings. The inner being's **transgressions are removed to an infinite distance** — "as far as the east is from the west" — the completeness of forgiveness *(stated)*. And, the psalm's tender centre: God's compassion is **fatherly** and **grounded in his *knowing our frailty*** — "he knows our *frame*; he remembers that we are *dust*" *(stated)*. The operation: God's tender regard **factors in the self's weakness** — his compassion turns on an *accounting of how frail the inner being is* (dust), like a father's toward a child *(inferred: "he knows our frame… we are dust" makes the divine compassion rest on a reckoning of human frailty; the same finding as Ps 78:39's "he remembered they were but flesh", here as a father's tenderness)*.

## What Psalm 103 says about the inner being
- **The self can *command its whole inner being to bless* (vv.1–2, 22).** "O my soul… all that is within me" — self-address in the mode of rousing to praise, mustering every faculty; and it governs its own *memory* ("forget not"), guarding against the ingratitude of forgetting.
- **The self can be *renewed / re-youthed* (v.5).** Satisfied with good, the inner being's youth is renewed like the eagle's — vitality restored, not merely maintained.
- **God's compassion is grounded in *knowing our frailty* (vv.13–14).** Fatherly, and turning on his accounting that "we are dust" — the tender regard for weakness (with Ps 78:39). And transgressions are removed to an infinite distance — forgiveness complete.

## Honest notes
- **A cornerstone self-address datum:** "Bless the LORD, O my soul" is the inner being's *self-government in the mode of praise* — mustering the whole interior and its memory (with Ps 42's self-interrogation, 57:8's "awake my glory", 62:5's self-commanded silence). A key exemplar of the dialogical/self-governing inner being.
- **"he knows our frame… we are dust" (v.14)** captured gate-2; the dust-frame compassion read from it — a tender datum (with Ps 78:39, 90:3).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp at v.2 "forget not"; bearer=LORD bleed pervasive incl. the psalmist's soul mis-assigned; intensity *all*; *renewed/frame/dust* gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *soul* (H5315, M47, vv.1,2,22); *forgives* (H5545, M11, v.3); *fear* (H3373, M01, vv.11,13); *shows-compassion* (H7355, M05, v.13). *forget/renewed/frame/dust/remove-transgressions* captured gate-2 — the self-address, renewal, and dust-frame compassion read from these.

# Psalm 104 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 104:1–35 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (14 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 104 is the great **creation hymn** — its body (light, waters, mountains, springs, birds, beasts, moon, sun, sea, Leviathan, vv.2–30) is *God's works*, not the inner being. The inner-being findings are three, and they **bookend and punctuate** the contemplation: the self **rousing itself to bless upon beholding creation** (vv.1, 35); creational **provision aimed at the heart** (v.15); and the **contemplation itself offered as worship** (v.34).

## The reading

**I. The self rousing itself to bless — upon beholding creation (vv.1, 35).**
"**Bless the LORD, O my soul** (H5315, the seat — M47)!… You are clothed with splendor and majesty" (v.1); and at the close, "**Bless the LORD, O my soul**! Praise the LORD!" (v.35). The finding — continuous with Ps 103 — the inner being **commands *itself* to bless God**, and here that self-address **frames a long contemplation of creation** *(stated)*. The operation: the self rouses itself to bless **as the response to *beholding God's works*** — the blessing is *evoked by contemplation*, the whole survey of creation gathered up into the self's "Bless the LORD, O my soul" *(inferred: the same self-address as 103 opens and closes 104, but here it brackets the creation-survey — the beholding of the works is what the self blesses God *for*; contemplation → blessing)*.

**II. Provision aimed at the heart (v.15).**
"…and **wine to gladden** (H8055, M04) the **heart** (H3824, M47) of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to **strengthen** man's heart" (v.15). The finding: God's material provision is **aimed at the inner being** — the wine *gladdens the heart*, the bread *strengthens the heart* *(stated)*. The operation: bodily provision **reaches through to the heart** — creation's gifts are not merely for the body but *gladden and sustain the inner being* *(inferred: "wine to gladden the heart… bread to strengthen the heart" makes the creational provision terminate in the heart's gladness and strength — the outer gift touches the inner life)*.

**III. The contemplation itself offered as worship (v.34).**
"May my **meditation** (H7879, M03) be pleasing to him, for I **rejoice** (H8055, M04) in the LORD" (v.34). The finding: the self **offers its *meditation*** to God and **rejoices** in him *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's *contemplation itself becomes an offering* — the very act of meditating on the works is presented *to God as pleasing*, and issues in rejoicing *(inferred: "may my meditation be pleasing… I rejoice in the LORD" turns the psalm's own act of beholding-creation into worship — the meditation is offered up, and the beholding gladdens the self; cf. Ps 19:14's "meditation of my heart… acceptable")*.

## What Psalm 104 says about the inner being
- **The self rouses itself to bless *upon beholding creation* (vv.1, 35).** The 103-style self-address here brackets a long contemplation — the survey of God's works is gathered into the self's "Bless the LORD, O my soul"; contemplation issues in blessing.
- **Creational provision *reaches the heart* (v.15).** Wine gladdens the heart, bread strengthens it — the outer gift terminates in the inner being's gladness and sustenance, not merely the body.
- **The *contemplation itself* is offered as worship (v.34).** The self presents its meditation to God as pleasing and rejoices in him — the act of beholding-creation becomes an inner offering.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** this is overwhelmingly a creation hymn; ~30 verses describe God's works. The inner-being weight is the bless-bookend (vv.1, 35, continuous with Ps 103), the heart-provision (v.15), and the offered meditation/rejoicing (v.34). I have *not* inflated the creation-body into inner-being content.
- **v.29 "they are dismayed"** (H0926, M01) is the *creatures'* dismay when God hides his face — a datum about creaturely dependence, not distinctively the human inner being; noted, not developed.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed pervasive — incl. the psalmist's "my soul"; intensity *all/very*; much of the creation-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *soul* (H5315, M47, vv.1,35); *gladden/rejoice* (H8055, M04, vv.15,34); *heart* (H3824, M47, v.15); *meditation* (H7879, M03, v.34). The many M22/M25/M42 creation-terms (splendor, beasts, roar, sing) are the arena, not inner-being findings here.

# Psalm 105 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 105:1–45 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (13 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 105 is a **historical recital** — God's covenant faithfulness through Abraham, Joseph, Egypt, and the Exodus (vv.7–45). Most of it narrates *God's dealings*, not the inner being. The inner-being findings are three, concentrated in the opening call and two narrative touch-points: the **rejoicing of the *seeking heart*** and the disposition to seek/remember (vv.3–5); **Joseph *tested by the word* until it came to pass** (vv.18–19); and a **heart *turned* to hate** (v.25).

## The reading

**I. The rejoicing of the seeking heart; the disposition to seek and remember (vv.3–5).**
"Glory in his holy name; **let the hearts** (H3820, the seat — M47) **of those who seek the LORD rejoice** (H8055, M04)! **Seek** (H1875, M41) the LORD and his strength; seek his presence continually! **Remember** (H2142, M41) the wondrous works that he has done" (vv.3–5). The gem-finding: the inner being that **seeks the LORD** is the one whose **heart *rejoices*** — seeking and gladness are joined *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being is summoned to a **posture of *continual seeking and remembering*** — "seek his presence *continually*," "*remember* the wondrous works" — and in that seeking the heart finds its joy *(inferred: "let the hearts of those who seek… rejoice / seek continually / remember" makes seeking-and-remembering the disposition, and gladness its fruit — the heart is glad *in the seeking*, not only in the finding; cf. Ps 27:8 "your face, LORD, do I seek")*.

**II. Joseph tested by the word until it came to pass (vv.18–19).**
"His feet were hurt with fetters; his **neck** (H5315 — *nephesh*, the self/soul — M47) was put in a collar of iron; until what he had said came to pass, **the word of the LORD tested him**" (vv.18–19). The gem-finding: in the fettered, imprisoned Joseph, "the word of the LORD **tested him**" — the *self* held under trial until the promise was fulfilled *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being is **proved / refined by *the word* over a long delay** — the interval between promise and fulfilment is itself the testing, the self held in iron until the word "came to pass" *(inferred: "until what he had said came to pass, the word… tested him" makes the *waiting on the word* the crucible — the self is tested precisely in the gap; cf. the purposed/tested heart of Ps 17:3, here stretched across years)*.

**III. A heart *turned* to hate (v.25).**
"He **turned their hearts** (H3820, M47) **to hate** (H8130, M06) his people, to deal craftily with his servants" (v.25). The finding: the Egyptians' **hearts were *turned* to hate** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's disposition can be **turned** — the heart is here *moved into hate* within God's sovereign ordering of the history *(inferred: "he turned their hearts to hate" presents the heart's hostility as something into which it was *turned*, a datum on the heart's turnability; noted, not developed — the arena is the Exodus narrative, cf. Ex 1's oppression)*.

## What Psalm 105 says about the inner being
- **The *seeking heart rejoices* (vv.3–5).** Seeking and gladness are joined — the inner being summoned to continual seeking and remembering finds its joy *in the seeking*, not only the finding.
- **The self is *tested by the word* across a long delay (vv.18–19).** Joseph, fettered, is proved in the gap between promise and fulfilment — the waiting on the word is itself the crucible.
- **The heart can be *turned* (v.25).** The disposition is turnable — here turned to hate — a datum on the heart's malleability within the ordering of events.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** this is overwhelmingly a historical recital; ~35 verses narrate God's covenant dealings (Abraham, Joseph, plagues, Exodus, wilderness). The recurring "he **remembered** his covenant/promise" (vv.8, 42) is *God's* faithful memory driving the history — the arena, not the human inner being. The inner-being weight is the seeking-heart call (vv.3–5), Joseph's testing (vv.18–19), and the turned heart (v.25).
- **v.19 "the word of the LORD tested him"** is the psalm's richest inner-being touch-point — the long testing of Joseph in the gap; the "neck/soul" of v.18 (H5315) anchors the self under trial.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer bleed — Lord/Israel/Egypt/Aaron; intensity *all*; prohibition over-stamp at vv.14–15 "allowed no one… harm"; much recital gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *hearts* (H3820, M47, vv.3,25); *rejoice/glad* (H8055, M04, vv.3,43); *seek* (H1875, M41, v.4); *remember* (H2142, M41, vv.5,8,42); *neck/soul* (H5315, M47, v.18); *hate* (H8130, M06, v.25); *dread* (H6343, M01, v.38, of Egypt). The many M22/M23/M44 recital-terms (thanks, strength, covenant) are the arena.

# Psalm 106 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 106:1–48 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (7 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The anatomy of a forgetting, craving, impatient heart — set against a God who remembers.** Psalm 106 is a **confession of Israel's rebellions**, and — unlike a bare recital — it is unusually rich on the inner being, because it *diagnoses* the failures. Its findings are operations of a **failing inner life**: the **failure of memory that breeds rebellion** (vv.7, 13); the **collapse of belief into forgetting** (vv.12–13); the **refusal to *wait* for counsel** (v.13); the **wanton craving that tests God — and is answered to its ruin** (vv.14–15); and the **despising of the gift through unbelief** (v.24).

## The reading

**I. The failure of memory that breeds rebellion (vv.7, 13).**
"Our fathers… **did not consider** (H7919, M15) your wondrous works; **they did not remember** (H2142, M41) the abundance of your steadfast love, but **rebelled** by the sea" (v.7); "But they soon **forgot** his works" (v.13). The gem-finding: the root of the rebellion is a **failure of memory** — *not considering, not remembering* God's works and love — *out of which* the rebellion grows *(stated; "did not remember… but rebelled")*. The operation: the inner being's **lapse of memory is the *seedbed of rebellion*** — when the recollection of God's works and steadfast love goes dark, the self turns to revolt; memory-failure *precedes and enables* the sin *(inferred: the "did not remember… but rebelled" structure makes forgetting the *cause*, not a side-effect — the whole psalm reads rebellion as un-remembering; cf. Ps 78:11 "they forgot his works")*.

**II. The collapse of belief into forgetting (vv.12–13).**
"Then they **believed** (H0539, M13) his words; they sang his praise. **But they soon forgot** his works" (vv.12–13). The gem-finding: faith and praise are **real but short-lived** — belief and song at the Red Sea collapse into forgetting *"soon"* after *(stated)*. The operation: the aroused inner being is **transient** — a genuine belief-and-praise that does not *hold*, dissolving almost at once into forgetfulness *(inferred: "they believed… they sang… but they soon forgot" names the tragic brevity of the roused heart — the problem is not the absence of faith but its *failure to endure*; cf. the stony ground of later Scripture, and Ps 78:36–37 "their heart was not steadfast")*.

**III. The refusal to *wait* for counsel (v.13).**
"they **did not wait** (H2442, M18) for his counsel" (v.13). The finding: the inner being **would not *wait*** for God's counsel *(stated)*. The operation: **impatience** — the self runs *ahead* of God's guidance, unwilling to hold still for the counsel that would order its steps *(inferred: "did not wait for his counsel" makes the failure a refusal to *wait* — the impatient heart that will not defer to God's timing or direction; the negative of the wait-on-the-LORD of Ps 27:14, 40:1)*.

**IV. The wanton craving that tests God — answered to its own ruin (vv.14–15).**
"But they had a **wanton craving** (H8378 / H0183, M28) in the wilderness, and **put God to the test**… he **gave them what they asked**, but sent a **wasting** disease among them" (vv.14–15). The gem-finding: the inner being's **craving** was so intense it **tested God** — *demanding* — and the answer is terrible: *the craving was granted, and it hollowed them out* ("he gave them what they asked, but sent a wasting disease") *(stated)*. The operation: **disordered craving is self-destructive even when satisfied** — the appetite that demands and tests God is *answered*, but the granting itself becomes the judgment, the fulfilled craving wasting the very self that craved *(inferred: "he gave them what they asked, but sent a wasting" welds the *granting* to the *wasting* — the got-what-it-wanted craving is the ruin; cf. Ps 78:29–31, the KJV "leanness into their soul")*.

**V. Despising the gift through unbelief (v.24).**
"Then they **despised the pleasant** (H2532, M28) land, **having no faith** (H0539, M13) in his promise" (v.24). The finding: the inner being **despised the good gift** — the pleasant land — *because it had no faith* in the promise *(stated)*. The operation: **unbelief turns the good gift *contemptible*** — the self, not trusting the promise, *despises* the very thing promised; faith and desire are linked, and where faith fails, the desirable becomes despised *(inferred: "despised the pleasant land, having no faith" makes the unbelief the ground of the contempt — the heart that will not trust cannot value the gift; cf. Num 14)*.

## What Psalm 106 says about the inner being
- **Forgetting is the *seedbed of rebellion* (vv.7, 13).** When the memory of God's works and steadfast love goes dark, the self turns to revolt — the psalm reads rebellion as fundamentally *un-remembering*.
- **The roused inner being is *transient* (vv.12–13).** Belief and praise are real but do not hold — they collapse "soon" into forgetting; the problem is faith's *failure to endure*, not its absence.
- **Impatience refuses to *wait* for counsel (v.13).** The self runs ahead of God's guidance, unwilling to hold still for the counsel that would order its steps.
- **Disordered craving is *self-destructive even when satisfied* (vv.14–15).** The appetite that demands and tests God is answered — and the granting itself becomes the judgment; the fulfilled craving wastes the craver.
- **Unbelief turns the good gift *contemptible* (v.24).** The heart that will not trust the promise despises the very thing promised — faith and valuing are linked.

## Honest notes
- **This closing psalm is *rich*, not thin** — because it is a *diagnostic* confession (not a bare recital like 105). It names the inner mechanisms of failure: un-remembering, transient faith, impatience, craving, unbelief. A cornerstone catalogue of the *failing* inner being (the shadow-side counterpart to the seeking/blessing heart of 103–105).
- **The frame — a God who remembers against a people who forget:** the human failure is un-remembering (vv.7, 13, 21); the resolution is that "he **remembered** his covenant, and relented according to the abundance of his steadfast love" (v.45). The contrast (human forgetting vs divine remembering) is the psalm's architecture — God's memory is the arena/hope against which the inner-being findings are set.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (prohibition over-stamp pervasive across the "did not…" confessions vv.7,13,24,25; bearer bleed — Egypt/Aaron/Phinehas/Ham mis-assigned; intensity *all*; much recital gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *consider* (H7919, M15, v.7); *remember/forgot* (H2142, M41, vv.7,13); *believed/faith* (H0539, M13, vv.12,24); *wait* (H2442, M18, v.13); *wanton/craving* (H8378/H0183, M28, v.14); *pleasant* (H2532, M28, v.24); *jealous/wrath/provoked/angered* (M02, of the people/God). The many M22/M10/M26 recital-terms (praise, sinned, righteousness) frame the confession.

# Psalm 107 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 107:1–43 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (8 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The soul at the end of itself cries out and is heard — four times over. Book V opens.** Psalm 107 is built on a fourfold refrain: four portraits of the self *in extremity*, each turning on "**Then they cried to the LORD in their trouble, and he delivered them**" (vv.6, 13, 19, 28). Its findings are operations of the **inner being pressed to its limit** — the *fainting/longing* soul (vv.5, 9), the *bowed-down* heart (v.12), the soul that *loathes food* at death's gate (v.18), the *melting, wits'-end* self in the storm (vv.26–27) — and the single move that answers each: **the cry that is heard**.

## The reading

**I. The cry from extremity that is heard — the fourfold refrain (vv.6, 13, 19, 28).**
Four times: "**Then they cried** (H2199, *zaaq*) **to the LORD in their trouble, and he delivered them** from their distress" (vv.6, 13, 19, 28). The gem-finding: the one operation that recurs at every depth is the **cry of the self at the end of itself** — and it is *always heard* *(stated)*. The operation: **extremity drives the inner being to cry out, and the cry is the hinge of deliverance** — wanderer, prisoner, fool, sailor all reach the point where nothing is left *but* to cry, and *that* cry turns the whole vignette *(inferred: the refrain makes the cry-from-the-bottom the universal inner-being move — not strength or merit but the honest cry of the undone self; cf. Ps 34:6 "this poor man cried")*.

**II. The fainting, longing soul satisfied (vv.5, 9).**
"hungry and thirsty, their **soul** (H5315, M47) **fainted** within them" (v.5)… "For he **satisfies** the **longing** soul, and the hungry soul he **fills** with good things" (v.9). The gem-finding: the *longing* soul — fainting with hunger and thirst — is **satisfied and filled** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being has a **capacity of *longing* that only God fills** — the fainting, craving soul is not rebuked but *satisfied*, its emptiness met with good *(inferred: "he satisfies the longing soul… fills the hungry soul with good" makes the soul's longing the very thing God meets; the appetite is answered, not shamed — contrast the disordered craving of Ps 106:15; here the honest longing is filled)*.

**III. The bowed-down heart; the soul that loathes food at death's gate (vv.12, 18).**
"So he **bowed** their **hearts** (H3820, M47) **down** (H3665) with hard labor; they fell down, with none to help" (v.12); and of the fools in their affliction, "their **soul loathed** (H8581, M06) any kind of food, and they drew near to the gates of death" (v.18). The finding: affliction **bows the heart down** and drives the soul to **loathe food** — the body's sustenance made repellent by inner distress *(stated)*. The operation: extremity **reaches into the inner being's very *appetites*** — the heart is pressed low, and the soul's aversion to food marks a self so afflicted it turns from life itself, at the gates of death *(inferred: "their soul loathed any food… near the gates of death" shows distress reaching down into appetite — the afflicted self loses even the will to eat; cf. Ps 102:4 "I forget to eat my bread")*.

**IV. The melting, wits'-end self in the storm (vv.26–27, 30).**
"They mounted up to heaven; they went down to the depths; their **courage** (H5315, *nephesh* — the self/soul — M47) **melted away** in their evil plight; they **reeled and staggered** like drunken men and were **at their wits' end**" (vv.26–27); then, delivered, "they were **glad** (H8055, M04) that the waters were quiet, and he brought them to their **desired** (H2656) haven" (v.30). The gem-finding: the storm-tossed self's **very courage *melts*** — the inner being unstrung, reeling, *at its wits' end* — and after the cry, made **glad** at the hushed sea, brought to its *desired* haven *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being can be **dissolved past its own competence** — "at their wits' end," every inner resource exhausted — and the cry from *that* place is answered with stillness and gladness *(inferred: "their courage melted… at their wits' end" names the total exhaustion of the self's coping, the precise point where the cry becomes the only move; the "glad… desired haven" is the inner rest on the far side; cf. Ps 46:10 the stilled)*.

## What Psalm 107 says about the inner being
- **The *cry from the bottom* is the universal move — and it is heard (vv.6, 13, 19, 28).** At every depth the one operation left to the undone self is the honest cry, and that cry is the hinge of deliverance; not strength or merit but the cry of the end-of-itself self.
- **The soul's *longing* is met, not shamed (vv.5, 9).** The fainting, hungry soul is satisfied and filled with good — the inner being's honest appetite answered by God.
- **Affliction reaches into the *appetites* (vv.12, 18).** The heart is bowed down; the soul loathes food at death's gate — distress penetrates to where the self turns from life itself.
- **The self can be *dissolved past its own competence* (vv.26–27).** Courage melts, the self reels "at its wits' end" — and from that exhaustion the cry is answered with stillness and gladness, brought to its desired haven.

## Honest notes
- **A coherent inner-being architecture:** four states of the self at its limit (fainting / bowed / loathing / melting), each resolved by the *same* cry-and-deliverance. The psalm is practically a *taxonomy of the inner being in extremity* — a strong Book-V-opening datum, and it closes urging the wise to "consider the steadfast love of the LORD" (v.43).
- **"soul/courage" (H5315)** carries much of the weight (vv.5, 9, 18, 26) — the *nephesh* as the self that faints, longs, loathes, and melts; a rich cluster of soul-language.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed; intensity *all/very*; some vignette-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *soul/courage* (H5315, M47, vv.5,9,18,26); *cried* (H2199, M42, vv.6,13,19,28); *hearts / bowed-down* (H3820/H3665, M47/M09, v.12); *loathed* (H8581, M06, v.18); *glad* (H8055, M04, v.30); *desired* (H2656, M04, v.30); *affliction* (H6040, M24, v.10). The M22 thanks-terms frame the four deliverances.

# Psalm 108 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 108:1–13 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 108 is a **composite** — its two halves are lifted from Ps 57:7–11 and Ps 60:5–12. The back half (vv.6–13) is the national petition/military plea of Ps 60 (the arena). The inner-being findings are concentrated in the opening (vv.1–3): the **steadfast/fixed heart** and the **self rousing its whole being to praise — waking the dawn itself**.

## The reading

**I. The steadfast/fixed heart, ready to praise (v.1).**
"My **heart** (H3820, the seat — M47) is **steadfast**, O God! I will sing and make melody with **all my being** (H3519 — *kabod*, glory/the honoured self)!" (v.1). The gem-finding (continuous with Ps 57:7): the inner being is **settled, fixed** — a *steadfast heart* — and *out of that settledness* it praises with its *whole self* *(stated)*. The operation: the heart's **fixed/anchored condition is the ground of wholehearted praise** — not a scattered or divided heart but a *settled* one, from which the song rises with "all my being" *(inferred: "my heart is steadfast… I will sing with all my being" makes the steadiness the precondition — the fixed heart can give itself *entire* to praise; cf. Ps 57:7, 112:7 "his heart is firm")*.

**II. Rousing the whole being to praise — waking the dawn (vv.1–2).**
"…I will sing and make melody with **all my being**! **Awake**, O harp and lyre! **I will awake** (H5782) **the dawn**!" (vv.1–2). The gem-finding: the self **musters its "glory" (its whole inner being) for praise** and is so eager it will **wake the dawn** — rouse the very morning to worship *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **stirs *itself* (and even the day) into praise** — a self-rousing so ardent it precedes and summons the dawn, the whole self and its world called up to worship *(inferred: "with all my being… I will awake the dawn" makes the praise an act of self-arousal that overflows onto creation — the eager self will not wait for the morning but *wakes* it; cf. Ps 57:8, 103:1's "all that is within me")*.

## What Psalm 108 says about the inner being
- **The *steadfast/fixed heart* is the ground of wholehearted praise (v.1).** A settled, anchored heart — not scattered or divided — can give itself *entire* to worship, singing "with all my being."
- **The self *rouses its whole being (and the dawn) to praise* (vv.1–2).** A self-arousal so ardent it summons the very morning — the inner being stirring itself, and its world, up to worship.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** a composite psalm; the second half (vv.6–13, "give us help against the foe… with God we shall do valiantly") is the national/military petition of Ps 60 — the arena, not the inner being. The inner-being weight is the steadfast heart and the self-rousing praise (vv.1–3), continuous with Ps 57.
- **Provenance note:** because 108 reuses 57 and 60, its inner-being findings are *not new* to the corpus — they re-attest the steadfast heart (57:7) and the awaking self (57:8). Recorded as re-attestation, not fresh discovery.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD/Ephraim bleed; intensity *all*; military-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *heart* (H3820, M47, v.1); *being/glory* (H3519, M22, vv.1,5); *make melody / sing praises* (H2167, M42, vv.1,3); *awake* (H5782, M25, v.2); *faithfulness* (H0571, M13, v.4). The M23 military-terms (valiantly, helmet) are the arena.

# Psalm 109 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 109:1–31 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (6 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The wronged self that will not retaliate but *gives itself to prayer*; the stricken heart.** Psalm 109 is the great imprecatory psalm — a long, terrible curse (vv.6–20). But its *inner-being* findings are not the curse-content; they are the operations of the **wronged self**: love repaid with hatred, met by **giving oneself to prayer** rather than revenge (vv.4–5); the **poor, needy, *stricken* heart** (v.22); and the self **physically wasted by grief and scorn** (vv.23–25).

## The reading

**I. Love repaid with hatred — met by *giving oneself to prayer* (vv.4–5).**
"In return for my **love** (H0160, M05) they accuse me, but **I give myself to prayer**. So they reward me evil for good, and **hatred** (H8135, M06) for my love" (vv.4–5). The gem-finding: to being *accused in return for love*, the self's response is not counter-attack but **prayer** — Hebrew literally "I *am* prayer" *(stated)*. The operation: the wronged inner being **converts its grievance into *prayer*** — where love has been repaid with hatred, the self does not retaliate in kind but *turns the whole matter Godward*, becoming prayer itself *(inferred: "in return for my love they accuse… but I give myself to prayer" makes the self's move a *handing-over to God* rather than revenge — the injustice is prayed, not avenged; this is the frame that makes even the fierce imprecation an act committed to God's court, cf. Rom 12:19, Ps 35:13)*.

**II. The poor, needy, *stricken* heart (v.22).**
"For I am **poor and needy**, and my **heart** (H3820, M47) is **stricken** (H2490 — pierced/wounded) within me" (v.22). The gem-finding: the self names itself *poor and needy*, its **heart *wounded within*** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being under sustained assault is **pierced at its core** — not merely troubled but *wounded within*, a heart stricken through *(inferred: "my heart is stricken within me" locates the injury *inside* — the persecution has reached the heart itself; the self's poverty/neediness is the honest confession of its emptied condition, the very ground on which it appeals; cf. Ps 34:18 "the brokenhearted," 69:20 "reproach has broken my heart")*.

**III. The self physically wasted by grief and scorn (vv.23–25).**
"I am gone like a **shadow** at evening; I am **shaken off** like a locust. My **knees are weak** through fasting; my **body** (H1320, the flesh — M47) has become **gaunt**… I am an object of **scorn** (H2781, M06) to my accusers; when they see me, they **wag their heads**" (vv.23–25). The finding: grief has **wasted the body** — knees weak, flesh gaunt, the self a fading shadow — and the scorn is *felt*, the wagging heads registering as reproach *(stated)*. The operation: inner distress **writes itself on the body** and the self **absorbs the contempt of others** — the fasting-worn flesh and the felt scorn are the outward form of a self ground down *(inferred: "knees weak… body gaunt… an object of scorn… they wag their heads" shows the affliction embodied and the mockery internalised — the self diminished to a shadow, cf. Ps 102:3–11, 22:6–7)*.

## What Psalm 109 says about the inner being
- **The wronged self *becomes prayer* rather than retaliating (vv.4–5).** Love repaid with hatred is met not by counter-attack but by handing the whole matter to God — the self *is* prayer; the grievance is committed to God's court, not avenged in kind.
- **The persecuted heart is *stricken within* (v.22).** The assault reaches the core — a heart *pierced/wounded* inside; the self's confessed poverty and neediness is the honest ground of its appeal.
- **Inner distress *writes itself on the body* and *absorbs others' scorn* (vv.23–25).** Grief wastes the flesh gaunt, the self fades like a shadow, and the mockery is felt as reproach — affliction embodied and contempt internalised.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty — the imprecation:** the long curse (vv.6–20, "may his days be few… may his children be fatherless") is aimed at the enemy; read morally it is *what the wronged self prays*, and its inner-being significance is precisely that — the rage is **committed to God in prayer** (v.4's frame), not enacted by the self's own hand. I have *not* treated the curse-content as inner-being findings; the finding is the self's recourse to prayer.
- **v.31 "he stands at the right hand of the needy one"** resolves the psalm — the answered hope of the stricken self; the arena of the plea.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=David/LORD bleed; prohibition over-stamp at vv.12–16 "no one to… did not remember"; intensity *very/many*; curse-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *love* (H0160, M05, vv.4,5); *hate/hatred/scorn* (H8135/H2781, M06, vv.3,5,25); *heart* (H3820, M47, v.22); *body/flesh* (H1320, M47, v.24); *brokenhearted* (H3512, M20, v.16); *put-to-shame/dishonor/shame* (H0954/H3639/H1322, M07, vv.28–29). The M10/M14/M26 terms (wicked, deceitful, condemn) frame the accusation.

# Psalm 110 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 110:1–7 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 110 is the **royal / priest-king enthronement** psalm ("The LORD says to my Lord, Sit at my right hand"). It is almost wholly about the *enthroned King-Priest* and his victory (the arena) — not the human inner being. There is **one** inner-being touch-point: the people's **willing self-offering** (v.3).

## The reading

**I. The willing self-offering of the people (v.3).**
"Your people will **offer themselves freely** (H5071 — *nedabot*, freewill offerings) on the day of your power, in holy garments" (v.3). The finding: on the day of the King's power, the people **give themselves *freely* / *willingly*** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's **glad, un-coerced *willingness*** — the self offered *freely*, not conscripted; a volunteered devotion *(inferred: "offer themselves freely" (nedabot = freewill) names a willing inner disposition — the people give *themselves*, and give *gladly*; the offering is of the will, cf. the "willing heart" of Ex 35:5, Ps 54:6 "with a freewill offering I will sacrifice")*.

## What Psalm 110 says about the inner being
- **The self can be *offered freely / willingly* (v.3).** A glad, un-coerced devotion — the people give *themselves*, and give *gladly*; the offering is of the will, not conscription.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** this is overwhelmingly a royal/messianic enthronement psalm — the right hand, the sceptre, the priest "after the order of Melchizedek," the shattering of kings (vv.1–2, 4–7) are all about the *King-Priest*, the arena. The only inner-being weight is the willing self-offering of v.3. I have *not* inflated the enthronement-content into inner-being findings.
- **v.4 "will not change his mind"** (H5162, *nacham*) is *God's* unwavering oath — his constancy, not a human inner-being operation; noted as arena.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=Zion/LORD bleed; royal-imagery gate-2) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** *offer-freely* (H5071, v.3, the sole inner-being datum); the M23 power/rule terms and M22 holy/garments are the enthronement arena; *mind* (H5162, M11, v.4) is God's constancy.

# Psalm 111 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 111:1–10 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Whole-hearted thanks; the works *studied by those who delight*; the fear of the LORD as *the beginning of wisdom*.** Psalm 111 is an acrostic hymn to God's works and character (the arena). Its inner-being findings are three, framing that praise: **thanks with the *whole heart*** (v.1); the works **studied by all who *delight* in them** (v.2); and the cornerstone — **the fear of the LORD is *the beginning of wisdom*** (v.10).

## The reading

**I. Thanks with the whole heart (v.1).**
"Praise the LORD! I will give thanks to the LORD with my **whole heart** (H3824, the seat — M47), in the company of the upright" (v.1). The finding: the thanksgiving is ***whole-hearted*** — the entire heart engaged, nothing withheld *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being praises **undividedly** — "whole heart" naming a self *gathered entire* into the thanks, not partial or distracted *(inferred: "with my whole heart" makes the thanks total — the undivided heart, cf. Ps 9:1, 138:1; the wholeness is itself the inner-being datum)*.

**II. The works *studied by those who delight* in them (v.2).**
"Great are the works of the LORD, **studied** (H1875 — *darash*, sought out) by all who **delight** (H2656, M04) in them" (v.2). The gem-finding: God's works are *sought out / studied* — and specifically by those who **delight** in them *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's **delight *drives inquiry*** — those who take pleasure in God's works *search them out*; delight and study are joined, the loved thing pondered *(inferred: "studied by all who delight in them" links affection to investigation — the self that delights *seeks out*; the works are searched *because* they are loved; cf. Ps 1:2 "his delight… on his law he meditates", 119:2 "seek him with their whole heart")*.

**III. The fear of the LORD — *the beginning of wisdom* (v.10).**
"The **fear** (H3373, M01) of the LORD is the **beginning of wisdom**; all those who practice it have a **good understanding**. His praise endures forever!" (v.10). The gem-finding — a cornerstone of the whole study: **wisdom *begins* with the fear of the LORD** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's **first and foundational orientation is reverent fear** — wisdom is not first intellect but a *right awe*, and out of that fear grows *good understanding*; the fear is the *starting-point*, the root from which the wise inner life develops *(inferred: "the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom… all who practice it have good understanding" makes reverent fear the foundation and *practice* the path — wisdom is a posture before it is knowledge; the master-datum linking M01 fear and M15 wisdom, cf. Prov 9:10, Ps 25:12,14, 34:11)*.

## What Psalm 111 says about the inner being
- **Thanks is *whole-hearted* (v.1).** The entire heart engaged, undivided — the self gathered *entire* into the praise, nothing withheld.
- **Delight *drives study* (v.2).** Those who delight in God's works *seek them out* — affection and inquiry joined; the loved thing is searched out *because* it is loved.
- **The fear of the LORD is *the beginning of wisdom* (v.10).** The inner being's first, foundational orientation is reverent awe — wisdom is a *posture* before it is knowledge, and good understanding grows from *practising* that fear. A master-datum linking fear and wisdom.

## Honest notes
- **v.10 is a cornerstone** — the hinge-verse of the biblical wisdom tradition, here in the Psalter. It roots the whole M15 (wisdom) cluster in M01 (fear): the inner being becomes wise not by cleverness but by *reverent fear practised*. A key cross-cluster datum for the study (with Ps 25, 34, 112:1, Prov 1:7, 9:10).
- **Scope honesty:** most of the psalm (vv.2–9) describes God's works and character — great, majestic, gracious, faithful, redeeming (the arena). The inner-being weight is vv.1, 2, 10.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed pervasive — incl. the psalmist's "whole heart"; intensity *all*; God's-works terms gate-1 but arena) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *heart* (H3824, M47, v.1); *studied* (H1875, M41, v.2); *delight* (H2656, M04, v.2); *fear* (H3373, M01, v.10). The M22/M26/M39 terms (praise, righteousness, gracious) describe God — the arena.
