# Psalm 146 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 146:1–10 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Trust redirected from mortal man to the enduring God. The final Hallel opens.** Psalm 146 begins the five closing praise-psalms. Its inner-being finding: the **deliberate redirection of trust/hope — away from mortal princes (whose plans perish) to the God whose help endures** (vv.3–5).

## The reading

**I. Trust redirected from mortal man to the enduring God (vv.3–5).**
"**Put not your trust in princes**, in a son of man, in whom there is **no salvation**. When his **breath departs**, he returns to the earth; on that very day his **plans perish**. **Blessed is he whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the LORD** his God" (vv.3–5). The gem-finding: the self is directed **not to trust mortal man** — because he *dies* and his plans *perish with him* — but to place its **hope in the LORD** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being **redirects its trust by *reasoning from mortality*** — it *weighs* where to lean, sees that the strongest human helper is *breath that departs*, and so *relocates* its hope in the God who endures; trust as a *reasoned choice* informed by the transience of every human refuge *(inferred: "put not your trust in princes… his plans perish… blessed is he whose hope is in the LORD" is the self *choosing* its ground by reckoning that man is mortal and God is not — the deliberate redirection of 118:8–9, here argued from death; misplaced trust exposed by the grave, right trust anchored in the enduring God; cf. Ps 118:8, 62:9, 115:9–11)*.

## What Psalm 146 says about the inner being
- **Trust is *redirected by reasoning from mortality* (vv.3–5).** The self weighs where to lean, sees that even princes are "breath that departs" whose plans perish, and *relocates* its hope in the enduring God — trust as a reasoned choice informed by the transience of every human refuge.

## Honest notes
- **A trust-redirection datum** (re-attesting and deepening 118:8–9): here the choice is *argued from death* — the mortality of the human helper is the reason to place hope elsewhere (with 62:9, 115:9–11). Foregrounded.
- **Scope honesty:** the bulk of the psalm (vv.6–10 — God who made heaven/earth, keeps faith, executes justice, feeds the hungry, frees prisoners, opens blind eyes, lifts the bowed-down, loves the righteous, reigns forever) is *God's character and action* (the arena that *grounds* the redirected hope). The inner-being weight is the trust-choice of vv.3–5. v.8's "lifts up those who are bowed down" is God's action, its inner-being fruit relief.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed; prohibition at v.3 "put not"; God's-works terms gate-1 but arena) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *trust* (H0982, M19, v.3); *hope* (H7664, M18, v.5); *praise* (M22, vv.1–2). The God's-works terms (vv.6–10) are the arena grounding the hope.

# Psalm 147 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 147:1–20 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (5 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **The brokenhearted healed; God's pleasure in the *fearing, hoping* heart, not in strength.** Psalm 147 is a praise-psalm on God's care and power. Its inner-being findings: the **brokenhearted *healed* and their wounds bound** (v.3); and the searching datum that **God's pleasure is in the *fearing, hoping* heart — not in human strength** (vv.10–11).

## The reading

**I. The brokenhearted healed (v.3).**
"He **heals the brokenhearted** (H3820, M47) and **binds up their wounds**" (v.3). The gem-finding: God's care reaches the *broken heart* — he *heals* it and *binds up* its wounds *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's ***wounds are tended*** — the broken heart is not left to bleed but *bound up*, the healing directed precisely at the *inner* injury; God as physician of the wounded self *(inferred: "he heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds" makes the *inner* wound the object of God's tender repair — the shattered heart mended, the hurt bound like a physician dressing a wound; God's nearness to the broken, cf. Ps 34:18, 51:17, Isa 61:1)*.

**II. God's pleasure in the *fearing, hoping* heart, not in strength (vv.10–11).**
"His **delight is not in the strength of the horse**, nor his pleasure in the legs of a man, but the LORD **takes pleasure in those who fear** (H3373, M01) him, in those who **hope** (H3176, M18) in his steadfast love" (vv.10–11). The gem-finding: what *pleases* God is **not power** (horse, man's legs) but the heart that **fears him and hopes in his steadfast love** *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being learns that **its *reverent fear and hope*, not its strength, are what *delight* God** — the self's value before God lies not in might or capability but in the *inward* posture of fear-and-hope; the fearing, hoping heart is the thing God *takes pleasure in* *(inferred: "his delight is not in the strength of the horse… but in those who fear him, who hope in his steadfast love" contrasts *external power* with the *inner posture* and locates God's pleasure entirely in the latter — the inner being's worth is its fear and hope, not its force; a searching datum on what God actually values in the self, cf. Ps 33:16–18, 1 Sam 16:7, Mic 6:8)*.

## What Psalm 147 says about the inner being
- **The *brokenhearted* are *healed* (v.3).** God's care reaches the inner wound — the shattered heart mended, its hurt bound up like a physician dressing a wound; the broken self not left to bleed.
- **God's pleasure is in the *fearing, hoping* heart, not in strength (vv.10–11).** What delights God is not power (horse, man's legs) but the inward posture of reverent fear and hope in his steadfast love — the inner being's worth lies in its fear and hope, not its force.

## Honest notes
- **A what-God-values datum:** vv.10–11 is a searching inner-being finding — God's pleasure located entirely in the *inner* posture (fear + hope), explicitly *over against* external strength (with 33:16–18, 1 Sam 16:7). The self's value is its fearing-hoping heart. Foregrounded, alongside the healed brokenhearted (v.3).
- **Scope honesty:** most of the psalm (vv.2, 4–9, 12–20 — God builds Jerusalem, counts the stars, covers the heavens with clouds, gives snow and frost, sends his word) is *God's power and providence* (the arena). The inner-being weight is v.3 and vv.10–11.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed pervasive; prohibition at v.10 "not in"; weather/creation-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *brokenhearted* (H3820, M47, v.3); *fear* (H3373, M01, v.11); *hope* (H3176, M18, v.11); *pleasant* (v.1). The building/stars/weather terms are the providence arena.

# Psalm 148 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 148:1–14 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (2 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 148 is the great cosmic doxology — every order of creation (angels, sun, moon, stars, sea creatures, weather, mountains, trees, beasts, kings, peoples, young and old) summoned to praise the LORD. It is a *universal call to praise* (the arena of worship). It yields **no distinct inner-being finding**; recorded honestly as an arena-only summons.

## The reading

**I. The universal summons to praise (throughout).**
"Praise the LORD from the heavens… Praise him, sun and moon… Praise the LORD from the earth… kings of the earth and all peoples… Young men and maidens together, old men and children! Let them praise the name of the LORD" (vv.1–13). The finding (arena): all creation, human and non-human, is called to praise — the human "young and old" taking their place in the cosmic chorus *(stated)*. There is no observed inner-being *operation* — the psalm *commands* praise across the whole created order; the only human-relevant note is that the self joins the *entire creation* in worship, one voice among all *(inferred, cautious: to read an inner-being process into a universal doxology would be to import; the transferable hint is only that the inner being's praise is *part of a cosmic whole* — the self takes its place in creation's chorus, not a self-movement the text describes)*.

## What Psalm 148 says about the inner being
- **(Arena-only) No distinct inner-being finding.** The psalm summons all creation — including "young and old" — to praise; the only human-relevant note is that the self's worship joins the *whole created order's*, one voice among all. Not an inner-being operation the text describes.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** an arena-only cosmic doxology (with Ps 117, 114, 134, 150) — I record no inner-being finding rather than manufacture one from a universal call to praise. The self's place *within* creation's chorus is noted, no more.
- **v.14 "the people… who are near to him"** is a positional/covenant note (nearness to God), not a described inner-being operation.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed pervasive; creation-catalogue gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.

# Psalm 149 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 149:1–9 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter (2 vv. backfilled with the fixed full-text logic). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Joy in God that overflows to the private hours; the humble adorned.** Psalm 149 is a praise-psalm of the godly. Its inner-being findings: **gladness in God that exults even *on the bed*** (vv.2, 5); and God's **pleasure in his people, *adorning the humble*** with salvation (v.4).

## The reading

**I. Joy in God overflowing to the private hours (vv.2, 5).**
"Let Israel be **glad** (H8055, M04) in his **Maker**; let the children of Zion **rejoice** in their King!… Let the godly **exult** in glory; let them **sing for joy on their beds**" (vv.2, 5). The gem-finding: the joy in God is so full it **sings even *on their beds*** — in the private, resting, night hours *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's gladness in God **overflows past public worship into the *intimate and hidden*** — "on their beds" locates the joy where no one sees, at rest, in the night; a delight that does not need an audience but sings in solitude *(inferred: "let them sing for joy on their beds" carries the joy into the private place — the self so glad in its Maker that it exults even lying down, alone; the gladness has soaked through to the intimate hours, cf. Ps 42:8 "at night his song is with me", 63:6 "on my bed")*.

**II. God's pleasure in his people; the humble adorned (v.4).**
"For the LORD **takes pleasure in his people**; he **adorns the humble** (H6035, M24) with **salvation**" (v.4). The gem-finding: God *delights* in his people and **beautifies the humble** with salvation *(stated)*. The operation: the inner being's ***humility* is what God *adorns*** — the lowly self is not despised but *decorated / crowned* with salvation; God's pleasure rests on his people, and his beautifying grace falls on *humility* *(inferred: "he adorns the humble with salvation" makes the humble inner being the object of God's *beautifying* — the self that is lowly is clothed with the ornament of salvation; humility is the condition God delights to dignify, cf. Ps 147:11, 138:6, 1 Pet 5:5 "God… gives grace to the humble")*.

## What Psalm 149 says about the inner being
- **Joy in God *overflows to the private hours* (vv.2, 5).** So full is the gladness in its Maker that the self sings "on their beds" — the joy soaked through past public worship into the intimate, resting, night hours; delight that needs no audience.
- **God *adorns the humble* (v.4).** The lowly self is not despised but *beautified* — clothed with salvation; humility is the condition God delights to dignify, his pleasure resting on his people.

## Honest notes
- **A private-joy datum:** "sing for joy on their beds" (v.5) — gladness that reaches the solitary, unwitnessed hours (with 42:8, 63:6); the joy is real enough to sing where no one sees. And the humble *adorned* (v.4) joins the humility-thread (147:11, 138:6).
- **Scope honesty:** the militant close (vv.6–9 — the two-edged sword, executing judgment on the nations) is the arena of vindication/judgment, not an inner-being operation; noted, not developed. The inner-being weight is the overflowing joy (vv.2, 5) and the adorned humble (v.4).
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD/Israel bleed; sword/judgment-imagery gate-2; backfilled vv. now full-text) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked, inner-being-relevant):** *glad/rejoice/exult* (H8055, M04, vv.2,5); *humble* (H6035, M24, v.4). The sword/judgment terms (vv.6–9) are the arena.

# Psalm 150 — what it tells us about the inner being (Phase-2 chapter reading)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Psa 150:1–6 (chapter-driven poetic build; roles sanity-checked; aheb-fix build). Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**, God-relation as arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Scope honesty up front:** Psalm 150 is the Psalter's closing doxology — a tenfold "Praise him" summoning every instrument and "everything that has breath" to praise. It is *pure worship-summons* (the arena). It yields **no distinct inner-being finding**; but as the **capstone of the whole Psalter**, it carries a structural note worth recording (below).

## The reading

**I. The final summons — everything that has breath (vv.1–6).**
"Praise the LORD! Praise God in his sanctuary… Praise him for his **mighty deeds**… **Let everything that has breath praise the LORD!**" (vv.1–6). The finding (arena): the Psalter ends in *unqualified praise* — every instrument, every breathing creature called to worship *(stated)*. There is no observed inner-being *operation*; the psalm is doxology *(inferred, cautious: to read a self-movement into a six-verse summons would be to import)*. **The one honest structural note:** the entire Psalter — which has traversed *every* state of the inner being (fear, grief, guilt, longing, waiting, trust, doubt, rage, joy) across 150 psalms — resolves here into *sheer praise*; the inner being's long journey through its whole range *arrives* at "let everything that has breath praise the LORD." That *terminus* is the datum: praise is where the whole inner life is bound, at last, to land *(inferred, structural: the Psalter's editors close the book on praise after every darker note has been sounded — the movement of the whole collection is *toward* praise; the inner being's varied journey has this as its endpoint, cf. the Psalter's five-book doxological seams, 41:13, 72:19, 89:52, 106:48)*.

## What Psalm 150 says about the inner being
- **(Arena-only, with a structural note) No distinct inner-being finding.** The psalm is pure praise-summons. But as the Psalter's capstone it marks the *terminus* of the inner being's whole journey: after every state — fear, grief, guilt, longing, waiting, trust, rage, joy — the collection resolves into unqualified praise. Praise is where the whole inner life is, at last, bound to land.

## Honest notes
- **Scope honesty:** an arena-only doxology (with Ps 148, 117, 134) — I record no inner-being *operation* rather than manufacture one from a summons. The *structural* observation (the Psalter arriving at praise after traversing the full inner-being range) is offered as a reading of the collection's shape, not as a datum extracted from these six verses alone.
- **A fitting close to the chapter-run:** the inner-being journey this project has traced through all 150 psalms — the fearing, grieving, trusting, longing, waiting, rejoicing self — ends where the Psalter ends: in praise. Noted for the eventual cross-chapter synthesis.
- **Systemic Phase-1 residuals** (bearer=LORD bleed; instrument-catalogue gate-2) — per the tracker's *Known Phase-1 residuals*; not re-detailed.
- **Characteristics (sanity-checked):** the terms are the praise-summons and instrument-catalogue (arena); no human inner-being operation observed — only the structural terminus-of-the-Psalter note.

# Proverbs 1 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** the `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals for Pro 1:1–33, read **per segmentation unit** (`segment_unit`, provenance `proverbs-segmentation-v1-20260703`). Complete chapter (3 vv. backfilled). Lexicals only; cited; grounded; inferences tagged *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**; wisdom/God-relation is the arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Method (unit meaning-synthesis):** each unit is read for its inner-being meaning, and that reading **reads back and validates the Phase-1 lexical** — checking the roles, the **pairs** (bearer / manner / coupling) and flags for sensibility, and **isolating hidden or less-obvious characteristics** the provisional segmentation did not name. Validation catches (bearer=LORD bleed; prohibition over-stamp) are logged per unit, not re-derived.

---

## PRO-01-A · Prov 1:1–6 · [D, multi] — the formation of the inner being (wisdom's aims)

**The reading.** The book opens not with a command but with a *list of what wisdom builds in a person* — "to **know** wisdom… to **understand** words of insight… to **receive** instruction… to give **prudence** to the simple, **knowledge** and **discretion** to the youth" (vv.2–4). The finding is the **inner faculties wisdom is meant to form**: knowing, understanding, prudence, discretion, and the disposition to *receive* instruction *(stated: these are the stated aims)*. The operation the unit foregrounds is **receptivity that grows** — "let the wise **hear** and **increase** in learning" (v.5): even the already-wise are defined by a *continuing intake*, a self that keeps taking in *(inferred: the aims are not a fixed state but a faculty-set held open to increase)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** Sound. The lexical correctly tags *know, understand, insight, wise-dealing, prudence, knowledge, wise, hear, guidance* as **characteristics** — the faculty-cluster the reading rests on. One **pair-sensibility note:** *simple* (H6612, v.4) is tagged `process-qualifier` welding *give* (manner/coupling pair `simple→give`); it is really the **recipient/target** of "give prudence *to* the simple," not a manner — a minor role-slippage (recipient read as manner). It does not affect the reading (the simple is still the one being formed). The genre/superscription terms of v.1 (*proverbs, Solomon, David, king, Israel*) correctly sit `standalone`.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **Receptivity-as-increase** (v.5) — distinct from mere "reception"; the wise self *keeps growing*, a hidden characteristic under the "aims." (2) The **transmission of the inner life** — wisdom is aimed *from* teacher *to* the simple/youth (vv.4–5); formation is relational, handed on, not self-generated.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *formation/faculties of the inner being* (new to the corpus — Proverbs' distinctive); *receptivity / teachability* (shared w/ Ps); *the transmission of wisdom* (new).

---

## PRO-01-B · Prov 1:7 · [S] — the fear of the LORD as the beginning/root

**The reading.** The single most load-bearing line in the book, given its own unit by weight: "The **fear** of the LORD is the **beginning** of knowledge; fools despise wisdom and instruction." The finding: the inner being's **foundational orientation is reverent fear** — knowledge does not *start* with intellect but with awe *(stated)*. The operation: fear is the *root from which the whole faculty-cluster of PRO-01-A grows* — and its refusal ("fools **despise**") is the inner posture that forfeits it *(inferred: the motto grounds vv.2–6 in a prior disposition; cf. 9:10, and bookended by 31:30)*. This is the same cornerstone as Ps 111:10, here at the head of Proverbs.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** The key term *fear* (H3374) is correctly a **characteristic**. But this verse is a clear case of the **bearer=LORD bleed** — the nearest-proper heuristic wrongly stamps `bearer=Lord` on *beginning, knowledge, fools, despise, wisdom, instruction* (pairs `H3068→…`). Read straight from the lexical, it would say *the LORD despises wisdom* — plainly wrong: it is the **fools** who despise. The reading takes the bearers from the text, not the tags (the fools despise; the fear is the person's). A flagged residual, not a defect in the reading.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** The verse holds a **paired opposition** the segmentation named as one characteristic but which is really two: *reverent fear* (the root) **and** *the despising of wisdom* (its refusal) — the fool's contempt is a distinct inner-being operation (the closed, scornful self), worth its own thread across the book (scoffer/fool).

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the fear of the LORD (as root)* (shared cornerstone w/ Ps 111:10); *the despising/scorning of wisdom* (new thread — the scoffer's closed heart).

---

## PRO-01-C · Prov 1:8–19 · [D, multi] — filial receptivity; the self-destructive greedy heart

**The reading.** Two inner-being movements held together. First, **filial receptivity**: "**Hear**, my son, your father's instruction, and **forsake not** your mother's teaching" (v.8) — the self that *takes in* the handed-down word, worn like a garland (v.9) *(stated)*. Second, and the unit's gem, the **self-destructive greedy heart**: the enticers say "let us **lie in wait** for blood… we shall **fill our houses** with plunder" (vv.11–13), but the trap they set closes on *themselves* — "these men **lie in wait for their own blood**; they set an ambush for their **own lives**" (v.18). The operation: **greed recoils on the greedy** — "such are the ways of everyone who is **greedy for unjust gain**; it takes away the **life** of its possessors" (v.19); the appetite for plunder is *self-consuming* *(inferred: the "own blood/own lives" turns the ambush self-ward — the greedy heart digs its own pit; cf. Ps 7:15–16, 9:15)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** The characteristics carrying the reading — *hear* (v.8, receptivity), *graceful* (v.9) — are correctly tagged. **Prohibition over-stamp** on v.8: the negation "forsake **not**" wrongly stamps `prohibition=forbidden` onto *father's, instruction, forsake, mother's, teaching* — the whole clause, not the verb; a known neg-particle bleed (the line is an *appeal*, not a legal prohibition). The greed-recoil of vv.17–19 sits largely in gate-2 content (*ambush, plunder, blood, life*); the reading is read from the structure (own-blood/own-lives), correctly.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** The **greed-that-self-destructs** is the deeper find — not "greed" as a label but the *mechanism* by which the acquisitive inner being **becomes its own victim** (the appetite consuming its owner). This is a Proverbs sharpening of a Psalter theme (the pit-digger caught in his own pit) and belongs to a cross-book thread on **self-inflicted ruin**.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *filial receptivity* (shared); *the self-destructive greedy heart / appetite that consumes its owner* (new — sharper than anything in Ps); *self-inflicted ruin (the pit-digger)* (shared w/ Ps 7/9).

---

## PRO-01-D · Prov 1:20–33 · [D, multi] — the refusal of wisdom; the security of the one who listens

**The reading.** Wisdom personified cries in the street, and the unit anatomises the **inner being that refuses her**: "How long, O **simple** ones, will you **love** being simple? How long will **scoffers delight** in their scoffing and **fools hate knowledge**?" (v.22). Three refusing dispositions are named as *loves and delights* — the self that **loves its own simplicity**, **delights in scoffing**, **hates knowledge** *(stated)*: refusal is not neutral ignorance but an *affection for un-wisdom*. Its end is the terrible reciprocity of vv.24–31 — "because you **ignored all my counsel**… I will not answer when you call" — and the un-answerable regret of a self that would not listen when it could. Against it stands the unit's resolution: "whoever **listens** to me will **dwell secure** and will be **at ease, without dread** of disaster" (v.33) — the **inner security of the receptive self** *(inferred: the listening heart's reward is not information but *rest without dread*, the same fearless security as Ps 112:7, 3:24)*.

**Lexical validation (read-back).** *love* (H0157, *aheb*, v.22 — "love being simple") is correctly a **characteristic** under the aheb-fix (PROMOTE_CHARACTERISTIC) — the *misdirected affection* toward simplicity, exactly parallel to Ps 4:2 "love vanity." *delight* and *hate* (v.22) likewise carry the refusing dispositions. The bearer/prohibition residuals recur (the "will not" of vv.24–28); the reading leans on the text. Pairs are sensible here.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **Refusal as *affection*** — the aheb-fix makes visible that the simple *love* their simplicity; un-wisdom is *desired*, not merely defaulted-to (a hidden characteristic the provisional "refusal of wisdom" flattened). (2) **The un-answerable regret** (vv.28–31) — a distinct inner state: the self that *finds no answer* because it refused to listen when answered (the mirror of the "he has heard" pivot in the Psalms — here, "I will not answer").

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the refusal of wisdom as misdirected affection (loving simplicity)* (new — surfaced by the aheb-fix); *the scoffer's delight / the closed scornful heart* (new thread); *the inner security of the listening self ("dwell secure, without dread")* (shared w/ Ps 112:7, 3:24).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Validation summary:** Phase-1 substrate is sound for reading; two systemic residuals recur exactly as in the Psalter — **bearer=LORD bleed** (acute at v.7) and **prohibition over-stamp** on negated appeals (v.8, vv.24–28). One **pair note**: recipient-read-as-manner at v.4 (*simple*→*give*). None touch the readings' spine; all are candidates for the same rule-adjustments flagged in the Psalms run.
- **New characteristics this chapter (for the fork-b control table):** *formation/faculties of the inner being*; *the transmission of wisdom*; *the despising/scorning of wisdom (the scoffer's closed heart)*; *the self-destructive greedy heart (appetite consuming its owner)*; *refusal of wisdom as misdirected affection*. **Shared with the Psalter:** *fear of the LORD (root)*; *receptivity/teachability*; *self-inflicted ruin*; *the inner security of the listening/trusting self*.

# Proverbs 2 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 lexicals (v1.1, construct-`specifier` + positional-`target` enriched) for Pro 2:1–22, read per `segment_unit`. Complete chapter. Lexicals only; cited; grounded; *stated* | *inferred*.
- **Lens:** the finding is the inner-being **operation**; wisdom/God is the arena (`feedback_lens_is_inner_being_process_not_god_relation`).
- **Method:** unit reading + lexical read-back/validation (now with specifier/target pairs) + hidden-characteristic isolation + characteristics-surfaced.

---

## PRO-02-A · Prov 2:1–11 · [D, multi] — the seeking of wisdom; reception that reshapes the heart

**The reading.** One long conditional: *if* the self does something, *then* something happens *to* it. The condition is a fivefold **active seeking** — "**receive** my words… **making your ear attentive**… **inclining your heart**… **call out** for insight… **seek** it like **silver** and **search** for it as for hidden treasures" (vv.1–4). The finding: understanding is not passively received but **strenuously sought** — the self *inclines its own heart* (an act of the will) and *digs* for wisdom as for buried treasure *(stated)*. The consequence is the reception that **reshapes the interior**: "then you will understand the **fear of the LORD**… **wisdom will come *into* your heart**, and knowledge will be **pleasant to your soul**" (vv.5,10). The operation: wisdom, once sought, **enters and re-forms the inner being** — it *comes into* the heart and becomes *pleasant to the soul*, and thereafter its faculties (discretion, understanding) **watch over** the self from within (v.11) *(inferred: the movement is self-seeks → God-gives (v.6) → wisdom-indwells → wisdom-guards; the inner being is remade by what it went after)*.

**Lexical validation.** The v1.1 substrate now carries the reading well: *fear* (H3374) → **specifier = of Lord** (the object of the fear captured); *heart* → seat + **specifier = of understanding**; and the seeking-verbs carry their objects positionally — *understand* → target **righteousness**, *walk* → target **integrity**, *gives* → target **wisdom**. The "wisdom comes *into* the heart" weld appears as *heart* (v.10) `manner/coupling` to *come-into* — correctly reading the heart as the place wisdom enters. Sound; the enrichment materially sharpens the "reshapes the heart" finding.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** (1) **Inclining the heart as an act of will** (v.2) — the self *directs* its own heart toward understanding; a volitional operation (with the "give me your heart" thread, 23:26). (2) **Wisdom as an *indwelling guardian*** (v.11) — "discretion will watch over you, understanding will guard you": the acquired faculties become *internal protectors*, a personified inner-being characteristic. (3) The **reciprocity** — the self seeks, but "the LORD *gives* wisdom" (v.6): the sought-for good is also a gift.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *the active seeking of wisdom* (new — Proverbs-distinctive, cf. the Psalter's seeking-God's-face); *inclining/directing the heart (volition)* (new); *wisdom indwelling and reshaping the heart* (new); *wisdom as internal guardian* (new); *the fear of the LORD* (shared, now object-tagged).

---

## PRO-02-B · Prov 2:12–22 · [D, multi] — discretion guarding the self; deliverance from evil

**The reading.** The indwelling faculties (from v.11) now *act*: they are "**delivering you** from the way of evil, from men of **perverted speech**… from the **forbidden woman** with her **smooth words**" (vv.12,16). The finding: the inner being's acquired discretion **functions as a deliverer** — wisdom internalised *extracts* the self from the paths of the crooked and the seductive *(stated)*. The unit's sharpest inner-being note is the anatomy of the seductress's *inner* failure: "who **forsakes** the companion of her youth and **forgets the covenant of her God**" (v.17) — her outward danger springs from an inward **forsaking and forgetting** *(inferred: the enticement is traced to a prior inner defection — she has *forgotten* a covenant; evil is diagnosed as a failure of inner fidelity/memory, cf. the Psalter's forgetting-as-seedbed-of-rebellion, Ps 106:13)*.

**Lexical validation.** The enrichment is telling here: *forsakes* → target **covenant**, *forgets* → target **covenant**, and *covenant* → **specifier = of God** — so the substrate now captures precisely the object of her defection ("the covenant *of God*"), which the reading rests on. The two "ways" close the unit as the moral-poles frame (paths *of uprightness* vs *of darkness* — both now specifier-tagged). Sound.

**Hidden / less-obvious characteristics isolated.** **Evil as inner infidelity** (v.17) — the seductress is defined not by her acts but by her *forgetting the covenant*; a hidden characteristic (the forgetting/forsaking heart) that the segmentation's "deliverance" framing didn't name, and which links to the Psalter's memory-and-fidelity thread.

**Characteristics surfaced:** *discretion as deliverer* (new); *evil as inner infidelity (forgetting the covenant)* (new — links to Ps memory thread); *the two ways* (shared frame).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Validation summary:** the v1.1 substrate is markedly richer for reading — construct `specifier` now supplies the *objects* of the characteristics (fear-of-Lord, covenant-of-God, heart-of-understanding) and positional `target` supplies the *objects of the operations* (walk→integrity, forsakes→covenant). Recurring residuals unchanged (bearer=LORD bleed at v.6; prohibition over-stamp on the "do not forsake" negations). No new anomalies.
- **New characteristics (fork-b control table):** *active seeking of wisdom*; *inclining the heart (volition)*; *wisdom indwelling / reshaping the heart*; *wisdom as internal guardian*; *discretion as deliverer*; *evil as inner infidelity (forgetting the covenant)*. **Shared:** *fear of the LORD*; *the two ways*.

# Proverbs 4 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 4:1–27, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation** (wisdom/God = arena).

---

**PRO-04-A · 4:1–9 · [D, multi] — the inherited, single-minded pursuit of wisdom.** A father hands on *his own father's* charge: "**Get wisdom**; get insight… The beginning of wisdom is this: **Get wisdom**, and whatever you get, **get insight**. **Prize her highly**, and she will exalt you; **embrace** her" (vv.5,7–8). The finding: wisdom is pursued as **the one acquisition worth everything** — "whatever you get, get insight" makes it the *priority over all gain* — and it is **loved and embraced** (v.6, *love her*), a beloved to be held *(stated)*. The operation: **the whole self bent on acquiring one thing**, and that acquiring is *affectionate* (prize, embrace, love) not merely diligent *(inferred; the single-minded pursuit, cross-book with Ps 27:4's "one thing")*. *Validation:* the imperative-with-object is now fully captured — *Get→target=wisdom/insight* (repeated), *Hear→sons*, *gain→insight*. *Hidden:* **transmission across three generations** (grandfather→father→son, vv.3–4) — wisdom is *handed down*, formation is inherited. *Surfaced:* single-minded pursuit of wisdom (new, cf. Ps one-thing); affectionate acquisition (love/embrace wisdom); transmission of the inner life.

**PRO-04-B · 4:10–19 · [D, multi] — evil as an inner compulsion that cannot rest.** The two paths: "the path of the righteous is like the **light of dawn**, shining **brighter and brighter**," but of the wicked — "they **cannot sleep** unless they have **done wrong**; they are **robbed of sleep** unless they have made someone **stumble**. For they **eat the bread of wickedness** and **drink the wine of violence**" (vv.16–18). The finding: wickedness is not occasional but a **compulsion** — the wicked *cannot rest* until they have done evil; doing wrong is their food and drink *(stated)*. The operation: evil has become the self's **appetite and its insomnia** — a driven interior that is *restless without sin* *(inferred; the darkest portrait of the captured will, cross-book with Ps 36:4 "he plots trouble on his bed")*. *Validation:* the paths now specifier-tagged — way→*of wisdom*, paths→*of uprightness*, path→*of the wicked*; bread→*of wickedness*, wine→*of violence*. *Hidden:* **evil as insomnia/appetite** (a compulsive interior). *Surfaced:* the two paths (frame); the compulsive-evil self (new — sharper than Ps).

**PRO-04-C · 4:20–27 · [D, multi] — keep the heart, the source of life.** The chapter's cornerstone: "**Keep your heart with all vigilance, for from it flow the springs of life**" (v.23); then the gates — "put away **crooked speech**… let your **eyes look directly forward**… **ponder the path of your feet**" (vv.24–26). The finding: the **heart is the *source*** from which the whole life flows, and therefore the object of the most vigilant **guarding** *(stated)*. The operation: the self is **the sentinel of its own heart** — because everything issues *from* the heart, guarding it is guarding the springs of the entire life; and that guarding extends to the *gates* (mouth, eyes, feet) through which the heart acts *(inferred; the master inner-being datum of Proverbs — the heart as origin, cross-book with Ps 51:10, 141:3–4, 119:9)*. *Validation (strong):* the enrichment captures it — *heart→specifier=of all* + intensity=all ("with ALL vigilance"), *all→of vigilance* welded to *Keep*, *springs→of life*. *Hidden:* **the heart as the *origin* of the life, not just a faculty** — vigilance is required *because* it is the source. *Surfaced:* guard-the-heart / the heart as source of life (★ cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps); governing the gates (speech/eyes/feet).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: v1.1 substrate strongly supports — the "get wisdom" objects and the "keep the heart with all vigilance" intensity/specifier are now fully pair-tagged; residuals unchanged. **New characteristics:** single-minded/affectionate pursuit of wisdom; transmission of the inner life; evil-as-compulsion (insomnia/appetite). **Shared/cornerstone:** ★ guard-the-heart (heart as source of life); the two paths; governing the gates.

# Proverbs 5 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 5:1–23, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation** (arena = the forbidden woman / the wife of youth).

---

**PRO-05-A · 5:1–6 · [D] — discernment of the sweet surface that ends bitter.** "The lips of a forbidden woman **drip honey**, and her speech is **smoother than oil**, but in the end she is **bitter as wormwood**… her steps follow the **path to Sheol**; she does not ponder the **path of life**" (vv.3–6). The finding: the inner being must learn to **read past the sweet surface to the end** — honey now, wormwood after *(stated)*. The operation: **discernment as looking-to-the-end** — the self weighs allure not by its present sweetness but by *where its path goes* (Sheol vs life) *(inferred; the anti-type of the naive who cannot see the end, cf. 14:12)*. *Validation:* *keep→discretion*, *guard→knowledge* (the discretion that protects); *drip→honey*, *go-down→death*, *path→Sheol* vs *path→of life* (the two ends captured). *Surfaced:* discernment-as-reading-the-end (new).

**PRO-05-B · 5:7–14 · [D, multi] — the retrospective regret of the un-teachable self.** The ruin of yielding is voiced *from its far end*: "at the end of your life you **groan**, when your **flesh and body are consumed**, and you say, '**How I hated discipline, and my heart despised reproof!** I did not listen to the voice of my teachers'" (vv.11–13). The finding — the sharpest inner-being note in the chapter: the self's undoing is traced to a **prior hatred of correction** — "how I *hated* discipline… my heart *despised* reproof… I did not *listen*" *(stated)*. The operation: the un-teachable interior **reaps regret** — the closed heart that despised reproof now *groans* at what it became, in a retrospective self-indictment *(inferred; teachability as life-or-death, the mirror of Ps 32:9's "be not like a horse without understanding")*. *Validation:* the enrichment names the objects precisely — *hated→target=discipline*, *despised→target=reproof*; *flesh→of body*. *Hidden:* **regret as the wage of un-teachability** (the self indicting its own past closedness). *Surfaced:* the un-teachable/despising heart (new — cross-book w/ Ps 32); retrospective self-indictment.

**PRO-05-C · 5:15–20 · [D] — rightly ordered, not extinguished, desire.** Against the adulteress: "**rejoice** in the wife of your youth… let her breasts **fill you at all times with delight**; be **intoxicated always in her love**" (vv.18–19). The finding: the answer to disordered desire is **not the killing of desire but its right direction** — the same intoxication (*shagah*) that would ruin the self with a stranger is *commanded* toward the wife *(stated)*. The operation: **desire redirected, not repressed** — the inner being's capacity for delight/intoxication is *good* when rightly aimed *(inferred; cross-book with the ordered-desire thread, Ps 37:4 "delight in the LORD")*. *Validation:* *all→of times* welded to *fill* ("fill you at all times"), *intoxicated→always*. *Hidden:* **the same passion is ruin or joy by its object** (desire is morally neutral, decided by direction). *Surfaced:* rightly-ordered desire (new — a Proverbs sharpening).

**PRO-05-D · 5:21–23 · [S] — the self bound in the cords of its own sin.** "A man's ways are before the **eyes of the LORD**… The **iniquities of the wicked ensnare him**, and he is **held fast in the cords of his sin**. He **dies for lack of discipline**" (vv.21–23). The finding: sin is **self-binding** — the wicked is *caught and held fast* not by an external trap but by *his own iniquity* *(stated)*. The operation: **iniquity as self-imposed bondage** — the sinning self *weaves the cords that hold it*; freedom is lost from within *(inferred; the self-ensnaring wicked, cross-book with Ps 7:15, 9:15, and Pro 1:18's greed recoiling)*. *Validation:* *iniquities→of wicked*, *held-fast→wicked*, **cords→specifier=of sin** — the substrate now captures "the cords *of his sin*". *Surfaced:* sin as self-binding bondage (shared thread, cross-book).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: v1.1 enrichment supplies the objects the readings turn on (hated→discipline, cords→of-sin); residuals unchanged. **New characteristics:** discernment-as-reading-the-end; regret-of-the-un-teachable; rightly-ordered (not repressed) desire; the same-passion-ruin-or-joy-by-object. **Shared:** the un-teachable heart (w/ Ps 32); sin as self-binding (w/ Ps 7/9).

*Section id 589 · status `approved` · v1 · 476 words · author `claude_code` · source `verse-analysis/proverbs/readings/wa-proverbs7-unit-synthesis-20260703.md`*

# Proverbs 7 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 7:1–27, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**.

---

**PRO-07-A · 7:1–5 · [D, multi] — wisdom held as beloved kin.** "Keep my commandments as the **apple of your eye**… Say to wisdom, '**You are my sister**,' and call insight your **intimate friend**" (vv.2,4). The finding: wisdom is to be held not as a rule but as a **beloved relation** — sister, intimate friend, guarded like the eye's pupil *(stated)*. The operation: **intimacy with wisdom** — the self is to *love* wisdom into the family, so that closeness to her keeps it from the stranger-woman *(inferred; affection as the guard, cross-book with Ps 119:97 "oh how I love your law")*. *Validation:* *teaching→of apple* ("keep as the apple of the eye"). *Surfaced:* intimacy/kinship with wisdom (new).

**PRO-07-B · 7:6–23 · [D, multi] — the anatomy of a naive heart yielding.** The long narrative of "a young man **lacking sense**" (v.7) taken step by step: she is "**wily of heart**" (v.10); "with **much seductive speech** she persuades him; with her **smooth talk** she compels him. **All at once** he follows her, as an ox goes to the **slaughter**… he **does not know** that it will cost him his **life**" (vv.21–23). The finding: the psalm-like narrative **anatomises the collapse of the naive self** — the sense-lacking heart, worked by *smooth speech*, yields "all at once" and *does not know* the cost *(stated)*. The operation: **the un-guarded interior overwhelmed** — persuasion works on a heart with no discernment until the will follows *unknowing* to its ruin; the tragedy is the *not-knowing* *(inferred; the mirror of the discerning self of 5:1–6; cross-book with the naive vs prudent, and Ps 19:12 "who can discern his errors")*. *Validation:* *wily→target=heart* ("wily of heart"), *much→of seductive speech*, *smooth→persuades*, *fill→target=love* — the enrichment captures the seduction's mechanics. *Hidden:* **ruin through not-knowing** (the naive self's fatal unawareness). *Surfaced:* the collapse of the un-discerning heart (new — the anti-type of discernment).

**PRO-07-C · 7:24–27 · [D] — guarding the heart against turning aside.** "**Let not your heart turn aside** to her ways; do not stray into her paths" (v.25). The finding: the defence is set at the **heart's inclination** — the danger is the *heart turning aside* *(stated)*. The operation: **the self guards the *direction* of its own heart** — the well-trodden path to death is entered by an inward *turning*, so the guarding is of the heart's leaning, before the feet move *(inferred; the same interiorised guard as 4:23, 6:25)*. *Surfaced:* guarding the heart's inclination (shared w/ 4:23; the turned-aside heart).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: v1.1 enrichment captures the seduction's mechanics (wily-of-heart, seductive-speech, fill-with-love). **New characteristics:** intimacy/kinship with wisdom; the collapse of the un-discerning heart (ruin through not-knowing). **Shared:** guarding the heart's inclination (w/ 4:23, 6:25).

*Section id 591 · status `approved` · v1 · 644 words · author `claude_code` · source `verse-analysis/proverbs/readings/wa-proverbs9-unit-synthesis-20260703.md`*

# Proverbs 9 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 9:1–18, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**. (Closes the ch 1–9 discourses; two rival banquets — Wisdom and Folly.)

---

**PRO-09-A · 9:1–6 · [D] — the summons to leave simplicity and live.** Wisdom's feast: "Whoever is **simple**, let him **turn in** here!… **Leave your simple ways, and live, and walk in the way of insight**" (vv.4,6). The finding: the call is to **abandon a settled inner condition** — "*leave* your simple ways" — as the price of life *(stated)*. The operation: **the self must renounce its own simplicity** — simplicity here is not innocence but a *chosen ease* the self is asked to *walk out of*; turning toward wisdom means turning *from* a former self *(inferred; cross-book with the "leave/turn" that begins the wise life)*. *Validation:* *Leave→target=ways*, way→*of insight*. *Surfaced:* renouncing one's own simplicity (new).

**PRO-09-B · 9:7–9 · [S, multi] — the response to reproof reveals the heart.** The chapter's gem: "**Reprove a scoffer, and he will hate you; reprove a wise man, and he will love you.** Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be **still wiser**" (vv.8–9). The finding: **the same reproof divides two hearts** — one *hates* the reprover, the other *loves* him *(stated)*. The operation: **the reaction to correction is the diagnostic of the inner being** — teachability is not measured by knowledge but by whether reproof is met with *hatred* or *love*; and the teachable heart *compounds* ("still wiser") while the closed heart only hardens *(inferred; the master teachability datum, cross-book with Ps 141:5 "let a righteous man strike me… it is a kindness")*. *Validation:* *increase→target=learning*; the aheb (love, 9:8) now tags characteristic under the v1.1/aheb rule — the *love* of the reproved wise. *Hidden:* **correction as the test that sorts the heart** (love-vs-hate of the reprover). *Surfaced:* teachability as the diagnostic of the heart (★ cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps 141:5).

**PRO-09-C · 9:10–12 · [S] — the fear of the LORD, the beginning of wisdom.** "**The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom**, and the knowledge of the Holy One is insight" (v.10). The motto restated at the discourses' close (bookending 1:7). The finding: reverent fear is the **root** of the whole wise inner life *(stated)*. *Validation:* *fear→specifier=of Lord*; *added→target=life*. *Surfaced:* fear of the LORD (★ shared cornerstone — re-attested, bookends ch 1).

**PRO-09-D · 9:13–18 · [D] — the counterfeit allure of Folly.** Folly, Wisdom's mirror-image, calls from the same "highest places": "**Stolen water is sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant.** But he does not know that the **dead are there**, that her guests are in the **depths of Sheol**" (vv.17–18). The finding: Folly's appeal is the **sweetness of the illicit** — *stolen*, *secret* — and its victim, like the naive of ch 7, **does not know** the end *(stated)*. The operation: **the allure of the forbidden precisely *because* it is forbidden** ("stolen… secret" are the selling points), working on a self that will not look to the end *(inferred; the counterfeit feast set exactly against Wisdom's, so the whole discourse-section closes on a *choice of two tables* — two loves, two ends)*. *Validation:* *woman→of Folly*, *bread→of secret*, *depths→of Sheol*. *Hidden:* **the forbidden desired *as* forbidden** (illicitness as the attraction). *Surfaced:* the counterfeit allure / the sweetness of the illicit (new); ruin-through-not-knowing (shared w/ 7:23).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: enrichment supplies fear→of-Lord and the feast-objects; the aheb love (9:8) now correctly a characteristic. **New characteristics:** renouncing one's own simplicity; teachability-as-diagnostic (★); the counterfeit allure of the illicit. **Shared:** ★ fear of the LORD (bookends ch 1); ruin-through-not-knowing (w/ ch 7). **This closes the ch 1–9 discourses — the whole section frames the inner life as a choice between two tables (Wisdom vs Folly), two loves, two ends.**

*Section id 593 · status `approved` · v1 · 611 words · author `claude_code` · source `verse-analysis/proverbs/readings/wa-proverbs12-unit-synthesis-20260703.md`*

# Proverbs 12 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 12, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**; righteous⇄wicked = arena.

---

**PRO-12-F · 12:2–28 · [F]** — the moral-poles frame. Arena.

**PRO-12-teachable · 12:1,15 · [S, multi] — loving discipline vs the self right in its own eyes.** "Whoever **loves discipline loves knowledge**, but he who **hates reproof is stupid**" (v.1); "the way of a fool is **right in his own eyes**, but a wise man **listens to advice**" (v.15). Finding: teachability is an *affection* — to love knowledge is to *love the discipline* that gives it; and the fool's fault is **self-certainty** ("right in his own eyes") *(stated)*. Operation: **the self that cannot see past its own view cannot learn** — self-certainty seals the heart, while the wise *hold their view open* to advice *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 36:2 self-flattery, and the teachability thread)*. *Hidden:* **self-certainty ("right in his own eyes") as the seal against wisdom** — recurs at 3:7, 26:12, 30:12. *Surfaced:* teachability-as-affection; self-certainty as the closed heart (new thread).

**PRO-12-speech · 12:6,13–14,17–19,22–23 · [T, multi] — the tongue that wounds or heals; truth that endures.** "**Rash words** are like **sword thrusts**, but the **tongue of the wise brings healing**"; "**truthful lips endure forever**, but a lying tongue is but for a **moment**"; "a **prudent man conceals** knowledge, but the **heart of fools proclaims folly**" (vv.18–19,23). Finding: speech wounds or heals, endures or vanishes, by its truth — and the *prudent conceal* while *fools broadcast* *(stated)*. Operation: **the governed tongue as healing and enduring** — truth in speech has a *permanence* the lie lacks; and prudence *withholds* what folly *spills* *(inferred; the speech-legibility thread, + the endurance-of-truth note)*. *Validation:* v1.1 supplies the fruit-of-the-mouth objects (12:14 "satisfied with good"). *Surfaced:* speech-legibility (shared); the endurance of truthful speech (new); prudent concealment vs folly's broadcast.

**PRO-12-heart-thoughts · 12:5,20 · [S, multi] — the heart's thoughts and plans.** "The **thoughts of the righteous are just**; the counsels of the wicked are deceitful"; "**deceit is in the heart** of those who devise evil, but those who **plan peace have joy**" (vv.5,20). Finding: the inner *thoughts/plans* are the moral root — deceit or peace lives *in the heart* before it acts, and *planning peace* carries joy *(stated)*. Operation: **the heart's inner counsel as the seat of character** — what the self *thinks/plans* is who it is *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 19:14 "meditation of my heart", 139:23 "know my thoughts")*. *Hidden:* **planning peace *has joy* now** — the disposition is already its own reward. *Surfaced:* the heart's thoughts/plans as character (shared w/ Ps).

**PRO-12-anxiety · 12:25 · [S, multi] — anxiety weighs the heart; a good word lifts it.** "**Anxiety in a man's heart weighs him down, but a good word makes him glad**" (v.25). Finding: anxiety is a *weight* on the heart, relieved by a kind word *(stated)*. Operation: **the felt interior — the heavy heart lightened from outside** (a good word) *(inferred; the felt-heart thread, cross-book w/ Ps 94:19 "when the cares of my heart are many, your consolations cheer my soul")*. *Surfaced:* the felt heart (weighed/gladdened) — ★ shared cross-book thread.

**PRO-12-diligence · 12:11,24,27 · [T] — diligence rules, sloth is enslaved.** "The **hand of the diligent will rule**, while the **slothful will be put to forced labor**" (v.24). Finding: diligence and sloth end in mastery vs servitude *(stated)*. *Surfaced:* diligence vs sloth (shared Proverbs thread).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: enrichment consistent (fruit-of-mouth, deceit-in-heart objects). **New:** self-certainty as the closed heart; endurance-of-truthful-speech; planning-peace-has-joy. **Shared:** the felt heart (★ w/ Ps 94:19); the heart's thoughts as character (w/ Ps 139); speech-legibility; diligence/sloth.

*Section id 594 · status `approved` · v1 · 502 words · author `claude_code` · source `verse-analysis/proverbs/readings/wa-proverbs13-unit-synthesis-20260703.md`*

# Proverbs 13 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 13, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**; righteous⇄wicked = arena.

---

**PRO-13-F · 13:5–25 · [F]** — the moral-poles frame. Arena.

**PRO-13-desire-hope · 13:4,12,19,25 · [T, multi] — craving, hope deferred, desire fulfilled.** The chapter's felt-interior cluster: "the **soul of the sluggard craves and gets nothing**, while the **soul of the diligent is richly supplied**" (v.4); "**HOPE DEFERRED makes the heart sick, but a desire fulfilled is a tree of life**" (v.12); "**a desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul**" (v.19). Finding: the inner being is a **creature of longing whose deferral *sickens* the heart and whose fulfilment is *life and sweetness*** *(stated)*. Operation: **hope has a bodily register — deferred, it makes the heart *sick*; met, it is a *tree of life*** — the timing of fulfilment is itself an inner-being event *(inferred; a cornerstone of the felt interior, cross-book w/ Ps 42:1–2's thirst, 130:5–6's aching wait, and the desire-met thread 145:19)*. *Hidden:* **the *sickness* of deferred hope** — waiting is not neutral; unmet longing *wounds* the heart (the shadow-side of the Psalter's hopeful waiting). *Surfaced:* hope-deferred/fulfilled (★ shared cornerstone, cross-book); the craving vs satisfied soul.

**PRO-13-speech · 13:2,3 · [S] — guarding the mouth guards the life.** "Whoever **guards his mouth preserves his life**; he who **opens wide his lips comes to ruin**" (v.3). Finding: speech-restraint is **self-preservation** — the guarded mouth guards the whole self *(stated; the self-governance-of-the-tongue thread, cross-book w/ Ps 141:3)*. *Surfaced:* restraint of the tongue as self-preservation (shared).

**PRO-13-teachable · 13:1,10,13,18 · [T, multi] — hearing, revering the word, heeding reproof.** "A wise son **hears** instruction, but a scoffer does not listen"; "by **insolence** comes strife, but with those who **take advice** is wisdom"; "whoever **despises the word** brings destruction, but he who **reveres the commandment** will be rewarded" (vv.1,10,13). Finding: teachability spans *hearing*, *taking advice*, and *revering the word* — insolence (pride) is its enemy *(stated)*. Operation: **reverence for the word vs contempt for it** as the fork of the inner life *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 119's love of the word)*. *Surfaced:* teachability / reverence-vs-contempt-for-the-word (shared w/ Ps 119).

**PRO-13-company · 13:20 · [S] — formation by company.** "**Whoever walks with the wise becomes wise, but the companion of fools will suffer harm**" (v.20). Finding: the self is **shaped by the company it keeps** — one *becomes* like one's companions *(stated)*. Operation: **formation-by-association** — a law of the inner life (you become your company), the same formation-principle as "you become what you trust" (Ps 115:8) applied to human company *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 1:1's refused seat, 26:4–5)*. *Hidden:* **the formation-law extended to company** — a Proverbs parallel to the trust-formation datum. *Surfaced:* formation-by-company (★ new — the formation-law applied to company, cross-book w/ Ps 1/115).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: enrichment consistent (craving/desire objects, soul-of-sluggard). **New/cornerstone:** hope-deferred-makes-the-heart-sick (★ felt interior); formation-by-company (★). **Shared:** the felt interior (w/ Ps 42/130); restraint-of-tongue; teachability/reverence-for-the-word (w/ Ps 119).

*Section id 595 · status `approved` · v1 · 627 words · author `claude_code` · source `verse-analysis/proverbs/readings/wa-proverbs14-unit-synthesis-20260703.md`*

# Proverbs 14 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 14, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**; wise⇄fool = arena.

---

**PRO-14-F · 14:1–35 · [F]** — the moral-poles frame. Arena.

**PRO-14-heart-known · 14:10,13 · [S, multi] — the heart's incommunicable interior.** "**The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger shares its joy**" (v.10); "**even in laughter the heart may ache, and the end of joy may be grief**" (v.13). Finding — a cornerstone of the felt interior: the heart's deepest states are **private and incommunicable** — its bitterness *known only to itself*, its joy *unshared*, and its surface (laughter) may *mask* an inward ache *(stated)*. Operation: **the inner life is finally solitary** — no one else fully enters the heart's grief or gladness, and the outward face can *contradict* the inward state *(inferred; the most explicit statement in Scripture of the *privacy* of the inner being; cross-book w/ Ps 38:8–9 "the tumult of my heart… my sighing is not hidden from you" — only God enters where no stranger can)*. *Hidden:* **the mask — laughter over ache** (the outward may belie the inward). *Surfaced:* the incommunicable/private heart (★ cornerstone — new to the corpus, deepens the felt-interior thread); the masking surface.

**PRO-14-temper · 14:17,29,30 · [T, multi] — anger vs the tranquil heart.** "Whoever is **slow to anger has great understanding**, but he who has a **hasty temper exalts folly**"; "**A tranquil heart gives life to the flesh, but envy makes the bones rot**" (vv.29–30). Finding: temper is a *cognitive* matter (slow-to-anger = *understanding*), and the **tranquil heart is bodily *life* while envy *rots the bones*** *(stated)*. Operation: **inner tranquillity as physical health, envy/rage as physical decay** — the emotional interior writes itself on the body *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 32:3 "my bones wasted", 38:3; the felt interior embodied)*. *Hidden:* **the heart's peace as *somatic*** (tranquil heart → life to the flesh). *Surfaced:* self-mastery/slow-to-anger (shared, cross-book w/ Ps); the tranquil-vs-envious heart embodied (★ new).

**PRO-14-fear · 14:26,27 · [T, multi] — the fear of the LORD as confidence and fountain of life.** "In the **fear of the LORD one has strong confidence**… the **fear of the LORD is a fountain of life**" (vv.26–27). Finding: reverent fear yields **confidence and life** — not dread but a *strong assurance* *(stated; the fear-of-LORD thread, cross-book w/ Ps 112, 27:1)*. *Surfaced:* fear of the LORD → confidence/life (shared cornerstone).

**PRO-14-self-deception · 14:12 · [S] — the way that seems right.** "**There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way to death**" (v.12). Finding: the self can **misread its own path** — subjective rightness is no guide to the true end *(stated)*. Operation: **self-deception about one's own way** — the inner sense of being right can be fatally wrong *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 19:12 "who can discern his errors")*. *Surfaced:* self-deception / the way-that-seems-right (★ new — recurs 16:25).

**PRO-14-simple · 14:15 · [S] — credulity vs considered steps.** "**The simple believes everything, but the prudent gives thought to his steps**" (v.15). Finding: the naive *believes all*, the prudent *weighs* — discernment as considered attention *(stated)*. *Surfaced:* discernment vs credulity (shared w/ ch 7's naive self).

**PRO-14-generosity · 14:21,31 · [S, multi] — regard for the poor as regard for the Maker.** "Whoever **oppresses a poor man insults his Maker**, but he who is **generous to the needy honors him**" (v.31). Finding: one's disposition toward the poor is a disposition **toward God** *(stated; the neighbour-facing heart, cross-book w/ Ps 41:1)*. *Surfaced:* regard-for-the-poor-as-regard-for-God (shared).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: enrichment consistent. **New/cornerstone:** the incommunicable/private heart (★ 14:10); the tranquil-vs-envious heart embodied (★ 14:30); self-deception (★ 14:12). **Shared:** self-mastery/slow-to-anger; fear-of-LORD→confidence; discernment; the neighbour-facing heart.

*Section id 596 · status `approved` · v1 · 737 words · author `claude_code` · source `verse-analysis/proverbs/readings/wa-proverbs15-unit-synthesis-20260703.md`*

# Proverbs 15 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 15, per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**; righteous⇄wicked = arena.

---

**PRO-15-F · 15:2–33 · [F]** — the moral-poles frame. Arena.

**PRO-15-anger · 15:1,18 · [S, multi] — the soft answer; slow-to-anger quiets strife.** "**A soft answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger**"; "a **hot-tempered man stirs up strife, but he who is slow to anger quiets contention**" (vv.1,18). Finding: the inner being can **de-escalate or inflame** by the temper of its speech — gentleness *turns away* wrath *(stated)*. Operation: **self-mastery expressed as gentleness** — the slow-to-anger self *quiets* what the hot-tempered *kindles* *(inferred; the self-mastery thread, cross-book w/ Ps 4:4 "be angry and do not sin")*. *Surfaced:* self-mastery / the soft answer (shared).

**PRO-15-heart-states · 15:13,15,30 · [T, multi] — the felt heart: glad, crushed, cheerful.** "**A glad heart makes a cheerful face, but by sorrow of heart the spirit is crushed**"; "the **cheerful of heart has a continual feast**"; "the **light of the eyes rejoices the heart**, and good news refreshes the bones" (vv.13,15,30). Finding — a felt-interior cornerstone: the heart's state **shows on the face**, *crushes the spirit* in sorrow, and the cheerful heart lives in a **continual feast** regardless of circumstance *(stated)*. Operation: **the inner disposition *colours all of life*** — "a continual feast" is not about events but about a *cheerful heart*; the interior sets the taste of existence *(inferred; the felt-interior thread at its fullest, cross-book w/ Ps 4:7 "more joy… than when grain and wine abound", 34:5 "radiant faces")*. *Hidden:* **the cheerful heart makes a *continual feast* out of ordinary days** — inner state over outer circumstance. *Surfaced:* the felt heart (glad/crushed/cheerful) — ★ shared cornerstone; the crushed spirit (w/ 17:22, Ps).

**PRO-15-god-sees-heart · 15:3,11 · [T, multi] — God sees the hearts.** "The **eyes of the LORD are in every place, keeping watch** on evil and good"; "**Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD; how much more the hearts of the children of man!**" (vv.3,11). Finding: the inner being is **wholly open to God's sight** — if even the realm of the dead lies open, *how much more the heart* *(stated)*. Operation (of the self): **living before an all-seeing gaze** — the heart is never unobserved *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 139 "you have searched me", 33:13–15 "he fashions their hearts and observes all their deeds")*. *Surfaced:* being-known/seen by God (★ shared cornerstone, cross-book w/ Ps 139).

**PRO-15-teachable · 15:14,31,32 · [T, multi] — the seeking heart, the listening ear.** "The **heart of him who has understanding seeks knowledge**"; "the **ear that listens to life-giving reproof will dwell among the wise**"; "whoever **ignores instruction despises himself**" (vv.14,31–32). Finding: the wise heart is **actively seeking**, and heeding reproof is **self-respect** ("ignores instruction *despises himself*") *(stated)*. Operation: **the seeking heart + the self-valuing that heeds correction** *(inferred; teachability as self-love, cross-book w/ 19:8)*. *Surfaced:* the seeking heart; heeding-reproof-as-self-respect (new).

**PRO-15-contentment · 15:16,17 · [S, multi] — the little with fear/love better than much with trouble.** "**Better is a little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure and trouble**… better a **dinner of herbs where love is** than a fattened ox and **hatred**" (vv.16–17). Finding: **contentment is a function of the inner condition** (fear, love), not the quantity of goods *(stated)*. Operation: **the inner good (fear/love) outvalues the outer abundance** *(inferred; cross-book w/ Ps 37:16 "better is the little of the righteous than the abundance of many wicked")*. *Surfaced:* contentment (inner-condition over abundance) — shared w/ Ps 37.

**PRO-15-ponder · 15:28 · [S] — the heart that ponders before answering.** "**The heart of the righteous ponders how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked pours out evil**" (v.28). Finding: the righteous heart **weighs before it speaks** — considered vs impulsive interior *(stated; the ponder/restraint thread)*. *Surfaced:* the pondering (vs impulsive) heart (new).

**PRO-15-humility · 15:33 · [S, multi] — fear and humility before honour.** "The **fear of the LORD is instruction in wisdom, and humility comes before honour**" (v.33). Finding: humility *precedes* honour — the lowered self is the one lifted *(stated; pride/humility thread, cross-book w/ Ps 138:6)*. *Surfaced:* humility-before-honour (shared cornerstone).

---
**Chapter notes.** Validation: enrichment consistent. **New/cornerstone:** the felt heart / cheerful-heart-as-continual-feast (★ 15:15); heeding-reproof-as-self-respect; the pondering heart. **Shared:** self-mastery/soft-answer; being-seen-by-God (★ 15:11, w/ Ps 139); contentment (w/ Ps 37); humility-before-honour.

*Section id 612 · status `approved` · v1 · 588 words · author `claude_code` · source `verse-analysis/proverbs/readings/wa-proverbs31-unit-synthesis-20260703.md`*

# Proverbs 31 — inner-being unit readings (Phase-2 meaning synthesis)

- **Source:** `lexical-model-2026` Phase-1 (v1.1 enriched) for Pro 31 (Lemuel + the woman of valour), per `segment_unit`. Grounded; *stated* | *inferred*. Lens: the inner-being **operation**. (Closes the book.)

---

**PRO-31-charge · 31:2–9 · [D, multi] — self-mastery for the sake of the voiceless.** The mother's charge to the king: "**do not give your strength to women**… **it is not for kings to drink wine**… lest they **drink and forget** what has been decreed and **pervert the rights of the afflicted**… **Open your mouth for the mute**, for the rights of all who are destitute" (vv.3–5,8). Finding: **self-mastery is charged for the sake of *others*** — the king must govern appetite (women, wine) *lest* he *forget* justice and fail the voiceless *(stated)*. Operation: **appetite-restraint in service of justice** — self-control is not private virtue only but the condition of *not forgetting* one's duty to the afflicted *(inferred; self-mastery + the neighbour-facing heart joined; cross-book w/ Ps 72:2–4)*. *Surfaced:* self-mastery-for-the-sake-of-the-voiceless (new — self-control as a *public* fidelity).

**PRO-31-noble-wife · 31:10–31 · [D, multi] — the woman who fears the LORD: trust, strength, fearless hope, the book's crown.** The acrostic portrait, read for the inner being: "the **heart of her husband trusts in her**" (v.11 — she is *trustworthy*); "she **dresses herself with strength**… **strength and dignity are her clothing, and she laughs at the time to come**" (vv.17,25 — inner strength and **fearless hope**); "she **opens her mouth with wisdom, and the teaching of kindness is on her tongue**" (v.26 — wise, kind speech); and the crown: "**charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised**" (v.30). Finding — the book's closing cornerstone: the whole excellence is finally reduced to **the fear of the LORD** — over charm and beauty (which are *deceitful* and *vain*) — and it *shows* as **trustworthiness, inner strength, fearless laughter at the future, and wise-kind speech** *(stated)*. Operation: **the fear of the LORD *embodied* as a life** — the abstract root of 1:7 is here *lived out* in a whole person: an inner being so settled it **laughs at the time to come** (the opposite of dread), so reliable that a heart *trusts* in her, so strengthened it needs no charm *(inferred; the book's frame closes — fear-of-the-LORD opened it (1:7) and crowns it here (31:30); cross-book w/ Ps 112 the God-fearer whose "heart is firm… not afraid of bad news", and the fearless-security thread)*. *Hidden:* **"she laughs at the time to come"** — fearless hope as the *affect* of the God-fearing self (the antithesis of anxiety about the future, cf. 27:1's refused presumption; here a *settled* facing of the future). *Surfaced:* fear-of-the-LORD embodied (★ book-closing cornerstone, bookends 1:7, cross-book w/ Ps 112); trustworthiness; inner strength + fearless hope ("laughs at the time to come"); wise-kind speech.

---
**Chapter notes.** **Book-closing cornerstone:** the fear of the LORD *embodied* as a whole life (★ 31:30, bookending 1:7). **New:** self-mastery-for-the-voiceless; fearless-hope ("laughs at the time to come"). **Shared:** the fear of the LORD (★ frame); trust/trustworthiness; inner strength; wise-kind speech.

---
*This completes the Proverbs unit meaning-synthesis (all 31 chapters, 150 units). The book's inner-being frame: it opens (1:7) and closes (31:30) on the **fear of the LORD** — abstract root, then embodied life — and between them maps the inner being as a **heart to be guarded, given, weighed, searched, and ruled**, its wisdom a matter of what it fears, trusts, desires, and how it governs itself.*
