# Genesis 24:1–67 — inner-being passage reading (ABR-16-wife-for-isaac)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-abraham-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The cycle's providence-and-love centre.
- **Check-back note:** `barak` (bless/praise) recurs 7× (blessing Abraham; doxology; blessing Rebekah) and `natan` 6× (God's giving; the gifts) — recurring operations named with their distinctions and verses referenced. `chesed`/`emet` (the covenant-pair), `charesh`, the heart's prayer, and `nacham` carry the depth.

---

## ABR-16-wife-for-isaac · Genesis 24:1–67 · [providence and the comfort of love] — the prayer for steadfast love, the silent discernment, the willing consent, and grief consoled

**The passage.** "The LORD had **blessed** (barak) Abraham in all things" (24:1); the servant "who **ruled** (mashal) over all he had" (24:2); "**take care** (shamar) that you do not take my son back… you will be **free** (naqah) from this oath" (24:6,8); "grant me success… show **steadfast love** (chesed) to my master… by this I shall **know** (yada)" (24:12,14); Rebekah "**attractive** (tov)… no man had **known** (yada) her" (24:16); "the man gazed in **silence** (charesh) to **learn** (yada)" (24:21); "**Blessed** (barak) be the LORD… who has not forsaken his **steadfast love** (chesed) and **faithfulness** (emet)" (24:27); "before I had finished speaking in my **heart** (lev)" (24:45); "if you will show **steadfast love** (chesed) and **faithfulness** (emet)… tell me" (24:49); "we **cannot** (yakhol) speak **bad** (ra) or **good** (tov)" (24:50); "they **called** (qara) Rebekah… Will you go?… I will go" (24:57–58); "may your offspring possess the gate of those who **hate** (sane) them" (24:60); "Isaac… **loved** her, and was **comforted** (nacham) after his mother's death" (24:67).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **barak (blessed) — the *comprehensively* blessed patriarch, and the *kneeling* root (24:1, 24:11, 24:31, 24:35, 24:48, 24:60).** The finding is "the LORD had **blessed** (barak) Abraham in all things" (24:1) *(stated)*. The operation is the blessing (← 12:2) *fulfilled* — the aged Abraham *blessed in everything*; the ground of his confident charge. The *same root barak* then runs several senses through the chapter, **kept distinct**: at **24:11** the servant "made the camels **kneel** (barak)" — the *physical root* of the word (to bend the knee), *not* blessing; at **24:31** Laban greets the servant as "**blessed** (barak) of the LORD"; at **24:35** "the LORD has **blessed** (barak) my master greatly" (the blessing *recounted*, with **gadal**); at **24:48** the servant "**blessed** (barak) the LORD" (*doxology*, ← 24:27); at **24:60** the family "**blessed** (barak) Rebekah". So barak spans *kneeling* (24:11), *being-blessed* (24:31), *God's blessing recounted* (24:35), *praising God* (24:48), and *blessing a person* (24:60) — one root, several distinct acts *(inferred: do not lump — 24:11 is the *knee-bending*, the others are blessing/praise)*.
- **mashal (ruled) — the steward's *delegated authority* (24:2).** The finding is "his servant who **ruled** (mashal) over all that he had" *(stated)*. The operation is *mashal* (govern, ← 1:16; 3:16; 4:7) as the *steward's stewardship* — trusted rule over the household; distinct from the husband's/sin's mashal — here *fiduciary authority* *(inferred)*.
- **shamar (take care) + naqah (free) — the oath's *condition and release* (24:6,8).** The finding is "**take care** (shamar) that you do not take my son back there… you shall be **free** (naqah) from this oath" *(stated)*. The operations: **shamar** — *taking-heed/guarding-against* (← the keeping-word, now vigilance over the oath's terms); **naqah** — being *cleared/free* from the oath if the woman refuses — the interior *bound but justly releasable* *(inferred)*.
- **natan (give) — the land-promise and the *gifts* (24:7, 24:32, 24:35, 24:36, 24:41, 24:53).** The finding is "the LORD… who swore to **give** (natan) this land to my offspring" (24:7) *(stated)*. The operation is the *promissory land-gift* (← 12:7) grounding Abraham's *faith*; and the *same natan* runs through the chapter in a *different* register — the *gifts* of hospitality and betrothal: Laban **gave** (natan) provender to the camels (24:32); "the LORD… has **given** (natan) my master flocks… all he has" (24:35–36, God's *giving* to Abraham recounted); the oath-clause "**give** (natan) her to me" (24:41); the servant "**gave** (natan) costly ornaments" to Rebekah's house (24:53). So natan spans the *land-promise* (24:7) and the *provision/betrothal-gifts* (24:32,35,36,41,53) — the promissory gift and the enacted generosity *(inferred: distinct natan registers — the promise vs the gifts)*.
- **chesed (steadfast love) + yada (know) — the *prayer for guidance* by a sign (24:12,14).** The finding is "grant me success… show **steadfast love** (chesed) to my master Abraham… by this I shall **know** (yada) that you have shown steadfast love" *(stated)*. The gems: **chesed** — the servant *prays for God's steadfast love* to Abraham (← 19:19 God's saving chesed); and **yada** — *knowing-by-a-sign* (as Abram "how shall I know", 15:8): the interior *seeking guidance* through a requested sign *(inferred: chesed = the divine loyalty invoked; yada = discernment sought)*.
- **tov (attractive) + yada (known) — Rebekah (24:16).** The finding is "the young woman was very **attractive** (tov)… a virgin, no man had **known** (yada) her" *(stated)*. The operations: **tov** — her beauty (← 6:2, here neutral/good); **yada** — *unrealized* conjugal knowing (virgin, ← 4:1) *(inferred)*.
- **charesh (silence) + yada (learn) — the *silent, watchful discernment* (24:21).** The finding is "the man gazed at her in **silence** (charesh) to **learn** (yada) whether the LORD had prospered his way" *(stated)*. The gem is the **first "silence/be-still" (charesh)** — the servant *watches wordlessly*, the interior *waiting in stillness to discern* God's leading (not rushing to conclude); paired with *yada* (to learn/know) — **discernment as silent attentiveness** *(inferred: charesh = attentive silence; the watching interior)*.
- **barak (blessed) + chesed + emet — the *doxology* for God's covenant character (24:27).** The finding is "**Blessed** (barak) be the LORD… who has not forsaken his **steadfast love** (chesed) and **faithfulness** (emet) toward my master" *(stated)*. The gems: **barak** — the servant *blesses/praises God* (doxology, ← 9:26; 14:20); and the **first "emet" (faithfulness/truth)** paired with **chesed** — the great covenant-couplet *chesed-and-emet* (steadfast-love and reliable-truth): the interior *recognises God's unforsaken loyal-faithfulness* in the providential leading *(inferred: chesed+emet = God's covenant character, praised)*.
- **lev (heart) — the *silent prayer* answered (24:45).** The finding is "before I had finished speaking in my **heart** (lev), behold, Rebekah came out" *(stated)*. The gem is *lev* as the place of **silent, inward prayer** — the servant prayed *in his heart* and was answered *before he finished*: the interior's *unspoken prayer met by immediate providence*; a distinct lev-use (the *praying* heart, against the evil 6:5, grieved 6:6, laughing 17:17, refreshed 18:5 hearts) *(inferred)*.
- **chesed + emet + o — the request for *loyal faithfulness* (24:49).** The finding is "if you will show **steadfast love** (chesed) and **faithfulness** (emet) to my master, tell me; and if not (o)…" *(stated)*. The operation *restates* the covenant-pair — the servant asks the family for *chesed-and-emet* (loyal, truthful dealing) in the decision *(inferred: chesed+emet again — the pair as the standard of dealing)*.
- **tov + ra + yakhol — "we cannot speak bad or good" (24:50).** The finding is "this has come from the LORD; we **cannot** (yakhol) speak **bad** (ra) or **good** (tov) to you" *(stated)*. The gem is the idiom: *ra* and *tov* — the **good-and-evil pair** (← the tree of the knowledge of *good and evil*, 2:9,17) — here in the sense "*we can say nothing* against it": the family *cannot gainsay* God's evident will; *yakhol* (human inability, ← 13:6; 15:5) before the divine leading *(inferred: tov/ra idiom = powerlessness to object)*.
- **qara + shaal — the *willing consent* (24:57–58).** The finding is "let us **call** (qara) the young woman and **ask** (shaal) her… they called Rebekah: Will you go? … **I will go**" *(stated)*. The gem is that Rebekah is *asked* (shaal) her consent and *freely says "I will go"* — the interior's **willing yes** to the leading (echoing Abraham's own obedient *going*, 12:4); consent, not compulsion *(inferred: shaal = the asking; the willing "I will go")*.
- **sane (hate) + barak — the blessing on Rebekah (24:60).** The finding is "they **blessed** (barak) Rebekah… may your offspring possess the gate of those who **hate** (sane) them" *(stated)*. The operations: **barak** — the family's *blessing*; **sane** — the *first "hate"* — the *enemies'* hostility over which the offspring will triumph (← oyev 22:17) *(inferred)*.
- **nacham (comforted) — grief *consoled by love* (24:67).** The finding is "Isaac took Rebekah… she became his wife, and he **loved** her; so Isaac was **comforted** (nacham) after his mother's death" *(stated)*. The gem is *nacham* — the word of God's *grief/regret* (6:6), the *comfort hoped* in Noah's naming (5:29) — here **consolation**: Isaac's *grief* (for Sarah, ABR-15) *met by comfort in love*; and *"he loved her"* (aheb — the **second "love"** in Scripture, after the *surrendered* love of 22:2) is now the **love that comforts**. The interior's grief *consoled by love* *(inferred: nacham = consolation; aheb = the comforting love, vs the surrendered love 22:2)*.

- **Near-context spans (coverage, low inner-being weight).** For completeness: the oath-*release* recurs (**naqah**, "you will be **free**", 24:8, ← 24:41); the *prayer/sign* is restated with **chesed**+**yada** (24:14, the same request as 24:12); the servant *runs to meet* Rebekah (**qara**-encounter, 24:17) and later Rebekah sees Isaac *coming to meet* them (**qara**, 24:65); Laban *heard* the account (**shama**, 24:30) and the servant *heard* their assent and worshipped (**shama**, 24:52); the servant *asked* whose daughter she was (**shaal**, 24:47); the family *called* Rebekah (**qara**, 24:58, the consent scene); and the particle **o** ("or/whether", glossed "desire" — a grammatical near-null, 24:50,55) carries *no* inner-being operation. Noted so no span is silently passed *(honest near-nulls / restatements)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the blessed patriarch's faith-charge (barak/mashal/shamar/naqah/natan 24:1–8):** the *comprehensively blessed* Abraham charges his *trusted steward* by oath (shamar/naqah) to seek a wife among his kin, *trusting God's leading* ("the LORD… will send his angel"); the land-*gift* (natan) grounds the faith.
2. **prayer, sign, and silent discernment (chesed/yada/charesh/lev 24:12–45):** the servant *prays for God's chesed* and a *sign to know* (yada), watches in *silence* (charesh) to discern, and finds his *heart's* (lev) prayer *answered before he finished* — the interior seeking and receiving guidance through *prayer, sign, stillness*, and *providence*.
3. **God's chesed-and-emet recognised (barak/chesed/emet 24:27,49):** the servant *praises* God for his *unforsaken steadfast-love-and-faithfulness*, and asks the family for the same *chesed-and-emet* — the providential leading read and required as *covenant loyalty*.
4. **the willing consent and the comfort of love (qara/shaal/nacham/aheb 24:57–67):** God's will is *unopposable* (tov/ra, yakhol 24:50); Rebekah *freely consents* ("I will go"); and Isaac *loves* her and is *comforted* (nacham) after his mother's death — the cycle's grief (ABR-15) *consoled by love*, the *second love* (comforting) answering the *first love* (surrendered, 22:2).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** barak — the *blessed* patriarch (24:1), the *doxology* (24:27,48), the *blessing on Rebekah* (24:60); mashal — the *steward's* rule; shamar/naqah — the oath's *condition/release*; natan — the land-*gift* and the *gifts*; **chesed — the *prayer* for God's steadfast love**, and **chesed+emet — the covenant-pair** (God's *unforsaken* loyal-faithfulness, recognised and required); yada — *knowing-by-sign*, *unrealized* (Rebekah), *discernment*; **charesh — the *first* "silence", the silent watchful discernment**; **lev — the *silent prayer* answered**; tov/ra + yakhol — *"cannot speak bad or good"* (powerless to object); qara/shaal — the *willing consent* ("I will go"); sane — the *first "hate"*; **nacham — grief *consoled*, and aheb the *comforting* love** (vs the surrendered love 22:2).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *trusting God's leading* (Abraham, the servant), *discerning in prayer and silence*, *freely consenting* (Rebekah), and *grieving then comforted by love* (Isaac); and the **divine** interior *steadfast in love-and-faithfulness*, *leading providentially*.
- **Threads:** chesed (← 19:19 God's saving; 20:13 compromised; 21:23 reciprocal → here God's covenant loyalty, paired with emet); the heart's prayer (lev, ← the heart-motif); nacham (← 5:29 comfort-hoped, 6:6 God's grief → here consolation); aheb/love (← 22:2 surrendered → here comforting; the two loves); the willing "I will go" (← 12:4 Abraham's going); tov/ra (← 2:9,17 the tree of good-and-evil, now an idiom); providence/leading (the cycle's guidance motif).
- **Guarded against:** inventing seven blessings from the recurring barak or six givings from natan (recurring operations, distinctions named); flattening chesed+emet into one word (they are a *pair* — loyal-love *and* faithful-truth); merging the yada-senses (sign / unrealized / discernment); missing that charesh (silence) is a *discernment* operation; reading nacham's *consolation* as identical to God's *grief* (6:6) or the *hoped-comfort* (5:29) — same root, distinct senses; importing NT bride typology (Isaac/Rebekah) — the operations the chapter states.

# Genesis 25:1–11 — inner-being passage reading (ABR-17-abraham-death)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-abraham-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the two `natan` (25:5, 25:6) treated distinctly.

---

## ABR-17-abraham-death · Genesis 25:1–11 · [the full death, the blessing passed] — the inheritance to the heir, the good old age fulfilled, and the promise carried on

**The passage.** "Abraham **gave** (natan) all he had to Isaac" (25:5); "to the sons of his concubines Abraham **gave** (natan) gifts, and while still **living** (chay) sent them away… eastward" (25:6); "the days of the years of Abraham's **life** (chayyim), 175 years, which he **lived** (chayah)" (25:7); "Abraham breathed his last and died in a **good** (tov) old age… and was gathered to his people" (25:8); "after Abraham's death, God **blessed** (barak) Isaac" (25:11).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **natan (give) #1 — *all* to the heir (25:5).** The finding is "Abraham **gave** (natan) all he had to Isaac" *(stated)*. The operation is the *inheritance* concentrated on the *covenant-heir* — the promised line secured in Isaac; the interior *settling its house* toward the promise *(inferred)*.
- **natan (give) #2 + chay — *gifts* to the rest, sent away (25:6).** The finding is "to the sons of his concubines Abraham **gave** (natan) **gifts**, and while still **living** (chay) sent them away… eastward, away from Isaac" *(stated)*. The gem is the *distinction*: Isaac receives *all* (the inheritance, 25:5); the others receive *gifts* and are *sent away* — the covenant-line *kept single*, the rest *provided for but separated*; and Abraham does this *while still living* (chay) — ordering his house *before* death *(inferred: natan #1 the inheritance vs natan #2 the parting-gifts; the line preserved)*.
- **chayyim + chayah — the *honoured* lifespan (25:7).** The finding is "the days of the years of Abraham's **life** (chayyim), 175 years, which he **lived** (chayah)" *(stated)*. The operation is the death-formula (← GEN-08) *dignifying* Abraham's life — the full count of his years *(inferred)*.
- **tov (good) — the *good, full, gathered* death (25:8).** The finding is "Abraham breathed his last and died in a **good** (tov) old age, an old man and full of years, and was **gathered to his people**" *(stated)*. The gem is *tov* naming the **fulfilled death**: a *good* old age, *full* of years, *gathered* — the exact promise of **15:15** ("you shall go to your fathers in *peace*, buried in a *good old age*") **kept**; the man of faith's life *completed and satisfied*. And "*gathered to his people*" (no span) hints at *continuity* — death as a *gathering*, not mere ceasing *(inferred: tov = the goodness of the completed life; the promised peaceful death fulfilled)*.
- **barak (blessed) — the blessing *passed to the heir* (25:11).** The finding is "after the death of Abraham, God **blessed** (barak) Isaac his son" *(stated)*. The gem is the *transmission*: the blessing (← 12:2) *does not die with Abraham* — God *blesses Isaac*, the covenant *continues* beyond the patriarch's death; and Isaac settles at *Beer-lahai-roi* (Hagar's well, El-Roi, 16:14) — a quiet echo of the God who sees *(inferred: barak passes to Isaac — the blessing outlives the man)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the house ordered toward the promise (natan 25:5–6):** Abraham *gives all* to Isaac and *gifts-and-sends* the rest — the covenant-line *kept single* and secure, the interior *settling its affairs* while still living.
2. **the fulfilled death (chayyim/chayah/tov 25:7–8):** Abraham dies *good, full, and gathered* — the promise of a *peaceful, good old age* (15:15) *kept*; the life of faith *completed and satisfied*, with a hint of *gathering* beyond death.
3. **the blessing outlives the man (barak 25:11):** God *blesses Isaac* — the blessing *transmitted*, the covenant *carried on*; the patriarch dies but the promise does not.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** natan — *all* to the heir (25:5) vs *gifts* to the rest, sent away (25:6); chayyim/chayah — the *honoured* lifespan; **tov — the *good, full, gathered* death** (the promise of 15:15 fulfilled); **barak — the blessing *passed to Isaac*** (the covenant outliving the man).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *completing* its life in faith — ordering its house, dying *good and full and gathered*; and the **divine** interior *transmitting the blessing* to the next generation.
- **Threads:** tov-good-death (← 15:15 the promised peaceful old age, now *kept*); the death-formula (← GEN-08, now over Abraham); barak (← 12:2, now *passed to Isaac*); Beer-lahai-roi / El-Roi (← 16:14); "gathered to his people" (the continuity-hint → the patriarchs' gathering).
- **Guarded against:** merging the two natan (inheritance vs parting-gifts — the line-preservation is the point); flattening tov here into generic "good" (it names the *fulfilled, satisfied* death, keeping 15:15); over-reading "gathered to his people" (a *hint* of continuity, not a doctrine — read what the verse gives); importing later resurrection theology.

# Genesis 25:12–18 — inner-being passage reading (ABR-18-ishmael-line)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-abraham-v1-20260704`). Every span in its verse; distinctions kept. A genealogical unit — thin inner-being yield; the *finding is the promise-to-the-outcast kept*.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; the single non-T2 span (chayyim, 25:17) engaged.

---

## ABR-18-ishmael-line · Genesis 25:12–18 · [the promise to the outcast kept] — the twelve princes, and Ishmael gathered like his father

**The passage.** The generations of Ishmael — twelve sons, "twelve princes according to their tribes" (25:12–16); "these are the years of the **life** (chayyim) of Ishmael, 137 years; he breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people" (25:17); his descendants "settled… over against all his kinsmen" (25:18).

### The operation

- **chayyim (life) — Ishmael's *honoured* death, the promise *fulfilled* (25:17).** The finding is "the years of the **life** (chayyim) of Ishmael, 137 years… he breathed his last and died, and was **gathered to his people**" *(stated)*. The gem is that this thin genealogy *records the promise kept*: **twelve princes** (25:16) fulfils God's word to Abraham — "I will make him a great nation… twelve princes" (17:20) — and to Hagar — "I will multiply your offspring… a great nation" (16:10; 21:18); and Ishmael dies "**gathered to his people**", the *same honour* given to Abraham (25:8, ABR-17). The outcast son, *heard and seen* by God (16:11,13; 21:17), is *blessed, multiplied, and gathered* — God's promise to the *cast-out* proves *as sure as* his promise to the heir *(inferred: the genealogy is the fulfilment; chayyim/gathered honours Ishmael as Abraham)*.
- **(25:18 — "over against all his kinsmen": no non-T2 span.)** The closing note that Ishmael's line settled "over against/in the presence of all his kinsmen" fulfils the word of 16:12 ("his hand against everyone… he shall dwell over against all his kinsmen") — read as context, the promise's *shape* kept *(no-span context)*.

### The web / note

The unit is a *bridge and a fulfilment*: it closes the Abraham cycle by showing that the promise to **Ishmael** — the *outcast* son — was *kept* (twelve princes, a great nation, an honoured death "gathered to his people", parallel to Abraham's). The *God who sees and hears the cast-out* (El-Roi, 16:13; "God hears", 16:11; 21:17) is *faithful to him too*. The covenant runs through *Isaac*, but the *blessing* reaches *Ishmael* — and the narrative *records both deaths in the same honoured terms*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** chayyim — Ishmael's *honoured* lifespan and death ("gathered to his people", as Abraham, 25:8); the *promise to the outcast fulfilled* (twelve princes, ← 17:20; 16:10; 21:18); the *dwelling "over against his kinsmen"* (← 16:12, no-span).
- **Whose interior:** minimal — the passage is a *genealogical fulfilment*; its inner-being weight is the *faithfulness of God to the cast-out son*.
- **Threads:** the outcast heard/seen (← 16:11,13; 21:17); the promise to Hagar/Ishmael (← 16:10; 17:20; 21:18, now *kept*); "gathered to his people" (← 25:8 Abraham — the *same* honour); the two sons (Isaac the covenant-line, Ishmael blessed-and-kept).
- **Guarded against:** manufacturing inner-being operations from a genealogy (thin by nature; the finding is the *promise kept*, not a forced reading); over-reading the single chayyim beyond the honoured death it names; importing later Ishmael/Isaac typology.

# Genesis 25:19–28 — inner-being passage reading (JAC-01-birth-oracle)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-jacob-v1-20260704`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; individual + interactive operations; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The naming *love* (25:28, aheb) and the *heel-grasp* (25:26, no non-T2 span) read as scene-context, anchored by atar/darash/ratsats/qara.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the two qara namings (25:25 vs 25:26) treated distinctly.

---

## JAC-01-birth-oracle · Genesis 25:19–28 · [the interior established at birth] — the barren-prayer, the womb-struggle, the oracle that inverts the order, and the two opposite characters

**The passage.** Isaac "**prayed** (atar) to the LORD… because she was **barren**" (25:21); "the children **struggled together** (ratsats) within her… so she went to **inquire** (darash) of the LORD" (25:22); the oracle — "two nations… the one shall be **stronger** (ammits) than the other, the older shall **serve** (avad) the younger" (25:23); the firstborn red and hairy, "they **called** (qara) his name Esau" (25:25); the second gripping the heel, "his name was **called** (qara) Jacob" (25:26); "the boys grew up (**gadal**), Esau a **skillful** (yada) hunter… Jacob a **quiet** (tam) man" (25:27); "Isaac loved Esau… but Rebekah loved Jacob" (25:28).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **atar (prayed) — the intercession that answers barrenness (25:21).** The finding is "Isaac **prayed** (atar) to the LORD for his wife, because she was barren, and the LORD **granted his prayer**" *(stated)*. The operation is atar — *entreat / plead* — the interior turning to God against the closed womb (the same barrenness-motif that gripped Abraham's cycle, but here *met by prayer* not by the scheming of ABR-06). The prayer is *heard*; conception follows. The interior's first move in the cycle is **entreaty, not seizure** *(inferred: atar = the pleading that receives)*.
- **ratsats (struggled together) — the strife *in the womb* (25:22a).** The finding is "the children **struggled together** (ratsats) within her" *(stated)*. The gem is that ratsats — *crush / smash / oppress* — is a *violent* word: the twins do not merely stir, they *crush each other*; the rivalry that will run the whole cycle is **prenatal, bodily, already violent** — the interior's conflict shown before either child can choose it *(inferred: ratsats = the crushing strife, the rivalry innate)*.
- **darash (inquire) — the perplexed interior *seeking* God (25:22b).** The finding is "'why is this happening to me?' So she went to **inquire** (darash) of the LORD" *(stated)*. The operation is darash — *seek / consult* — Rebekah's *bewildered* interior ("why am I thus?") *turning to God for the meaning* of what her body is doing. The interior *seeks an oracle* rather than resolving the confusion herself — a receiving-posture like Isaac's prayer *(inferred: darash = the seeking that asks God to interpret)*.
- **ammits (stronger) + avad (serve) — the oracle that *inverts* the order (25:23).** The findings are "the one shall be **stronger** (ammits) than the other" and "the older shall **serve** (avad) the younger" *(both stated)*. Two operations: **ammits** — *be strong / mighty* — sets the twins as unequal *powers*; **avad** — *serve* — but the strength runs *backward*, the *elder serving the younger*, the natural birthright-order **overturned by decree** before either has acted. This is the cycle's engine stated at the outset: the blessing will run *against* nature/precedence — and the whole grasping/deceiving struggle to come is the human attempt to *secure by scheme* what the oracle has already *given*. (avad here = the servitude *decreed*; contrast the avad Jacob will *do* for Rachel, JAC-09.) *(inferred: ammits/avad = the God-decreed inversion of the elder/younger order)*.
- **qara (called Esau) — the naming off the *red/hairy* body (25:25).** The finding is "he came out red, all his body like a hairy cloak, so they **called** (qara) his name Esau" *(stated)*. The operation is qara — *call/name* — here the name read *off the visible body* (Esau ≈ hairy; red → Edom later). The naming fixes Esau as the *outward, bodily, hunter* man *(inferred: qara = the name that fixes the outward nature)*.
- **qara (called Jacob) — the naming off the *heel-grasp* (25:26).** The finding is "his hand holding Esau's **heel**, so his name was **called** (qara) Jacob" *(stated)*. *Distinct from 25:25:* here qara names *not a body-feature but an act* — the *grasping of the heel* (Jacob ≈ heel/supplanter). The name itself *encodes the grasping interior*: he is called "**heel-grabber**" from the womb. Where Esau is named for *what he looks like*, Jacob is named for *what he does* — **seizes** — the supplanter-interior *inscribed in the name* it will spend the cycle either enacting or being delivered from *(inferred: qara = the name that fixes the grasping act; the two namings distinguished — body vs act)*.
- **gadal (grew) — the boys *grow up* into their divergence (25:27a).** The finding is "when the boys **grew up** (gadal)" *(stated)*. The operation is gadal — *become great / grow* — the *maturing* into the two settled characters that follow; a plain growth-word here (against 26:13 where gadal will mean *become rich/great*), marking the passage from oracle to lived difference *(inferred: gadal = the growth into character)*.
- **yada (skillful) — Esau's *knowing* of the field/hunt (25:27b).** The finding is "Esau was a **skillful** (yada) hunter, a man of the field" *(stated)*. The gem is that *skillful* here is **yada — *to know*** — Esau's is a *knowing of the hunt*, a practical, outward, bodily *know-how*; the interior aimed *at the field and the game* (yada in its craft-sense, distinct from the covenant-knowing of God) *(inferred: yada = practical outward mastery)*.
- **tam (quiet) — Jacob's *complete/settled* interior (25:27c).** The finding is "Jacob was a **quiet** (tam) man, dwelling in tents" *(stated)*. The gem: *quiet* is **tam — *complete / blameless / whole*** — the very word for Noah "blameless" (6:9) and the demand on Abraham "be blameless" (17:1). Applied to *Jacob the heel-grabber* it is arrestingly *ambivalent*: "**tam**" = *settled, contained, at home* (over against Esau's roving) — yet the man so described *will deceive his father*. The passage sets the tension the cycle explores: the *tam*/settled man who must *become* what the word claims *(inferred: tam = the settled/whole interior, held in tension with Jacob's grasping)*.
- **(25:28 — the parental loves, no non-T2 span.)** Flagged: "Isaac **loved** (aheb) Esau because he ate of his game, but Rebekah **loved** Jacob" carries no flagged non-T2 span, but it is the scene's *pivot into division*: the parents' *split affections* — Isaac's love *appetite-driven* ("because he ate of his game"), Rebekah's love *un-reasoned* (simply "loved Jacob") — the household **divided along the same line as the oracle**, seeding the deception of ch 27. Read as context, anchored by the oracle (25:23) and the two namings *(no-span context; the divided parental love)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **barrenness answered by prayer (atar 25:21):** the cycle opens not with a scheme but with *entreaty* — Isaac prays, God grants; the receiving-posture set (contrast the seized promise of ABR-06).
2. **the innate rivalry → the seeking interior (ratsats 25:22a → darash 25:22b):** the *crushing* struggle in the womb drives Rebekah to *seek* God for meaning — conflict provokes *inquiry*, not self-resolution.
3. **the oracle inverts the order (ammits/avad 25:23):** the answer is that *strength runs backward* — elder serves younger; the blessing is *decreed against precedence*, and everything that follows (birthright bought, blessing stolen) is the *human scramble* to secure by grasping what is *already given by decree*.
4. **the two names fix the two interiors (qara 25:25 vs 25:26):** Esau named for his *body* (outward), Jacob for his *act* (grasping) — the supplanter *inscribed in his name*.
5. **grown into divergence, and a divided love (gadal/yada/tam 25:27 → aheb 25:28):** the boys mature into *outward-knowing hunter* vs *settled/whole tent-man*, and the parents' *split love* aligns with the oracle's split — the stage set for the grasp.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** atar (the *entreaty* that answers barrenness); ratsats (the *crushing*, prenatal rivalry); darash (the *seeking* of the perplexed interior); ammits/avad (the *oracle's inversion* — elder serves younger, the cycle's engine); qara ×2 *distinguished* (Esau named off the *body*, Jacob off the *heel-grasping act*); gadal (growth into character); yada (Esau's *outward craft-knowing*); tam (Jacob "quiet/**whole**" — held in tension with his grasping); the *divided parental love* (no-span context).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *entreating* (Isaac), *seeking/bewildered* (Rebekah), and *innately rivalrous* (the twins); the **divine** interior *decreeing the inversion* (elder serves younger) — grace running against precedence.
- **Threads:** the supplanter-name (→ 27:36 "is he not rightly called Jacob? he has supplanted me twice"; → 32:28 the *re*-naming Israel); the *inverted order* (elder serves younger → the birthright bought JAC-02, the blessing stolen JAC-05); barrenness-answered (← Sarah, ABR; → Rachel, JAC-10 "God remembered Rachel"); tam ("blameless" ← Noah 6:9, Abraham 17:1 — now *ambivalently* of Jacob); the divided love (→ the ch-27 deception).
- **Guarded against:** reading Jacob's later transformation *back into* the birth-oracle (the text gives only the *name* and the *decree* here, not yet the man's change); softening ratsats into gentle "jostling" (the word is *crush*); flattening tam into mere "quiet/plain" when it is the loaded *whole/blameless* word (the tension is the finding); treating the two qara namings as one naming-operation (Esau off the body, Jacob off the act — distinct); importing Romans 9 ("Jacob I loved, Esau I hated") over the *domestic* divided-love the verse actually narrates — the operations shown, not the epistle.

# Genesis 25:29–34 — inner-being passage reading (JAC-02-birthright-sold)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-jacob-v1-20260704`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The *swear/sold* (25:33) and *ate-drank-rose-went* (25:34a) carry no non-T2 span — read as scene-context, anchored by zid/qara/natan/bazah.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; no repeated gloss in this passage.

---

## JAC-02-birthright-sold · Genesis 25:29–34 · [the grasp met by contempt] — the boiling stew, the birthright bought, and "Esau despised his birthright"

**The passage.** "Once when Jacob was **cooking** (zid) stew, Esau came in from the field, and he was **exhausted**" (25:29); "'let me eat some of that red stew, for I am exhausted!' Therefore his name was **called** (qara) Edom" (25:30); "'Sell me your birthright now'… 'I am about to die; of what use is a birthright?'… he swore… and sold his birthright" (25:31–33); "Jacob **gave** (natan) Esau bread and lentil stew… Thus Esau **despised** (bazah) his birthright" (25:34).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **zid (cooking/boiling) — the stew that becomes the *snare* (25:29).** The finding is "Jacob was **cooking** (zid) stew" *(stated)*. The operation is zid — *boil/seethe* — a plain domestic act, but *positioned* as the opportunity: Jacob is *already at the pot* when the famished brother arrives. The interior reads as *opportunistic readiness* — the settled/tent-man (tam, 25:27) *has the thing the field-man now craves*; the boiling stew is the *bait the moment supplies* *(inferred: zid = the cooking that, in context, becomes the leverage)*.
- **qara (called Edom) — the naming off the *craving* (25:30).** The finding is "'let me eat some of that **red** stew…' Therefore his name was **called** (qara) Edom" *(stated)*. The operation is qara — *call/name* — here the name (Edom ≈ red) fixed *off Esau's own greedy cry for the red stuff*; where JAC-01 named him for his *body* (hairy/Esau), here he is *re-named for his appetite* — the interior *defined by what it hungers for*. The naming *records the craving as identity* *(inferred: qara = the name that fixes the appetite; distinct from the birth-namings of JAC-01)*.
- **natan (gave) — the *giving that acquires* (25:34a).** The finding is "Jacob **gave** (natan) Esau bread and lentil stew" *(stated)*. The gem is the *inverted* natan: normally natan is *open-handed provision* (18:7; 24:53), but here Jacob's giving is *the closing of a bargain* — he *gives food to take a birthright*; a natan that **acquires rather than bestows**. The grasping interior's characteristic move: *give the lesser to seize the greater* — the same logic that will steal the blessing (ch 27) *(inferred: natan = the calculated giving that gains; contrast the bestowing natan)*.
- **bazah (despised) — the narrator's *verdict on Esau's interior* (25:34b).** The finding is "Thus Esau **despised** (bazah) his birthright" *(stated)*. The gem is that this is the passage's *one stated inside*: the narrator names Esau's interior operation as **bazah — *to despise / hold in contempt / count as worthless***. The birthright — the *decreed inheritance* — is *scorned* for a bowl; the string of blunt verbs ("ate, drank, rose, went") enacts the contempt. Where Jacob *grasps* (natan-to-acquire), Esau *despises* (bazah) — **two faults, not one**: the grasp and the contempt. The interior that *treats the holy thing as nothing* *(inferred: bazah = the contempt that counts the birthright worthless)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the moment supplies the bait (zid 25:29 → 25:30 the craving):** Jacob is *at the pot*; Esau arrives *famished and crying for the red*; the settled man holds what the field man now *cannot do without* — opportunity meeting appetite.
2. **appetite becomes name (qara/Edom 25:30):** Esau's *craving cry* is fixed as his *name* — the interior *defined by the hunger it could not master*.
3. **the calculated giving seizes the birthright (natan 25:34a):** Jacob *gives* bread-and-lentils *to take* the birthright — the grasping interior's signature (give-lesser-to-gain-greater), a rehearsal of the blessing-theft.
4. **the two faults named (bazah 25:34b):** the narrator's verdict falls on *Esau* — he **despised** the birthright — so the scene indicts *both* interiors: Jacob's *grasp* and Esau's *contempt*; the birthright *changes hands* because one *seizes* and the other *scorns*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** zid (the *boiling stew* that, in context, becomes the leverage); qara (Esau re-named *off his appetite* — Edom/red — distinct from the birth-namings of JAC-01); natan (the *calculated giving that acquires*, inverting the bestowing natan); bazah (the narrator's stated verdict — Esau **despised** the birthright, the *contempt* fault set beside Jacob's *grasp*).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *grasping/calculating* (Jacob) and *craving-then-despising* (Esau); no divine operation in view — the decreed inversion of JAC-01 now *worked out through two human faults*.
- **Threads:** the grasp (← Jacob "heel-holder" 25:26; → the blessing stolen JAC-05, the natan-to-acquire recurring); the despised birthright (→ the blessing Esau will *weep* for, 27:34,38 — too late; the interior that scorns then mourns); Edom/red (← the birth 25:25; → Esau's line JAC-19); the inverted-order oracle (25:23) *executed* here by sale.
- **Guarded against:** excusing Jacob because Esau "despised" it (the verse indicts *both* — I kept the grasp and the contempt as two distinct faults); reading Hebrews 12:16 ("Esau… sold his birthright") *back* as the verdict when the text's own verdict-word is *bazah* right here; over-reading zid into the homonym "act presumptuously" (the gloss and scene are *boil/cook* — the presumption is *inferred from the bargain*, not claimed off the word); flattening natan into simple generosity when the giving *acquires*.

# Genesis 26:1–11 — inner-being passage reading (JAC-03-isaac-gerar-fear)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-jacob-v1-20260704`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The *laughing* (26:8, tsachaq — the give-away) carries no non-T2 span — read as scene-context, anchored by yare/arakh/qara.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; natan (26:3,4) and barakh (26:3,4) each treated distinctly.

---

## JAC-03-isaac-gerar-fear · Genesis 26:1–11 · [the father's fault re-run in the son] — the promise renewed on Abraham's obedience, and the sister-lie repeated out of fear

**The passage.** Famine drives Isaac to Gerar; the LORD appears — "**bless** (barakh) you… I will **give** (natan) all these lands… establish the oath I swore to Abraham" (26:3); "I will **multiply** (ravah) your offspring… **give** (natan) all these lands… in your offspring all nations **blessed** (barakh)" (26:4); "because Abraham **obeyed** (shama) my voice and **kept** (shamar) my charge" (26:5); then the men **asked** (shaal) about his wife, "'She is my **sister**,' for he **feared** (yare) to say 'my wife'… because she was **attractive** (tov)" (26:7); "a **long** (arakh) time" passes, Abimelech sees him "laughing with Rebekah" (26:8); "Abimelech **called** (qara) Isaac… 'How could you say she is your sister?'" (26:9); "you would have brought **guilt** (asham) upon us" (26:10).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **barakh (bless you) — the covenant *personally renewed to Isaac* (26:3a).** The finding is "I will be with you and will **bless** (barakh) you" *(stated)*. The operation is barakh — *bless* — spoken now *directly to Isaac* (not merely inherited): the interior *addressed and reassured* against the famine that drove him. The Abrahamic blessing *lands on the son in his own right* *(inferred: barakh = the personal blessing spoken to Isaac)*.
- **natan (give all these lands) — the land-gift *to Isaac and his seed* (26:3b).** The finding is "to you and to your offspring I will **give** (natan) all these lands" *(stated)*. The operation is natan — *give* — the *land* bestowed, here framed *to-you-and-seed*: the gift **received**, not secured; the same *given* register as Abraham's cycle *(inferred: natan = the land freely given to Isaac's line)*.
- **natan (give to offspring) — the land-gift *within the innumerable-seed promise* (26:4b).** *Distinct from 26:3:* the finding is "I will **multiply** your offspring as the stars… and **give** (natan) to your offspring all these lands" *(stated)*. Here natan is *folded into the multiply-as-stars* clause — the land given *to a seed made countless*; the emphasis shifts from *Isaac-and-seed* (26:3) to *the vast seed* — the gift *enlarged*. Kept distinct: the same verb, but 26:3 = land to *you-and-line*, 26:4 = land to the *stars-numerous* offspring *(inferred: natan = the land given to the multiplied seed)*.
- **barakh (all nations blessed) — the *world-blessing through the seed* (26:4c).** *Distinct from 26:3a:* the finding is "in your offspring all the nations of the earth shall be **blessed** (barakh)" *(stated)*. Where 26:3a *blessed Isaac*, here barakh reaches *all nations* — the *outward, universal* blessing (← 12:3), not the *personal* one. Two barakh operations: the son blessed / the world blessed through the son *(inferred: barakh = the nations blessed in the seed; distinct from the personal blessing)*.
- **ravah (multiply) — the seed made *countless* (26:4a).** The finding is "I will **multiply** (ravah) your offspring as the stars of heaven" *(stated)*. The operation is ravah — *multiply/increase* — the creation-blessing word (1:28; 9:1) now the *covenant-increase* promise; the interior assured of *fruitfulness* against a barren start (25:21) *(inferred: ravah = the promised increase of the seed)*.
- **shama (obeyed) + shamar (kept) — the promise *grounded in Abraham's obedience* (26:5).** The findings are "Abraham **obeyed** (shama) my voice and **kept** (shamar) my charge, commandments, statutes, laws" *(both stated)*. Two distinct operations: **shama** — *hear/obey* (the *heeding* of God's voice — the very faculty misused at the fall, 3:17, here *rightly* used by Abraham); **shamar** — *keep/guard/obey* (the *sustained keeping* of the charge). The gem is *whose* obedience grounds the gift: **Isaac inherits on Abraham's shama/shamar** — the blessing *given* to the son *rests on the father's obedience*, not the son's; inheritance as *received on another's faithfulness* *(inferred: shama/shamar = the father's obedience, ground of the son's inheritance)*.
- **shaal (asked) — the *question* that triggers the fear (26:7a).** The finding is "when the men of the place **asked** (shaal) him about his wife" *(stated)*. The operation is shaal — *ask/inquire* — a neutral question that *exposes the interior's fear*; the outward prompt to which the fear-lie is the response *(inferred: shaal = the inquiry that occasions the fear)*.
- **yare (feared) — the *sister-lie repeated*, the father's exact fault (26:7b).** The finding is "'She is my sister,' for he **feared** (yare) to say 'my wife'… lest the men kill me" *(stated)*. The gem is the *repetition*: this is **Abraham's fear-lie run a third time** (12:11–13; 20:11) — now in *the son*, unprompted by any new revelation. yare — *fear/dread* — the *self-protecting* fear that *sacrifices the wife's safety* to preserve the self; the interior's inherited flaw, showing the fault-line *passes down the family* as surely as the blessing does *(inferred: yare = the self-protecting fear driving the inherited lie)*.
- **tov (attractive) — the beauty that *occasions* the fear (26:7c).** The finding is "because she was **attractive** (tov) in appearance" *(stated)*. The operation is tov — *good/pleasant* — here *of appearance*: Rebekah's beauty is the *external fact* the fearful interior *cannot trust God to guard*; the same tov-of-appearance that made Sarah a danger in Abraham's fear (12:11) *(inferred: tov = the desirable appearance that the fear fixes on)*.
- **arakh (a long time) — the lie *sustained over time* (26:8).** The finding is "when he had been there a **long** (arakh) time… Abimelech saw" *(stated)*. The operation is arakh — *be/grow long, prolong* — the fear-lie is not a single lapse but *maintained across a long dwelling*, until the truth *leaks* (the laughing/tsachaq — his own name's word — betrays the marriage). The interior's deception *has duration* before exposure *(inferred: arakh = the prolonging of the maintained lie)*.
- **qara (called Isaac) — the *summons to account* (26:9).** The finding is "Abimelech **called** (qara) Isaac and said, 'she is your wife!'" *(stated)*. *Distinct from the naming-qara of JAC-01/02:* here qara is *call-to / summon* — the pagan king **summons the patriarch to answer** for the lie; the interior *exposed and questioned by the outsider* (as Abraham was by the earlier Abimelech, 20:9) *(inferred: qara = the summons that calls the deceiver to account)*.
- **asham (guilt) — the *near-guilt* the lie risked (26:10).** The finding is "one might easily have lain with your wife, and you would have brought **guilt** (asham) upon us" *(stated)*. The gem is that the *pagan* names the moral stakes: **asham — *guilt / guilt-incurring*** — the fear-lie *endangered a whole people* with guilt; the outsider's conscience *sharper than the patriarch's fear*. The interior's self-protection is exposed as *reckless of others' guilt* *(inferred: asham = the corporate guilt the fear-lie nearly caused)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the blessing renewed and grounded (barakh/natan 26:3 → ravah/natan/barakh 26:4 → shama/shamar 26:5):** the covenant lands *personally on Isaac* (bless-you, land-given), *enlarges* (stars-many seed, all-nations blessed), and is *grounded on Abraham's obedience* — the son *receives* on the father's *shama/shamar*.
2. **the inherited fault surfaces (shaal 26:7a → yare 26:7b → tov 26:7c):** a mere *question* triggers the *self-protecting fear*, which fixes on Rebekah's *beauty* and repeats the father's sister-lie — the blessing inherited, and *so is the flaw*.
3. **the lie has duration, then leaks (arakh 26:8):** maintained *over a long time* until the marriage betrays itself (the tsachaq/laughing) — deception *sustained*, not momentary.
4. **the outsider exposes and names the stakes (qara 26:9 → asham 26:10):** the pagan king *summons* Isaac and *names the guilt* the lie risked — the interior's fear shown to be *reckless of a whole people's guilt*, the outsider's conscience the sharper.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** barakh ×2 *distinguished* (26:3 the *personal* blessing on Isaac / 26:4 *all nations* blessed through the seed); natan ×2 *distinguished* (26:3 land to *you-and-line* / 26:4 land to the *stars-many* seed); ravah (the promised *increase*); shama + shamar (the *father's* obedience, ground of the *son's* inheritance — inheritance *received on another's faithfulness*); shaal (the *question* that triggers fear); **yare — the sister-lie repeated, the father's fault in the son**; tov (the *beauty* the fear fixes on); arakh (the lie *sustained over time*); qara (the *summons to account*, distinct from naming); asham (the *near-guilt* on a whole people).
- **Whose interior:** the **divine** interior *blessing, giving, grounding the gift on obedience*; the **human** interior *fearful and self-protecting* (Isaac's inherited lie); and the **outsider's** interior *more morally alert* than the patriarch's fear (Abimelech naming the guilt).
- **Threads:** the fear-lie (← Abraham 12:11–13, 20:11 — now the *third* run, in the son; the family fault); inheritance grounded on the father's obedience (shama/shamar 26:5 ← Abraham's proven fear-of-God 22:12, 22:18); the wells and oath to come (JAC-04); tov-of-appearance (← 12:11 Sarah); asham/guilt named by a pagan (← 20:9 the earlier Abimelech).
- **Guarded against:** merging the two barakh and two natan into single "blessing/giving" operations (personal vs universal; land-to-line vs land-to-stars-seed — kept distinct); claiming Isaac's *own* obedience grounds the gift when 26:5 grounds it on *Abraham's* (the finding is *received* inheritance); reading the fear-lie as unique when it is the *inherited* repeat; importing a NT "sin of the fathers" doctrine over the plain *narrated* recurrence; treating qara here as a naming (it is a *summons*).

# Genesis 26:12–35 — inner-being passage reading (JAC-04-wells-oath)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-jacob-v1-20260704`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The wells' *stopping* (26:15) and the *feast* (26:30) carry no non-T2 span — read as scene-context.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the repeated qara (5 namings + 1 worship), riv (3 wells), barakh (3 senses), shalom (2) each treated distinctly.

---

## JAC-04-wells-oath · Genesis 26:12–35 · [the received blessing, and the yielding that makes room] — prosperity and envy, the wells re-dug and ceded, the night "fear not", and the covenant of peace

**The passage.** Isaac sowed and reaped a hundredfold, "the LORD **blessed** (barakh) him" (26:12); "the man **became rich** (gadal), **gained more and more** (gadel), very wealthy" (26:13); the Philistines **envied** (qana) his flocks and **servants** (avuddah) (26:14); "**mightier** (atsom) than we — go away" (26:16); he re-dug his father's wells and **called** (qara) them by the old names (26:18); found a **spring** (chay, living water) (26:19); the herdsmen **quarreled** (riv), so he **called** (qara) it Esek (26:20); another, quarreled, **called** (qara) Sitnah (26:21); another, no quarrel, "the LORD has **made room** (rachav)", **called** (qara) Rehoboth (26:22); the night word — "**Fear not** (yare)… I will **bless** (barakh) you and **multiply** (ravah) your offspring for Abraham's sake" (26:24); he **called** (qara) on the name of the LORD at an altar (26:25); "you **hate** (sane) me" (26:27); "let us **make** (karat) a **covenant** (berit)" (26:28); "do us no **harm** (raah)… we sent you away in **peace** (shalom)… you are the **blessed** (barakh) of the LORD" (26:29); they departed in **peace** (shalom) (26:31); he **called** it Shibah (26:33); Esau's wives made life **bitter** (morah) (26:35).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **barakh (blessed him) — the blessing *materialised in harvest* (26:12).** "The LORD **blessed** (barakh) him" *(stated)* — barakh here is the blessing *enacted in a hundredfold reaping*: the promised favour *made visible as produce*. The blessing *received* becomes *wealth*, not by scheme but by the LORD's act *(inferred: barakh = the blessing embodied in a harvest)*.
- **gadal (became rich) + gadel (gained more) — the *escalating* increase (26:13).** "The man **became rich** (gadal)… **gained more and more** (gadel) until very wealthy" *(stated)*. Two forms of one root, kept distinct: **gadal** — *became great* (the state reached); **gadel** — *growing / going-on-growing* (the *continuous* increase). The doubling *stresses the momentum* of the blessing — the interior *carried upward* by God's favour, wealth *compounding* *(inferred: gadal/gadel = greatness reached and greatness still-increasing)*.
- **qana (envied) — the blessing *provokes jealousy* (26:14).** "So the Philistines **envied** (qana) him" *(stated)* — qana, *be jealous/envious*: the blessed man's prosperity *breeds resentment* in the watchers. The first appearance of the envy-operation that will run through the wives' rivalry (30:1) and Laban's sons (31:1) — the interior *provoked by another's blessing* *(inferred: qana = the envy the blessing provokes in others)*.
- **avuddah (servants) — the *household-service* that marks the wealth (26:14).** "possessions of flocks and herds and many **servants** (avuddah)" *(stated)* — avuddah, *service / a body of servants*: a *mark* of the greatness, the retinue the blessing gathers *(inferred: avuddah = the servant-household of the prospered man)*.
- **atsom (mightier) — the blessed man grown *too vast* to keep near (26:16).** "Go away… you are much **mightier** (atsom) than we" *(stated)* — atsom, *be vast/numerous/mighty*: Abimelech *fears* the sheer *bigness* of the blessed man; the blessing makes Isaac *a power* the host cannot hold — expulsion by *intimidation* (contrast the oracle-word ammits, 25:23, of Esau/Jacob's strength) *(inferred: atsom = the fearsome vastness the blessing produces)*.
- **qara (re-named the wells) — *restoring the father's names* (26:18).** "he **called** (qara) them by the names his father had given" *(stated)* — the *first* qara of the chapter is *restorative*: Isaac *re-opens Abraham's stopped wells and re-gives Abraham's names* — the interior *honouring and continuing the father*, not innovating or seizing; continuity with the received inheritance *(inferred: qara = the naming that restores the father's markers)*.
- **chay (spring/living water) — the *living* water found (26:19).** "his servants dug and found a well of **spring** (chay, living) water" *(stated)* — chay, *living/alive*: *mayim chayyim*, **living water** — a *fresh, self-renewing* source (the lexeme's range reaches kin/community, but *here* it is the *living* water). The gift *found in the ground* over which the strife then breaks *(inferred: chay = living/fresh water, the contested good)*.
- **riv (Esek) + qara (Esek) — the *first contested* well (26:20).** "the herdsmen **quarreled** (riv)… he **called** (qara) it Esek, because they **contended**" *(stated)*. **riv** — *strive/contend/bring a suit*: the *dispute* over the living water; **qara** — the naming *records the strife itself* (Esek ≈ contention). The interior *does not fight to hold it* — he *names the strife and moves on* *(inferred: riv = the contention; qara = the name that memorialises it)*.
- **riv (Sitnah) + qara (Sitnah) — the *second, sharper* strife (26:21).** *Distinct from 26:20:* "they **quarreled** (riv) over that also, so he **called** (qara) it Sitnah" *(stated)*. Here riv *escalates* — Sitnah ≈ *hostility/accusation* (a harsher word than Esek's mere contention); the *second* well *more bitterly* opposed. Isaac *again yields* rather than contend — the *repeated* ceding, each time named *(inferred: riv = the sharpened hostility; qara = the name of enmity — distinct from Esek)*.
- **rachav (made room) + qara (Rehoboth) + riv (no quarrel) — the *strife ended, room given* (26:22).** *Distinct again:* "another well, and they did **not quarrel** (riv) over it… the LORD has **made room** (rachav)… he **called** (qara) it Rehoboth" *(stated)*. Three operations resolve the sequence: the *absence* of riv (the third well *uncontested*); **rachav** — *widen/enlarge*: the LORD *makes broad room*; **qara** — Rehoboth ≈ *broad places*. The gem is the *pattern*: the interior that *yields ground repeatedly* is *given room by God* — **space received, not seized** — "we shall be fruitful in the land." The Isaac-interior's non-grasping *rewarded with breadth* *(inferred: rachav = the God-given room that ends the strife; the yielding vindicated)*.
- **yare (Fear not) — the *reassurance* against the pressure (26:24a).** "the LORD appeared… '**Fear not** (yare), for I am with you'" *(stated)* — yare in the *dispelled* register (← 15:1 to Abraham): the interior, *pressed by envy and expulsion*, is met with *"do not fear"* — the same word that *drove the lie* (26:7) now *disarmed by God's presence* *(inferred: yare = the fear God dispels by his nearness)*.
- **barakh (I will bless) — the blessing *re-spoken*, grounded on Abraham (26:24b).** *Distinct from 26:12:* "I will **bless** (barakh) you and multiply your offspring **for Abraham's sake**" *(stated)*. Where 26:12 barakh was the blessing *enacted*, here it is *spoken as promise* and *grounded on Abraham* — again the son blessed *on the father's account* (as 26:5) — inheritance *received* *(inferred: barakh = the spoken blessing, grounded on the father)*.
- **ravah (multiply) — the *increase* re-promised (26:24c).** "and **multiply** (ravah) your offspring for my servant Abraham's sake" *(stated)* — ravah, *increase*: the seed-promise renewed against the household strife *(inferred: ravah = the promised increase re-spoken)*.
- **qara (called on the name) — *worship* at the altar (26:25).** *Distinct from all the naming-qara:* "he built an altar and **called** (qara) upon the name of the LORD" *(stated)* — here qara is *call-to / invoke*: not naming a well but **invoking God in worship** (as Abraham, 12:8; 13:4) — the interior's *response* to the theophany is *worship*, marking the place with an altar not a claim *(inferred: qara = the worship-invocation, distinct from the well-namings)*.
- **sane (hate) — the *acknowledged enmity* now reversed (26:27).** "why come to me, seeing you **hate** (sane) me and sent me away?" *(stated)* — sane, *hate*: Isaac *names the past hostility* of those now seeking him; the interior *honest about the enmity* that the coming covenant will *close* *(inferred: sane = the hostility owned before it is resolved)*.
- **karat (make) + berit (covenant) — the *treaty cut* by the former enemies (26:28).** "let us **make** (karat) a **covenant** (berit) with you" *(stated)* — **karat** *cut* + **berit** *covenant*: the Philistines *initiate a sworn pact* — the party that *envied and expelled* now *binds itself in peace*, *because* "we see the LORD is with you." The blessing *compels a covenant of peace from outsiders* (cf. Abraham & the earlier Abimelech, 21:27) *(inferred: karat/berit = the peace-treaty the blessing draws out of former enemies)*.
- **raah (harm) — the *harm renounced* in the oath (26:29a).** "that you will do us no **harm** (raah)" *(stated)* — raah, *harm/injury*: the covenant's *content* is the mutual renunciation of harm — the interior's *security* secured by oath *(inferred: raah = the harm the treaty forswears)*.
- **barakh (the blessed of the LORD) — the *outsiders' recognition* of the blessing (26:29b).** *Distinct from 26:12 and 26:24:* "you are now the **blessed** (barakh) of the LORD" *(stated)* — here barakh is *confessed by the Philistines*: the very ones who envied now *name Isaac as God's blessed*. The blessing *acknowledged by those it once provoked* — the third distinct barakh *(inferred: barakh = the blessing recognised aloud by former enemies)*.
- **shalom (in peace) — the *peaceful sending* (26:29c).** "we have… sent you away in **peace** (shalom)" *(stated)* — shalom, *peace/wholeness*: the Philistines *claim* to have dealt in peace; the term of the reconciliation *(inferred: shalom = the peace claimed as the basis of the pact)*.
- **shalom (departed in peace) — the peace *enacted* in parting (26:31).** *Distinct from 26:29:* "they exchanged oaths… and departed from him in **peace** (shalom)" *(stated)* — where 26:29 shalom was *claimed* as basis, here shalom is the *actual parting* — the treaty *concluded and the men leave whole*; peace *achieved*, not just asserted *(inferred: shalom = the peace realised in the parting)*.
- **qara (Shibah) — the *oath-well named* (26:33).** *Distinct from the earlier namings:* "he **called** (qara) it Shibah; therefore Beersheba" *(stated)* — qara names the well *for the oath* (Shibah ≈ oath/seven) — the naming that *commemorates the covenant of peace*, not a strife (contrast Esek/Sitnah) *(inferred: qara = the naming that memorialises the oath — distinct from the contention-namings)*.
- **morah (bitter) — the *domestic bitterness* that closes the chapter (26:35).** "Esau's wives made life **bitter** (morah) for Isaac and Rebekah" *(stated)* — morah, *bitterness/grief of spirit*: the chapter of *peace with outsiders* ends in *bitterness within the house* — the parents grieved by Esau's foreign wives; the interior's *domestic sorrow* that *motivates* the sending of Jacob for a wife (28:1) and shadows the coming deception *(inferred: morah = the bitterness of spirit within the family)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the blessing materialises and provokes envy (barakh 26:12 → gadal/gadel 26:13 → qana/avuddah 26:14 → atsom 26:16):** the received favour becomes a *hundredfold harvest* and *compounding wealth* and a *great household*, which *breeds envy* and makes Isaac *too mighty to keep near* — the blessing *itself* generates the conflict.
2. **the yielding that is given room (qara-restore 26:18 → chay 26:19 → riv/qara Esek 26:20 → riv/qara Sitnah 26:21 → riv-none/rachav/qara Rehoboth 26:22):** Isaac *re-digs and re-names the father's wells* (continuity, not seizure), finds *living water*, and when it is *contended* (Esek) and *more bitterly opposed* (Sitnah) he *yields and moves* each time — until God *makes room* (Rehoboth). The non-grasping interior *receives breadth* — space **given, not seized** (the Isaac counter-note to Jacob's grasping).
3. **fear dispelled, blessing re-grounded, worship offered (yare/barakh/ravah 26:24 → qara-worship 26:25):** pressed, the interior is met with *"fear not"*, the blessing *re-spoken on Abraham's account*, and *responds in worship* — building an altar, *invoking* God rather than *claiming* ground.
4. **enmity closed by covenant (sane 26:27 → karat/berit 26:28 → raah/barakh/shalom 26:29 → shalom 26:31 → qara-Shibah 26:33):** the *hated*-and-expelled man is *sought by his enemies*, who *cut a covenant*, *renounce harm*, *confess him blessed*, and *part in peace* — the well of the *oath* named; the blessing *turns former enemies into covenant-partners*.
5. **peace outside, bitterness inside (morah 26:35):** the chapter of *outward peace* ends on *inward grief* — Esau's foreign wives *embitter* the parents; the domestic sorrow that sets the stage for Jacob's sending and the deception to come.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** barakh ×3 *distinguished* (26:12 *materialised* in harvest / 26:24 *spoken* & grounded on Abraham / 26:29 *confessed* by former enemies); gadal + gadel (greatness *reached* + *still-increasing*); qana (the *envy* the blessing provokes); avuddah (the *servant-household*); atsom (grown *too vast* to keep near); qara *5 namings distinguished* (26:18 *restoring* the father's names / 26:20 Esek *contention* / 26:21 Sitnah *hostility* / 26:22 Rehoboth *room* / 26:33 Shibah *oath*) + 26:25 qara = *worship-invocation*; chay (the *living* water contested); riv ×3 (Esek *contend* / Sitnah *sharper hostility* / Rehoboth *no-quarrel*); rachav (God *makes room* — the yielding vindicated); yare (the *fear dispelled* — vs the fear that drove the lie 26:7); ravah (increase re-promised); sane (the *enmity owned*); karat/berit (the *peace-treaty* drawn from enemies); raah (the *harm forsworn*); shalom ×2 (*claimed* basis / *realised* parting); morah (the *domestic bitterness* that closes).
- **Whose interior:** the **divine** interior *blessing, dispelling fear, making room, grounding the gift on Abraham*; the **human** interior *non-grasping and yielding* (Isaac cedes the wells, worships, receives room) — the Isaac counter-image to Jacob's seizing; the **outsiders'** interior turning from *envy/hatred* to *covenant/peace*; and the *bitterness* within the house (Esau's wives).
- **Threads:** *received vs grasped* (Isaac *yields* the wells and is *given room* — contrast the birthright *bought* JAC-02, the blessing *stolen* JAC-05); the fear-lie's fear (26:7) vs the *"fear not"* (26:24); inheritance grounded on Abraham (26:24 ← 26:5, 22:18); envy (qana → 30:1 Rachel, 31:1 Laban's sons); covenant with an Abimelech (← 21:22–34); the domestic bitterness (morah 26:35 → the sending of Jacob 28:1, the deception 27).
- **Guarded against:** collapsing the three barakh into one "blessing" (materialised / spoken / confessed — distinct); lumping the five well-namings or the three riv into single operations (Esek/Sitnah/Rehoboth each a *distinct stage* — contention, hostility, room; and 26:25 qara is *worship* not naming); reading Isaac's yielding as mere weakness when the text *rewards* it with rachav/room (the finding is the *vindicated non-grasping*); importing a "living water" NT symbol over the plain *fresh-water* the verse means; over-reading morah into a theological judgment when the verse states *domestic grief of spirit*.

# Genesis 27:1–29 — inner-being passage reading (JAC-05-blessing-stolen)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-jacob-v1-20260704`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. The *disguise* (27:15–16, goat-skins/garments) and the *lie* "I am Esau" (27:19,24 — no non-T2 span) read as scene-context, anchored by shama/barakh/nephesh.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 8 barakh (27:4,7,10,19,23,25,27,29), 3 nephesh, 2 shama-hear, 2 shama-obey each treated distinctly.

---

## JAC-05-blessing-stolen · Genesis 27:1–29 · [the blessing seized by deceit] — the blind father's soul-blessing purposed for Esau, overheard and redirected by scheme, and conferred on the disguised son

**The passage.** Blind Isaac **called** (qara) Esau — "I am old, I do not **know** (yada) my death… hunt game… that my **soul** (nephesh) may **bless** (barakh) you" (27:1–4); Rebekah was **listening** (shama) (27:5); "I **heard** (shama) your father… he will **bless** (barakh) you before the LORD" (27:6–7); "**obey** (shama) my voice" (27:8); "two **good** (tov) young goats… that he may **bless** (barakh) you" (27:9–10); Jacob fears "a **curse**… not a **blessing** (berakhah)" (27:12); "**obey** (shama) my voice" (27:13); the disguise; "I am Esau… that your **soul** (nephesh) may **bless** (barakh) me" (27:19); "the voice is Jacob's, the hands are Esau's… so he **blessed** (barakh) him" (27:22–23); "that my soul (nephesh) may **bless** (barakh) you… he ate and drank" (27:25); "he smelled his garments and **blessed** (barakh) him" (27:27); "God **give** (natan) you… **plenty** (rov) of grain" (27:28); "peoples **serve** (avad) you… **cursed** (arar) be who curses you, blessed (barakh) who blesses you" (27:29).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **qara (called Esau) — the *summons to bless* (27:1).** "he **called** (qara) Esau… 'My son'" *(stated)* — qara, *call-to*: the blind father *summons the elder to receive the blessing*; the scene's opening move, and the sound Rebekah will *overhear* *(inferred: qara = the summons that sets the blessing in motion)*.
- **yada (know) — the *not-knowing* of death that hurries the blessing (27:2).** "I am old; I do not **know** (yada) the day of my death" *(stated)* — yada in the *negated* mode: Isaac's *ignorance of his death* is what *presses* him to bless *now*; the interior's *mortality-awareness* driving the act — and (dramatic irony) the same not-knowing that will *fail to recognise* the disguised son *(inferred: yada = the not-knowing of death that hastens the blessing)*.
- **nephesh (soul) + barakh (bless you) — Isaac's *whole-self intent* to bless Esau (27:4).** "that my **soul** (nephesh) may **bless** (barakh) you before I die" *(stated)*. **nephesh** — *soul / very self / life*: the blessing purposed from the *deepest self*, not a formula — a *whole-life* bestowal. **barakh (1st)** — the *purposed* blessing, *aimed at Esau*, and *appetite-linked* ("delicious food such as I love"). The interior *wills its deep-self blessing toward the elder* *(inferred: nephesh/barakh = the whole-souled blessing intended for Esau)*.
- **shama (listening) — Rebekah's *covert overhearing* (27:5).** "Rebekah was **listening** (shama) when Isaac spoke" *(stated)* — shama, *hear*: the *secret listening* that *arms the scheme* (as Sarah overheard, 18:10 — but there incredulous, here *plotting*); the interior *eavesdropping to seize the moment* *(inferred: shama = the covert overhearing that launches the plot)*.
- **shama (heard) — the *reported hearing* that authorises the scheme (27:6).** *Distinct from 27:5:* "I **heard** (shama) your father speak" *(stated)* — here shama is *cited as warrant*: Rebekah *reports* her hearing to *justify and instruct* Jacob; the overhearing turned into *the basis of a command* *(inferred: shama = the hearing invoked to authorise the deception)*.
- **barakh (he will bless you) — the intent *re-told, heightened "before the LORD"* (27:7).** *Distinct from 27:4:* "that I may bless you **before the LORD** before I die" *(stated)* — Rebekah's re-telling *adds "before the LORD"*, sacralising the blessing she is about to *subvert*; the interior *invokes God's presence over the very blessing it will steal* *(inferred: barakh = the God-witnessed blessing, cited as she plots to divert it)*.
- **shama (obey) — the *command to obey* the scheme (27:8).** *Distinct from the hear-senses:* "**obey** (shama) my voice as I command you" *(stated)* — shama in the *obey* mode: Rebekah demands *filial obedience* — but *to a deception*. The gem: the *right* faculty (heeding a parent) *bent to a wrong end* — obedience *weaponised* *(inferred: shama = obedience commanded, but toward deceit)*.
- **tov (good) — the *good* goats for the counterfeit dish (27:9).** "two **good** (tov) young goats… food such as he loves" *(stated)* — tov, *good/pleasant*: the *choice* kids for the *counterfeit* of Esau's game; the interior's care *lavished on the deception's props* *(inferred: tov = the good goats serving the fraud)*.
- **barakh (that he may bless you) — the blessing *redirected to Jacob* (27:10).** *Distinct from 27:4,7:* "bring it to your father… that he may **bless** (barakh) *you* [Jacob]" *(stated)* — the *pivot*: the blessing purposed for Esau (27:4) is now *aimed at Jacob* by the scheme; the same act, its *recipient switched by deceit* *(inferred: barakh = the blessing re-aimed at the wrong son)*.
- **berakhah (blessing) — Jacob's *fear of the curse-risk* (27:12).** "I shall seem to be **mocking**… and bring a **curse** upon myself and not a **blessing** (berakhah)" *(stated)* — berakhah, the *noun*: Jacob's hesitation is **not moral** — he fears *being caught and cursed*, losing *the blessing itself*; the interior *calculates the risk*, not the wrong. The gem is *what he fears*: exposure, not sin *(inferred: berakhah = the prize whose loss Jacob fears — a risk-calculation, not a conscience)*.
- **shama (obey) — the command *repeated over the hesitation* (27:13).** *Distinct from 27:8:* "only **obey** (shama) my voice, and go" *(stated)* — the *second* obey-command *overrides Jacob's fear*; Rebekah takes the curse on herself and *presses the obedience through*; obedience *insisted upon* against the flinch *(inferred: shama = obedience re-commanded to push the wavering son forward)*.
- **nephesh (soul) + barakh (bless me) — the blessing *solicited under the lie* (27:19).** *Distinct from 27:4:* "I am Esau… that your **soul** (nephesh) may **bless** (barakh) me" *(stated)* — Jacob *echoes Isaac's own phrase* (27:4) *inside the lie*: the deep-self blessing now *asked for under a false name*; the interior *appropriating the very words of the intended blessing to steal it* *(inferred: nephesh/barakh = the soul-blessing solicited by the impostor, mirroring 27:4)*.
- **barakh (blessed him) — the blessing *conferred on the disguised son* (27:23).** *Distinct — the deed itself:* "he did not recognise him… so he **blessed** (barakh) him" *(stated)* — the *pivotal barakh*: the blessing *actually bestowed* on the deceiver; Isaac's *senses divided* ("the voice is Jacob's, the hands are Esau's", 27:22) yet the touch prevails — the blessing *lands on the wrong son through deceived senses*. The irrevocable act *(inferred: barakh = the blessing conferred, the deception succeeding through the failed senses)*.
- **nephesh (soul) + barakh (bless you) — the *renewed intent* at the meal (27:25).** *Distinct from 27:4,19:* "that my **soul** (nephesh) may **bless** (barakh) you… he ate and drank" *(stated)* — Isaac *repeats the soul-blessing purpose* just before the formal words, *after eating the counterfeit game and wine*: the blessing *nourished by the fraud*, the deep self *satisfied and ready to bless* the impostor *(inferred: nephesh/barakh = the soul-blessing renewed, fed by the deception)*.
- **barakh (blessed him) — the blessing *sealed by the scent* (27:27).** *Distinct — the sensory seal:* "he smelled his garments and **blessed** (barakh) him… 'the smell of my son is as a field the LORD has blessed'" *(stated)* — the *last sense* (smell of Esau's garments) *clinches* the deception; barakh *pronounced* over the *scent* — the field-smell *(inferred: barakh = the blessing sealed by the deceiving scent)*.
- **natan (give) + rov (plenty) — the blessing's *content: God-given abundance* (27:28).** "God **give** (natan) you the dew… **plenty** (rov) of grain and wine" *(stated)*. **natan** — the blessing *invokes God's giving* (dew, fatness); **rov** — *abundance*: the *material fullness* pronounced. The blessing's substance is *God-given plenty* — ironically *received* language over a *seized* blessing *(inferred: natan/rov = the God-given abundance the blessing confers)*.
- **avad (serve) + arar (cursed) + barakh (blessed) — the blessing's *content: lordship and reciprocal curse/bless* (27:29).** "peoples **serve** (avad) you… be lord over your brothers… **cursed** (arar) be who curses you, **blessed** (barakh) who blesses you" *(stated)*. Three operations close the blessing: **avad** — *nations serve* him (the oracle's inversion, 25:23, *pronounced into effect* — the elder's servitude now spoken over Esau); **arar** — the *curse* on his enemies; **barakh (8th)** — the *reciprocal blessing* on his friends — the Abrahamic curse/bless formula (12:3) *transferred to Jacob*. The stolen blessing carries the *covenant lordship and the curse/bless reciprocity* *(inferred: avad/arar/barakh = lordship + the reciprocal curse-and-bless, the covenant content conferred)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the blind father's whole-souled intent (qara 27:1 → yada 27:2 → nephesh/barakh 27:4):** *summoning* Esau, *pressed by not-knowing his death*, Isaac purposes a *deep-self blessing* on the elder — *appetite-linked* to the game.
2. **overhearing → scheme → weaponised obedience (shama-hear 27:5 → shama-heard 27:6 → barakh-heightened 27:7 → shama-obey 27:8/27:13 → barakh-redirected 27:10):** Rebekah *secretly hears*, *cites the hearing as warrant*, *sacralises the blessing "before the LORD"*, and *commands Jacob's obedience* — the blessing *re-aimed at the wrong son*; the parent-heeding faculty *bent to deceit*.
3. **the calculating hesitation (berakhah 27:12):** Jacob flinches — but for *fear of the curse-if-caught*, not conscience; the interior *weighs the risk to the prize*, and is *pushed through* (27:13).
4. **the lie appropriates the very words (nephesh/barakh 27:19):** disguised, Jacob *echoes Isaac's own "that your soul may bless me"* — stealing the blessing *in its own language*.
5. **the blessing conferred through failed senses (barakh 27:23 → nephesh/barakh 27:25 → barakh 27:27):** hearing *doubts* ("the voice is Jacob's") but touch, taste (the counterfeit meal), and smell *prevail* — the deep-self blessing *bestowed on the impostor*, *fed and sealed by the fraud*.
6. **the covenant content pronounced (natan/rov 27:28 → avad/arar/barakh 27:29):** the stolen blessing carries *God-given abundance*, *lordship (the oracle's inversion spoken into effect)*, and the *Abrahamic curse/bless reciprocity* — the whole inheritance *seized by deceit*, over against Isaac's own *received* blessing (JAC-04).

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** qara (the *summons* to bless); yada (the *not-knowing of death* that hurries it — and the failed recognition); barakh **×8 distinguished** (27:4 *purposed* for Esau / 27:7 *heightened "before the LORD"* / 27:10 *redirected* to Jacob / 27:19 *solicited under the lie* / 27:23 *conferred* on the disguised son / 27:25 *renewed*, fed by the fraud / 27:27 *sealed by the scent* / 27:29 the *reciprocal* curse/bless formula); nephesh ×3 (27:4 Isaac's *purposed* soul-blessing / 27:19 Jacob *echoing* it in the lie / 27:25 Isaac's *renewed* soul-intent); shama ×4 across two senses (27:5 *overhearing* / 27:6 hearing *cited as warrant* / 27:8, 27:13 obedience *commanded then re-commanded* toward deceit); tov (the *good goats* serving the fraud); berakhah (Jacob's *risk-fear*, not conscience); natan/rov (*God-given abundance*); avad (the *oracle's inversion spoken into effect*); arar (the *curse* on enemies).
- **Whose interior:** the **human** interior *blind and appetite-led* (Isaac), *scheming and overhearing* (Rebekah), *calculating and grasping* (Jacob — fearing the curse, not the sin); no divine word here — God is *invoked* by the deceivers ("before the LORD" 27:7; "the LORD your God granted me success" 27:20, no span) but does not speak: the blessing *seized*, not *given*.
- **Threads:** *grasping vs received* (the blessing *stolen* here vs Isaac's *received* blessing JAC-04, vs the wrestling-blessing *given through brokenness* JAC-15); the oracle's inversion (avad 27:29 ← 25:23 "elder serve younger" — now *pronounced*); the supplanter (→ 27:36 "he has supplanted me"); overhearing (← Sarah 18:10, but incredulous not plotting); the deep-self irrevocable blessing (nephesh → the blessing *cannot be recalled* when Esau comes, JAC-06); shama-obedience bent (← 3:17 the fall's mis-heeding).
- **Guarded against:** collapsing the 7 barakh or 3 nephesh into one blessing-operation (purposed / heightened / redirected / solicited / conferred / renewed / reciprocal — each a *distinct stage of the theft*); reading Jacob's 27:12 flinch as conscience when the verse says he fears *a curse* (risk, not repentance); importing the NT "Jacob have I loved" or "faith" framing over the *deceit* the chapter narrates; treating avad here as generic service when it *executes the birth-oracle*; making the counterfeit meal a mere detail when the *senses* (taste/smell/touch) are precisely what *carry* the deception past the doubting *hearing*.
