# Genesis 42:1–38 — inner-being passage reading (JOS-08-first-descent-guilt)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-joseph-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: the **brothers** (buried guilt surfacing), **Joseph** (testing, remembering, weeping in secret), and **Jacob** (grief renewed). The "life of Pharaoh" oath (`chay`, 42:15–16) reads as the Egyptian oath-formula.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 3 shama, 2 chayah, 2 qara, 2 qasheh, 3 yada, 3 natan, 2 yare each treated distinctly.

---

## JOS-08-first-descent-guilt · Genesis 42:1–38 · [the dreams fulfilled and the guilt surfaced] — the roughness, the confession, the hidden weeping

**The passage.** "Go buy grain, that we may **live** (chayah)" (42:2); Jacob feared harm might **happen** (qara) to Benjamin (42:4); Joseph the **governor** (shallit), the brothers bow (42:6); he spoke **roughly** (qasheh) (42:7); Joseph **remembered** (zakhar) the dreams (42:9); "by the **life** (chay) of Pharaoh… whether there is **truth** (emet) in you" (42:15, 42:16); "do this and **live** (chayah), for I **fear** (yare) God" (42:18); "your words **verified** (aman)" (42:20); "we are **guilty** (ashem)… we saw the **distress** (tsarah) of his **soul** (nephesh) when he **begged** (chanan) and we did not **listen** (shama)" (42:21); Reuben — "did I not say, do not **sin** (chata)? … a **reckoning** (darash) for his blood; you did not **listen** (shama)" (42:22); they did not **know** (yada) Joseph **understood** (shama) (42:23); he turned and **wept** (bakhah) (42:24); he **gave** (natan) orders to fill the bags (42:25); the money **given** (natan) back found (42:27); their **hearts** (lev) failed, **trembling** (charad) — "what has God done?" (42:28); "he spoke **roughly** (qasheh)" (42:30); "by this I shall **know** (yada)… **leave** (nuach) one brother… I shall **know** (yada), and I will **deliver** (natan) your brother" (42:33, 42:34); they were **afraid** (yare) at the money (42:35); "you would bring my gray hairs with **sorrow** (yagon) to Sheol" if harm **happen** (qara) (42:38).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **shama (heard) + chayah (live) — the *survival errand* (42:2).** "I have **heard** (shama) there is grain… go, that we may **live** (chayah) and not die" *(stated)*. **shama** — Jacob *hears* of grain; **chayah** — the *survival* motive: the famine *drives the brothers toward Joseph* — the interior of *a family seeking to live* *(inferred: shama/chayah = the survival errand that sends the brothers to Egypt)*.
- **qara (happen) — Jacob's *dread for Benjamin* (42:4).** "he feared harm might **happen** (qara) to him" *(stated)* — qara in the *chance/befall* sense: the gem is the *father's dread* — he *withholds Benjamin* (Rachel's other son), *fearing to lose him too*; the interior *guarding the last of the beloved* *(inferred: qara = the dread of harm befalling Benjamin)*.
- **shallit (governor) — the *dreams fulfilled* (42:6).** "Joseph was **governor** (shallit)… his brothers bowed with faces to the ground" *(stated)* — shallit, *ruler*: the gem is the *fulfilment* — the brothers *bow before Joseph* (← the sheaves/stars bowing, 37:7,9) *unknowing*; the *resented dominion* now *fact* *(inferred: shallit = the governor before whom the dreams are fulfilled)*.
- **qasheh (roughly) — the *disguising harshness* (42:7).** "he treated them as strangers and spoke **roughly** (qasheh)" *(stated)* — qasheh, *hard/severe*: the gem is that the *roughness is a disguise* — Joseph *conceals himself* to *test* them; the interior *hiding recognition behind severity* *(inferred: qasheh = the disguising harshness that masks recognition)*.
- **zakhar (remembered) — the *dreams recalled* (42:9).** "Joseph **remembered** (zakhar) the dreams he had dreamed of them" *(stated)* — zakhar, *remember*: the gem is that *seeing them bow, he remembers his dreams* — the memory *shapes the test* (he probes for the youngest, Benjamin); the interior *reading the present against the old dream* *(inferred: zakhar = the dreams remembered, shaping the test)*.
- **chay (life of Pharaoh) + emet (truth) — the *oath and the test of honesty* (42:15, 42:16).** "by the **life** (chay) of Pharaoh… whether there is **truth** (emet) in you" *(stated)*. **chay** — the *Egyptian oath* ("by Pharaoh's life"); **emet** — *truth/honesty*: the gem is *what Joseph tests* — *whether they are truthful* (about the youngest, the "one who is no more"); the interior *probing their honesty* *(inferred: chay/emet = the oath-bound test of the brothers' truthfulness)*.
- **chayah (live) + yare (fear God) — the *reassurance* of a God-fearer (42:18).** *chayah distinct from 42:2:* "do this and you will **live** (chayah), for I **fear** (yare) God" *(stated)*. **chayah** — the *promise of life* (softening the test); **yare** — the gem: *"I fear God"* — Joseph *reassures them he will not abuse his power* (a God-fearer, ← the midwives 1:17; the fear-of-God that restrains). The interior *identifying itself as God-fearing*, its severity *bounded by reverence* *(inferred: chayah/yare = the God-fearer's reassurance — power bounded by the fear of God)*.
- **aman (verified) — the *test's proof* (42:20).** "your words will be **verified** (aman), and you shall not die" *(stated)* — aman, *be confirmed/faithful*: the *test's condition* — bring Benjamin and *be proven true*; the interior-context of *truth put to proof* *(inferred: aman = the test that will verify their words)*.
- **ashem (guilty) + tsarah (distress) + nephesh (soul) + chanan (begged) + shama (listen) — the *buried guilt surfaced* (42:21).** "we are **guilty** (ashem) concerning our brother, in that we saw the **distress** (tsarah) of his **soul** (nephesh) when he **begged** (chanan) us and we did not **listen** (shama)" *(stated)*. The **central gem**: the *20-year-buried guilt surfaces* — under pressure the brothers *name their sin to one another*. **ashem** — *guilt*; **tsarah** — Joseph's *distress* they *saw*; **nephesh** — his *soul*'s anguish; **chanan** — he *begged* (the detail *not narrated in ch37* — now *remembered*: Joseph *pleaded* and they *ignored*); **shama** — they *did not listen*. The interior's *long-suppressed guilt breaking surface* — conscience *catching up* *(inferred: ashem/tsarah/nephesh/chanan/shama = the buried guilt surfaced — the ignored pleading remembered)*.
- **chata (sin) + darash (reckoning) + shama (listen) — Reuben's *"I told you"* and the *reckoning* (42:22).** *shama distinct from 42:21:* "'did I not say, do not **sin** (chata) against the boy? you did not **listen** (shama); now a **reckoning** (darash) for his blood'" *(stated)*. **chata** — the *sin* named; **shama** — the *not-listening to Reuben* (distinct from not-listening to Joseph, 42:21); **darash** — the gem: *"a reckoning is required"* (darash = *seek/require*) — the sense that *the blood is being called to account*; the interior *reading a divine reckoning* on the old sin *(inferred: chata/shama/darash = Reuben's reproach and the sense of a divine reckoning for the sin)*.
- **yada (know) + shama (understood) — the *hidden comprehension* (42:23).** "they did not **know** (yada) that Joseph **understood** (shama) them, for there was an interpreter" *(stated)*. **yada** — the brothers' *ignorance*; **shama** in the *understand* sense — Joseph *hears their confession*: the gem is the *dramatic irony* — they *confess their guilt in his very hearing*, thinking him a stranger; the interior *overhearing the guilt it caused* *(inferred: yada/shama = the confession overheard by the one it concerns)*.
- **bakhah (wept) — the *hidden weeping* (42:24).** "he turned away from them and **wept** (bakhah)" *(stated)* — bakhah, *weep*: the gem — *hearing their guilt-confession, Joseph weeps* — the *disguise conceals a weeping heart*; the interior's *compassion barely held* (he *returns and composes himself*, binds Simeon). Not vengeance but *grief and love* behind the severity *(inferred: bakhah = the hidden weeping — compassion behind the disguise)*.
- **natan (gave) — the *secret kindness* begun (42:25).** "he **gave** (natan) orders to fill their bags… replace each man's money" *(stated)* — natan, *give*: the gem is the *hidden generosity* — even while testing, Joseph *returns their money* and *provisions them*; the interior's *kindness working under the disguise* *(inferred: natan = the secret provision under the test)*.
- **natan (given back) — the *money found* (42:27).** *natan distinct from 42:25:* "he saw his money **put back** (natan) in his sack's mouth" *(stated)* — the *returned money discovered* — the kindness *misread as threat*; the interior-context of *a mercy that alarms* *(inferred: natan = the returned money found — mercy that alarms)*.
- **charad (trembling) + lev (hearts) — the *dread reading God's hand* (42:28).** "their **hearts** (lev) failed, they **trembled** (charad): 'what is this God has done to us?'" *(stated)*. **charad** — *tremble* (← Isaac's violent trembling, 27:33; Jacob's family); **lev** — *heart*: the gem — the brothers *read the returned money as God's doing* — *"what has God done to us?"* — the interior *sensing divine reckoning* in the unexplained; guilt *interpreting every reversal as judgment* *(inferred: charad/lev = the trembling hearts reading God's judgment in the returned money)*.
- **qasheh (roughly) — the *rough speech reported* (42:30).** *qasheh distinct from 42:7:* "'the lord of the land spoke **roughly** (qasheh) to us'" *(stated)* — the *report* of the harshness to Jacob (42:7 the act, 42:30 the retelling) *(inferred: qasheh = the rough speech reported to the father)*.
- **yada (know) + nuach (leave) + yada (know) + natan (deliver) — the *test's terms recounted* (42:33, 42:34).** "'by this I shall **know** (yada) you are honest: **leave** (nuach) one brother… bring the youngest, then I shall **know** (yada)… and I will **deliver** (natan) your brother'" *(stated)*. **yada ×2** — the *knowing* the test will yield (distinct from 42:23); **nuach** — *leave/deposit* (Simeon held); **natan** — the *release* promised. The interior-context of *the condition laid on the family* *(inferred: yada/nuach/natan = the test's terms — a brother held, the youngest demanded)*.
- **yare (afraid) — the *fear at the money* (42:35).** *yare distinct from 42:18:* "when they saw the money, they were **afraid** (yare)" *(stated)* — where 42:18 was Joseph's *fear of God*, 42:35 is the brothers' *fear/dread* at the unexplained money — the interior *alarmed by the mercy it cannot read* *(inferred: yare = the brothers' fear at the returned money)*.
- **yagon (sorrow) + qara (happen) — Jacob's *renewed grief and refusal* (42:38).** "'if harm **happen** (qara) to him, you would bring my gray hairs with **sorrow** (yagon) to Sheol'" *(stated)*. **yagon** — *grief/sorrow*; **qara** *distinct from 42:4* — the *second* dread of harm to Benjamin: the gem is the *father's grief renewed* — "Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more" — he *refuses to risk Benjamin*, expecting *sorrow to the grave* (← 37:35). The interior *clinging to the last beloved son* *(inferred: yagon/qara = the father's renewed grief, refusing to risk Benjamin)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the errand into the dreams' fulfilment (shama/chayah 42:2 → qara 42:4 → shallit 42:6):** the *famine drives* the brothers to Egypt; Jacob *withholds Benjamin* in dread; and the brothers *bow before Joseph* — the dreams *fulfilled unknowing*.
2. **the disguised test (qasheh 42:7 → zakhar 42:9 → chay/emet 42:15, 42:16 → chayah/yare 42:18 → aman 42:20):** Joseph *hides behind roughness*, *remembers his dreams*, and *tests their truthfulness* — reassuring them he *fears God* (power bounded by reverence).
3. **the buried guilt surfaces, overheard, and wept over (ashem/tsarah/nephesh/chanan/shama 42:21 → chata/darash/shama 42:22 → yada/shama 42:23 → bakhah 42:24):** under pressure the brothers *confess their old sin* — the *ignored pleading remembered*, a *reckoning* sensed — *in Joseph's very hearing*; and Joseph *turns and weeps* — compassion behind the disguise.
4. **the mercy that alarms, the grief renewed (natan 42:25 → natan 42:27 → charad/lev 42:28 → qasheh 42:30 → yada/nuach/natan 42:33, 42:34 → yare 42:35 → yagon/qara 42:38):** Joseph's *secret kindness* (returned money) is *misread as God's judgment* — trembling hearts; and Jacob, *hearing the terms*, *refuses Benjamin* in *renewed grief*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** shama ×3 + understand (report *heard* / not-listening to *Joseph* / not-listening to *Reuben* / Joseph *understood*); chayah ×2 (the *survival* errand / the *promise of life* on the test); qara ×2 (Jacob's *first* / *second* dread of harm to Benjamin); shallit (the *dreams fulfilled* — bowing); qasheh ×2 (the *disguising harshness* / its *report*); zakhar (the *dreams remembered*, shaping the test); chay/emet (the *oath-bound test* of truth); **yare ×2 (Joseph's *"I fear God"* — power bounded by reverence / the brothers' *fear* at the money)**; aman (the *verification*); **ashem/tsarah/nephesh/chanan/shama (the *buried guilt surfaced* — the ignored pleading remembered)**; chata/darash (the sin and the *reckoning* sensed); yada ×3 (the *ignorance* / the test's *knowings*); **bakhah (the *hidden weeping* — compassion behind the disguise)**; natan ×3 (the *secret provision* / the *money found* / the *release* promised); **charad/lev (the *trembling* reading God's judgment)**; nuach (Simeon *held*); yagon (Jacob's *renewed grief*).
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** the **brothers** — the *20-year-buried guilt surfacing* (the ignored pleading remembered), *sensing a divine reckoning*, *trembling* at every reversal; **Joseph** — *testing behind a disguise*, *remembering the dreams*, yet *weeping in secret* and *secretly kind* (power *bounded by the fear of God*, not vengeance); **Jacob** — *grief renewed*, clinging to Benjamin. The confession *overheard by the one it wronged* is the pivot.
- **Threads:** **the dreams fulfilled** (shallit/bowing 42:6 ← 37:7,9; JOS-01); **the buried guilt surfaces** (ashem 42:21 — the *new detail* that Joseph *begged*, `chanan`; → their deepening reckoning, JOS-10; the guilt they carry from JOS-02); *the fear of God* bounds power (yare 42:18 ← the midwives 1:17; Joseph won't abuse rule); **Joseph's weeping** (bakhah 42:24 → 43:30; 45:2,14–15; 50:17 — the recurring, ever-nearer weeping); *reading God's hand* (charad/lev 42:28 → "you meant evil, God meant good", 50:20 — the providence-reading the brothers grope toward in fear here); Jacob's *inconsolable grief* (yagon 42:38 ← 37:35); the *reckoning* (darash 42:22 — the past catching up).
- **Guarded against:** lumping the three shama, two chayah/qara/qasheh/yare, three yada/natan; reading Joseph's roughness as cruelty when the text shows it *masks a weeping, kind heart* (the disguise *tests*, it does not avenge — 42:24,25 prove it); missing the *new detail* at 42:21 (Joseph *begged* — `chanan` — deepening the brothers' guilt beyond ch37's telling); over-reading the brothers' "what has God done?" (42:28) as faith when it is *guilty dread* (they read *judgment*, groping toward the providence they'll later hear named); treating Jacob's refusal as mere stubbornness when it is *renewed, clinging grief*.

# Genesis 43:1–34 — inner-being passage reading (JOS-09-second-descent-compassion)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-joseph-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: **Judah** (surety), **Jacob** (grief-resignation), the **brothers** (guilt-fear), and **Joseph** (compassion overflowing). The "alive/well" formulas (`chay`/`shalom`) cluster in the welfare-inquiry.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 3 chay, 2 yada, 2 shaal, 2 techillah, 2 yare, 3 shalom, 2 natan, 2 rachamim, 2 baqash each treated distinctly.

---

## JOS-09-second-descent-compassion · Genesis 43:1–34 · [the surety, the mercy invoked, and the compassion barely held] — Judah's pledge, Benjamin brought, and the weeping in the chamber

**The passage.** "The man **solemnly** (ud) warned us" (43:3); "why did you treat me so **badly** (raa)?" (43:6); "he **questioned** (shaal) us: is your father **alive** (chay)? could we **know** (yada)?" (43:7); "send the boy, that we may **live** (chayah)" (43:8); "I will be a pledge… from my hand **require** (baqash) him… let me bear the **blame** (chata)" (43:9); "God Almighty **grant** (natan) you **mercy** (rachamim)… if I am bereaved, I am bereaved" (43:14); the brothers **afraid** (yare) at Joseph's house, the money "the **first time** (techillah)" (43:18); "we do not **know** (yada) who put it" (43:22); "**Peace** (shalom), do not be **afraid** (yare); your God put treasure" (43:23); water **given** (natan) (43:24); they **heard** (shama) they'd eat there (43:25); Joseph **inquired** (shaal): "is your father **well** (shalom), still **alive** (chay)?" (43:27); "he is **well** (shalom), **alive** (chay)" (43:28); "God be **gracious** (chanan) to you" (43:29); his **compassion** (rachamim) grew warm, he **sought** (baqash) a place to **weep** (bakhah) (43:30); the Egyptians **could** (yakhol) not eat with Hebrews — an **abomination** (toevah) (43:32); the brothers in **amazement** (tamah) (43:33); Benjamin's portion **five times** (ravah) (43:34).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **ud (solemnly) — the *condition* that binds the return (43:3).** "the man **solemnly** (ud) warned us: 'you shall not see my face without your brother'" *(stated)* — ud, *testify/warn solemnly*: the *binding condition* (Benjamin must come) — the interior-context of *the demand that forces Jacob's hand* *(inferred: ud = the solemn condition binding the second descent)*.
- **raa (badly) — Jacob's *reproach* (43:6).** "'why did you treat me so **badly** (raa) as to tell him you had a brother?'" *(stated)* — raa, *be evil/do harm*: the gem is the *father's blame* — he *reproaches the sons* for exposing Benjamin's existence; the interior *lashing at the messengers of the demand* *(inferred: raa = the father's reproach of the sons)*.
- **shaal (questioned) + chay (alive) + yada (know) — the *sons' defence* (43:7).** "'he **questioned** (shaal) us: is your father **alive** (chay)?… could we **know** (yada) he'd say bring your brother?'" *(stated)*. **shaal** — the *questioning* recalled; **chay** — the father's *life* asked after; **yada** — the sons plead *ignorance* of where it would lead. The interior *defending itself against the reproach* *(inferred: shaal/chay/yada = the sons' defence — they could not have known)*.
- **chayah (live) — Judah's *survival argument* (43:8).** "'send the boy… that we may **live** (chayah) and not die — we, you, and our little ones'" *(stated)* — chayah, *live*: Judah *presses the survival stakes* — *all die* if they do not go; the interior *urging the necessary risk* *(inferred: chayah = the survival argument for sending Benjamin)*.
- **baqash (require) + chata (blame) — Judah's *surety* (43:9).** "'I will be a pledge; from my hand **require** (baqash) him… let me bear the **blame** (chata) forever'" *(stated)*. **baqash** — *require/seek* (the surety-language: *hold me accountable*); **chata** — the gem: Judah *pledges to bear the blame* for Benjamin — the *very brother-role he failed with Joseph* (whom he *sold*, JOS-02) now *assumed as guarantor*. Judah's *transformation* deepening (← the Tamar-turn, JOS-03): the interior *taking responsibility for the brother* *(inferred: baqash/chata = Judah's surety — bearing the blame for the brother he once failed)*.
- **natan (grant) + rachamim (mercy) — Jacob's *grief-resignation* (43:14).** "'God Almighty **grant** (natan) you **mercy** (rachamim)… if I am bereaved, I am bereaved'" *(stated)*. **natan** — *give*; **rachamim** — *compassion/mercy*: the gem is the *father's surrender* — he *invokes God's mercy* and *resigns himself to loss* ("if I am bereaved, I am bereaved") — the interior *releasing his grip in trust-and-grief* *(inferred: natan/rachamim = the invoked mercy and the grief-resignation)*.
- **techillah (first time) + yare (afraid) — the *guilt-fear* at the house (43:18), then explained (43:20).** "the men were **afraid** (yare)… 'because of the money replaced the **first time** (techillah, 43:18), he will assault us'" — and to the steward, "'we came down the **first time** (techillah, 43:20) to buy food'" *(stated)*. **techillah** ×2 — the *first time* (the returned money): 43:18 the *fearful reasoning* among themselves / 43:20 the *explanation* to the steward; **yare** — the gem: the brothers *read the invitation as a trap* — *guilt makes them fear* the very kindness (a meal) as an ambush; the interior *interpreting mercy as menace* *(inferred: techillah/yare = the guilt-fear that reads the meal as a trap, then explained away)*.
- **yada (know) — the *ignorance* of the money (43:22).** *yada distinct from 43:7:* "'we do not **know** (yada) who put our money in our sacks'" *(stated)* — the brothers' *bafflement* — the returned money *inexplicable* to them (God's hidden hand, unread) *(inferred: yada = the unknowing about the returned money)*.
- **yare (afraid) + shalom (Peace) — the *steward's reassurance* (43:23).** *yare distinct from 43:18:* "'**Peace** (shalom), do not be **afraid** (yare); your God and your father's God put treasure in your sacks'" *(stated)*. **shalom** — *peace*; **yare** — the *fear dispelled*: the gem is that the *Egyptian steward names their God* — *"your God put the treasure"* — reading the money as *God's gift*, not a trap; the interior *reassured*, the mercy *named as God's* *(inferred: shalom/yare = the reassurance — the returned money named God's gift)*.
- **natan (given) — the *hospitality* (43:24).** *natan distinct from 43:14:* "he **gave** (natan) them water… and their donkeys fodder" *(stated)* — natan, *give*: the *welcome* extended — the interior-context of *hospitality* replacing the feared assault *(inferred: natan = the hospitality given — the feared trap becomes a welcome)*.
- **shama (heard) — the *meal announced* (43:25).** "they **heard** (shama) they should eat bread there" *(stated)* — shama, *hear*: the *meal* announced — the brothers *prepare the present*, still uneasy *(inferred: shama = the meal heard of)*.
- **shaal (inquired) + shalom (well) + chay (alive) — Joseph's *tender inquiry* (43:27).** *shaal distinct from 43:7; shalom/chay distinct:* "he **inquired** (shaal) about their **welfare** (shalom): 'is your father **well** (shalom)… still **alive** (chay)?'" *(stated)*. **shaal** — Joseph *asks after* them; **shalom** — their *welfare*; **chay** — the *father's life*. The gem: the disguised Joseph's *tender concern for his father* — the interior's *love leaking through the disguise* *(inferred: shaal/shalom/chay = Joseph's tender inquiry after his father)*.
- **shalom (well) + chay (alive) — the *answer* (43:28).** *shalom/chay distinct from 43:27:* "'your servant our father is **well** (shalom); he is still **alive** (chay)'" — and they bowed *(stated)* — the *answer* (the father lives) — and the *bowing* (the dreams' fulfilment continuing) *(inferred: shalom/chay = the father's welfare confirmed, the bowing continued)*.
- **chanan (gracious) — the *blessing on Benjamin* (43:29).** "seeing Benjamin: 'God be **gracious** (chanan) to you, my son'" *(stated)* — chanan, *be gracious*: the gem is the *tenderness* — Joseph *blesses his full brother* ("my mother's son") with *grace*; the interior's *love for Benjamin surfacing* *(inferred: chanan = the gracious blessing on the full brother)*.
- **rachamim (compassion) + baqash (sought) + bakhah (weep) — the *compassion overflowing* (43:30).** *rachamim distinct from 43:14; baqash distinct from 43:9:* "his **compassion** (rachamim) grew warm for his brother; he **sought** (baqash) a place to **weep** (bakhah), and wept in his chamber" *(stated)*. The **central gem**: **rachamim** — Joseph's *compassion grows warm* (the yearning of the innards); **baqash** — he *must seek privacy*; **bakhah** — he *weeps*. The disguise *strains to breaking* — the interior's *love overwhelming its control* (← the hidden weeping 42:24, now *warmer, harder to hold* → the disclosure, JOS-11) *(inferred: rachamim/baqash/bakhah = the compassion overflowing — the disguise nearly broken)*.
- **yakhol (could) + toevah (abomination) — the *separation at the meal* (43:32).** "the Egyptians **could** (yakhol) not eat with the Hebrews — an **abomination** (toevah)" *(stated)*. **yakhol** — the *inability*; **toevah** — *what is abhorred*: the interior-context of *the cultural/sacred separation* (Egypt abhors eating with Hebrews, ← the shepherds' abomination 46:34) — Joseph *set apart even at his own table* *(inferred: yakhol/toevah = the separation Egypt's abhorrence imposes)*.
- **tamah (amazement) — the *seating* wonder (43:33).** "seated in birth order… the men looked at one another in **amazement** (tamah)" *(stated)* — tamah, *be astounded*: the gem is the *uncanny knowledge* — the stranger *seats them in exact birth order*; the interior *baffled by a knowing it cannot explain* (Joseph's hidden knowledge) *(inferred: tamah = the amazement at the uncanny seating)*.
- **ravah (five times) — the *favour shown Benjamin* (43:34).** "Benjamin's portion was **five times** (ravah) as much" *(stated)* — ravah, *multiply/abundance*: the gem is the *lavish favour* on Benjamin — whether *test* (do they envy the favoured youngest, as they envied Joseph?) or *love*, the interior *singles out the full brother*; and they *drink and are merry* (the tension easing for a moment) *(inferred: ravah = the fivefold favour on Benjamin — love, and perhaps a test of their envy)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the surety and the resignation (ud 43:3 → raa 43:6 → shaal/chay/yada 43:7 → chayah 43:8 → baqash/chata 43:9 → natan/rachamim 43:14):** the *binding condition* forces Jacob's hand; he *reproaches* the sons, they *defend*; and *Judah pledges himself* — bearing the blame for the brother he once failed — while Jacob *invokes God's mercy and resigns himself* to possible loss.
2. **the guilt-fear reassured (techillah/yare 43:18 → yada 43:22 → shalom/yare 43:23 → natan 43:24 → shama 43:25):** the brothers *read the meal as a trap* (guilt reading mercy as menace); the steward *reassures* — *"your God put the treasure"* — and *welcomes* them.
3. **the tender inquiry and the overflowing compassion (shaal/shalom/chay 43:27 → shalom/chay 43:28 → chanan 43:29 → rachamim/baqash/bakhah 43:30):** the disguised Joseph *asks after his father* and *blesses Benjamin* — and his *compassion grows warm*, driving him to *seek a place and weep*; the disguise *nearly breaks*.
4. **the separated meal and the favoured brother (yakhol/toevah 43:32 → tamah 43:33 → ravah 43:34):** Joseph *eats apart* (Egypt's abhorrence), the brothers *amazed* at the uncanny seating, and Benjamin *favoured fivefold* — the tension *easing into merriment*, the disclosure a step nearer.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** ud (the *solemn condition*); raa (the father's *reproach*); shaal ×2 (the *questioning* recalled / Joseph's *tender inquiry*); chay ×3 (the father's *life* asked / *inquired* / *confirmed*); yada ×2 (the sons' *ignorance* of the demand / the *unknowing* about the money); chayah (Judah's *survival* argument); **baqash/chata (Judah's *surety* — bearing the blame for the brother he once failed)**; **natan/rachamim (Jacob's *invoked mercy and grief-resignation*)**; techillah/yare (the *guilt-fear* reading the meal as a trap); shalom ×3 (the steward's *peace* / the *welfare* inquiry / the *answer*); natan (the *hospitality*); chanan (the *gracious blessing* on Benjamin); **rachamim/baqash/bakhah (Joseph's *compassion overflowing* — the disguise nearly broken)**; yakhol/toevah (the *separation* at the meal); tamah (the *amazement* at the seating); ravah (the *fivefold favour* on Benjamin — love, perhaps a test of envy).
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **Judah** — *surety*, bearing blame for the brother (the transformation deepening ← Tamar); **Jacob** — *grief-resignation* trusting God's mercy; the **brothers** — *guilt reading mercy as menace*, then reassured; **Joseph** — *tender concern for his father* and *compassion overflowing* (the disguise straining to breaking); the **steward** — naming the money *God's gift*. The rachamim thread (Jacob *prays* mercy, Joseph's mercy *wells*) binds the passage.
- **Threads:** **Judah's transformation** (baqash/chata 43:9 — surety for Benjamin ← the Tamar-turn JOS-03; → the substitute plea JOS-10; the ascendancy 49:8); **Joseph's escalating weeping** (rachamim/bakhah 43:30 ← the hidden weeping 42:24 → the disclosure 45:2,14; 50:17 — the compassion ever-nearer the surface); the **dreams fulfilled** (bowing 43:28 ← 37:7,9); *God's hidden hand* named (shalom/"your God put the treasure" 43:23 → "God sent me", 45:5; "God meant it for good", 50:20); the **favoured youngest** (ravah 43:34 ← Joseph the favoured son 37:3 — a possible *test* of the brothers' old envy); the *abomination* (toevah 43:32 ← 46:34); **rachamim** (Jacob's prayer 43:14 answered in Joseph's welling mercy 43:30).
- **Guarded against:** lumping the pairs/triples (three chay/shalom, two yada/shaal/techillah/yare/natan/rachamim/baqash — each a distinct beat); reading Judah's surety as mere pragmatism when it *reverses his failure with Joseph* (bearing blame for the brother — the transformation); missing that the brothers' *fear* (43:18) is *guilt reading mercy as menace*; over-reading Benjamin's fivefold portion (43:34) as only favour when it may *test* their envy (I hold both — love and possible test); treating Joseph's weeping as weakness when it is *compassion straining the disguise* (love, not loss of control — he *composes himself*, 43:31); importing the messianic Judah-line over the passage's own *surety-and-transformation*.

# Genesis 44:1–34 — inner-being passage reading (JOS-10-cup-judah-plea)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-joseph-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: **Joseph** (the final test), the **brothers** (guilt fully owned), and **Judah** (the substitute — transformation complete). **Note:** the `'o'`/"desire" spans at 44:8 ("silver *or* gold") and 44:19 ("a father *or* a brother") are the conjunction *"or"* — mis-tags, not read.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 3 yakhol, 2 raah + raa, 2 naqi, 2 yada each treated distinctly.

---

## JOS-10-cup-judah-plea · Genesis 44:1–34 · [the test met; the substitute offered] — the planted cup, the guilt owned, and Judah in Benjamin's place

**The passage.** Fill the sacks as much as they **can** (yakhol) carry, the cup in Benjamin's (44:1–2); "why repaid **evil** (raah) for good? you have **done evil** (raa)" (44:4, 44:5); "he who is found with it my servant, the rest **innocent** (naqi, naqi)" (44:10); the cup found in Benjamin's sack; "do you not **know** (yada) a man like me divines?" (44:15); Judah — "how **clear ourselves** (tsadeq)? God has found out the **guilt** (avon)" (44:16); "go up in **peace** (shalom) to your father" (44:17); "let not your anger **burn** (charah)" (44:18); "my lord **asked** (shaal)" (44:19); "the boy **cannot** (yakhol) leave his father" (44:22); "we **cannot** (yakhol) go down without him" (44:26); "you **know** (yada) my wife bore me two" (44:27); "harm… bring my gray hairs in **evil** (raah) to Sheol" (44:29); "his **life** (nephesh) bound up in the boy's life" (44:30); "with **sorrow** (yagon) to Sheol" (44:31); "I became a pledge… I shall bear the **blame** (chata)" (44:32); "let me remain instead of the boy" (44:33).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **yakhol (can) — the *staged sacks* (44:1).** "fill the sacks as much as they **can** (yakhol) carry… the cup in the youngest's" *(stated)* — yakhol, *be able*: the *staging of the test* — the cup *planted* in Benjamin's sack; the interior-context of *the trap laid to probe the brothers* *(inferred: yakhol = the sacks filled to capacity, the cup planted — the test staged)*.
- **raah (evil) + raa (done evil) — the *false accusation* (44:4, 44:5).** "'why repaid **evil** (raah) for good?… you have **done evil** (raa)'" *(stated)*. **raah/raa** — *evil*: the *charge* of ingratitude and theft — the gem is the *irony*: the *brothers* are accused of *"evil for good"* — the very thing *they* did to *Joseph* (repaid his seeking-them with the pit); the accusation *names their old pattern* unknowingly *(inferred: raah/raa = the evil-for-good charge — echoing their own old deed)*.
- **naqi (innocent ×2) — the *terms* that isolate Benjamin (44:10).** "'he who is found with it my servant; the rest **innocent** (naqi)'" *(stated)* — naqi, *innocent/free*: the gem is the *terms* — *only the guilty one* held, *the rest free to go*; the interior-context of *the test's design* — *will they take their innocence and abandon Benjamin?* (as they abandoned Joseph) *(inferred: naqi = the innocent-rest terms — the test that isolates the youngest)*.
- **yada (know) — Joseph's *divining claim* (44:15).** "'do you not **know** (yada) a man like me can divine?'" *(stated)* — yada, *know*: Joseph *presses the pretence* of supernatural knowledge (he *does* know all, but not by divination) — the interior *maintaining the disguise's pressure* *(inferred: yada = the divining claim that maintains the pressure)*.
- **tsadeq (clear ourselves) + avon (guilt) — the *guilt fully owned* (44:16).** "'how can we **clear ourselves** (tsadeq)? God has found out the **guilt** (avon) of your servants'" *(stated)*. The **central gem for the brothers**: **tsadeq** — they *cannot justify themselves*; **avon** — *iniquity/guilt*: Judah *names their guilt as exposed by God* — *"God has found out"* — reading the cup-discovery as *divine exposure of their old sin* (← the surfacing at 42:21). The interior *ceasing to defend itself, owning the guilt before God* *(inferred: tsadeq/avon = the guilt fully owned — no self-justification, God has exposed it)*.
- **shalom (peace) — the *test's sharpest point* (44:17).** "'only the man with the cup shall be my servant; the rest, go up in **peace** (shalom) to your father'" *(stated)* — shalom, *peace*: the gem is the *offer that tests them* — *go home in peace, leave Benjamin* — the *exact* choice they faced with Joseph (abandon the favoured brother and go free). The interior *offered its old escape* — will it take it? *(inferred: shalom = the peace-offer that tests whether they will abandon Benjamin)*.
- **charah (burn) + shaal (asked) — Judah's *deferential approach* (44:18–19).** "'let not your anger **burn** (charah)… my lord **asked** (shaal) his servants'" *(stated)*. **charah** — *anger* (Judah begs it not kindle); **shaal** — the *questioning* recalled: Judah *approaches humbly* and *recounts the whole history* — the interior *pleading, not defending* *(inferred: charah/shaal = the deferential approach, the history recounted)*.
- **yakhol (cannot) — the *impossibility of separation* (44:22).** *yakhol distinct from 44:1:* "'the boy **cannot** (yakhol) leave his father, for his father would die'" *(stated)* — the gem is the *bond*: Benjamin *cannot* be separated from Jacob without killing him; the interior *naming the father's fragile life* *(inferred: yakhol = the impossibility — the boy cannot leave the father and live)*.
- **yakhol (cannot) — the *condition* restated (44:26).** *yakhol distinct from 44:22:* "'we **cannot** (yakhol) go down unless our youngest is with us'" *(stated)* — the *condition* the family faced — the interior recounting *the bind they were in* *(inferred: yakhol = the condition — no descent without Benjamin)*.
- **yada (know) — Jacob's *word* recalled (44:27).** *yada distinct from 44:15:* "'my father said: you **know** (yada) my wife bore me two sons'" *(stated)* — yada, *know*: Judah *quotes Jacob's own words* — the *two sons of Rachel* (Joseph and Benjamin); the interior *bringing the father's grief into the room* *(inferred: yada = Jacob's word recalled — the two beloved sons)*.
- **raah (evil) — the *father's dreaded ruin* (44:29).** *raah distinct from 44:4:* "'harm… you will bring my gray hairs in **evil** (raah) to Sheol'" *(stated)* — raah, *evil/calamity*: the *father's dreaded end* (← 42:38; 37:35) — the interior *foreseeing the father's death-in-grief* *(inferred: raah = the calamity that would take the father to Sheol)*.
- **nephesh (life) — the *bound souls* (44:30).** "'his **life** (nephesh) is bound up in the boy's life'" *(stated)* — nephesh, *life/soul*: the gem is the *knot* — *Jacob's very soul tied to Benjamin's* — lose the boy, lose the father; the interior *naming the father's life as hostage to Benjamin's return* *(inferred: nephesh = the father's soul bound to the boy — the knot the test would sever)*.
- **yagon (sorrow) — the *death-grief* named (44:31).** "'your servants will bring the gray hairs of our father with **sorrow** (yagon) to Sheol'" *(stated)* — yagon, *sorrow* (← 42:38): the gem is that *Judah names the grief they would cause* — the *very grief they once caused* with Joseph (37:34–35); the interior *seeing the father's death-sorrow and recoiling from repeating it* *(inferred: yagon = the death-sorrow the brothers would cause — the one they once caused)*.
- **chata (blame) — Judah's *pledge* invoked (44:32).** *chata distinct from JOS-09:* "'I became a pledge… I shall bear the **blame** (chata) before my father all my life'" *(stated)* — chata, *blame/sin*: Judah *invokes his surety* (← 43:9) — he *staked himself* for Benjamin; the interior *bound by its own pledge* *(inferred: chata = the blame Judah pledged to bear)*.
- **(44:33–34 — "let me remain instead of the boy… I fear to see the evil that would find my father"; no non-T2 span.)** Flagged: the *climax* carries no flagged span, but it is the *gem of the whole passage*: **Judah offers himself as a substitute** — *"let me remain instead of the boy, and let the boy go back"* — and *"how can I go back… I cannot bear to see the evil that would find my father."* The gem: the man who *sold Joseph* and *callously watched his father grieve* (JOS-02) now *offers his own freedom to spare his father more grief* — **Judah's transformation complete**: from *causing* the father's sorrow to *sacrificing himself to prevent it*. Read as context, anchored by nephesh/yagon/chata *(no-span context; the substitute — the completed transformation)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the test staged and sprung (yakhol 44:1 → raah/raa 44:4, 44:5 → naqi 44:10 → yada 44:15):** the *cup planted* in Benjamin's sack, the *evil-for-good* charge (echoing their own old deed), the *innocent-rest* terms that *isolate Benjamin* — the trap *probing whether they will abandon the favoured brother*.
2. **the guilt owned (tsadeq/avon 44:16 → shalom 44:17):** the brothers *cease to justify themselves* — *"God has found out our guilt"* — and Joseph *offers them their old escape*: go home in *peace*, leave Benjamin.
3. **Judah's plea — the father's bound soul (charah/shaal 44:18–19 → yakhol 44:22 → yakhol 44:26 → yada 44:27 → raah 44:29 → nephesh 44:30 → yagon 44:31 → chata 44:32):** Judah *recounts the whole history*, naming the *father's soul bound to Benjamin*, the *death-sorrow* his loss would cause — *the very grief they once caused* — and his *own pledge*.
4. **the substitute (44:33–34):** Judah *offers himself in Benjamin's place* — *"let me remain instead of the boy"* — unable to *bear seeing his father's grief*. **The transformation complete**: the seller of Joseph now *the self-offering guarantor* — the test *passed*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** yakhol ×3 (the sacks' *capacity*, test staged / the *impossibility* of separation / the *condition* restated); raah/raa (the *evil-for-good* charge echoing their own deed / the *father's dreaded ruin* 44:29); naqi (the *innocent-rest* terms isolating Benjamin); yada ×2 (Joseph's *divining claim* / Jacob's *word* recalled); **tsadeq/avon (the *guilt fully owned* — "God has found out", no self-justification)**; **shalom (the *peace-offer* that tests whether they'll abandon Benjamin — their old escape)**; charah/shaal (the *deferential* approach); nephesh (the *father's soul bound* to the boy); yagon (the *death-sorrow* they'd cause — the one they once caused); chata (Judah's *pledge* invoked); **the substitute (44:33–34, no-span — Judah offering himself, the transformation complete)**.
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **Judah** — the *substitute*: self-offering love for father and brother, the *completed transformation* (from selling Joseph and watching his father grieve, to sacrificing himself to spare that grief); the **brothers** — *guilt fully owned* before God (no self-justification); **Joseph** — the *final test* (will they abandon the favoured youngest, as they abandoned him?). The test *answered* by Judah's self-offering.
- **Threads:** **Judah's transformation COMPLETE** (the substitute 44:33 ← the surety 43:9 ← the Tamar-turn 38:26 ← the seller 37:26 — the full arc; → the ascendancy 49:8–12); **the brothers' guilt fully surfaced** (avon 44:16 ← the surfacing 42:21 ← the sin JOS-02 — "God has found out"); the **test** (naqi/shalom — will they repeat the abandonment? ← the favoured-youngest Benjamin echoing the favoured Joseph); the **father's bound soul** (nephesh 44:30 → Jacob's near-death at the news, reversed by Joseph's living, 45:26–27); *evil-for-good* (raah 44:4 ← their own deed → "you meant evil, God meant good", 50:20); Jacob's *grief* (yagon 44:31 ← 37:35; 42:38).
- **Guarded against:** lumping the three yakhol or two raah/naqi/yada; reading the cup-test as Joseph's *cruelty* when it is a *probe of their change* (met and *passed* by Judah's self-offering — the test *reveals* transformation, it does not avenge); missing that the *peace-offer* (44:17) is the *sharpest test* (their old escape re-offered); over-reading the substitute (44:33) into NT substitutionary-atonement typology over the *completed transformation* the passage shows (Judah's self-offering *for his father's sake*); treating the brothers' "God has found out our guilt" (44:16) as despair when it is *honest ownership* (no self-justification — the interior finally straight with its sin).

# Genesis 45:1–28 — inner-being passage reading (JOS-11-disclosure-providence)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-joseph-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: **Joseph** (the disguise broken; the providence-reading), the **brothers** (dismay → reconciliation), **Jacob** (numbness → revival), **Pharaoh** (glad). The "alive" formulas (`chay`) thread the passage.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 2 yakhol, 2 shama, 3 chay, 2 chayah, 2 mashal, 2 bakhah, 3 natan each treated distinctly.

---

## JOS-11-disclosure-providence · Genesis 45:1–28 · [the disguise broken; "God sent me to preserve life"] — the weeping revelation, the providence that forgives, and the father revived

**The passage.** Joseph **could** (yakhol) not control himself, **cried** (qara) to clear the room, **made himself known** (yada) (45:1); he **wept** aloud (bekhi), the Egyptians **heard** (shama) (45:2); "I am Joseph! is my father **alive** (chay)?" — they **could** (yakhol) not answer, **dismayed** (bahal) (45:3); "do not be **distressed** (atsav) or **angry** (charah)… God sent me to **preserve life** (michyah)" (45:5); "to keep **alive** (chayah) many survivors" (45:7); "not you but God… **ruler** (mashal) over Egypt" (45:8); "tell my father of my **honor** (kavod)" (45:13); he **wept** (bakhah) on Benjamin (45:14) and **wept** (bakhah) on all his brothers (45:15); it **pleased** (yatav) Pharaoh, the report **heard** (shama) (45:16); "I will **give** (natan) the best of Egypt" (45:18); "no **concern** (chus) for your goods" (45:20); Joseph **gave** (natan) wagons (45:21) and **gave** (natan) changes (chaliphah) of clothes (45:22); "do not **quarrel** (ragaz)" (45:24); "Joseph is **alive** (chay), **ruler** (mashal)" — Jacob's **heart** (lev) numb, he did not **believe** (aman) (45:26); his spirit **revived** (chayah) (45:27); "Joseph my son is **alive** (chay); I will go see him" (45:28).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **yakhol (could not) + qara (cried) + yada (made known) — the *disguise broken* (45:1).** "Joseph **could** (yakhol) not control himself; he **cried** (qara), 'clear the room!'… he **made himself known** (yada)" *(stated)*. **yakhol** — the gem: the *compassion* (welling since 42:24; 43:30) *finally overwhelms control* — he *cannot hold the disguise*; **qara** — he *clears the room* (privacy for the revelation); **yada** — *makes himself known*. The interior's *long-restrained love breaks free* *(inferred: yakhol/qara/yada = the compassion that breaks the disguise — Joseph made known)*.
- **shama (heard) + bekhi (aloud) — the *weeping heard through the house* (45:2).** "he **wept** aloud (bekhi); the Egyptians **heard** (shama)" *(stated)*. **bekhi** — *weeping*; **shama** — the *sound reaching the household*: the gem is the *unrestraint* — the weeping so loud it *carries through the palace*; the interior's *emotion no longer hidden* (← the *hidden* weeping 42:24; 43:30 — now *public*) *(inferred: bekhi/shama = the loud, unhidden weeping heard through the house)*.
- **chay (alive) + yakhol (could not) + bahal (dismayed) — "*is my father alive?*" and the *dismay* (45:3).** "'I am Joseph! is my father **alive** (chay)?' — they **could** (yakhol) not answer, **dismayed** (bahal)" *(stated)*. **chay** — Joseph's *first question* is *his father's life* (love outrunning everything); **yakhol** *distinct from 45:1* — the brothers *cannot answer* (speechless); **bahal** — *terror/dismay*: the gem is their *dread* — the man they *wronged* now *holds their lives*; the interior *paralysed by the revelation* *(inferred: chay/yakhol/bahal = Joseph's love-question and the brothers' terrified speechlessness)*.
- **atsav (distressed) + charah (angry) + michyah (preserve life) — the *providence-reading* (45:5).** "'do not be **distressed** (atsav) or **angry** (charah) with yourselves… God sent me to **preserve life** (michyah)'" *(stated)*. The **central gem**: **atsav** — *be grieved/hurt* (← the grieved heart 6:6); **charah** — *be angry* (at themselves); **michyah** — *preservation of life*. Joseph *tells them not to grieve or self-reproach* — because *God overruled their evil for life*: **"God sent me to preserve life."** The interior *reframes the betrayal as God's saving providence* — the *same event, two agencies* (they sold, God sent) — the ground of *forgiveness* *(inferred: atsav/charah/michyah = the providence-reading — God sent me to preserve life, grounding the forgiveness)*.
- **chayah (alive) — the *remnant kept* (45:7).** "'God sent me… to keep **alive** (chayah) for you many survivors'" *(stated)* — chayah, *live*: the gem is the *purpose named* — a *remnant preserved*; the interior *reading its suffering as the means of the family's survival* *(inferred: chayah = the remnant kept alive — the suffering's saving purpose)*.
- **mashal (ruler) — "*not you but God*" (45:8).** "'it was **not you** who sent me, but God… **ruler** (mashal) over Egypt'" *(stated)* — mashal, *rule*: the gem is the *sharpest form* — *"not you but God"* — Joseph *removes the agency from the brothers to God*; the *rule* the dreams promised (← 37:8, "will you rule?") *given by God*. The interior *attributing its whole story to God* *(inferred: mashal = the God-given rule — "not you but God")*.
- **kavod (honor) — the *glory to tell the father* (45:13).** "'tell my father of all my **honor** (kavod) in Egypt'" *(stated)* — kavod, *glory/honour*: Joseph *wants his father to know his honour* — the interior's *longing for the father* (the son once "dead" now *glorified*, to comfort the grieving father) *(inferred: kavod = the honour told to comfort the father)*.
- **bakhah (wept) — the *weeping on Benjamin* (45:14).** "he fell on Benjamin's neck and **wept** (bakhah); Benjamin **wept**" *(stated)* — bakhah, *weep*: the gem is the *reunion of the full brothers* — the *open, mutual* weeping (← the *hidden* weeping) *(inferred: bakhah = the open weeping with Benjamin)*.
- **bakhah (wept) — the *weeping on all the brothers* (45:15).** *bakhah distinct from 45:14:* "he **kissed** all his brothers and **wept** (bakhah) on them; then they talked with him" *(stated)* — the gem: the weeping *extends to all* — even the ones who *sold* him — and *then they talk*; the *reconciliation* enacted through tears and kisses *(inferred: bakhah = the weeping over all the brothers — reconciliation enacted)*.
- **yatav (pleased) + shama (heard) — Pharaoh's *gladness* (45:16).** *shama distinct from 45:2:* "the report **heard** (shama) in Pharaoh's house **pleased** (yatav) Pharaoh" *(stated)*. **shama** — the *report* reaching the court; **yatav** — Pharaoh *glad*: the interior of the *king pleased* at Joseph's family — the reconciliation *welcomed at the highest level* *(inferred: yatav/shama = Pharaoh's gladness at the report)*.
- **natan (give) — Pharaoh's *lavish offer* (45:18).** "'I will **give** (natan) you the best of Egypt'" *(stated)* — natan, *give*: the *best of the land* offered — the interior-context of *royal generosity* to Joseph's kin *(inferred: natan = the best of Egypt offered)*.
- **chus (concern) — "*no concern for your goods*" (45:20).** "'have no **concern** (chus) for your goods, for the best of Egypt is yours'" *(stated)* — chus, *pity/spare/regard*: the gem is *the letting-go* — *do not spare a thought* for possessions left behind; the interior *freed from clinging to goods* by the abundance ahead *(inferred: chus = the goods not spared a thought — freedom from clinging)*.
- **natan (gave) — Joseph's *provision* (45:21).** *natan distinct from 45:18:* "Joseph **gave** (natan) them wagons and provisions" *(stated)* — the *provision for the journey* — the interior's *care for the family's road* *(inferred: natan = the wagons and provisions given)*.
- **natan (gave) + chaliphah (change) — the *gifts, Benjamin favoured* (45:22).** *natan distinct from 45:18,21:* "to each he **gave** (natan) a **change** (chaliphah) of clothes; to Benjamin, five" *(stated)* — the gem is the *lavish favour on Benjamin again* (five, ← the fivefold portion 43:34) — the interior *singling out the full brother in love* (no longer a test — now open affection) *(inferred: natan/chaliphah = the gifts, Benjamin favoured fivefold in love)*.
- **ragaz (quarrel) — the *caution* against blame (45:24).** "'do not **quarrel** (ragaz) on the way'" *(stated)* — ragaz, *tremble/be agitated/quarrel*: the gem is Joseph's *knowing caution* — the brothers might *blame one another* over the old guilt on the road home; the interior *forestalling their recrimination* — mercy *guarding their peace* *(inferred: ragaz = the caution against quarrelling — forestalling their mutual blame)*.
- **chay (alive) + mashal (ruler) + aman (believe) + lev (heart) — Jacob's *numb disbelief* (45:26).** *chay/mashal distinct:* "'Joseph is **alive** (chay), **ruler** (mashal) over Egypt' — his **heart** (lev) became numb, he did not **believe** (aman)" *(stated)*. **chay** — the *son alive* (the news); **mashal** — *ruler*; **aman** — *believe*; **lev** — *heart*: the gem is the *shock* — the news *too good* — the father's *heart goes numb*, he *cannot believe*; the interior *stunned by a joy too large for a grief so old* *(inferred: chay/mashal/aman/lev = the numb, unbelieving heart at the too-good news)*.
- **chayah (revived) — the *spirit revived* (45:27).** *chayah distinct from 45:7:* "when he saw the wagons, the spirit of Jacob **revived** (chayah)" *(stated)* — chayah, *live/revive*: the gem is the *reversal* — the father who expected to *"go down to Sheol mourning"* (37:35) is *revived*; the *dead-thought son alive* *raises the father's spirit from the grave of grief* *(inferred: chayah = the father's spirit revived — grief reversed)*.
- **chay (alive) — "*Joseph my son is alive*" (45:28).** *chay distinct from 45:3,26:* "'it is enough; Joseph my son is **alive** (chay); I will go see him before I die'" *(stated)* — the gem: the father's *affirmation* — the *one thing that matters* is *the son lives*; the interior *content to die once it has seen him*; the grief *undone* *(inferred: chay = the father's affirmation — the son alive is enough)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the disguise broken in weeping (yakhol/qara/yada 45:1 → bekhi/shama 45:2 → chay/yakhol/bahal 45:3):** the *compassion overwhelms control*, Joseph *clears the room and weeps aloud* (heard through the palace), and *reveals himself* — his *first question his father's life* — while the brothers stand *dismayed and speechless*.
2. **the providence-reading (atsav/charah/michyah 45:5 → chayah 45:7 → mashal 45:8 → kavod 45:13):** Joseph *forgives by reframing* — *"do not grieve; God sent me to preserve life… not you but God"* — the betrayal *overruled for the family's survival*; the interior *attributing its whole story to God*.
3. **reconciliation enacted (bakhah 45:14 → bakhah 45:15):** he *weeps on Benjamin*, then *on all his brothers* — even the sellers — *and then they talk*: the reconciliation *through tears and kisses*.
4. **the sending home and the father revived (yatav/shama 45:16 → natan 45:18 → chus 45:20 → natan 45:21 → natan/chaliphah 45:22 → ragaz 45:24 → chay/mashal/aman/lev 45:26 → chayah 45:27 → chay 45:28):** Pharaoh *glad and generous*, Joseph *lavishes gifts* (Benjamin fivefold, in love) and *guards their peace* ("do not quarrel"); and Jacob — *stunned numb, unbelieving* — is *revived* by the wagons: *"Joseph my son is alive."* The grief of 37:35 *undone*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** yakhol ×2 (Joseph *cannot control himself* / the brothers *cannot answer*); qara/yada (the room *cleared*, Joseph *made known*); bekhi/shama (the *loud weeping heard* — no longer hidden); bahal (the brothers' *terror*); chay ×3 (Joseph's *"is my father alive?"* / the *news* to Jacob / Jacob's *affirmation*); **atsav/charah/michyah (the *providence-reading* — "God sent me to preserve life", grounding forgiveness)**; chayah ×2 (the *remnant kept alive* / Jacob's *spirit revived*); mashal ×2 (the *God-given rule* "not you but God" / the *news* he is ruler); kavod (the *honour* told to comfort the father); bakhah ×2 (weeping on *Benjamin* / on *all the brothers* — reconciliation); yatav/shama (Pharaoh's *gladness*); natan ×3 (Pharaoh's *offer* / the *wagons* / the *gifts*, Benjamin fivefold); chus (*no concern* for goods); chaliphah (the *changes* of clothes); ragaz (the *caution* against mutual blame); aman/lev (Jacob's *numb disbelief*).
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **Joseph** — the *compassion breaking the disguise*, the *providence-reading* that *forgives* ("God sent me… not you but God"), and *lavish, peace-guarding love*; the **brothers** — *dismay/terror* → *reconciliation*; **Jacob** — *numb disbelief* → *revival* (the grief of 37:35 undone); **Pharaoh** — *glad and generous*. The providence-reading is the theological heart.
- **Threads:** **the providence-reading** (michyah/"not you but God" 45:5,8 → "you meant evil, God meant good", 50:20 — the two statements of the cycle's theology; ← the son-names' reframe 41:51–52); **Joseph's weeping** (bakhah 45:14–15 — now *open* ← the *hidden* weeping 42:24; 43:30 — the arc of restrained love breaking free); **the dreams fulfilled** (mashal 45:8 ← 37:8 "will you rule?"); **Jacob's grief reversed** (chayah 45:27 ← the inconsolable mourning 37:35; "I shall go down to Sheol mourning" — now *revived*); the *favoured Benjamin* (chaliphah 45:22 ← 43:34 — now *love*, not test); *guarding their peace* (ragaz 45:24 — mercy forestalling their recrimination); the *remnant preserved* (chayah 45:7 → the nation in Egypt).
- **Guarded against:** lumping the pairs/triples (two yakhol/shama/chayah/mashal/bakhah, three chay/natan — each a distinct beat); reading the providence-reading (45:5) as *excusing* the brothers' sin when Joseph *names it* ("whom you sold", 45:4) *and* reframes it — the sin *real*, God's overruling *also* real (both held, as 50:20 will confirm); over-reading michyah/"not you but God" into a determinism debate over the *forgiveness-grounding* the verse gives; missing that Joseph's *first* word after "I am Joseph" is *"is my father alive?"* (love outrunning everything); treating Jacob's numbness (45:26) as faithlessness when it is *joy too large for an old grief*; importing NT typology (Joseph forgiving = Christ) over the *providence-grounded forgiveness* the passage states.

# Genesis 46:1–34 — inner-being passage reading (JOS-12-descent-to-egypt)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-joseph-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: **God** (the "fear not" at the threshold), **Jacob** (content to die reunited), **Joseph** (the reunion weeping). The census (46:8–27) is a **thin genealogy** — the `nephesh` are a *persons*-count (the seventy), read as the census, not soul-depth.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 6 nephesh (census), 2 natan, 2 qara treated distinctly.

---

## JOS-12-descent-to-egypt · Genesis 46:1–34 · [the exile's threshold blessed; the reunion] — "fear not to go down", the seventy souls, and "now let me die, I have seen you"

**The passage.** God — "do not be **afraid** (yare) to go down to Egypt… I will go with you" (46:3–4); the census — Leah's line (**persons**, nephesh, 46:15), Zilpah's, whom Laban **gave** (natan) (46:18), Rachel's (46:22), Bilhah's, whom Laban **gave** (natan) (46:25), the sixty-six and the seventy **persons** (nephesh, 46:26–27); Joseph went to **meet** (qara) his father, fell on his neck and **wept** (bakhah) (46:29); "now let me die, since I have seen you **alive** (chay)" (46:30); "when Pharaoh **calls** (qara)…" (46:33); "every shepherd is an **abomination** (toevah) to Egypt" (46:34).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **yare (afraid) — the *"fear not" at the exile's threshold* (46:3).** "God said: 'do not be **afraid** (yare) to go down to Egypt, for there I will make you a great nation… I will go with you and bring you up'" *(stated)* — yare, *fear*: the gem is *where* the "fear not" comes — at the *threshold of the descent* that begins the *foretold sojourn* (the 400 years, 15:13). God *sanctions the descent* and *promises to go with them* — the interior *reassured to enter what will become bondage*, because *God accompanies it* ("I will go down with you… and bring you up"). The divine "fear not" at the *edge of the exile* (← 15:1; 26:24; 28:15) *(inferred: yare = the "fear not" that blesses the descent — God accompanying the exile's threshold)*.
- **nephesh (persons) ×6 — the *seventy souls* (46:15, 46:18, 46:22, 46:25, 46:26, 46:27).** "Leah's… **persons** (nephesh) thirty-three (46:15)… Zilpah's sixteen (46:18)… Rachel's fourteen (46:22)… Bilhah's seven (46:25)… sixty-six **persons** (46:26)… all the **persons** of Jacob's house, seventy (46:27)" *(stated)* — nephesh in the *census/person* sense: the gem is the *smallness of the seed* — *seventy souls* go down — a **thin genealogy** (head-count, not soul-depth), but the number *matters*: the *seventy* that will *multiply into a nation* (← "seventy persons", the very count Exodus opens on, Exo 1:5; the seed before the increase). Read as the *census of the seed*, not over-read *(inferred: nephesh = the seventy persons — the small seed that becomes the nation)*.
- **natan (gave) — the *maids given* (46:18, 46:25).** "Zilpah, whom Laban **gave** (natan) to Leah (46:18)… Bilhah, whom Laban **gave** (natan) to Rachel (46:25)" *(stated)* — natan, *give*: the *genealogical note* (the maids given as part of the wives' households, ← Gen 29–30) — thin, the census's family-structure *(inferred: natan = the maids given — the census's family note)*.
- **qara (meet) + bakhah (wept) — the *reunion* (46:29).** "Joseph went to **meet** (qara) his father… fell on his neck and **wept** (bakhah) a good while" *(stated)*. **qara** — *encounter/meet*; **bakhah** — *weep*: the gem is the *long weeping* — the son and father *reunited after 22 years* of (false) death; the interior's *grief-and-joy poured out* on the father's neck (the *longest* weeping yet — "a good while") *(inferred: qara/bakhah = the reunion — the long weeping on the father's neck)*.
- **chay (alive) — "*now let me die, I have seen you*" (46:30).** "'now let me die, since I have seen your face and know you are **alive** (chay)'" *(stated)* — chay, *alive*: the gem is the *father's contentment* — *the one thing he needed* was to *see the son alive*; now he can *die satisfied* (← 45:28; the grief of 37:35 *fully undone*). The interior *at rest* — the reunion *completes* the father's life *(inferred: chay = the father content to die, having seen the son alive)*.
- **qara (calls) — the *coaching* for Pharaoh (46:33).** *qara distinct from 46:29:* "'when Pharaoh **calls** (qara) you: what is your occupation?'" *(stated)* — qara, *call-to*: Joseph *coaches the family* on what to say — the interior's *practical care* for their settling *(inferred: qara = the anticipated summons Joseph coaches them for)*.
- **toevah (abomination) — the *separation that preserves* (46:34).** "'say you are shepherds… for every shepherd is an **abomination** (toevah) to Egypt'" *(stated)* — toevah, *abomination*: the gem is the *strategy* — *because* Egypt *abhors* shepherds, Israel will be *settled apart in Goshen* — the *very abhorrence keeps them a distinct people* (not absorbed into Egypt); the interior-context of *a separation that preserves identity* (← 43:32; → the distinct people of the Exodus) *(inferred: toevah = the abomination that settles Israel apart — the separation that preserves)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the threshold blessed (yare 46:3 → 46:4):** at the *edge of the descent* (the foretold exile), God says *"fear not… I will go with you and bring you up"* — the *descent into what becomes bondage* sanctioned by *God's accompanying presence*.
2. **the seventy souls go down (nephesh 46:15–27 → natan 46:18,25):** the *small seed* — *seventy persons* — enters Egypt; the census (thin) of the *seed that will become the nation* (the count Exodus opens on).
3. **the reunion and the content father (qara/bakhah 46:29 → chay 46:30):** Joseph *weeps long* on his father's neck; Jacob, *having seen the son alive*, is *content to die* — the grief *fully undone*.
4. **the separation that preserves (qara 46:33 → toevah 46:34):** Joseph *coaches* the family; the *Egyptian abhorrence of shepherds settles Israel apart in Goshen* — a *separation that keeps them a distinct people*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** **yare (the *"fear not" at the exile's threshold* — God accompanying the descent that becomes bondage)**; nephesh ×6 (the *seventy souls* — the census of the *small seed* that becomes the nation, ← thin genealogy, not soul-depth); natan (the *maids given* — the census's family note); **qara/bakhah (the *reunion* — the long weeping on the father's neck)**; **chay (the *content father* — "now let me die, I have seen you alive")**; qara (the *coaching* for Pharaoh); **toevah (the *separation that preserves* — Egypt's abhorrence settling Israel apart)**.
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **God** — the *"fear not"* that *blesses the descent* (presence promised at the exile's edge); **Jacob** — *content to die*, the grief *undone* by the reunion; **Joseph** — the *long reunion weeping* and *practical care*. The census is *thin* (the seventy-count), its weight the *seed → nation* link.
- **Threads:** the **"fear not" at the exile's threshold** (yare 46:3 ← 15:1; 26:24; 28:15 — God accompanying the descent foretold at 15:13 → the Exodus deliverance); the **seventy souls** (nephesh 46:27 → Exo 1:5 "seventy persons, Jacob" — the *seed* before the *multiplication* → the nation the Exodus frees); **Joseph's weeping** (bakhah 46:29 — the *longest*, ← the hidden weeping 42:24; the open weeping 45:14 — the arc's fullest release with the *father*); **Jacob's grief undone** (chay 46:30 ← 37:35; 45:28 — content to die); the **separation that preserves** (toevah 46:34 ← 43:32 → the distinct people in Goshen, kept from absorption).
- **Guarded against:** over-reading the *thin* census (46:8–27) into interior operations (the nephesh are a *head-count* — the seventy — not soul-depth; the natan a *family note* — per "never over-read genealogies"); missing the *significance of the seventy* (the seed → nation, the Exodus link) even while keeping the census thin; reading God's "fear not" (46:3) as merely comfort when it *sanctions the descent into the foretold exile* (God accompanying what becomes bondage); over-reading toevah as mere cultural friction when it *functions to preserve* Israel's distinctness; importing later exile-theology over the *threshold-blessing* the verse gives.

# Genesis 47:1–31 — inner-being passage reading (JOS-13-jacob-pharaoh-famine)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `genesis-joseph-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: **Jacob** (blessing the king; the sober life; the pull to the land), the **Egyptians** (desperation → servitude), **Israel** (multiplying), **Joseph** (steward). The second chesed span at 47:29 carries an alternate gloss "shame" — the word is chesed = *steadfast kindness*.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 2 barakh, 3 chayyim, 6 natan, 3 chayah, 2 chen each treated distinctly.

---

## JOS-13-jacob-pharaoh-famine · Genesis 47:1–31 · [the patriarch blesses the king; Egypt enslaved, Israel multiplied; the pull to the land] — few and evil my days, and bury me with my fathers

**The passage.** "If you **know** (yada) **able** (chayil) men, set them over my livestock" (47:6); Jacob **blessed** (barakh) Pharaoh (47:7); "how many the days of your **life** (chayyim)?" (47:8); "few and **evil** have been the days of my **life** (chayyim)" (47:9); Jacob **blessed** (barakh) Pharaoh (47:10); Joseph **gave** (natan) a possession (47:11); "**give** (natan) your livestock… I will **give** (natan) food" (47:16, 47:17); "**give** (natan) us seed, that we may **live** (chayah)" (47:19); the famine **severe** (chazaq), the land became Pharaoh's (47:20); the priests' allowance Pharaoh **gave** (natan) (47:22); "**give** (natan) a fifth to Pharaoh" (47:24); "you have saved our **lives** (chayah)… may it **please** (chen) my lord, we will be servants" (47:25); Israel **multiplied** (ravah) in Goshen (47:27); Jacob's **life** (chayyim) 147 years, he **lived** (chayah) (47:28); "if I have found **favor** (chen)… deal **kindly** (chesed) and **truly** (emet)… bury me with my fathers" — he **called** (qara) Joseph (47:29).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **yada (know) + chayil (able) — Pharaoh's *trust extended* (47:6).** "'if you **know** (yada) any **able** (chayil) men, set them over my livestock'" *(stated)*. **yada** — *know*; **chayil** — *strength/capability*: Pharaoh *entrusts his own herds* to Joseph's kin — the interior-context of *favour extended to the family for Joseph's sake* *(inferred: yada/chayil = the able men entrusted with Pharaoh's livestock)*.
- **barakh (blessed) — the *patriarch blesses the king* (47:7).** "Jacob **blessed** (barakh) Pharaoh" *(stated)* — barakh, *bless*: the gem is the *inversion* — the *nomad shepherd* **blesses the king of Egypt**; the *lesser (in worldly power) blessing the greater* — Jacob a *conduit of the Abrahamic blessing* to Pharaoh (← "in you all families blessed", 12:3; Joseph blessing Potiphar's house 39:5). The interior *bestowing blessing from above its station* *(inferred: barakh = the patriarch's blessing on the king — the blessing-conduit)*.
- **chayyim (life) — Pharaoh's *question* about the years (47:8).** "'how many are the days of the years of your **life** (chayyim)?'" *(stated)* — chayyim, *life*: Pharaoh *asks the old man's age* — the occasion of Jacob's *self-assessment* *(inferred: chayyim = the years asked after)*.
- **chayyim (life) — Jacob's *sober self-judgment* (47:9).** *chayyim distinct from 47:8:* "'**few and evil** have been the days of the years of my **life** (chayyim)… not attaining my fathers' years'" *(stated)* — the gem: Jacob names his life *"few and evil"* (ra) — a *sober, honest self-judgment* of a *hard, grasping, grieving life* (the deceptions, the exile, the losses); the interior *reckoning its own days as hard* (contrast Abraham "full of years", 25:8) — a *pilgrim's weary honesty* *(inferred: chayyim = the life reckoned "few and evil" — Jacob's sober self-judgment)*.
- **barakh (blessed) — the *departing blessing* (47:10).** *barakh distinct from 47:7:* "Jacob **blessed** (barakh) Pharaoh and went out" *(stated)* — the *second* blessing *brackets* the audience (entering and leaving) — the interior *blessing the king again on departure* *(inferred: barakh = the departing blessing — the audience bracketed by blessing)*.
- **natan (gave) — the *possession given* (47:11).** "Joseph **gave** (natan) them a possession in the best of the land" *(stated)* — natan, *give*: the *settling* of the family — the interior-context of *Joseph's provision* *(inferred: natan = the possession given to the family)*.
- **natan (give ×2) — the *livestock-for-food exchange* (47:16, 47:17).** *natan distinct:* "'**give** (natan) your livestock, I will **give** (natan) food'… he **gave** (natan) food for the livestock" *(stated)* — the *famine economy's second stage* — the Egyptians *trading livestock for bread*; the interior-context of *the desperation deepening* *(inferred: natan = the livestock exchanged for food)*.
- **natan (give) + chayah (live) — the *last resort: land and selves* (47:19).** *natan/chayah distinct:* "'**give** (natan) us seed that we may **live** (chayah)… buy us and our land'" *(stated)*. **natan** — the plea for *seed*; **chayah** — *live*: the gem is the *final surrender* — the Egyptians *sell their land and themselves* to survive; the interior *reduced to servitude by the famine* *(inferred: natan/chayah = the land and selves surrendered to live)*.
- **chazaq (severe) — the famine's *pressure* (47:20).** "the famine was **severe** (chazaq)… the land became Pharaoh's" *(stated)* — chazaq, *severe/strong*: the *pressure* that *centralizes all Egypt under Pharaoh* — the interior-context of *the crisis that makes the people Pharaoh's servants* (and, the dark irony, *concentrates the Pharaonic power* that will later *enslave Israel*) *(inferred: chazaq = the famine's severity that reduces Egypt to Pharaoh's servitude)*.
- **natan (gave) — the *priests' exemption* (47:22).** *natan distinct:* "the priests' allowance Pharaoh **gave** (natan) them; they did not sell" *(stated)* — the *one exempt class* — the interior-context of *the priests kept from the servitude* (a note on the policy's limit) *(inferred: natan = the priests' allowance — the exemption)*.
- **natan (give) — the *fifth to Pharaoh* (47:24).** *natan distinct:* "'at harvest, **give** (natan) a fifth to Pharaoh'" *(stated)* — the *statute* of the fifth — the interior-context of *the settled tenancy* under Pharaoh *(inferred: natan = the fifth rendered to Pharaoh — the settled order)*.
- **chayah (live) + chen (please) — the *grateful servitude* (47:25).** *chayah distinct from 47:19; chen:* "'you have saved our **lives** (chayah)… may it **please** (chen) my lord, we will be servants'" *(stated)*. **chayah** — *life* (saved); **chen** — *favour/grace*: the gem is the *gratitude in servitude* — the Egyptians *thank Joseph for saving their lives*, *content to be Pharaoh's servants*; the interior *grateful even as it is reduced* — bread valued above freedom *(inferred: chayah/chen = the grateful servitude — lives saved, freedom yielded)*.
- **ravah (multiplied) — *Israel fruitful in Goshen* (47:27).** "Israel **multiplied** (ravah) greatly in Goshen" *(stated)* — ravah, *multiply* (← Gen 1:28; the creation-blessing): the gem is the *contrast* — *while Egypt is reduced to servitude, Israel multiplies* — the *seed becoming a nation* (← the seventy, 46:27; → Exo 1:7, the *exact* echo "fruitful and multiplied"). The interior-context of *the blessed seed growing* even in Egypt *(inferred: ravah = Israel multiplying in Goshen — the seed becoming a nation)*.
- **chayyim (life) + chayah (lived) — *Jacob's total years* (47:28).** *chayyim distinct from 47:8,9; chayah:* "Jacob **lived** (chayah) in Egypt seventeen years; his **life** (chayyim) 147 years" *(stated)* — the *span* of Jacob's life closing — the interior-context of *the pilgrim's years numbered* *(inferred: chayyim/chayah = Jacob's total years, the life closing)*.
- **chen (favor) + chesed (kindly) + emet (truly) + qara (called) — the *burial-oath: the pull to the land* (47:29).** *chen distinct from 47:25:* "he **called** (qara) Joseph: 'if I have found **favor** (chen)… deal **kindly** (chesed) and **truly** (emet) with me: do not bury me in Egypt… but with my fathers'" *(stated)*. **qara** — the *summons*; **chen** — *favour* sought; **chesed** — *steadfast kindness*; **emet** — *truth/faithfulness* (the covenant-character pair, ← 24:27,49; 32:10): the gem is the *pull toward the land* — Jacob, *dying in Egypt*, *binds Joseph by oath* to *bury him in Canaan with his fathers*; the interior's *faith looks beyond Egypt* — *Egypt is not home; the promised land is* (the exile's temporary-ness held in faith) *(inferred: chen/chesed/emet/qara = the burial-oath — the dying faith that looks past Egypt to the land)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the patriarch blesses the king (yada/chayil 47:6 → barakh 47:7 → chayyim 47:8 → chayyim 47:9 → barakh 47:10):** Pharaoh *entrusts his herds* to the family; and Jacob *blesses the king* (entering and leaving) — the *conduit of blessing from above his station* — while reckoning his own life *"few and evil"* (the pilgrim's sober honesty).
2. **the famine reduces Egypt (natan 47:11 → natan 47:16, 47:17 → natan/chayah 47:19 → chazaq 47:20 → natan 47:22 → natan 47:24 → chayah/chen 47:25):** the Egyptians *sell money, livestock, land, and themselves* to survive — *grateful even in servitude* ("you saved our lives"); Joseph's policy *centralizes Egypt under Pharaoh* (the dark irony seeding the later bondage).
3. **Israel multiplies (ravah 47:27):** *while Egypt is enslaved, Israel is fruitful and multiplies* in Goshen — the *seed becoming a nation* (the Exodus echo).
4. **the pull to the land (chayyim/chayah 47:28 → chen/chesed/emet/qara 47:29):** the dying Jacob *binds Joseph by oath* to *bury him with his fathers, not in Egypt* — the interior's *faith looks past Egypt to the promised land*; *Egypt is not home*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** yada/chayil (the *able men* entrusted); **barakh ×2 (the patriarch's *entering* / *departing* blessing on the king — the blessing-conduit)**; chayyim ×3 (Pharaoh's *question* / Jacob's *"few and evil"* self-judgment / the *147 years*); natan ×6 (the *famine economy* — possession / livestock-for-food ×2 / seed / priests' allowance / the fifth); chazaq (the famine's *severity* reducing Egypt to servitude); chayah ×3 (that-we-may-*live* / *lives*-saved / Jacob *lived*); chen ×2 (the Egyptians' *"please"* / Jacob's *"favor"*); **ravah (Israel *multiplying* in Goshen — the seed → nation, while Egypt is enslaved)**; **chesed/emet (the *burial-oath* — the dying faith that looks past Egypt to the land)**; qara (the *summons* for the oath).
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **Jacob** — *blessing the king* (conduit), the *sober "few and evil"* self-judgment, and the *faith that looks to the land* (the burial-oath); the **Egyptians** — *desperation → grateful servitude* (bread above freedom); **Israel** — *multiplying* (the blessed seed); **Joseph** — the *steward* administering the famine. The Israel-multiplied / Egypt-enslaved *contrast* is the pivot.
- **Threads:** the **blessing-conduit** (barakh 47:7,10 ← 12:3; 39:5; Joseph blessing Egypt — Jacob blesses Pharaoh); the **seed → nation** (ravah 47:27 ← the seventy 46:27; Gen 1:28 → Exo 1:7 "fruitful and multiplied" — the *exact* echo; the bondage narrative's opening); the **dark irony** (chazaq 47:20 — Joseph's policy *concentrates the Pharaonic power* that will *enslave Israel*, Exo 1); **chesed-and-emet** (47:29 ← 24:27; 32:10 — the covenant-character pair); the **pull to the land** (the burial-oath 47:29 → Jacob buried in Machpelah 50:13; the exile *temporary* in faith); Jacob's *sober life* (47:9 — the grasping, grieving pilgrim's honest reckoning ← the whole Jacob cycle).
- **Guarded against:** lumping the six natan (the distinct stages of the famine economy) or the pairs (two barakh/chen, three chayyim/chayah); reading a "shame" operation into the mis-glossed second chesed (the word is *kindness*); missing the **Israel-multiplied / Egypt-enslaved contrast** (the blessed seed vs the servitude) and the **Exodus echo** (ravah 47:27 → Exo 1:7); over-reading the famine-policy into a moral verdict on Joseph (the text *reports* the centralization; the *irony* — it seeds the later bondage — is a thread, not a condemnation); treating Jacob's "few and evil" (47:9) as mere complaint when it is a *pilgrim's sober self-judgment*; importing later "Egypt = the world" typology over the *faith-looks-to-the-land* the burial-oath gives.
