# Exodus 32:30–33:6 — inner-being passage reading (GLD-04-blot-me-out)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-goldencalf-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: **Moses** (intercession deepened to self-offering), **God** (refusing the substitution, relenting from destruction but withdrawing his presence), **Israel** (the first mourning/contrition). The plague (32:35, no non-T2 span) reads as scene-context.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the sin-forms (chata/chataah/chattat), 2 qasheh treated as the recurring naming of the one great sin / the repeated verdict.

---

## GLD-04-blot-me-out · Exodus 32:30–33:6 · [the mediator's self-offering; the presence withdrawn; the first mourning] — "blot me out of your book", and "I will not go up among you"

**The passage.** "You have **sinned** (chata) a great **sin** (chataah); perhaps I can make **atonement** (kipper/kaphar) for your **sin** (chattat)" (32:30); "this people has **sinned** (chata) a great **sin** (chataah)" (32:31); "if you will forgive their **sin** (chattat) — but if not, **blot me out** of your book" (32:32); "whoever has **sinned** (chata), I will blot out" (32:33); "in the day I visit, I will visit their **sin** (chattat)" (32:34); a plague (32:35); "go up to the land I swore to **give** (natan)… but I will not go up among you… for you are **stiff-necked** (qasheh), lest I consume you" (33:1–3); the people **mourned** (aval) the **disastrous** (ra) word, stripped their ornaments (33:4); "you are **stiff-necked** (qasheh)… take off your ornaments, that I may know what to do" (33:5–6).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **chata / chataah / chattat (sin) + kipper / kaphar (atonement) — the *tentative atonement sought* (32:30).** "'you have **sinned** (chata) a great **sin** (chataah)… perhaps I can make **atonement** (kipper/kaphar) for your **sin** (chattat)'" *(stated)*. The *sin*-root sounds three times (the calf-sin *named and re-named* — the scene's dominating fact); **kipper/kaphar** — *atone/cover*: the gem is the *tentative "perhaps"* — even Moses is *unsure atonement is possible* for so great a sin; the interior of *the mediator going up not in confidence but in hope* — *"perhaps"* — to *stand between the sin and its penalty* *(inferred: chata/kipper = the tentative atonement sought — "perhaps I can atone", the mediator's uncertain hope)*.
- **chata / chataah (sin) — the *sin owned before God* (32:31).** "'alas, this people has **sinned** (chata) a great **sin** (chataah); they have made gods of gold'" *(stated)* — the mediator *names the sin plainly before God* (no minimizing — unlike Aaron, 32:24): the interior of *honest confession on the people's behalf* — *owning the gravity* he pleads against *(inferred: chata/chataah = the sin owned before God — honest confession, not minimized)*.
- **chattat (sin) — the *self-offering* (32:32).** "'if you will forgive their **sin** (chattat) — but if not, **blot me out** of your book that you have written'" *(stated)*. **chattat** — *sin*: the gem is *THE peak of intercession* — Moses offers *his own place in God's book* for the people: *"blot ME out"*. Where GLD-02 pleaded God's *name and oath*, here the mediator *offers himself* — *he would rather be erased than see the people destroyed*. And the *broken sentence* — *"if you will forgive their sin—"* trails off, *unable to finish* — the *anguish* of a love that cannot voice the alternative. The interior of *self-substituting love* — *the mediator laying down his own life/standing for the guilty* *(inferred: chattat = the self-offering — "blot me out", the mediator's self-substituting love)*.
- **chata (sinned) + chattat (sin) — *God's answer: each bears his own* (32:33–34).** "'whoever has **sinned** (chata) against me, I will blot out… in the day I visit, I will visit their **sin** (chattat)'" *(stated)*: the gem is *the answer that refuses the substitution* — *God will not blot Moses for the people* (*"whoever has sinned"* — individual responsibility), yet *relents from total destruction* (*"go, lead the people"*, the angel sent); *judgment deferred, not erased* (*"in the day I visit"*). The interior (of God) of *justice that holds the sinner accountable* — *the mediator's offer honored but not accepted*; each *bears his own sin* *(inferred: chata/chattat = each bears his own — the substitution refused, judgment deferred)*.
- **natan (give) + qasheh (stiff-necked) — the *terrible mercy: the presence withdrawn* (33:1–3).** "'go up to the land I swore to **give** (natan)… but I will **not go up among you**… for you are **stiff-necked** (qasheh), lest I consume you'" *(stated)*. **natan** — *give*; **qasheh** — *stiff-necked*: the gem is *the most terrible consequence* — *not destruction but ABSENCE*: God will *keep his promise* (the land *given*) and *send an angel*, but *will not go himself* — *because his holiness would consume a stiff-necked people*. The interior finding: *the withdrawal of the Presence is the deepest judgment* — worse than the plague; *the gift without the Giver*; and it is a *terrible mercy* (he withdraws *lest he consume*) *(inferred: natan/qasheh = the presence withdrawn — the gift kept but the Giver absent, a terrible mercy toward the stiff-necked)*.
- **aval (mourned) + ra (disastrous) — the *first mourning* (33:4).** "when the people heard this **disastrous** (ra) word, they **mourned** (aval), and no one put on his ornaments" *(stated)*. **aval** — *mourn*; **ra** — *evil/disastrous*: the gem is *the first sign of contrition* — the *stiff-necked* people, hearing *"I will not go with you"*, **mourn**; the interior of *grief that God's absence, not merely his wrath, would be unbearable* — *the loss of the Presence felt as the true disaster*; the beginning of a *turning* *(inferred: aval/ra = the first mourning — the loss of the Presence felt as the real disaster, the beginning of contrition)*.
- **qasheh (stiff-necked) — the *stripping as humbling* (33:5).** *qasheh distinct from 33:3:* "'you are **stiff-necked**… take off your ornaments, that I may know what to do with you'" *(stated)*: where 33:3 gave the *verdict*, 33:5 turns it to a *summons to humble* — the *ornaments stripped* as a sign; the interior-context of *the proud neck bent* — *the humbling that opens a space for mercy* ("that I may know what to do") *(inferred: qasheh = the stripping as humbling — the stiff neck bent, a space opened for mercy)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the self-offering (chata/kipper 32:30 → chata/chataah 32:31 → chattat 32:32 → chata/chattat 32:33–34):** Moses goes up *"perhaps"* to atone, *owns the sin honestly*, and *offers himself* — *"blot me out"*; God *refuses the substitution* (each bears his own) yet *relents from destruction* and *defers judgment* — the mediator's *self-offering love* met by *justice that will not erase the guilty by erasing the innocent*.
2. **the presence withdrawn, the first mourning (natan/qasheh 33:1–3 → aval/ra 33:4 → qasheh 33:5):** God keeps the *promise* but withholds the *Presence* (*"I will not go up"*) — the *terrible mercy* toward the stiff-necked; and the people, hearing it, **mourn** and *strip their ornaments* — *the loss of God himself felt as the real disaster* — the *first contrition*, the *proud neck beginning to bend*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** the *sin*-forms (chata/chataah/chattat — the *one great calf-sin* named and re-named through the scene: Moses' *tentative atonement* / his *honest owning* / his *plea for forgiveness* / God's *deferred visiting*); **kipper/kaphar (the *tentative* atonement sought — "perhaps")**; **chattat 32:32 (the *self-offering* — "blot me out")**; natan (the land *given* — promise kept); **qasheh ×2 (the *stiff-necked* verdict that withdraws the Presence / the *humbling* that strips the ornaments)**; **aval/ra (the *first mourning* — the loss of the Presence felt as the real disaster)**.
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **Moses** — *intercession deepened to self-offering* ("blot me out" — self-substituting love, the broken sentence of anguish); **God** — *refusing the substitution* (each bears his own sin), *relenting from destruction* but *withdrawing his Presence* (the terrible mercy toward the stiff-necked); **Israel** — the *first mourning*, the *stripping* — contrition beginning. The two gems: **the mediator's self-offering** and **the presence withdrawn**.
- **Threads:** **the self-substituting mediator** (32:32 → "I could wish myself accursed for my brothers", Rom 9:3; the Servant "poured out his soul to death… bore the sin of many", Isa 53:12; Christ the substitute — Moses' offer *refused here* because *no man can*, pointing beyond himself); **each bears his own sin** (32:33 → "the soul who sins shall die", Ezek 18:20 — individual responsibility, held with the later true substitution); **the presence as the true good** (33:3 "I will not go up" → Moses' whole plea "if your presence does not go, do not bring us up" 33:15 — the withdrawal *the* disaster; the gift without the Giver worthless); **stiff-necked** (qasheh 33:3,5 ← 32:9 → 34:9 — the obstinate interior, the reason for withdrawal); **contrition** (aval 33:4 — the first genuine mourning of the people, the turning that the whole wilderness-testing arc had not yet produced).
- **Guarded against:** reading Moses' "blot me out" as a bargaining ploy when it is *self-substituting love* (the broken sentence marks anguish, not tactic); collapsing the many *sin*-forms into nothing when each occurrence *does* something (sought-atonement / owned / pled / visited) — but not inventing distinct *meanings* for the same calf-sin; treating God's refusal (32:33) as mere severity when it holds *justice* (each bears his own) *with* mercy (relenting from destruction); missing that the *withdrawal of Presence* (33:3) is the *deepest* judgment (worse than the plague) — the finding the people themselves grasp by mourning; not over-reading the ornament-stripping (33:6) beyond the *humbling* the text gives.

# Exodus 33:7–23 — inner-being passage reading (GLD-05-presence-glory)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-goldencalf-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: **Moses** (the seeker who stakes all on the Presence and longs to see the glory), **God** (restoring the Presence, the sovereign freedom of grace, the limit of the vision), **Israel** (those who seek the LORD). The "face to face, as a friend" (33:11, no non-T2 span) reads as scene-context anchored by baqash (33:7).
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the ~4 chen, 2 kavod, 2 qara treated distinctly.

---

## GLD-05-presence-glory · Exodus 33:7–23 · [the Presence is everything; the longing to see God; the freedom of grace] — "if your presence does not go, do not bring us up", and "show me your glory"

**The passage.** The tent outside the camp, everyone who **sought** (baqash) the LORD going out; Moses **called** (qara) it the tent of meeting (33:7); face to face as a friend (33:11); "you say I have found **favor** (chen)… show me your ways, that I may know you and find **favor** (chen)… this nation is your people" (33:12, 33:13); "my presence will go with you, and I will give you **rest** (nuach)" (33:14); "if your presence will not go, do not bring us up" (33:15); "how shall it be known that I have found **favor** (chen)… unless you go with us?" (33:16); "you have found **favor** (chen), and I know you by name" (33:17); "show me your **glory** (kavod)" (33:18); "I will make my goodness pass, **proclaim** (qara) my name, and be **gracious** (chanan) to whom I will be gracious, show **mercy** (racham) on whom I will" (33:19); "you cannot see my face and live" (33:20); hidden in the cleft while the **glory** (kavod) passes (33:22); "I will **take away** (sur) my hand, and you shall see my back" (33:23).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **baqash (sought) + qara (called) — the *seeking of God* after the breach (33:7).** "Moses pitched the tent outside the camp… everyone who **sought** (baqash) the LORD would go out to it; he **called** (qara) it the tent of meeting" *(stated)*. **baqash** — *seek*; **qara** — *name/call*: the gem is that *after the calf, seeking God moves "outside the camp"* — the Presence no longer *among* them (33:3), those who *seek* must *go out*; the interior of *the earnest seeking of God* in the wake of the breach — *the tent of meeting a place for the hungry* (and Moses meets God there *as a friend*, 33:11) *(inferred: baqash/qara = the seeking of God — those who seek go outside the camp to meet him)*.
- **chen (favor) — *Moses leverages the favor to know God* (33:12, 33:13).** "'you say "I know you by name and you have found **favor** (chen)"… show me your ways, that I may know you and find **favor** (chen)… this nation is your people'" *(stated)* — chen, *favor/grace*: the gem is *the mediator pressing the favor he has toward two ends* — to *know God's ways* (not just be led blindly) and to *bind the people to his own standing* (*"this nation is YOUR people"*); the interior of *favor turned into a plea to know God and to carry the people* — *the friend asking to understand the friend* *(inferred: chen = Moses leveraging the favor — to know God and to carry the people)*.
- **nuach (rest) — the *Presence restored, and rest given* (33:14).** "'my presence will go with you, and I will give you **rest** (nuach)'" *(stated)* — nuach, *rest*: the gem is *the reversal of the withdrawal* — where 33:3 said *"I will not go up"*, now *"my presence will go"* — and *rest* is its gift; the interior-context of *the Presence conceded, and with it rest* — *the mediator's plea beginning to prevail* *(inferred: nuach = the Presence restored — "my presence will go", and rest its gift)*.
- **chen (favor) — the *everything staked on the Presence* (33:15–16).** *chen distinct from 33:12, 33:13:* "'if your presence will not go, do not bring us up… how shall it be known that I have found **favor** (chen)… unless you go with us? — it is your going that makes us distinct'" *(stated)*: the gem is *THE heart of the whole block* — Moses *stakes everything on the Presence*: *better no land than land without God*; the *proof* of favor is *not the gift but the Giver's going*; *what makes Israel Israel is God with them*, nothing else. The interior of *desiring God himself above every blessing* — *the Presence is the covenant's whole worth* *(inferred: chen = everything staked on the Presence — better no land than land without God; the Giver, not the gift)*.
- **chen (favor) — the *plea granted for Moses' sake* (33:17).** *chen distinct from 33:16:* "'this very thing I will do, for you have found **favor** (chen), and I know you by name'" *(stated)*: the gem is *the Presence granted on the ground of the mediator's favor* — *"for YOU have found favor"* — the people carried *on Moses' standing*; the interior-context of *the many spared for the one God knows by name* *(inferred: chen = the plea granted for Moses' sake — the people carried on the mediator's favor)*.
- **kavod (glory) — the *longing to see God* (33:18).** "'please show me your **glory** (kavod)'" *(stated)* — kavod, *glory*: the gem is *the mediator's hunger for more* — having won the Presence, Moses asks to *see the glory itself*; the interior of *the friend of God longing to behold him* — *not content with guidance, he wants God's own face/weight* — *the deepest desire, to see God* *(inferred: kavod = the longing to see God — the hunger to behold the glory itself)*.
- **qara (proclaim) + chanan (gracious) + racham (mercy) — the *sovereign freedom of grace* (33:19).** "'I will make my goodness pass, **proclaim** (qara) my name "the LORD", and be **gracious** (chanan) to whom I will be gracious, show **mercy** (racham) on whom I will'" *(stated)*. **qara** — *proclaim*; **chanan** — *be gracious*; **racham** — *have compassion* (womb-love): the gem is *the freedom of grace* — God answers the request for glory by *proclaiming his name* and declaring his grace *sovereign*: *"to whom I WILL"* — *grace is not compelled, not owed*; the interior (of God) of *free, self-determined mercy* — *goodness that gives itself where it wills*, not as debt but as gift *(inferred: qara/chanan/racham = the sovereign freedom of grace — "gracious to whom I will", mercy free and unowed)*.
- **kavod (glory) + sur (take away) — the *limit and the mercy of the vision* (33:20–23).** *kavod distinct from 33:18:* "'you cannot see my face and live'… hidden in the cleft while the **glory** (kavod) passes… 'I will **take away** (sur) my hand, and you shall see my back'" *(stated)*. **kavod** — the *glory* passing; **sur** — *remove*: the gem is *the limit held with mercy* — *even the friend of God cannot see the FACE* (the full glory would *kill*), yet God *makes a way*: the *cleft*, the *hand covering*, the *back* shown. The interior finding: *the vision of God is real but bounded* — *God gives as much of himself as a mortal can bear, and shields the rest* — *a mercy in the hiding* *(inferred: kavod/sur = the limit and mercy of the vision — the face unseeable, yet God shows his back and shields with his hand)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the seeking and the knowing (baqash/qara 33:7 → chen 33:12, 33:13):** after the breach, *seeking God moves outside the camp*; and Moses, *known by name and favored*, presses to *know God's ways* and to *carry the people* — *the friend asking to understand the friend*.
2. **the Presence staked and restored (nuach 33:14 → chen 33:15–16 → chen 33:17):** God concedes *"my presence will go"* and gives *rest*; Moses *stakes everything on it* — *better no land than land without God*, the *Giver over the gift*; and the plea is *granted for the mediator's sake*.
3. **the longing and the limit (kavod 33:18 → qara/chanan/racham 33:19 → kavod/sur 33:20–23):** Moses asks to *see the glory*; God answers with the *proclamation of his free grace* (*"gracious to whom I will"*), and with the *bounded vision* — *the face unseeable, yet the back shown, the hand shielding* — *as much of God as a mortal can bear.*

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** baqash/qara (the *seeking* of God, outside the camp); **chen ×4 (the favor *leveraged to know God* / the *everything staked on the Presence* / the plea *granted for Moses' sake*)**; **nuach (the *Presence restored* and rest given)**; **kavod ×2 (the *longing to see* the glory / the *glory passing* in the bounded vision)**; **qara/chanan/racham (the *sovereign freedom of grace* — "gracious to whom I will")**; **sur (the hand *taken away* — the back shown, the mercy in the hiding)**.
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **Moses** — the *seeker* who *stakes everything on the Presence* (the Giver over the gift) and *longs to see the glory* (the hunger for God himself); **God** — *restoring the Presence*, the *free sovereignty of grace*, and the *bounded-but-merciful vision*; **Israel** — those who *seek the LORD*, carried on the mediator's favor. The gems: **the Presence is everything**, **the longing to see God**, and **the freedom of grace**.
- **Threads:** **the Presence as the one good** (33:15 ← the withdrawal 33:3; → "one thing I have asked… to gaze on the beauty of the LORD", Ps 27:4; "whom have I in heaven but you?", Ps 73:25 — God himself the treasure, not his gifts); **the longing to see God** (kavod 33:18 → "you cannot see my face" 33:20; "no one has ever seen God" Jn 1:18; "we shall see him as he is" 1 Jn 3:2 — the bounded vision now, the beatific vision hoped); **the free grace** (chanan/racham 33:19 → quoted at Rom 9:15 "I will have mercy on whom I have mercy" — the sovereignty of grace; and the *name* proclaimed here is *sounded in full* at 34:6, GLD-06); **face to face** (33:11 ← "the LORD spoke to you face to face" Deut 5:4; the friend of God, cf. Abraham "the friend of God" Jas 2:23); **the mediator's standing carrying the people** (chen 33:17 ← "blot me out" 32:32 — the many spared on the one's favor).
- **Guarded against:** reducing "show me your glory" to curiosity when it is the *deepest desire — to see God himself* (the finding); reading the *free grace* of 33:19 as arbitrariness when it is *sovereign self-giving goodness* (the name-proclamation of goodness, not caprice); collapsing the four chen into one when each *does* work (know God / stake all / granted for Moses); over-reading the *cleft and the back* into speculation when the finding is the *bounded-but-merciful vision* the verses give; not forcing the people's watching/worshipping (33:8–10, no non-T2 spans) beyond scene-context; keeping "face to face as a friend" (33:11) as the intimacy it states, *held with* "you cannot see my face" (33:20) — the paradox left, not resolved.

# Exodus 34:1–9 — inner-being passage reading (GLD-06-name-proclaimed)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-goldencalf-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. This is the **fullest self-revelation of God's character in the Torah** — given *after* the calf, as the answer to "show me your glory." **Multiple interiors**: **God** (his own character proclaimed), **Moses** (worship, and a plea grounded in the Name). **Lexical note:** the second chesed span at 34:6 and 34:7 carries the homonym gloss "shame" — here every chesed is *steadfast love*.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 2 qara, 4 chesed, 2 avon, the sin-words each treated distinctly or noted.

---

## GLD-06-name-proclaimed · Exodus 34:1–9 · [the glory revealed as mercy; mercy held with justice; the stiff neck turned into the plea] — "The LORD, the LORD, a God merciful and gracious… forgiving iniquity… yet by no means clearing the guilty"

**The passage.** New tablets cut; the LORD descended and **proclaimed** (qara) the name (34:5); "The LORD, the LORD, a God **merciful** (rachum) and **gracious** (channun), slow to anger, abounding in **steadfast love** (chesed) and **faithfulness** (emet)" — **proclaimed** (qara, 34:6); "keeping **steadfast love** (chesed) for thousands, forgiving **iniquity** (avon) and **transgression** (pesha) and **sin** (chattaah), but who will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the **iniquity** (avon)… to the third and fourth generation" (34:7); Moses bowed and worshiped (34:8); "if I have found **favor** (chen)… let the LORD go in our midst, for it is a **stiff-necked** (qasheh) people, and **pardon** (salach) our **iniquity** (avon) and **sin** (chattat), and take us for your inheritance" (34:9).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **qara (proclaimed) — the *self-naming of God* (34:5).** "the LORD descended in the cloud and **proclaimed** (qara) the name of the LORD" *(stated)* — qara, *proclaim/call out*: the gem is that *God himself proclaims his own name* — this is not Moses' inference but *God's self-disclosure*; the interior-context of *God defining himself* — answering the request for glory (33:18) by *speaking his own character* *(inferred: qara = the self-naming of God — God proclaims his own name)*.
- **rachum (merciful) + channun (gracious) + chesed (steadfast love) + emet (faithfulness) + qara (proclaimed) — the *glory revealed as mercy* (34:6).** "the LORD passed before him and **proclaimed** (qara): 'The LORD, the LORD, a God **merciful** (rachum) and **gracious** (channun), slow to anger, abounding in **steadfast love** (chesed) and **faithfulness** (emet)'" *(stated)*. **rachum** — *compassionate* (womb-love); **channun** — *gracious* (the channun of 22:27 now *fully sounded*); **chesed** — *steadfast/loyal love* (the second span's *shame* gloss the homonym artifact); **emet** — *faithfulness/truth*: the gem is *THE revelation* — when Moses asks to see the *glory*, what God shows is *his goodness proclaimed as MERCY*: *compassionate, gracious, slow to anger, overflowing in loyal love and faithfulness*. The interior finding of the whole block: **the glory of God, when shown, is his mercy** — God's deepest self is *love that abounds* — and this proclaimed *after the calf*, to a people who had just betrayed him *(inferred: rachum/channun/chesed/emet = the glory revealed as mercy — God's own self proclaimed as compassion, grace, loyal love, faithfulness)*.
- **chesed (steadfast love) + avon (iniquity) + pesha (transgression) + chattaah (sin) — *mercy held with justice* (34:7).** "'keeping **steadfast love** (chesed) for thousands, forgiving **iniquity** (avon), **transgression** (pesha), and **sin** (chattaah), but who will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the **iniquity** (avon) to the third and fourth generation'" *(stated)*. **chesed** — *loyal love kept for thousands* (again the *shame* gloss the artifact); **avon/pesha/chattaah** — *iniquity / transgression / sin* (the **three** words for sin — the *whole vocabulary* of wrong): the gem is *the tension the Name holds* — God's *steadfast love reaches thousands* and *forgives the whole range of sin* (iniquity, rebellion, failure — all of it), **yet** *"will by no means clear the guilty"* — *grace does not cancel accountability*. The interior finding: *God is not merely soft* — he *forgives AND holds guilt*; and the *asymmetry* is decisive — *chesed to THOUSANDS*, iniquity visited to *the third and fourth generation* — **mercy vastly outweighs judgment** (as at 20:5–6). *Love that forgives all, yet justice that will not pretend guilt is nothing* *(inferred: chesed/avon/pesha/chattaah = mercy held with justice — forgiving the whole range of sin, yet not clearing the guilty; mercy to thousands dwarfing judgment)*.
- **chen (favor) + qasheh (stiff-necked) + salach (pardon) + avon (iniquity) + chattat (sin) — *the stiff neck turned into the plea* (34:9).** "Moses: 'if I have found **favor** (chen)… let the LORD go in our midst, **for it is a stiff-necked** (qasheh) people, and **pardon** (salach) our **iniquity** (avon) and **sin** (chattat), and take us for your inheritance'" *(stated)*. **chen** — *favor*; **qasheh** — *stiff-necked*; **salach** — *forgive/pardon*; **avon/chattat** — *iniquity/sin*: the gem is *the daring reversal* — the *stiff-neckedness* that was God's *reason to withdraw* ("I will not go up… for you are stiff-necked, lest I consume you", 33:3,5) Moses now makes the *reason to STAY*: *"go in our midst BECAUSE we are stiff-necked"* — *the very worst of the people pleaded as the ground of God's presence* (they *need* him all the more; only his presence can change the hard neck). And, having *just heard the Name*, Moses *pleads it back* — asking the *forgiving* God to *forgive*, the *loyal-love* God to *claim them as inheritance*. The interior of *intercession that turns depravity into the argument for grace* — *pardon us and possess us precisely because we cannot mend ourselves* *(inferred: chen/qasheh/salach = the stiff neck turned into the plea — the worst of the people made the ground of the plea for presence and pardon)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the glory revealed as mercy (qara 34:5 → rachum/channun/chesed/emet 34:6):** God answers *"show me your glory"* by *proclaiming his own name* — and the glory is *MERCY*: *compassionate, gracious, slow to anger, abounding in loyal love and faithfulness* — *God's deepest self is abounding love*, declared *to the very people who betrayed him*.
2. **mercy held with justice (chesed/avon/pesha/chattaah 34:7):** the same Name *forgives the whole range of sin* and *keeps love to thousands*, **yet** *will not clear the guilty* — *grace does not erase accountability*; mercy *dwarfs* judgment (thousands vs three-or-four generations) but does not *pretend*.
3. **the stiff neck turned into the plea (chen/qasheh/salach 34:8–9):** Moses *worships*, then *pleads the Name back* — turning the people's *stiff-neckedness* (the reason for withdrawal) into the *reason for God's presence and pardon*: *go with us, forgive us, keep us — because we cannot mend ourselves.*

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** **qara ×2 (the *self-naming* / the *character proclaimed*)**; **rachum/channun/chesed/emet (the *glory revealed as mercy* — compassionate, gracious, loyal love, faithfulness)**; **chesed (the loyal love *abounding* 34:6 / *kept for thousands* 34:7 — the "shame" gloss the homonym artifact)**; **avon/pesha/chattaah (the *three words for sin*, all *forgiven*, yet iniquity *visited*)**; **chen/qasheh/salach (the *stiff neck turned into the plea* — the worst made the ground of the plea for presence and pardon)**.
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **God** — his *own character proclaimed*: *mercy* overwhelmingly (compassionate, gracious, slow to anger, abounding in chesed and emet), *forgiving all sin*, **yet** *just* (not clearing the guilty) — the glory shown as *goodness/mercy*; **Moses** — *worship*, and *intercession that pleads the Name back* and *turns the stiff neck into the argument for grace*. The gems: **the glory is mercy**, **mercy held with justice**, and **the stiff neck made the plea**.
- **Threads:** **the great self-revelation** (34:6–7 — the most-quoted self-description of God in the OT: Num 14:18; Neh 9:17; Ps 86:15; 103:8; 145:8; Joel 2:13; Jonah 4:2 — "gracious and merciful, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love"; the *channun* of 22:27 and the *free grace* of 33:19 now *fully named*); **the glory is goodness/mercy** (34:6 ← "I will make my goodness pass" 33:19 — the *glory* Moses asked to see *is* God's mercy); **mercy and justice held** (34:7 ← 20:5–6 — chesed to thousands / iniquity to 3–4 generations; the tension carried, not collapsed → the cross, where both meet); **the three words for sin forgiven** (avon/pesha/chattaah 34:7 → Ps 32:1–2; 1 Jn 1:9 — the comprehensive pardon); **the stiff neck as the plea** (qasheh 34:9 ← 33:3,5 — the daring reversal: the reason to withdraw made the reason to stay → grace *for* the undeserving, Rom 5:8).
- **Guarded against:** softening the Name into *only* mercy when the text holds *justice* with it ("by no means clear the guilty" — the finding is the *tension*, not a sentimental God); hardening it into *only* justice when the weight is overwhelmingly *mercy* (compassionate, gracious, slow to anger, abounding — and mercy to *thousands* vs judgment to *3–4 generations*); reading Moses' plea (34:9) as mere repetition when it *dares to turn the stiff neck into the argument* (the reversal is the finding); importing the full NT resolution of mercy-and-justice (the cross) as the *meaning* here when the text *leaves the tension open* — the Name states *both* and does not yet show *how*; keeping the chesed "shame" gloss as the homonym artifact it is (every chesed here is *steadfast love*).

# Exodus 34:10–35 — inner-being passage reading (GLD-07-covenant-renewed-shining-face)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-goldencalf-v1-20260705`). Every non-T2 span in its verse; *stated* | *inferred*; distinctions kept. **Multiple interiors**: **God** (re-cutting the covenant, jealous, guarding), **Israel** (warned against whoring, awed by the shining face), **Moses** (radiant from the presence). The covenant terms (34:18–26) largely *re-issue* ch23; surfaced, the genuine spans read. **Lexical note:** zakhar "male" at 34:19 is the homonym of "remember" — here the firstborn *male*.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the 5 berit / 4 karat (God's covenant vs the forbidden Canaanite one), 2 yare, 3 shamar, 2 qara, 2 zanah each treated distinctly.

---

## GLD-07-covenant-renewed-shining-face · Exodus 34:10–35 · [the covenant re-cut after the breach; idolatry as whoring; the mediator radiant] — the bond remade, the jealous God, and Moses' shining face

**The passage.** "I am **making** (karat) a **covenant** (berit); I will do **marvels** (pala)… an **awesome** (yare) thing" (34:10); **observe** (shamar) my commands (34:11); **take care** (shamar) lest you **cut** (karat) a **covenant** (berit) with the land (34:12); "the LORD, whose name is **Jealous** (qanna), is a jealous God" (34:14); lest you **cut** (karat) a **covenant** (berit), be **invited** (qara), and **whore** (zanah) after their gods (34:15); their daughters **whore** (zanah, 34:16); **keep** (shamar) the feast (34:18); the firstborn **male** (zakhar, 34:19) **redeemed** (padah, 34:20); six days **work** (avad, 34:21); "no one shall **covet** (chamad/chamudah) your land" (34:24); "in accordance with these words I have **made** (karat) a **covenant** (berit)" (34:27); the words of the **covenant** (berit, 34:28); Moses' face shone; the people were **afraid** (yare, 34:30); Moses **called** (qara, 34:31); he **removed** (sur) the veil before the LORD (34:34).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **karat (making) + berit (covenant) + pala (marvels) + yare (awesome) — the *covenant re-cut, with wonders* (34:10).** "'I am **making** (karat) a **covenant** (berit); I will do **marvels** (pala)… it is an **awesome** (yare) thing'" *(stated)*. **karat** — *cut* (the covenant-verb); **berit** — *covenant*; **pala** — *do wonders*; **yare** — *awe/fear*: the gem is *the covenant remade after the breach* — *God re-cuts the bond the calf shattered*, promising *marvels* that evoke *awe*; the interior finding: *grace remakes the covenant with a people who broke faith* — the bond *restored, not abandoned* — and its renewal is *an awesome thing* *(inferred: karat/berit/pala/yare = the covenant re-cut with wonders — grace remaking the broken bond, an awesome thing)*.
- **shamar (observe) — the *command to keep* (34:11).** "'**observe** (shamar) what I command you'" *(stated)* — shamar, *keep/obey*: the *renewed covenant's call to obedience* — the interior-context of *the bond requiring keeping* *(inferred: shamar = the command to keep the renewed covenant)*.
- **shamar (take care) + karat (cut) + berit (covenant) — the *forbidden covenant* (34:12).** *shamar/karat/berit distinct from 34:10–11:* "'**take care** (shamar) lest you **cut** (karat) a **covenant** (berit) with the land's inhabitants, lest it be a snare'" *(stated)*: the gem is the *contrast of two covenants* — where 34:10 was *God's* covenant with Israel, 34:12 forbids a *rival* covenant with the Canaanites (a *snare*); the interior of *exclusive loyalty* — *no bond that would rival the bond with God* *(inferred: shamar/karat/berit = the forbidden covenant — no rival bond, lest it snare)*.
- **qanna (Jealous) — the *jealous God* (34:14).** "'you shall worship no other god, for the LORD, whose name is **Jealous** (qanna), is a jealous God'" *(stated)* — qanna, *jealous*: the gem is *God's jealousy as his very name* — *"his name is Jealous"* — the *exclusive covenant-love that will not share* (← 20:5); the interior (of God) of *a love so committed it will not tolerate a rival* — *jealousy as the fierce face of covenant-love* *(inferred: qanna = the jealous God — the exclusive covenant-love, his very name)*.
- **karat (cut) + berit (covenant) + qara (invited) + zanah (whore) — *idolatry as whoring* (34:15).** *karat/berit distinct from 34:12:* "'lest you **cut** (karat) a **covenant** (berit)… and when they **whore** (zanah) after their gods and you are **invited** (qara), you eat of the sacrifice'" *(stated)*. **qara** — *invited/called*; **zanah** — *fornicate/whore*: the gem is *the naming of idolatry as sexual unfaithfulness* — *whoring* after other gods — the covenant is a *marriage*, and idolatry *adultery*; the interior of *the heart's unfaithfulness* — *drawn by invitation into betrayal* *(inferred: karat/berit/qara/zanah = idolatry as whoring — the covenant a marriage, idolatry adultery)*.
- **zanah (whore) — the *contagion of unfaithfulness* (34:16).** *zanah distinct from 34:15:* "'their daughters **whore** (zanah) after their gods and make your sons **whore** (zanah) after their gods'" *(stated)*: the gem is *the spreading of the unfaithfulness* — *intermarriage carries the whoring into the next generation*; the interior of *betrayal that propagates* — *the heart's adultery passed to the children* *(inferred: zanah = the contagion of unfaithfulness — betrayal propagated through the generations)*.
- **shamar (keep) + zakhar (male) + padah (redeem) + avad (work) — the *covenant terms restored* (34:18–21).** "'**keep** (shamar) the feast… all that open the womb are mine, the firstborn **male** (zakhar); the firstborn you shall **redeem** (padah)… six days you shall **work** (avad), the seventh rest'" *(stated)*. **shamar** — *keep*; **zakhar** — *male* (the homonym of *remember*); **padah** — *ransom/redeem*; **avad** — *labor*: the *covenant obligations re-given* (feasts, firstborn, sabbath — restoring ch13/23) — the genuine note among them is *padah* (the firstborn *redeemed*, ← the Passover firstborn 13:13); the interior-context of *the bond's rhythms restored* — *the redeemed firstborn, the kept feast, the rested seventh day* *(inferred: shamar/zakhar/padah/avad = the covenant terms restored — the firstborn redeemed, the feasts and sabbath re-given)*.
- **chamad (covet) + chamudah (desirable) — the *land guarded from coveting* (34:24).** "'no one shall **covet** (chamad) your land when you go up to appear before the LORD three times a year'" *(stated)*. **chamad** — *covet*; **chamudah** — *desirable thing*: the gem is *the providential guard* — while Israel *leaves the land to worship*, God *keeps their enemies from coveting it*; the interior (of the would-be covetous, restrained) — *the coveting held back* so that worship costs no vulnerability; *God guards what obedience leaves exposed* *(inferred: chamad/chamudah = the land guarded from coveting — worship made safe, the enemy's coveting restrained)*.
- **karat (made) + berit (covenant) — the *covenant written* (34:27–28).** *karat/berit distinct from 34:12,15:* "'write these words, for in accordance with them I have **made** (karat) a **covenant** (berit) with you and Israel'… he wrote the words of the **covenant** (berit), the Ten Words" *(stated)*: the gem is *the renewed covenant set in writing* — the bond *the calf broke* now *re-inscribed*; the interior-context of *the covenant remade and recorded* — *the tablets rewritten* (← the broken tablets 32:19) *(inferred: karat/berit = the covenant written — the broken bond re-inscribed)*.
- **yare (afraid) + qara (called) + sur (removed) — the *mediator radiant, the people in awe* (34:29–35).** "Moses' face shone from speaking with God; the people were **afraid** (yare) to come near (34:30); Moses **called** (qara) them (34:31)… whenever he went before the LORD he **removed** (sur) the veil" *(stated)*. **yare** — *fear/awe* (distinct from 34:10's *awesome thing*); **qara** — *call*; **sur** — *remove*: the gem is *the presence made visible on the mediator* — *proximity to God transfigures*: Moses' *face shines* (he does not know it), and the people are *afraid* (reverent awe); he *veils* it, *unveiling* only before the LORD. The interior finding: *the glory Moses beheld now radiates from him* — *the one who dwells in the presence is changed by it, and carries its light outward* — and the people meet that light with *fear/awe* *(inferred: yare/qara/sur = the mediator radiant — the presence transfigures him, the people in reverent awe)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the covenant re-cut, the jealous God (karat/berit/pala/yare 34:10 → shamar 34:11 → shamar/karat/berit 34:12 → qanna 34:14):** *God remakes the shattered bond*, with *marvels* and *awe*; calls for *keeping*; forbids a *rival covenant*; and names himself *Jealous* — *exclusive covenant-love remaking and guarding the bond*.
2. **idolatry as whoring (karat/berit/qara/zanah 34:15 → zanah 34:16 → covenant terms 34:18–24):** the danger named — *idolatry is whoring*, the covenant a *marriage*, and unfaithfulness *propagates through intermarriage*; the *covenant obligations restored* (firstborn redeemed, feasts, sabbath), and the land *guarded from coveting* while they worship.
3. **the covenant written and the radiant mediator (karat/berit 34:27–28 → yare/qara/sur 34:29–35):** the bond *re-inscribed* (the tablets rewritten); and Moses comes down *shining* — *the presence transfigures the mediator*, the people *afraid*, the veil worn and removed — *the glory beheld now radiating outward*.

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** **berit/karat (God's *covenant re-cut* with Israel 34:10,27,28 / the *forbidden* Canaanite covenant 34:12,15)**; **pala/yare (the *marvels* and the *awesome* thing of the renewal)**; **shamar ×3 (*observe* commands / *take care* against rival covenant / *keep* the feast)**; **qanna (the *jealous* God — his name is Jealous)**; **zanah ×2 (idolatry as *whoring* / the *contagion* through intermarriage)**; qara (the *invitation* to idolatry / Moses *calling* the people); zakhar/padah/avad (the covenant terms — firstborn *male* *redeemed*, the sabbath *work/rest*); **chamad/chamudah (the land *guarded from coveting* during worship)**; **yare/sur (the people *afraid* at the shining face / the veil *removed* before the LORD)**.
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **God** — *re-cutting the covenant* (grace after breach), *jealous* (exclusive love, his very name), *guarding* Israel's land; **Israel** — *warned against whoring* (unfaithfulness of the heart), *awed* by the shining face; **Moses** — *radiant from the presence* (transfigured, carrying the glory outward). The gems: **the covenant renewed**, **idolatry as whoring**, and **the radiant mediator**.
- **Threads:** **the covenant renewed** (karat/berit 34:10,27 ← the broken tablets 32:19; the ratification 24:8 — grace *remaking* the bond the calf shattered → the new covenant, Jer 31:31); **the jealous God** (qanna 34:14 ← 20:5; "his name is Jealous" → "I feel a divine jealousy for you", 2 Cor 11:2 — covenant-love as marriage); **idolatry as adultery** (zanah 34:15–16 → Hosea; Ezek 16; James 4:4 "you adulterous people" — the covenant a marriage, sin unfaithfulness — the dominant prophetic metaphor begins here); **coveting** (chamad 34:24 ← the tenth word 20:17 — here God *restrains* the enemy's coveting); **the shining face** (34:29–35 → "we all, with unveiled face, beholding the glory… are being transformed", 2 Cor 3:18 — the presence transfigures; Paul reads the veil as the fading glory of the old covenant); **the redeemed firstborn** (padah 34:20 ← 13:13 — the Passover redemption re-affirmed).
- **Guarded against:** collapsing the two covenants (God's renewed bond vs the forbidden Canaanite one) into one berit-motif; reading the covenant terms (34:18–26) as fresh revelation when they *re-issue* ch13/23 (surfaced, the genuine spans read, the repetition not padded); over-reading the *shining face* into the later 2 Cor typology as its *meaning* here when the text gives *the presence transfiguring the mediator and the people's awe* (the resonance flagged, the finding kept to the verses); treating *zanah* as literal fornication when the text uses it *metaphorically* for idolatry (the covenant-as-marriage, the finding); not forcing the food/feast regulations (34:25–26, no non-T2 spans) beyond scene-context; keeping zakhar "male" (34:19) as the homonym it is (the firstborn male, not "remember").

# Exodus 35:1–35 — inner-being passage reading (CON-01-willing-offering-skilled-called)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-construction-v1-20260705`). Within a thin block, **this chapter genuinely carries content** — the *willing-heart* offering enacted (the payout of 25:2) and Bezalel's *Spirit-skill* extended to *teaching* (the payout of 31:3). **Multiple interiors**: **Israel** (the willing, generous hearts; the wise-hearted makers), **Bezalel/Oholiab** (skill filled and given to teach), **God** (who calls, fills, and inspires to teach). Construction lists (35:11–19) read as scene-context.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the many lev, the nadav/nadiv, chakham, chashav/machashavah each treated by their distinct function.

---

## CON-01-willing-offering-skilled-called · Exodus 35:1–35 · [the willing heart enacted; skill given to teach] — "everyone whose heart stirred him", and "he has put in his heart to teach"

**The passage.** The **holy** (qodesh) sabbath (35:2); "whoever is of a **generous heart** (lev + nadiv), let him bring" (35:5); every **wise-hearted** (chakham + lev) craftsman (35:10); "everyone whose **heart** (lev) stirred him and spirit **moved** (nadav) him brought" for the **holy** (qodesh) garments and the **service** (avodah, 35:21); the **willing-hearted** (lev + nadiv, 35:22); who could **contribute** (rum), for the **work** (avodah, 35:24); every **wise-hearted** (chakham + lev) woman spun (35:25); whose **hearts** (lev) stirred them (35:26); whose **heart** (lev) **moved** (nadav) them, a freewill offering (35:29); Bezalel **called** (qara) by name (35:30), filled with the Spirit — **understanding** (tevunah), **knowledge** (daat, 35:31), to **devise** (chashav) **designs** (machashavah, 35:32, 35:33); "he has put in his **heart** (lev) to teach" (35:34); filled them, the **designers** (chashav + machashavah + lev, 35:35).

### The operations, span by span (individual)

- **qodesh (holy) — the *sabbath first* (35:2).** "'six days work, but the seventh a **holy** (qodesh) sabbath'" *(stated)* — qodesh, *holy*: before the building begins, *the sabbath is set first* — the interior-context of *even the holy work bounded by the holy rest* (the making does not override the sabbath) *(inferred: qodesh = the sabbath set first, before the work)*.
- **lev (heart) + nadiv (generous) — the *generous heart called out* (35:5).** "'whoever is of a **generous heart** (lev + nadiv), let him bring the LORD's contribution'" *(stated)*. **lev** — *heart*; **nadiv** — *noble/willing/generous*: the gem is *the offering keyed to the heart's generosity* — *not levied but drawn from the willing* (← 25:2, now *enacted*); the interior of *voluntary, open-handed giving* — *the generous heart the qualification* *(inferred: lev/nadiv = the generous heart called out — the offering drawn from willingness)*.
- **chakham (wise) + lev (heart) — the *wise-hearted maker* (35:10).** "'let every **wise-hearted** (chakham + lev) craftsman come and make'" *(stated)*. **chakham** — *wise/skilled*; **lev** — *heart*: the gem is *skill seated in the heart* — the *wise-hearted* (skill as an *interior* gift) summoned to make; the interior-context of *ability as a matter of the heart* *(inferred: chakham/lev = the wise-hearted maker — skill seated in the heart)*.
- **lev (heart) + nadav (moved) + qodesh (holy) + avodah (service) — the *stirred and moved bring* (35:21).** "'everyone whose **heart** (lev) stirred him and whose spirit **moved** (nadav) him brought the contribution… for the **service** (avodah) and the **holy** (qodesh) garments'" *(stated)*. **nadav** — *be willing / offer freely*; **avodah** — *service*: the gem is *the interior impulse enacted* — *the heart stirred, the spirit moved* — the giving *welling up from within*, not commanded; the interior of *the moved heart that gives to the holy service* *(inferred: lev/nadav = the stirred and moved bring — the interior impulse to give, enacted)*.
- **lev (heart) + nadiv (willing) — the *willing-hearted, men and women* (35:22).** *lev/nadiv distinct from 35:5:* "'both men and women, all who were of a **willing heart** (lev + nadiv), brought'" *(stated)*: the gem is *the breadth of the willing* — *men and women alike*, stripping their own jewelry; the interior-context of *a whole people's willing generosity* (contrast the same gold given to the *calf*, 32:3 — now given to *God's dwelling*) *(inferred: lev/nadiv = the willing-hearted, men and women — the whole people's generosity)*.
- **rum (contribute) + avodah (work) — the *lifted contribution* (35:24).** "'everyone who could **contribute** (rum) silver or bronze… for any use in the **work** (avodah) brought it'" *(stated)*. **rum** — *lift/raise* (the heave-contribution); **avodah** — *work*: the *offering lifted up for the work* — the interior-context of *each giving what he had for the making* *(inferred: rum/avodah = the lifted contribution for the work)*.
- **chakham (wise) + lev (heart) — the *wise-hearted women spin* (35:25).** *chakham/lev distinct from 35:10:* "'every **wise-hearted** (chakham + lev) woman spun with her hands'" *(stated)*: the gem is *the women's skill named* — *wise-hearted women* spinning the yarn (the *skill* of the ordinary craftswoman honored as a heart-gift); the interior-context of *the whole community's gifted skill*, women included *(inferred: chakham/lev = the wise-hearted women — skill honored across the community)*.
- **lev (hearts) — the *hearts stirred to skill* (35:26).** *lev distinct:* "'all the women whose **hearts** (lev) stirred them to use their skill spun the goats' hair'" *(stated)*: the gem is *skill joined to the stirred heart* — *not only the willing to give but the willing to make*; the interior of *the heart moved to labor its gift* *(inferred: lev = the hearts stirred to skill — the willing to make, not only to give)*.
- **lev (heart) + nadav (moved) — the *freewill offering summed* (35:29).** *lev/nadav distinct from 35:21:* "'all whose **heart** (lev) **moved** (nadav) them brought a freewill offering to the LORD'" *(stated)*: the gem is *the summary of the willing* — the whole giving named a *freewill offering* *of the moved heart*; the interior-context of *the freely-given, the payout of 25:2 complete* *(inferred: lev/nadav = the freewill offering summed — the willing giving, complete)*.
- **qara (called) + tevunah (understanding) + daat (knowledge) + chashav (devise) + machashavah (designs) — *Bezalel called and filled* (35:30–33).** "'the LORD has **called** (qara) Bezalel by name and filled him with the Spirit — skill, **understanding** (tevunah), **knowledge** (daat) — to **devise** (chashav) **designs** (machashavah)'" *(stated)*: the gem (← 31:2–4, restated to the people) — *skill as a Spirit-filling*: *called, filled, gifted with understanding and knowledge and the devising-power* — *the interior gifted for making* *(inferred: qara/tevunah/daat/chashav = Bezalel called and filled — skill a Spirit-gift)*.
- **lev (heart) + chashav (designer) + machashavah — *skill given to teach* (35:34–35).** "'he has put in his **heart** (lev) to **teach**, both him and Oholiab… filled them with skill to do every work of the **designer** (chashav + machashavah)'" *(stated)*: the gem, the *new note beyond ch31* — *the Spirit-skill is not hoarded but given to TEACH*: God *put teaching in his heart*; the interior of *gifted ability meant to be imparted* — *skill multiplied by teaching others* — *the gift that reproduces itself* *(inferred: lev/chashav = skill given to teach — the Spirit-gift meant to be imparted, not hoarded)*.

### The web (interactive)

1. **the willing heart enacted (qodesh 35:2 → lev/nadiv 35:5 → lev/nadav/qodesh/avodah 35:21 → lev/nadiv 35:22 → rum/avodah 35:24 → lev/nadav 35:29):** the sabbath set first; then *the generous, stirred, moved hearts bring* — men and women, freely — *the willing-heart of 25:2 now enacted*; the *same gold once given to the calf* now *given to God's dwelling*.
2. **skill as a heart-gift, given to teach (chakham/lev 35:10 → chakham/lev 35:25 → lev 35:26 → qara/tevunah/daat/chashav 35:30–33 → lev/chashav 35:34–35):** the *wise-hearted* (men and women) make; Bezalel *called and filled with the Spirit* for the *devising* — and, the new note, *given to teach* — *the interior gift meant to be imparted and multiplied.*

---

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced (kept distinct):** qodesh (the *sabbath* set first / the *holy* garments); **lev + nadiv/nadav (the *willing/generous heart* enacted — stirred, moved, freely giving; men and women — the payout of 25:2)**; **chakham + lev (the *wise-hearted maker* — skill a heart-gift, men and women)**; avodah (the *service/work*); rum (the *lifted* contribution); **qara/tevunah/daat/chashav/machashavah (Bezalel *called and filled* — skill a Spirit-gift)**; **lev (skill *given to teach* — the gift imparted, not hoarded)**.
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **Israel** — the *willing, generous hearts* (voluntary giving welling up from within) and the *wise-hearted makers* (skill as a heart-gift, women included); **Bezalel/Oholiab** — *Spirit-filled for making and for teaching*; **God** — who *calls, fills, and inspires to teach*. The two gems: **the willing heart enacted** and **skill given to teach**.
- **Threads:** **the willing heart** (nadav/nadiv 35:5,21,29 ← 25:2 "whose heart moves him" — the *payout*, the offering *drawn from willingness* → the restraint 36:5–6; "God loves a cheerful giver" 2 Cor 9:7); **the redeemed gold** (35:22 ← the calf's gold 32:3 — the *same jewelry* now given to *God's dwelling* — the interior's offering *redirected* from the idol to the LORD); **skill as Spirit-gift, extended to teach** (35:31,34 ← 31:3; 28:3 — the *first* Spirit-filling for *making*, now *for teaching* — the gift that *reproduces*); **the devising heart** (machashavah 35:32 ← Gen 6:5's "evil devising" — the scheming faculty *turned to beauty*); **skill honored across the community** (35:25–26 — the *wise-hearted women* — the gift not confined).
- **Guarded against:** over-reading the construction lists (35:11–19) into meaning; flattening the many *lev* into one when they move between *willing-to-give*, *wise-to-make*, and *moved-to-teach*; forcing the *sabbath* note (35:2) beyond its placement (the holy rest bounding the holy work); not inflating *rum* ("contribute") or *avodah* ("service/work") beyond their plain sense; keeping the *skill-to-teach* (35:34) as the genuine *new* note it is (beyond ch31) without importing a full pedagogy — the finding is that *the gift is given to be imparted*.

# Exodus 36:1–38 — inner-being passage reading (CON-02-wise-hearted-build-restraint)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-construction-v1-20260705`). The **one strong gem** is the *restraint* (36:5–6) — the willing hearts bring *more than enough* and must be *stopped*; the rest (the tabernacle curtains, frames, veil, 36:8–38) is **construction** repeating ch26, captured honestly. **Multiple interiors**: **Israel** (the overflowing willing heart), **Moses** (who must restrain), **the wise-hearted craftsmen** (Spirit-given skill).
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the construction repeats (chakham ×4, lev ×3, qodesh ×4, avodah ×3, chashav ×2) noted honestly.

---

## CON-02-wise-hearted-build-restraint · Exodus 36:1–38 · [the generosity that must be stopped] — "the people bring much more than enough", and the tabernacle made

**The passage.** Bezalel, Oholiab, every craftsman in whom the LORD put **skill** (chakham + lev) and **understanding** (tevunah) for the **work** (avodah) on the **sanctuary** (qodesh, 36:1); Moses **called** (qara) the **skilled** (chakham + lev, 36:2); the freewill offerings kept coming for the **work** (avodah) on the **sanctuary** (qodesh, 36:3); the **craftsmen** (chakham) on the **sanctuary** (qodesh, 36:4); "the people bring **much more** (ravah) than enough for the **work** (avodah)" (36:5); the people **restrained** from bringing for the **sanctuary** (qodesh, 36:6); the **craftsmen** (chakham + lev) made the tabernacle with cherubim **skilfully worked** (chashav, 36:8); the frames **joined** (tam, 36:29); the veil **skilfully worked** (chashav, 36:35).

### The operations (the genuine inner-being content)

- **chakham (skill) + lev (heart) + tevunah (understanding) — the *Spirit-given skill at work* (36:1–2).** "'Bezalel, Oholiab, and every **skilled** (chakham + lev) craftsman in whom the LORD put **skill** and **understanding** (tevunah)… shall work'; Moses **called** (qara) everyone whose **heart** (lev) stirred him" *(stated)*. **chakham/lev** — *wise-hearted*; **tevunah** — *understanding*: the gem (← 35:31) — *the skill is God-given and now set to work* — the *wise-hearted whose heart stirred them* come to the task; the interior-context of *gifted ability enacted in labor* *(inferred: chakham/lev/tevunah = the Spirit-given skill at work — the wise-hearted whose heart stirred them)*.
- **ravah (much more) + avodah (work) — the *generosity that must be stopped* (36:3–7).** "'the freewill offerings kept coming every morning… "the people bring **much more** (ravah) than enough for the **work** (avodah)"'; so Moses commanded, and the people were **restrained** from bringing… the material was more than enough" *(stated)*. **ravah** — *be much / multiply*; **avodah** — *work*: the gem is *extraordinary* — *the willing hearts give SO MUCH that they must be RESTRAINED*: the offerings *keep coming morning by morning* until the craftsmen report a *surplus*, and Moses *proclaims a stop*. The interior finding: *the willing heart overflowing beyond need* — *the payout of 25:2 at its climax* — and *the only collection in Scripture halted because there is too much*. The generosity that had to be *checked*, not begged (the exact reverse of every ordinary appeal) *(inferred: ravah/avodah = the generosity that must be stopped — the willing heart overflowing beyond need, restrained)*.

### Construction detail (surfaced honestly, not read)

The rest of the chapter (36:8–38) is *making-instruction fulfilled* — the tabernacle curtains, frames, bars, veil, and screen made (repeating ch26). Captured, **not** inner-being:

- **chakham + lev (craftsmen)** 36:4, 36:8 — the *skilled workmen* doing the tasks (the skill-gift enacted; noted).
- **chashav (skilfully worked)** 36:8, 36:35 — the cherubim *skilfully devised* into the curtains and veil (the *design-skill* enacted, ← 26:1, 31 — the faint skill-thread; noted).
- **tam (joined)** 36:29 — the corner frames *joined at the top*. An assembly term.
- **qodesh (sanctuary)** 36:1, 36:3, 36:4, 36:6 — the *sanctuary* being built (the holy space; a location/designation term here).
- The dimensions, loops, clasps, bases (36:9–38) carry no non-T2 spans — pure construction.

### The web (interactive)

The chapter's genuine finding stands clear: **the willing hearts gave too much.** The *Spirit-given skill* is *set to work*; and the *freewill offerings overflow* — *more than enough* — until Moses must *restrain* the people from giving. Around it, the *tabernacle made* (construction). No more is claimed than the verses give — but the *generosity that had to be stopped* is a real and striking span, the climax of the willing-heart thread.

## Chapter-level notes
- **Surfaced:** **ravah/avodah (the *generosity that must be stopped* — the willing heart overflowing beyond need, the only collection halted for surplus)**; **chakham/lev/tevunah (the *Spirit-given skill at work* — the wise-hearted whose heart stirred them)**. Construction/skill-enacted terms (chashav ×2 "skilfully worked", tam "joined", qodesh ×4 "sanctuary", avodah ×3 "work") noted, not read.
- **Whose interior (multi-interior):** **Israel** — the *willing heart overflowing* (generosity so great it must be checked); **Moses** — who must *restrain* the giving; **the wise-hearted craftsmen** — *Spirit-given skill* enacted; **God** — who *put the skill in them*. The gem: **the generosity that must be stopped.**
- **Threads:** **the willing heart** (ravah 36:5 ← 25:2; 35:5,21,29 — the *payout* at its *climax*: the willing giving *overflows* → "they gave beyond their means", 2 Cor 8:3; the abundance that must be *restrained*, not begged); **skill as Spirit-gift** (chakham/lev 36:1 ← 31:3; 35:31 — the gift *enacted in labor*); **the design-skill** (chashav 36:8,35 ← 26:1 — the *devising* thread; noted, construction); **the redeemed giving** (the same people who stripped gold for the *calf*, 32:3, now give *too much* for God's dwelling — the interior's generosity *rightly directed*).
- **Guarded against:** over-reading the construction (36:8–38) into meaning — the *tabernacle made* is fulfilment-detail, not inner-being; inflating the many *qodesh* ("sanctuary") into interior holiness-states when they mark the *space* being built; not padding the *skill-enacted* notes (chakham, chashav) beyond their plain sense; **keeping the restraint (36:5–6) at its own weight — the genuine, striking finding — without stretching the surrounding construction to match.**

# Exodus 37:1–38:31 — inner-being passage reading (CON-03-furniture-altar-court)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-construction-v1-20260705`). **NEAR-EMPTY of inner-being content.** These two chapters (the ark, table, lampstand, incense altar, anointing oil; the bronze altar, laver, court; and the metals tally) are **pure construction and inventory** — the fulfilment of ch25, 27, 30. Every non-T2 span is a *material, dimension, space, or skill* term. Captured honestly below; nothing forced.
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the construction repeats (tahor "pure" ×11, qomah "height" ×5, qodesh ×5) noted as making/inventory terms.

## CON-03-furniture-altar-court · Exodus 37:1–38:31 · [construction and inventory; no inner-being content] — the furniture, altar, and court made, and the metals counted

**The passage.** Bezalel makes the ark (**height** qomah 37:1, **pure** gold tahor 37:2, 37:6), the table (qomah 37:10, tahor 37:11, 37:16), the lampstand (tahor 37:17, 37:22, 37:23, 37:24), the incense altar (qomah 37:25, tahor 37:26), the **holy** (qodesh) anointing oil (tahor 37:29); the bronze altar (qomah 38:1), the court (qomah 38:18); the tally — the **service** (avodah) of the Levites (38:21), Oholiab the **designer** (chashav, 38:23), and the metals weighed by the **sanctuary** (qodesh) shekel (38:24, 38:25, 38:26, 38:27).

### The honest finding: no inner-being spans

This unit is **architecture and accounting**. Its spans are:

- **qomah (height)** 37:1, 37:10, 37:25, 38:1, 38:18 — the *dimensions* of the ark, table, incense altar, bronze altar, and court. Measurement.
- **tahor (pure)** 37:2, 37:6, 37:11, 37:16, 37:17, 37:22, 37:23, 37:24, 37:26, 37:29 — *"pure gold"*, the material spec throughout (ark, table, lampstand, incense altar, oil). A material-purity term, **not** an interior operation (as at 25:11 — the honest reading resists the easy allegory of "purity").
- **qodesh (holy / sanctuary)** 37:29 (the *holy* anointing oil), 38:24, 38:25, 38:26, 38:27 (the *sanctuary*-shekel by which the census metals were weighed) — designation terms (the holiness of the oil; the standard weight).
- **avodah (service)** 38:21 — the *service of the Levites* under Ithamar (the administrative oversight of the tally). Function.
- **chashav (designer)** 38:23 — Oholiab, the *engraver and designer* (the skill-thread enacted, ← 26:1; 31:4 — noted, construction).

### The one faint connective note (offered, not forced)

The metals tally (38:24–27) records that the **silver** came from the *census* — *"a beka a head… from everyone numbered"* — weighed by the **sanctuary shekel** (qodesh, 38:25–26), and this silver became the **bases** (foundations) of the tabernacle (38:27). That silver is the **atonement / ransom money** of 30:12–16 (*"a ransom for his life"*, each life counted and equal). So — a *quiet* observation, not an inner-being span here: **the ransom-for-a-life became the sanctuary's foundation** — the redeemed lives *materially undergirding* God's dwelling. The verse gives only the *tally*; the connection belongs to 30:12–16, where the interior finding was read. Noted for the record, not read into these verses.

### Note on the block
This is the *thin core* of the construction block — pure fulfilment-detail. That is the honest finding: **no inner-being content to capture here.** The meaning of the furniture (the ark, the mercy seat, the lampstand) is real theology, but it is *not carried by inner-being spans* in these making-and-counting verses, and forcing it would be over-reading. The genuine gems of Block 5 are elsewhere (the willing heart, CON-01/02; the glory filling the tent, CON-05).

- **Surfaced:** *nothing inner-being.* Construction/inventory terms only — qomah (height ×5), tahor (pure gold ×10–11), qodesh (the holy oil / the sanctuary-shekel), avodah (the Levites' service/oversight), chashav (Oholiab the designer). The one *connective note* (not a span here): the census/ransom-silver (38:25–27 ← 30:12–16) became the sanctuary's foundation-bases.
- **Whose interior:** **none in view** — this unit is architecture and accounting. Honestly, there is no interior to read; the wise-hearted *skill* (chashav 38:23) is the only thing even glanced at, and only as a name in the tally.
- **Threads:** **the ransom-silver as foundation** (38:25–27 ← the atonement money 30:12–16 — the redeemed lives undergirding the dwelling; a connection *noted*, its inner-being reading belonging to 30:12–16); **the design-skill** (chashav 38:23 ← 26:1; 31:4; 35:35 — the skill-thread, enacted, construction).
- **Guarded against:** forcing *"pure gold"* (tahor ×10) into an interior "purity" motif (material purity, not interior — the honest reading); reading the *ark, mercy seat, lampstand* into their (real) later theological weight when the text here gives only *making*; over-reading the *census-silver* connection into a developed theology when the verse gives a *tally* (the inner-being reading is at 30:12–16, not here); **stating plainly that this unit has no inner-being content — captured, not padded.**

# Exodus 39:1–43 — inner-being passage reading (CON-04-garments-made-as-commanded)

- **Source:** verse-first lexicals over the passage (provenance `exodus-construction-v1-20260705`). The priestly garments are **made** (fulfilling ch28) — mostly *construction*. The genuine note is **structural**, not in a single span: the relentless refrain *"as the LORD had commanded Moses"* (≈8×) and the climax (39:42–43) — **the exact obedience** that answers the golden calf. Read honestly off the *work completed as commanded* (avodah 39:32, 42), with the construction captured and not forced. **Interior in view:** **Israel** (restored fidelity), **Moses** (who sees, and blesses).
- **Check-back:** gate run post-draft; every non-T2 verse/gloss engaged; the construction repeats (chashav ×2, tahor ×4, avodah ×3) noted honestly.

---

## CON-04-garments-made-as-commanded · Exodus 39:1–43 · [the exact obedience; the work done "as the LORD commanded"] — the garments made, and "Moses blessed them"

**The passage.** The garments made "as the LORD commanded" (39:1); the ephod in **skilled** (chashav) design (39:3); the breastpiece in **skilled** (chashav) work (39:8); **pure** (tahor) gold chains (39:15), bells (39:25); the plate "**Holy** (qodesh) to the LORD" of **pure** (tahor) gold (39:30); "thus all the **work** (avodah) was finished; the people did according to all the LORD commanded" (39:32); the **pure** (tahor) lampstand (39:37), all the utensils for the **service** (avodah, 39:40); "according to all the LORD commanded, so they had done all the **work** (avodah)" (39:42); "Moses saw all the work… as the LORD commanded, so had they done it; then Moses blessed them" (39:43).

### The operations (the genuine note is structural)

- **avodah (work) — the *exact obedience: the work done as commanded* (39:32, 39:42).** "'thus all the **work** (avodah) was finished; the people did according to all that the LORD had commanded Moses'" (39:32); "'according to all the LORD commanded, so they had done all the **work** (avodah)'" (39:42) *(stated)*. **avodah** — *work/labor*: the gem is not a single word but the *structure the word closes* — the chapter's **refrain**, *"as the LORD had commanded Moses"*, sounds ≈8 times (39:1, 5, 7, 21, 26, 29, 31, 42), and the *work* is *twice* declared *done exactly as commanded*. The interior finding: **the restored fidelity** — *the same people who at the calf made what THEY wanted* (*"these are your gods"*, 32:4) now make *exactly what GOD commanded*, in *precise obedience*; the *self-willed making* of ch32 answered by the *God-directed making* of ch39. Obedience *rebuilt* after the breach *(inferred: avodah = the exact obedience — the work done precisely as commanded, the self-willed calf answered by God-directed fidelity)*.
- **avodah (service) — the *utensils for the service* (39:40).** *avodah distinct from 39:32:* "'all the utensils for the **service** (avodah) of the tabernacle'" *(stated)* — here avodah is the *functional service* the equipment enables (the tabernacle's *use*); the interior-context of *the completed provision for worship* *(inferred: avodah = the service the completed work enables)*.
- **chashav (skilled design) — the *skill enacted in the garments* (39:3, 39:8).** "'in **skilled** (chashav) design'" (39:3); "the breastpiece in **skilled** (chashav) work" (39:8) *(stated)* — chashav, *devise/design*: the *design-skill* enacted (← 28:6, 15; the Bezalel skill-thread); the interior-context of *the gifted skill carried through to the finish* *(inferred: chashav = the skill enacted in the garments)*.
- **qodesh (Holy) + tahor (pure) — the *consecrated crown* (39:30).** "'the plate of the **holy** (qodesh) crown of **pure** (tahor) gold: "Holy to the LORD"'" *(stated)* — the *"Holy to the LORD"* plate made (← 28:36); the interior-context of *the consecrated identity worn* (noted; the reading was at 28:36) *(inferred: qodesh/tahor = the consecrated crown — "Holy to the LORD" made)*.

### Construction detail (surfaced honestly, not read)

- **tahor (pure gold)** 39:15, 39:25, 39:37 — the material spec for the chains, bells, and lampstand. Construction.
- The garment-making (39:2–29) largely carries no non-T2 spans — the ephod, breastpiece, robe, coats, turban made (fulfilling ch28), pure making-detail.

### The web (interactive)

The chapter's genuine movement is *structural and clear*: **the work was done exactly as the LORD commanded** — the refrain drives it home eight times, and the *work* is twice declared *finished as commanded*. And it closes with a deliberate echo: *"Moses saw all the work, and behold, they had done it… then Moses blessed them"* (39:43) — the language of *creation* (*"God saw all that he had made, and behold, it was very good"*, Gen 1:31; the *blessing*). The interior finding: **restored obedience** — the people who *broke faith* at the calf now render *precise fidelity*, and the mediator, *seeing* it complete, *blesses* them.

- **Surfaced:** **avodah (the *exact obedience* — the work done precisely "as the LORD commanded"; the refrain ≈8×; the self-willed calf answered by God-directed fidelity)**; avodah (the *service* the work enables); chashav (the *skill enacted* in the garments); qodesh/tahor (the *"Holy to the LORD"* crown made). Construction (tahor "pure gold" ×3, the garment-making) noted, not read.
- **Whose interior:** **Israel** — *restored fidelity* (the precise obedience that answers the calf's self-willed making); **Moses** — who *sees* the completed work and *blesses* the people (the creation-echo). The genuine note is the *exact obedience*, carried by the chapter's structure more than by any single span.
- **Threads:** **the exact obedience** (39:32, 42 — "as the LORD commanded" ≈8× → the contrast to the calf, 32:4 "these are your gods"; the *self-willed* making answered by *God-directed* making — obedience rebuilt after the breach); **the creation-echo** (39:43 "Moses saw… and behold… and blessed" ← Gen 1:31; 2:3 — the tabernacle a *new creation* / *ordered cosmos*, the maker *seeing* and *blessing*); **the skill-thread** (chashav 39:3,8 ← 28:6; 31:4; 35:35 — enacted to the finish); **the consecrated crown** (qodesh 39:30 ← 28:36 — "Holy to the LORD").
- **Guarded against:** over-reading the garment-construction (39:2–29) into meaning when it is fulfilment-detail; forcing *tahor* "pure gold" into interior purity; **letting the genuine finding be the *structural* one (the exact obedience, the refrain) without pretending a single span carries it** — the honest reading names *where* the content lives (the repeated "as the LORD commanded" + the closing blessing), anchored on the *work done as commanded* (avodah); not importing the creation-typology as the chapter's *meaning* (the echo flagged, the finding kept to the restored obedience the verses show).
