# M02 — Cluster-Wide Findings and Observations

*"Anger, Wrath and Indignation" — synthesis across characteristics C1–C7*

- **File:** wa-m02-cluster-findings-v1_0-20260619.md · **Date:** 2026-06-19
- **Version:** v1_0 · **Author:** le Roux Cilliers
- **Prior output (this session):** wa-m02-lexical-coverage-audit-v1_1-20260619.md; the seven per-characteristic tier analyses (C1–C4 v1_1, C5–C7 v1_0)
- **Inputs:** the four M02 ve_lexical extracts (wa-ve-lexical-extract-M02-20260619-b1..4of4.json); the seven characteristic documents; WA tier catalogue v2 (used as a *guide*, not a template — per researcher instruction); the M02 science extract (T7-lens material)

**Change control (v1_0):** First issue. Cluster-wide synthesis across all seven M02 characteristics. Tier structure used as an organising guide; findings are grouped by phenomenon, not by tier.

**Scope and completeness.** M02 comprises **671 inner-being occurrences** across seven characteristics — C1 Human anger (228), C2 Divine wrath (145), C3 Provoking to anger (85), C4 Jealousy/zeal (77), C5 Indignation (49), C6 Strife/quarrel (83), C7 Bitterness (4) — plus **32 tsur occurrences excluded** (besiege/bind senses, 0/32 anger; exclusion proposal pending). A full occurrence-level re-read confirms the assignment is **exhaustive with no orphans** (671 + 32 = 703 focus occurrences) and that every distinct sense-strand in the data is reflected in the per-characteristic documents (see the coverage audit). Findings below are grounded in that complete set; each is labelled **Observation** (what the data shows), **Interpretation** (what it appears to mean), or **Flag** (a data-quality or method caution). Inferential connections are marked.

---

## F1 — Two vocabulary architectures in one cluster *(guide: T1, T7)*

**Observation.** The cluster does not run on a single vocabulary. A **shared burning-heat family** — cheˈmah, chaˈrah, chaˈron, qaˈtsaph, qeˈtseph, kaˈaˈs, aˈnaph, orgē — supplies **C1 (human anger), C2 (divine wrath), and C3 (provoking)** and *only* those three. The lemma map is unambiguous: cheˈmah appears in C1/C2/C3 (60/51/4), chaˈrah in C1/C2/C3 (56/26/6), orgē in C1/C2/C3 (23/5/5), and so on for every burning-heat term. By contrast **C4 (jealousy/zeal: qinˈah/qaˈna), C5 (indignation: zaˈam/zaˈaph), C6 (strife: riv/eris), and C7 (bitterness: pikria) each run on a distinct root that is shared with no other characteristic.**

**Interpretation.** M02 is therefore **one affect under three relations plus four distinct affects/events**. C1/C2/C3 are not three vocabularies but one heat-architecture differentiated by *relation to the subject*: the same kindling is **experienced** (C1, human bearer), **borne** (C2, divine bearer), or **aroused** (C3, God or a person as object). The boundary between them is relational, not lexical — which is why their edges leak (see F10). C4–C7, having their own roots, are genuinely separate inner phenomena that sit in the cluster by conceptual kinship and co-occurrence, not by shared word-stock. The "burning/heat" root meaning (chaˈron "burning"; cheˈmah "heat, fury, also venom/poison" — Deu 32:33; Psa 58:4) is the conceptual centre of gravity; jealousy adds "ardour," indignation "denunciation/scorching," strife "contention," bitterness "sourness."

---

## F2 — The Divine–Human correspondence runs through the whole cluster *(guide: T0, T4)*

**Observation.** God appears in a defined role in a large share of occurrences: as **bearer** (possessor/agent) of wrath (C2: 144), jealousy (C4: 22), and indignation (C5: 18); as the **object** provoked to anger (C3: 60) and to jealousy (C4: 8); as **contending party** in the covenant-lawsuit (C6: agent 4, object 5); and as **addressee** in prayer across several (C1, C5, C6). The same vocabulary that names God's wrath (cheˈmah/chaˈron) names human anger (C1); the same root that names God's jealousy (qanˈna, used *only* of God — Exo 20:5; 34:14) names human zeal and envy (C4).

**Interpretation.** Anger, wrath, jealousy, and indignation are presented **primarily as divine attributes that the creature images** — rightly (Phinehas' zeal "with my jealousy," Num 25:11; Moses' anger at the calf, Exo 32:19; righteous indignation, Psa 119:53) or in distortion (envy, Gen 30:1; sullen indignation, 1Ki 21:4). This is the cluster's strongest contribution to the programme's Divine-Human Correspondence dimension: the inner capacity for kindled moral response is a point of likeness to God, and its disorder is the corruption of that likeness. **Bitterness (C7) is the one exception** — never borne by God, set explicitly against "the grace of God" (Heb 12:15); it images nothing of God and has no righteous form.

---

## F3 — One cluster, three constitutional kinds *(guide: T2, T3)*

**Observation.** By the term-intrinsic **faculty** field the cluster splits sharply:
- **C1–C5 are affects** — faculty=affect dominates (C1 196/228, C2 140/145, C3 78/85, C4 70/77, C5 45/49), frequently overlapping **moral_evaluation** (C1 31; C4's "jealous God" tagged moral_evaluation).
- **C6 is a relational event** — faculty-NONE in 82/83 (strife is not an inner state but a contention between parties).
- **C7 is a settled disposition** — faculty-NONE in all 4 (bitterness named as a condition, not analysed as a faculty-act).

Where a **constitutional seat** is named (sparse — 45/671), it is the **heart** (dominant), **soul**, and notably the **body**: envy "makes the bones rot" (Pro 14:30, heart|flesh); divine indignation leaves "no soundness in my flesh" (Psa 38:3); zeal reaches the "inward parts" (Isa 63:15). By **type**, the cluster is **status-heavy** (the affects are named as states more than acts), the exception being **C3 (provoking), which is action-dominant** (69/85) because it names a *doing*.

**Interpretation.** M02 is not a uniform field of "emotions." It holds (i) genuine **inner affects** seated in the heart/soul and at times felt in the body, (ii) an **external relational event** (strife) that the affects *produce* but which is not itself an inner state, and (iii) a **settled resentful disposition** (bitterness). This tripartite shape governs how the cluster relates to the inner being: C1–C5 are constitutive of it; C6 is downstream of it; C7 is a chronic corruption of it. The status-heavy typing suggests Scripture treats anger more as a **condition one is in** than an act one does — except provocation, which is inherently an act done to another.

---

## F4 — The cluster is morally graded by bearer and direction *(guide: T0.2, T1.7, T3.8; valence)*

**Observation (valence, CC-confirmed current).** The moral framing differs systematically by characteristic:

| Characteristic | neutral | righteous | sinful | forbidden | commanded |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| C1 Human anger | 117 | 13 | 58 | 8 | 1 |
| C2 Divine wrath | 97 | 7 | 7* | 0 | 0 |
| C3 Provoking | 15 | 3 | 57 | 4 | 1 |
| C4 Jealousy/zeal | 28 | 24 | 16 | 5 | 0 |
| C5 Indignation | 29 | 4 | 7 | 2 | 0 |
| C6 Strife | 41 | 0 | 33 | 1 | 0 |
| C7 Bitterness | 0 | 0 | 3 | 1 | 0 |

*\*C2's 7 "sinful" tags are anomalous for divine wrath — see F10.*

**Interpretation.** The valence is patterned, not random. **Divine-borne** characteristics (C2) are overwhelmingly **neutral/righteous** — God's wrath is never sin. **Human-Godward** provocation (C3) is overwhelmingly **sinful** — provoking God is the gravest misuse. **Jealousy/zeal (C4)** is the most balanced — its single root carries righteous zeal (24), sinful envy (16), and neutral/legal jealousy (28), confirming its tri-valent character. **Strife (C6)** divides between neutral just-cause and sinful quarrelling. **Bitterness (C7)** is uniquely **wholly negative**. The cluster as a whole demonstrates that the *same* inner capacity (kindled response) is righteous, neutral, or sinful **depending on who bears it and toward whom it is directed** — the programme's clearest case that moral valence is set by relation, not by the affect itself.

---

## F5 — The cluster has an internal causal structure *(guide: T6)*

**Observation.** The characteristics are not a flat list; the co-occurrence and "produced-by" data show a chain:
- **Provocation (C3) → anger/jealousy (C1/C2/C4):** "provoked him to jealousy... to anger" (Deu 32:16,21); "provoked him... full of wrath" (Psa 78:58–59). C3 is action-typed and causally prior.
- **Anger/jealousy/hatred/pride → strife (C6):** "pressing anger produces strife" (Pro 30:33); "jealousy and strife" of the flesh (1Cor 3:3); "hatred stirs up strife" (Pro 10:12); the prideful dispute over greatness (Luk 22:24). C6 is faculty-NONE and causally downstream — the relational *output* of the affects.
- **Bitterness (C7)** sits as the **settled root** heading the anger list — "bitterness and wrath and anger and clamor" (Eph 4:31), "root of bitterness springs up" (Heb 12:15) — i.e. the chronic residue underlying the louder forms (inferential, from word-order and the root-image).
- **Indignation (C5)** is the **cooler/judicial sibling** of wrath, paired with it ("wrath, indignation," Psa 78:49) and shading toward grief at its sullen edge (1Ki 21:4) and its godly-grief edge (2Cor 7:11).

**Interpretation.** Read structurally, M02 maps a **lifecycle of kindled response**: a provocation arouses an affect (anger, jealousy, or the cooler indignation), the affect is borne rightly or sinfully, and — if unmastered — it issues outward as strife or settles inward as bitterness. The cluster is therefore not seven parallel topics but a **connected system** with provocation at the front, the affects at the centre, and strife/bitterness as the two terminal outputs (outward and inward). This is the natural spine for any Session B/C synthesis and for the eventual constitutional mapping.

---

## F6 — The relational interfaces are symmetrical and reversible *(guide: T4, T5)*

**Observation.** Every direction of the inner-being relational map is populated:
- **God → human:** wrath (Exo 22:24), jealousy *for* and *against* (Zec 1:14; Deu 29:20), indignation (Isa 10:5), covenant-lawsuit (Mic 6:2).
- **Human → God:** provoking to anger/jealousy (Deu 4:25; 32:21), zeal *for* God (Num 25:11; Psa 69:9), bearing God's indignation penitently (Mic 7:9), committing one's cause to God (Jer 11:20).
- **Human → human:** anger (Gen 4:5), envy (Gen 30:1), strife (Gen 13:7), provocation (1Sa 1:6), bitterness/cursing (Rom 3:14) — and the **positive** "stir up to love" (Heb 10:24).

A recurring feature is **reversibility/turnability**: divine wrath and indignation are repeatedly "turned away," "quenched," or "relented" on repentance/intercession (Jos 7:26; 2Ki 22:17; Jon 3:10; Exo 32:14); envy is corrected "in the sanctuary" (Psa 73:17); bitterness is "put away" and replaced by kindness (Eph 4:31–32).

**Interpretation.** The cluster portrays the inner being as **relationally embedded and morally plastic**: these affects arise *within* relationships (covenant, family, community) and *bear on* them, and most are presented as **changeable** — God's by His own will toward the penitent, the human's by repentance, reframing, or deliberate put-off. The affect is rarely treated as fixed fate; it is something turned, quenched, or put away. (Strife and bitterness, the terminal outputs, are correspondingly addressed by *prevention* — keep aloof, watch the root — Pro 20:3; Heb 12:15.)

---

## F7 — Anger in M02 is densely bound to sin and to the moral order *(guide: T3.8, T6, T7)*

**Observation.** Beyond the anger lemmas, the most frequent cluster-wide co-occurrence partners are **sin and evil vocabulary**: chaˈta "to sin" (15), chatˈtat "sin" (13), raˈah "evil/distress/harm" (12+9). Anger also co-occurs heavily with **the heart** (lev "co-seated," 10), **the face** (aph, the anger idiom, 14), **destruction** (shaˈchat "to ruin" 10; kaˈlah "to consume/expend" 10), and **hearing** (shaˈma "to hear," 13) and **serving** (aˈvad, 11 — idolatrous service). The faculty overlap **affect|moral_evaluation** is itself substantial (C1 31; C4 5; C3 5).

**Interpretation.** The cluster's affects are not free-floating feelings; they are **welded to the moral order**. Anger appears as a response *to* sin (provocation by idolatry/evil, aˈvad/chaˈta), as God's verdict *against* sin (wrath, chatˈtat), and as itself morally evaluated (the affect|moral_evaluation overlap). The "hearing" co-occurrence ties anger to the covenant word heard and disobeyed (and resonates with Registry 213 *listen*). The destruction co-occurrence (shaˈchat/kaˈlah) shows the affects' frequent terminal in judgment. This is the cluster's deepest theological observation: **M02's inner states are the affective dimension of the covenant moral order** — kindled by its breach, expressed as its enforcement, and themselves judged by it.

---

## F8 — Developmental and eschatological orientation *(guide: T5)*

**Observation.** Several characteristics carry an explicit forward horizon: divine wrath as the coming "wrath" (Rom 9:22; Rev 14:10; 16:19) and bounded "indignation" with an appointed end (Isa 10:25; Dan 11:36); jealousy/zeal as the "zeal of the LORD" that "will do this" (Isa 9:7; 37:32) and the consuming "fire of my jealousy" at the end (Zep 3:8); strife as awaiting the "day of recompense for the cause of Zion" (Isa 34:8). Within the sanctification arc, the cluster supplies both vices to put off (anger, bitterness, strife — Eph 4:31; Col 3:8) and a righteous indignation that is *fruit* of repentance (2Cor 7:11).

**Interpretation.** The cluster is **eschatologically loaded on its divine side and formatively addressed on its human side**: God's wrath/jealousy/indignation point to a consummation of judgment; the human affects are placed under a programme of formation (put off the sinful forms, exercise the righteous — zeal, godly indignation). The same word (e.g. indignation) is at once a divine end-time instrument and a sanctifying human fruit — a compact instance of the cluster's divine-human correspondence across time.

---

## F9 — Cross-cluster bridges *(guide: T6.4; flagged for Session D)*

**Observation / Flag.** The data shows defined seams to other clusters:
- **→ M03 Grief.** kaˈaˈs (H3708B) is glossed "vexation/grief" and is read "grief" in C1 (Psa 6:7; 31:9; Pro 17:25) — anger and grief share this term. And the OT "bitterness of soul" field (marah/mar — Ruth 1:20; 1Sa 1:10; Job 7:11), *outside* C7's NT-only focus set, is grief-borne bitterness. Two distinct anger↔grief bridges.
- **→ M06 Hate / M08 Pride.** Strife (C6) is produced by hatred ("hatred stirs up strife," Pro 10:12) and pride (the dispute over greatness, Luk 22:24).
- **→ M10c Defilement.** Bitterness "defiles many" (miainō, Heb 12:15) — a lexical link to the defilement field.
- **→ Love.** Jealousy stands beside love "strong as death" (Song 8:6); provocation can be "to love and good works" (Heb 10:24).

**Interpretation.** These are not noise but **genuine cluster boundaries** that Session D (cross-cluster synthesis) should carry: the anger↔grief seam (via kaˈaˈs and OT bitterness-of-soul) is the most substantial and may bear on C7's membership and on M03.

---

## F10 — Data-quality and method observations *(guide: T7.3.4; carried for researcher review)*

**Flags.**
1. **C1/C2 boundary leakage.** Because C1↔C2 are one vocabulary split only by divine_involvement (a read-resolved field), their edges leak: divine-subject verses (Exo 4:14; 2Ki 13:3) fell into C1, and C2 carries **7 occurrences tagged valence=sinful** — anomalous for God's wrath. These need verse-confirmation; the split rests on a read-resolved field and so carries a **circularity caution** (the boundary cannot be validated from the same read field without independent verse re-reading).
2. **object_type under-population (programme-wide).** Raw `object` is a mechanical hint; `object_type` is read-authoritative but incomplete in places (e.g. C2 object_type=God read as possessor-genitive, not target). Any object-based signature for these characteristics is therefore provisional.
3. **C6 procedural sense.** A material share of C6 is judicial-procedural ("lawsuit/case," Exo 23:2–3; Deu 17:8) that is **inner-being-peripheral** and should be filtered out at VC classification per GR-PROG-007; only the flesh-strife, cause-committing, and covenant-lawsuit strands engage the inner being.
4. **C7 scope.** C7 is NT-only pikria (4 verses); the OT marah/mar bitterness-of-soul field is excluded — membership review recommended (F9).
5. **tsur exclusion.** 32 tsur occurrences (besiege/bind, 0/32 anger) are mis-seeded; exclusion proposal drafted, pending CC patch on approval.
6. **`mode` field absent** from the M02 extract schema (0/703) — no morphological-mode data; sourced from `morph` only if required.

---

# M03 · Grief, Sorrow and Mourning — Cluster-wide synthesis by tier

- **File:** wa-m03-cluster-tier-synthesis-v1_0-20260619.md · **Date:** 2026-06-19
- **Related:** the ten per-characteristic findings wa-m03-char-{a…j}-tier-findings (a at v1_1, b–j at v1_0, 20260619); tier framework wa-tier-catalogue-restructured-v2-20260611.md; science lens wa-m03-grief-scienceextract-v1_0-20260513.md; obslog wa-obslog-m03-ve-char-derive-v3-20260619.md.
- **Scope:** one cluster-wide synthesis, organised by tier (T0–T7), rolling up all ten M03 characteristics *within* the cluster. The cross-*cluster* pass (M03 against other clusters) is a separate, later step. Findings are self-contained (prose can be written from them without returning to source data), grounded in characteristic letters, aggregate counts, and key verses. Observation and interpretation are distinguished where it matters; genuinely open cross-cluster items are flagged, not resolved.
- **Status:** v1_0.

## The ten characteristics (orientation)
Grief in M03 resolves into ten characteristics, which group by what they *are*:
- **Felt interior states:** **A** inner pain/sorrow · **B** distress/constriction · **F** bitterness of soul · **I** debilitating grief.
- **Outward expressions:** **C** mourning/lament (enacted observance) · **D** weeping/tears · **E** sighing/groaning (breath-voice) · **J** voiced complaint (articulate grievance).
- **A figure:** **H** travail/labour-pangs (productive anguish, metaphorical).
- **An extremity:** **G** torment (acute, inflicted, often eschatological).

**Cluster scale:** 580 distinct in-scope verses; OT-dense (OT 529 / NT 114 occurrences); 83 lemmas. The cluster is the largest single body of inner-being expression vocabulary in the programme's grief territory.

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**Observation.** Across the cluster God appears overwhelmingly as the **agent** of grief (25 of 36 divine-role occurrences). He inflicts it in judgement — multiplied pain (A, Gen 3:16–17), anguish of soul (B, Deu 28:65), bitterness administered (F, Rut 1:13; Job 27:2), the Servant put to grief (I, Isa 53:10) — and he reverses it in mercy — mourning turned to dancing (C, Psa 30:11), every tear wiped away (D, Rev 7:17; 21:4). God is never said, in this vocabulary, to *bear* grief as his own state, with one deliberate exception: the Suffering Servant, who bears sorrows (A, Isa 53:3–4) and is put to grief (I, Isa 53:10).

**Interpretation.** The cluster's answer to "does God grieve?" is therefore precise: God is sovereign *over* grief — its author in judgement and its ender in mercy — and, in the Servant alone, he takes it up vicariously. The image grief bears is not a shared divine emotion but a creaturely condition under divine governance, with the cross as the point where the boundary is crossed.

**Created purpose (T0.2).** No characteristic claims original-design status; grief is uniformly a response to the fallen condition — to loss, sin, oppression, and judgement. Yet two purposive movements recur. First, grief turns the person Godward: godly grief works repentance (A, C, via 2Cor 7:9–11), distress drives the cry to God (B, Psa 107). Second, grief is given a productive figure: travail strains toward a birth (H, Gal 4:19). And a strong **eschatological reversal** orients the cluster toward its own cessation — pain no more, mourning ended, tears wiped (A, C, D all converge on Rev 21:4; tears→joy, Psa 126:5–6).

**Typology (T0.4).** The cluster's typology is concentrated and christological-eschatological: the **Servant thread** (A `makh.ov`, I `cha.lah`, Isa 53), the **mourners' comfort** Beatitude (C, Mat 5:4), the **tears-to-joy / wiped-tears** promise (D, Psa 126; Rev 21:4), the **birth-pangs to new birth** figure (H, Rev 12:2), and the **eschatological torment** of judgement (G, Rev 20:10). The direction is divine→human and present→consummation: the Servant establishes the pattern; present grief points toward future reversal — or, for the impenitent, toward final torment.

**Image-bearer (T0.3).** Uniform negative: no characteristic ties grief to the image of God as an attribute. Grief is creaturely; its only God–human sharing is christological.

---

## T1 — Definition

**The cluster's shape.** Grief in M03 spans a structure from interior to expressed to figured to extreme. The **felt** characteristics are borne conditions (A, B, F, I lean status/quality); the **expressive** ones are enacted or voiced acts (C and D are action-led; E is breath-sound; J is articulate speech); **H** is a figure; **G** is an inflicted extremity. Read together they describe a single movement — grief felt within, surfacing in body and voice, sometimes hardening, sometimes relieved.

**Boundary (T1.3).** The cluster's structural opposite is **joy / gladness / comfort** (M04), named explicitly against mourning (Psa 30:11), weeping (Ecc 3:4), and inner pain (Rev 21:4). Internally the cluster is finely bounded: felt vs expressed (A vs C/D/E/J), ache vs pressure (A vs B), grief vs embittered verdict (A vs F), felt vs somatic collapse (A vs I), wordless vs articulate (E vs J), ordinary vs inflicted extremity (A vs G).

**Modes (T1.4).** The cluster operates interiorly (A, B, F, I), in enacted rite (C), somatically (D, E, I, H), articulately (J), figuratively (H), and at the inflicted extreme (G). A substantial **speech-based** sub-cluster gives grief a voice: lament and dirge (C), bitter speech (F), weeping aloud (D), and reasoned complaint (J).

**Immediate response and sustained effect (T1.5–T1.6).** The recurrent immediate movement is *expression* or *the cry to God*. Over time the cluster runs in two directions: a **deforming** trajectory (A consumes, I sickens, F hardens, G is unending) and a **relieving/redemptive** one (A and C turn to repentance, B's cry is delivered, D's tears reap joy, J's complaint relieves). Sustained grief in M03 either corrodes the person or, turned Godward, is answered.

**Reception (T1.7).** Uniform across the cluster: grief is borne, undergone, or inflicted — not received as a gift. Reception-framing does not apply.

---

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**Two uniform negatives, cluster-wide.** No characteristic locates grief at the **spirit** level, and none locates it in the **mind** — not even the cognitive (J) or evaluative (F) members. This is one of the cluster's clearest structural findings: grief is not, in this evidence, a spirit-level or a mind-level phenomenon.

**The seat.** Grief is seated in the **heart–soul** region (aggregate: soul 44, heart 41, flesh 7, inward-parts 3), with a consistent **split by characteristic**: inner pain (A) is heart-biased (11 heart / 6 soul); distress (B) and bitterness (F) are soul-biased (B soul 12; F soul 10). The felt ache gravitates to the heart; pressure and bitterness to the soul.

**The body (T2.6–T2.7).** The cluster is strongly **embodied**. The somatic characteristics carry grief into the flesh — weeping as tears (D), groaning as breath (E), debilitation as sickness and faintness (I), travail as pangs (H) — and the direction is consistently **soul→body**: inner grief expressed and registered bodily. M03 treats grief as a bodily event at least as much as a mental one (a point the science independently confirms; see T7.3).

**Origin (T2.9).** Origin is predominantly **received-from-outside** — loss, adversity, oppression, judgement — with God named as the bestowing agent across A, B, C, F, H, I. Bitterness (F) is distinctive in carrying a **God-as-giver** origin (Job 9:18, "filled me with bitterness"). Origin is typically multiple: the proximate external cause and the ultimate divine permission together.

**Movement (T2.10).** The cluster's constitutional movement is soul→body (somatic expression) and outward-and-upward — groaning, weeping, and complaint rising to God.

---

## T3 — The Inner Faculties

**M03 is, overwhelmingly, an affective cluster.** Affect accounts for 540 of the ~572 faculty tags. Eight of the ten characteristics engage affect alone or chiefly (A, B, C, D, E, G, I, and H which is figurative and tags no faculty). Grief is, first and last, feeling.

**Two characteristics break the pattern — and define the cluster's edges.**
- **F (bitterness)** is the only characteristic with a **moral-evaluative** core (moral-evaluation 12): bitterness is grief that has taken up a *verdict* about its cause (this was unjust / should not have been). This is why bitterness can be both a legitimate lament before God and a forbidden hardening toward others (Col 3:19).
- **J (complaint)** is the only characteristic engaging **cognition** throughout (cognition 14): complaint is grief made into a *reasoned case*, ordered and brought before God (Job 23:2–4; Psa 142:2). G (torment) adds a smaller cognitive edge (the anguish of awareness, 2Pe 2:8), and I (debilitation) a perceptual one (the felt failing of the body).

**Interpretation.** The faculty map runs: a pure-affect core (A, B, C, D, E) → affect with a somatic edge (I) → affect with a moral verdict (F) → affect with reasoned articulation (J) → affect at the extreme (G) → figure (H). The cluster floods affect and, at its two edges, touches the evaluating and the reasoning faculties — the points at which grief becomes a verdict (F) or a case (J). Conscience appears only adjacently, in the godly grief that works repentance (A, C).

---

## T4 — Relational Interfaces

**God→human (T4.1).** Strong and double across the cluster: God both **inflicts** grief in judgement (A, B, C, F, I) and **relieves or reverses** it (Psa 30:11; Psa 107; Rev 21:4). The basis is covenantal and responsive — grief follows covenant breach and lifts on the cry.

**Human→God (T4.2) — the cluster's defining relational pattern.** Grief is the inner state most characteristically **brought before God**. A **God-directed axis** runs through the expressive characteristics: weeping *before* God (D, 7 verses — Num 11:18; Judg 20:23,26), groaning that *rises to* God and is heard (E, Exo 2:23–24), complaint *poured out before* God (J, Psa 142:2; 64:1), distress *crying to* God (B, Psa 107), godly grief turning Godward (A, C, 2Cor 7), and bitterness voiced *to and against* God in lament (F, Job; Naomi). The posture throughout is honest, often raw, dependence.

**Human→human (T4.3–T4.5).** Grief is **shared** (mourning-with, weeping-with — C, D), **inflicted** (distress, bitterness, torment received from others), and once **borne for another** (travail, H — Paul's labour until Christ is formed, Gal 4:19). It crosses every bond — personal, familial, national, even over enemies (weeping over Moab, Isa 16:9) — and can be covenantally **suspended** (Ezekiel forbidden to mourn his wife as a sign, C, Eze 24:16–17).

**Spiritual beings (T4.6).** A sharp cluster finding: **only torment (G)** has a developed interface — demons dread it (Mat 8:29; Mar 5:7), and it is the content of the devil's final judgement (Rev 20:10). For the other nine characteristics the finding is a uniform negative. Grief in M03 is almost entirely a matter between God and humans; only at the inflicted extremity does it touch the adversarial.

---

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

**Transformation (T5.1–T5.3).** The cluster's formative patterns are recognisable arcs: godly grief → repentance → salvation (A, C, 2Cor 7); distress → cry → deliverance → thanks (B, Psa 107); tears sown → joy reaped (D, Psa 126); complaint poured out → relief (J, Hannah, 1Sa 1:18); travail → birth (H, Gal 4:19). The mechanisms differ — conviction (A, C), pressure breaking self-reliance (B), articulation before God (J), productive labour (H) — but the shape is shared: grief, when turned Godward, moves toward an outcome.

**Suffering (T5.4) — the cluster's native soil.** Every characteristic operates in relation to suffering: as its felt product (A, B, I, G), its enacted response (C, D, E, J), its embittering residue (F), or its productive figure (H). Suffering deepens, reveals, and produces the whole cluster — there is no M03 characteristic that stands apart from affliction.

**Sanctification (T5.5).** Grief participates in formation where it is godly: the repentance of godly grief (A, C), the instruction of the house of mourning (C, Ecc 7:2–4), the marked remnant who sigh over evil (E, Eze 9:4), and the commanded refusal of settled bitterness (F, Col 3:19).

**Eschatology (T5.6) — a double trajectory.** Toward reversal: the wiping of tears, the end of mourning, pain no more (Rev 21:4 gathers A, C, D), the comfort of mourners (Mat 5:4), tears reaping joy (Psa 126). Toward judgement: eschatological **torment** (G, Rev 20:10) and **judgement-weeping** — weeping and gnashing of teeth (D, Mat 13:42,50; Luk 13:28). The birth-pangs (H) point to a coming new birth. The cluster's end is thus split: grief abolished for the comforted, grief as final reality for the impenitent.

---

## T6 — Structural Relationships (within the cluster)

**Co-occurrence (T6.1).** The dominant same-verse pairing is **C–D** (mourning–weeping, 19 shared verses) — a near-fused expressive pair, the observance and the tears within it. Inner pain (A) bridges outward to sighing (E, ×4), mourning (C, ×4), debilitation (I, ×2) and distress (B, ×2) — the felt ache surfacing audibly, somatically, or under pressure. Other co-occurrence is modest, and the extremity (G) and figure (H) largely stand alone.

**Sequential and causal-constitutive (T6.2–T6.3).** A causal map emerges across the cluster: external adversity / loss / God → **felt states** (A, B, I) → **expressed forms** (C, D, E, J) → **residues** (F bitterness if unrelieved; G torment at the extreme). Grief moves felt → expressed → (relieved or hardened).

**Vocabulary and roots (T6.4).** Internal root families bind the expressive characteristics (mourning `sa.phad`/`mis.ped`; weeping `ba.khah`/`be.khi`; sighing `a.nach`; bitterness `mar`/`ma.rar`). Several **cross-cluster bridges** are flagged for the later pass: `e.tsev` painful-toil (A ↔ labour/toil), `mar`/`ma.rar` (F ↔ M02 anger — the held-open anger-bleed), `thlibō`/`thlipsis` (B ↔ affliction).

**Distinctions (T6.5).** The cluster is internally differentiated along four axes: **seat** (A heart vs B/F soul), **medium** (C observance vs D tears vs E breath vs J speech), **faculty** (affect core vs F's verdict vs J's reasoning), and **intensity/imposition** (A ordinary vs G inflicted extremity; A felt vs I somatic collapse). The fine boundaries — A↔B, C↔D, E↔J, A↔F, A↔I, A↔G — are what keep the ten distinct rather than collapsing into a single "grief."

---

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**Lexical (T7.1).** 83 lemmas, Hebrew-dense (OT 529 / NT 114). The vocabulary distinguishes felt grief (`makh.ov`, `ya.gon`, `tsa.rah`), enacted/expressed grief (`a.val`, `ba.khah`, `a.nach`, `si.ach`), the evaluative (`mar`), the figurative (`che.vel`, `ōdinō`), and the extreme (`basanizō`). OT→NT continuity is strong: the Hebrew felt and expressed terms are answered by Greek `lupeō`, `pentheō`, and `klaiō`; the NT then develops two registers the OT does not — eschatological **torment** (`basanizō`) and **godly grief** unto repentance (2Cor 7).

**Literary (T7.2).** The cluster spans every literary form — narrative, covenant law, wisdom, psalm/lament, prophecy, gospel, epistle, and apocalyptic — with the **lament tradition** (Psalms, Lamentations) as its liturgical home. The **primary cluster anchor is Isaiah 53** (53:3 "a man of sorrows"; 53:10 "put him to grief") — the deepest point the cluster reaches, where grief is borne vicariously and ordained redemptively; **Matthew 5:4** and **Revelation 21:4** stand as the cluster's comfort-and-reversal anchors.

**Science (T7.3).** The science lens maps cleanly onto the cluster — grief/bereavement research (C, D), pain/suffering research (A, G), somatic/physiological research (D, E, H, I), distress/trauma and embitterment research (B, F, J), and communal-mourning research (C, E). It illuminates the evidence at several points: Bowlby's finding that grief is the measure of attachment explains the sheer extent and intensity of the cluster's vocabulary; Eisenberger's social-pain neuroscience gives the pain terms a literal, not merely metaphorical, basis; the psychosomatic and bereavement-physiology research (van der Kolk; broken-heart syndrome; immune suppression) confirms the cluster's somatic density (D, E, I, H); and Linden's embitterment concept confirms the distinctness of bitterness (F) from acute grief.

The decisive **divergence** is consistent across the cluster: the science is therapeutic — grief is a process to be moved through toward restored functioning — whereas the biblical material both **sustains unresolved lament before God** (J; Lamentations) without forcing resolution, and gives grief **vicarious and redemptive meaning** (the Servant; godly grief; travail toward birth) that lies outside the clinical frame. The cluster's distinctive is the **God-directed axis** (D, E, J, and the godly grief of A, C): grief is not merely processed but *addressed to God* — wept before him, groaned up to him, poured out as complaint before him, and finally, in the Servant, borne by him.

---

## Open items carried to the cross-cluster pass
- **A↔B** (inner pain vs distress): a confirmed within-cluster distinction (heart-ache vs soul-pressure); confirm it holds against neighbouring clusters.
- **C↔D fusion** (19 shared verses): test whether mourning and weeping should be treated as one expressive complex when M03 is set beside other clusters.
- **B→F hardening** and **F↔M02** (the `mar`/`ma.rar` anger-bleed): the bitterness/anger boundary is the key unresolved cross-cluster question.
- **The God-directed grief axis** (D, E, J; godly grief A, C): a candidate cross-cluster interface pattern — grief addressed to God.
- **The Servant thread** (A, I; Isa 53): a christological anchor shared across two characteristics, to be related to other clusters' christological anchors.
- **Held-open reassignment candidates** (`a.mal` toil/moral-evil; `pid` disaster; `sumpaschō` co-suffering): unresolved until the relevant cluster relationships are set.

# M04 — Cluster-wide tier synthesis
## Joy, Gladness and Delight — folding the seven characteristics together by tier

**File:** wa-m04-cluster-tier-synthesis-v1_0-20260620.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-20
**Prior outputs:** wa-m04-char-*-tiers-v1_0-20260620.md (per-char tier answers) · wa-m04-char-*-v1_2-20260620.md (deep dives + synergy) · wa-m04-ib-characteristics-v1_0-20260620.md (distillation). **Sources:** wa-ve-lexical-extract-M04-20260620-b1of7…b7of7.json · WA-tier-catalogue-current-state-v2-20260619.md · wa-cluster-overview-20260610.md · wa-m04-joy-scienceextract-v1_0-20260513.md.
**Status:** Cluster-wide synthesis. Grounded in the lexical evidence and the per-char tier analyses; interpretation labelled; per GR-PROC-002 a working synthesis. Open programme items (tov relevance on C; nichoach human-relevance on G) carried forward.

**Change control (v1_0):** first issue.

---

## 1. The cluster at a glance

M04 holds **seven characteristics** across **1,236 focus-term occurrences in 1,103 verses**. Three affect-core characteristics carry roughly nine-tenths of the volume; four smaller satellites each engage a *different* faculty, extending the cluster beyond pure affect.

| Char | Characteristic | Occ | Verses | Dominant faculty | Grammatical kind | Constitutional seat | Valence character |
|---|---|--:|--:|---|---|---|---|
| A | Rejoicing & gladness | 545 | 446 | affect (pure) | act + status | heart (64) > soul (18) | righteous-led; real sinful/forbidden register |
| B | Delight (pleasure-in) | 189 | 186 | affect + volition + cognition | act + status (willed) | soul (13) > heart (7) | neutral/righteous; notable sinful |
| C | Pleasantness (quality) | 339 | 335 | affect + cognition | quality | heart (16) ≈ soul (13) | neutral/righteous; minor sinful |
| D | Wonder & marvel | 97 | 95 | affect + cognition + moral-eval | act | barely seated | neutral/righteous |
| E | Thankfulness | 16 | 16 | perception + memory | status | barely seated | righteous/commanded |
| F | Cheer & courage | 7 | 7 | perception | act | barely seated | neutral/commanded |
| G | Soothing aroma | 43 | 43 | none tagged | status | not seated | righteous (cultic) |

The cluster therefore has a **core triad** and a **satellite ring**:

- **Core triad** — **A Rejoicing** (gladness as state and act), **B Delight** (that gladness made *directional and willed* — pleasure *in* an object), and **C Pleasantness** (the object-pole: the *quality* that A and B reach toward). Together these are the affective heart of the cluster.
- **Satellite ring** — **D Wonder** (a cognitive amazement at what exceeds the frame), **E Thankfulness** (a perceptual/memorial recognition of benefit), **F Cheer/courage** (a perceptual morale toward the future), and **G Soothing** (a cultic predicate — God's acceptance, not a human state). Each satellite reaches into a different faculty and a different neighbouring cluster.

The M04 cluster definition (wa-cluster-overview-20260610.md) explicitly lists the wonder, thankfulness, cheer and soothing terms, so all seven are M04 by definition; the satellites' distinct faculties describe the cluster's *internal range*, not a mis-assignment.

---

## 2. Synthesis by tier

### T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

The cluster carries a **strong, patterned divine dimension**. God appears as *agent* of the affect in A, B, C and D (he rejoices — Deu 28:63; he delights; he pronounces the created good; he does the wonders), as *giver* of joy and pleasantness (A, C), as *object* of joy and wonder (A, D), and as *addressee* of thanks and the pleasing aroma (E, G). The split is telling: for the affect-core and wonder (A/B/C/D) God is shown **bearing** the characteristic, so these read as **shared between God and the person** — a genuine image-bearing — whereas gratitude and soothing (E/G) are **creaturely movements directed to God**, not states God bears.

On **created design vs the fallen condition**, the cluster's most important T0 finding is the **valence asymmetry across the ring**: the affect-core A and B carry a real *sinful/forbidden* register (A: 44 sinful+forbidden; B: 19) — joy and delight wrongly placed (gloating over a fall, illicit pleasure) — while the satellites D/E/F/G are righteous or neutral. Positive affect, in this cluster, is **not self-justifying**: its standing as created good or fallen distortion turns on its *object*. **Eschatology and typology are silent** across all seven in the lexical (the term *makarismos*, 'blessedness', is present in A but carries no eschatological marker here); these belong to an evidence layer the lexical does not supply.

### T1 — Definition

Definitionally the cluster spans a **gradient from a single pure affect to a non-faculty predicate**. A is *simple* (affect only); B, C and D are *compound* (affect joined to volition, cognition, or moral-evaluation); E is perceptual/memorial; G engages no inner faculty at all. By **grammatical kind** the cluster ranges across the full set — act (A, B, D, F), status/condition (A, B, E, G), and quality (C) — so M04 describes joy both as *something done*, *something borne*, and (in C) *a quality of what pleases*.

The **internal boundaries** are now precise: A→B is the addition of an object and a will (gladness becomes delight-*in*); B→C is the shift from a borne state to an object-property (delighting vs pleasant); A→D is the shift from affect to cognitive affect (gladness vs being-exceeded). The **external** structural opposite of the core is **Grief (M03)**. A **commanded mode** is prominent in A (joy enjoined, 69) and E (thanks enjoined, 6) — a definitional peculiarity: this cluster's affects can be *summoned*, not only *reacted*.

### T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

This tier yields the cluster's **clearest constitutional structure: a heart/soul division of labour**.

| Char | heart | soul | flesh | inward-parts |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| A Rejoicing & gladness | 64 | 18 | 6 | 2 |
| B Delight (pleasure-in) | 7 | 13 | 1 | 2 |
| C Pleasantness (quality) | 16 | 13 | 3 | 0 |
| D Wonder & marvel | 2 | 3 | 1 | 0 |
| E Thankfulness | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| F Cheer & courage | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| G Soothing aroma | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

**Rejoicing (A) is heart-seated** (heart 64 over soul 18); **Delight (B) is soul-seated** (soul 13 over heart 7); **Pleasantness (C) straddles** the two (heart 16 ≈ soul 13). The satellites are barely located at all. **No characteristic ever engages spirit, mind, or conscience.** This is a substantive cluster finding: M04's affects live in the heart and soul, not in the spirit or the mind, and the gladness/delight pair are seated *differently* from one another — a constitutional distinction, not noise.

On **body direction**, only A shows a clear link, and it runs **outward** (soul→body): joy breaks into the shout (*renanah*) and the leap (*salad*). On **origin**, the cluster is mostly unmarked (generated within), with God marked as *giver* in A and C; no characteristic shows movement up the spirit→soul→body axis.

### T3 — The Inner Faculties

The faculty map is the cluster's spine, and it cleanly separates the core from the ring.

| Char | affect | cognition | volition | moral-eval | perception | memory |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| A Rejoicing & gladness | ✓ (544) | · | · | · | · | · |
| B Delight (pleasure-in) | ✓ (186) | ✓ (21) | ✓ (24) | · | · | · |
| C Pleasantness (quality) | ✓ (333) | ✓ (306) | · | · | · | · |
| D Wonder & marvel | ✓ (97) | ✓ (82) | · | ✓ (13) | · | · |
| E Thankfulness | · | · | · | · | ✓ (15) | ✓ (1) |
| F Cheer & courage | · | · | · | · | ✓ (3) | · |
| G Soothing aroma | · | · | · | · | · | · |

Read across, the cluster occupies **affect** (A/B/C/D) and **cognition** (B/C/D) as its main territory, with **volition** appearing only in B (the choosing of *eudokeo*), **moral-evaluation** only in D (the 'surpassing' of *pele*), and **perception/memory** carrying E and F. Two faculties are **absent across all seven — creativity and conscience.** That double silence is a genuine cluster-wide statement: M04 is an affective-evaluative cluster that does **not** touch the sin-witness of conscience or the originating power of creativity. Agency is engaged only derivatively (through the action terms); relational capacity is engaged wherever the affect is directed at persons or God (A, B, C).

### T4 — Relational Interfaces

The cluster is **overwhelmingly a God-and-person affair, and strongly bidirectional on the divine axis.** God moves toward the person as *giver* and *agent* of joy, delight and pleasantness (A, B, C); the person moves toward God as the *object* of rejoicing and delight and the *addressee* of thanks and the pleasing aroma (A, B, E, G). The **human-to-human** interface is thin but real — A rejoices *with* and *over* another, B delights *in* a person — and the **spiritual-beings** interface is minimal (a handful of occurrences in A, B, D; no adversarial weaponisation or angelic mediation is evidenced). The relational scope of A notably reaches even to enemies (joy expressed *over* a defeated foe — Relational, M44).

### T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

This is the **thinnest tier in the lexical**, and the synthesis must say so plainly. The lexical records no sustained-effect, sanctification-arc, or eschatological field, so most T5 questions return silence across all seven. The **one substantive datum** is **A's co-occurrence with Grief (M03, 57 links) and Weakness (M24, 22)** — the lexical footprint of the **sorrow-into-joy movement** and of **joy in the presence of suffering** (e.g. Ezr 3:12, weeping and shouting in one verse). The science review reinforces this as the cluster's distinctive against the immanent model (joy that co-exists with grief, joy in suffering). The formative *depth* of M04 — how joy forms a person over time — lies beyond what the lexical alone can establish and is a candidate for verse-level work.

### T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics

This tier carries the **interrelationships** most fully — both within M04 and outward.

**Within the cluster**, the nearest-neighbour map is: A↔B (gladness vs directed delight — a difference of *direction and will*); B↔C (state vs object-quality — a difference of *constitutional pole*); A↔D (affect vs cognitive affect — a difference of *faculty*); E and G stand apart by faculty (perception/memory; none). The core triad coheres as **state (A) → directed state (B) → object-quality (C)**.

**Outward**, each characteristic reaches into a characteristic neighbourhood (co-term links, names resolved against the cluster overview):

- **A Rejoicing & gladness** → Joy (M04) 170 · Grief (M03) 57 · Love (M05) 52 · Praise (M22) 49 · Righteousness (M26) 48 · Speech (M42) 32
- **B Delight (pleasure-in)** → Righteousness (M26) 21 · Love (M05) 20 · Life (M25) 19 · Remembrance (M41) 14 · Joy (M04) 11 · Calling (M37) 11
- **C Pleasantness (quality)** → Wisdom (M15) 30 · Joy (M04) 25 · Love (M05) 24 · Life (M25) 23 · Righteousness (M26) 23 · Praise (M22) 22
- **D Wonder & marvel** → Wisdom (M15) 21 · Praise (M22) 9 · Love (M05) 8 · Remembrance (M41) 8 · Strength (M23) 6 · Pride (M08) 5
- **E Thankfulness** → Prayer (M21) 5 · Love (M05) 3 · Truth (M13) 3 · Wisdom (M15) 2 · Praise (M22) 2 · Joy (M04) 2
- **F Cheer & courage** → Life (M25) 1 · Repentance (M11) 1
- **G Soothing aroma** → Life (M25) 2 · Repentance (M11) 2 · Desire (M29) 1 · Relational (M44) 1 · Salvation (M38) 1 · Anger (M02) 1

Three cluster-wide patterns emerge. First, **Joy externalises** — A's heaviest non-self links are Praise (M22) and Speech (M42): joy becomes song and shout. Second, **the cluster attaches to the righteous and the beloved** — Righteousness (M26) and Love (M05) recur across A, B and C as the bearers and objects of joy and delight. Third, **the satellites each have their own home neighbourhood** — Wonder with Wisdom and Remembrance, Gratitude with Prayer and Praise, Soothing with Repentance, Salvation and Purity. Under the shared-verse architecture these reaches are read here from joy's perspective and re-presented when those clusters are processed; the reach is by design, not leakage.

### T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**Lexically** the cluster is **trilingual**: a Hebrew core throughout, Greek carrying A/B/D and *all* of E, Aramaic traces in A and D. The Testamental pattern is itself informative — **gratitude (E) is Greek-only** (an NT-register development, *eucharistia*), while **soothing (G) is Hebrew-only** (the OT sacrificial cult). The act/status/quality spread (T1.2) gives the vocabulary its range from the *act* of rejoicing to the *condition* of joy to the *quality* of the pleasant.

**Scientifically** (T7.3), the cluster maps comprehensively onto **positive psychology and affective neuroscience** — joy to Fredrickson's broaden-and-build, delight to Berridge's wanting/liking, wonder to awe/elevation research, gratitude to Emmons & McCullough, pleasantness to eudaimonic-flourishing models, cheer to self-efficacy/optimism. The science **illuminates** the expansive, social, savouring character of biblical joy; it **diverges** at three theological distinctives the lexical insists on — *commanded* joy, joy that *co-exists with grief and suffering*, and joy *grounded in a certain future* — none of which an immanent, circumstance-reactive model accommodates; and it **surfaces a gap**: hedonic adaptation predicts joy fades to baseline, which throws the cluster's tie to *renewed encounter, remembrance and praise* into relief as an anti-adaptation mechanism worth verse investigation. For **G (Soothing)** the science *divergence is the finding*: the wellbeing frame does not apply to a human subject, because *nichoach* describes God's acceptance — reinforcing the open relevance question.

---

## 3. Cluster-wide integration — the picture that emerges

Folded together, **M04 is an affective–evaluative cluster whose centre of gravity is gladness-and-delight, seated in the heart and the soul, whose rightness is determined by its object — God and his acts pre-eminently — and which externalises into praise and song.** Around that core sit four faculty-distinct satellites that extend the cluster into cognition (wonder), perception and memory (gratitude, cheer), and the sacrificial cult (soothing), each reaching by design into a neighbouring cluster.

Five findings hold across the whole cluster:

1. **A constitutional division of labour** — joy seats in the heart, delight in the soul; neither touches spirit, mind, or conscience.
2. **Object-determined morality** — the affect-core is morally bivalent; joy and delight are good or sinful according to what they rest on, not in themselves.
3. **A strong, shared divine dimension** — God bears joy, delight, pleasantness and wonder (image-bearing), and is the chief object and addressee of the cluster's God-ward movements.
4. **Outward expression and living tension** — joy issues in praise and song and stands in lexically-evidenced tension with grief and suffering (the sorrow-into-joy movement).
5. **A bounded faculty range** — the cluster occupies affect, cognition, and (at its edges) volition, moral-evaluation, perception and memory, but is wholly silent on creativity and conscience.

**What the lexical cannot yet establish**, and the synthesis flags honestly: the cluster's **formative depth** (T5), its **eschatological trajectory** (T0.2.3/T5.6), and its **typology** (T0.4) all return silence — these require a verse-reading layer beyond the lexical decomposition. And two term-level items remain open and unaffected by this synthesis: the **tov relevance pass** (C) and the **nichoach human-relevance test** (G).

---

*Grounded in the lexical evidence of the source extract, the seven per-char tier analyses, and the science review. Counts are exact; verse references are citation-ready against the extract (ESV).*

# M05 Cluster-Wide Synthesis — by Tier (T0–T7) across All Six Characteristics

- **Filename:** wa-m05-cluster-synthesis-by-tier-v1_0-20260620.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-20
- **Cluster:** M05 — "Love, Compassion and Kindness"
- **Characteristics synthesised:** **A** Love · **B** Compassion · **C** Kindness/steadfast-love (chesed) · **D** Comfort · **E** Gentleness · **F** Friendship
- **What this is:** the cluster-level synthesis that reads the six per-characteristic tier-answer files *across* each tier — for every tier T0–T7, how the characteristics agree, differ, and together describe one region of the inner being. Each comparative claim is grounded in the quoted verse evidence carried in the six tier-answer files (wa-m05-{a–f}-tier-answers-v1_0-20260620.md), which remain the exhaustive per-characteristic record.
- **Counting basis:** distinct (verse, term) occurrences after de-duplication and the chesed merge — A 300 · B 257 · C 323 · D 237 · E 30 · F 32.
- **Change note (v1_0):** first issue; finalises the M05 tier-catalogue application.

---

## Orientation — what the cluster is

M05 gathers the inner-being characteristics by which a person is **bound to, moved toward, and faithful to another** — God, neighbour, kin, the afflicted, the stranger. Read across the tiers, the six are not synonyms but a **structured field**: **love (A)** is the affective centre and generative root; **compassion (B)** and **chesed (C)** are its mercy-faces — the *felt* stirring and the *kept* loyalty; **comfort (D)** is mercy *enacted* toward the afflicted; **gentleness (E)** is the *mind-governed restraint* in which the bond meets others; **friendship (F)** is the *relational frame* within which love is exercised. The single most powerful discriminator among them is the **faculty signature** (T3); the strongest unifier is a shared **received→given grammar** (T2/T4/T5) and a **scope that exceeds reciprocity** (T4/T7).

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**The cluster is overwhelmingly God-borne — with one telling exception.** Five of the six are predicated of God himself: love (God *is* love; agent, giver, object — 1Jn 4:7–11), compassion (agent-dominant; "the Father of mercies", 2Cor 1:3), chesed (possessor-dominant; God's self-named "abounding in steadfast love", Exo 34:6), comfort ("the God of all comfort", 2Cor 1:3), and gentleness (possessor; "your gentleness made me great", Psa 18:35; and "the meekness … of Christ", 2Cor 10:1). **Friendship alone has no divine-bearer tag** — God is not said to *be* friendship; he *enters* it ("Abraham … called a friend of God", Jam 2:23; "I have called you friends", Joh 15:15). The cluster therefore images God's self-giving character directly, while friendship images the creaturely *relation* into which that character condescends.

| Char | Primary divine relation (T0.1) | Borne by God? |
|---|---|---|
| A Love | agent + object + giver ("God is love") | Yes — originally and definitionally |
| B Compassion | **agent-dominant** (God does mercy) | Yes — a revealed attribute |
| C Kindness/chesed | **possessor-dominant** (chesed is God's) | Yes — his covenant name (Exo 34:6) |
| D Comfort | agent ("God of all comfort") | Yes — a divine title |
| E Gentleness | possessor + object (God's / Christ's) | Yes — Christ-pattern |
| F Friendship | **none tagged**; God *enters* as friend | No — a relation he enters |

**Created design vs fallen condition.** Three characteristics carry a disorder at the edge: **love** and **friendship** can be rightly aimed or sinfully misaimed (love of the world, Jam-register 1Jn 2:15; "friendship with the world is enmity with God", Jam 4:4); **compassion** is uniquely *bounded* (rightly withheld in judicial/herem contexts). The rest read as restored, commanded goods (gentleness and kindness as fruit of the Spirit, Gal 5:22–23). **Typology** is uniform: every characteristic points christologically/covenantally, the divine instance establishing the pattern (Exo 34:6; Luk 1:78; 2Cor 10:1; Joh 15:13).

---

## T1 — Definition

**Kind (T1.2) sorts the six along an act↔disposition axis.** Comfort is the **most enacted** (action 188 of 237); compassion is **action-heavy**; love is **evenly act-and-state**; kindness/chesed and gentleness are **borne qualities** (chesed the most disposition-like of all — status+quality 307 of 323); friendship is a **borne relation**.

| Char | Dominant type | Structural opposite (T1.3.1) |
|---|---|---|
| A Love | action ≈ status (even) | hatred |
| B Compassion | action-heavy | cruelty / mercilessness |
| C Kindness/chesed | **borne quality/status** (most disposition-like) | cruelty / faithlessness |
| D Comfort | **action-dominant** (most enacted) | affliction unrelieved / discouragement |
| E Gentleness | borne quality/status | harshness / violence / contention |
| F Friendship | borne relation (quality) | enmity |

**All six are compound** (T1.2.2) and **all operate through speech** (T1.4.3) — a cluster-wide trait: love is commanded ("You shall love"), compassion is cried for ("Have mercy on me"), chesed is invoked ("show me the steadfast love"), comfort is the speech-act *par excellence* (parakaleō — appeal/exhort/console), gentleness governs *how* one speaks (1Pe 3:15; 2Ti 2:25), and friendship is address and greeting (Luk 14:10; 3Jo 15). The region of the inner being these characteristics occupy is **enacted largely in words**.

---

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**Seat (T2.1) descends from the whole person to the viscera to the barely-located.** Love is the only characteristic seated in the **whole inner being at once** — "heart … soul … mind" (the Great Commandment, Mat 22:37). Compassion is seated in the **viscera** — the womb/bowels (rachamim/splanchna; "my heart yearns", Jer 31:20). Kindness uniquely touches the **conscience** (the "good conscience" of the agathos stream). Comfort and gentleness sit in the **heart and soul**. Friendship is **the least interiorly-seated** (soul, once) — the structural ground of its scope flag.

| Char | Constitutional seat (T2.1) | Distinctive |
|---|---|---|
| A Love | **heart + soul + mind** (whole) | broadest seat in the cluster |
| B Compassion | **viscera / womb / bowels** | most somatic; emphatic body-origin |
| C Kindness/chesed | heart, soul, **conscience** | only one engaging conscience substantially |
| D Comfort | heart, soul (+ mind via exhortation) | — |
| E Gentleness | heart, soul, inward | mind-governed (see T3) |
| F Friendship | soul (once) — **least located** | scope flag |

**Movement (T2.10) is the cluster's shared grammar: from God, onto the person, outward to others.** This received→relayed motion is explicit everywhere — love ("we love because he first loved us", 1Jn 4:19), mercy ("from God the Father"), chesed (God's own, mirrored), and, most sharply, **comfort's received→given relay** ("comforts us … so that we may be able to comfort … with the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God", 2Cor 1:4). The **body link** is emphatic only for compassion (the womb originates it) and expressive for love (kiss, embrace).

---

## T3 — The Inner Faculties (the primary discriminator)

**The faculty signature is what most precisely distinguishes the six.** Four are **affect-led**; gentleness is **cognition-only** and never affect (its defining silence); friendship is **affect-only**; compassion adds **perception** (the eye that pities); comfort adds **cognition** (the exhortation pole); kindness adds **conscience**.

| Char | Affect | Cognition | Perception | Conscience | Moral-eval | Signature |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A Love | ●● dominant | ○ light | ○ light | ○ light | ● flips on object | whole-faculty; morally pivotal |
| B Compassion | ●● dominant | — (pre-deliberative) | ● the eye pities | ○ | ● bounded by justice | perceptually-triggered, visceral |
| C Kindness | ● partial | ○ light | — | ● good conscience | ● sins by absence | borne, conscience-engaging |
| D Comfort | ●● dominant | ● exhortation | — | ○ one case | ○ neutral-heavy | enacted; consolation+exhortation |
| E Gentleness | **— never** | ●● the only faculty | — | — | ● wholly positive | **mind-governed restraint** |
| F Friendship | ●● dominant | ○ disclosure | — | — | ● flips on object | felt relational bond |

**The moral-evaluation row (T3.8) is itself a finding.** Love and friendship **flip on their object** (right or sinful by *whom/what* is loved or befriended — 1Jn 2:15; Jam 4:4). Compassion is **bounded by justice** (the one affection rightly *withheld* — Deu 19:21; 1Sa 15:3). Kindness **sins by absence or pretence**, not misdirection (withholding, boasting, fickleness — Job 6:14; Pro 20:6; Hos 6:4). Gentleness and comfort are near-wholly positive. **Relational capacity (T3.11)** is engaged by all six, but in friendship it is engaged *as the bond between persons* rather than as one faculty within a person — the recurring scope flag.

---

## T4 — Relational Interfaces

**Every characteristic runs in both vertical directions and is, at root, other-directed.** God extends each toward the person (T4.1) — loving, pitying, keeping chesed, comforting, exalting the gentle, befriending; and each appears in the person's movement toward God (T4.2) — loving God (the first commandment), crying for mercy, the chasid's devotion, pleading with God, seeking humility, Abraham's friendship with God.

**Two cluster-wide rules emerge:**

1. **Received-before-given (T4.3.3).** A person must first have *received* the characteristic from God before extending it: love ("if God so loved us, we also ought to love", 1Jn 4:11; "he first loved us", 1Jn 4:19); mercy ("the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God", 2Cor 1:4 — mercy/comfort both); chesed (answering prior chesed, 1Ch 19:2; "put on … kindness", Col 3:12); gentleness ("received with meekness", then extended, Jam 1:21). The cluster's outward flow is always downstream of a divine gift.

2. **Scope exceeds reciprocity (T4.5).** Five of six **cross relational and covenantal boundaries** — love to the neighbour and enemy (Luk 10:27), gentleness "toward all people" (Tit 3:2) including "the unjust" (1Pe 2:18), comfort to any in affliction, kindness to outsiders (1Sa 15:6), friendship even to sinners (Jesus, Luk 7:34). **Compassion is the lone exception that is also *bounded*** — extended widely to the needy and guilty, yet explicitly *withheld* in judicial/herem contexts (Deu 19:21; 1Sa 15:3). **Comfort is the most *received*** (highest self-experiencer share — it is felt *in* the afflicted, not only extended).

**Spiritual-beings interface (T4.6) is silent across all six** — no characteristic in M05 is shown operating toward, attacked by, or mediated through angelic or adversarial beings. This is a uniform cluster-level silence (a candidate finding for Session D).

---

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

**Sanctification (T5.5) gathers the cluster into one renewed character.** Col 3:12 puts them on together — "compassionate hearts, kindness, humility, meekness, and patience" — and Gal 5:22–23 names love, kindness/goodness, and gentleness as the Spirit's single fruit. The six are formed *together* as the relational face of the renewed person.

**Suffering (T5.4) relates to each differently** — and this is a clean cross-cluster gradient: compassion **arises from** the sight of suffering; comfort **answers** affliction (its native context); gentleness **endures** injustice (1Pe 2:18; 2Ti 2:24); love is **costly self-giving** under affliction (Joh 15:13); friendship is **proven** in danger and death (Joh 15:13; Luk 21:16); kindness/chesed is the **refuge** appealed to in distress (its "endures forever", 1Ch 16:34).

**Eschatology (T5.6) is uniform in direction, varied in image:** love "never ends" and "abides" (1Cor 13:8, 13); the meek "inherit the earth" (Mat 5:5); mercy yields "a living hope" (1Pe 1:3); chesed "endures forever" (1Ch 16:34); comfort sustains toward hope and salvation; friendship is "received … into the eternal dwellings" (Luk 16:9). The whole cluster leans toward a consummation in which the bond endures.

---

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics

**The six are internally interlocked, and the nearest-neighbour map is precise.**

| Char | Nearest neighbour | Precise distinction (T6.5) |
|---|---|---|
| A Love | F Friendship | love = the affection/act given to any object; friendship = the standing mutual bond hosting it |
| B Compassion | C Kindness/chesed | compassion = **felt, momentary** visceral stirring; chesed = **kept, durable** loyalty |
| C Kindness/chesed | B Compassion | (same axis — felt vs kept) |
| D Comfort | B Compassion | compassion = mercy **felt**; comfort = mercy **enacted/spoken** toward the afflicted |
| E Gentleness | Humility (M09 territory) | gentleness = manner **toward others**; humility = posture **before God / concerning self** |
| F Friendship | A Love | act/affection vs standing relation (a *category* distinction — scope flag) |

**Root architecture (T6.4) confirms the field.** The **phil-** root generates love, friendship, brotherly-love, and benevolence (A/F and kin) — friendship is a *species of love's bonding*. The **chesed** field and the "gracious and merciful … steadfast love" formulae bridge compassion (B) and kindness (C) as **adjacent covenant mercies**. The **racham/womb** root is compassion's alone. **parakaleō** generates comfort's consolation-exhortation core. **praus/anavah** generate gentleness, with anavah reaching into humility.

**Causal/constitutive links (T6.3):** love "is patient and kind" (1Cor 13:4) — it **contains** kindness (C) and patience as its own operations; compassion **issues in** comfort ("the Father of mercies and God of all comfort", 2Cor 1:3 — B→D); wisdom **produces** gentleness ("the meekness of wisdom", Jam 3:13); friendship is the **frame** within which love is laid down (Joh 15:13). **Love is the generative centre**; the others are its specifications, mercies, manners, and frames.

---

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**Anchors and person-types (T7.1, T7.2).**

| Char | Primary anchor (T7.2.5) | Person-type term (T7.1.6) | Supplication term (T7.1.7) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A Love | 1Jn 4:10 ("he loved us … and sent his Son") | the beloved (agapētoi) | — |
| B Compassion | Luk 1:78 ("the tender mercy of our God") | the merciful (rachum/eleēmōn) | the cry "Have mercy on me" |
| C Kindness/chesed | Exo 34:6 ("abounding in steadfast love") | the godly one (chasid) | "show me the steadfast love" |
| D Comfort | 2Cor 1:3–4 (the received→given relay) | the comforter | parakaleō (the plea itself) |
| E Gentleness | 2Cor 10:1 ("meekness … of Christ") | the meek (praus) | — |
| F Friendship | Joh 15:13 ("lay down his life for his friends") | the friend (filos) | — |

**OT→NT development (T7.1.8)** is consistent: the Hebrew covenant-and-affection field (ahavah, racham, chesed, nacham, anavah) carries into a differentiated and elevated Greek vocabulary — **agapē** elevated to name God's self-giving love; **splanchna** preserving the visceral mercy; **chrēstotēs/agathōsynē** rendering chesed's benevolence; **parakaleō** developing consolation into a fuller come-alongside (and standing behind the *Paraclete*); **praotēs** moving gentleness's centre from posture-before-God to manner-toward-others.

**Human science (T7.3) — the cluster's unifying divergence.** Each characteristic has rich science coverage (attachment theory for love; empathy/social-neuroscience for compassion; prosocial/positive psychology for kindness and gentleness; clinical/consolation psychology for comfort; belonging/social-capital for friendship), and in each the science *illuminates* the embodied and dispositional data (oxytocin and the embrace/kiss vocabulary; shared-pain circuits and the splanchna idiom; agreeableness and gentleness as settled self-regulation; the receiving of comfort; belonging as a fundamental need). **But the divergence is the same across all six:** the corpus commands and grounds these bonds **beyond reciprocity and natural affiliation** — love to the enemy, mercy to the guilty who return, kindness as covenant loyalty, gentleness to the unjust, friendship with sinners and with God — anchored in **God's character and covenant**, a scope and ground the human-science frameworks (evolved bonding, in-group preference, reciprocity, therapeutic technique) **cannot generate**. This is the cluster's theological signature.

---

## Cluster-level conclusions

1. **One region, six members, sorted by faculty.** M05 describes the inner being's capacity for *bonded, faithful, other-directed* life. The members are most precisely told apart by **faculty signature** (T3): love whole-faculty and affect-led; compassion perceptual-visceral; kindness borne and conscience-bearing; comfort enacted with a cognitive exhortation pole; **gentleness mind-governed and never affective**; friendship purely the felt relational bond.

2. **Love is the generative centre.** By root (phil-), by content (love "is patient and kind"), and by structure (the frame friendship hosts; the affection compassion and chesed specify), love grounds the cluster; the others are its mercies, manners, enactments, and frames.

3. **A shared grammar: received-before-given, and scope beyond reciprocity.** The cluster flows from God onto the person and out to others (T2/T4/T5), and reaches past natural affiliation to enemy, stranger, sinner, and the guilty (T4/T7) — except where compassion is justly bounded.

4. **Two structural distinctives at the edges.** **Compassion** is uniquely *bounded by justice* (the one affection rightly withheld). **Friendship** carries a standing *scope flag* (relational category vs inner-being characteristic) — the least interiorly-seated, the only one with no divine bearer.

---
