# M06 — Cross-Characteristic Cluster Review by Tier (consolidation)

**File:** wa-m06-cluster-review-by-tier-v1_0-20260620.md · **Date:** 2026-06-20
**Cluster:** M06 — Hate, Contempt and Hostility
**Consolidates:** wa-m06-char-{a,b,c,d,e,f}-tieranswers-v1_0-20260620.md (the six per-characteristic tier files)
**Evidence base:** wa-ve-lexical-extract-M06-20260620 (b1–b3) + the six discovery files + wa-m06-hate-scienceextract §1–4 (T7.3)

> Purpose: read the cluster *down each tier*, showing what each characteristic contributes to that tier and the pattern they form together. Every claim ties to the per-characteristic evidence; gaps are stated as silences. The six characteristics: **C-A** aversive affect · **C-B** appraisive contempt · **C-C** loathing · **C-D** reproach/taunt · **C-E** adversarial enmity · **C-F** cruelty/ruthlessness. (431 occ; C-A 175 · C-D 111 · C-B 69 · C-F 38 · C-C 29 · C-E 9.)

---

## Tier-engagement map (orientation)

| Tier | C-A | C-B | C-C | C-D | C-E | C-F |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **T0** Divine image | strong (God hates evil) | partial (God mostly object) | strong (God abhors; eschatology) | strong (God object+remover) | silent (no God) | strong-negative (no divine instance) |
| **T1** Definition | full | full | full | full | partial | full |
| **T2** Location | soul>heart | soul≈heart | flesh+soul (only flesh) | heart>soul (social) | unseated (none) | soul (mostly unseated) |
| **T3** Faculties | affect+cognition | moral_evaluation | none (act/category) | affect (borne) | none (relation) | partial affect |
| **T4** Relational | both God-dirs + person | human→God dominant | God→human; spiritual-being | both God-dirs + borne | person-role only | person (victims) |
| **T5** Formative | mostly silent | mostly silent | eschatology | suffering+eschatology | silent | suffering (inflicts) |
| **T6** Structural | hub (root→enemy) | pairs with C-D | disgust-pair w/ C-B | pairs with C-B | relation-pole of C-A | disposition-pole of C-E |
| **T7** Evidential | OT; anchor Psa 139:21–22 | OT; anchor Isa 53:3 | OT+NT; anchor Deu 7:26 | OT; anchor Psa 69 | OT+NT; anchor Exo 23:22 | OT+NT; anchor Pro 12:10 |

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**Cluster finding.** M06 displays a clear **divine-instance gradient**. At one end, **hatred and loathing *of evil* are borne by God himself** (C-A divine agent ×15; C-C divine agent ×3) — these are holy aversions with a created-design pole. At the other end, **enmity (C-E) and cruelty (C-F) have no divine instance at all** — purely creaturely, wholly fallen. Between them, **contempt (C-B)** and **reproach (C-D)** are chiefly things done *to* God (object ×15 and ×18) which God answers — God as the one despised/defied, and (C-D) the one who lifts disgrace.

**Per-characteristic contribution.**
- **C-A** — the cluster's strongest image-bearing case: God hates evil/false-worship (Pro 6:16; Isa 1:14; Mal 1:3), so *hatred of evil* is a shared, valence-differentiated likeness. Typology: Mal 1:2–3 (election).
- **C-C** — divine abhorrence of bloodshed/pride (Psa 5:6; Amo 6:8); the **only characteristic with an eschatological T0.2.3** (everlasting abhorrence, Dan 12:2). Typology: de.ra.on (final judgement).
- **C-D** — God is the defied object (Goliath/Rabshakeh) *and* the redemptive remover of reproach (Jos 5:9; Zep 3:18); eschatological removal of shame. Typology: Psa 69 (reproach borne for God / christological).
- **C-B** — predominantly creaturely contempt *of* God (Num 16:30; Psa 10:13); God's agency is rare and **judicial** (Deu 32:19). Typology: Isa 53:3 (the despised servant).
- **C-E** — **silent**: no God-relation tagged (the covenant-court adversary register sits outside the extract).
- **C-F** — **the sharpest negative finding**: zero divine involvement — cruelty has **no holy analogue**, the only such characteristic in M06.

**Pattern.** The "holy end" of M06 is *aversion/loathing of evil*; the "fallen end" is *enmity/cruelty*; *contempt/reproach* are the provocations against God. Created-design vs fallen (T0.2.2) tracks the bivalence gradient (below).

## T1 — Definition

**Cluster finding.** Across the six, M06 instantiates **the full range of inner-being phenomenon-kinds**: an **act** (C-A `sa.ne`), a **verdict** (C-B `buz`), a **condition** (C-D `cher.pah`), a **visceral/ritual repudiation** (C-C `ta.av`/`she.qets`), a **relation** (C-E `antidikos`), and a **character quality** (C-F `a.rits`). The cluster is not one kind of thing negatively valenced — it is the negative pole expressed in act, verdict, condition, relation, and disposition.

**Per-characteristic kind (T1.2.1) and compound structure (T1.2.2).**
- **C-A** act+status; compound **affect+cognition** (felt + appraised).
- **C-B** verdict (status) + act; two-register (moral_evaluation verdict + faculty-absent acts + `ba.ash` object-side).
- **C-C** act + object-noun; dual **ritual/somatic + moral** register.
- **C-D** condition + act; **affect-condition (cher.pah) + faculty-absent act (cha.raph)** — the clearest condition/act pairing.
- **C-E** relation (status); **simple**.
- **C-F** quality; quality + partial-affect (`a.rits` ferocity).

**Structural opposites (T1.3.1) — the positive characteristics M06 opposes.** C-A↔**love** (M05); C-B↔**honour/esteem**; C-C↔**delight/clean**; C-D↔**honour/glory**; C-E↔**friendship/peace**; C-F↔**mercy/compassion**. *Consolidation point:* M06 is the systematic negative of **love, honour, delight, peace, and mercy** — a multi-front "anti" cluster, not the inverse of a single positive.

**Speech-mode (T1.4.3).** Strongest in **C-D** (taunt is intrinsically a speech-act); present as *commanded* speech in C-A and C-C (hate/detest evil); as insolent mistreatment in C-F (`hubrizō`); largely absent in C-B and C-E.

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**Cluster finding.** When seated at all, M06 sits in **soul and heart**; **flesh is engaged only by C-C** (the ritually detestable); **spirit, mind, and conscience are never engaged** anywhere in the cluster. A large share is **unseated** — the outward/relational/dispositional terms (C-D social, C-E entirely, C-F mostly).

**Per-characteristic seat.**
- **C-A** soul (16) > heart (8) > flesh (1) — soul-leaning; the deepest-seated.
- **C-B** soul (7) ≈ heart (6); never flesh — cognitive/evaluative.
- **C-C** **flesh (3)** + soul (3) + heart (2) — the **only flesh-seating set** (ritual detestable); body link **indicative**.
- **C-D** heart (5) > soul (3); 103 unseated — **social/relational** location (science §4).
- **C-E** **entirely unseated** — a relation, not a located state.
- **C-F** soul (4) + flesh (1); 34 unseated — a disposition.

**Origin/movement (T2.9–T2.10).** Mostly unstated; **received-from-outside** appears in C-A (3), C-D (2), C-C (1), C-E (1) — hatred and reproach can arrive *onto* a person from another. No spirit→soul→body movement tagged.

## T3 — The Inner Faculties

**Cluster finding (the major T3 result).** M06 engages a **narrow faculty band**: only **affect**, **cognition** (as appraisal), and **moral_evaluation** are tagged anywhere. **Eight of the eleven faculties are never engaged across the whole cluster** — perception, memory, creativity, volition, agency, conscience, conscientiousness, and relational-capacity are *silent at the tag level* in all 431 occurrences. Where these faculties are arguably implicated (volition in commanded hatred; relational-capacity throughout; conscience-suppression in cruelty), the connection is **inferential**, not tagged.

**Faculty-depth ordering across the six:**
1. **C-A** — affect (175, all) **+ cognition** (143) — the deepest interior engagement; hatred as feeling-fused-with-judgement.
2. **C-B** — **moral_evaluation** (19) — the evaluative faculty; contempt as a worth-verdict (only 3 affect).
3. **C-D** — **affect** on the borne-disgrace pole (`cher.pah` 72); the act-pole (`cha.raph`) is faculty-absent.
4. **C-F** — **partial affect** (`a.rits` 21, ferocity); the `akhzar`-family faculty-absent.
5. **C-C** — **no faculty** (act/category); interior signal only via 3 flesh-seats.
6. **C-E** — **no faculty** (relation); blanket silence across all 33 T3 questions.

*Consolidation point:* the inner/outer boundary does **not** run between characteristics; it runs **through** them. C-B (verdict + acts), C-D (felt disgrace + taunt), and C-F (ferocity + named trait) each carry an interior pole and a faculty-absent outer pole. Any "interior vs expression" modelling must operate *within* characteristics, not by sorting whole characteristics to one side (this is the evidence's answer to the earlier IC3).

## T4 — Relational Interfaces

**Cluster finding.** M06 is intensely relational, and its God-interface is **asymmetric and direction-specific**:
- **God → human** (T4.1): God hates evil (C-A 15), abhors evil (C-C 3), removes/imposes reproach (C-D 9), judicially rejects (C-B 3). **C-E, C-F: none.**
- **Human → God** (T4.2): the dominant negative vectors — **despising God** (C-B 15), **taunting/defying God** (C-D 18), **hating God** (C-A 10). **C-C, C-E, C-F: none.** Human hostility *toward God* is carried by contempt, reproach, and hatred.
- **Human → human** (T4.3–T4.5): person-directed in every characteristic — C-A (75), C-D (27), C-B (22), C-C (7), C-E (3), C-F (acts on victims). Reproach is notably **borne/received** (C-D self 17); cruelty is **suffered** by victims (C-F).
- **Spiritual beings** (T4.6): only **C-C** (object spiritual-being ×1 — idols/false worship) and **C-E** (`antidikos` cosmic-adversary sense — inferential flag, untagged). Otherwise silent.

**Per-characteristic vector summary.** C-A both God-directions + the person mass; C-B human→God dominant; C-C God→human + the spiritual-being case; C-D both God-directions + the borne-disgrace; C-E person-role only (no God); C-F victims only (no God).

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

**Cluster finding.** T5 is the cluster's **thinnest tier** — the lexical extract is per-occurrence and carries little transformation/sanctification data, so most T5 questions are **SILENT** across all six characteristics. Three threads carry real evidence:
- **Eschatology (T5.6):** **C-C** (everlasting abhorrence, Dan 12:2) and **C-D** (removal of reproach at restoration, Joe 2:19; Zep 3:18) — the cluster's only eschatological orientations.
- **Suffering (T5.4):** **C-D** — reproach *is* borne social suffering (Psa 69; Lam 3:61); **C-F** — cruelty is the *agent* of affliction (Luk 18:32; Act 14:5; 1Th 2:2). Reproach is suffering *received*; cruelty is suffering *inflicted*.
- **Mechanism of change (T5.3):** only **C-D** shows one — divine intervention *removing* reproach (Jos 5:9).

**Per-characteristic.** C-A, C-B mostly silent (a few eliciting sequences only); C-E entirely silent (no developmental dimension — consistent with its role-only nature); C-C, C-D, C-F carry the eschatology/suffering content above.

*Gap note:* T5's heavy silence is a **data-shape limitation** (per-occurrence lexical), not evidence of absence. A verse-narrative pass (e.g. Gen 37 Joseph; 2Sa 13 Amnon; the Saul–David arc) would likely surface developmental sequences the lexical extract cannot.

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics

**Cluster finding (the key structural result).** The six characteristics are not merely parallel negatives — they are **compositionally related**, and the science framework (Sternberg's duplex theory, §1) maps onto the cluster's own internal structure:
- **Contempt (C-B, devaluation)** and **loathing (C-C, revulsion)** read as **constituents of hatred (C-A)** — the "devaluation" and "negation-of-intimacy/disgust" components of the duplex model. The internal co-occurrence and the faculty logic support treating C-B and C-C as **elements that can compose C-A**, not only as neighbours.
- **Enmity (C-E)** is the **relational outworking** of aversive affect — the `sa.ne` root itself generates "enemy" (`sone'`), so C-A (feeling) and C-E (relation) are **one phenomenon across two characteristics**.
- **Cruelty (C-F)** is the **dispositional end** of the same hostility continuum as C-E (relation vs character-trait).
- **Reproach (C-D)** is the **public voicing** of contempt — the strongest internal co-occurrence is **C-B↔C-D (5)** (verdict → taunt).

**Vocabulary/root sharing (T6.4).** `sa.ne` → "enemy" links **C-A↔C-E**; `ba.ash`/`ta.av` disgust-register links **C-B↔C-C**; `cher.pah` honour–shame links **C-D** to the honour cluster.

**Distinctions (T6.5) — nearest-neighbour map.**
- C-A ↔ C-B: felt rejection vs cold worth-verdict (kind: affect vs evaluation; valence: bivalent vs sinful).
- C-B ↔ C-D: inner verdict vs voiced/borne disgrace (mode).
- C-A ↔ C-C: affective vs visceral/ritual; soul vs flesh (constitutional level).
- C-E ↔ C-F: relation vs disposition (kind).
- C-E ↔ C-A: relation vs feeling (the enemy concept shared).

**External clusters.** **Love (M05)** recurs across C-A/C-D/C-F (the love↔hate axis, and love as a *cause* of hate); **wisdom (M15)** frames the moral evaluation of hatred and cruelty; **grief (M03), anger (M02), fear (M01)** cluster around the *reproached/hated person's* experience (esp. C-D).

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**Cluster finding.** M06 is **OT-weighted**: of 34 terms, NT vocabulary appears only in **C-C** (`bdelussomai`), **C-E** (`antidikos`), and **C-F** (`hubrizō`, `afilagathos`). C-A, C-B, and C-D — the cluster's core mass — are **OT-only**, so a cross-testament characterisation rests heavily on the OT, with NT continuity carried mainly by the abhorrence line (`ta.av`→`bdelussomai`).

**Lexical/semantic (T7.1).**
- *Grammatical spread across the cluster:* verbs (acts), nouns (verdicts/conditions), adjectives (qualities), participles (person-types) — the full range.
- *Person-type terms (T7.1.6):* strongest in **C-F** (`a.rits`/`akhzari` "the ruthless/cruel one"), **C-E** (`antidikos`/`yariv` "adversary/opponent"), and **C-A** (`sone'` "the hater/enemy"). C-B/C-C/C-D lack clean agent person-types.
- *Opposites (T7.1.5):* love, honour, delight/clean, glory, peace, mercy (see T1).
- *OT↔NT continuity (T7.1.8):* clean only for **C-C** (`ta.av`→`bdelussomai`); the affect (`miseō`), contempt (`kataphroneō`), and reproach (`oneidismos`) continuations lie **outside the focus set** — flagged for any cross-testament claim.
- *NT coinage (T7.1.9):* **C-F** `afilagathos` ("hating good", 2Ti 3:3) — cruelty conceptualised as privation of love-of-good.

**Anchor verses (T7.2.5; authorial-judgement candidates).** C-A **Psa 139:21–22** (righteous hatred aligned to God's) · C-B **Isa 53:3** (the despised servant) · C-C **Deu 7:26** (commanded detestation; Lev 11 ritual / Amo 6:8 divine) · C-D **Psa 69** (reproach borne for God) · C-E **Exo 23:22** (enmity within God's covenant defence) · C-F **Pro 12:10** (cruelty as the wicked's disposition).

**Literary form (T7.2.2).** The cluster lives chiefly in **psalm, wisdom, and prophecy**, with narrative carrying the personal cases. The **psalmic/lament** weighting is decisive for C-A and C-D (hatred and reproach as the cry of the afflicted before God); **wisdom** for the moral evaluation (C-A, C-B, C-F); **Levitical law + apocalyptic** uniquely for C-C.

**Human-science (T7.3).** The science review's four sections map onto the six characteristics and illuminate them as follows:
- **§1 (hate) → C-A:** Sternberg's duplex theory (devaluation + disgust + passion) coheres with C-A's affect+cognition fusion *and* with the T6 finding that C-B/C-C are its constituents.
- **§2 (contempt/disgust) → C-B + C-C:** Gottman (contempt as the most relationship-destructive emotion) → C-B; Haidt/Rozin (bodily→moral disgust) → C-C's flesh-seated ritual + moral registers.
- **§3 (hostility/cruelty) → C-E + C-F:** reactive/proactive aggression and moral disengagement (Bandura) → C-F's trait-vs-act structure and "unmoved by suffering."
- **§4 (rejection/reproach) → C-D:** Eisenberger (social pain = physical pain) coheres with `cher.pah` being **affect-tagged** — disgrace internalised as felt pain.

**Principal science divergence (T7.3.3) — cluster-level.** Science treats this whole field as **pathology to be reduced**; the biblical evidence contains **commanded/righteous hatred and abhorrence of evil** (C-A, C-C), **divine hatred/abhorrence** (C-A, C-C), and the categorical point that **cruelty alone has no divine instance** (C-F) — normative and theological categories science has no framework to evaluate.

---

## Consolidated open questions (carried for researcher decision)

Grounded by this tier review; these refine the earlier IC1–IC4:

1. **Compositional modelling (new, from T6).** The evidence supports treating **C-B (devaluation)** and **C-C (revulsion)** as *constituents* of **C-A (hatred)** (Sternberg), and **C-E/C-F** as the *relation/disposition* poles of hostility. Should the cluster map be **layered** (C-A as composite; C-B/C-C as its elements; C-E/C-F as hostility's relation/trait) rather than six flat parallels? (Supersedes/sharpens IC1.)
2. **C-E status (from T3/T0/T5).** C-E is silent across all of T3, all of T5, and all of T0 (no faculty, no development, no God-relation). On the evidence it is a **relational-interface layer**, not a standalone inner-being characteristic. Confirm demote-to-layer, or retain. (IC1/IC3.)
3. **Inner/outer (resolved direction, confirm).** The boundary runs *through* C-B, C-D, C-F — model an **expression sub-layer within** characteristics, not a flat split. (IC3.)
4. **Bivalence (from T0/valence).** Commanded/righteous hatred and abhorrence live only on `sa.ne`/`ta.av` (C-A, C-C). Treat as a **valence-axis** within those characteristics rather than a separate characteristic. (IC4.)
5. **Overlap-term placements (carried).** `mas.te.mah` (C-A↔C-E), `shut` (C-A↔C-B), `hubrizō` (C-F↔C-D), `sho.tet` (re-place/exclude), `sa.ni` (C-A↔borne-condition). (IC2.)
6. **NT thinness (from T7).** Cross-testament claims for C-A/C-B/C-D need terms outside the focus set (`miseō`/`kataphroneō`/`oneidismos`); flag whether to widen the NT seed before any continuity finding.

---

### Coverage statement
This review consolidates all six characteristics across all eight tiers (126 questions each; 756 answer-points). Tier richness across the cluster: **T0, T1, T6, T7 strong; T4 strong; T2 moderate; T3 narrow-but-decisive (3 of 11 faculties); T5 thin (data-shape limited).** All silences are evidenced absences in the lexical extract, recorded as such, not unexamined questions.

# M07 — Cluster-Wide Synthesis by Tier, with Cross-Characteristic and Boundary Findings
**File:** wa-m07-cluster-synthesis-bytier-v1_0-20260621.md · 2026-06-21
**Draws on:** the twelve characteristic findings v2_0 (A, B, C, C-neg, D, E, F, G, H, J, K, RESID) and wa-m07-phase2-assessment-v1_0-20260621.md.
**Cluster:** M07 — Shame, Disgrace and Humiliation. 359 focus occurrences, 302 verses, 31 lemmas.

## Method note
This synthesis reads **upward** from the twelve verse-grounded characteristic findings into one cluster picture, tier by tier (T0–T7). Three registers are kept distinct:
- **Observation** — what the verses, across the characteristics, show.
- **Cluster finding** — a pattern that holds across characteristics, traceable to the underlying evidence.
- **Interpretation / boundary judgement** — a structural or relevance call. The six carried boundary flags are presented in Part 3 as **findings-with-recommendations for researcher decision**, not as resolved changes.

---
# PART 1 — Synthesis by tier

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design
**Observation.** God stands at **both ends** of shame across the cluster: as the one who **exposes / imposes / abases** (A exposes false trust; D decrees disgrace in judgment, Eze 16:52; F abases pride, Isa 2:11-17; E is dishonoured by sin, Rom 2:23; G turns glory to shame, Hos 4:7) **and** as the one who **removes / vindicates / reverses** (B keeps the truster from shame, Isa 49:23; D removes it, Isa 54:4; G turns shame to honour, Isa 61:7; Zep 3:19). The **baseline of the image is shame-less integrity** — "naked and not ashamed" (Gen 2:25). The **apex** is the Servant/Christ bearing disgrace unto glory — "despising the shame… seated at the right hand of God" (Heb 12:2; Isa 50:6).

**Cluster finding.** In M07, shame is fundamentally a **relational-standing reality before God, with God as its decisive arbiter in both directions.** The image is portrayed as a **trusting, honour-bearing being**: its shame marks misdirected trust (A), a marred moral faculty (C-neg), a borne standing (D), or pride under judgment (F); its vindication is God's reversal (B, G). The capacity for shame is **created design** (its loss is ruin, C-neg); the *occasion* of shame is **fallen** (Gen 2:25 baseline) — except where disgrace is **assumed innocently** (the Servant), which redeems it.

## T1 — Definition
**Observation.** The cluster's shame vocabulary is not one thing. It spans a **felt collapse of falsified trust** (A), the **vindication/non-shaming of trust** (B), **penitential conscience-shame** (C), the **absence/inversion of the faculty** (C-neg), **borne disgrace as standing** (D), **inflicted dishonour/contempt** (E), the **abasement of pride** (F), the **honour↔shame axis** (G), the **norm of the disgraceful** (H), the **innocence antonym** (J), **silencing/defilement** (K), and a **non-shame sense** (RESID).

**Cluster finding.** Shame in M07 is a **family of related but distinct phenomena**: a felt **affect** (A, C), a relational **standing** (D, G), an inflicted **act** (E), a **status-movement** (F), a **norm** (H), a **faculty** (C/C-neg), and an **outcome of trust** (A/B). The **compound (affect + cognition)** signature is tagged on the bosh-heavy bands (A, B, C-neg, D). Internal **opposites** are explicit: honour/glory (G), vindication (B), innocence (J), and shamelessness-as-inversion (C-neg).

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries
**Observation.** M07 rarely names a **constitutional seat** (spirit/soul/heart). Where inner seat-language appears it is the **heart/conscience** (Psa 119:80 blameless heart; Gen 20:5 integrity of heart; C's conscience). Far more often the location is the **face and body**: covered/lowered face (D — Psa 69:7; Jer 51:51), the unblushing forehead (C-neg — Jer 3:3; 6:15), the radiant face (B — Psa 34:5), the face set like flint while bearing disgrace (B/D — Isa 50:7), haughty eyes (F), washed hands (J), struck back (Isa 50:6).

**Cluster finding.** Shame in M07 is **overwhelmingly embodied and registered on the face/body** — the face is its primary theatre (covered, lowered, blushing, radiant, flint-set). The inner seat, where present, is the **heart/conscience** (C, J, B). **Boundary observation / additional-discovery flag:** the programme's governing **spirit–soul–body partition is *not* directly illuminated by M07** — shame surfaces on the body and engages heart/conscience, but these verses do not address the tripartite boundary. M07 contributes to the **faculty map**, not to the constitutional-boundary question; this gap should be noted at programme level.

## T3 — The Inner Faculties
**Observation.** Faculties engaged across the cluster: **affect** (all felt bands), **cognition** (the trust/expectation bands A, B; awareness of standing, D), **moral evaluation** (pervasive — C, C-neg, D, E, F, G, H, J), **conscience** (C the seat; C-neg its searing; J integrity; B "good conscience," 1Pe 3:16), **volition** (B taking refuge; C-neg refusing shame; D/Servant bearing; E inflicting; J keeping clean), **agency** (E the agent pole), and **relational capacity** (pervasive). **Not** engaged cluster-wide: **memory (T3.3), creativity (T3.5), conscientiousness (T3.10).**

**Cluster finding.** The inner-being faculties most engaged by shame are **moral evaluation, conscience, relational capacity, and affect** — shame is a **moral-relational-affective complex**, not a bare emotion. The sharpest faculty finding is the **conscience axis**: shame is the conscience's **affective signal at moral failure** (C), and its **searing/inversion is moral ruin** (C-neg, Jer 6:15 "did not know how to blush"). C and C-neg are the **same faculty operative and failed** — a paired finding.

## T4 — Relational Interfaces
**Observation.** The cluster maps a dense relational web. **God→human:** exposes (A), vindicates (B), imposes & removes disgrace (D), abases pride (F), reverses the axis (G), is dishonoured by sin (E). **Human→God:** trust/refuge (B — the heart of the Godward movement), confession under disgrace (D, Ezr 9:6-7), reverence (G, Heb 12:9), innocence brought to the altar (J, Psa 26:6); and negatively, the refusal of shame Godward (C-neg, Jer 3:3). **Person→person:** contempt/dishonour inflicted (E), disgrace borne from enemies (D), respect/regard (G). **Person←person:** receiving dishonour (E, D), with a distinct **honourable response** — rejoice (Act 5:41), despise the shame (Heb 12:2), do not repay reviling (1Pe 3:9). **Covenantal/nations:** shame crosses to the **nations** extensively (A, B, D, F, G). **Spiritual beings:** **absent** (T4.6 silent cluster-wide; only idols *qua* empty, A).

**Cluster finding.** M07 is the cluster **most constituted by relational interface** — shame *is* standing before God and others. The **Godward interface concentrates in B** (trust→vindication); the **human giving/receiving in E/D**. A distinct **NT development** is the **honourable bearing of inflicted shame** (endure, rejoice, despise it, do not retaliate — Act 5:41; Heb 12:2; 1Pe 3:9). **Boundary finding:** the **absence of any spiritual-being interface** is itself a cluster-wide result — in M07's verses shame is a **God-and-neighbour** reality, not an angelic/demonic one.

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension
**Observation.** Shame's arcs in the cluster: it is **removed/reversed** (B vindication; D, Isa 54:4; G, shame→honour) — the dominant redemptive movement; it is **seared/lost** (C-neg) — the pathological movement; it is **borne through suffering unto vindication** (B, D, the Servant/Christ); and it is **eschatologically weighted** throughout (B at his coming, 1Jo 2:28; D final removal; G final exchange; F the day of the Lord; C-neg "their end is destruction," Phil 3:19).

**Cluster finding.** M07 has a strong **eschatological spine**: shame and honour are **finally and decisively sorted by God** — the believing not put to shame, the proud abased, the shamed exalted, the impenitent fixed in disgrace. A **sanctification thread** runs alongside: bearing reproach **for God** (Psa 69:7; 1Pe 4:16) and **despising the shame** (Heb 12:2). This tier intersects the programme's **transformation/renewal** register (shame removed = renewal).

## T6 — Structural Relationships  *(this tier is the cross-characteristic core — developed fully in Part 2)*
**Observation.** The lemmas are **shared across bands** (bosh in A/B/C-neg/D/E; ka.lam in A/B/C/C-neg/E/RESID; cha.pher, qa.lon, ke.lim.mah, atimia across several), with each band reading the **same term under a different characteristic** by its use in the verse.

**Cluster finding.** M07 is **not a flat list of twelve parallel characteristics** but a **structured field** organised by three faculty/standing axes (trust, conscience, honour-standing), a normative frame (H/J), and two edges (K/RESID). The shared-lemma pattern **confirms the characteristic-perspective model** (GR-PROG-006): the unit is the term-in-its-use, not the term. *(Architecture in Part 2.)*

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation
**Observation.** The cluster rests on a **Hebrew core** — **bosh (BWŠ) as the master root** (108 occ), with ka.lam (KLM), cha.pher, qa.lon, ke.lim.mah, bo.shet, sha.phel — and a **Greek set** — aischunō/kataischunō, atimazō/atimia, exoutheneō, entrepō, aischros/aschēmosunē, fimoō. **Literary forms:** prophecy dominates (Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel), with heavy psalm (lament/trust, esp. B), wisdom (Proverbs/Job, esp. E's household-shame and F), narrative, epistle (the NT bands), gospel, and apocalyptic.

**Cluster finding (OT→NT).** Continuity is **strongest in B** — the Zion-stone "**not put to shame**" (Isa 28:16) taken up verbatim in Rom 9:33; 10:11; 1Pe 2:6 — and in **D** — the Servant's borne disgrace (Isa 50:6) consummated in "despising the shame" (Heb 12:2). The **NT develops the agent vocabulary** (exoutheneō, atimazō — E) and the **honourable-bearing motif** (Act 5:41; Heb 12:2; 1Pe 3:9).

**Cluster finding (science lens, T7.3).** The science extract illuminates the **descriptive** shape — shame-psychology (felt shame), honour-shame anthropology (standing), stigma (borne disgrace), disgust-purity (propriety/defilement), contempt (agent pole). The biblical material **adds a moral-theological axis the clinical frame lacks**: **appropriate/commanded shame** (vs the clinical "shame is maladaptive"), **shamelessness as ruin** (vs "less shame is healthier"), and **vicarious/redemptive shame** (Heb 12:2) with no clinical analogue. [source: wa-m07-shame-scienceextract; divergences per its T7.3.3]

---
# PART 2 — Cross-characteristic architecture (the M07 field)

**Cluster finding — M07 is organised by three axes, a normative frame, and two edges:**

**1. The trust axis — A ↔ B.** The same faculty (trust/hope) with opposite outcomes by **object**: a **false object → shame** (A), the **true object (God) → vindication** (B). This is the cluster's **theological spine** and its **clearest OT→NT continuity** (B's "not put to shame"). *Finding:* A and B are two halves of one faculty, divided by the object of trust, not by degree.

**2. The conscience axis — C ↔ C-neg.** The same faculty (conscience) **operative** (penitential shame at one's own sin, C) and **failed** (seared / refused / inverted, C-neg). *Finding:* shame is the conscience's affective signal at moral failure; its absence is moral ruin (Jer 6:15). C-neg is the **privation-and-inversion** of C.

**3. The honour-standing axis — G, with D and E as its poles, and F as movement along it.**
- **G is the axis itself** (honour/glory ↔ shame/dishonour), reversed by God in both directions.
- **D is the borne pole** (disgrace carried) and **E is the inflicting pole** (dishonour/contempt done).
- **F is the judgment-movement** down the axis (the abasement of pride).
*Findings:* **(i) E produces D** — the agent's dishonouring (E) creates the borne disgrace (D) in the other; one event, two poles. **(ii) B reverses D** — vindication is the removal of borne disgrace; Isa 54:4 sits on their seam. **(iii) G is the scale on which D and E move** — supporting the reading of G as an axis rather than a seventh parallel band. **(iv) F's abasement of pride feeds the axis** — the lowering of the proud is registered as shame on the honour-standing scale, with F bordering M09 (humility).

**4. The normative frame — H and J.** **H** supplies the **standard** (what counts as disgraceful); **J** supplies the **antonym** (innocence — the unashamed clean state). Together they **bound the field conceptually**: H says what *ought* to occasion shame; J shows what shame's *absence* looks like.

**5. The edges — K and RESID.** **K** is mostly **behavioural/physical** (silencing, casting-off), inner-being-relevant only at ni.dah (defilement, Lam 1:8). **RESID** is a **non-shame sense** of ka.lam (harm/injure). Both are gathered for completeness and flagged for set-aside/exclusion.

**Cross-char synthesis finding.** The twelve "characteristics" are best understood as **positions within a structured field**, not as twelve equal, independent inner states. The felt/borne/agent core (A, B, C, C-neg, D, E) carries the inner-being weight; G is the axis that organises the standing-bands; F is a status-judgment at the M07/M09 seam; H and J are the conceptual frame; K and RESID are edges. This structure should govern the **chapter's organisation** and the eventual **Session D** cross-registry mapping.

---
# PART 3 — Boundary findings and carried flags (recommendations for researcher decision)

Per GR-PROC-004 these are **proposals**, not applied changes. Each states the evidence, a recommendation, and the decision required.

**Flag 1 — D sub-bands: D1 (imposed-verdict) vs D8 (innocent/vicarious).**
Evidence: D's 136 occ span **deserved** disgrace (Ezr 9:7; Pro 13:18; Eze 16), **enemy-imposed** disgrace (Psa 69:19), and **innocent/vicarious** disgrace (Isa 50:6; Heb 12:2; Psa 69:7 "for your sake"). The moral difference is real, not degree.
*Recommendation:* **retain D as one characteristic** but carry a **documented two-part sub-distinction**; surface the **vicarious sub-band** (Servant/Christ) prominently in the chapter — it is theologically central. *Decision required:* approve the sub-band documentation, or split D.

**Flag 2 — F and the M09 (humility) boundary.**
Evidence: sha.phel is a **status-movement** (high→low), not an affect; "lowly in spirit will obtain honour" (Pro 29:23) is humility language.
*Recommendation:* **retain F in M07** as the "abasement / judgment-of-pride" pole of the honour-shame field, **with a cross-reference to M09**; flag sha.phel as a possible **shared term** with M09 (shared-verse model). *Decision required:* keep in M07, route to M09, or treat as cross-linked.

**Flag 3 — G: axis vs characteristic.**
Evidence: G's verses are the **honour↔shame exchange** and the **reverence pole** (entrepō); its lemmas also appear in D and E.
*Recommendation:* present **G as the organising axis** of the standing-bands (D, E, F) in the chapter, **not as a seventh parallel characteristic**; treat the **entrepō reverence/regard** pole as the positive complement to E's contempt. *Decision required:* approve axis-treatment, or retain G as a discrete band.

**Flag 4 — J: relevance of the innocence antonym.**
Evidence: niq.qa.von / qe.ha.von mean **innocence/cleanness** — the **antonym** of shame, not shame.
*Recommendation:* **retain J as the contrast pole** for definitional clarity (brief), explicitly marked **antonym**; consider whether these terms belong **primarily to a purity/righteousness registry**. *Decision required:* keep as antonym-pole, or relocate.

**Flag 5 — K: set-aside vs retain.**
Evidence: fimoō/afōnos/apoballō are **silencing/casting acts**, not inner states; ni.dah (Lam 1:8) is genuine defilement-disgrace.
*Recommendation:* **retain ni.dah** as M07 defilement-disgrace; **set aside** fimoō/afōnos/apoballō as non-inner-being. *Decision required:* approve the partial set-aside.

**Flag 6 — RESID: exclude.**
Evidence: ka.lam at 1Sa 25:7,15 is the **"harm/injure" sense**, no inner-being shame content.
*Recommendation:* **formally exclude** from M07 shame analysis (sense-split). *Decision required:* approve exclusion.

---
# PART 4 — Gaps, additional discovery, and cross-registry candidates

**Where additional data/discovery may be needed:**
- **Constitutional boundary (programme governing question).** M07 does **not** illuminate the spirit–soul–body partition (Part 1, T2). If the programme needs M07's contribution to that question, the answer is that shame is **embodied (face/body) and seated in heart/conscience** — it does not adjudicate the tripartite boundary. Flag for the programme-level constitutional synthesis.
- **Faculty map completeness.** Memory, creativity, and conscientiousness are **unengaged** by M07's shame vocabulary (Part 1, T3). If the programme expects every faculty to be touched per cluster, this is a true absence, not a coverage gap.
- **Spiritual-being interface.** Entirely **absent** in M07 (Part 1, T4). If cross-registry work expects an adversarial-shame interface (e.g., the accuser motif), it is **not present in these lemmas' verses** and would have to come from another registry.

**Cross-registry connection candidates (for Session D, when the relevant clusters complete):**
- **M01 (Fear/Dread):** A's collapse-cluster (shame + dismay + dread + terror) binds shame to fear — a strong semantic-overlap / co-occurrence link.
- **M08 (Pride/Arrogance):** F (abasement of pride) and G (glory→shame for the proud) connect directly — theological/semantic-opposition link.
- **M09 (Humility/Meekness):** F's "lowly in spirit obtains honour" (Pro 29:23) — shared-root/shared-term link.
- **Honour/glory registry (if/when scoped):** G's honour↔shame axis is the natural seam.
- **A guilt/conscience registry:** C and C-neg connect to guilt and conscience (note the prior G4893 suneidēsis ownership lies with Registry 112/mind).

---
# Close
M07 reads as a **structured field of shame** before God and neighbour, organised by a **trust axis** (A/B), a **conscience axis** (C/C-neg), and an **honour-standing axis** (G, with D borne / E inflicted / F abasing), framed by a **norm** (H) and an **antonym** (J), with two **edges** (K, RESID). Its theological centre of gravity is the movement from shame to honour that God works — culminating in the One who **despised the shame** and was seated in glory (Heb 12:2). The outstanding work is **interpretive**: the six boundary decisions in Part 3, then the M07 chapter built on this field-structure, and in due course the cross-registry links in Part 4.

# WA — M08 (Pride, Arrogance and Boasting): Cluster-Wide Synthesis by Tier

**File:** wa-m08-cluster-synthesis-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Prior output reference:** the seven tier-answer files wa-m08-{a,b,c1,c2,d,e,f}-tier-answers-v1_0-20260621.md (each 126 questions answered from its own verse evidence); the seven characteristic analyses wa-m08-{a…f}-*-v1_0-20260621.md; WA-tier-catalogue-current-state-v2-20260619.md; wa-m08-pride-scienceextract-v1_0-20260513.md (T7.3 only).
**Purpose:** the cluster-level synthesis. It folds the seven characteristics into one by-tier account (T0–T7), makes the cross-characteristic architecture explicit (axes, poles, nearest-neighbours, which characteristics work together), and is written to stand on its own feet so that reader-facing essays can be drafted from it without returning to source. Boundary and relationship judgements are carried as **flagged recommendations** for researcher decision, not resolved here.
**Discipline:** every substantive statement is grounded in a cited verse or is marked as framing (FA-21); the synthesis asserts nothing the captured findings do not carry (FA-22); no superlative stands without evidence (FA-23). Science is confined to the T7.3 section and attributed to the extract. Quotes ≤15 words.

---

## 0. The characteristics in view

Seven characteristics, kept distinct by researcher decision (bundling reduces accuracy):

- **A — Self-exaltation:** the active lifting of the self (rum, ga.vah, ga.ah; hupsēlos).
- **B — Settled pride:** the entrenched, often corporate, state of haughtiness (ga.on, ga.a.vah, ge.eh; huperēfanos).
- **C1 — Presumption / defiance toward God and authority:** the self-willed refusal of ordained limit (zid, za.don; authadēs, tolmētēs).
- **C2 — Insolence / contempt toward other people:** pride turned outward as derision and oppression (zed, za.don, ra.hav, shal.le.tet).
- **D — Boasting / glorying:** the declared exultation, two-poled by its object (kauchaomai, kauchēsis/kauchēma, ha.lal; alazōn, alazoneia).
- **E — Conceit / puffed-up:** the inflation of the mind (fusioō, tufoō, fusiōsis; huperfroneō, hupsēlofroneō).
- **F — Self-love / self-sufficiency:** the terminus — the self as its own god and beloved (filautos; a.din).

---

## 1. The field model (the cluster's internal architecture)

*This section is framing — it states the structure the by-tier synthesis below substantiates from the verses.*

The cluster is not a list of synonyms but a single reality worked out in modes that relate to one another along a small number of axes:

**The core disposition.** **B (settled pride)** is the resting condition of the family — the entrenched height of heart that the others arise from or express. It carries the cluster's defining theological frame: "God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble" (James 4:6).

**The vertical axis — act and state (A ↔ B).** **A** is the *motion* of self-lifting; **B** is the *state* of height attained. They share the height-roots g-'-h and r-w-m, and the seam where one becomes the other is visible in a single verse: "it towered high… its heart was proud of its height" (Ezekiel 31:10). A → B is developmental (lifting settles into condition).

**The directional axis — against whom (C1 ↔ C2).** From the settled disposition the pride discharges outward in two directions, sharing the root z-d: **C1** against God and his appointed authority ("she has proudly defied the Lord", Jeremiah 50:29), **C2** against other people ("the insolent utterly deride me", Psalm 119:51). One disposition, two objects.

**The voiced form, two-poled (D).** **D** is pride made audible — but uniquely it bifurcates by object. Its sinful pole voices A/B ("you boast in your arrogance", James 4:16); its righteous pole voices faith and is *commanded* ("Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord", 1 Corinthians 1:31). D shares ha.lal with praise.

**The cognitive corner (E).** **E** is pride localised in the mind — inflation rather than elevation (the bellows fusioō, the befogging smoke tufoō). It meets A at the high-minded compounds (hupsēlofroneō) but differs in kind: hollow swelling, not solid height. Its named opposite is **love**, not humility (1 Corinthians 8:1).

**The terminus (F).** **F** is where the whole movement arrives: the self made ultimate. A reaches *toward* God's place ("I will make myself like the Most High", Isaiah 14:14); F *occupies* it in speech ("I am, and there is no one besides me", Isaiah 47:8). F is small in lexical base and decisive in structure.

**The single counter-current.** Only **D's righteous pole** runs the other way — glory referred away from the self to God. It is the cluster's one point of created-design positivity, eschatological hope, and constructive relation.

**The unifying logic.** The whole field is organised around one theological reality: the creature's relation to the exaltedness, majesty, and glory that belong to God alone. Pride is the disordered seizure of it; right boasting is its rightly-ordered return. The seat is the **heart** throughout; the occasion is **prosperity/fullness/sufficiency**; the end is being **brought low** — except where the boast is in the Lord, whose end is glory.

---

## 2. Synthesis by tier

### T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

Across all seven, the characteristic is **never borne by God** — a uniform finding. God enters the cluster's verses as the **object** the self exalts against (A: "above the stars of God", Isaiah 14:13; C1: "proudly defied the Lord", Jeremiah 50:29; F: the self taking God's own "I am", Isaiah 47:8) or as the **opponent and judge** who abases it (A/B: "God opposes the proud", James 4:6; "the Lord tears down the house of the proud", Proverbs 15:25). The one place the lemma-family names God is its legitimate counterpart — "the majesty of the Lord" (ge.ut, Isaiah 26:10): the divine reality the creature's pride counterfeits. The cluster's governing theological claim, then, is that **exaltation, majesty, and glory are God's prerogative**; pride is the creature's illegitimate seizure of them, "the Lord alone will be exalted" (Isaiah 2:11, 17).

On created design versus the fall, six of the seven are **wholly fallen** — they have no place in created design and no orientation toward future fullness; their only future is to be brought low. **D is the sole exception**, and the exception is structurally important: D answers "both" (T0.2.2) — its God-directed pole belongs to created design (boasting in the Lord is commanded) and its self-directed pole to the fall — and it alone carries an eschatological orientation, "we boast in hope of the glory of God" (Romans 5:2). D's right pole alone instantiates the divine image rightly (the creature glorying in its source); the rest, and F most extremely, are the image's **counter-form** — the creature in God's place.

Typology runs through three points: A's "I will ascend" read traditionally of the adversary (Isaiah 14:13, inferential); D's redirection to the cross ("boast… in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ", Galatians 6:14, christological); and F's self-deifying power (Isaiah 47, the creature usurping divine self-predication).

*Essay seam:* the cluster's deepest theme is set here — pride as the creature's disordered grasp at what is God's, with right boasting as its redeemed inverse. Isaiah 14:14 ("like the Most High") and Isaiah 47:8 ("I am, none besides me") frame the disorder; 1 Corinthians 1:31 ("boast in the Lord") states the cure.

### T1 — Definition

The seven name one reality — the self made high or made much of — in distinct **modes**: act (A), settled condition (B), self-willed defiance (C1), outward contempt (C2), declared exultation (D), mental inflation (E), and terminal self-orientation (F). The **kinds** differ accordingly: A is an act, B and F are conditions/dispositions, C1 and C2 are acts issuing from disposition, D is an affect-laden speech-act, E is a condition of the mind.

The **structural opposite** is, for most, humility/lowliness of heart ("my heart is not lifted up", Psalm 131:1; "gives grace to the humble", James 4:6) — but two exceptions are diagnostic: **E's** opposite is **love** ("Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up", 1 Corinthians 8:1), and **D's** right pole excludes not pride-of-heart but **self-reliance** ("so that no one may boast", Ephesians 2:9; "no confidence in the flesh", Philippians 3:3). The cluster's opposite is therefore primarily humility, with love and trust naming the boundary at its cognitive and declarative edges.

Three further uniformities. First, the cluster is a **speaking** family: every characteristic has a communicative mode — A's "I will ascend" (Isaiah 14:13), B's arrogant speech (Isaiah 9:9), C1's presumptuous word (Deuteronomy 18:20), C2's derision (Psalm 119:51), D's boast, F's "I am" (Isaiah 47:10). Second, the **conditions of taking hold** are consistently fullness and sufficiency — prosperity and strength (A: 2 Chronicles 26:16; B: Ezekiel 16:49; F: Isaiah 47:10), and, for E, knowledge ("knowledge puffs up", 1 Corinthians 8:1). Third, **none operates rightly** except D's God-directed pole — the only licit form in the family.

### T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

The **heart is the dominant seat** across the cluster (A, B, C1, C2, D, F are heart-located: "your heart be lifted up", Deuteronomy 8:14; "arrogant in heart", Proverbs 16:5; "you said in your heart, 'I am'", Isaiah 47:10). **B** engages the whole inner being — heart, soul, and spirit together (Proverbs 16:5; Amos 6:8; Ecclesiastes 7:8) — confirming pride as a **whole-self disposition** rather than a discrete faculty; this is why the faculty field reads as "absent" so often: the seat is the person, not an organ of the soul. **E is the exception** that proves the rule — it alone is seated in the **mind/cognition** ("puffed up… by his sensuous mind", Colossians 2:18) — and **D** alone foregrounds **affect** ("my soul makes its boast in the Lord", Psalm 34:2).

The **body link is expressive throughout** and never the seat: the haughty eyes and neck (A, B: Proverbs 30:13; Psalm 75:5), the stiffened neck (C1: Nehemiah 9:16), the boasting mouth (D). The direction is uniform — soul/spirit expressing outward through the body (the inner height shown in the lifted eye), "the haughty eyes you bring down" (Psalm 18:27).

**Origin** is uniformly **within the person**, self-generated and occasioned by prosperity — with one structurally crucial exception: **D's right pole originates in God-given knowledge received** ("that he… knows me", Jeremiah 9:24). No characteristic states an external-spirit origin; the only adversarial thread is inferential (Job 41:34, Leviathan "king over all the sons of pride"). This near-total silence on a spiritual-being origin is noted for Session D (§4).

### T3 — The Inner Faculties

The cluster engages the faculties **selectively**, and the pattern is itself a finding:

- **Volition** is engaged across most of the family and is the **core** of C1 (self-will, authadēs — "Bold and willful", 2 Peter 2:10); pride is substantially a matter of the will (A's fivefold "I will", Isaiah 14:13; D's chosen object, Galatians 6:14).
- **Agency** is strong wherever pride acts on others — A casting down (Daniel 11:12), B and C2 oppressing (Psalm 10:2; 119:85), C1 defying (Deuteronomy 1:43). The proud act from their height.
- **Relational capacity** is **damaged by all** — the self lifted above brothers, the lowly held in contempt (Deuteronomy 17:20; Psalm 123:4) — and is where **C2** concentrates. **D alone** carries a **constructive** relational mode: pride *in another* that honours them ("great is my pride in you", 2 Corinthians 7:4).
- **Moral evaluation** is doubly engaged: pride **is** judged (an abomination, sin — Proverbs 16:5; 21:4) and pride **inverts** evaluation (exalting folly and vileness — Psalm 12:8; calling wickedness safety — Isaiah 47:10; arrogance displacing grief over sin — 1 Corinthians 5:2).
- **Cognition** concentrates in **E** (the cognitive characteristic) and in **D's** right pole (knowledge of God); it is the NT register of **A** (high-mindedness).
- **Memory** is engaged by its **failure** — self-exaltation and settled pride both produce the forgetting of God ("their heart was lifted up; therefore they forgot me", Hosea 13:6; "they do not return to the Lord", Hosea 7:10). A shared, non-obvious finding (A, B).
- **Affect** is isolated in **D** — the cluster's one affect-bearing characteristic ("I will boast all the more gladly", 2 Corinthians 12:9); elsewhere pride is disposition, not feeling.
- **Conscience** is engaged chiefly by **suppression** (C1: "they do not tremble as they blaspheme", 2 Peter 2:10); otherwise largely silent.
- **Perception** appears as the **haughty eye** (A, B: Proverbs 30:13) and little else.
- **Creativity** is **uniformly silent** across all seven — a clean cross-cluster data-silence, not a gap in the reading.

*Synthesis:* the cluster's faculty-signature is **volition + agency + relational damage + moral inversion**, with affect isolated in D, cognition in E, a shared memory-failure (forgetting God) in A and B, and creativity uniformly absent.

### T4 — Relational Interfaces

This tier carries the cluster's **defining negative shape**. God does **not extend** pride to the person (T4.1), and pride is **not given or received** between persons as a gift (T4.3, T4.4): these are structural silences across A, B, C1, E, and F. Pride is not a relational good that passes between persons — it is self-generated and self-referring.

**D inverts this entirely.** Boasting is God-ward (T4.2: "in God we have boasted continually", Psalm 44:8), and it can pass constructively from person to person ("the proof… of our boasting about you", 2 Corinthians 8:24). D is the cluster's relational outlier precisely because it alone is object-directed rather than self-enclosed.

The **human-to-God** interface (T4.2) is, across the family, the cluster's worst and its best at once. Its worst is **usurpation and defiance** (A, C1, F: "I will make myself like the Most High", Isaiah 14:14; "proudly defied the Lord", Jeremiah 50:29; "I am, none besides me", Isaiah 47:8) and **disregard** (B, C2: "they do not return to the Lord", Hosea 7:10). Its best is **D's worshipful boasting in the Lord** — the same interface redeemed.

On **boundaries** (T4.5), pride operates across every relational distance — above brothers within the covenant (Deuteronomy 17:20), over enemies and the lowly (Psalm 13:2; 123:4), within the believing community (E: "one against another", 1 Corinthians 4:6) — and B adds a **corporate** mode (peoples bearing pride together: "the pride of Moab", Isaiah 16:6).

The **spiritual-being interface** (T4.6) is **near-uniformly silent**: the only threads are inferential — Isaiah 14 (A, the adversary's self-exaltation), Job 41:34 (B, Leviathan over the proud), 2 Peter 2:10 (C1, blaspheming the glorious ones), 1 Timothy 3:6 (E, "the condemnation of the devil"). No confirmed angelic mediation appears. This is carried to Session D (§4).

### T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

The cluster's developmental arc is **uniform and severe**: prosperity/fullness → pride (lifting, settling, defying, vaunting) → displacement of God and contempt of others → **being brought low**. The downfall comes by **divine judgment**, imposed and often sudden ("I will bring you down", Obadiah 4; "ruin shall come upon you suddenly", Isaiah 47:11); the **only off-ramp is self-humbling**, chosen before the fall (Hezekiah, "humbled himself for the pride of his heart", 2 Chronicles 32:26; Nebuchadnezzar, "those who walk in pride he is able to humble", Daniel 4:37).

Pride's relation to **suffering** (T5.4) is, for most of the family, that of a **producer** (it brings its own downfall) arising in **ease, not affliction** — and affliction or its threat **breaks** it (2 Chronicles 32:25–26). Two inversions stand out. **D's righteous pole** operates *in* suffering and is *perfected* by it — "I will boast of my weaknesses… that the power of Christ may rest upon me" (2 Corinthians 12:9); "we boast in our sufferings" (Romans 5:3): the cluster's one positive relation to affliction, where pride's logic is turned inside out. **C2** inverts differently: its developmental fruit appears not in the proud agent but in the **sufferer** who endures contempt and keeps faith ("The insolent utterly deride me, but I do not turn away from your law", Psalm 119:51).

The **eschatological** trajectory (T5.6) is uniformly **abolition** — the pride of the nations laid low at the day of the Lord (Isaiah 13:11; Zechariah 10:11) — except, again, **D's right pole**, oriented to glory (Romans 5:2).

### T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics

This tier states the architecture of §1 from the verse evidence.

- **A ↔ B** — act and state, sharing g-'-h / r-w-m; A precedes and settles into B; both precede the fall ("Pride goes before destruction… a haughty spirit before a fall", Proverbs 16:18). The seam is Ezekiel 31:10.
- **C1 ↔ C2** — one disposition, two directions, sharing the z-d root; both produced by B (the settled pride that discharges outward).
- **D** — the voiced form; its sinful pole follows A/B (pride made audible, James 4:16), its righteous pole follows faith. D shares **ha.lal** with **praise** (a cross-cluster link to the praise/joy field) and **alazoneia** with the "pride of life" (1 John 2:16).
- **E ↔ A** — the high-minded compounds (hupsēlofroneō) join them at the mind; they differ in kind (E's hollow inflation vs A's solid elevation). E follows knowledge ungoverned by love (1 Corinthians 8:1) and produces division.
- **F** — the terminus on which the family converges; F's nearest neighbour is A (aspiration toward God's place vs arrival at it), and F co-heads the vice-list with D (alazōn) and B (huperēfanos) in 2 Timothy 3:2.

**Vocabulary/roots (T6.4) across the cluster:** g-'-h (A, B), r-w-m (A, B), z-d (C1, C2), hupsēlo-/fron- (A, E), kauchaomai (D), ha.lal (D ↔ praise), filautos (F). The root-sharing maps the family: height binds A–B, presumption binds C1–C2, and the mind binds A–E; D and F stand on their own terms (boasting; self-love), D reaching outward to praise.

### T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**Lexical (T7.1).** The cluster's vocabulary is built on five images: **height** (g-'-h, r-w-m, hupsēl-), **boiling-over/presumption** (z-d), **making-much-of** (kauchaomai, ha.lal), **inflation** (fusioō/tufoō — bellows and smoke), and **self-love** (filautos). It is unusually rich in **person-types** — the proud (ge.eh, huperēfanos), the haughty, the insolent (zed), the braggart (alazōn), the self-lover (filautos): pride is heavily lexicalised as a settled **character**, not only an act. The opposites are the humility/lowliness vocabulary, with **love** (E) and **trust** (D) at the edges; there is **no supplication/seeking term** in the whole family — pride, uniquely among inner-being characteristics, is never sought from another. Across the Testaments the height-image continues (rum → hupsoō); the principle "God opposes the proud, gives grace to the humble" (Proverbs 3:34) crystallises in the NT (James 4:6; 1 Peter 5:5); **D's** boasting theology is **developed** by Paul into boasting-in-weakness; **E** is a NT naming (bellows/smoke) with no OT counterpart; **F's** filautos is a NT lexicalisation of the terminus.

**Literary (T7.2).** The evidence spans every major genre, each requiring its own reading: the prophetic **taunt-oracle** against the nations' pride (Isaiah 14; 47), the **proverb** (Proverbs 16:18), the **lament from the sufferer's vantage** (Psalm 119, where C2 is seen from beneath), royal **narrative** (Daniel; Chronicles), and the **pastoral correction** of the epistles (D and E in the Corinthian correspondence). The **anchors**, taken together, form the cluster's master-frame: A = Isaiah 14:13–14; B = James 4:6 / Proverbs 16:18; C1 = Deuteronomy 17:12 / Jeremiah 50:29; C2 = Psalm 119:51; D = Jeremiah 9:23–24 / 1 Corinthians 1:31; E = 1 Corinthians 8:1; F = Isaiah 47:8, 10. The pair **Isaiah 14:14 and Isaiah 47:8** frames the disorder from aspiration to arrival; **1 Corinthians 1:31** states the redeemed alternative.

**Human science (T7.3) — attributed to the M08 science extract.** The science lenses map onto the family: the **status/dominance** literature (extract §3, including Keltner's power paradox) onto A and C2; **narcissism** research (extract §2) onto B, C1, and F; the **cognitive-superiority** component onto E; **impression-management/self-promotion** (extract §4) onto D's sinful pole; and Tracy & Robins' **two-facet** model (extract §1) onto D's authentic/hubristic split. The consistent **register-divergence** (extract T7.3.3): science problematises only *pathological* pride and treats achievement-based pride as healthy, whereas the biblical material judges pride **categorically before God** — even legitimate pride becomes disordered when it forgets the giver. Three things the science cannot reach are the cluster's theological distinctives: **God's ontological majesty** (the divine edge of the vocabulary), **D's righteous God-directed boast** (boasting in weakness so another's power may rest), and the **theological gravity** the Law assigns presumption (C1). One science-surfaced **gap** (extract T7.3.4) is carried forward, not asserted: the vulnerable-narcissism finding (grandiosity defending against shame) suggests testing whether the cluster's arrogance masks shame — an **M07 ↔ M08** question that the verse evidence does **not** itself raise.

---

## 3. Cross-cutting findings (the cluster's distinctive shape)

1. **One reality, seven modes, one seat.** The family is a single disposition — the creature making itself high or much-of — seated in the **heart** and worked out as act (A), state (B), defiance (C1), contempt (C2), boast (D), inflation (E), and terminus (F). Grounded throughout T1–T2.
2. **The theological axis is the organising principle.** Every characteristic is defined by its relation to the exaltedness that belongs to God (T0): pride seizes it, F occupies it, D returns it. The cluster cannot be read as merely social or psychological without losing its centre (T0; T7.3.3).
3. **A single legitimate pole, located entirely in D.** The cluster's one created-design, eschatologically-hopeful, constructively-relational, suffering-perfected form is the boast in the Lord (T0.2.2, T4.2, T4.3, T5.4, T5.6 — all D). This is the cluster's most distinctive structural feature.
4. **The relational interface is the diagnostic.** Pride's structural silence — not extended by God, not given or received between persons (T4.1/T4.3/T4.4) — holds across A, B, C1, E, F and is **inverted by D alone**. The shape of the silence *is* the finding.
5. **Faculty-signature: will, agency, relational damage, moral inversion** — with affect isolated in D, cognition in E, memory engaged by failure (forgetting God) in A and B, and **creativity uniformly silent** (T3).
6. **One arc, one off-ramp.** Prosperity → pride → downfall, with **self-humbling** the only escape and **suffering** the corrective — except D's right pole, where weakness is embraced and perfected (T5).
7. **The vocabulary is character-deep and seeking-less.** Pride is richly lexicalised as a person-type and has **no term for being sought from another** (T7.1) — a lexical confirmation of its self-referring nature.

---

## 4. Flags and open structural questions (for researcher decision — not resolved here)

*Carried per §6 as recommendations; the boundary and data questions below bear on claims made above and should be resolved before the cluster is closed.*

**Bearing on synthesis claims:**
1. **D — OT righteous-boasting coverage.** Confirm whether Jeremiah 9:24, Psalm 34:2, and Psalm 44:8 are tagged to M08, set aside, or absent. The "both-design" and cross-Testament claims for D (T0.2.2, T7.1.8) rest partly on the OT presence of the righteous boast.
2. **F — self-trust / self-sufficiency register ownership.** Confirm whether the self-sufficiency register (a.din; the "I am, none besides me" complex) is owned by M08 or by a separate cluster. F's 2-occurrence direct base means the **terminus** claim (§1; T6) leans on Isaiah 47 as anchor; ownership affects its evidentiary weight.

**Data-quality (CC review — gloss/faculty artefacts):**
3. **C1 — zid faculty = perception** appears to be a mechanical tag artefact (the characteristic is volitional); recommend CC re-gloss review (FA-14).
4. **E — fusioō/tufoō faculty under-tag.** E's cognition seat is carried by verse reading despite a thin faculty tag; recommend review.
5. **B — literal-height set-asides + set-aside file candidates.** Confirm the per-occurrence filtering of literal-height lemmas (ma.rom, qo.mah) and the standing set-aside proposals (archō "began/rulers"; ro.hav "span"; akratēs ownership query) from wa-m08-set-asides-v1_0-20260621.md.

**Cross-cluster / Session-D candidates (uniform silences and shared roots — not to be forced):**
6. **Spiritual-being interface (T4.6) — uniform near-silence.** Only inferential threads (Isaiah 14; Job 41:34; 2 Peter 2:10; 1 Timothy 3:6). Recommend carrying as a Session-D question rather than answering at cluster level.
7. **Creativity (T3.5) — uniform silence** across all seven. A clean cross-cluster absence worth noting at programme level.
8. **Pride ↔ Humility axis (M08 ↔ M09).** The structural opposite of most of the family is humility, and "God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble" (James 4:6) binds the two clusters. Recommend as a Session-D pairing.
9. **ha.lal (M08-D ↔ M04 praise).** Root-level link between right boasting and praise/joy. Recommend as a Session-D cross-cluster note.
10. **Shame ↔ Pride (M07 ↔ M08).** The science-surfaced vulnerable-narcissism question (grandiosity defending shame) is **absent from M08's verse evidence**; recommend as a Session-D test, explicitly not an M08 finding (GR-PROG-009 — inferential, not confirmed).

| Char | Answered (of 126) | Profile |
|---|---:|---|

| C1 — presumption | ~104 | narrow, will-centred; rich human-to-God; T4.6 answered (2 Peter 2:10) |
| C2 — insolence | ~101 | thin agent-interior, rich human-interface; fruit on the sufferer |

| E — conceit | ~89 | narrowly cognitive; opposite is love; no OT counterpart |
| F — self-love | ~88 | thinnest base; terminus (self usurps God's "I am") |

The coverage **gradient is itself meaningful**: D highest (object-directed, relational, affective, two-poled) and E/F lowest (small, narrowly-located bases) trace the real distribution of inner-being content across the family, not unevenness in the reading. The recurring structural silences (T4.1/T4.3/T4.4 across A, B, C1, E, F; creativity across all seven; the spiritual-being interface) are **findings about the characteristic's nature**, recorded as classified silences rather than gaps.

This synthesis is the essay-substrate for the cluster. A reader-facing study can be drafted from §1 (the field model), §2 (the by-tier account), and §3 (the cross-cutting findings) without returning to source, drawing anchors from §2/T7.2 and the science register from §2/T7.3. The flags in §4 should be resolved with Claude Code and the researcher before the cluster is formally closed; items 6–10 are Session-D candidates, not cluster-level deliverables. - **What this is:** the cluster-level synthesis that reads the eight per-characteristic tier-answer files *across* each tier — for every tier T0–T7, how the characteristics agree, differ, and together describe one region of the inner being. Each comparative claim is grounded in the verse evidence carried in the eight tier-findings files (`wa-m09-char-{a–h}-tier-findings-v1_0-20260621.md`), which remain the exhaustive per-characteristic record.
- **Counting basis:** 95 focus occurrences — A 23 · B 13 · C 13 · D 31 · E 4 · F 5 · G 3 · H 1 (= 93 placed) + 2 set-aside (okneō, diatassō). Counts indicative, not yet CC-version-locked.
