---

## Orientation — what the cluster is

M09 gathers the inner-being characteristics by which a person is brought, or brings themselves, **low** — before God and under authority — and the inner posture by which that lowering is freely owned. Read across the tiers, the eight are not synonyms but a **structured field** with three regions and two edges:

- a **humility triad (A / B / C)** — one lexical field (*tapein-* / *ka.na*) sorted by **voice**: the chosen act (A), the settled trait (B), the imposed condition (C);
- an **authority pair (D / E)** — obedience (the active complying) and submission (the ordered placing-under);
- a **willing interior (F)** — the glad volition (*na.div*) that makes submission and obedience freely given rather than extracted;
- two **peripheral edges (G, H)** — dignity (gravity rooted in reverence) and gentle-forbearance (affect-moderation), each pointing outward to other clusters.

The single most powerful discriminator among them is the **voice-and-faculty signature** (T1.2 + T3); the strongest unifiers are the **humble↔exalted reversal** (T0/T5) and a **christological grounding** (T0).

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**The cluster is christologically grounded throughout — its dominant T0 finding.** The four core characteristics each ground in Christ: he **humbled himself** (A — Phil 2:8), he **is lowly in heart** (B — Mat 11:29), he **assumed humiliation** (C — Act 8:33, Isa 53), and **by his obedience the many are made righteous** (D — Rom 5:19; "he learned obedience", Heb 5:8). The willing offering, dignity, and gentle-forbearance edges (F/G/H) carry the pattern only obliquely (H typologically, via the high-priest argument, Heb 5:2).

**"Borne by God" (T0.1.2) sorts the cluster.** Self-humbling (A) is **never** God's act — it is creaturely-only, the creature bending before God. But the **trait** (B) is borne by God-in-Christ (Mat 11:29 — the one M09 characteristic predicated of the incarnate Son as his own settled heart-state); the **condition** (C) is assumed by Christ (Act 8:33; the lowly body conformed to his glorious body, Phil 3:21); and **obedience** (D) is borne by Christ as the salvific act (Rom 5:19).

| Char | Primary God-relation (T0.1) | Borne by God? |
|---|---|---|
| A Self-humbling | God is **object/addressee** and responsive agent ("before the Lord", 1Ki 21:29; "he will exalt", Jam 4:10) | **No** — creaturely-only (uniquely in M09); christologically *patterned* in Phil 2:8 |
| B Lowliness | God **gives grace to the humble** (Jam 4:6) and **bears** it in Christ (Mat 11:29) | **Yes** — in Christ, as his settled heart-state |
| C Being brought low | God is **agent** of lowering and of reversal (2Ch 28:19; Luk 1:52) | **Yes** — assumed by Christ (Act 8:33) |
| D Obedience | God/Christ is **object** of obedience and (in Christ) its **bearer** (Heb 5:8; Rom 5:19) | **Yes** — Christ's obedience is salvific |
| E Submission | God **glorified** by gospel-confessing submission (2Cor 9:13) | No — creaturely |
| F Willing-heartedness | God **receives** the offering and **upholds** the willing spirit (Psa 51:12) | No — creaturely, God-sustained |
| G Dignity | paired with **godliness** (1Ti 2:2) | No — creaturely bearing |
| H Gentle forbearance | the human high priest's gentleness, **typological** of Christ (Heb 5:2) | No in-verse; christological by typology |

**Created design vs fallen condition.** The humility triad answers the **fallen condition** (pride relinquished — 2Ch 32:26; judgment borne — 2Ch 28:19) while imaging the **right creaturely posture** before God. Obedience (D) is **both** created order (the household and the obedience of faith) and **redemption's means** (Christ's obedience), with a fallen distortion at its edge (obeying sin, Rom 6:12). Three characteristics carry an explicit **counterfeit** at the edge: false humility / asceticism (B — Col 2:18, 23), eye-service obedience (D — Col 3:22), and submission rightly **refused** when it would betray the gospel (E — Gal 2:5).

**Future fullness / typology (T0.2.3 / T0.4.1) is uniform in direction:** the cluster leans on the **humble→exalted reversal** ("whoever humbles himself will be exalted", A — Mat 23:12; "he has exalted those of humble estate", C — Luk 1:52; grace-then-rest for the humble, B — Mat 11:29) and on **obedience→salvation** (D — Heb 5:9). The divine instance establishes the pattern; the human moves toward the reversal.

---

## T1 — Definition

**Kind (T1.2) sorts the eight along an act↔disposition↔condition axis.**

| Char | Dominant kind | Structural opposite (T1.3.1) |
|---|---|---|
| A Self-humbling | **act** (chosen, reflexive) | pride / self-exaltation |
| B Lowliness | **disposition** (borne trait, affect) | pride / haughtiness |
| C Being brought low | **condition/status** (undergone) | exaltation / being lifted up |
| D Obedience | **act + status** | disobedience / rebellion |
| E Submission | **status / posture** | insubordination / self-assertion |
| F Willing-heartedness | **disposition of will**, expressed in act | a grudging / coerced heart |
| G Dignity | **quality of bearing** | frivolity / levity |
| H Gentle forbearance | **act/disposition** of moderated feeling | harshness / severity |

**The cluster's master-antonym is pride and its kin.** Five of the eight stand against pride/self-exaltation/rebellion directly (A, B, D, E, and — as gravity-without-arrogance — G); C's opposite is the structural one of *being lifted*; F's is grudging compulsion; H's is harshness. Pride (M08) is the field this whole cluster negates.

**All but the simplest are compound (T1.2.2), and the cluster is heavily commanded (T1.4.3).** The humility triad and the authority pair run largely in **imperatives and address** — "humble yourselves" (A — Jam 4:10), "put on… humility" (B — Col 3:12), "children, obey" (D — Eph 6:1) — making M09 a strongly **paraenetic** region. Obedience uniquely operates through **hearing** a proclamation ("obey the gospel", D — 2Th 1:8); submission through the **posture of learning** (E — 1Ti 2:11).

**Conditions of reception (T1.7) expose a "true vs hollow / mis-aimed" axis** that recurs across the cluster: false humility that is fleshly self-abasement (B — Col 2:23), obedience that is mere **eye-service** without the heart (D — Col 3:22), obedience **mis-aimed at sin** (D — Rom 6:12), and submission that is **rightly withheld** (E — Gal 2:5). In every case the inner reality, not the outward form, is decisive.

---

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**The cluster is heart-centred (T2.1).** The **heart** is the recurring seat: the penitent heart of self-humbling (A — 2Ki 22:19), the lowly heart of the trait (B — Mat 11:29), the bowed heart of the one brought low (C — Psa 107:12), obedience "from the heart" (D — Rom 6:17), and the willing heart (F — Exo 35:5). The **soul** appears in B ("rest for your souls", Mat 11:29) and D ("purified your souls by your obedience", 1Pe 1:22); the **spirit** once, in F ("a willing spirit", Psa 51:12). The least interiorly-seated are E (a relational posture), G (a bearing), and H (affect un-seated) — the three edges.

**Origin and movement (T2.9 / T2.10) split cleanly.** A, B(true), and F **originate within** the person (B received/put on from Christ; F God-sustained, Psa 51:12); D **responds to external authority** but originates in the heart; and **C is the one characteristic that moves onto the person from outside** — God, enemies, or circumstance bring the lowering upon the patient (2Ch 28:19; Psa 106:42; 2Cor 12:21). This external-origin is the constitutional ground of C's distinctness.

| Char | Primary seat | Origin |
|---|---|---|
| A | heart | within (prompted by hearing God's word) |
| B | heart / soul / mind | received / put on from Christ |
| C | heart + affect (inner pole); body / social estate (outer pole) | **external** (God / enemies / circumstance) |
| D | heart / soul | response to authority + from the heart |
| E | (unseated — relational posture) | will + the relationship (from confession, 2Cor 9:13) |
| F | heart / spirit | within, God-sustained (Psa 51:12) |
| G | (unseated — bearing) | settled inner gravity / godliness |
| H | (unseated — affect) | felt solidarity in weakness |

---

## T3 — The Inner Faculties (the cluster's sharpest discriminator)

**The faculty signature tells the eight apart more precisely than anything else.** The cluster distributes across a **will-region** (A/E/F), a **perception-region** (D), an **affect-region** (C/H), a **cognition–affect–relational trait** (B), and a **conduct-bearing** (G).

| Char | Defining faculty | Other engaged | Notable |
|---|---|---|---|
| A Self-humbling | **volition** (chosen act) | affect (contrition), moral-eval, conscience, agency | the will bends itself before God |
| B Lowliness | **cognition + relational** | affect, volition, moral-eval, conscientiousness | the other-regarding trait (Phil 2:3) |
| C Being brought low | **affect** (downcast) | relational (as recipient of comfort) | **agency suspended** — undergone, not enacted |
| D Obedience | **perception** ("hearing-under") | cognition, affect, volition, agency, moral-eval, conscientiousness, relational | the **most faculty-rich** char |
| E Submission | **volition + relational** | cognition (learning), moral-eval (Gal 2:5 limit) | yielded posture, truth-limited |
| F Willing-heartedness | **volition** (the only volition-led) | **positive affect** (glad), agency, relational | glad free devotion — the affective opposite of C |
| G Dignity | **conduct / relational** | moral-eval (inferential) | a bearing-disposition, not a seated state |
| H Gentle forbearance | **affect** (moderated feeling) | relational, moral-eval (inferential) | affect-moderation (contrast M05 *praus*) |

**The sharpest internal line is the agency contrast A↔C:** self-humbling is **enacted** (the experiencer is the agent — "humble *yourselves*"), while being-brought-low has the experiencer's **agency suspended** (the agent is God/enemies/circumstance). Same lexical field (*ka.na* / *tapeinoō*), opposite voice — this is the cluster's defining structural seam.

---

## T4 — Relational Interfaces

**Every characteristic runs in a relational direction, and the cluster's God is one who lifts the low and saves the yielded.** God's side (T4.1): he **gives grace to the humble** (B — Jam 4:6), **comforts the downcast** and **exalts the lowly** (C — 2Cor 7:6; Luk 1:52), **responds to self-humbling with mercy** (A — 2Ch 7:14), and **saves the obedient** (D — Heb 5:9). The human side (T4.2) is the cluster's centre of gravity: self-humbling, willing offering, obedience and submission are all **movements toward God** (A — 2Ch 7:14; F — Exo 35:5; D — 1Pe 1:2; E — 2Cor 9:13).

**Directional map (T4.2 / T4.3):**

| Direction | Characteristics |
|---|---|
| God-ward (toward God) | **A** (self-humbling before God), **F** (offering to the Lord); **D/E** also God-ward (obedience/submission to God, gospel, faith) |
| Human-authority-ward | **D** (parents, masters, Abraham), **E** (household, church) |
| Toward-one-another | **B** ("humility toward one another", 1Pe 5:5; Phil 2:3) |
| Toward the failing / others | **G** (leadership/teaching bearing), **H** (the ignorant and wayward) |
| Received *onto* the person | **C** (lowered by God/enemies); **comfort received** by the downcast (2Cor 7:6) |

**Received-before-given grammar (T4.3.3 / T4.4).** B is explicit: a person **puts on** Christ's lowliness (received) before extending humility **toward one another** (given) — Col 3:12 then Phil 2:3. Obedience (D) is likewise **received** from an authority/proclamation and **rendered** in turn (2Cor 7:15; Phm 21). H requires the giver to **himself know weakness** before he can deal gently (Heb 5:2).

**Scope (T4.5) exceeds the immediate.** The **obedience of faith** crosses to **all nations** (D — Rom 1:5; 16:26); humility is owed **toward all / the lowly** (B — Rom 12:16); God's reversal **lifts the low across social status** (C — Luk 1:52); and submission is **truth-limited**, rightly refused where it would betray the gospel (E — Gal 2:5).

**Spiritual-beings interface (T4.6) — not blanket silence.** Six characteristics (A/C/E/F/G/H) are data-silent here — a candidate uniform cross-cluster silence for Session-D (as in M05/M07). But **two genuine exceptions** stand: B — counterfeit humility tied to **"worship of angels"** and elemental spirits (Col 2:18), so humility is a **site of adversarial distortion**; and D — "take every thought captive **to obey Christ**" within spiritual warfare (2Cor 10:5), so obedience is the **goal of the warfare** against false arguments.

---

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

**Suffering is a major cluster engine (T5.4).** Affliction **triggers** self-humbling (A — Manasseh "in his distress… humbled himself", 2Ch 33:12); the low estate often **is** the suffering (C — Psa 107:12; Phil 4:12); and **Christ "learned obedience through what he suffered"** (D — Heb 5:8), making suffering the school of obedience.

**Transformation and sanctification (T5.1 / T5.5).** B and D are **put-on-the-new-self** virtues (Col 3:12); obedience **purifies the soul** and **works salvation** (D — 1Pe 1:22; Phil 2:12; Heb 5:9); the humbling of C **forms** the person (guards Paul from pride, 2Cor 12:21; teaches contentment, Phil 4:12).

**Eschatology (T5.6) is the cluster's clearest shared trajectory — the humble→exalted reversal.** The self-humbled "will be exalted" (A — Mat 23:12); the lowly are exalted and the lowly body becomes glorious (C — Luk 1:52; Phil 3:21); grace-to-the-humble yields soul-rest (B — Mat 11:29); obedience yields eternal salvation (D — Heb 5:9). The whole cluster leans toward a consummation in which **the low are lifted**.

---

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics

### Internal architecture

**The humility triad A/B/C is one lexical field sorted by voice — the cluster's strongest internal structure.** *ka.na* and *tapeinoō* supply the **chosen act** (A, reflexive), the *tapein-* root supplies the **settled trait** (B), and the passive voice supplies the **imposed condition** (C). They are told apart by **voice and agency**, not vocabulary.

**The authority pair D/E is adjacent and possibly continuous:** obedience is the **active complying** (the act), submission the **ordered placing-under** (the posture). **F is the willing interior** that makes D/E freely given. **A and D meet at the cross** (Phil 2:8 — "he humbled himself by becoming obedient").

| Char | Nearest neighbour | Precise distinction |
|---|---|---|
| A | C (same verbs) | **agency/voice** — chosen act vs imposed condition |
| B | A | **kind** — settled trait vs chosen act |
| C | A | **agency/voice** — undergone vs enacted |
| D | E | **kind** — active complying vs ordered placing-under |
| E | D | posture vs act |
| F | D/E | **kind** — glad willing interior vs ordered compliance |
| G | (none internal) | **distinct register** — gravity/honour, not lowliness |
| H | M05 Gentleness | **faculty/level** — affect-moderation vs mind-governed restraint |

### Cross-cluster synthesis

| Cluster | Connection | Verse/lexical anchor |

| **M05** Love/Compassion/Kindness | **the meekness hinge** — humility (B) and meekness listed together; M05 holds gentleness (*praus*, cognition-only), M09's H is its affective complement (*metriopatheō*) | Col 3:12; Eph 4:2; Heb 5:2; M05 T6 boundary statement |
| **M23** Strength/Power/Authority/Dominion | **submission split** — the submission *verb* (*hupotassō*) is tagged M23; M09 holds the *noun* (*hupotagē*, E). Coverage flag. | 1Pe 5:5 (verb, M23) vs 2Cor 9:13 (noun, M09) |
| **M36** Service/Ministry | **willing service** — F's offering "for all the service of the house of God"; obedience's *doulos* / slavery frame (D) | 1Ch 28:21 (*avodah*); Rom 6:16 (*doulos*) |

---

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**Lexical arc (T7.1).** The cluster's vocabulary is four families: the *tapein-* / *ka.na* lowering field (A/B/C), the *hupakouō* / *hupotagē* heeding-and-ordering field (D/E), *na.div* willing-devotion (F), and the two singletons *semnotēs* (G) and *metriopatheō* (H). **OT→NT development is marked:** *ka.na* (OT — the king-before-God, national subjection) gives way to *tapeinoō* (NT — universalised maxim and christological act); the NT **coins/revalues** *tapeinofrosunē* (lowliness as a *virtue*, against the pagan-negative servile *tapeinos*) and *hupakoē pisteōs* (the "obedience of faith"). The cluster's lowness is thus **revalued upward** — from servile or judicial low estate into Christic excellence.

**Anchor verses (T7.2.5):** A — 2Ch 7:14 / Phil 2:8 · B — Mat 11:29 · C — Luk 1:52 · D — Rom 5:19 · E — 2Cor 9:13 · F — Exo 35:5 · G — 1Ti 3:4 · H — Heb 5:2.

**Human science (T7.3) — the cluster's unifying divergence.** Three science fields map onto the cluster: humility psychology (A/B/C — Tangney, VIA, Davis), self-regulation / virtue psychology (G/H — Baumeister, Hicks), and social/obedience psychology (D/E/F — Milgram, compliant-vs-internalised). The science **illuminates** real structure that the verses confirm:
- **situational / dispositional / imposed** humility → maps cleanly onto **A (act) / B (trait) / C (condition)**;
- **compliant vs internalised** obedience → maps onto **eye-service vs from-the-heart** (D — Col 3:22 vs Rom 6:17);
- **voluntary vs coerced** submission → *na.div* (F) is the named voluntary case.

**But the divergence is uniform across the cluster, and it is the cluster's theological signature:** the corpus presents **voluntary, willing, love-grounded humbling and submission *before God*** as the **highest expression of human freedom**, not its negation — a scope and ground (the **identity of the One submitted to** is decisive) that the science frameworks (compliance mechanics, self-appraisal, self-regulatory capacity) **cannot generate**. Milgram's dominant warning is the *danger* of obedience; M09 makes obedience to God salvific and obedience to **sin** the real danger (D — Rom 6:12, 16). This matches the science extract's own outside-science inventory: M09 has a proportionally large outside-science content for its size.

---

## Closing synthesis — the field model

1. **One region, three sub-regions, two edges.** M09 describes the inner being's capacity for **going low — before God and under authority — and freely owning it.** Members: a **humility triad** (A act / B trait / C condition), an **authority pair** (D obedience / E submission), a **willing interior** (F), and two **peripheral edges** (G dignity, H gentle-forbearance) that point outward.
2. **Sorted by voice-and-faculty.** The triad is one lexical field told apart by **voice/agency** (enacted A / borne B / undergone C); the cluster as a whole is told apart by **faculty** — will (A/E/F), perception (D), affect (C/H), cognition-affect-relational trait (B), bearing (G).
3. **Unified by the humble↔exalted reversal and a christological spine.** The reversal is the cluster's eschatological signature (T0/T5); the spine is that A/B/C/D each ground in Christ (T0.1.2).
4. **Master-antonym: pride** (M08). The cluster is the structured negation of self-exaltation.
5. **Heart-centred** (T2): the heart is the recurring seat across A/B/C/D/F.
6. **Cross-cluster:** meekness → M05; the submission-verb → M23; willing service → M36; the obedience of faith → M31; reverent obedience → M01; glad offering / reversal → M04 / M38.

---

## Open items carried to the researcher (not resolved here — §6 / GR-PROG-005 / GR-RD-007)

**Structural forks (interpret decisions):**
1. **A + B merge?** — Act (A) and trait (B) are one lexical field; verse-likeness keeps them distinct (chosen act vs borne disposition), but a single "humility" head is defensible. *Recommendation: retain distinct — the agency difference is real and load-bearing.*
2. **D + E merge?** — Obedience (act) and submission (posture) are adjacent; E is only 4 verses and its verb is in M23. *Recommendation: retain distinct but note E's thinness and the M23 split.*
3. **C inner / outer** — now evidenced: the **inner-being-relevant** pole is heart/affect (bowed heart Psa 107:12; downcast 2Cor 7:6); the **outer edge** is somatic/social (lowly body Phil 3:21; humble estate Luk 1:48). *Recommendation: keep C whole, flag the 2 somatic/social occurrences as outer-edge; do not split.*
6. **Set-aside okneō (Act 9:38) + diatassō (Luk 17:10)** — confirm (term-level filter fails for both).
7. **Coverage confirmations:** praotēs → M05, *hupotassō* → M23, and the **absence of Hebrew ʿānāw/ʿānāh (H6035/H6031)** from M09 — confirm by design or flag as an extraction gap (cf. DIM-187-SD001 sweep).

# M07 — Findings for Characteristic A: Felt shame at falsified trust / dashed expectation
**File:** wa-m07-char-a-felt-shame-trust-findings-v2_0-20260621.md · 2026-06-21 · **Supersedes v1_0** (scripted) — this is the verse-read re-answer.
**Evidence:** wa-m07-char-a-felt-shame-trust-v2_0-20260621.md (20 occ — bosh, cha.pher, ka.lam; all OT). Catalogue: 126 Q (T0–T7). Silent = A's own evidence is genuinely silent.

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design
- **T0.1.1** — God appears as the **true glory before whom false radiance is shamed** ("the moon confounded and the sun ashamed, for the Lord of hosts reigns… and his glory," Isa 24:23) and as the one who exposes the idols' emptiness ("their images are false, and there is no breath in them," Jer 51:17). Otherwise the shame is pronounced over idol-trusters.
- **T0.1.2** — Borne only by the creature (the wrongly-trusting); God is never the bearer — he is the true glory over against which false trust is shamed.
- **T0.2.1** — The role shown is **exposure/disabusing**: the shame reveals the trusted object as profitless ("the things they delight in do not profit," Isa 44:9) and the false lights as eclipsed by God's glory (Isa 24:23).
- **T0.2.2** — Both: the *capacity* to be shamed by failed trust presupposes the trusting faculty (created design); its *occasion* — reliance on idols/false refuges — belongs to the fallen condition. [inferential]
- **T0.2.3** — Yes — the horizon of the Lord's reign before which false radiance fades: "the Lord of hosts reigns on Mount Zion… his glory will be before his elders" (Isa 24:23).
- **T0.3.1** — Instantiates, negatively, the image as a **trusting/relying being** — shame marks the misdirection of a faculty made to rest in God. [inferential]
- **T0.3.2** — Exclusively creaturely; God does not trust-and-fail. This is the creature's experience of misplaced reliance.
- **T0.3.3** — Where present, it marks a self that has anchored on the wrong object — a disordering of the image's trust. [inferential]
- **T0.4.1** — Typological/eschatological at Isa 24:23: the shaming of the false lights before the reigning Lord prefigures God's final vindication over every rival; direction = the divine glory establishing the pattern.

## T1 — Definition
- **T1.1.1** — Carried by bosh, cha.pher, ka.lam ("be ashamed / confounded / disappointed"). Essential nature: the **inner collapse of a falsified trust**.
- **T1.1.2** — Hebrew only: bosh (be ashamed, disconcerted, disappointed), cha.pher (be confounded, abashed), ka.lam (be humiliated, confounded) — a confusion-plus-shame complex.
- **T1.1.3** — Directional toward the **object trusted** (idol, nation, refuge); the shame turns on the relation between truster and the thing trusted.
- **T1.2.1** — A **kind of event/act** (type=action throughout) — being shamed/confounded.
- **T1.2.2** — Compound: fuses **cognitive falsification** (expectation proven false) with **affect** (dismay/dread); co-terms confounded, dismayed, terrified, dread, anxiety.
- **T1.3.1** — Structural opposite: **trust vindicated / not put to shame** (char B) — the same faculty with a true object.
- **T1.3.2** — It excludes the security the idol promised; it is a passive collapse, resisting nothing actively. [partial]
- **T1.3.3** — Not shame at one's own moral sin (char C) nor inflicted disgrace (char E): it is the exposure of a *failed reliance*.
- **T1.4.1** — Operates as a verb (action), characteristically in the **prophetic declarative** ("shall be put to shame"); Hebrew Qal.
- **T1.4.2** — Largely uniform — oracle declaration over the wrongly-trusting.
- **T1.4.3** — Partly: some occurrences are addressed ("be ashamed because of Cush their hope," Isa 20:5 addressed to the confident), but most are third-person declaration.
- **T1.5.1** — Immediate response: **covering the head** (Jer 14:3,4), **turning back** (Isa 42:17), **melting / troubled like the sea** (Jer 49:23), terror (Isa 44:11). A somatic collapse.
- **T1.5.2** — Consistent — collapse / covering / turning.
- **T1.6.1** — Sustained effect: the **standing exposure** of the trust as vain — the truster left without the refuge they leaned on.
- **T1.6.3** — Immediate = the felt dismay and covering; sustained = the abiding verdict that the trusted thing was empty.
- **T1.7.1** — Silent — A frames shame as a negative outcome, not a faculty with conditions for "right" operation.
- **T1.7.2** — Silent — no distortion-by-another-spirit content.
- **T1.7.3** — Silent.

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries
- **T2.1.1** — No constitutional seat tagged; the verses locate the response in the **head/face** ("cover their heads," Jer 14:3,4) and the **body** ("melt," Jer 49:23) — bodily expression, not a seated faculty.
- **T2.1.2** — Recorded as situational/relational; expressed through head/face/body, not seated in spirit/soul/heart.
- **T2.7.1** — Body link runs **inner collapse expressing through the body** — covering the head, melting.
- **T2.9.1** — Origin: **the failure of the trusted object** (the idol's emptiness, the ally's defeat) — an externally-occasioned collapse; not God-given or generational.
- **T2.9.2** — Single pattern (failed trust).
- **T2.10.1** — Movement: from the **external event (the object's failure) onto the person** → felt collapse.

## T3 — The Inner Faculties
- **T3.1.1** — Perception engaged at the edge: the trusted idols "neither see nor know" (Isa 44:9) — the shame attends a failure of true discernment.
- **T3.1.2** — It exposes the perceptual blindness of trusting what cannot see or profit.
- **T3.1.3** — Perception engaged as the failed discernment behind the misplaced trust, not as sensory perception.
- **T3.2.1** — Cognition strongly engaged — **falsified expectation**: "ashamed because they were confident… disappointed" (Job 6:20). A's signature.
- **T3.2.2** — It is the collapse of a knowing — the judgement that the object would hold is proven wrong.
- **T3.2.3** — Cognition tagged on every bosh occurrence — the band's defining faculty alongside affect.
- **T3.3.1 / .2 / .3** — Silent — memory not engaged.
- **T3.4.1** — Affect engaged — the felt dismay/dread/shame of the collapse.
- **T3.4.2** — Produces dismay, dread, anxiety (the collapse-cluster: Isa 44:11; Jer 49:23).
- **T3.4.3** — Affect present throughout, bound to the cognitive falsification.
- **T3.5.1 / .2 / .3** — Silent — creativity not engaged.
- **T3.6.1** — Partial: the prior **mis-trust** was a (mis)directed reliance, but the shame itself is not volitional. Mostly the verses present passive collapse.
- **T3.6.2 / .3** — Silent on volition's operation within the shame.
- **T3.7.1 / .2 / .3** — Silent — the experiencers are passive recipients of the verdict, not agents.
- **T3.8.1** — Moral evaluation engaged where the object is idolatry (valence sinful: Isa 44:9,11; Psa 97:7; Hos 10:6) — the shame carries a verdict on the *object* of trust.
- **T3.8.2** — It judges the trusted object worthless/false ("worthless idols," Psa 97:7).
- **T3.8.3** — Moral weight enters through the object (idolatry), not uniformly.
- **T3.9.1 / .2 / .3** — Silent — this is not shame at one's own moral guilt (that is char C).
- **T3.10.1 / .2 / .3** — Silent — no integrated moral awareness→volition→action here.
- **T3.11.1** — Relational capacity engaged — the shame is relational to the **trusted object** (idol/nation) and, contrastively, to God as the true object (Isa 24:23).
- **T3.11.2** — It exposes the relation to a false object as ruinous of standing.
- **T3.11.3** — Engaged as the misdirected trust-relation across the band.

## T4 — Relational Interfaces
- **T4.1.1** — God → human: God **exposes/shames the false trust** — the Lord reigns and the false lights are shamed (Isa 24:23); the idols shown false (Jer 51:17).
- **T4.1.2** — Basis: judicial/responsive — the exposure follows the misplaced trust.
- **T4.1.3** — Silent / inferential (his glory eclipses rivals).
- **T4.2.1** — Silent for A directly — the verses do not show the truster moving toward God; the Godward movement is the *contrast* gathered under char B.
- **T4.2.2 / .3** — Silent.
- **T4.3.1 / .2 / .3** — Silent — the shame is not inflicted by a person; it is the failure of an object.
- **T4.4.1 / .2 / .3** — Silent.
- **T4.5.1** — Silent.
- **T4.5.2** — Crosses covenantal boundaries: applied to the **nations** (Moab, Egypt, Damascus, Babylon — Jer 48:13; Isa 20:5; Jer 49:23) as well as Israel.
- **T4.5.3** — Scope: any who trust a false object — covenant people and nations alike.
- **T4.6.1** — The failed objects include **idols** ("mute… no breath," Jer 51:17) — a false-spiritual object, though the point is their emptiness, not active spiritual agency.
- **T4.6.2 / .3** — Silent.

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension
- **T5.1.1** — Silent — no transformation shown; A is a verdict, not a change worked in the person.
- **T5.1.2** — Silent.
- **T5.2.1** — A micro-sequence is shown: **confidence → disappointment → shame** (Job 6:20).
- **T5.3.1** — Mechanism: the **failure of the trusted object** (the idol's emptiness; the ally's defeat; the drought, Jer 14:3-4).
- **T5.3.2** — Uniform mechanism across the band (a failed reliance).
- **T5.4.1** — Operates within affliction/judgment: drought and famine (Jer 14:3,4), military defeat (Jer 49:23), the day of the Lord (Zec 9:5).
- **T5.4.2** — The affliction is the occasion that exposes the trust as vain.
- **T5.5.1** — Silent — no sanctifying arc shown in A.
- **T5.6.1** — Eschatological at Isa 24:23 — the false lights finally shamed before the reigning Lord's glory.

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics
- **T6.1.1** — Co-occurs with **trust** (ba.tach), **confidence** (miv.tach), **expectation** (mab.bat), **boast** (ha.lal), and the collapse-cluster confounded / dismayed / dread / anxiety.
- **T6.1.2** — Shows shame as the **affective face of falsified trust**, bound to fear and dismay. [inferential]
- **T6.2.1** — Within A, shame **follows** misplaced confidence (Job 6:20 sequence).
- **T6.2.2** — The relationship is causal/developmental — false confidence produces the shame.
- **T6.3.1** — Silent (cross-char — interpret phase).
- **T6.3.2** — Produced by **misplaced trust / false confidence** (the trust precedes and causes the shame).
- **T6.3.3** — Silent (cross-char).
- **T6.4.1** — Shares lemmas (bosh, cha.pher, ka.lam) with chars B, C, D, E, G.
- **T6.4.2 / .3** — Silent (root-architecture analysis is interpret-phase).
- **T6.5.1** — Nearest neighbour is **char B** (same faculty of trust, opposite outcome); the distinction is the *object* (idol/false refuge vs God). [flag for cross-char confirmation]
- **T6.5.2** — Boundary: A and B divide by whether the trusted object fails (A) or holds because it is God (B).
- **T6.5.3** — Distinction of **direction/object**, not degree.

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation
- **T7.1.1** — bosh (BWŠ — be ashamed/confounded), cha.pher (be abashed), ka.lam (KLM — be humiliated/confounded).
- **T7.1.2** — Grammatical range: verbs (action); prophetic imperfect dominant.
- **T7.1.3** — Semantic range: ashamed / confounded / disappointed / dismayed.
- **T7.1.4** — Silent — all occurrences are the verbal/action kind; no disposition-vs-act split within A.
- **T7.1.5** — The opposite is the "**not put to shame**" of vindicated trust (char B).
- **T7.1.6** — Silent — no person-type term.
- **T7.1.7** — Silent — no seeking term.
- **T7.1.8** — A is **OT-only**; its NT continuation is char B (kataischunō "not put to shame" of the believer) — a development from the negative pole (idol-trust shamed) to the positive (faith vindicated).
- **T7.1.9** — Silent.

- **T7.3.1** — Lens: clinical psychology of shame as the collapse of self-relevant expectation, plus honour-shame (trusting a false refuge = loss of standing) [source: wa-m07-shame-scienceextract, Sec1/2].
- **T7.3.2** — Illumination: science's "disappointed confidence / dashed expectation" maps closely onto A's core (Job 6:20). [source: science extract]

# M07 — Characteristic A: Felt shame at falsified trust / dashed expectation
**File:** wa-m07-char-a-felt-shame-trust-v2_0-20260621.md · 2026-06-21 · **Supersedes v1_0** (v1_0 = occurrence list only; v2_0 adds verse-read analysis).
**Phase:** Evidence gather + ANALYSIS (verse-read). **Occurrences:** 20 (bosh ×16, cha.pher ×2, ka.lam ×2 — all OT, all Hebrew).
**Prior:** wa-m07-deepread-analysis-v1-20260621.md; evidence set wa-m07-evidence-allocc-v1-20260621.json.

## Analytical narrative

**What this characteristic is.** In this band, shame is not first a moral feeling about a wrong done; it is the *experiential exposure of a trust that proved false*. The person (or nation) leaned on something — an idol, an ally, a hope — and the thing gave way; the shame is the inner collapse of that misplaced reliance. The diagnostic is the **object of trust**, and across the band it is overwhelmingly an idol or a false refuge: "carved idols… metal images" (Isa 42:17), "the makers of idols" (Isa 45:16), "Chemosh… Bethel, their confidence" (Jer 48:13), "worthless idols" (Psa 97:7), "his idols… images are false, and there is no breath in them" (Jer 51:17), "his idol" (Hos 10:6), and the political hopes "Cush their hope and Egypt their boast" (Isa 20:5). The shame transfers from the emptiness of the trusted object to the exposure of the one who trusted it.

**Why it is the only band tagged affect *and* cognition.** The verses justify the double faculty directly. Shame here is a *falsified expectation* — a cognitive event — felt as dismay: "They are ashamed because they were confident; they come there and are disappointed" (Job 6:20). The reliance was a judgement about what would hold; when the judgement is proven wrong, the knowing and the feeling fail together. This is why the band's vocabulary pairs shame with a whole cluster of collapse-states: **confounded** (ka.lam — Isa 41:11; 45:16; Jer 14:3), **dismayed** (cha.tat — Isa 20:5; 37:27; Jer 14:4), **terrified** and **dread** (Isa 44:11), **anxiety** and "melt in fear" (Jer 49:23). Shame is the affective face of an expectation that has just been falsified.

**How it operates — voice and direction.** The experiencer is "other" in every occurrence: this is shame *pronounced over* the wrongly-trusting in the prophetic oracle voice (Moab, Damascus, Egypt's clients, the idol-makers), declared as the certain outcome of false reliance rather than narrated as a first-person feeling. Its valence sits mostly **neutral** (a stated consequence) shading to **sinful** where the misplaced trust is idolatry (Isa 44:9,11; Psa 97:7; Hos 10:6) — the moral weight enters through the *object*, not the emotion itself.

**Somatic expression.** Where the band touches the body it is the gesture of dashed hope: "they are ashamed and confounded and **cover their heads**" (Jer 14:3; cf. 14:4, the farmers with no rain), "turned back" (Isa 42:17), "melt… troubled like the sea" (Jer 49:23). The shame of failed trust shows outwardly as covering, turning, dissolving.

**The contrastive apex.** One verse inverts the field and exposes its logic: "the moon will be confounded and the sun ashamed, for the Lord of hosts reigns… and his glory" (Isa 24:23). Here even the brightest created lights are "ashamed/confounded" before the true glory. Set against this, the whole band reads as the shaming of every false radiance and false refuge before the one trustworthy object — which is exactly the positive pole gathered under characteristic B (trust in God that is *not* put to shame).

**Boundary (read from the cause).** This band is defined by its *cause*: the falsification of trust. That distinguishes it from characteristic C (shame at one's *own sin* before God — there the cause is moral guilt, not a failed reliance) and from characteristic E (disgrace *inflicted* by an agent). Where a verse's shame arises because the trusted object collapsed, it belongs here.

**Significance for the inner being.** This characteristic shows the inner person as constitutively a *trusting / relying* faculty, and shame as the experiential signal that the trust was placed in what cannot bear it. It is the negative diagnostic of where the self has anchored itself — and so it sits directly on the programme's question of the inner being's orientation and its interfaces (here, the interface with idols and false refuges, over against God).

### Internal movements (grounded)
- **A1 — Idol-trust exposed.** Isa 42:17; 44:9; 44:11; 45:16; Jer 51:17; Psa 97:7; Hos 10:6; Jer 48:13 (Chemosh/Bethel). Shame as the verdict on trusting the breathless/false.
- **A2 — Political/false-refuge trust exposed.** Isa 20:5 (Cush/Egypt); Jer 49:23 (Damascus, "bad news"); 2Ki 19:26 / Isa 37:27 (the strengthless inhabitants); Jer 14:3,4 (the failed cisterns / no rain).
- **A3 — The falsified-confidence core.** Job 6:20 ("confident… disappointed"); Zec 9:5 ("hopes are confounded"). The explicit confidence→disappointment movement.
- **A4 — Abashment before the true glory (contrastive).** Isa 24:23 — false radiance confounded before the Lord's glory; the hinge to characteristic B.

### Pattern notes
- **Faculty:** affect + cognition on all bosh occ (the band's signature); affect on cha.pher/ka.lam.
- **Experiencer:** other ×20 — prophetic-oracle declaration, not first-person.
- **Valence:** neutral (consequence) dominant; sinful where the trust is idolatry.
- **Seat:** none tagged — recorded as situational/relational (the shame of a failed reliance), not located in a constitutional seat.
- **Co-terms:** trust (ba.tach), confidence (miv.tach), expectation (mab.bat), boast (ha.lal), deception (she.qer), and the collapse-cluster confounded/dismayed/dread/anxiety.

# M07 — Findings for Characteristic B: Trust → vindication axis (shame vs honour as the outcome of hope in God)
**File:** wa-m07-char-b-vindication-axis-findings-v2_0-20260621.md · 2026-06-21 · **Supersedes v1_0**. Verse-read re-answer.
**Evidence:** 56 occ — bosh (heavy in the Psalter), kataischunō (the NT pole), cha.pher, ka.lam, aischunō. The band's signature is the formula **"shall not be put to shame"** for the one who trusts God, set against the shaming of the adversary. Richest OT→NT continuity in the cluster.

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design
- **T0.1.1** — God is the **active vindicator**: "those who wait for me shall not be put to shame" (Isa 49:23); "the Lord God helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced" (Isa 50:7); "in you they trusted and were not put to shame" (Psa 22:5). Shame and its absence are dispensed by God toward those related to him by trust.
- **T0.1.2** — Not borne by God; God is the one who **keeps the truster from** shame and **lays it on** the adversary (Psa 35:4).
- **T0.2.1** — The role shown: shame functions as the **negative verdict that trust in God averts** — "hope does not put us to shame" (Rom 5:5). Its purpose is to mark the truster as vindicated and the treacherous as exposed (Psa 25:3).
- **T0.2.2** — Both: the **trusting faculty** is created design (made to rest in God and be honoured); the *threat* of shame is the fallen world's pressure that God's vindication answers.
- **T0.2.3** — Yes, strongly eschatological: "when he appears we may have confidence and **not shrink in shame** at his coming" (1Jo 2:28); "everyone who believes in him will not be put to shame" (Rom 10:11) — a final, public non-shaming of faith.
- **T0.3.1** — Instantiates the image as a **God-trusting being whose hope is honoured** — "those who look to him are radiant, and their faces shall never be ashamed" (Psa 34:5).
- **T0.3.2** — The honouring is God's; the trusting and its vindication are the creature's experience of the relation.
- **T0.3.3** — Present and rightly ordered: the image functioning as designed — resting in God and therefore unashamed.
- **T0.4.1** — The Zion-stone oracle (Isa 28:16 → Rom 9:33; 10:11; 1Pe 2:6) is typological: the one who believes on the cornerstone "will not be put to shame," fulfilled in Christ — direction = OT promise consummated in the NT.

## T1 — Definition
- **T1.1.1** — The nature is **vindication vs shame as the outcome of trust** — to "not be put to shame" is to be publicly upheld by God; to "be put to shame" (of the adversary) is to be exposed and defeated.
- **T1.1.2** — bosh (be ashamed) and kataischunō (put to shame), characteristically **negated** for the truster; the affect+cognition complex (confident hope vindicated).
- **T1.1.3** — Directional/relational: defined by the **trust-relation to God** and the contrasting relation of the adversary.
- **T1.2.1** — An **outcome/event** of vindication or shaming.
- **T1.2.2** — Compound: confident expectation (cognition) + the felt security/relief or dread (affect); bosh tagged affect+cognition throughout.
- **T1.3.1** — Opposite within the band: the **shaming of the enemy/treacherous** (Psa 25:3; 35:4; 83:17) — the same axis inverted onto the adversary.
- **T1.3.2** — It excludes self-confidence apart from God — the treacherous "shall be ashamed" (Psa 25:3).
- **T1.3.3** — It is **not** felt shame at one's own sin (char C) nor the bearing of disgrace (char D); it is the *averted/inflicted verdict* keyed to trust.
- **T1.4.1** — Operates in **petition** ("let me not be put to shame," Psa 25:2; 31:1), **confession of confidence** ("I have not been disgraced," Isa 50:7), and **promise** ("you shall not be put to shame," Isa 45:17).
- **T1.4.2** — Three grammatical modes: prayer (jussive/cohortative), testimony (perfect), promise/citation (imperfect/future).
- **T1.4.3** — Yes — heavily in **direct address to God** (the Psalter's "let me not be put to shame").
- **T1.5.1** — For the truster the response is **radiance / unshaken standing** ("their faces shall never be ashamed," Psa 34:5; "I have set my face like a flint," Isa 50:7); for the adversary, being "turned back" and "dismayed."
- **T1.5.2** — Two consistent responses by party (vindicated radiance vs adversary's rout).
- **T1.6.1** — Sustained: an **everlasting** non-shaming — "saved… with everlasting salvation; you shall not be put to shame… to all eternity" (Isa 45:17).
- **T1.6.3** — Immediate = the rescue/relief; sustained = the abiding, even eternal, security of the vindicated.
- **T1.7.1** — Right operation: trust **rightly placed in God** is the condition under which shame is averted ("none who wait for you shall be put to shame," Psa 25:3).
- **T1.7.2** — Partial: the adversary's slander/reviling assaults the truster (1Pe 3:16), but God's vindication overturns it.
- **T1.7.3** — The threatened shame **fails to take hold** of the truster precisely because God upholds (Psa 119:116).

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries
- **T2.1.1** — Seat language present: the **heart** — "may my heart be blameless in your statutes, that I may not be put to shame" (Psa 119:80); and the **face** as the site of vindication/radiance (Psa 34:5; Isa 50:7). Refuge is "in you" — the trust seated in the God-relation.
- **T2.1.2** — Located in the heart's trust and shown on the face; relationally anchored in God.
- **T2.7.1** — Body link: **face/countenance** — radiant and unashamed (Psa 34:5), set like flint (Isa 50:7).
- **T2.9.1** — Origin: arises from the **God-relation of trust** — the non-shaming is *given by God* in response to refuge taken in him.
- **T2.9.2** — Single relational source (trust in God), with the adversary's shame as its judicial complement.
- **T2.10.1** — Movement: from God (the upholder) toward the truster (kept from shame) and against the adversary (put to shame).

## T3 — The Inner Faculties
- **T3.1.1** — Perception engaged: "having my **eyes fixed** on all your commandments" (Psa 119:6) — the gaze that keeps one from shame.
- **T3.2.1** — Cognition central — **confident expectation / hope**: "hope does not put us to shame" (Rom 5:5); "my eager expectation and hope that I will not be at all ashamed" (Phil 1:20). bosh tagged cognition throughout.
- **T3.2.2** — The cognition is a **settled assurance** that God will vindicate.
- **T3.4.1** — Affect engaged — security, radiance, relief (Psa 34:5), and its averted opposite, dread.
- **T3.4.2** — Produces confidence/boldness (Phil 1:20; 1Jo 2:28 "confidence") rather than the dismay of the shamed.
- **T3.6.1** — Volition engaged — the act of **taking refuge / waiting / clinging**: "in you, O Lord, do I take refuge" (Psa 31:1); "I cling to your testimonies" (Psa 119:31); "those who **wait** for you" (Psa 25:3).
- **T3.6.2** — The will actively casts itself on God as the ground of non-shame.
- **T3.8.1** — Moral evaluation present: the **righteous-vs-treacherous** sorting — "they shall be ashamed who are wantonly treacherous" (Psa 25:3); the wicked/Zion-haters shamed (Psa 129:5).
- **T3.9.1** — Conscience engaged at 1Pe 3:16 — "**a good conscience**, so that… those who revile your good behaviour may be put to shame" — clear conscience as the ground of vindication.
- **T3.11.1** — Relational capacity is the band's centre — the **trust-bond to God** that is honoured rather than shamed.
- **T3.11.2** — It exhibits the relation to God as the secure ground of standing.

## T4 — Relational Interfaces
- **T4.1.1** — God → human: God **keeps the truster from shame and vindicates** — "the Lord is his refuge" (Psa 14:6); "you have saved us… and have put to shame those who hate us" (Psa 44:7).
- **T4.1.2** — Basis: **covenant faithfulness / God's promise** — "uphold me according to your **promise**… let me not be put to shame" (Psa 119:116).
- **T4.1.3** — Disposition: God as **helper and refuge**, disposed to honour the trusting (Isa 50:7; Psa 25:20).
- **T4.2.1** — Human → God: the band's heartbeat — **trust, wait, take refuge, hope, call upon, cling** (Psa 22:5; 25:2; 31:1; 119:31). This is the most God-directed band in the cluster.
- **T4.2.2** — The movement is **dependence/petition** — casting oneself on God against the threat of shame.
- **T4.2.3** — Expressed in prayer and testimony before God and "before kings" (Psa 119:46).
- **T4.3.1** — Person → person: the **adversary** is the one shamed — enemies, accusers, the treacherous, Zion-haters (Psa 35:4; 71:13; 129:5).
- **T4.4.1** — Person ← person: the truster **receives reviling/slander** from adversaries (1Pe 3:16) but is vindicated by God against it.
- **T4.5.2** — Crosses to **the nations / Zion's enemies** (Psa 83:17 "let them be put to shame… forever"; 129:5).
- **T4.6.x** — Silent — no angelic/adversarial-spirit interface in B's verses.

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension
- **T5.1.1** — Formative: trust **sustained through trial** matures into vindication — "not put to shame in evil times; in the days of famine they have abundance" (Psa 37:19).
- **T5.2.1** — Sequence: cried/trusted → rescued → **not put to shame** (Psa 22:5) — trust precedes and grounds the vindication.
- **T5.3.1** — Mechanism: **God's intervention** in response to refuge taken in him.
- **T5.4.1** — Operates squarely **within suffering**: famine, enemies, slander, the cross — "if anyone suffers as a Christian, let him **not be ashamed**" (1Pe 4:16); Christ honoured "whether by life or by death" (Phil 1:20).
- **T5.4.2** — Suffering is the very arena where non-shame is proven.
- **T5.5.1** — Sanctification-adjacent: hope **produced through** affliction "does not put us to shame, because God's love has been poured into our hearts" (Rom 5:3-5).
- **T5.6.1** — Eschatological: final non-shaming at Christ's appearing (1Jo 2:28; Rom 10:11) — the consummation of the axis.

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics
- **T6.1.1** — Co-occurs with **trust** (ba.tach), **refuge** (cha.sah), **hope** (qa.vah / elpis), **wait**, **salvation**, and the adversary-cluster (enemies, the treacherous).
- **T6.1.2** — Shows shame/honour as the **outcome term of the trust-faculty** — the affective-relational payoff of hope. [inferential]
- **T6.2.1** — Within B, trust **precedes** vindication; the shaming of enemies **follows** their hostility to the truster.
- **T6.3.2** — Produced by the **trust-relation to God** (non-shame for the truster) and by hostility to God's people (shame for the adversary).
- **T6.4.1** — Shares bosh/kataischunō/cha.pher/ka.lam with chars A, C, D, E, G.
- **T6.5.1** — Nearest neighbour **char A** (same trust-faculty; B = true object → vindication, A = false object → shame) and **char D** (the enemy-shaming overlaps D's borne disgrace and E's imprecation). [flag for cross-char confirmation]
- **T6.5.2** — Boundary with A is the **object of trust**; with D/E, B reads the *same* shaming under the lens of the truster's vindication.

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation
- **T7.1.1** — bosh (BWŠ), kataischunō (kata + aischunō), cha.pher, ka.lam, aischunō.
- **T7.1.2** — Petitionary jussives, perfect-tense testimony, future/citation promise.
- **T7.1.3** — Range: not-ashamed / not-disgraced / not-confounded / vindicated; and (of enemies) put-to-shame / dismayed / turned-back.
- **T7.1.5** — The contrast term within the band is the **shaming of the adversary**.
- **T7.1.8** — **The clearest OT→NT continuity in M07**: the Psalter's "none who wait for you shall be put to shame" (Psa 25:3) and Isaiah's Zion-stone "will not be put to shame" (Isa 28:16) are taken up verbatim by Paul (Rom 9:33; 10:11) and Peter (1Pe 2:6) and extended to faith in Christ.
- **T7.1.9** — Silent — kataischunō is an existing compound, not a coinage.
- **T7.1.10** — Range: the vindication/non-shaming of trust across lament, promise, and gospel.
- **T7.2.1** — Functions as **petition, testimony, and promise** that trust will be vindicated.
- **T7.2.2** — Literary forms: **psalm** (lament/trust) dominant; **prophecy** (Isaiah); **epistle** (Romans, 1Pe, Phil, 1Jo); **gospel** (Luk 13:17, adversaries put to shame).
- **T7.2.3** — Logical structure (Psa 22:5): they cried/trusted (ground) → were rescued (act) → **were not put to shame** (conclusion).
- **T7.2.4** — Setting: individual/communal lament and prayer; apostolic exhortation under suffering.
- **T7.2.5** — Anchor: **Psa 25:3 / Rom 10:11** — "none who wait for you shall be put to shame" → "everyone who believes in him will not be put to shame" — the axis stated and consummated.
- **T7.2.6** — The anchor uniquely binds **trust** to **non-shame** as a covenant promise carried from Psalter to gospel.
- **T7.3.1** — Lens: psychology of **hope/secure attachment** and the social vindication of standing [source: wa-m07-shame-scienceextract Sec1/2].
- **T7.3.2** — Illumination: the secure, "unshamed" standing of one held by a trusted other parallels the believer's confidence before God. [source: science extract]
- **T7.3.3** — Divergence: the band grounds non-shame **eschatologically and theologically** (God's promise, Christ's appearing) — beyond what a this-worldly attachment frame supplies. [source: science extract T7.3.3]
- **T7.3.4** — Gap: the **public, forensic** vindication ("before kings," Psa 119:46; at his coming, 1Jo 2:28) exceeds the clinical, intrapsychic account of shame-relief. [source: science extract]

B is unusually **full**: its trust-relation, God→human and human→God interfaces, eschatology, and OT→NT spine answer most tiers directly.

# M07 — Characteristic B: The trust→vindication axis (shame vs honour as the outcome of hope in God)
**File:** wa-m07-char-b-vindication-axis-v2_0-20260621.md · 2026-06-21 · **Supersedes v1_0** (adds verse-read analysis).
**Phase:** Evidence gather + ANALYSIS (verse-read). **Occurrences:** 56 — bosh, cha.pher, ka.lam (OT); kataischunō, aischunō (NT). Testament: both — the clearest OT→NT continuity in M07.
**Prior:** wa-m07-deepread-analysis-v1-20260621.md; evidence set wa-m07-evidence-allocc-v1-20260621.json.

## Analytical narrative

**What this characteristic is.** Here shame is not a feeling but a **relational verdict** — the outcome of trust directed at God. The band turns on a single question the verses ask again and again: *will the one who trusts be put to shame, or vindicated?* Shame and honour/vindication are the two poles of one axis, and which pole a person lands on is decided by the **object** of their trust. Characteristic A showed trust in idols and false refuges ending in shame; characteristic B is the same human capacity — trust — sorted to the opposite result because its object is God: "in you they trusted and **were not put to shame**" (Psa 22:5). A and B are the negative and positive verdicts on the one faculty of reliance. This makes B the most theologically load-bearing band in the cluster.

**The petition core.** The dominant OT form is a plea whose *ground* is trust: "O my God, in you I trust; **let me not be put to shame**" (Psa 25:2); "In you, O Lord, do I take refuge; let me never be put to shame" (Psa 31:1; cf. 25:20; 71:1; 119:116). The co-terms make the logic explicit and repeated — ba.tach "to trust," cha.sah "to seek refuge," qa.vah "to wait for," se.ver "hope." Shame is the **feared** outcome; not-shame is the **hoped** vindication. The petitioner stakes his standing on God honouring the trust.

**The realised affirmation.** The axis also appears answered: "in you they trusted and were not put to shame" (Psa 22:5), and most luminously, "Those who look to him are radiant, and their faces **shall never be ashamed**" (Psa 34:5). Trust produces a radiant face; misplaced trust (char A) produces a covered one. The **face** is the recurring somatic register of the verdict — downcast in shame, radiant in vindication (Psa 34:5), or "set like a flint" in confident endurance (Isa 50:7).

**The enemy pole — vindication as the enemy's shame.** A large set of verses prays "let them be put to shame who seek my life" (Psa 35:4,26; 40:14; 70:2; 71:13; 83:17; 109:28; 129:5). In the petition's logic these are not a separate theme: the **enemy's shame is the petitioner's vindication** — one event from two sides. The co-terms show the petitioner's nephesh "soul/life" sought (ba.qash) by foes who are then "put to shame and turned back," and God is the **agent** who effects it ("you put them to shame," Psa 44:7; 53:5; "you would shame the plans of the poor, but the Lord is his refuge," Psa 14:6).

**The covenant-eschatological promise.** In Isaiah and Joel the vindication becomes corporate and **permanent**: "Israel is saved by the Lord… you shall not be put to shame… **to all eternity**" (Isa 45:17); "you will not be ashamed… you will forget the shame of your youth" (Isa 54:4); "my people shall **never again** be put to shame" (Joe 2:26,27). Here shame is removed forever as the mark of final salvation — and God's own honour is bound up in it ("let not those who hope in you be put to shame… O God of Israel," Psa 69:6, div=object).

**The NT continuity — the band's centre of gravity.** kataischunō carries the OT axis straight into the gospel and reattaches it to faith in Christ: "whoever believes in him **will not be put to shame**" (Rom 9:33; 10:11; 1Pe 2:6 — the Zion cornerstone; co-term pisteuō "to believe/trust"). And it is grounded constitutionally: "**hope does not put us to shame**, because God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit" (Rom 5:5) — the not-shaming of hope is worked in the **heart** by the **Spirit** (co-terms elpis, agapē, kardia co-seated, pneuma co-seated). The OT "not put to shame" of the truster becomes the NT "not put to shame" of the believer.

**The eschatological form.** With aischunō the verdict moves to the last day: "abide in him, so that… we may have confidence and **not shrink from him in shame at his coming**" (1Jo 2:28); "I will not be at all ashamed, but… Christ will be honored in my body" (Phili 1:20); "let him not be ashamed" as a Christian (1Pe 4:16). Co-terms parrēsia "boldness," elpis "hope." Shame here is an **eschatological category** — to be unashamed before the returning Christ is the final form of vindication.

**Apostolic confidence (a relational sub-use).** Paul's "I was not put to shame" (2Cor 7:14; 9:4; 10:8) applies the axis to his confidence/boast in the churches and his authority — vindicated, not shamed (co-term kauchaomai "to boast").

**Significance for the inner being.** This characteristic reveals the inner person as constituted by **trust/hope toward an object on which its vindication depends**, with shame as the experiential register of the verdict on that trust. It is vertical (Godward), relational, and constitutionally deep (Rom 5:5 locates it in the heart, worked by the Spirit). It carries a **temporal arc** — present petition → realised vindication → non-shame at the final appearing — so that in this band shame is not only a feeling but a status across time, finally abolished in salvation.

### Internal movements (grounded)
- **B1 Petition grounded in trust:** Psa 25:2,3,20; 31:1,17; 71:1; 119:6,31,46,80,116; 86:17. ("let me not be put to shame, for I take refuge in you")
- **B2 Realised vindication / radiant face:** Psa 22:5; 34:5; 37:19; 127:5.
- **B3 Enemy pole (vindication = the foe's shame), God as agent:** Psa 35:4,26; 40:14; 69:6; 70:2; 71:13,24; 83:17; 109:28; 129:5; 14:6; 44:7; 53:5; Luk 13:17; 1Pe 3:16.
- **B4 Covenant-eschatological permanence:** Isa 45:17; 54:4; Joe 2:26,27.
- **B5 Servant confidence ("face like flint"):** Isa 50:7.
- **B6 NT faith-vindication (Spirit-grounded):** Rom 5:5; 9:33; 10:11; 1Pe 2:6.
- **B7 NT eschatological (unashamed at his coming):** 1Jo 2:28; Phili 1:20; 1Pe 4:16.
- **B8 Apostolic confidence not shamed:** 2Cor 7:14; 9:4; 10:8; Luk 16:3.

### Pattern notes
- **Faculty:** affect (+cognition on bosh). **Experiencer:** both self (petitioner) and other/other-addressed (enemies; Israel) — the axis is two-poled.
- **Valence:** mostly neutral; **forbidden** on Joe 2:26,27 (the *prohibition* of shame as eschatological promise — "never again").
- **Divine involvement:** agent (God shames the foe / saves), object (God's honour bound to the people's vindication), addressee (the prayed-to Lord).
- **Seat:** heart + Spirit named at Rom 5:5; nephesh "soul" co-seated in the petitions (Psa 25:20; 35:4; 70:2). Otherwise relational/situational.
- **Co-terms:** trust/refuge/wait/hope/believe (ba.tach, cha.sah, qa.vah, se.ver, elpis, pisteuō); boldness (parrēsia); on the enemy side hate (sa.ne), seek-the-life (ba.qash + nephesh).
- **Boundary:** distinguished from A by the *object* of trust (God vs idol/false refuge); from D by being a *relational verdict on trust* rather than a borne standing. Enemy-shame verses overlap D/E (imposed) but sit here because the frame is the petitioner's vindication.

# M07 — Findings for Characteristic C: Conscience — shame at one's own sin
**File:** wa-m07-char-c-conscience-sin-findings-v2_0-20260621.md · 2026-06-21 · **Supersedes v1_0** (v1_0 was scripted field-aggregation; this v2_0 is a verse read).
**Method:** every question answered by reading C's 22 verses and applying judgement; **Silent only where the text is genuinely silent.**
**Evidence (22 occ):** bosh, ka.lam, bo.shet, ke.lim.mah (OT penitential) + entrepō, entropē (NT admonitory). Core verses: Ezr 9:6,7; Dan 9:7,8; Jer 3:25; Jer 31:19; Eze 16:52,54,61,63; 36:32; 43:10,11; 1Cor 4:14; 6:5; 15:34; 2Th 3:14; Tit 2:8.

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design
- **T0.1.1** — God is the reference point and prompt: shame is felt *before him* ("ashamed… to lift my face to you, my God," Ezr 9:6), grounded in his righteousness against the person's sin ("to you, O Lord, belongs righteousness, but to us open shame… because we have sinned against you," Dan 9:7-8), commanded by him ("Be ashamed and confounded for your ways," Eze 36:32), produced through his instruction (Jer 31:19), and resolved by his atonement (Eze 16:63). Roles: addressee, instructor, commander, atoner.
- **T0.1.2** — Borne only by the creature — God never bears shame-at-sin; yet it exists *only* by relation to his righteousness (Dan 9:7). Exclusively creaturely, wholly God-referenced.
- **T0.2.1** — Purpose is stated repeatedly: it leads to remembering, being confounded, and ceasing ("that you may remember and be confounded, and never open your mouth again," Eze 16:63), to confession (Dan 9; Ezr 9), to relenting/turning (Jer 31:19), and is the precondition God sets before restoration ("that they may be ashamed of their iniquities; and they shall measure the plan," Eze 43:10-11). NT: corrective — "that he may be ashamed" (2Th 3:14), "do not go on sinning" (1Cor 15:34).
- **T0.2.2** — Both: the *capacity* (conscience, shame at one's own wrong before God) reads as created design; its *occasion* (sin to be ashamed of) belongs to the fallen condition. [inferential]
- **T0.2.3** — Yes — oriented toward atonement and restoration: "when I atone for you" (Eze 16:63), the restored temple (Eze 43:10-11), the new-covenant turning (Jer 31:19).
- **T0.3.1** — Instantiates moral answerability before God — the image as a being who can recognise and own its wrong against a holy standard. [inferential]
- **T0.3.2** — Exclusively creaturely; it is the creature's penitent analogue *over against* God's righteousness, not a likeness God shares.
- **T0.3.3** — Where present (Ezr 9; Dan 9; Jer 31:19) the image's moral witness is operative and rightly oriented; its absence is the shameless condition (char C-neg).
- **T0.4.1** — Typological/covenantal: the shame→atonement pattern (Eze 16:63) points beyond itself to the divine act of atonement; direction = human penitence pointing toward God's atoning act. [inferential]

## T1 — Definition
- **T1.1.1** — The inward acknowledgment of one's own guilt before God — penitent shame. Carried by bosh/ka.lam (be ashamed, blush, be confounded), bo.shet/ke.lim.mah (the disgrace owned in confession), and NT entrepō/entropē (corrective shame).
- **T1.1.2** — Hebrew = the felt-and-confessed shame of the guilty (bosh + "confounded"; bosheth/kelimmah owned, "let our dishonor cover us," Jer 3:25). Greek = entrepō/entropē, shame as a turning-inward provoked by admonition.
- **T1.1.3** — Vertical and inward: shame felt *Godward* (the face that cannot be lifted to God, Ezr 9:6) and turned on the self. Relational force is coram Deo.
- **T1.2.1** — Spans act → condition: the act of being ashamed/blushing (bosh, ka.lam — action) which, owned, is borne as a state (bosheth, kelimmah — status).
- **T1.2.2** — Compound: integrates moral recognition (knowing the sin), affect (shame/blush), memory, and willed cessation/confession — Eze 16:63 binds remember + be confounded + "never open your mouth."
- **T1.3.1** — Structural opposite: shamelessness (char C-neg) — the refusal/inability to be ashamed at sin; resolution-opposite is the atonement that removes the ground of shame.
- **T1.3.2** — Resists self-justification and the covering of sin; excludes the presumption of lifting the face to God while guilty (Ezr 9:6 cannot).
- **T1.3.3** — Not social embarrassment (char A) nor disgrace inflicted by enemies (char E); it is self-recognised guilt before God. The boundary is the *cause*: one's own sin, Godward.
- **T1.4.1** — Modes: spontaneous confession (Ezr 9:6); commanded imperative ("Be ashamed," Eze 36:32); instructed outcome ("after I was instructed… I was ashamed," Jer 31:19); admonitory provocation (NT entrepō). Hebrew stems: bosh Qal/Hithpael, ka.lam Niphal.
- **T1.4.2** — Yes — from spontaneous conviction (Ezr/Dan) to commanded (Eze 36:32) to externally-provoked correction (NT).
- **T1.4.3** — Strongly: commanded ("Be ashamed," Eze 36:32), addressed ("that you may be ashamed," Eze 16), and confessed in speech (Dan 9; Ezr 9 prayers; "I say this to your shame," 1Cor 6:5; 15:34).
- **T1.5.1** — Immediate response: blushing and inability to lift the face (Ezr 9:6), being confounded (Jer 31:19; Eze 16:63), striking the thigh (Jer 31:19), falling silent / "never open your mouth again" (Eze 16:63), lying down in shame (Jer 3:25). Somatic-penitential and verbal-cessation.
- **T1.5.2** — Consistent in kind: downcast, silenced, self-abasing across the penitential verses.
- **T1.6.1** — Establishes a penitent orientation over time: turning from sin (Jer 31:19 relented), cessation (Eze 16:63), readiness to receive restoration (Eze 43:10-11).
- **T1.6.3** — Immediate = the felt collapse (blush, confounded, silenced); sustained = the settled repentant orientation and the ending of the sin.
- **T1.7.1** — Takes hold rightly when joined to instruction (Jer 31:19 "after I was instructed") and to acknowledgment of God's righteousness (Dan 9:7).
- **T1.7.2** — Blocked by the shameless condition (char C-neg, "did not know how to blush") and, in C's own evidence, by "having no knowledge of God" (1Cor 15:34). No adversarial-spirit interference shown — **Silent** on that sub-part.
- **T1.7.3** — The person in whom the occasion is present but does not take hold is the shameless one (char C-neg).

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries
- **T2.1.1** — Though the coded seat is largely untagged, the verses locate it across faculties/body: the face ("lift my face," Ezr 9:6) and blush (bodily expression); memory ("remember… and be ashamed," Eze 16:61,63); the mind/heart ("after I was instructed," Jer 31:19) turning; the mouth (silenced, Eze 16:63); the thigh struck (Jer 31:19).
- **T2.1.2** — Not a single seat: conscience here runs memory → moral recognition → affect → bodily/verbal expression → the will's turning. The heart is the implicit seat of the turning.
- **T2.7.1** — Body link runs **soul/heart expressing through the body**: downcast face, blush, struck thigh, silenced mouth — inner conviction shown outwardly.
- **T2.9.1** — Origin is God-prompted (instruction, Jer 31:19; command, Eze 36:32) *and* arises from the person's recognition of guilt (Ezr 9; Dan 9).
- **T2.9.2** — Multiple: external prompt (God's word/instruction) and internal recognition both attested.
- **T2.10.1** — Movement: from God's instruction/word onto the person → inward conviction → outward bodily/verbal expression → turning. A definite sequence.

## T3 — The Inner Faculties
- **T3.1.1** — Perception engaged: "describe the temple, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities" (Eze 43:10) — perceiving the holy pattern exposes the sin; "remember and be confounded" (Eze 16:63). [moderate]
- **T3.1.2** — It sharpens inner sight of one's own deeds against God's standard.
- **T3.1.3** — Perception engaged as the recognition that triggers the shame, not as sensory perception per se.
- **T3.10.1** — Conscientiousness (integrated moral awareness + volition + action) is engaged: Jer 31:19 runs instructed → ashamed → relented → struck thigh — awareness, will, and act together.
- **T3.10.2** — It integrates the moral self into a single penitent response — recognition issuing in turning and confession.
- **T3.10.3** — Across the verses this integration is the characteristic's signature (Ezr 9; Dan 9; Jer 31:19; Eze 16:63).
- **T3.11.1** — Relational capacity engaged vertically: the shame is felt within the God-relationship (Ezr 9:6; Dan 9:7-8) and, in the NT, within the church family.
- **T3.11.2** — It restores right relational standing by owning the breach before God.
- **T3.11.3** — Predominantly God-directed (vertical), secondarily community (NT admonition).
- **T3.2.1** — Cognition strongly engaged: it requires knowing one's sin ("ashamed of all that you have done," Eze 16:54; "because we have sinned," Dan 9:8).
- **T3.2.2** — It is cognitively mediated — recognition of guilt is constitutive, not incidental.
- **T3.2.3** — Cognition engaged in every verse where the sin is named as the ground of the shame.
- **T3.3.1** — Memory explicitly engaged: "you will remember your ways and be ashamed" (Eze 16:61); "that you may remember and be confounded" (Eze 16:63).
- **T3.3.2** — Memory is the trigger — recalling the deeds produces the shame.
- **T3.3.3** — Where memory of sin is named, shame follows; a clear memory→shame link.
- **T3.4.1** — Affect engaged: the felt shame, blush, and confoundedness (Ezr 9:6; Jer 31:19).
- **T3.4.2** — Produces the painful, self-lowering feeling of guilt before God.
- **T3.4.3** — Affect present throughout, but bound to moral recognition (not free-floating feeling).
- **T3.5.1** — **Silent** — no engagement of the creative faculty in this characteristic's evidence.
- **T3.6.1** — Volition engaged: it issues in willed turning/cessation — "I relented" (Jer 31:19), "never open your mouth again" (Eze 16:63), "do not go on sinning" (1Cor 15:34).
- **T3.6.2** — It moves the will from the sin toward turning; the will's response completes the characteristic.
- **T3.6.3** — Volitional turning is the consistent outcome where the verses follow the shame through.
- **T3.7.1** — Agency engaged at the response: striking the thigh, confessing, ceasing — the person acts. [moderate]
- **T3.7.2** — It mobilises penitent action (confession, reform).
- **T3.7.3** — Agency appears as the penitent's responsive acts, not as initiating power.
- **T3.8.1** — Moral evaluation strongly engaged — the characteristic *is* moral self-assessment against God's standard (valence sinful/righteous/commanded).
- **T3.8.2** — It renders a verdict on the self: guilty before a righteous God (Dan 9:7).
- **T3.8.3** — Moral framing present on nearly every occurrence; this is the characteristic's core faculty.
- **T3.9.1** — Conscience is the defining faculty here — the acute inner witness of sin and guilt (Ezr 9:6 "our iniquities… our guilt"; Dan 9 confession). This characteristic *is* conscience operating.
- **T3.9.2** — It convicts and lowers the self, opening the way to confession and turning.
- **T3.9.3** — Conscience-engagement is universal across C's evidence — its constitutive faculty.

## T4 — Relational Interfaces
- **T4.1.1** — God → human: he prompts and commands the shame ("Be ashamed… declares the Lord God," Eze 36:32) and instructs toward it (Jer 31:19).
- **T4.1.2** — Covenantal and responsive — within the covenant lawsuit (Eze 16; Jer 3), responsive to sin, ordered toward atonement (Eze 16:63).
- **T4.1.3** — That he commands shame-then-atonement shows a disposition toward restoration, not bare condemnation — shame is the door he opens to cleansing. [inferential]
- **T4.2.1** — Human → God: confession/prayer Godward (Ezr 9:6 "O my God, I am ashamed… to lift my face to you"; Dan 9; Jer 3:25 "we have sinned against the Lord").
- **T4.2.2** — Requires humility, acknowledgment of God's righteousness and one's guilt, the lowered face.
- **T4.2.3** — Shows a penitent, covenant-aware relationship — the person owns guilt before a righteous God and seeks restoration.
- **T4.3.1** — Person → person: NT admonitory shame — one provokes shame in another to correct ("that he may be ashamed," 2Th 3:14; 1Cor 6:5; 15:34).
- **T4.3.2** — Done in love, not contempt — "not… to make you ashamed, but to admonish you as my beloved children" (1Cor 4:14): parental care.
- **T4.3.3** — The admonisher must speak from blameless standing — "sound speech that cannot be condemned" (Tit 2:8).
- **T4.4.1** — Receiving: the admonished one is to take up the shame and turn (2Th 3:14).
- **T4.4.2** — Uptake is blocked by "having no knowledge of God" (1Cor 15:34) and by the shameless condition (C-neg).
- **T4.4.3** — The one who meets it but does not take it up is the shameless (char C-neg).
- **T4.5.1** — Operates within covenant bonds (Israel; the church as "beloved children," "brothers").
- **T4.5.2** — Predominantly covenantal/in-community — distinct from imposed shame on the nations (char D/E).
- **T4.5.3** — Scope: those in covenant relationship with God / within the believing community.
- **T4.6.1** — **Silent** — no angelic/adversarial interface in C's evidence.
- **T4.6.2** — **Silent.**
- **T4.6.3** — **Silent.**

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension
- **T5.1.1** — Yes — it transforms both condition and orientation: "after I was instructed… I was ashamed… I relented" (Jer 31:19) — shame is the hinge of repentance.
- **T5.1.2** — The turning it produces is presented as enduring — cessation, "never open your mouth again" (Eze 16:63). [enduring in the evidence]
- **T5.2.1** — Sequence is explicit: turned away → instructed/relented → ashamed → confounded → struck thigh (Jer 31:19); and remember → be ashamed/confounded → silenced → atoned (Eze 16:61-63).
- **T5.3.1** — Mechanism: instruction/discipline and confrontation with one's deeds (Jer 31:19; Eze 43:10 "describe the temple, that they may be ashamed"); in the NT, admonition.
- **T5.3.2** — Varies — spontaneous conviction (Ezr/Dan), commanded (Eze 36:32), instructed (Jer 31:19), externally admonished (NT).
- **T5.4.1** — Operates within affliction: shame borne amid exile/judgment (Ezr 9:7; Dan 9 captivity context); affliction is its setting.
- **T5.4.2** — The affliction of exile brings the sin to memory and deepens the penitent shame (Eze 36; Dan 9). [inferential]
- **T5.5.1** — Central to sanctification — shame-at-sin is the penitent turn that precedes and enables restoration (Eze 43:10-11).
- **T5.6.1** — Eschatologically oriented — toward final atonement/restoration where the shame is resolved (Eze 16:63; 36; 43; Jer 31).

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics
- **T6.1.1** — Within C's verses, shame co-occurs with guilt/iniquity (Ezr 9:6,7; Dan 9), with "confounded" (the bosh/ka.lam pairing), and with disgrace/dishonour owned ("let our dishonor cover us," Jer 3:25).
- **T6.1.2** — It sits at the junction of guilt, memory, and repentance — the affective face of conviction. [inferential]
- **T6.2.1** — Within C, shame follows instruction/recognition and precedes turning/atonement (sequence above).
- **T6.2.2** — Developmental and causal — the shame drives the turn.
- **T6.3.1** — Produces repentance/turning (Jer 31:19 "I relented"). 
- **T6.3.2** — Produced by conviction/instruction and the recognition of guilt.
- **T6.3.3** — A constituent element of conviction/repentance. [inferential — cross-char confirmation pending]
- **T6.4.1** — Shares lemmas with chars A, B, D, E, G: bosh, ka.lam, bo.shet, ke.lim.mah (same terms, different use); entrepō/entropē shared with E/G.
- **T6.4.2** — Root sharing: bosh/bo.shet share the BWŠ root; ka.lam/ke.lim.mah share the KLM root — the same roots generate both the felt-shame and the borne-disgrace terms used here.
- **T6.4.3** — Conscience-shame is lexically continuous with disgrace-shame; what distinguishes it is the Godward, self-at-own-sin orientation, not the vocabulary.
- **T6.5.1** — Nearest neighbours: char A (felt shame) and char D (borne disgrace). Distinction: C is shame at one's *own sin before God*; A is shame at falsified trust; D is disgrace as imposed/borne standing. [flag for cross-char confirmation]
- **T6.5.2** — Precise boundary = the *cause*: own sin coram Deo (C) vs external defeat (A) vs another's act (E).
- **T6.5.3** — Difference of **direction** (self-at-own-sin, Godward) and **moral register** (conviction), not merely degree.

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation
- **T7.1.1** — Primary terms: bosh (BWŠ — be ashamed, confounded), ka.lam (KLM — be humiliated, blush), bo.shet (shame), ke.lim.mah (disgrace), entrepō/entropē (turn-in, be made ashamed).
- **T7.1.2** — Both verbs (bosh, ka.lam, entrepō) and nouns (bo.shet, ke.lim.mah, entropē) — the act of being shamed and the borne state.
- **T7.1.3** — Semantic range: blushing/being confounded → bearing disgrace → being admonished to shame.
- **T7.1.4** — Verb (act of being ashamed) vs noun (borne shame); the conscience-use foregrounds the act + recognition.
- **T7.1.5** — Absence/opposite: shamelessness ("did not know how to blush," cross-ref C-neg); atonement removes the ground (Eze 16:63).
- **T7.1.6** — **Silent** — no person-type term in C's evidence.
- **T7.1.7** — No dedicated seeking-lemma, but the confessional-prayer form (Dan 9; Ezr 9) is the vehicle of seeking. [partial]
- **T7.1.8** — OT = penitential conviction before God (Hebrew terms); NT = admonitory shame toward repentance (entrepō). Continuity: shame as the doorway to turning; development: NT foregrounds relational correction within the church.
- **T7.1.9** — **Silent** — no NT coinage; entrepō/entropē are existing terms used in the corrective sense.
- **T7.1.10** — Full arc: act + state, Hebrew + Greek, conviction → admonition — shame functioning to turn the person from sin.
- **T7.2.1** — The term governs the confession (Ezr 9:6 verb heads "I am ashamed… to lift my face"), the imperative (Eze 36:32), or the corrective clause ("I say this to your shame," 1Cor 6:5).
- **T7.2.2** — Forms: penitential prayer (Ezr 9; Dan 9), prophetic covenant-lawsuit (Eze 16; 36; 43; Jer 3; 31), epistolary admonition (1Cor; 2Th; Tit) — each read on its own terms.
- **T7.2.3** — Logical structure (Dan 9:7-8): premise (God is righteous) + premise (we have sinned) → conclusion (ours is the open shame).
- **T7.2.4** — Setting: covenantal/judicial (lawsuit, exile) and liturgical (confessional prayer).
- **T7.2.5** — Primary anchor: **Ezr 9:6** — "I am ashamed and blush to lift my face to you, my God, for our iniquities…" — the fullest expression of conscience-shame before God.
- **T7.2.6** — The anchor uniquely shows shame as the *inability to lift the face to God* under the weight of guilt — the vertical, coram-Deo essence the other verses assume.
- **T7.3.1** — Lens: clinical/moral psychology — the shame/guilt distinction (Lewis; Tangney & Dearing) [source: wa-m07-shame-scienceextract, Sec1/3].
- **T7.3.2** — Illumination: this characteristic sits closest to science's *guilt* pole — shame at the deed, leading to reparative turning — which matches the repentance outcome the verses show (Jer 31:19). Honour-shame framing adds the Godward, public dimension.
- **T7.3.3** — Divergence: science generally treats shame as maladaptive; here shame at sin is *appropriate and God-commanded*, ordered toward restoration (Eze 36:32; 43:10-11) — a normative reversal of the clinical default.
- **T7.3.4** — Gap surfaced: science's somatic markers (downcast face, hiding, gaze-aversion) are present in the verses (blush, the unliftable face, struck thigh) and worth tagging explicitly; and the shame→repentance mechanism invites testing against the programme's repentance/turning vocabulary.

---
**Genuine Silence in C (after reading): 6 of 126** — T1.7.2 (adversarial-spirit part only), T3.5 (creativity), T4.6.1/.2/.3 (spiritual beings), T7.1.6 (person-type term), T7.1.9 (NT coinage). Everything else is answered from the verses. (v1_0 had ~70 Silent — the difference is reading vs field-aggregation.)
