# M07 — Characteristic C: Conscience — shame at one's own sin
**File:** wa-m07-char-c-conscience-sin-v2_0-20260621.md · 2026-06-21 · **Supersedes v1_0** (adds verse-read analysis).
**Phase:** Evidence gather + ANALYSIS (verse-read). **Occurrences:** 22 — bosh, ka.lam, bo.shet, ke.lim.mah (OT penitential) + entrepō, entropē (NT admonitory). Testament: both.

## Analytical narrative

**What this characteristic is.** Here shame is the **inward acknowledgment of one's own guilt before God** — penitent shame, felt *coram Deo*. Unlike characteristic A (shame at a failed reliance) the cause is moral: the person's own sin. Its definitive image is the unliftable face: "O my God, I am ashamed and blush to **lift my face to you**, my God, for our iniquities have risen higher than our heads" (Ezr 9:6); "to you, O Lord, belongs righteousness, but to us **open shame**… because we have **sinned against you**" (Dan 9:7-8). Shame is measured against God's righteousness and owned in confession.

**Two registers.** The OT material is penitential **confession** in prayer and covenant-lawsuit (Ezr 9; Dan 9; Jer 3:25; 31:19; Eze 16; 36; 43). The NT material is **admonitory** — corrective shame deliberately provoked to turn a believer back: "that he may be **ashamed**" (2Th 3:14), "I say this to your **shame**" (1Cor 6:5; 15:34), and pointedly *not* in contempt but in love: "I do not write these things to make you ashamed, but to admonish you as my **beloved children**" (1Cor 4:14).

**The purpose is stated, repeatedly — this is shame that works.** It is ordered toward turning: "after I was **instructed**, I struck my thigh; I was ashamed, and I was confounded" (Jer 31:19 → "I relented"); "that you may **remember and be confounded, and never open your mouth again** because of your shame, **when I atone for you**" (Eze 16:63); and it is the precondition God sets before restoration: "that they may be **ashamed of their iniquities**; and they shall measure the plan" of the temple (Eze 43:10-11). God even **commands** it: "Be ashamed and confounded for your ways, O house of Israel" (Eze 36:32). Shame here is the doorway God opens to confession, cessation, atonement, and restoration.

**The sequence and the faculties.** The verses lay out a movement — *instruction/memory → recognition of guilt → shame/confoundedness → bodily expression → turning*: Jer 31:19 (instructed → ashamed → confounded → struck the thigh → relented); Eze 16:61-63 (remember → be ashamed/confounded → silenced → atoned). It therefore engages **conscience** (the witness of guilt, Ezr 9:6), **memory** (Eze 16:61,63), **cognition** (knowing the sin, Dan 9:8), **moral evaluation** (the verdict against God's standard), **affect** (the blush/confoundedness), and **volition** (the turning, the silenced mouth). It integrates these into a single penitent response — conscientiousness in the full sense.

**The body.** Conviction shows outwardly: the unliftable face and blush (Ezr 9:6), the struck thigh (Jer 31:19), the silenced mouth (Eze 16:63), lying down in shame (Jer 3:25). Soul/heart expressing through the body.

**Significance for the inner being.** This characteristic is the **conscience operating rightly** — the inner witness that registers one's own wrong before a holy God and turns the person toward restoration. It is the morally-fitting use of the shame-faculty; its absence and inversion are characteristic C-neg. Crucially, the evidence shows shame functioning not as mere damage but as a God-given hinge of repentance and a precondition of atonement.

### Internal movements (grounded)
- **C1 Penitential confession before God:** Ezr 9:6,7; Dan 9:7,8; Jer 3:25.
- **C2 Instructed/remembered conviction → turning:** Jer 31:19; Eze 16:54,61,63; 36:32; 43:10,11.
- **C3 NT admonitory (corrective, in love):** 1Cor 4:14; 6:5; 15:34; 2Th 3:14; Tit 2:8.

### Pattern notes
- **Faculty:** affect (tagged); but the verses engage conscience, memory, cognition, moral-evaluation and volition together (field tags under-record this).
- **Experiencer:** self (confession) and other-addressed (covenant address / admonition). **Valence:** sinful / commanded / righteous — the moral weight is intrinsic.
- **Divine involvement:** addressee (prayed-to), agent/commander (Eze 36:32), atoner (Eze 16:63). **Seat:** face/body expression, memory, heart-turning (verse-located, not field-tagged).
- **Boundary:** vs A — the cause is one's *own sin* (not a failed trust); vs C-neg — this is the faculty *alive and operative*, C-neg its absence/inversion; vs D — penitent self-recognition, not an imposed standing.

# M07 — Findings for Characteristic C-neg: Shamelessness (absence / inversion of the shame-faculty)
**File:** wa-m07-char-cneg-shamelessness-findings-v2_0-20260621.md · 2026-06-21 · **Supersedes v1_0**. Verse-read re-answer.
**Evidence:** 8 occ — Jer 6:15 / 8:12 (bosh + ka.lam), Jer 3:3 (ka.lam), Hos 4:18 (qa.lon), Phil 3:19 & Jude 13 (aischunē). The faculty is **dead, refused, or inverted (loved/gloried in)**.

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design
- **T0.1.1** — God is the one who **diagnoses the missing faculty**: "Were they ashamed when they committed abomination? No… they did not know how to blush" (Jer 6:15; 8:12) — a divine indictment of a self that can no longer register shame.
- **T0.1.2** — Borne by the creature; God names its loss, never bears it.
- **T0.2.1** — The role shown is the **failure-state** of shame: where it should signal abomination it is silent ("not at all ashamed").
- **T0.2.2** — Reveals the faculty as **created design** (the capacity to blush) and its loss/inversion as the **fallen** pathology — the seared conscience.
- **T0.2.3** — Silent — no future-fullness statement (the band describes ruin, not restoration).
- **T0.3.1** — Negatively instantiates the moral image: to be unable to blush (Jer 6:15) is a **marred image**, a self that has lost a God-given moral signal.
- **T0.3.2** — Creaturely pathology; not a divine attribute.
- **T0.3.3** — Its **absence** signals an image in advanced disorder — moral perception severed from moral affect.
- **T0.4.1** — Silent.

## T1 — Definition
- **T1.1.1** — The nature is **the non-functioning of shame** — its death ("did not know how to blush," Jer 6:15), its refusal ("you refuse to be ashamed," Jer 3:3), or its inversion ("they glory in their shame," Phil 3:19; "their rulers dearly love shame," Hos 4:18).
- **T1.1.2** — Carried by **negated** bosh/ka.lam (be ashamed → were not), and by qa.lon / aischunē taken as the *object loved or gloried in* — shame embraced rather than felt.
- **T1.1.3** — Constitutional: a defect/perversion of the faculty itself, not merely an outward act.
- **T1.2.1** — A **state/condition** (the faculty's deadness) more than an act.
- **T1.2.2** — Compound — it negates the affect+cognition complex of shame (Jer 6:15 tags both faculties) and, in Phil 3:19 / Hos 4:18, inverts the valuation.
- **T1.3.1** — Opposite: a **functioning** shame-faculty (chars A and C).
- **T1.3.2** — It excludes the restraining check that shame provides — "the forehead of a whore" that will not colour (Jer 3:3).
- **T1.3.3** — It ends where genuine contrition begins; its hallmark is precisely the refusal/inability to feel what char C feels.
- **T1.4.1** — Expressed as a **negation** ("were not ashamed") or an **inversion verb** ("glory in," "love").
- **T1.4.2** — Two modes: deadness (Jer) and perverse delight (Hos 4:18; Phil 3:19; Jude 13).
- **T1.4.3** — Silent.
- **T1.5.1** — The "response" is the **absence of response** — no blush, no covering, where shame would produce them.
- **T1.5.2** — Consistent absence/inversion.
- **T1.6.1** — Sustained: a settled hardness — "they did not know how to blush; **therefore** they shall fall" (Jer 6:15) — the deadened faculty issues in ruin.
- **T1.6.3** — The condition is durative (a standing incapacity), not a momentary lapse.
- **T1.7.1** — This band **is** the answer to "what does shame look like when it fails" — it is the malfunction itself.
- **T1.7.2** — Partial: the faculty is **distorted** — but the verses ascribe the distortion to the person's own hardening, not to an external spirit.
- **T1.7.3** — Yes — present-but-not-taking-hold is the essence: the occasion for shame arises (abomination) and the faculty does not engage (Jer 6:15).

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries
- **T2.1.1** — No abstract seat tagged, but the loss is registered in the **face/forehead**: "the forehead of a whore; you refuse to be ashamed" (Jer 3:3); "did not know how to blush" (Jer 6:15).
- **T2.1.2** — Located as a **conscience-level** deadness expressed in the unblushing face.
- **T2.7.1** — Body link: the **absent blush** — the somatic sign of shame that fails to appear.
- **T2.9.1** — Origin: a **self-hardening** through repeated abomination (Jer's context) — the faculty atrophies by use against it.
- **T2.9.2** — Single mechanism (hardening), with the inverted-delight variant (Phil/Hos).
- **T2.10.1** — Movement: the occasion for shame meets a faculty that **no longer moves**.

## T3 — The Inner Faculties
- **T3.1.x** — Partial: a failure of **moral perception** — they do not perceive abomination as shameful (Jer 6:15).
- **T3.2.x** — Cognition tagged (Jer 6:15) — the knowing that should accompany shame is absent ("did not **know** how to blush").
- **T3.3.x / T3.5.x** — Silent.
- **T3.4.1** — Affect is the faculty **defined by its absence/inversion** here — the proper shame-affect is missing (Jer) or perversely positive (Hos 4:18 "love," Phil 3:19 "glory").
- **T3.4.2** — Where present, the affect is **misdirected delight** in what should bring shame.
- **T3.6.1** — Volition engaged — "you **refuse** to be ashamed" (Jer 3:3) — a willed rejection of the faculty.
- **T3.6.2** — The will is set against the conscience's signal.
- **T3.8.1** — Moral evaluation is **inverted**: shame is "loved" and "gloried in" (Hos 4:18; Phil 3:19) — the moral compass reversed.
- **T3.8.2** — It calls evil good — embracing what ought to be renounced.
- **T3.9.1** — Conscience is **the** engaged faculty — here **seared/dead**: the inner witness that should accuse is silent (Jer 6:15), refused (Jer 3:3), or perverted.
- **T3.9.2** — Conscience fails to accuse — the diagnostic core of the band.
- **T3.9.3** — Engaged precisely by its non-operation.
- **T3.10.1** — Conscientiousness is **absent** — moral awareness no longer issues in restraint or action.
- **T3.11.1** — Relational capacity engaged: the shamelessness is public/covenantal — "love shame" rulers (Hos 4:18) corrupt the people; "enemies of the cross" (Phil 3:19).

## T4 — Relational Interfaces
- **T4.1.1** — God → human: God **exposes and judges** the shameless ("therefore they shall fall," Jer 6:15).
- **T4.1.2** — Basis: the response to entrenched, unrepented abomination.
- **T4.2.1** — Inverted human→God: the shameless **refuse** the contrition God seeks ("you refuse to be ashamed," Jer 3:3).
- **T4.3.1** — Person→person: shameless **rulers** propagate the corruption (Hos 4:18); the "enemies of the cross" lead others astray (Phil 3:19).
- **T4.5.2** — Within the covenant people (Judah's priests/prophets, Jer 6:13-15) and among false teachers (Phil/Jude).
- **T4.6.x** — Silent.

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension
- **T5.1.1** — A **negative formation** — the faculty is *deformed* over time, not transformed for good.
- **T5.2.1** — Sequence implied: repeated abomination → loss of the blush → falling (Jer 6:15).
- **T5.3.1** — Mechanism: **habituation to abomination** sears the conscience.
- **T5.4.1** — Set against judgment (withheld rains, Jer 3:3) that still fails to provoke shame.
- **T5.5.1** — Silent (anti-sanctification, if anything).
- **T5.6.1** — Eschatological edge at Phil 3:19 ("their **end** is destruction") and Jude 13 ("wandering stars, for whom the gloom of darkness is reserved").

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics
- **T6.1.1** — Co-occurs with abomination, whoring/idolatry, hardness ("forehead of a whore").
- **T6.3.2** — It is the **privation/inversion** of chars A and C — the same faculty, dead or loved instead of rightly felt. [flag: cross-char]
- **T6.4.1** — Shares bosh/ka.lam/qa.lon/aischunē with the felt bands but **negated or inverted**.
- **T6.5.1** — Nearest neighbour: char C (conscience-shame) — C-neg is its **failure-state**. [flag for cross-char confirmation]

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation
- **T7.1.1** — Negated bosh (BWŠ) and ka.lam (KLM); qa.lon (shame, here *loved*); aischunē (shame, here *gloried in*).
- **T7.1.2** — Negated finite verbs (Jer); plus noun-as-object-of-delight (Hos 4:18; Phil 3:19).
- **T7.1.3** — Range: not-ashamed / refuse-shame / love-shame / glory-in-shame.
- **T7.1.5** — The opposite term is functioning shame (chars A/C).
- **T7.1.8** — OT (Jer, Hos) → NT (Phil, Jude) continuity: the **seared conscience** motif carries into the apostolic warning against the shameless.
- **T7.2.1** — Functions as **indictment** — the prophetic/apostolic charge that the faculty is dead or inverted.
- **T7.2.2** — Prophecy (Jer, Hos) and **epistle** (Phil, Jude).
- **T7.2.3** — Logical structure (Jer 6:15): they were not ashamed → they did not know to blush → **therefore** they shall fall.
- **T7.2.4** — Setting: indictment of corrupt leaders / false teachers.
- **T7.2.5** — Anchor: **Jer 6:15 / 8:12** — "they did not know how to blush" — the definitive statement of the dead faculty.
- **T7.2.6** — The anchor uniquely shows shame as a faculty that can be **lost**, not only felt.
- **T7.3.1** — Lens: the clinical picture of a **blunted/absent shame signal** and moralised "shamelessness" [source: wa-m07-shame-scienceextract Sec1].
- **T7.3.2** — Illumination: science's account of shame as an adaptive social-moral signal makes the *loss* of it legible as a deficit, matching "did not know how to blush." [source: science extract]
- **T7.3.3** — Divergence: where some clinical framing treats *less* shame as healthier, the text treats the **absence** of shame as ruin (Jer 6:15). [source: science extract T7.3.3]
- **T7.3.4** — Gap: the **inverted-delight** form ("glory in their shame," Phil 3:19) is a moral-spiritual category the clinical literature does not centre. [source: science extract]

---
**Genuine Silence in C-neg (after reading): ~22 of 126** — memory (T3.3), creativity (T3.5), agency (T3.7), the human-receiving interface (T4.4), spiritual-being interfaces (T4.6), and the positive developmental/sanctification questions (T5.1 positive sense, T5.5) — because C-neg describes a **faculty in failure**, so the questions that presuppose its healthy or transformative operation are genuinely empty.

# M07 — Characteristic C-neg: Shamelessness — the absence or inversion of the shame-faculty
**File:** wa-m07-char-cneg-shamelessness-v2_0-20260621.md · 2026-06-21 · **Supersedes v1_0** (adds verse-read analysis).
**Phase:** Evidence gather + ANALYSIS (verse-read). **Occurrences:** 8 — bosh, ka.lam, qa.lon (OT); aischunē (NT).

## Analytical narrative

**What this characteristic is.** This is the **negative image of conscience-shame (characteristic C)**: the inner condition in which the shame-signal at one's own sin is **dead, refused, or inverted**. Scripture treats it not as freedom from shame but as a grave moral-spiritual defect, and attaches judgment to it.

**Three forms the verses show.**
1. **Inability — the atrophied faculty.** "Were they ashamed when they committed abomination? No, they were not at all ashamed; **they did not know how to blush**" (Jer 6:15 = 8:12). The capacity to feel shame at one's own wrong is simply gone — and the very next clause is judgment: "therefore they shall fall."
2. **Refusal — willed hardening.** "You have the **forehead of a whore**; you **refuse to be ashamed**" (Jer 3:3). Here the brazen face is the deliberate inverse of the blush — shame is not absent by accident but refused.
3. **Inversion — shame embraced and boasted.** "They **glory in their shame**, with minds set on earthly things" (Phili 3:19); "their rulers **dearly love shame**" (Hos 4:18); "casting up the **foam of their own shame**" (Jude 13). The faculty is reversed: what should produce shame produces pride.

**The face as the diagnostic.** In characteristic C true shame shows as the blush and the unliftable face; here shamelessness shows as the **brazen forehead** "of a whore" (Jer 3:3). The face is the somatic site of both the presence and the absence of shame.

**The moral company it keeps.** Shamelessness recurs with sexual immorality (za.nah — Jer 3:3; Hos 4:18) and abomination (to.e.vah — Jer 6:15; 8:12), and with a disordered mind ("their god is their belly… minds set on earthly things," Phili 3:19, co-term froneō "to reason"). It is consistently bound to judgment: "they shall fall" (Jer 6:15), "their end is destruction" (Phili 3:19), "the gloom of utter darkness reserved forever" (Jude 13).

**Significance for the inner being.** This characteristic establishes, by its absence, that the **capacity to feel shame at one's own wrong is itself a moral good** — a working conscience. Its loss (inability), its hardening (refusal), and its perversion (glorying) are three degrees of corruption of that faculty. For the programme's question this is a second-order finding about the inner being: the shame/conscience faculty can be alive (char C), or dead, refused, or inverted (char C-neg), and the latter is treated as a defining mark of the reprobate condition.

### Internal movements (grounded)
- **Cn1 Inability ("could not blush"):** Jer 6:15; Jer 8:12.
- **Cn2 Refusal (the brazen face):** Jer 3:3.
- **Cn3 Inversion (glory in / love shame):** Phili 3:19; Hos 4:18; Jude 13.

### Pattern notes
- **Faculty:** the negative space of conscience/moral-evaluation — the verses concern the *failure* of the shame-faculty, so faculty tags are sparse by nature.
- **Experiencer:** other / none (indictment voice). **Valence:** sinful (and the neutral-tagged Jer 6:15/8:12 are plainly indictments).
- **Seat:** the face/forehead (brazenness) as the inverse of the blush. **Co-terms:** abomination (to.e.vah), fornication (za.nah), disordered reasoning (froneō).
- **Boundary:** strictly the *absence/inversion* of the shame-faculty (esp. char C). Distinct from every band where shame is present and felt.

# M07 — Findings for Characteristic D: Disgrace as a borne condition / standing (imposed, deserved, or vicarious)
**File:** wa-m07-char-d-borne-disgrace-findings-v2_0-20260621.md · 2026-06-21 · **Supersedes v1_0**. Verse-read re-answer.
**Evidence:** 136 occ — the cluster's largest, most heterogeneous band: bosh, ke.lim.mah, bo.shet, qa.lon, bushah, ke.lim.mut, bosh.nah; with the disgrace pole of atimia/aischunē/entropē. It covers **disgrace one *carries*** — imposed by enemies, decreed in God's judgment, deserved by sin, or **borne innocently/vicariously**. Two sub-bands flagged: **D1 imposed-verdict**; **D8 vicarious/innocent disgrace** (Isa 50:6; Heb 12:2; Psa 69:7).

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design
- **T0.1.1** — God stands at both ends: he **decrees disgrace in judgment** ("you shall **bear your disgrace**," Eze 16:52,54) and he **removes it** ("you will **forget the shame** of your youth," Isa 54:4). The **baseline** is imageal: "the man and his wife were both naked and were **not ashamed**" (Gen 2:25) — unfallen humanity without disgrace.
- **T0.1.2** — Borne by the creature; yet at the band's apex it is **borne by the Servant / by Christ** for others (Isa 50:6; Heb 12:2) — disgrace voluntarily assumed.
- **T0.2.1** — Disgrace functions as the **marked standing** of one exposed — by sin (Ezr 9:7), by judgment (Eze 16), by enemies (Psa 69:19), or **for God's sake** (Psa 69:7).
- **T0.2.2** — Gen 2:25 shows the **created design** as shame-*less* integrity; borne disgrace is therefore a **fallen** condition — except where assumed innocently (the Servant), which redeems it.
- **T0.2.3** — Yes — the **removal** of borne disgrace is promised: "you will not be put to shame… you will forget the shame of your youth and remember the reproach of your widowhood no more" (Isa 54:4).
- **T0.3.1** — Bears on the image as **exposure of the self before others/God** — nakedness (Gen 2:25; Eze 16) is the figure of a standing laid bare.
- **T0.3.3** — Present as a **wound to standing**; its **removal** (Isa 54:4) restores the image's honour.
- **T0.4.1** — **Christological apex**: "who for the joy set before him endured the cross, **despising the shame**, and is seated at the right hand of God" (Heb 12:2); foreshadowed in the Servant who "**hid not his face from disgrace and spitting**" (Isa 50:6). Direction = OT Servant → NT Christ; disgrace borne unto vindication.

## T1 — Definition
- **T1.1.1** — The nature is **a borne condition of disgrace/dishonour** — a standing one carries, whether laid on, deserved, or assumed.
- **T1.1.2** — bosh (be in disgrace), ke.lim.mah / bo.shet / bushah / ke.lim.mut / bosh.nah (shame, disgrace, ignominy), qa.lon (dishonour); atimia/aischunē (the borne pole).
- **T1.1.3** — **Constitutional/relational** — a state of the self in its standing before others and God.
- **T1.2.1** — A **condition/standing** (state), with the **act of bearing** it (Eze 16:52 "bear your disgrace"; Heb 12:2 "despising the shame").
- **T1.2.2** — Compound — the **felt disgrace** (affect) joined to the **objective standing** of dishonour; bosh tagged affect+cognition.
- **T1.3.1** — Opposite: **honour / vindication** (char B; "instead of shame, a double portion," cf. G).
- **T1.3.2** — Excludes the secure standing of the unashamed (Gen 2:25; Isa 54:4).
- **T1.3.3** — Not the *inflicting* of disgrace (char E) nor the felt collapse of trust (char A) — the **borne standing** itself.
- **T1.4.1** — Stative ("are disgraced," "shame has covered our face") and **borne-active** ("bear your disgrace," "despising the shame").
- **T1.4.2** — Several modes: **imposed** (judgment, Eze 16; Jer), **deserved** (Ezr 9:7; Pro 13:18), **enemy-heaped** (Psa 69:19), **innocently/vicariously borne** (Isa 50:6; Heb 12:2). [D1/D8 flags]
- **T1.4.3** — Yes — addressed ("**bear** your disgrace," Eze 16:52) and confessed ("we are in great **shame**," Ezr 9:7).
- **T1.5.1** — Immediate signs: **the face covered** ("dishonour has **covered my face**," Psa 69:7; "shame has covered our face," Jer 51:51), **nakedness/exposure** (Eze 16), turning to the **lowest place** in disgrace (Luk 14:9).
- **T1.5.2** — Consistent somatic image: covered/lowered face, exposure.
- **T1.6.1** — **Durative by nature** — disgrace is a *standing* that persists ("everlasting… shall not be forgotten," Jer 20:11 of the persecutors' shame; the removal in Isa 54:4 presupposes long-borne shame).
- **T1.6.3** — Immediate exposure vs the **abiding stigma** that lingers until removed.
- **T1.7.1** — "Right" bearing appears in the **innocent/vicarious** sub-band: the Servant sets his face like flint while bearing disgrace (Isa 50:6-7); Christ **despises** (scorns) the shame (Heb 12:2).
- **T1.7.2** — Partial — the disgrace is heaped by enemies (Psa 69:19) but God overturns it.
- **T1.7.3** — In the vindicated, the threatened disgrace **does not finally hold** (Isa 50:7-8; Heb 12:2).

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries
- **T2.1.1** — Seat shown as **the face** ("dishonour has covered my face," Psa 69:7; Jer 51:51) and the **body's exposure/nakedness** (Gen 2:25; Eze 16:37; Isa 50:6 "my back… my face"); bosh's affect locates the felt component in the inner self.
- **T2.1.2** — Recorded as a **standing of the whole self** before others/God, surfacing on the face and body.
- **T2.7.1** — Strong body link: **face covered/lowered, back struck, nakedness exposed** — disgrace is the most **embodied** of the bands.
- **T2.9.1** — Origin is **plural**: laid on by God's judgment (Eze 16), incurred by sin (Ezr 9:7; Pro 18:3), heaped by enemies (Psa 69:19), or **assumed** for others (Isa 50:6).
- **T2.9.2** — **Multiple origins** — the defining heterogeneity of D.
- **T2.10.1** — Movement: disgrace **settles onto/over** the self (covering the face), or is **lifted off** (Isa 54:4), or **taken up** (Heb 12:2).

## T3 — The Inner Faculties
- **T3.1.1** — Perception: disgrace is **seen** — exposure "in the sight of the nations" (Eze 16:37,41); "all who **see** me mock me" (cf. Psa 22 context).
- **T3.2.1** — Cognition engaged (bosh tagged) — the **awareness of one's marked standing** ("you know my **reproach**… my shame and my dishonour," Psa 69:19).
- **T3.4.1** — Affect central — the **felt weight** of borne disgrace (Psa 69:7,19; Job 10:15 "filled with disgrace").
- **T3.4.2** — Produces the downcast, face-covering response; in the vicarious case, endured without flinching (Isa 50:7).
- **T3.6.1** — Volition at the apex: the Servant **chooses** not to hide his face (Isa 50:6); Christ **chooses** to despise the shame (Heb 12:2) — disgrace **willingly borne**.
- **T3.7.1** — Agency in the **bearing** ("**bear** your disgrace," Eze 16:52) — the self made to carry the standing.
- **T3.8.1** — Moral evaluation **discriminates**: disgrace **deserved** for sin (Ezr 9:7; Pro 13:18; Eze 16) vs **innocent/vicarious** (Isa 50:6; Psa 69:7 "for your sake"; Heb 12:2). The band's moral charge is **not uniform**.
- **T3.9.1** — Conscience at the deserved pole: "I am **ashamed and blush** to lift my face to you… our iniquities have risen" (Ezr 9:6-7) — borne disgrace fused with guilt (overlaps char C).
- **T3.11.1** — **Relational capacity central** — disgrace is a standing **before others and God**; "for your sake I have **borne reproach**" (Psa 69:7) makes it a Godward relation.
- **T3.3 / 3.5 / 3.10** — Silent.

## T4 — Relational Interfaces
- **T4.1.1** — God → human: God **imposes** disgrace in judgment (Eze 16; Jer 13:26) and **removes** it (Isa 54:4); he **knows** the sufferer's reproach (Psa 69:19).
- **T4.1.2** — Basis: **judicial** (against sin) and **redemptive** (the disgrace removed / borne by the Servant).
- **T4.2.1** — Human → God: disgrace **borne for God's sake** (Psa 69:7) and **confessed** before God (Ezr 9:6-7) — the disgraced self turned Godward.
- **T4.2.2** — Movement of **lament and confession** under borne disgrace.
- **T4.3.1** — Person → person: enemies/mockers **heap** disgrace (Psa 69:19; the lowest place, Luk 14:9) — though that *inflicting* is char E's focus; here it is the **standing received**.
- **T4.4.1** — Person ← person (received) is the band's centre — disgrace **suffered from** enemies, nations, accusers.
- **T4.4.2** — The honourable response: **endure** (Isa 50:7), **despise the shame** (Heb 12:2), **confess** (Ezr 9).
- **T4.5.2** — Crosses to **the nations** extensively (Moab, Egypt, Babylon, Edom in Jer/Eze) and to **corporate Israel** (Ezr 9:7; Jer 51:51).
- **T4.6.x** — Silent.

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension
- **T5.1.1** — Transformative: borne disgrace **removed/reversed** — "you will **forget** the shame of your youth" (Isa 54:4); the Servant's disgrace turns to **vindication** (Isa 50:7-8); Christ's shame to **enthronement** (Heb 12:2).
- **T5.2.1** — Sequence: sin/judgment → borne disgrace → (for the penitent/vindicated) **removal/reversal**.
- **T5.3.1** — Mechanism: disgrace **laid on** (judgment), **incurred** (sin), or **assumed** (vicarious), and **lifted** by God's salvation.
- **T5.4.1** — Operates squarely **within suffering and judgment** — exile, defeat, mockery, the cross.
- **T5.4.2** — Suffering is the very **medium** in which disgrace is borne — and, redemptively, transfigured (Heb 12:2).
- **T5.5.1** — Sanctification: bearing **reproach for God** (Psa 69:7) prefigures the disciple's bearing of Christ's reproach.
- **T5.6.1** — Eschatological: disgrace **finally removed** for God's people (Isa 54:4) and **finally fixed** on the impenitent (Jer 20:11; 23:40 long-shame motif).

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics
- **T6.1.1** — Co-occurs with **reproach** (cherpah), **nakedness/exposure**, **mocking**, **judgment**, **confession of sin**.
- **T6.2.1** — Within D, disgrace **follows** sin or assault and **precedes** either removal (penitent/vindicated) or perpetuity (impenitent).
- **T6.3.2** — D is **produced by** char E's inflicting and by God's judgment; it is **answered by** char B's vindication. [flag: cross-char]
- **T6.4.1** — Shares bosh/bo.shet/ke.lim.mah/qa.lon/atimia/aischunē with A, B, E, G.
- **T6.5.1** — Nearest neighbours: **char E** (E inflicts what D bears), **char B** (B's vindication is D's reversal), **char G** (G is the axis on which D's pole sits), and **char C** (the deserved/penitent overlap, Ezr 9). [flag for cross-char confirmation]
- **T6.5.2** — Boundary: D = the **borne standing**; E = the **act**; A/C = the **felt episode**; G = the **axis**.
- **T6.5.3** — Internally, D needs the **D1 (imposed-verdict)** vs **D8 (innocent/vicarious)** distinction — a moral, not merely degree, difference. [flag retained]

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation
- **T7.1.1** — bosh (BWŠ), bo.shet, ke.lim.mah, bushah, ke.lim.mut, bosh.nah, qa.lon; atimia, aischunē, entropē.
- **T7.1.2** — Stative verbs + abstract **disgrace-nouns** (the band is noun-heavy — disgrace as a *thing borne*).
- **T7.1.3** — Range: disgrace / dishonour / ignominy / reproach / shame-as-standing.
- **T7.1.4** — Yes — a **state/standing** emphasis (the nouns) vs the **act** of bearing (Eze 16:52; Heb 12:2).
- **T7.1.5** — Opposite term: honour/glory; vindication (char B).
- **T7.1.6** — Silent (no person-type noun).
- **T7.1.7** — Silent.
- **T7.1.8** — OT→NT: the **Servant's borne disgrace** (Isa 50:6) and the psalmist's "**reproach for your sake**" (Psa 69:7, cited of Christ in Rom 15:3; Joh 2:17 context) consummate in **Christ despising the shame** (Heb 12:2) — borne disgrace becomes the very path to glory.
- **T7.1.9** — Silent.
- **T7.1.10** — Range: disgrace as a borne standing across judgment, lament, wisdom, and the cross.
- **T7.2.1** — Functions as **lament, judgment-oracle, confession, wisdom-maxim, and gospel proclamation**.
- **T7.2.2** — **Prophecy** dominant (Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel — the bulk), **psalm** (lament), **wisdom** (Proverbs, Job), **narrative** (Gen 2:25; 1Sa 20:34), **epistle** (2Cor 11:21; Heb 12:2), **gospel** (Luk 14:9).
- **T7.2.3** — Logical structure (Ezr 9:6-7): our iniquities have mounted → therefore we are **in shame** → confessed before God. And (Heb 12:2): **despising** the shame → therefore **seated** at God's right (shame-through-to-glory).
- **T7.2.4** — Settings: exile and judgment, individual/corporate lament, the passion of the Servant/Christ.
- **T7.2.5** — Anchors: **Psa 69:7** — "for your sake I have **borne reproach**; **dishonour has covered my face**" (borne, even Godward) — paired with **Isa 50:6 / Heb 12:2** (the innocent/vicarious apex) and **Gen 2:25** (the shame-less baseline).
- **T7.2.6** — These anchors uniquely show disgrace as a **standing that can be laid on, deserved, or assumed** — and, in Christ, **borne unto glory** — the full moral range no single verse holds.
- **T7.3.1** — Lens: the **stigma / spoiled-identity** and **honour-shame** literatures (disgrace as a socially-marked, borne standing) and the **exposure/nakedness** strand [source: wa-m07-shame-scienceextract Sec2/3].
- **T7.3.2** — Illumination: clinical "stigma as a borne, durable mark" closely fits D's noun-heavy, standing-centred disgrace (Eze 16; Psa 69). [source: science extract Sec2]
- **T7.3.3** — Divergence: D's **deserved** disgrace (a just verdict on sin, Ezr 9) and its **vicarious/innocent** bearing (Isa 50:6; Heb 12:2) are moral-theological categories the descriptive stigma literature does not carry. [source: science extract T7.3.3]
- **T7.3.4** — Gap: "**despising the shame**" (Heb 12:2) — disgrace *scorned and transcended* en route to honour — has no clean clinical analogue. [source: science extract]

**Genuine Silence in D (after reading): ~14 of 126** — memory (T3.3), creativity (T3.5), conscientiousness (T3.10), spiritual-being interfaces (T4.6), and a few cross-char synthesis questions (interpret-phase). As the cluster's largest band, D answers nearly every tier directly — its only structural gaps are the faculties it never engages. Sub-band flags **D1 (imposed-verdict)** and **D8 (vicarious/innocent)** are carried to the interpret phase, not resolved here.

# M07 — Characteristic D: Disgrace as a borne condition / standing (covering); imposed or deserved
**File:** wa-m07-char-d-borne-disgrace-v2_0-20260621.md · 2026-06-21 · **Supersedes v1_0** (adds verse-read analysis).
**Phase:** Evidence gather + ANALYSIS (verse-read). **Occurrences:** 136 — the cluster's largest and most heterogeneous band: bosh (45), ke.lim.mah (27), bo.shet (22), qa.lon (14), atimia (7), ka.lam (6), cha.pher (5), bu.shah (4), aischunē (3), + bosh.nah, ke.lim.mut, qi.qa.lon (1 each).
**Prior:** wa-m07-deepread-analysis-v1-20260621.md; evidence set wa-m07-evidence-allocc-v1-20260621.json.

> **Scope note (flagged for the interpret phase).** This band gathers shame *as a borne standing* — what a person or people **wears, bears, or is sentenced to** — as distinct from the felt collapse of trust (char A) or the relational verdict on trust (char B). Reading the 136 verses, D is wide enough to contain at least two sub-structures that the interpret phase should weigh separating: **(i) the imposed judicial verdict** (shame *pronounced over* nations, idolaters, and the wicked), and **(ii) innocent/vicarious borne disgrace** (the Servant, Christ) which is the moral opposite of deserved disgrace. These are kept here, fully analysed and flagged, not pre-split.

## Analytical narrative

**What this characteristic is.** In this band shame is a **standing**, not primarily a passing feeling — a condition of dishonour that one *bears*, *wears*, or is *sentenced to*. Its grammar is telling: people are **"clothed with shame"** (Job 8:22; Psa 35:26; 109:29; 132:18), **"wrapped in their own shame as a cloak"** (Psa 109:29), with **"shame… covered my face"** (Psa 44:15; 69:7; 51:51), commanded to **"bear your disgrace"** (Eze 16:52,54; 32:24; 44:13). Shame is something put on, covering the person — and the recurring somatic locus is the **face** (covered, "on all faces," Eze 7:18; the skirts lifted so "your shame will be seen," Jer 13:26; Nah 3:5).

**Six movements the verses show.**
1. **The imposed judicial verdict** — much of bosh. In the prophetic oracle shame is *pronounced* as sentence over the nations and the wicked: Moab (Jer 48:1,20,39), Egypt (46:24), Babylon (50:2; 51:47), Damascus, the wise men (8:9), the idol-makers, "the house of Israel shall be shamed: they, their kings, their officials" (2:26). Here shame is a declared status, often with the Lord as the one who imposes or guarantees it.
2. **Borne disgrace as covering/garment** — ke.lim.mah, bo.shet, bu.shah: the cloak/covering imagery above. Shame as an enveloping condition worn visibly.
3. **The deserved disgrace of sin and idolatry** — bo.shet frequently *is* the disgrace intrinsic to the idol ("the **shameful thing** has devoured," Jer 3:24; altars "to shame," Jer 11:13; "consecrated themselves to the shameful thing," Hos 9:10; "devised shame for your house," Hab 2:10).
4. **The deserved disgrace of folly and pride (wisdom register)** — qa.lon: "When **pride** comes, then comes **disgrace**" (Pro 11:2); "the wise will inherit honour, but **fools get disgrace**" (Pro 3:35; 6:33; 13:18; 18:3). Disgrace as the lawful wage of folly, paired against honour.
5. **Corporate / national reproach borne, then removed by God** — ke.lim.mah in Ezekiel: "bear / **suffer the reproach of the nations**" (Eze 34:29; 36:6,7,15; 39:26), with God's promise to end it ("I will not let you hear anymore the reproach"). A collective standing God lifts.
6. **Dishonour as standing over against glory** — atimia: "It is **sown in dishonour**; it is raised in glory" (1Cor 15:43); vessels "for **dishonourable use**" (Rom 9:21; 2Ti 2:20); "through honour and dishonour" (2Cor 6:8). Dishonour as a quality/standing contrasted with glory (the hinge to char G).

**Two flagged specials within D.**
- **Public exposure / uncovering** as the form disgrace takes under judgment: "I myself will lift up your skirts over your face, and your **shame will be seen**" (Jer 13:26; Nah 3:5; Mic 1:11 "nakedness and shame"; Rev 3:18). Disgrace enacted as forced exposure.
- **Innocent / vicarious borne disgrace** — the moral inversion of the whole band: the Servant, "I gave my back to those who strike… I hid not my face from **disgrace** and spitting" (Isa 50:6), and Christ, "who… endured the cross, **despising the shame**" (Heb 12:2). Here disgrace is *accepted by the guiltless*, the opposite of the deserved standing elsewhere in D. [flag for interpret phase]

**Shame ordered toward repentance.** Even within this judicial band, disgrace is sometimes a means, not only a sentence: "**Fill their faces with shame, that they may seek your name**, O Lord" (Psa 83:16); and the restoration verses promise its removal ("instead of your shame there shall be a double portion," Isa 61:7 — the hinge to char G).

**Significance for the inner being.** This characteristic shows shame as the inner person's **standing of honour or dishonour before God and the community** — a status borne on the self, frequently visible on the face, that can be imposed as sentence, deserved through sin or folly, suffered corporately, or (exceptionally) accepted innocently. It engages the inner being as the bearer of public worth/standing: shame here is what the self *is reckoned to be* in the eyes of God and others, not merely what it feels.

### Internal movements (grounded)
- **D1 Imposed judicial verdict (nations / wicked):** bosh — Jer 2:26; 2:36; 8:9; 9:19; 15:9; 46:24; 48:1,20,39; 50:2,12; 51:47,51; 17:13,18; 20:11; 22:22; Eze 32:30; Mic 3:7; 7:16; Zec 10:5; Psa 6:10; 119:78; Isa 23:4; 41:11; 30:5; Hos 2:5; 4:19; Isa 1:29; chapher oracle verses.
- **D2 Borne disgrace as covering/garment:** Psa 35:26; 44:15; 69:7,19; 71:13; 109:29; 51:51; Job 8:22; Psa 132:18; Eze 7:18; Obd 10; Mic 7:10; Psa 89:45.
- **D3 Deserved disgrace of sin / idolatry (the "shameful thing"):** Jer 3:24; 7:19; 11:13; 20:18; Hos 9:10; Hab 2:10; 2Ch 32:21.
- **D4 Deserved disgrace of folly / pride (wisdom):** Pro 3:35; 6:33; 9:7; 11:2; 12:16; 13:18; 18:3; 22:10.
- **D5 Corporate reproach borne / removed by God:** Eze 16:52,54; 32:24,25,30; 34:29; 36:6,7,15; 39:26; 44:13; Jer 23:40.
- **D6 Dishonour as standing vs glory:** atimia — 1Cor 11:14; 15:43; 2Cor 6:8; 11:21; 2Ti 2:20; Rom 1:26; 9:21.
- **D7 [flag] Public exposure / uncovering:** Jer 13:26; Nah 3:5; Mic 1:11; Rev 3:18; qi.qa.lon Hab 2:16.
- **D8 [flag] Innocent / vicarious borne disgrace:** Isa 50:6; Heb 12:2.
- **D9 Shame as means to repentance / its promised removal:** Psa 83:16; Isa 29:22; 54:4; 61:7; Zep 3:11.

### Pattern notes
- **Faculty:** affect (Greek/Hebrew); the imposed-verdict bosh verses also carry cognition. **Type:** action + status — the largest concentration of *status/condition* terms in the cluster (bo.shet, ke.lim.mah, qa.lon, atimia).
- **Experiencer:** predominantly other / other-addressed (the band is about disgrace *borne by* or *pronounced over* a party). **Valence:** sinful (deserved) and neutral (declared) dominant; a few righteous (Ezr 8:22; the Servant verses).
- **Seat:** the **face** recurs as the somatic site (covered, on all faces, exposed); otherwise relational/situational. **how-field:** clothed / covered / wrapped / bear / suffer — the covering-and-bearing grammar.
- **Divine involvement:** God as the one who imposes the verdict, guarantees it, or lifts it from his people. **Co-terms:** reproach (cher.pah), dishonour, glory (the contrast pole), and the covering verbs.
- **Boundary:** D = shame as a *borne standing*. Overlaps A (idol-shame felt), B (enemy-shame = the vindication pole), E (some imposed cases shade into the agent pole), G (glory↔shame reversal), C ("bear your disgrace for your sins" sits next to conscience). Defining note: a *condition worn/borne/sentenced*, not the felt collapse (A) or the relational verdict on trust (B).

# M07 — Findings for Characteristic E: Dishonouring / despising another (agent pole) + contempt-disposition
**File:** wa-m07-char-e-agent-dishonour-findings-v2_0-20260621.md · 2026-06-21 · **Supersedes v1_0**. Verse-read re-answer.
**Evidence:** 58 occ — ka.lam (transitive humiliation), exoutheneō (despise/contempt), atimazō (dishonour), bosh (household-shaming), kataischunō, entrepō/entropē (admonitory), loidoria/kakologeō/paradeigmatizō (verbal abuse), cha.pher, qa.lah, aischunē, bo.shet. The **agent pole**: shame/contempt *inflicted on* another — exposing the heart's power to withhold or assault honour.

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design
- **T0.1.1** — The dishonour can be aimed **at God himself**: "you **dishonor me**" (Joh 8:49); "you **dishonor God** by breaking the law" (Rom 2:23) — the inner being's capacity to despise reaches even its Maker. Conversely, dishonour borne **for God** is honour: "rejoicing that they were counted worthy to **suffer dishonor for the name**" (Act 5:41).
- **T0.1.2** — Borne by the one dishonoured; **inflicted** by the agent — and God can be its object (Joh 8:49).
- **T0.2.1** — Contempt functions as the **withholding/assaulting of due honour** — a disposition that reckons another (or God) worthless.
- **T0.2.2** — Reveals a **created capacity to assign honour** (design) turned to its sinful inverse, contempt (fallen) — "let no one **despise** him" (1Cor 16:11) presupposes the duty to honour.
- **T0.3.1** — Instantiates the image's **relational-evaluative power**: to honour or despise the worth of another image-bearer (Jam 2:6, dishonouring the poor) and of God.
- **T0.3.3** — Its sinful exercise marks a **disordered image** — the heart that despises the brother (Rom 14:10) or dishonours God (Rom 2:23).
- **T0.4.1** — Typological at Act 4:11: "the stone **rejected/despised** by you, the builders" — the despised one becomes the cornerstone; God reverses the contempt of men.

## T1 — Definition
- **T1.1.1** — The nature is **the act/disposition of dishonouring or despising another** — humiliating (ka.lam), holding in contempt (exoutheneō), treating shamefully (atimazō), reviling (loidoria).
- **T1.1.2** — exoutheneō (count as nothing), atimazō (un-honour), ka.lam (humiliate/insult transitively), kataischunō (put to shame), entrepō (shame, admonitorily).
- **T1.1.3** — **Directional toward another** — the act/disposition terminates on a second party (or God).
- **T1.2.1** — Both an **act** (humiliating, reviling) and a **disposition** (contempt, scorn) — exoutheneō especially names the settled inner stance.
- **T1.2.2** — Compound: a **scornful valuation** (cognition/affect) issuing in **dishonouring action**.
- **T1.3.1** — Opposite: **honouring / esteeming** another (the entrepō "respect" pole; cf. char G).
- **T1.3.3** — Not the felt shame of the *recipient* (A/C) nor the borne standing (D) — this is the **doer's** side.
- **T1.4.1** — Transitive verbs of action; some **imperatival prohibitions** ("do not despise," Rom 14:3; 1Th 5:20; "do not reproach her," Rut 2:15).
- **T1.4.2** — Modes: sinful infliction (most), **righteous endurance** of dishonour (Act 5:41), and **loving admonition** (entrepō, 1Cor 4:14; 2Th 3:14).
- **T1.4.3** — Yes — frequently **commanded/prohibited** in direct address ("let no one despise…").
- **T1.5.1** — The agent's act produces, in the other, humiliation/being-made-low; the **disposition** shows as scorn, mockery (Luk 23:11 "treated him with contempt and **mocked**").
- **T1.5.2** — Varied by sub-movement (scorn, reviling, beating-and-shaming, admonishing).
- **T1.6.1** — Sustained: contempt as a **settled orientation** (Rom 14, the habitual despising of a brother).
- **T1.6.3** — Immediate act vs durative disposition both present.
- **T1.7.1** — "Right operation" appears only as **loving admonition** — shame deployed redemptively, "to **admonish** you as my beloved children" (1Cor 4:14).
- **T1.7.2** — Partial — the contempt is the agent's own sin, not externally induced.
- **T1.7.3** — Silent.

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries
- **T2.1.1** — No single seat tagged; contempt is a **disposition of the heart/will** (the inner stance that counts another as nothing), enacted bodily (beating, spitting — Num 12:14; Mar 12:4).
- **T2.7.1** — Body link: enacted through **the mouth** (reviling, mocking, speaking evil — loidoria, kakologeō) and **the hand** (beating, Luk 20:11).
- **T2.9.1** — Origin: arises from the **agent's own valuation** of the other as low/worthless (exoutheneō); for household-shame, from foolish/lawless conduct (Pro 17:2; 19:26).
- **T2.10.1** — Movement: **outward from the agent onto the other** (or onto God).

## T3 — The Inner Faculties
- **T3.1.1** — Perception engaged as **mis-valuation** — seeing the other as "of no account" (2Cor 10:10; 1Cor 1:28).
- **T3.2.1** — Cognition: the **reckoning** of another's worth as nil (exoutheneō = to count as nothing).
- **T3.4.1** — Affect: **scorn/disdain** (Luk 18:9 "treated others with contempt"), mockery (Luk 23:11).
- **T3.6.1** — Volition/agency strongly engaged — the band is **agentive**: one chooses to dishonour, revile, or (rightly) admonish.
- **T3.7.1** — Agency: the agent **acts upon** another — humiliating, casting reproach, holding up to public disgrace (Heb 6:6).
- **T3.8.1** — Moral evaluation central and **double-edged**: despising the brother is **forbidden** (Rom 14:10); dishonouring God is **sin** (Rom 2:23); yet admonitory shame and suffering dishonour for Christ are **righteous** (1Cor 4:14; Act 5:41).
- **T3.8.2** — It renders verdicts on conduct (the household-shamer, Pro 19:26) and is itself judged (contempt condemned).
- **T3.11.1** — **Relational capacity is the core** — the faculty by which the inner being **assigns or withholds honour** to others and to God.
- **T3.11.2** — Exhibits the relation as **honour-bearing or honour-denying** — the moral charge of how one regards another.
- **T3.9 conscience** — partial: admonitory shame (2Th 3:14 "that he may be ashamed") aims to **awaken** the other's conscience.
- **T3.3 / 3.5 / 3.10** — Silent.

## T4 — Relational Interfaces
- **T4.1.1** — God → human: God **vindicates the despised** (the rejected stone, Act 4:11) and is **dishonoured by sin** (Rom 2:23).
- **T4.2.1** — Human → God (negative): **dishonouring God** (Joh 8:49; Rom 2:23) — contempt aimed Godward.
- **T4.3.1** — **Person → person is the band's centre**: despising/dishonouring/reviling/humiliating another — brother (Rom 14:10), poor man (Jam 2:6), servant/son in parables (Mar 12:4; Luk 20:11), prophet/apostle (Gal 4:14).
- **T4.3.2** — The act **withholds or assaults** the other's honour.
- **T4.4.1** — Person ← person (received): being **despised/dishonoured** — Paul "weak… of no account" (2Cor 10:10), the apostle not scorned (Gal 4:14), the despised-yet-chosen (1Cor 1:28).
- **T4.4.2** — The honourable response to received dishonour: **rejoice** (Act 5:41), do not repay reviling for reviling (1Pe 3:9).
- **T4.5.2** — Within the church (Rom 14; 1Cor; Jam 2) and toward Christ/apostles.
- **T4.6.x** — Silent.

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension
- **T5.1.1** — Formative on the **agent's character**: habitual contempt marks the self-righteous (Luk 18:9); and the disciple is **formed by suffering dishonour** worthily (Act 5:41).
- **T5.2.1** — Sequence in the parables: servant sent → **dishonoured/beaten** → judgment (Mar 12; Luk 20).
- **T5.3.1** — Mechanism: the agent's **scornful valuation** issuing in act.
- **T5.4.1** — Operates within **persecution/suffering** — dishonour inflicted on Christ's servants (Act 5:41; Gal 4:14).
- **T5.5.1** — Sanctification: **not repaying** reviling, blessing instead (1Pe 3:9) — the redemptive handling of contempt.
- **T5.6.1** — Eschatological at Heb 6:6 — those who "**hold up to contempt**" the Son of God; and the reversal of the rejected stone (Act 4:11).

## T6 — Structural Relationships
- **T6.1.1** — Co-occurs with mocking, reviling, beating, judging (Rom 14 "pass judgment… despise"), boasting.
- **T6.3.2** — The agent pole **produces** the borne disgrace of char D and the felt shame of A/C in the recipient. [flag: cross-char]
- **T6.4.1** — Shares ka.lam/bosh/cha.pher/qa.lah/kataischunō/aischunē with A, B, C, D, G.
- **T6.5.1** — Nearest neighbours: **char D** (E inflicts what D bears) and **char G** (entrepō's respect↔shame). [flag for cross-char confirmation]
- **T6.5.2** — Boundary: E = the **doer**; D = the **borne standing**; the same event seen from opposite poles.

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation
- **T7.1.1** — ka.lam (humiliate, transitive), exoutheneō (count as nothing), atimazō (dishonour), kataischunō, entrepō/entropē, loidoria (reviling), kakologeō (speak evil), paradeigmatizō (public disgrace), cha.pher, qa.lah, aischunē, bo.shet.
- **T7.1.2** — Transitive verbs + agent-nouns; prohibitions and imperatives.
- **T7.1.3** — Range: despise / dishonour / humiliate / revile / hold-in-contempt / shame (admonitory).
- **T7.1.4** — Yes — a **disposition/act split** within the band: exoutheneō (settled contempt) vs ka.lam/atimazō (the inflicting act).
- **T7.1.5** — Opposite term: honour/esteem (timaō; the entrepō respect pole).
- **T7.1.6** — Silent (no person-type noun).
- **T7.1.8** — OT→NT continuity: the **household-shamer** of Proverbs (bosh) and the transitive ka.lam carry into the NT's developed vocabulary of contempt (exoutheneō, atimazō) — and into dishonouring/honouring **God**.
- **T7.2.1** — Functions as **prohibition, narrative report, and admonition**.
- **T7.2.2** — **Epistle** dominant (Rom, 1Cor, Gal, Jam, 1Pe), **gospel/parable** (Mar 12; Luk 20; 23), **narrative** (2Sa 10; 1Ch 19), **wisdom** (Proverbs), **prophecy** (Isa 16:14; 3:5).
- **T7.2.3** — Logical structure (Rom 2:23): you boast in the law → you break the law → therefore you **dishonour God**.
- **T7.2.4** — Settings: church-life disputes (Rom 14; 1Cor 11), persecution (Act 5; Gal 4), kingship/diplomacy (2Sa 10).
- **T7.2.5** — Anchor: **Rom 14:10** — "why do you **despise** your brother?" — contempt as a forbidden inner disposition toward another image-bearer; paired with **Joh 8:49 / Rom 2:23** for contempt aimed at God.
- **T7.2.6** — The anchor shows the **relational-evaluative faculty** at its sharpest: the heart's power to count a brother — or God — as nothing.
- **T7.3.1–.4** — Lens: psychology of **contempt** (the other-directed "moral emotion" that lowers another's status) and **humiliation** [source: wa-m07-shame-scienceextract Sec1/2]; illumination — contempt-as-status-denial maps onto exoutheneō; divergence — the text makes contempt **sin** (esp. toward God), and commends **suffering** dishonour, beyond the descriptive frame; gap — the **admonitory/redemptive** use of shame (1Cor 4:14) is not a clinical category. [source: science extract]

---
**Genuine Silence in E: ~24 of 126** — memory (T3.3), creativity (T3.5), conscientiousness (T3.10), most God-disposition detail (T4.1.3), spiritual-being interfaces (T4.6), and several cross-char synthesis questions. E answers richly across volition/agency, moral evaluation, the relational interface (person→person and the God-object), and the literary tiers.

# M07 — Characteristic E: Dishonouring / despising another (agent pole) + contempt-disposition
**File:** wa-m07-char-e-agent-dishonour-v2_0-20260621.md · 2026-06-21 · **Supersedes v1_0** (adds verse-read analysis).
**Phase:** Evidence gather + ANALYSIS (verse-read). **Occurrences:** 58 — ka.lam (15), exoutheneō (11), atimazō (7), bosh (7), entrepō (3), kataischunō (3), entropē/loidoria/cha.pher/qa.lah (2 each), aischunē/kakologeō/paradeigmatizō/bo.shet (1).

## Analytical narrative

**What this characteristic is.** This is the **agent pole** of the cluster: not the shame a person *feels* or *bears*, but the shame, dishonour, and contempt a person *inflicts on another*. Where the other bands look at the experiencer, this band looks at the **doer** — and so it exposes a disposition of the inner being, the heart that withholds or assaults another's worth.

**The movements.**
- **E1 Humiliation as injury done to another (transitive).** "**do not reproach her**" (Rut 2:15, *forbidden*); "are you not ashamed to **wrong me**?" (Job 19:3); "your neighbour **puts you to shame**" (Pro 25:8); "you have today **covered with shame the faces** of all your servants" (2Sa 19:5); "you have rejected us and **disgraced us**" (Psa 44:9). And the imprecation that dishonours enemies, "let them be put to shame and **dishonor** who seek my life" (Psa 35:4; 40:14; 69:6; 70:2).
- **E2 Contempt / despising as an inner disposition.** exoutheneō: "**despise** your brother" (Rom 14:3,10, *forbidden*); "let no one **despise** him" (1Cor 16:11); "do not **despise** prophecies" (1Th 5:20); "treated others with **contempt**" (Luk 18:9); Herod "treated him with **contempt** and mocked him" (Luk 23:11). And its receiving end — the despised/rejected one: "the stone **rejected** by the builders" (Act 4:11), "God chose what is low and **despised**" (1Cor 1:28). Contempt is a posture of the heart toward another's worth.
- **E3 Active dishonouring of another — and of God.** atimazō: "treated him **shamefully**" (Mar 12:4; Luk 20:11); "**you dishonor me**" (Joh 8:49); "**dishonor God** by breaking the law" (Rom 2:23); "**dishonored the poor**" (Jam 2:6). The inner being can dishonour even God — the essence of the offence in Rom 2:23.
- **E4 Dishonouring in worship/propriety.** kataischunō: "**dishonors his head**" (1Cor 11:4,5); "**humiliate** those who have nothing" (1Cor 11:22).
- **E5 Verbal abuse / reviling.** loidoria "**reviling** for reviling" (1Pe 3:9); kakologeō "**speaking evil** of the Way" (Act 19:9); paradeigmatizō "hold up to **public disgrace**… crucifying again the Son of God" (Heb 6:6); qa.lah "held in **contempt**" (Isa 16:14; 3:5).
- **E6 Bringing shame on one's own household (agent by conduct).** bosh: "a son who **brings shame**" (Pro 10:5; 17:2; 19:26; 29:15); "she who **brings shame** is like rottenness in his bones" (Pro 12:4); cha.pher "the wicked **brings shame and disgrace**" (Pro 13:5).
- **E7 Admonitory shame given in love (the redemptive agent — overlaps char C).** entrepō/entropē: "that he may be **ashamed**" (2Th 3:14); "I say this **to your shame**" (1Cor 6:5; 15:34); and pointedly "I do not write these things to **make you ashamed**, but to admonish you as my **beloved children**" (1Cor 4:14).

**The band is not uniformly sinful.** It spans **sinful contempt** (Rom 14; Luk 18:9), **righteous endurance of dishonour** ("counted worthy to **suffer dishonor** for the name," Act 5:41), and **loving correction** (1Cor 4:14). The moral charge is on the *disposition*: despising the brother is forbidden, dishonouring God is the heart of sin, but admonishing in love and suffering dishonour for Christ are honourable.

**Significance for the inner being.** This characteristic reveals an inner-being **interface capacity**: the heart's power to **assign or withhold honour** to others — and to God. Contempt (exoutheneō) is a settled inner orientation that reckons another worthless; dishonouring (atimazō) is its enactment. Because it can be directed at God ("you dishonor me," Joh 8:49), it is a primary site of the inner being's relation to God and neighbour, with a strong moral valence.

### Pattern notes
- **Experiencer:** other / other-addressed dominant (the act is toward another). **Valence:** sinful (contempt) dominant, with *forbidden* (Rom 14; 1Cor 16:11; 1Th 5:20; Rut 2:15) and *righteous* (Act 5:41; 2Th 3:14) present.
- **Boundary:** the *agent* of dishonour/contempt — distinct from D (the borne standing) and the felt bands (A, C). Overlaps the imprecatory verses (also char B's enemy-shame = vindication pole) and the admonitory verses (also char C). Contempt-as-disposition is the inner-being core; reviling/verbal-abuse terms (loidoria, kakologeō) sit at the band's edge.

# M07 — Findings for Characteristics F and G (verse-read re-answers)
**File:** wa-m07-char-fg-findings-v2_0-20260621.md · 2026-06-21 · **Supersedes the v1_0 findings for F and G.**

---
# F — Abasement: the bringing-low of pride (status reversal high↔low) — 22 occ (all sha.phel)
**Evidence:** sha.phel throughout — the divine lowering of the haughty, set against exaltation. **No affect/faculty tag** on any occurrence: F names a **status movement**, not a felt state. [boundary flag: M09 / "action that produces shame"]

## T0
- **T0.1.1** — God is the **sole agent** of the lowering: "he **brings low** and he exalts" (1Sa 2:7); "it is God who executes judgment, **putting down** one and lifting up another" (Psa 75:7); "the Lord alone will be exalted" (Isa 2:11,17).
- **T0.1.2** — Borne by the **proud** whom God lowers; never by God.
- **T0.2.1** — Functions as the **judicial reversal of pride** — bringing the lofty down to where the humble are raised.
- **T0.2.2** — Engages **pride** as a fallen inner orientation that God's design-order opposes ("the haughty eyes you **bring down**," Psa 18:27).
- **T0.3.1** — Bears on the image via the **posture of the heart** — haughtiness vs lowliness — that God honours or abases (Pro 29:23).
- **T0.4.1** — Eschatological/typological at Isa 2:11-17 — "the day of the Lord" against all that is proud — the final humbling before the Lord alone exalted.

## T1
- **T1.1.1** — The nature is **being brought low in status** — abasement, the lowering of height/pride.
- **T1.1.2** — sha.phel (be/become low, sink, be humbled, be abased).
- **T1.1.3** — Relational/positional — a movement **down the honour-status axis**.
- **T1.2.1** — An **action/status-change** (not an affect).
- **T1.2.2** — Simple at the lexical level (a status verb), but **morally loaded** by its object (pride).
- **T1.3.1** — Opposite: **exaltation / being lifted up** ("makes high the low tree," Eze 17:24; "obtain honour," Pro 29:23).
- **T1.3.3** — Not felt shame; the **lowering of standing** that pride incurs — bordering M09 humility. [flag]
- **T1.4.1** — Causative/passive verbs ("he abases," "is brought low").
- **T1.5.1 / T1.6.x / T1.7.x** — Silent — F describes a status outcome, not a response with somatic onset, duration, or malfunction.

## T2
- **T2.1.1** — No inner seat; the thing lowered is **height/pride** ("the **lofty pride** of men shall be brought low," Isa 2:17) — a posture, registered in "**haughty eyes/looks**" (Isa 2:11; 5:15; Psa 18:27).
- **T2.7.1** — Body image: **eyes/looks** (haughty), the high brought to the **dust** (Isa 29:4).
- **T2.9.1** — Origin: the **pride** of the one lowered occasions it; the **agent** is God.
- **T2.10.1** — Movement: **downward**, God acting on the proud (high→low).

## T3
- **T3.8.1** — **Moral evaluation** engaged: pride is **judged** and lowered; lowliness is honoured ("he saves the lowly," Job 22:29; "he who is lowly in spirit will obtain honour," Pro 29:23).
- **T3.6.1** — Volition at the human edge: pride is a **chosen self-exaltation** that God reverses (Jer 13:18 "take a lowly seat").
- **T3.11.1** — Relational — the proud are lowered **before God and others** (the honour-status order).
- **T3.1 / 3.2 / 3.3 / 3.4 / 3.5 / 3.7 / 3.9 / 3.10** — Silent — no perception/cognition/memory/affect/creativity/agency/conscience content tagged or shown; F is a status verb.

## T4
- **T4.1.1** — God → human: God **abases the proud** (Isa 2; 5; 13; Job 40:11 "abase him").
- **T4.1.2** — Basis: **judgment on pride/haughtiness**.
- **T4.2.1** — Human → God (implied imperative): **humble yourself / take the low seat** (Jer 13:18).
- **T4.5.2** — Crosses to **nations and rulers** (the king and queen mother, Jer 13:18; the proud world, Isa 13:11).
- **T4.3 / 4.4 / 4.6** — Silent.

## T5
- **T5.1.1** — Formative reversal: pride **brought low**, lowliness **lifted** — the moral order God enforces (Pro 29:23).
- **T5.4.1** — Operates within **judgment** (the day of the Lord, Isa 2:12).
- **T5.6.1** — Eschatological humbling (Isa 2:11-17).
- **T5.2 / 5.3 / 5.5** — Silent.

## T6
- **T6.1.1** — Co-occurs with **pride/haughtiness** (ga'avah, gevohim), **exalt** (the antithesis), eyes/loftiness.
- **T6.3.2** — F is the **action/status-movement** that can *produce* shame; nearest the abasement edge of char G (the honour-status axis). [flag: M09 boundary; action-vs-state]
- **T6.4.1** — sha.phel unique to this band (no lemma overlap with the felt bands).
- **T6.5.1** — Boundary with **M09 (humility)** — "lowly in spirit" (Pro 29:23) is humility language; F's M07 claim rests on its tie to pride and the honour-shame field. [flag]

## T7
- **T7.1.1** — sha.phel (ŠPL — be low, be abased).
- **T7.1.3** — Range: brought low / humbled / abased / laid low.
- **T7.1.5** — Opposite: exalted/lifted up.
- **T7.2.2** — **Prophecy** dominant (Isaiah heavily; Eze; Jer), **wisdom** (Pro 25:7; 29:23; Job), **psalm** (75:7; 147:6; 18:27), **narrative-song** (1Sa 2:7; 2Sa 22:28).
- **T7.2.3** — Logical structure (Pro 29:23): pride → brings low; lowly-in-spirit → obtains honour (antithetic).
- **T7.2.5** — Anchor: **Pro 29:23** — "One's pride will **bring him low**, but he who is lowly in spirit will obtain honour" — the inner orientation (pride) tied to the status outcome (abasement), with the M09 seam visible.
- **T7.2.6** — The anchor uniquely links **pride (inner)** to **abasement (status)** and names the humble counter-pole.
- **T7.3.1–.4** — Lens: **pride/humiliation and status** psychology [source: wa-m07-shame-scienceextract Sec2]; illumination — abasement as enforced status-loss parallels humiliation dynamics; divergence — F's agent is **God's judgment**, and the humble are **honoured**, a theological reversal; gap — F is **status, not affect**, so the clinical shame-feeling frame mostly does not engage. [source: science extract]

**Genuine Silence in F: ~55 of 126 — largely structural.** The entire affect/somatic/process register (much of T3, T1.5–1.7, T2.9 onset-detail, T5.2–5.3) is empty **because sha.phel names a status movement, not a felt inner state.** F's real content sits in T0/T3.8/T4.1/T6/T7 — divine agency, the judgment of pride, the honour-status axis, and the M09 boundary.

# G — Honour↔shame / glory↔shame reversal (relational standing) — 19 occ
**Evidence:** atimia (honour/dishonour pairing), entrepō (respect/regard pole), kataischunō (1Cor 1:27), bo.shet, ke.lim.mah, qa.lon. The **axis** on which standing moves — shame and honour/glory as exchangeable poles, reversed by God in both directions. [status flag: axis-vs-characteristic; reverence pole]

## T0
- **T0.1.1** — God is the **agent of reversal on the axis**: "I will **change their shame into praise**" (Zep 3:19); "instead of your shame… a double portion" (Isa 61:7); and downward, "I will **change their glory into shame**" (Hos 4:7). And the cross-shaped inversion: "God chose what is **weak**… to **shame the strong**" (1Cor 1:27).
- **T0.1.2** — Both poles assigned by God to creatures; God himself is the **glory** that defines the axis.
- **T0.2.1** — Shame/honour function as the **two ends of relational standing**, with movement (reversal) the key phenomenon.
- **T0.2.2** — Reveals standing as a **God-conferred** reality — vessels "for honourable" or "dishonourable use" at the potter's right (Rom 9:21).
- **T0.3.1** — The image lives on an **honour↔shame continuum**; the entrepō "respect/regard" pole is the inner posture that **confers** honour (Heb 12:9).
- **T0.4.1** — Eschatological reversals: shame→honour for the people (Isa 61:7; Zep 3:19) and glory→shame for the proud (Hos 4:7; Hab 2:16), often final.

## T1
- **T1.1.1** — The nature is **standing as a two-poled axis** (honour/glory ↔ shame/dishonour) and **movement along it**.
- **T1.1.2** — atimia (dishonour, paired with doxa/timē), entrepō (regard/reverence; or be-shamed), bo.shet/ke.lim.mah/qa.lon (shame, exchanged with glory).
- **T1.1.3** — **Relational/positional** — defined by where one stands on the honour-shame scale.
- **T1.2.1** — A **standing/quality** and its **reversal** (an event).
- **T1.2.2** — Compound — binds **shame** to its opposite **honour/glory** as matched terms.
- **T1.3.1** — Opposite pole built in: **honour/glory** (the axis contains its own antithesis).
- **T1.3.3** — More **axis than discrete state** — threads through D (the borne pole) and E (the inflicting pole). [flag]
- **T1.4.1** — Stated as **exchange** ("instead of," "turned into," "changed into") and as **regard** (entrepō "they will respect").
- **T1.5.x / T1.6.x** — Partial: the reversal is often **eschatological and enduring** ("a double portion… everlasting joy," Isa 61:7) rather than a momentary response.
- **T1.7.x** — Silent.

## T2
- **T2.1.1** — No inner seat; standing is **conferred and displayed** (vessels of honour/dishonour, Rom 9:21; 2Ti 2:20); the **face/name** carry it (honour turned to shame, Psa 4:2).
- **T2.7.1** — Body/figure: vessels, garments, "sown in dishonour, raised in glory" (1Cor 15:43, the body itself).
- **T2.9.1** — Origin: **God's conferral/reversal** of standing.
- **T2.10.1** — Movement: **along the axis**, in either direction, by God.

## T3
- **T3.8.1** — Moral evaluation: standing is reordered **morally** — the proud's glory → shame (Hos 4:7), the lowly's shame → honour (Isa 61:7).
- **T3.11.1** — **Relational capacity central** — standing **is** a relational reality; the entrepō pole is the inner act of **regarding/reverencing** another's standing (Heb 12:9 "we respected our earthly fathers"; Mat 21:37 "they will respect my son").
- **T3.4.1** — Affect at the edge: "**to my shame**, I must say" (2Cor 11:21).
- **T3.1 / 3.2 / 3.3 / 3.5 / 3.6 / 3.7 / 3.9 / 3.10** — Silent — G is about conferred standing, not a process of perception/memory/volition/conscience.

## T4
- **T4.1.1** — God → human: God **reverses standing** (Isa 61:7; Zep 3:19; Hos 4:7; 1Cor 1:27).
- **T4.2.1** — Human → God: **reverence/regard** Godward — "shall we not much more be subject to the **Father**?" (Heb 12:9) — the honour-conferring inner posture.
- **T4.3.1** — Person→person: **respect** (the vineyard-son, Mat 21:37; Mar 12:6; Luk 20:13) or its refusal ("neither feared God nor **respected man**," Luk 18:2,4).
- **T4.5.2** — Crosses to nations and the proud (Hab 2:16; Hos 4:7) and the church (vessels, 2Ti 2:20).
- **T4.6.x** — Silent.

## T5
- **T5.6.1** — Strongly eschatological: the **final exchange** of shame for glory (Isa 61:7) and glory for shame (Hab 2:16; Hos 4:7); the resurrection reversal "sown in dishonour, **raised in glory**" (1Cor 15:43).
- **T5.1.1** — Transformative reversal of standing (shame→praise, Zep 3:19).
- **T5.4.1** — Set within judgment (downward) and restoration (upward).
- **T5.2 / 5.3 / 5.5** — Silent.

## T6
- **T6.1.1** — Co-occurs with **glory/honour** (doxa, timē, kavod), **praise**, **boast**, and the shame-cluster.
- **T6.3.2 / T6.5.1** — G is best read as the **axis** underlying D (borne pole) and E (inflicting pole), and the **reverence pole** complements E's contempt. [flag: axis-vs-characteristic]
- **T6.4.1** — Shares atimia/bo.shet/ke.lim.mah/qa.lon/kataischunō/entrepō with D and E.

## T7
- **T7.1.1** — atimia (dishonour), entrepō (regard/shame), kataischunō, bo.shet, ke.lim.mah, qa.lon.
- **T7.1.4** — Note the **entrepō duality**: same root yields "be ashamed" and "regard/reverence" — shame and respect as two faces of regard for standing.
- **T7.1.5** — The contained opposite: **honour/glory** (timē/doxa/kavod).
- **T7.1.8** — OT→NT: the prophetic **shame↔glory exchange** (Isa 61:7; Hos 4:7) carries into the NT's honour/dishonour-vessel and resurrection-glory language (Rom 9:21; 1Cor 15:43).
- **T7.2.2** — **Prophecy** (Isa, Zep, Hos, Hab), **epistle** (Rom, 1-2Cor, 2Ti), **gospel/parable** (Mat 21; Mar 12; Luk 18; 20), **psalm** (4:2).
- **T7.2.3** — Logical structure: "**instead of** X (shame) — Y (honour)" / "**changed** glory **into** shame" (exchange formulae).
- **T7.2.5** — Anchor: **Isa 61:7** — "instead of your **shame** there shall be a **double portion**" — the axis and its God-wrought reversal in one line; paired with **1Cor 1:27** (the cross-shaped reversal of worldly standing).
- **T7.2.6** — The anchor shows standing as a **reversible axis** in God's hand, not a fixed state.
- **T7.3.1–.4** — Lens: **honour-shame social dynamics** (status as a relational good that can be conferred or stripped) [source: wa-m07-shame-scienceextract Sec2]; illumination — the honour/shame axis is exactly the social-anthropological model; divergence — God **reverses** the axis eschatologically and cross-shapedly (1Cor 1:27), inverting worldly honour; gap — the **reverence/regard** pole (entrepō) as a positive inner posture is under-treated in the clinical shame literature. [source: science extract]

**Genuine Silence in G: ~50 of 126 — structural.** As an **axis** rather than a felt state, G leaves the inner-process tiers (perception, memory, volition, conscience, somatic onset) empty; its dense content is in standing, reversal, divine agency, eschatology, the relational/reverence interface, and the literary tiers. [axis-vs-characteristic flag retained]

# M07 — Characteristic F: Abasement — the bringing-low of pride (status reversal high↔low)
**File:** wa-m07-char-f-abasement-pride-v2_0-20260621.md · 2026-06-21 · **Supersedes v1_0** (adds verse-read analysis).
**Phase:** Evidence gather + ANALYSIS (verse-read). **Occurrences:** 22 — all sha.phel (H8213). **No occurrence carries an affect/faculty tag.**

> **Boundary flag (for interpret phase).** sha.phel names a **positional/status movement** (high→low), not a felt shame. Its place in M07 rests on its tie to **pride** (an inner orientation) and its role in the honour-shame/abasement field; it also borders **M09 (humility/meekness)** — "he who is **lowly in spirit** will obtain honour" (Pro 29:23). Whether F is an M07 characteristic, an M09 term, or the *action that produces* shame is deferred.

## Analytical narrative

**What this characteristic is.** Across all 22 verses sha.phel is the **bringing-low of the proud** — a movement of *status*, not of feeling. It is almost always set against exaltation in a fixed reversal: "he **brings low** and he exalts" (1Sa 2:7); "it is God who executes judgment, **putting down** one and lifting up another" (Psa 75:7); "the Lord lifts up the humble; he **casts the wicked to the ground**" (Psa 147:6; cf. 2Sa 22:28 = Psa 18:27, "the haughty eyes you bring down"); "I **bring low** the high tree, and make high the low tree" (Eze 17:24; 21:26).

**Its target is pride.** The thing brought low is consistently *haughtiness*: "The **haughty looks** of man shall be brought low, and the **lofty pride** of men shall be humbled, and the Lord alone will be exalted" (Isa 2:11; cf. 2:9,12,17; 5:15; 10:33; 13:11; 25:11 "the Lord will **lay low his pompous pride**"; 26:5; 29:4; Job 40:11 "look on everyone who is proud and **abase** him"). The wisdom register states the law directly: "One's **pride** will bring him low, but he who is **lowly in spirit** will obtain honour" (Pro 29:23).

**Significance for the inner being.** F engages the inner being through the **orientation of pride** and God's judicial reversal of it. The "haughty eyes/looks" and "lofty pride" are inner postures; abasement is what God does to them. It is the status-judgment counterpart to shame: where the felt bands register shame as an experience, F registers the *lowering of standing* that pride incurs — and, conversely, the honour the lowly receive. Its strong overlap with humility marks the seam between M07 (shame/dishonour) and M09 (humility/meekness).

### Pattern notes
- **Faculty:** none tagged (status, not affect). **Type:** action/status. **Experiencer:** mostly other / other-addressed (the proud who are lowered). **Valence:** sinful (the proud), neutral (the reversal stated), righteous (the lowly exalted — Job 22:29; Pro 29:23; Isa 25:11).
- **Divine involvement:** God is the agent of the lowering throughout. **Boundary:** status-movement (high→low); borders M09; candidate "action that produces shame." Flag retained.

# M07 — Findings for Characteristics F and G (verse-read re-answers)
**File:** wa-m07-char-fg-findings-v2_0-20260621.md · 2026-06-21 · **Supersedes the v1_0 findings for F and G.**

# F — Abasement: the bringing-low of pride (status reversal high↔low) — 22 occ (all sha.phel)
**Evidence:** sha.phel throughout — the divine lowering of the haughty, set against exaltation. **No affect/faculty tag** on any occurrence: F names a **status movement**, not a felt state. [boundary flag: M09 / "action that produces shame"]

## T0
- **T0.1.1** — God is the **sole agent** of the lowering: "he **brings low** and he exalts" (1Sa 2:7); "it is God who executes judgment, **putting down** one and lifting up another" (Psa 75:7); "the Lord alone will be exalted" (Isa 2:11,17).
- **T0.1.2** — Borne by the **proud** whom God lowers; never by God.
- **T0.2.1** — Functions as the **judicial reversal of pride** — bringing the lofty down to where the humble are raised.
- **T0.2.2** — Engages **pride** as a fallen inner orientation that God's design-order opposes ("the haughty eyes you **bring down**," Psa 18:27).
- **T0.3.1** — Bears on the image via the **posture of the heart** — haughtiness vs lowliness — that God honours or abases (Pro 29:23).
- **T0.4.1** — Eschatological/typological at Isa 2:11-17 — "the day of the Lord" against all that is proud — the final humbling before the Lord alone exalted.

## T1
- **T1.1.1** — The nature is **being brought low in status** — abasement, the lowering of height/pride.
- **T1.1.2** — sha.phel (be/become low, sink, be humbled, be abased).
- **T1.1.3** — Relational/positional — a movement **down the honour-status axis**.
- **T1.2.1** — An **action/status-change** (not an affect).
- **T1.2.2** — Simple at the lexical level (a status verb), but **morally loaded** by its object (pride).
- **T1.3.1** — Opposite: **exaltation / being lifted up** ("makes high the low tree," Eze 17:24; "obtain honour," Pro 29:23).
- **T1.3.3** — Not felt shame; the **lowering of standing** that pride incurs — bordering M09 humility. [flag]
- **T1.4.1** — Causative/passive verbs ("he abases," "is brought low").
- **T1.5.1 / T1.6.x / T1.7.x** — Silent — F describes a status outcome, not a response with somatic onset, duration, or malfunction.

## T2
- **T2.1.1** — No inner seat; the thing lowered is **height/pride** ("the **lofty pride** of men shall be brought low," Isa 2:17) — a posture, registered in "**haughty eyes/looks**" (Isa 2:11; 5:15; Psa 18:27).
- **T2.7.1** — Body image: **eyes/looks** (haughty), the high brought to the **dust** (Isa 29:4).
- **T2.9.1** — Origin: the **pride** of the one lowered occasions it; the **agent** is God.
- **T2.10.1** — Movement: **downward**, God acting on the proud (high→low).

## T3
- **T3.8.1** — **Moral evaluation** engaged: pride is **judged** and lowered; lowliness is honoured ("he saves the lowly," Job 22:29; "he who is lowly in spirit will obtain honour," Pro 29:23).
- **T3.6.1** — Volition at the human edge: pride is a **chosen self-exaltation** that God reverses (Jer 13:18 "take a lowly seat").
- **T3.11.1** — Relational — the proud are lowered **before God and others** (the honour-status order).
- **T3.1 / 3.2 / 3.3 / 3.4 / 3.5 / 3.7 / 3.9 / 3.10** — Silent — no perception/cognition/memory/affect/creativity/agency/conscience content tagged or shown; F is a status verb.

## T4
- **T4.1.1** — God → human: God **abases the proud** (Isa 2; 5; 13; Job 40:11 "abase him").
- **T4.1.2** — Basis: **judgment on pride/haughtiness**.
- **T4.2.1** — Human → God (implied imperative): **humble yourself / take the low seat** (Jer 13:18).
- **T4.5.2** — Crosses to **nations and rulers** (the king and queen mother, Jer 13:18; the proud world, Isa 13:11).
- **T4.3 / 4.4 / 4.6** — Silent.

## T5
- **T5.1.1** — Formative reversal: pride **brought low**, lowliness **lifted** — the moral order God enforces (Pro 29:23).
- **T5.4.1** — Operates within **judgment** (the day of the Lord, Isa 2:12).
- **T5.6.1** — Eschatological humbling (Isa 2:11-17).
- **T5.2 / 5.3 / 5.5** — Silent.

## T6
- **T6.1.1** — Co-occurs with **pride/haughtiness** (ga'avah, gevohim), **exalt** (the antithesis), eyes/loftiness.
- **T6.3.2** — F is the **action/status-movement** that can *produce* shame; nearest the abasement edge of char G (the honour-status axis). [flag: M09 boundary; action-vs-state]
- **T6.4.1** — sha.phel unique to this band (no lemma overlap with the felt bands).
- **T6.5.1** — Boundary with **M09 (humility)** — "lowly in spirit" (Pro 29:23) is humility language; F's M07 claim rests on its tie to pride and the honour-shame field. [flag]

## T7
- **T7.1.1** — sha.phel (ŠPL — be low, be abased).
- **T7.1.3** — Range: brought low / humbled / abased / laid low.
- **T7.1.5** — Opposite: exalted/lifted up.
- **T7.2.2** — **Prophecy** dominant (Isaiah heavily; Eze; Jer), **wisdom** (Pro 25:7; 29:23; Job), **psalm** (75:7; 147:6; 18:27), **narrative-song** (1Sa 2:7; 2Sa 22:28).
- **T7.2.3** — Logical structure (Pro 29:23): pride → brings low; lowly-in-spirit → obtains honour (antithetic).
- **T7.2.5** — Anchor: **Pro 29:23** — "One's pride will **bring him low**, but he who is lowly in spirit will obtain honour" — the inner orientation (pride) tied to the status outcome (abasement), with the M09 seam visible.
- **T7.2.6** — The anchor uniquely links **pride (inner)** to **abasement (status)** and names the humble counter-pole.
- **T7.3.1–.4** — Lens: **pride/humiliation and status** psychology [source: wa-m07-shame-scienceextract Sec2]; illumination — abasement as enforced status-loss parallels humiliation dynamics; divergence — F's agent is **God's judgment**, and the humble are **honoured**, a theological reversal; gap — F is **status, not affect**, so the clinical shame-feeling frame mostly does not engage. [source: science extract]

**Genuine Silence in F: ~55 of 126 — largely structural.** The entire affect/somatic/process register (much of T3, T1.5–1.7, T2.9 onset-detail, T5.2–5.3) is empty **because sha.phel names a status movement, not a felt inner state.** F's real content sits in T0/T3.8/T4.1/T6/T7 — divine agency, the judgment of pride, the honour-status axis, and the M09 boundary.
