## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**T0.1.1** — Relation to God: God is the **bearer** of jealousy — "the LORD your God is a jealous God" (Exo 20:5; Deu 4:24; 6:15; possessor/agent), the **object** of jealousy provoked ("they moved him to jealousy," Deu 32:16,21; Psa 78:58), and the one **for whom** human zeal is exercised (Num 25:11 "jealous with my jealousy"; 1Ki 19:10). All three relations occur.

**T0.1.2** — Across C4 the characteristic is **borne by God himself** (Exo 34:14; Isa 42:13 "he stirs up his zeal/jealousy") and by the creature (Gen 30:1; Num 25:11). *Interpretation:* jealousy/zeal is a **shared** characteristic — supremely a divine covenant-attribute that the creature bears both rightly (zeal, Num 25:11) and wrongly (envy, Gen 30:1).

**T0.2.1** — Stated purpose/effect: divine jealousy **accomplishes** salvation/judgment — "the zeal of the LORD of hosts will do this" (Isa 9:7; 37:32); Phinehas' jealousy **turns away wrath and makes atonement** (Num 25:11,13). Human envy, by contrast, **rots/consumes** (Pro 14:30 "envy makes the bones rot"; Job 5:2 context). Record none where unstated.

**T0.2.2** — Both: **zeal and divine jealousy** belong to created/holy design (Num 25:11; Isa 9:7), while **envy** belongs to the fallen condition (Gen 30:1; 37:11; Pro 14:30; Ecc 4:4 "all toil... comes from envy"). The same root spans the right and the disordered forms.

**T0.2.3** — Future-fullness orientation: yes — "the zeal of the LORD of hosts will do this" establishes a **future accomplishment** (Isa 9:7 the messianic kingdom; 37:32 the remnant). Divine jealousy is oriented to covenant consummation. Human envy has no such orientation. Record where present.

**T0.3.1** — Divine-likeness aspect: the aspect instantiated in the person is **covenant-protective ardour / zeal for God's honour** (Num 25:11; Psa 69:9; 1Ki 19:10) — a true image of God's jealousy; envy is the **counterfeit** that images nothing of God.

**T0.3.2** — Shared: jealousy/zeal is borne by both God and the person under the same root (qinˈah/qaˈna). It is **primarily a divine attribute** that the creature reflects (rightly as zeal, wrongly as envy).

**T0.3.3** — Where right jealousy/zeal is present it indicates **covenant loyalty** (Phinehas, Num 25:11–13; Elijah, 1Ki 19:10); where envy is present it indicates a **disordered, rotting inner state** (Pro 14:30); where divine jealousy rests against a person it indicates they have **violated the covenant** (Deu 29:20 "the anger and jealousy of the LORD will smoke against that man").

**T0.4.1** — Typological use: yes — "the zeal of the LORD of hosts will do this" (Isa 9:7) functions **messianically/eschatologically**, the divine instance establishing the pattern of God's saving zeal. Direction: divine instance outward. Elsewhere narrative/wisdom, no typology.

---

## T1 — Definition

**T1.1.1** — Programme name: **Jealousy / zeal**. The name signals a **passionate, possessive ardour** over what is one's own or one's due; essential nature is intense protective/competitive heat. Senses cluster as jealousy/zeal/envy.

**T1.1.2** — Primary terms: qinˈah (noun, "jealousy/zeal/ardour") and qaˈna (verb, "to be jealous / envy / be zealous"); the adjective qanˈna/qanˈno ("jealous"), used only of God. The root carries **ardour to the point of heat** — "jealousy is fierce as the grave... a most vehement flame" (Song 8:6).

**T1.1.3** — Directional/relational: jealousy/zeal is inherently **toward** something valued — *for* God/His house (Psa 69:9), *over* a spouse (Num 5:14), *against* a rival (Gen 30:1). It presupposes a valued bond or possession and a perceived threat to it.

**T1.2.1** — Mixed: a **status/condition** (noun qinˈah, 40 occurrences — "jealousy," Pro 27:4), an **act** (verb qaˈna, 29 — "envied," Gen 30:1), and a **quality** (adjective qanˈna, 8 — "jealous God," Exo 20:5). It is borne as a state, exercised as an act, and predicated as an attribute.

**T1.2.2** — **Compound** — jealousy fuses with **anger/wrath** (Pro 27:4 "wrath... anger... but who can stand before jealousy?"; Deu 29:20 "anger and jealousy"; Zep 1:18 "fire of his jealousy"), and at the negative pole with **envy/covetousness** (Ecc 4:4; Pro 14:30). It is rarely simple — it carries an anger or envy element.

**T1.3.1** — Structural opposite: **security/contentment** (the absence of perceived threat) — implied where envy is contrasted with a "tranquil heart" ("a tranquil heart gives life... but envy makes the bones rot," Pro 14:30). Contentment stands against envy; **indifference** stands against zeal.

**T1.3.2** — At its edge it excludes **contentment and trust**: envy resists a tranquil heart (Pro 14:30); divine jealousy excludes **rival worship** ("you shall worship no other god, for the LORD... is a jealous God," Exo 34:14).

**T1.3.3** — It ends where **simple anger** begins (jealousy is anger *over a threatened bond*, Pro 27:4 distinguishes them) and where **covetousness** begins (envy shades into coveting what another has, Ecc 4:4). Divine jealousy is not envy — it is rightful covenant-protectiveness.

**T1.4.1** — Modes: as a **possessive attribute** (qanˈna "jealous God," Exo 20:5); as a **kindled act** ("envied," Gen 30:1); as a **consuming fire** ("the fire of his jealousy," Zep 1:18; "consumed by my jealousy," Eze 36:5); as a **spirit that comes over** a person ("the spirit of jealousy comes over him," Num 5:14). Grammatically piel/qal verbs and an adjective.

**T1.4.2** — Yes — mode varies by direction and level: **divine** jealousy as consuming covenant-fire (Zep 1:18); **zealous** ardour acting for God (Isa 9:7 "will do this"); **human** envy as an inward rot (Pro 14:30); the **marital** "spirit of jealousy" rising over a husband (Num 5:14). Same root, distinct modes.

**T1.4.3** — Communicative/spoken mode: yes — God **declares** his jealousy ("I have spoken in my jealous wrath," Eze 36:5–6; Zec 1:14 "I am jealous for Jerusalem... with great jealousy," spoken oracle). Recorded; elsewhere none.

**T1.5.1** — Immediate response following jealousy: it issues in **action** — Phinehas' jealousy → he acts to stay the plague (Num 25:7–8,11); Rachel's envy → "Give me children, or I shall die!" (Gen 30:1); divine jealousy → judgment declared (Eze 36:5–6). Record none where unstated.

**T1.5.2** — Varied: the immediate response ranges from zealous decisive action (Num 25:7–8) to desperate demand (Gen 30:1) to consuming judgment (Zep 1:18). No single response.

**T1.6.1** — Sustained effect: right jealousy/zeal **establishes covenant outcomes** — Phinehas' jealousy secures "a covenant of perpetual priesthood" (Num 25:13); divine zeal "will do this" lastingly (Isa 9:7). Envy's sustained effect is **bodily/inner decay** ("rots the bones," Pro 14:30). Record none where unstated.

**T1.6.3** — Immediate response is the act/flash (Num 25:7–8; Gen 30:1); sustained effect is the **established covenant/decay** (perpetual priesthood, Num 25:13; rotted bones, Pro 14:30). Episode vs enduring result.

**T1.7.1** — It "takes hold rightly" where there is a **genuine threat to a rightful bond** — God's covenant honour (Num 25:11; Exo 34:14), a husband's exclusive marriage (Num 5:14), God's house (Psa 69:9). The condition is a valued, rightful relation under threat.

**T1.7.2** — It is **distorted** where the threatened "possession" is not rightfully one's own or the response is rivalrous resentment — envy of a sibling's children (Gen 30:1), of a brother's favour (Gen 37:11), of the wicked's prosperity (Psa 73:3; Pro 23:17 "let not your heart envy sinners"). No verse attributes the jealousy to another spirit (the "spirit of jealousy," Num 5:14, is a disposition that "comes over," not an external being) — **silent** on adversarial origin.

**T1.7.3** — Where envy is present and unmastered, the person is shown **inwardly decaying and self-destructive** ("envy makes the bones rot," Pro 14:30; "a fool... envy slays the simple," Job 5:2 context) — and counselled away ("let not your heart envy sinners," Pro 23:17).

---

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**T2.1.1** — Locations: **soul/nephesh** (1Ki 19:10,14 Elijah "I have been very jealous for the LORD," lit. of the soul's ardour); **heart** (Pro 23:17 "let not your heart envy"; Song 8:6 "jealousy... set me as a seal upon your heart"); **heart|flesh** (Pro 14:30 envy reaching the bones/flesh); **inward parts** (Isa 63:15 "the stirring of your inner parts and your compassion / zeal"); **heart|soul** (Eze 36:5). 70/77 occurrences locate no seat — record none (Gen 30:1).

**T2.1.2** — The pattern: where located, jealousy/zeal is seated in the **heart and soul** (the deep affective-volitional centre) and is uniquely shown reaching the **body** — "rots the bones" (Pro 14:30). It is a deep-seated, even somatically-felt ardour; the body link is **expressive/indicative** (envy's bodily corrosion).

**T2.10.1** — Movement: the **marital** form moves **onto the person from outside the will** — "the spirit of jealousy comes over him" (Num 5:14,30), an external-feeling onset; divine jealousy moves **from God onto** the covenant-breaker (Deu 29:20). Envy is generated **within** at the sight of another (Gen 30:1). No angelic introduction is named. Record the onsets shown.

**T2.7.1** — Body direction: where a body link exists it runs **soul/heart expressing into the body** — envy "rots the bones / makes the flesh waste" (Pro 14:30), the inner ardour felt in the "inward parts" (Isa 63:15). Inner-to-body. No body-to-soul feedback shown — **silent** on that direction.

**T2.9.1** — Origin: **generated within the person** at the sight of a rival (Gen 30:1 "Rachel envied her sister"; Ecc 4:4 from comparison; Pro 23:17); **borne by God** intrinsically (Exo 20:5); and, in the marital case, arising as a **"spirit" that comes over** the husband (Num 5:14). Multiple origins.

**T2.9.2** — Origin is **multiple** and context-dependent: within-person comparison (Gen 30:1), intrinsic to God (Exo 34:14), and the onset-"spirit" of the marriage law (Num 5:14). It changes with context.

---

## T3 — The Inner Faculties

**T3.1.1** — Perception: jealousy/envy is **triggered by sight** — "Rachel saw that she bore no children... and envied" (Gen 30:1); the comparison arises from "seeing a neighbour's skill" (Ecc 4:4) and "seeing sinners" (Pro 23:17). Perception is the gate.

**T3.1.2** — Effect on perception: envy **fixes the gaze** on the rival/the wicked's prosperity (Psa 73:3 "I was envious... when I saw the prosperity of the wicked") — distorting perception until corrected "in the sanctuary" (Psa 73:17). Recorded.

**T3.1.3** — Pattern: jealousy/envy is **perception-driven** — it arises from and skews what is seen (the rival, the prosperity), confirming its comparative, relational nature.

**T3.2.1** — Cognition: engaged as the **appraisal of threat/comparison** (Psa 73:3 the reasoning about the wicked's prosperity; the "jealous God" of moral evaluation, Exo 20:5; Deu 4:24, faculty moral_evaluation).

**T3.2.2** — Effect on cognition: envy **troubles and embitters** thought until reframed (Psa 73:2–3,16–17 "it was a wearisome task... until I went into the sanctuary"); right zeal **clarifies** purpose (Num 25:11–13). 

**T3.2.3** — Pattern: jealousy/zeal is **appraisal-bound** — it both rests on a cognitive comparison and reshapes judgment (distorted by envy, clarified by zeal).

**T3.3.1** — Memory: thin — zeal is tied to **remembered covenant** (Elijah's "they have forsaken your covenant," 1Ki 19:10,14) and divine jealousy to remembered idolatry (Psa 78:58 context). Direct memory-faculty engagement is limited. Mostly **silent**.

**T3.3.2** — **Silent** on jealousy acting on a memory faculty.

**T3.3.3** — The thinness indicates jealousy/zeal is framed as **present, perception-triggered ardour**, with covenant memory as backdrop rather than mechanism.

**T3.4.1** — Affect: the core faculty (70/77 affect) — jealousy/envy/zeal is first an **intense feeling** (Gen 30:1; Pro 27:4 "who can stand before jealousy?"; Song 8:6 "vehement flame").

**T3.4.2** — Effect on affect: it is among the **most intense** affects — "fierce as the grave" (Song 8:6), unbearable ("more than wrath or anger," Pro 27:4), and consuming ("the fire of his jealousy," Zep 1:18). It overwhelms the affective field.

**T3.4.3** — That affect dominates, with the highest intensity language in the cluster (Song 8:6; Pro 27:4), confirms jealousy/zeal as a **peak-intensity emotion**.

**T3.5.1** — Creativity: not engaged. **Silent.**

**T3.5.2** — **Silent.**

**T3.5.3** — Absence indicates no relation to the originative faculty.

**T3.6.1** — Volition: engaged where jealousy **drives decisive choice** (Phinehas chooses to act, Num 25:7–8,11; Elijah's zealous resolve, 1Ki 19:10) and where envy is **commanded against** ("let not your heart envy sinners," Pro 23:17; "fret not... do not be envious," Psa 37:1).

**T3.6.2** — Effect on volition: right zeal **mobilises** the will for God (Num 25:11); envy **disorders** it toward rivalry and discontent (Gen 30:1; Ecc 4:4). It strongly engages the will at both poles.

**T3.6.3** — Pattern: jealousy/zeal is a **powerfully volitional** characteristic — it propels action (zeal) and must be governed (envy), repeatedly placed under command (Pro 23:17; Psa 37:1).

**T3.7.1** — Agency: jealousy/zeal is intensely **action-issuing** — Phinehas acts (Num 25:7–8); the LORD's zeal "will do this" (Isa 9:7; 37:32); divine jealousy executes judgment (Eze 36:5–6; Zep 1:18).

**T3.7.2** — Effect on agency: right zeal **produces atoning/saving action** (Num 25:13; Isa 9:7); envy **produces rivalrous harm** (the brothers' envy → selling Joseph, Gen 37:11 → 37:28). It is a strong motor of action.

**T3.7.3** — The jealousy→act pattern marks it as **highly agency-generating**, for good (zeal) or ill (envy).

**T3.8.1** — Moral evaluation: directly engaged — God's jealousy *is* a moral attribute defending exclusive worship (Exo 20:5; 34:14; Deu 4:24, faculty moral_evaluation); envy is morally condemned ("let not your heart envy," Pro 23:17); zeal is morally commended (Num 25:11,13).

**T3.8.2** — Effect: it **expresses and enacts** a moral verdict — God's jealousy condemns idolatry (Exo 34:14); the wise condemn envy (Pro 14:30; 23:17). 

**T3.8.3** — Pattern: jealousy/zeal is **morally tri-valued** — righteous (divine jealousy, zeal), sinful (envy), and a regulated marital safeguard (Num 5). Its morality depends on the rightness of the threatened bond and the response.

**T3.9.1** — Conscience: thin — the marital "spirit of jealousy" ordeal (Num 5:14–30) engages a quasi-juridical inner suspicion, but the acute witness of guilt is not the faculty in view. Mostly **silent**.

**T3.9.2** — **Silent** on jealousy operating on conscience as such.

**T3.9.3** — The thinness indicates jealousy/zeal is primarily an **affective-relational** characteristic, not a faculty of self-conviction.

**T3.10.1** — Conscientiousness: engaged where zeal is the **integrated moral-volitional-active** defence of the covenant (Phinehas, Num 25:11 perceives, resolves, acts; Elijah, 1Ki 19:10) and where envy must be integrally **resisted** (Pro 23:17; Psa 37:1).

**T3.10.2** — Effect: right zeal **secures** covenant good (Num 25:13); unmastered envy **corrodes** the whole person (Pro 14:30).

**T3.10.3** — The pattern marks jealousy/zeal as a **test-site of integrated moral character** — rightly directed it is exemplary virtue (Num 25:11), wrongly directed it is corrosive vice.

**T3.11.1** — Relational capacity: jealousy/zeal is **constitutively relational** — over a bond (marriage, Num 5:14; God's covenant, Exo 34:14) or against a rival (Gen 30:1; 37:11). It cannot exist without a relationship and a third party/threat.

**T3.11.2** — Effect on relational capacity: envy **fractures** bonds (the brothers sell Joseph, Gen 37:11,28; Rachel's strife with Leah, Gen 30:1); right jealousy **guards** them (the marriage, Num 5; the covenant, Exo 34:14). It both protects and ruptures, by pole.

**T3.11.3** — The strongly relational pattern shows jealousy/zeal is **inherently social** — the science extract's point that it "cannot arise in isolation" matches the evidence (always a bond and a threat, Gen 30:1; Num 5:14).

---

## T4 — Relational Interfaces

**T4.1.1** — God-toward-human: yes — God's jealousy operates from God toward the person, **for** them (jealous *for* Jerusalem/Zion, Zec 1:14; 8:2; Joe 2:18 "the LORD became jealous for his land") and **against** them in covenant breach (Deu 29:20; Eze 36:5–6).

**T4.1.2** — Basis: **covenantal** — God's jealousy is grounded in the exclusive covenant ("you shall have no other gods... for I the LORD your God am a jealous God," Exo 20:3–5; 34:14). It is responsive to covenant fidelity/breach.

**T4.1.3** — What it shows of God's disposition: God is **passionately committed** to His people — His jealousy is the measure of His covenant love (jealous *for* Zion, Zec 1:14; Joe 2:18), and of His refusal to share their worship (Exo 34:14).

**T4.2.1** — Human-to-God: yes — the person's **zeal for God** moves toward God ("I have been very jealous for the LORD," 1Ki 19:10,14; "zeal for your house has consumed me," Psa 69:9; Phinehas "jealous with my jealousy," Num 25:11). And the person can **provoke God to jealousy** (Deu 32:16,21 — overlaps C3).

**T4.2.2** — Inner posture: zeal for God requires **wholehearted covenant loyalty and indignation at His dishonour** (1Ki 19:10; Psa 69:9). Provoking-to-jealousy reveals the opposite — covenant betrayal (Deu 32:21).

**T4.2.3** — What it shows: right zeal shows a person **identified with God's honour** (Num 25:11; Psa 69:9); envy of the wicked, corrected in God's presence, shows the relationship **restoring right perception** (Psa 73:17).

**T4.3.1** — Person-to-person extension: yes (negatively) — envy is "extended" toward another as **rivalrous resentment** (Rachel toward Leah, Gen 30:1; brothers toward Joseph, Gen 37:11; envy of neighbour's skill, Ecc 4:4).

**T4.3.2** — Inner conditions accompanying it: **comparison and perceived disadvantage** (Gen 30:1 the barren sister; Ecc 4:4; Psa 73:3). Right jealousy in the marital case accompanies **rightful exclusive claim** (Num 5:14).

**T4.3.3** — What the giver must have: envy requires only a **valued, threatened or coveted** good (Gen 30:1); the evidence states no virtue the envier must first have. Record none for a precondition of envy.

**T4.4.1** — Receiving: the object of envy **receives harm** — Joseph is sold by his envious brothers (Gen 37:11,28); the object of marital jealousy undergoes the ordeal (Num 5:15–28). Uptake is endured consequence, not adoption.

**T4.4.2** — Conditions of uptake: the envied party's **favour/prosperity** is what draws it (Joseph's favour, Gen 37:11; the wicked's prosperity, Psa 73:3). 

**T4.4.3** — The person who is the object of envy is shown **endangered** (Joseph, Gen 37:11→28) — the inner-being state of the *envier*, by contrast, is the rotting one (Pro 14:30).

**T4.5.1** — Within bonds vs across distance: jealousy/zeal operates **within close bonds** (siblings, Gen 30:1; 37:11; marriage, Num 5:14; God's covenant, Exo 34:14) and across rivalry (envy of strangers' prosperity, Psa 73:3). Both.

**T4.5.2** — Covenantal scope: divine jealousy is **covenant-grounded** (Exo 34:14) yet reaches the nations in judgment (Zep 3:8 "all the earth shall be consumed in the fire of my jealousy"). Human envy crosses any line. Both.

**T4.5.3** — Relational scope: **wide** — God (Exo 20:5), spouse (Num 5:14), siblings (Gen 30:1; 37:11), the wicked/strangers (Psa 73:3), the nations (Zep 3:8). Jealousy/zeal reaches across the relational field, always over a valued stake.

**T4.6.1** — Spiritual beings: not shown operating toward angelic/adversarial beings (the rival objects of divine jealousy are **idols/"other gods,"** Exo 34:14; Deu 32:16,21 — false gods as the rival, Deu 32:17 "demons"). Recorded: idolatry as the rival drawing divine jealousy involves false-god objects; otherwise **silent** on angelic interface.

**T4.6.2** — Adversarial site: not evidenced as a site of adversarial weaponising. **Silent** (recorded as not evidenced).

**T4.6.3** — Angelic mediation: not evidenced. **Silent.**

---

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

**T5.1.1** — Transformation: right jealousy/zeal **transforms condition** — Phinehas' jealousy turns a plague and establishes a covenant (Num 25:11–13); envy transforms the person toward **decay** (Pro 14:30) and the envied toward harm (Gen 37:28). Record none where unstated.

**T5.1.2** — Reversible/irreversible: envy is shown **correctable** — Asaph's envy of the wicked is reversed "in the sanctuary" (Psa 73:3,17); the wise are counselled out of it (Pro 23:17). Divine jealousy's judgment, once executed, stands (Zep 3:8). Both, by pole.

**T5.2.1** — Sequence: **seeing → envy → harmful act** (Gen 30:1; 37:11→28) and **covenant threat → zeal → atoning action** (Num 25:6–13). For envy corrected: **envy → near-stumbling → reframing in God's presence → restored footing** (Psa 73:2–3,16–17,28). Record none where no sequence appears.

**T5.3.1** — Mechanism of change: **encounter/reframing** corrects envy (the sanctuary, Psa 73:17); **decisive zealous act** effects covenant change (Num 25:11–13). Record none where unstated.

**T5.3.2** — Differs: envy is changed by **reappraisal/encounter** (Psa 73:17), zeal effects change by **action** (Num 25:13). Context-dependent.

**T5.4.1** — Relation to suffering: envy **produces inner suffering** (the rotting bones, Pro 14:30; Asaph's "wearisome task," Psa 73:16) and arises amid the suffering of perceived disadvantage (Gen 30:1 barrenness; Psa 73:3 the contrast of the afflicted righteous and prospering wicked). Right zeal arises amid covenant affliction (Elijah's despair, 1Ki 19:10).

**T5.4.2** — What suffering does to it: the suffering of envy, brought into God's presence, is **dissolved/reframed** (Psa 73:17,28); the affliction of covenant betrayal **stirs** God's jealousy for His people (Joe 2:18). Suffering can both feed envy and, redirected, end it.

**T5.5.1** — Sanctification arc: jealousy/zeal participates — the formed person **puts away envy** ("let not your heart envy sinners, but continue in the fear of the LORD," Pro 23:17) and grows in **rightly-directed zeal** for God (Psa 69:9; Num 25:11 as exemplar). It is a long-term work of redirecting ardour from rivalry to covenant loyalty.

**T5.6.1** — Eschatological orientation: yes — "the zeal of the LORD of hosts will do this" (Isa 9:7; 37:32) orients divine jealousy/zeal toward the **consummated kingdom/remnant**; "all the earth consumed in the fire of my jealousy" (Zep 3:8) toward final judgment. Present zeal anticipates that accomplishment.

---

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics

**T6.1.1** — Co-occurring characteristics: **anger/wrath** (Pro 27:4 jealousy beside wrath/anger; Deu 29:20 "anger and jealousy"; Zep 1:18 "fire of his jealousy" = wrath), **provocation** ("provoked him to jealousy," Deu 32:16,21 — C3), **love** (Song 8:6 jealousy beside love "strong as death"), and **envy/covetousness** at the negative pole (Ecc 4:4). Strong pairing with anger and provocation.

**T6.1.2** — Co-occurrence places C4 **adjacent to and fused with divine wrath** (Zep 1:18) and as the **affect that provocation arouses** (Deu 32:21), while at the human pole it sits beside love (Song 8:6) and envy.

**T6.2.1** — Sequence: jealousy is **aroused by provocation** ("provoked him to jealousy," Deu 32:16,21) and **precedes wrath/action** (Deu 29:20 jealousy → smoking anger; Num 25:11 jealousy → atoning act). 

**T6.2.2** — The relationship is **causal**: provocation causes jealousy; jealousy causes wrath/action (Deu 32:16,21; Num 25:11). Causal chain.

**T6.3.1** — Produces: jealousy **produces** wrath/judgment (Deu 29:20; Zep 1:18), atoning/saving action (Num 25:13; Isa 9:7), and, as envy, inner decay and interpersonal harm (Pro 14:30; Gen 37:28). 

**T6.3.2** — Produced by: jealousy is **produced by** provocation (C3; Deu 32:21), by perceived threat/comparison (Gen 30:1; Psa 73:3), and by covenant betrayal (Exo 34:14).

**T6.3.3** — Constituent relation: divine jealousy and divine wrath **interpenetrate** — "the fire of his jealousy" *is* a wrathful consuming (Zep 1:18; 3:8); jealousy is thus a constituent of the divine-wrath response (cf. C2 T6.3.3).

**T6.4.1** — Shared vocabulary: qinˈah/qaˈna is **distinct** from the anger-lemmas (it has its own root) but is repeatedly **collocated** with cheˈmah/chaˈron/aph (Pro 27:4; Deu 29:20; Zep 1:18) — shared collocation, not shared lemma.

**T6.4.2** — Root-level: the qnˈ root generates qinˈah/qaˈna/qanˈna across the jealousy/zeal/envy senses; it does **not** share a root with the burning-anger family — the connection is collocational and conceptual, not etymological.

**T6.4.3** — The vocabulary picture shows C4 is a **distinct affect** (its own root) that **fuses with** anger/wrath in operation (especially in God) — explaining why it sits in the anger cluster (DEC-4 retained it) yet remains lexically its own.

**T6.5.1** — Nearest neighbour: **C2 divine wrath** (they fuse in God — "fire of his jealousy," Zep 1:18) and **C3 provocation** (jealousy is what provocation arouses, Deu 32:21). The distinction from wrath: jealousy adds the **relational-possessive** note (over a *valued bond*), which bare wrath lacks.

**T6.5.2** — Apparent overlap: in Zep 1:18 / Deu 29:20 wrath and jealousy run together; the **precise boundary** is the *object* — jealousy is anger specifically **over a threatened exclusive bond** (covenant, marriage), whereas wrath is the broader judicial heat. The marital "spirit of jealousy" (Num 5) marks jealousy's distinct relational-possessive core.

**T6.5.3** — Distinction from C2 is of **kind/relational-object** (possessive ardour over a bond vs judicial heat), not of vocabulary-root; from envy-as-vice it is one of **direction/rightness** (zeal for the rightful vs resentment of the rival).

---

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**T7.1.1** — Primary terms/roots: **qinˈah** (noun) and **qaˈna** (verb), from a root meaning "to be intensely red/ardent" — ardour, zeal, jealousy, envy; the adjective **qanˈna/qanˈno** ("jealous"), reserved for God. The root meaning centres on **burning ardour over what is one's own/one's due**.

**T7.1.2** — Grammatical range: **noun/status** (qinˈah, 40 — "jealousy," Pro 27:4), **verb/action** (qaˈna, 29 — "envied/was jealous," Gen 30:1), **adjective/quality** (qanˈna, used only of God, Exo 20:5). The range shows jealousy as a **state, an act, and a divine attribute**.

**T7.1.3** — Semantic range: a single root spans **zeal** (Num 25:11; Psa 69:9), **(righteous) jealousy** (Exo 34:14; Num 5:14), and **envy** (Gen 30:1; Ecc 4:4; Pro 14:30). Breadth: passionate devotion → protective jealousy → rivalrous envy — the positive and negative held in one word.

**T7.1.4** — Distinguishing terms: the **same root** carries disposition (qanˈna "jealous," an attribute) and act (qaˈna "envied"); condition (qinˈah "jealousy") and quality (qanˈna). The notable feature is that **zeal, jealousy, and envy are not lexically separated** — context, not vocabulary, distinguishes them.

**T7.1.5** — Opposite/absence term: no single antonym lexeme; the contrast is carried by **"a tranquil heart"** (Pro 14:30) for envy and by **indifference/lukewarmness** for zeal (cf. zestos "hot" vs its opposite elsewhere). Idiomatic.

**T7.1.6** — Person-type term: the adjective **qanˈna "jealous"** functions as a fixed attribute of God ("a jealous God," Exo 20:5; 34:14) — a quality-term, used of God rather than a human person-type. Record: a divine-attribute adjective, not a human person-type noun.

**T7.1.7** — Supplication/seeking term: none — there is no term for seeking jealousy/zeal from another. Record none.

**T7.1.8** — OT→NT relationship: C4's data is **OT-only** (qinˈah/qaˈna). The NT counterpart (zēlos/zēloō, and the rivalry terms eritheia/phthonos) is carried in the **C6 strife** and broader cluster vocabulary rather than in C4's focus set; per the science extract the NT continues both the zeal and envy poles. Within C4 proper, continuity is **inferred**, not present in the OT-only set — labelled inferential.

**T7.1.9** — NT-coined term: none in C4's OT-only set. Record none (the NT zēlos vocabulary lies outside this focus set).

**T7.1.10** — Full vocabulary arc: a **single root** holding the full range from **divine covenant-jealousy** (Exo 34:14) through **human zeal for God** (Num 25:11; Psa 69:9) to **rivalrous envy** (Gen 30:1; Pro 14:30) — the most semantically unified term in the cluster, its valence set entirely by direction and object.

**T7.2.1** — Function of the primary term in its primary verse: in Exo 34:14 qanˈna is the **predicate nominative defining God** ("the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God") — the term *names* God and grounds the prohibition of other gods. In Num 25:11 qinˈah is the **causal ground** of Phinehas' commended act and reward.

**T7.2.2** — Literary forms: **covenant law** (Exo 20:5; 34:14; Deu 4:24), **narrative** (Gen 30:1; 37:11; Num 25; 1Ki 19), **ritual law** (Num 5:14–30, the jealousy ordeal), **wisdom** (Pro 14:30; 23:17; Ecc 4:4), **psalm** (Psa 69:9; 73:3), **prophecy** (Eze 36:5; Zec 1:14; Zep 1:18; Isa 9:7). Responsible reading distinguishes the covenant-attribute texts, the narrative exemplars, the ritual-legal ordeal, and the wisdom warnings (BOOK distribution: Eze 13, Num 12, Isa 8).

**T7.2.3** — Logical structure: **covenant-exclusive** — *because* the LORD is a jealous God, *therefore* no other gods/idols (Exo 20:3–5; 34:14); **wisdom-consequential** — *if* the heart envies, *then* it rots / strays (Pro 14:30; 23:17); **narrative-exemplary** — Phinehas' jealousy → atonement and covenant (Num 25:11–13).

**T7.2.4** — Contextual settings: **covenantal/cultic** (Exo 34:14; Deu 4:24), **ritual-juridical** (the marriage ordeal, Num 5), **communal/familial** (Gen 30:1; 37:11), **liturgical-wisdom** (Psa 73; Pro 23:17), **eschatological-prophetic** (Isa 9:7; Zep 3:8). The settings show jealousy as covenant-attribute, marital safeguard, family fault-line, and eschatological zeal.

**T7.2.5** — Primary anchor verse: **Exodus 34:14** (with 20:5) — "the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God" — most fully and directly expresses the characteristic's essential character: jealousy as God's covenant-exclusive, possessive ardour. (The human-zeal anchor is Num 25:11; the envy anchor Pro 14:30.)

**T7.2.6** — Exo 34:14 shows what no other verse shows: that jealousy is **God's very name/attribute** — not a passing affect but a defining covenant characteristic that grounds the whole demand of exclusive worship. No other verse predicates jealousy of God's *name* this directly.

**T7.3.1** — Most useful human-science lens: per the science extract, **social and evolutionary psychology** — jealousy as "protective of valued bonds and resources" (mate-guarding, social comparison), with the noted caveat that **divine jealousy lies outside science's scope**.

**T7.3.2** — Where the framework illuminates: the evolutionary account (jealousy = response to threat against a *valued* relationship/resource) illuminates why qinˈah arises only over **valued, rightful bonds** — the covenant (Exo 34:14), the marriage (Num 5:14), and why God's jealousy carries **positive** valence as covenant-protection (per the science extract's explicit point). Social-comparison theory illuminates the envy pole (Gen 30:1; Psa 73:3; Ecc 4:4 "from a man's envy of his neighbour").

**T7.3.3** — Where they diverge: clinical accounts **pathologise** jealousy, whereas the C4 evidence presents **divine jealousy and righteous zeal as positive** (Exo 34:14; Num 25:11–13) — "a genuine divergence from the pathologising tendency of clinical accounts" (science extract). Science also does not adjudicate the **covenantal-ontological** claim that God is rightly jealous.

**T7.3.4** — Gaps surfaced by science: the **attachment dimension** (secure vs anxious attachment predicting jealousy sensitivity) may illuminate differences between the cluster's jealousy terms — e.g. whether the marital "spirit of jealousy" (Num 5:14) and covenant jealousy encode a security/insecurity axis the biblical pass should test (per the science extract's T7.3.4). Labelled inferential — a prompt for further verse work.

## Closing notes
- **Questions answered:** all 126. Silence recorded where C4 verses do not speak (T3.5 creativity; parts of T3.3 memory / T3.9 conscience; T4.6 angelic mediation; T7.1.8/9 NT coinage — C4 is OT-only).
- **Key data feature:** one root (qinˈah/qaˈna) holding three poles — divine jealousy, righteous zeal, sinful envy — plus the marital "spirit of jealousy" (Num 5). Distinct affect that fuses with wrath in God (Zep 1:18). OT-only focus set; NT zēlos vocabulary lies outside it (T7.1.8 inferential).
- **Provenance:** read-resolved fields supporting; valence used; T7.3 from the science extract.

# M03 · Characteristic A — Inner pain / sorrow · Findings by tier question

- **File:** wa-m03-char-a-tier-findings-v1_1-20260619.md · **Date:** 2026-06-19
- **Related:** evidence base wa-m03-char-a-inner-pain-v1_1-20260619.md; tier framework wa-tier-catalogue-restructured-v2-20260611.md (T-codes are the reference key); science lens wa-m03-grief-scienceextract-v1_0-20260513.md (Section 2); obslog wa-obslog-m03-ve-char-derive-v2-20260619.md.
- **Scope:** every live tier question answered as a self-contained finding (prose can be written from it without returning to source data); citations inline. Negative findings stated explicitly. Retired constructs (T1.2.3, T1.8, T2.8, T5.7, T6.6, T6.7) omitted. Field-absent questions answered by inference from verse identities and present fields, as agreed.
- **Status:** v1_1 (supersedes v1_0; re-pitched to stand-alone level for consistency with B–J).
- **Evidence summary:** 101 verses (OT-led, with a NT lupeō group); faculty = affect (104/104, pure affect); seat heart 11 / soul 6 / flesh 1 (no spirit, no mind); God = agent ×10 (he both inflicts and removes pain); valence neutral 61 / sinful 9 / righteous 3 / forbidden 1; lead terms `makh.ov` (15), `lupeō` (21), `ya.gon` (14); christological anchor at Isa 53:3–4.

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design
**T0.1.1** — Inner pain images God as the righteous author and sovereign over human sorrow: where God is the subject he multiplies pain in judgement (Gen 3:16–17), gives "anguish of soul" (Deu 28:65), adds it (Jer 45:3), and finally abolishes it (Rev 21:4). The verses picture a God who governs grief — imposing, permitting, and ending it — rather than one driven by it. The single place the boundary is crossed is the Servant who bears sorrows (Isa 53:3–4).
**T0.1.2** — Inner pain is related to God as **agent** in 10 verses (Gen 3:16,17; Deu 28:65; Isa 14:3; Isa 50:11; Jer 45:3; 2Cor 7:9,11; Eph 4:30); it is not predicated of God as his own felt state. The qualified exception is Isa 53:3–4, where `makh.ov` ("sorrows") is borne by the Servant — read christologically, sorrow is taken up into the divine–human.
**T0.1.3** — That God inflicts and removes but is not said to bear this pain frames inner pain as a creaturely condition under divine governance rather than a shared divine attribute — with Isa 53 the deliberate exception in the Servant.
**T0.2.1** — Where a purpose is stated, godly grief "equips" repentance unto salvation (2Cor 7:9–11); elsewhere inner pain's purpose is not stated at verse level. Its served end, where named, is to turn the person toward repentance.
**T0.2.2** — Inner pain is presented as a feature of the fallen condition: it enters with the fall (Gen 3:16–17) and is abolished in the consummation (Rev 21:4), so it is not part of the original or final design.
**T0.2.3** — Strongly oriented to future fullness by way of its cessation: Rev 21:4 promises that pain shall be no more — present inner pain is oriented toward its own abolition.
**T0.3.1–.3** — No verse ties the felt-pain state to the image of God as an attribute. Negative on image-bearing; the capacity to grieve over loss and sin reflects a being made for attachment and moral response, but this is inference, not verse-stated.
**T0.4.1–.2** — Inner pain carries christological typology: Isa 53:3–4 deploys `makh.ov` of the Suffering Servant, and Lam 1:12 ("any sorrow like my sorrow") functions in the typology of Zion's suffering. The direction is divine→human / pattern-establishing — the human lament points toward the Servant who bears the sorrows of others.

## T1 — Definition
**T1.1.1** — "Inner pain / sorrow": the felt interior state of grief — the ache itself, not its expression (weeping, mourning) or its cause. The name signals an interior, borne suffering.
**T1.1.2** — Hebrew `makh.ov` (pain), `ya.gon` (grief/sorrow), `ka.av`/`ke.ev` (pain), `e.tsev` (pain/toil); Greek `lupeō`/`lupē` (grief), `perilupos` (deeply grieved), `odunē` (anguish), `ponos` (pain) — pain, sorrow, and anguish as borne states.
**T1.1.3** — The terms are constitutional (heart/soul-seated) and largely non-directional — inner pain is borne within, not aimed at an object the way a relational characteristic is.
**T1.2.1** — Predominantly a **status/condition** (status 63, action 34, quality 7) — a state borne by the person, with a minority of act-forms (to grieve, `lupeō`) and quality-forms (`perilupos`, "sorrowful").
**T1.2.2** — Simple at first encounter — a single felt state — though it co-occurs with audible expression (mourning, sighing) and with external pressure (distress).
**T1.3.1** — Structural opposite: joy / gladness (M04) — the felt-state contrary of inner pain. Cross-cluster, named only.
**T1.3.2** — Inner pain excludes comfort and consolation; Rev 21:4 sets the wiping-away of pain as the mark of consummated joy.
**T1.3.3** — It ends where the felt ache becomes outward expression (mourning, weeping, sighing) or external pressure (distress); its boundary is seat (heart/soul) and the fact that it is felt rather than enacted.
**T1.4.1** — Operates as a borne inner state (the standing condition of sorrow), occasionally as an act of grieving (`lupeō`), and as a quality (`perilupos`, the sorrowful person).
**T1.4.2** — Operates at the heart and soul levels, not at spirit or mind; no directional dependence is evidenced — it is consistently an interior state.
**T1.4.3** — Inner pain is not itself speech-based (it is the felt ache, which other characteristics voice). Negative finding on a communicative mode.
**T1.5.1** — The immediate inner response is low-signal and verse-specific; no single dominant reaction attends the onset of inner pain across the evidence.
**T1.5.2** — Variable across the evidence rather than uniform.
**T1.6.1** — Sustained inner pain tends to consume — sorrow increasing with knowledge (Ecc 1:18), days full of grief (Ecc 2:23) — yet in the godly case it turns to repentance and is not regretted (2Cor 7:9–11).
**T1.7.1–.3** — Inner pain is borne, not received as a gift; reception-framing largely does not apply. The one reception-adjacent case is godly grief willingly entered (2Cor 7).

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries
**T2.1** — No occurrence locates inner pain at the spirit level. Negative.
**T2.2** — Located at the **soul** level in 6 occurrences — the felt ache reaching the innermost self.
**T2.3** — Located in the **heart** in 11 occurrences — the **dominant** seat; inner pain is pre-eminently a heart-state, engaging the heart's feeling function.
**T2.4** — No mind-location. Negative — inner pain does not engage the mind as a seat (Ecc 1:18's cognitive *cause* is not a mind-seat).
**T2.5** — No soul-subset location beyond heart and soul. Negative.
**T2.6** — Linked to the **flesh** once (Job 33:19, pain in the body); a minimal, functional body-link.
**T2.7** — Where the flesh-link appears, direction runs soul→body: the inner pain registering bodily. Single data point, held lightly.
**T2.9.1** — Origin is predominantly received-from-outside (external adversity, divine action), with `origin` explicitly received-from-outside in 3 occurrences and God named as bestowing agent in 10.
**T2.9.2** — Origin is multiple: external infliction and divine bestowal both appear.
**T2.9.3** — Origin shifts by context: divinely imposed (Gen 3; Deu 28), relationally inflicted (2Cor 2:2), and self-incurred (1Ti 6:10, those who pierce themselves with many griefs).
**T2.10** — Movement is limited to heart–soul co-seating; no spirit-level movement is evidenced.

## T3 — The Inner Faculties
Inner pain is **pure affect** (104/104).
**T3.1 Perception / T3.2 Cognition / T3.3 Memory** — Not engaged at faculty level. Negative findings (the cognitive *cause* in Ecc 1:18 is not the faculty inner pain engages).
**T3.4 Affect** — Engaged wholly: inner pain *is* the affective faculty in its pain mode; it intensifies and dominates affect.
**T3.5 Creativity / T3.6 Volition / T3.7 Agency** — Not engaged; inner pain is borne, not chosen or initiated (the repentance of 2Cor 7 is a downstream volitional act, not inner pain's faculty).
**T3.8 Moral evaluation / T3.9 Conscience** — Not at faculty level; the moral framing sits in valence (sinful/righteous grief), not in an engaged faculty — though godly grief (2Cor 7) is conviction-adjacent.
**T3.11 Relational** — Not at faculty level, though inner pain is frequently *about* persons (object person ×10).
**Pattern** — Inner pain engages a single faculty, affect, purely; it neither enables nor impairs the other faculties in the evidence. This marks it as the cluster's clearest pure-affect state — the felt ache that the expressive and somatic characteristics give form to.

## T4 — Relational Interfaces
**T4.1 God→human** — God extends or imposes inner pain as agent (Gen 3:16–17; Deu 28:65; Jer 45:3; struck down, Psa 69:26) and removes it (Rev 21:4). Basis: judgement and discipline — conditional and covenantal.
**T4.2 Human→God** — Limited: inner pain is felt rather than directed at God; the godward case is godly grief turning to repentance (2Cor 7:9–11), whose inner posture is openness to conviction.
**T4.3 Giving** — Inner pain is not extended person-to-person (contrast compassion). Negative.
**T4.4 Receiving** — Inner pain is received in the inflicted sense: from circumstances and persons (Eze 28:24, the contempt of neighbours; 2Cor 2:2, pain caused relationally) — involuntarily.
**T4.5 Boundaries** — Operates both within bonds (pain *over*/​*for* persons, object person ×10) and across distance; relational scope is wide.
**T4.6 Spiritual beings** — No occurrence relates inner pain to angelic or adversarial beings. Negative.

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension
**T5.1 Transformation** — Inner pain produces transformation in one clear case: godly grief → repentance → salvation (2Cor 7:9–11), changing both condition and orientation; the change is explicitly "without regret" (irreversible-for-good). Elsewhere transformation is not stated.
**T5.2 Sequence** — 2Cor 7:9–11 gives a before→during→after: grief → repentance → salvation without regret.
**T5.3 Mechanism** — Encounter and conviction — godly grief as the mechanism that moves the person toward repentance.
**T5.4 Suffering** — Central: inner pain is most often the **product of** suffering (it *is* the felt suffering) and a **response to** loss — oppression (Exo 3:7), divine wounding (Job 5:18; Psa 69:26), the sorrows of Zion (Lam 1:12,18). Suffering produces and deepens it; in 2Cor 7 it also reveals repentance.
**T5.5 Formation/sanctification** — Godly grief participates in the sanctification arc, working repentance unto salvation (2Cor 7:10).
**T5.6 Eschatological** — Strongly oriented: Rev 21:4 orients inner pain toward eschatological abolition — present pain anticipates a future where it is wiped away.

## T6 — Structural Relationships
**T6.1 Co-occurrence** — Same-verse with C (mourning, ×4) and E (sighing, ×4), and with B (distress, ×2) and I (debilitation, ×2). The pattern: inner pain is the felt state that the expressive characteristics (mourning, sighing) make audible and that debilitation carries into the body.
**T6.2 Sequential** — Limited same-verse sequence; the clearest is inner pain → repentance (2Cor 7).
**T6.3 Causal/constitutive** — Produced by external adversity (the cause field) and by God (agent ×10); inner pain produces repentance in the godly case (2Cor 7).
**T6.4 Vocabulary/root sharing** — `e.tsev`/`its.tsa.von` carry "painful toil" (Gen 3:16–17), bridging inner pain with labour/toil vocabulary; `lupeō` is shared NT grief vocabulary. (Cross-cluster — flagged.)
**T6.5 Distinctions** — Nearest neighbour is **B (distress)**. The distinction is constitutional and qualitative: inner pain is the heart's felt ache; distress is the soul's experience of external pressure (constriction). The difference is of kind and seat, not degree.

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation
**T7.1.1** — Primary terms `makh.ov`, `ya.gon`, `ka.av`/`ke.ev`, `e.tsev` (Hebrew); `lupeō`/`lupē`, `odunē`, `ponos` (Greek) — pain/sorrow/anguish as felt suffering (root glosses per the lexicon; deeper etymology not asserted beyond it).
**T7.1.2** — Grammatical range: nouns (the borne state), verbs (`lupeō`, `ka.av` — the act of grieving), adjective (`perilupos` — the quality) — inner pain operates as both borne state and act.
**T7.1.3** — Semantic range: pain ↔ sorrow ↔ anguish ↔ grief — a felt-suffering band.
**T7.1.4** — The vocabulary distinguishes the condition (`makh.ov`) from the act (`lupeō`) from the quality (`perilupos`).
**T7.1.5** — Opposite/absence term: comfort/joy vocabulary (cross-cluster); within inner pain itself, none.
**T7.1.6** — No distinct person-type term ("the sorrowful one"); `perilupos` is a quality, not a person-type. Negative.
**T7.1.7** — No supplication or seeking term (inner pain is not sought). Negative.
**T7.1.8** — OT `makh.ov`/`ya.gon` are answered by NT `lupeō`/`odunē`; the felt-pain experience is continuous across the Testaments, with the NT adding the godly-grief framing (2Cor 7).
**T7.1.9** — No clearly NT-coined term for inner pain. Negative.
**T7.1.10** — The vocabulary arc runs pain/sorrow/anguish across both Testaments, climaxing in the Servant's `makh.ov` (Isa 53) and in godly grief (2Cor 7).
**T7.2.1** — In Isa 53:3 `makh.ov` functions predicatively, defining the Servant as "a man of sorrows."
**T7.2.2** — Forms span narrative (Genesis), covenant law (Deu 28), wisdom (Ecclesiastes), prophecy (Isaiah, Jeremiah), lament (Lamentations), epistle (2 Corinthians), and apocalyptic (Revelation).
**T7.2.3** — Logical structure example: 2Cor 7:9–11 — godly grief → repentance → salvation, "without regret."
**T7.2.4** — Settings are covenantal (Deu 28), eschatological (Rev 21), and christological (Isa 53).
**T7.2.5** — Primary anchor: **Isaiah 53:3** — "a man of sorrows" most fully and directly expresses inner pain and carries the cluster's deepest theological weight.
**T7.2.6** — The anchor uniquely reveals that inner pain is taken up and borne **vicariously** by the Servant — the deepest theological turn the characteristic makes.
**T7.3.1** — Framework: clinical psychology of pain and suffering — Eisenberger (social-pain neuroscience), Cassell (the nature of suffering), Frankl (meaning).
**T7.3.2** — Eisenberger's finding that social/psychological pain shares neural circuits with physical pain gives the biblical pain-of-grief vocabulary a literal, not merely metaphorical, basis; Cassell's account of suffering as a threat to the whole person aligns with inner pain reaching beyond bodily hurt.
**T7.3.3** — Divergence: the science is primarily therapeutic (move through pain toward restored function); the biblical material includes pain sustained unresolved (Lamentations) and given vicarious, redemptive meaning (Isa 53; 2Cor 7) that the therapeutic frame does not capture.
**T7.3.4** — The science's meaning-making pathway invites testing whether inner pain presents meaning as the turning point — and 2Cor 7's godly grief supports exactly that, a coherent and evidence-grounded extension.

# M01 c1 — Reverent fear / awe: synthesis across all tiers

- **File:** `wa-m01-c01-reverent-synth-v1_0-20260619.md` · **Date:** 2026-06-19 · **Prefix:** WA · **Version:** v1_0
- **Characteristic:** c1 — reverent fear / awe (chiefly toward God). **Primary anchor:** Psa 130:4 — "But with you there is forgiveness, that you may be feared."
- **Purpose:** consolidated grounding for prose on reverent fear, drawing c1's thread across all seven tiers. Foundation layer — not the essay.
- **Grounding source:** `WA-m01-findings-NEW-merged-bytier-v1-20260619.md`. **Discipline:** no-new-claims; tier refs `(T…)` and verse anchors retained; inferential/silence labels preserved.

## 1. Identity
The name fuses **fear + reverence + awe** — fear in a reverent register, a God-directed honouring disposition, not mere fright (T1.1.1). It is the **richest and most positive member** of the cluster. Primary terms: the *yare* root itself (H3372H *ya.re* "to fear: revere", H3373; H4172A/B *mo.rah*; H6345 *pach.dah* "dread/awe"; Greek G6015 *deos*, reverent uses of G5401 *fobos*) — the root carries fear-and-reverence as one range (T1.1.2). It is a **disposition** held as a standing orientation (action 123 / status 66 / quality 48; T1.2.1), operating in three modes: Qal active ("you fear"), Niphal *nora'* ("to-be-feared/awesome" — God as the quality feared), and the commanded imperative (T1.4.1). It is **composite**: fuses affect with cognition and memory ("to know", "to remember" co-terms) — not reducible to a single label (T1.2.2).

## 2. God-relation, image, typology
God is the **object** of c1 in 128 records, and the quality feared is his own awesomeness; the cause-fields name his attributes, acts, and his **forgiveness** (Psa 130:4) (T0.1.1). God is never its experiencer (T0.1.2). c1 carries the cluster's **most meaningful silence** about God: reverent fear images "not what God is but how the creature rightly stands before God" — a creaturely orientation toward the Creator (T0.1.3). It is the **only characteristic that positively instantiates an image-bearing excellence** — the creature's right acknowledgement of the Creator (T0.3.1) — and it is an exclusively creaturely analogue, not shared with God (T0.3.2). Its **absence or misdirection is the disorder** (not fearing God, sinful 14; fearing other gods, forbidden 5 — Judg 6:10; 2Ki 17:7); its presence marks a rightly-ordered image (T0.3.3). Typology: **covenantal** (reverent fear sits inside the covenant frame); eschatological thin (Joe 2:11); **christological absent in c1's own OT-anchored data** (T0.4.1).

## 3. Created purpose / design-or-fall
c1 **equips the person for right relation and glad obedience to God** — valence righteous 110 + commanded 52 (the refined reverent set stronger still). Its enacted fruit is obedience and worship (Lev 19:3, reverence of parents/Sabbath; Deu 6:2, keeping commandments) (T0.2.1). It reads as **created design** — a proper orientation to be cultivated (T0.2.2). Sustained, it produces a **lifelong standing orientation** — a settled God-fearing character ("all the days of your life," Deu 6:2) (T1.6.1–1.6.2). Its immediate response is uniformly **obedience and worship**, highly consistent (T1.5.1–1.5.2); the immediate acts mature into a settled character (T1.6.3).

## 4. Constitution
Located chiefly in the **heart** (13 — the dominant seat), with soul 5 and flesh 3 (T2.3.1; T2.6.1). It is **silent on spirit-level and on mind-location** (T2.1; T2.4 — mind is 0 across the whole cluster). Origin, where recorded, is **received-from-outside** (8), with God as **giver** in the conquest context (Deu 11:25, the fear of Israel laid on the nations) carried under `divine_involvement` (T2.9.1). No internal constitutional movement is evidenced (T2.10.3).

## 5. Faculties
Constitutively **affective**, affect-dominant with a knowing blend (T3.4.1). It **operates with sound cognition** — *ya.da* "to know" 6, *cha.kham* "wise" 3 — felt as affect but operating with knowing (neither impairs nor bypasses; *inferential*) (T3.2). It is the cluster's **recollective** member, operating alongside memory (*za.khar* "to remember" 4 — recalling God's acts/commands; *inferential*) (T3.3). It engages **volition** faintly (*ba.char* "to choose"; the obedience fruit implies a volitional outworking; *inferential*) and **enables agency** toward obedience (T3.6/T3.7). It is the **ground of right moral orientation** — the commanded/righteous fear from which obedience flows, deepening moral seriousness (T3.8). It carries the cluster's lone **conscience** trace (*suneidesis* 1 — too thin to build on) and comes closest to **conscientiousness** (moral awareness + volition + action co-occur; *inferential*) (T3.9/T3.10).

## 6. Relational interfaces
**God is the dominant object** (object=God 98) — the human reveres God as worship and obedience (Lev 19:14, "you shall fear your God: I am the LORD") (T4.2.1). The required posture is **acknowledgement, reverence, humble submission**, grounded in God's attributes and his forgiveness (Psa 130:4) (T4.2.2); the relationship imaged is **creature-before-Creator**, reverent dependence (T4.2.3). God **instils** it covenantally (Deu 11:25), on the basis of his act, not a condition met (T4.1.2). At the human interface, c1 is the **rendering of due reverence** to rightful authority (parents — Lev 19:3) (T4.3.1/T4.3.3). It operates **within bonds** (family/covenant) and **across distance** (apprehension of Esau, Gen 32:11) (T4.5.1). Spiritual-beings interface: its **forbidden** form is fear of other gods (Judg 6:10) (T4.6.1).

## 7. Over time, suffering, eschatology
The cluster's one genuinely **orientation-forming / transformative** member — it forms a standing Godward orientation over a lifetime (*inferential*; T5.1.1). The only characteristic participating in the **sanctifying arc** — a lifelong orientation forming a God-fearing character that issues in obedience (*inferential*; T5.5.1–5.5.2). Present in Job in modest measure (6 refs) (T5.4). Eschatological markers thin — Joe 2:11; Rev 11/18 (T5.6.1).

## 8. Within the cluster
Its structural opposite is not "no emotion" but **fear misdirected** (other gods) or **withheld where owed** (T1.3.1). Nearest neighbour is **c2 (ordinary fear)** — same *yare* root — distinguished by **valence + object**: reverent = Godward, commanded/righteous; ordinary = threat-facing, forbidden/neutral. The seam is **moral, not lexical** (T6.5.1; T1.3.3). It also borders **c10 (astonishment)**: awe honours, astonishment is stunned (T6.5.1). The *pachad* root reaches from dread (c3) into c1's reverent awe (H6345), showing threat-fear and God-fear are lexically continuous (T6.4.2). Cross-cluster, c1's leading partners are **wisdom (M15) and righteousness (M26)** — "the fear of the LORD is the beginning…" (T6.1.1; held → Session D). Co-occurrence is broad.

## 9. Interpretive lens
Genre: the **broadest** of the cluster — narrative, psalm, prophecy, wisdom, gospel, epistle (T7.2.2). Logical structure: premise "fear the LORD" → conclusion "keep his commandments / live" (Deu 6:2); the wisdom maxim fear→wisdom (T7.2.3). Anchor **Psa 130:4** uniquely grounds reverent fear in **forgiveness/grace** — fear *because of* mercy, not terror (T7.2.6). Science lens: **psychology of awe / religion** (Otto's numinous; self-diminishment, prosocial orientation) illuminates how reverent fear produces obedience/worship — "self before the vast" matching creature-before-Creator (T7.3.1–7.3.2).

## 10. Inferential flags & silences
*Inferential:* operates-with-cognition; recollective (memory); volitional outworking; conscientiousness; sanctifying/formative role. *Silences:* spirit-location, mind-location, creativity, transformation-as-event, christological typology in c1's own data. Present these as the findings labelled them (GR-PROG-009).

## 11. Essence
Reverent fear is the cluster's **created, image-bearing, formative** member: the rightly-ordered, Godward register of fear — grounded in God's holiness *and* his forgiveness — that knows, remembers, obeys, and forms a God-fearing life. Where it is absent or misdirected, the image is disordered.

*Section id 251 · status `approved` · v1_0 · 1003 words · author `claude_ai` · source `wa-m01-c02-fear-afraid-synth-v1_0-20260619.md`*

# M01 c2 — Fear / being afraid: synthesis across all tiers

- **File:** `wa-m01-c02-fear-afraid-synth-v1_0-20260619.md` · **Date:** 2026-06-19 · **Prefix:** WA · **Version:** v1_0
- **Characteristic:** c2 — fear / being afraid (apprehension of danger). **Primary anchor:** Isa 41:13 — "Fear not… I am the one who helps you."
- **Purpose:** consolidated grounding for prose on ordinary fear, across all seven tiers. Foundation layer — not the essay.
- **Grounding source:** `WA-m01-findings-NEW-merged-bytier-v1-20260619.md`. **Discipline:** no-new-claims; tier refs and verse anchors retained; inferential/silence labels preserved.

## 1. Identity
The plain affect of being afraid — the cluster's **core and largest member** — signalling episodic apprehension of danger (T1.1.1). Terms: H3372G *ya.re* (danger sense), H3374 *yir.ah*, H3025/H3016 *ya.gor*, H7297 *ra.hah*, Aramaic H1763 *de.chal*, and Greek **G5399 *fobeō*** — the Greek pair makes c2 genuinely **bi-testamental** (T1.1.2). It is an **act** (episodic affect — 76% action, 289 of records; T1.2.1), predominantly **Qal active** ("something one does"), with no "to-be-feared" group (contrast c1) (T1.4.1). It is a **perceptual-affective compound** — couples affect with perception (43 affect+perception blends) (T1.2.2). The same *yare* lemma it shares with c1 operates as ordinary or reverent **by object and valence** (T1.4.2).

## 2. God-relation, image, typology
God is the **object** (71) and his self-revelation arouses fear (theophany, divine power — Exo 20:20 context) (T0.1.1); never its experiencer (T0.1.2). The silence marks it as a creaturely response (T0.1.3); exclusively a creaturely analogue (T0.3.2). It instantiates the image **only in its God-directed minority**; otherwise it expresses the creature under threat (T0.3.1). Presence is **mixed**: God-directed fear is right; forbidden fear ("do not be afraid") is a failure to trust — the "fear not" formula treats its presence as something to be removed (T0.3.3). Typology: **christological — the strongest candidate in the cluster.** NT occurrences arouse fear at **Jesus' divine acts** — calming the sea (Mar 4:41), the transfiguration (Mat 17:7), the cross/earthquake (Mat 27:54). The fear the OT reserves for Yahweh is, in the NT, aroused by Christ; direction is **fulfilment** (T0.4.1–0.4.2). Eschatological: Rev 14:7; Rev 18:10.

## 3. Created purpose / design-or-fall
Predominantly **forbidden 106 / neutral 128**; its fruit is dismay and flight; purpose-as-design is weak, its commendable form the God-directed minority overlapping c1 (T0.2.1). Reads as **fallen-condition response (dominant)**, but **held as mixed** — some neutral fear is ordinary creaturely self-preservation, so a flat "fallen only" reading would overreach (T0.2.2; the cluster's T0 reading most needing T7.2 corroboration). Immediate response: **dismay, trembling, panic, flight/avoidance** — disturbance and withdrawal — consistent in direction, varied in form (T1.5.1–1.5.2). Thin/near-silent on sustained effect (episodic) (T1.6.1).

## 4. Constitution
**Heart** is the leading seat (23 — the most of any characteristic; "their heart melted") (T2.3.1); soul 4, flesh 3 (T2.2; T2.6.1). **Silent on spirit and mind** (T2.1; T2.4). Origin **received-from-outside** (9 — fear "comes/falls upon" via perceived threat) and also **God-sent** in some contexts (agent 16) (T2.9.1/2.9.3). Movement is **onto the person from outside** (T2.10.1).

## 5. Faculties
Constitutively **affective**, affect-dominant (T3.4). Strong **cognitive co-operation** (*ya.da* "to know" 7, *da.at* 6, *bi.nah* 3) yet can **bypass** deliberate cognition in the fast immediate alarm — mixed, not cleanly resolved (T3.2). **Perception is the faculty that most distinguishes ordinary fear from reverent**: it **presupposes** perception — the affective response *to* what is seen/heard (Mat 14:26) (T3.1). The **"fear not" command addresses the will** (fear is to be refused) — an indirect volitional engagement (T3.6); it can **impair agency** (flight/avoidance) or, when resisted, leave it intact (T3.7). Moral evaluation partial — the "forbidden" framing evaluates it as a failure to trust (T3.8). Fear of others can **impair relational connection**, restored by reassurance (T3.11).

## 6. Relational interfaces
God-object 63 (the reverent overlap) — fear before God in theophany/exposure (T4.2.1). The **clearest reception interface in the cluster**: experiencer **addressed 131** — fear is overwhelmingly operated through **person-to-person address**, most often the reassurance "do not be afraid of them"; the giving is of *relief* from fear (Gen 15:1, "Fear not, Abram"; T1.4.3/T4.4.1). Persons make others afraid (object_type person 65) (T4.3.1). Operates **across distance** (enemies, kings, crowds) and crosses covenant boundaries (1Sa 4:7) (T4.5.1–4.5.2). Spiritual-beings: **forbidden** fear of other gods (2Ki 17:35) and dread of "a god" (1Sa 4:7) (T4.6.1). God's disposition toward his own is **reassuring/liberating** ("Fear not, I am with you," Isa 41:13) (T4.1.3).

## 7. Over time, suffering, eschatology
Silent on a transformation arc (T5.1). Present in **Job/Lam** (14 refs — fear at "all his suffering," "seeing Job's calamity") — a product/context of affliction (T5.4). Silent on sanctification (T5.5). **Strongest eschatological orientation** of the cluster — apocalyptic refs in Daniel, Joel, Revelation (17), oriented toward the **hour of judgement** (Rev 14:7); present Godward fear anticipates the universal reverence at the reckoning (T5.6).

## 8. Within the cluster
Opposite: **courage / strength / trust** ("be strong and do not fear" — *am.mits*, *cha.zaq*, *ko.ach*) (T1.3.1); commanded *away* (forbidden 106) (T1.3.2). Nearest neighbour **c1** (same root; distinguished by valence/object) and contrasted with **c9** (anxiety: settled/cognitive/interior vs c2 episodic/perceptual) (T6.5.1). c2 **produces trembling (c5)** and **dismay/flight (c7)** — the "fear not, neither be dismayed" pairing treats dismay as fear's collapse-product (T6.3.1). Cross-cluster partners: **shame / courage** (T6.1.1; held → Session D). Co-occurs heavily within the terror-complex.

## 9. Interpretive lens
Genre: **narrative-dominant (122)** + prophecy 72 + gospel 60 — "fear not" scenes need attention to speaker/situation (T7.2.2). Logical structure: the **grounded imperative** — command ("fear not") + ground clause ("for I am with you," Isa 41:13) (T7.2.3). Anchor **Isa 41:13** uniquely ties the "fear not" to **God's hand-holding presence** as antidote (T7.2.6). Science lens: **affective neuroscience** (amygdala, fight/flight/freeze) (T7.3.1).

## 10. Inferential flags & silences
*Inferential:* cognition-bypass reading; agency-impairment; relational-impairment. *Held as mixed:* design-vs-fall status. *Silences:* spirit, mind, sustained effect, transformation, sanctification.

## 11. Essence
Ordinary fear is the cluster's **core, episodic, perceptually-triggered** member — apprehension of danger, mostly forbidden where it should yield to trust, yet not wholly fallen (creaturely self-preservation residue). It is the chief site of the gospel's recurring word, "Fear not… I am with you," and in the NT it is the fear Christ's divine acts arouse.

# M01 c3 — Dread: synthesis across all tiers

- **File:** `wa-m01-c03-dread-synth-v1_0-20260619.md` · **Date:** 2026-06-19 · **Prefix:** WA · **Version:** v1_0
- **Characteristic:** c3 — dread (anticipatory, forward-looking apprehension). **Primary anchor:** Job 3:25 — "For the thing that I fear comes upon me, and what I dread befalls me."
- **Purpose:** consolidated grounding for prose on dread, across all seven tiers. Foundation layer — not the essay.
- **Grounding source:** `WA-m01-findings-NEW-merged-bytier-v1-20260619.md`. **Discipline:** no-new-claims; tier refs and verse anchors retained; inferential/silence labels preserved.

## 1. Identity
Anticipatory, forward-looking apprehension — a weight of something feared ahead, **a condition one is *in*** (T1.1.1). The ***pachad* core**: H6343 *pa.chad* (noun), H6342 (verb), with H2844A *chat*, H4034 *me.go.rah*, H0366 *a.yom* "terrible" — OT Hebrew (T1.1.2). A **condition/state** (status 52 / action 24), largely **nominal** — operates as a state named, not an act done (T1.2.1/T1.4.1). Its name carries a **temporal** implication (forward-looking) (T1.1.3). Appears **simple** at first encounter (purely affective) (T1.2.2).

## 2. God-relation, image, typology
God's role is chiefly **agent** (14) — "the dread of the LORD fell"; the character imaged is God's **dread-inspiring might against his enemies**, with a small reverent object set (7) (T0.1.1). Never God's experiencer (T0.1.2); a creaturely response, exclusively a creaturely analogue (T0.1.3/T0.3.2). Expresses **creaturely finitude/vulnerability** — the image under threat, not an excellence (T0.3.1); presence reveals the creature under threat, valence mostly neutral (T0.3.3). Typology: **silent** — christological 0 / eschatological 0 / covenantal 0 (T0.4.1/0.4.3).

## 3. Created purpose / design-or-fall
**Neutral 57-dominant** — a state one is in, not an equipping; small "dread of God" (righteous 9) the commendable residue (T0.2.1). Reads as **fallen-condition response** (T0.2.2). Immediate response: **shaking / dismay / the dreaded thing arriving** (Job 3:25) (T1.5.1). As an abiding **status**-typed state, what it "produces over time" is the **continuance of the condition** (T1.6.1); immediate and sustained largely coincide (T1.6.3).

## 4. Constitution
**Heart** 6; soul silent; flesh 1 (T2.3.1; T2.2; T2.6.1). **Silent on spirit and mind** (T2.1; T2.4). Origin **received-from-outside** (2), and **God-sent** (agent) when inflicted on enemies (T2.9.1/2.9.3). Movement: **onto the person from outside** ("the dread came/fell upon") (T2.10.1).

## 5. Faculties
Constitutively **affective**, affect-only at the faculty level (T3.4). Lighter cognitive co-terms (know/understand/remember) (T3.2/T3.3). **Silent** on volition, agency, perception-as-faculty, moral evaluation, creativity, conscience (neutral-dominant — morally inert) (T3.6–3.11). Its anticipatory dimension is best lit by clinical anxiety research alongside c9 (T7.3.1).

## 6. Relational interfaces
God object 17 (minority reverence) (T4.2.1). Persons as the dread-inspiring party (dread of persons 11) (T4.3.1); received from a threatening party (addressed 13) (T4.4.1). God's agent-mode (sending dread on opposition) is **responsive/judicial** (T4.1.2). **Silent** on the spiritual-beings interface (T4.6.4).

## 7. Over time, suffering, eschatology
Silent on transformation/sanctification (T5.1/T5.5). **Concentrated in the suffering literature** — 15 Job/Lam refs; `cause` = "calamity from God and his majesty" (Job 3:25; Job 4:14, "dread came upon me, and trembling, which made all my bones shake") — a product and inner context of affliction (T5.4). Faint sequence: dread giving way to **security** in deliverance (Pro 1:33) (T5.2). **Silent** on eschatological trajectory (T5.6.3).

## 8. Within the cluster
Opposite: **security / safety** (*be.tach*, *ma.oz*) — Pro 1:33, "whoever listens to me will dwell secure… without dread of disaster" (T1.3.1); excludes security/ease (T1.3.2). Distinguished from **c4 (terror)** by **form + intensity**: dread = verb-capable **state that arrives**, opposite security; terror = nominal, overwhelming, soul-deep, opposite peace (T6.5.1). The ***pachad* root** reaches from dread into c1's reverent awe (H6345) — threat-fear and God-fear are lexically continuous (T6.4.2). Within the terror-complex, dread **produces trembling (c5)** (Job 4:14) (T6.3.1). Word-paired with terror (Deu 11:25) — accompanying rather than sequential (T6.2.1).

## 9. Interpretive lens
Genre: **wisdom (Job) + prophecy 23 + psalm 15** — a wisdom/suffering word, read in the Job dialogues (T7.2.2). Logical structure: affliction lament — "the thing I dread befalls me" (Job 3:25), premise(dread) realised as conclusion(calamity arrives) (T7.2.3). Anchor **Job 3:25** uniquely names dread's **self-fulfilling arrival** (T7.2.6). Science lens: **clinical anxiety research** (anticipatory dimension) (T7.3.1).

## 10. Inferential flags & silences
*Silences:* spirit, mind, typology, eschatological trajectory, volition/agency/moral faculties; transformation/sanctification. Dread is the affliction-register fear par excellence, but morally inert in the fields.

## 11. Essence
Dread is the **anticipatory state that arrives** — the forward-leaning weight of feared calamity, most at home in Job's suffering, in which "the thing I dread befalls me." Its foil is security; its kin is terror; its root reaches, surprisingly, into reverent awe.

# M01 c4 — Terror: synthesis across all tiers

- **File:** `wa-m01-c04-terror-synth-v1_0-20260619.md` · **Date:** 2026-06-19 · **Prefix:** WA · **Version:** v1_0
- **Characteristic:** c4 — terror (the overwhelming, often inflicted pole). **Primary anchor:** Exo 15:16 — "Terror and dread fall upon them… they are still as a stone."
- **Purpose:** consolidated grounding for prose on terror, across all seven tiers. Foundation layer — not the essay.
- **Grounding source:** `WA-m01-findings-NEW-merged-bytier-v1-20260619.md`. **Discipline:** no-new-claims; tier refs and verse anchors retained; inferential/silence labels preserved.

## 1. Identity
The overwhelming, often inflicted pole of fear — acute, **soul-deep** (T1.1.1). Terror core: H0367 *e.mah*, H4032 *ma.gor*, H2851 *chit.tit*, H1091 *bal.la.hah* (14 terms) + Greek G1630 *ekfobos*, G5398 *foberos*, G5400 *fobetron* (T1.1.2). A **state** — 90% status, **entirely nominal** (47 nouns + adjectival), operating purely as a condition (T1.2.1/T1.4.1). Its name carries a **constitutional (soul-deep)** implication (T1.1.3). Appears **simple** (purely affective) at first encounter (T1.2.2).

## 2. God-relation, image, typology
**Agent-dominant** (8 of ~11 divine) — God **spreads terror**: Exo 15:16, "because of the greatness of your arm, they are still as a stone" — imaging God's **overwhelming might in deliverance/judgement** (T0.1.1). Never God's experiencer (T0.1.2); creaturely, an exclusively creaturely analogue (T0.3.2). Expresses **creaturely finitude/vulnerability** under threat (T0.3.1); presence reveals the creature under threat (neutral) (T0.3.3). Typology: **eschatological** (Luk 21:11; Heb 10:27) and **theophanic/christological** (Heb 12:21 Sinai; Mar 9:6 transfiguration) candidates in NT verse_text; direction is divine-instance-establishes-the-pattern (T0.4.1–0.4.2).

## 3. Created purpose / design-or-fall
**Neutral 50 of 53** — no equipping purpose; an overwhelming condition (T0.2.1). **Fallen-condition response** (T0.2.2). Immediate response: **paralysis / petrification** — Exo 15:16, "still as a stone" — consistent (freezing) (T1.5.1–1.5.2). As a status state, its sustained form is the **continuance of the condition** (T1.6.1).

## 4. Constitution
The **first characteristic where terror reaches the soul as much as the heart** — soul 3 ≥ heart 3 — the soul-deep register (Psa 31:13, "terror on every side!"); this reveals it as the **innermost-personal** fear (T2.2.1–2.2.2). **Silent on spirit and mind** (T2.1; T2.4). **No specific body-part link** — it reaches the soul, not the body (T2.6.3/T2.7.3). Origin: **God-sent** (agent) on enemies; **falls upon / seizes** peoples — downward-onto, no internal level-crossing (T2.9.3/T2.10.1).

## 5. Faculties
Constitutively **affective**, affect-dominant (T3.4). One perception blend (Luk 21:11, "fearful sights" — terror at perceived eschatological signs) (T3.1). **Acute and pre-reflective** — minimal cognitive co-operation (T3.2.3). **Impairs/overrides volition** — it **freezes agency** ("still as a stone"), the limit case where fear suspends the will (*inferential*, strongly supported by the paralysis response) (T3.6/T3.7). Morally **neutral** — moral-evaluation faculty not engaged (T3.8).

## 6. Relational interfaces
God object 2 (T4.2.1). At the human interface, terror is **inspired in another by threatening power** — Pro 20:2, "The terror of a king is like the growling of a lion" (T4.3.1–4.3.2); received from the powerful (addressed 6) (T4.4.1). God's agent-mode is **responsive/judicial** against opposition (Exo 15:16) (T4.1.2). **Silent** on the spiritual-beings interface (T4.6.4).

## 7. Over time, suffering, eschatology
Silent on transformation/sanctification (T5.1/T5.5). **Concentrated in the suffering literature** — 13 Job/Lam refs; terror as the inner register of calamity (T5.4). **Eschatological terror** genuinely evidenced (Luk 21:11; Heb 10:27) (T5.6.1).

## 8. Within the cluster
Opposite: **peace** (*sha.lom*) (T1.3.1); excludes peace (T1.3.2). Distinguished from **c3 (dread)** by form + intensity (terror = nominal, overwhelming, soul-deep, ↔peace; dread = verb-capable state, ↔security), and from **c5 (trembling)** by kind (terror = nominal state; trembling = act/bodily expression) (T6.5.1). **Terror is the intensified pole of dread** — constitutively related by degree (T6.3.3); the *chatat* root bridges terror (c4) and dismay (c7) (T6.4.2). Word-paired with dread (Deu 11:25). Cross-cluster: the **love-casts-out-fear** territory and the peace foil (held → Session D).

## 9. Interpretive lens
Genre: **prophecy 22 + wisdom (Job) 14** — terror in prophetic judgement and Joban affliction (T7.2.2). Anchor **Exo 15:16** uniquely shows terror **freezing agency** ("still as a stone") as God's deliverance-instrument (T7.2.6). Science lens: **affective neuroscience** (the freeze response) and **psychophysiology** (the collapse/freeze register) — and a flagged open question (Porges' polyvagal): whether the terror-paralysis carries a **dissociative/shutdown** sense distinct from arousal (worth testing in the verse evidence; T7.3.4).

## 10. Inferential flags & silences
*Inferential:* volition/agency-freezing reading. *Open question:* freeze/shutdown vs arousal register (→ T7.2/Session B). *Silences:* spirit, mind, body-link, moral faculties; transformation/sanctification.

## 11. Essence
Terror is the **overwhelming, soul-deep, inflicted** pole — the nominal state God spreads on his enemies and the petrifying response that leaves the creature "still as a stone." It reaches the soul (not the body), freezes agency, and its foil is peace.
