# M01 c5 — Trembling / quaking: synthesis across all tiers

- **File:** `wa-m01-c05-trembling-synth-v1_0-20260619.md` · **Date:** 2026-06-19 · **Prefix:** WA · **Version:** v1_0
- **Characteristic:** c5 — trembling / quaking (fear named by its bodily realisation). **Primary anchor:** Isa 66:2 — "he who is humble and contrite in spirit and trembles at my word" (+ Psa 2:11, "Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling").
- **Purpose:** consolidated grounding for prose on trembling, across all seven tiers. Foundation layer — not the essay.
- **Grounding source:** `WA-m01-findings-NEW-merged-bytier-v1-20260619.md`. **Discipline:** no-new-claims; tier refs and verse anchors retained; inferential/silence labels preserved.

## 1. Identity
Fear named by its **bodily realisation** — the body shaken, the visible crossing of the inner state (T1.1.1). The *ragaz*/*charad* family: H7264 *ra.gaz*, H2729 *cha.rad*, H7460 *ra.ad*, H6426 *pa.lats* "to shudder" + Greek **G5156 *tromos*, G1790 *entromos*** (T1.1.2). An **act** (the body shaking — action 83), with a strong **causative Hiphil** (25) alongside Qal and Hithpael — operates both as something done and something *made* to happen (T1.2.1/T1.4.1). Its name is **constitutional (bodily)** (T1.1.3). A **constitutional compound** — couples an inner state with bodily expression (T1.2.2). It is the characteristic whose mode **varies by constitutional level** — as deep as the spirit, through soul/heart, out to the body and cosmos (T1.4.2).

## 2. God-relation, image, typology
**Agent** (17) — God **makes** creation and peoples tremble: Psa 99:1, "The LORD reigns; let the peoples tremble!" — imaging God's **reigning lordship** (T0.1.1). Never God's experiencer (T0.1.2); a creaturely analogue (T0.3.2). It instantiates the image in its **contrite, submissive** form — the spirit that trembles at God's word (Isa 66:2) and before the reigning Lord (Psa 99:1) (T0.3.1); its right (contrite/commanded) form is the rightly-ordered presence (T0.3.3). Typology: **theophanic** (Sinai, Exo 19:18), **eschatological** (day of the LORD near), **christological** (NT *tromos*) candidates (T0.4.1).

## 3. Created purpose / design-or-fall
Neutral 77, **with a created-design signal** in the commanded/righteous forms (commanded 7 + righteous 13) — the contrite spirit trembling at God's word (Isa 66:2) and trembling commanded before the reigning Lord (Psa 99:1): a bodily form that, **rightly directed, equips reverent submission** (T0.2.1). Reads as **both** — its commanded/righteous strand is created design (T0.2.2). Immediate response: **the shaking itself, reaching the body** — Hab 3:16, "my body trembles; my lips quiver… my legs tremble" — consistent (T1.5.1–1.5.2). Sustained, it can produce the **trembling heart** as a chronic affliction (Deu 28:65, "a trembling heart") (T1.6.1–1.6.2); the immediate shaking differs from the sustained chronic state (T1.6.3).

## 4. Constitution — the cluster's key witness
**The movement witness of the whole cluster** (T2.10.1): it crosses the **entire constitutional range** — **spirit** (Isa 66:2, the deepest and most positive case in the cluster), through **soul/heart** (heart 7 / soul 2), **outward to the body** (Job 4:14, "made all my bones shake"; Hab 3:16), and even the **cosmos** (Exo 19:18 Sinai; Psa 99:1, "let the earth quake!"). Movement is **inner-to-outer** — the inner state made visible — making the body the **visible crossing of the spirit-soul-body boundary**, permeable outward (T2.7.2; T2.10.2). It is not *primarily* spirit-level (heart-dominant), but it is the one fear that reaches the spirit (T2.1.2/2.1.3). Body-link is most developed here — bones, lips, legs — and **expressive** (the inner state moved outward) (T2.6.1–2.6.2). **Silent on mind** (T2.4).

## 5. Faculties
Constitutively **affective**, single-faculty (T3.4). Lighter cognitive/memory co-terms (T3.2/T3.3). **Silent** on volition, agency, moral evaluation, creativity, conscience at the faculty level (T3.6–3.10). Its distinctiveness is constitutional/somatic, not faculty-based.

## 6. Relational interfaces
God object 13 — **commanded worship-trembling**: Psa 2:11, "Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling"; Php 2:12, "work out your own salvation with fear and trembling" (T4.2.1). Required posture: **contrite, humble submission** (Isa 66:2) (T4.2.2). Persons as the trembling-inducing party (person 9) (T4.3.1). God's agent-mode makes peoples/creation tremble (Psa 99:1) (T4.1.1). **Silent** on the spiritual-beings interface (T4.6.4).

## 7. Over time, suffering, eschatology
A genuine **sequence toward restoration**: Hos 11:10–11, "when he roars, his children shall come trembling… and I will return them to their homes" — trembling **leads to** homecoming; the trembling is the **threshold** of restoration, not the end-state (*inferential*; T5.2.1–5.2.2). Present in Job (6 refs) (T5.4). **Eschatological — the day of the LORD**: Joe 2:1, "Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, for the day of the LORD is coming" (T5.6.1).

## 8. Within the cluster
Opposite: **rest / quiet / security** (*ra.ga*, *na.chat*, *sha.a.nan*, *be.tach*, *nu.ach*) (T1.3.1); excludes rest (T1.3.2). Distinguished from **c4 (terror)** by kind (act/bodily expression vs nominal state) and from **c6 (horror)** by quality (shaking vs recoil/bristling) (T6.5.1). **Co-occurs most broadly** within the terror-complex — with fear (c2), dread (c3), terror (c4), horror (c6): Psa 55:5, "Fear and trembling come upon me, and horror overwhelms me"; Job 4:14 (T6.1.1). **Produced by fear/dread** (c2/c3) as the inner affect realised in the body, and intensifying into **horror** (c6) (T6.2.1/T6.3.1–6.3.2); it is the **bodily constituent** of the fear-experience (T6.3.3). Cross-cluster partners: **rest / righteousness** (held → Session D).

## 9. Interpretive lens
Genre: **prophecy-dominant (47)** + narrative 34 — trembling in theophany/prophetic settings (Sinai, day of the LORD) (T7.2.2). Logical structure: the **worship paradox** — "Serve the LORD with fear, *and* rejoice with trembling" (Psa 2:11), fear and joy held together (T7.2.3). Anchor **Isa 66:2** uniquely locates trembling in the **contrite spirit** — the cluster's deepest, most positive constitutional case (T7.2.6). Science lens: **psychophysiology / somatic research** (Cannon; James-Lange; Damasio; Porges) — illuminating the cluster's **unusually high somatic density**, of which c5 is the chief witness (T7.3.1–7.3.2).

## 10. Inferential flags & silences
*Inferential:* trembling-as-threshold-of-restoration (Hos 11). *Silences:* mind; volition/agency/moral faculties. The somatic/constitutional reach is the load-bearing finding.

## 11. Essence
Trembling is the cluster's **constitutional witness** — fear made body. It crosses the whole spirit-soul-body range outward into shaking bones and quivering lips, and even into the quaking earth; yet its deepest and most positive form is the trembling of a **contrite spirit** at God's word, held paradoxically together with rejoicing.

# M01 c6 — Shuddering / horror: synthesis across all tiers

- **File:** `wa-m01-c06-shuddering-synth-v1_0-20260619.md` · **Date:** 2026-06-19 · **Prefix:** WA · **Version:** v1_0
- **Characteristic:** c6 — shuddering / horror (fear named as recoil/bristling). **Primary anchor:** Psa 55:5 — "Fear and trembling come upon me, and horror overwhelms me."
- **Purpose:** consolidated grounding for prose on horror, across all seven tiers. Foundation layer — not the essay.
- **Grounding source:** `WA-m01-findings-NEW-merged-bytier-v1-20260619.md`. **Discipline:** no-new-claims; tier refs and verse anchors retained; inferential/silence labels preserved. **Note:** c6 is a **thin** characteristic — several tiers are silent, recorded honestly as such.

## 1. Identity
Fear named as **recoil / bristling** — appalled revulsion (T1.1.1). Terms: H6427 *pal.la.tsut* "shuddering", H2189 *za.a.vah* "horror", H8178A / H8175A *sa.ar* "to shudder/bristle", H2113 *ze.va.ah* — OT Hebrew (T1.1.2). A **state** (recoil — status 12 / action 3) (T1.2.1), largely **nominal** (T1.4.1); name is **constitutional (flesh — bristling)** (T1.1.3); appears **simple** (T1.2.2).

## 2. God-relation, image, typology
**Agent** (6) only — the character imaged is God as the one whose acts appal (**thin**) (T0.1.1). Never God's experiencer (T0.1.2); a creaturely analogue (T0.3.2). Expresses **creaturely finitude/vulnerability** — the image under threat (T0.3.1); presence reveals the creature under threat (neutral) (T0.3.3). Typology: **silent** — no NT, no eschat/covenant/christological markers (T0.4.3).

## 3. Created purpose / design-or-fall
Neutral 14 — recoil at the appalling, **no equipping** (T0.2.1); **fallen-condition response** (T0.2.2). Immediate response: **being seized / overwhelmed** — Psa 55:5, "horror overwhelms me"; Job 18:20, "horror seizes them" — consistent (recoil) (T1.5.1–1.5.2). As a status state, its sustained form is the **continuance of the condition** (T1.6.1).

## 4. Constitution
Heart 1; soul 2; **flesh** (the **bristling flesh** — H8175A "to shudder/bristle with horror") (T2.3.1; T2.2; T2.6.1). Body-link is **expressive** — the flesh bristles, visceral recoil; direction **inner horror → bristling flesh** (soul-to-body) (T2.6.2/T2.7.1). **Silent on spirit and mind** (T2.1; T2.4). Falls upon / seizes the person (downward-onto) (T2.10.1).

## 5. Faculties
Constitutively **affective**, single-faculty (T3.4). Lighter cognitive/memory co-terms (T3.2/T3.3). **Silent** across volition, agency, moral evaluation, perception-as-faculty, creativity, conscience (T3.6–3.10).

## 6. Relational interfaces
**Silent / thin** on a person actively extending or receiving it (T4.3.4/T4.4.4). **Silent** on Godward operation (no Godward-reverent object) (T4.2.4) and on the spiritual-beings interface (T4.6.4). Relational-boundary evidence thin/silent (T4.5.4).

## 7. Over time, suffering, eschatology
Silent on transformation/sequence/mechanism/sanctification (T5.1/5.2/5.3/5.5). Present in Job in lesser measure (2 refs) (T5.4). **Silent** on eschatological trajectory (T5.6.3).

## 8. Within the cluster
Opposite: **composure** — not lexically marked; set against composure in the verse (Isa 21:4, "My heart staggers; horror has appalled me") (T1.3.1); boundary-by-contrast rather than active exclusion (T1.3.2). Distinguished from **c5 (trembling)** by quality (recoil/bristling vs shaking) and from **c7 (dismay)** by direction (recoil-from vs collapse-of) (T6.5.1). Within the terror-complex it sits **beside trembling and dismay** (Isa 21:4, horror "turned… into trembling") and is **produced by fear+trembling** as the **culminating overwhelm** (Psa 55:5) (T6.1.1/T6.2.1/T6.3.2); constitutively includes **recoil + trembling** (T6.3.3). Terror-glossed breadth spans c3/c4/c6 (T6.4.2).

## 9. Interpretive lens
Genre: **prophecy 12** — horror in prophetic oracle (T7.2.2). Anchor **Psa 55:5** uniquely stacks the **fear → trembling → horror** sequence in one verse (T7.2.6). Science lens: **psychophysiology / somatic research** (the recoil/bristling as somatic expression), alongside c5 (T7.3.1).

## 10. Inferential flags & silences
*Silences (extensive):* spirit, mind, typology, Godward operation, spiritual-beings, eschatology, sequence/mechanism, and all moral/volitional faculties. c6 is a thin, somatic, neutral-valence member — to be handled with restraint in prose.

## 11. Essence
Horror is fear as **appalled recoil** — the bristling flesh, the overwhelm that follows fear and trembling (Psa 55:5). It is a thin, neutral, somatic member of the terror-complex, set against composure, with little to say about God, the image, or the long arc.

# M01 c7 — Dismay / being shattered: synthesis across all tiers

- **File:** `wa-m01-c07-dismay-synth-v1_0-20260619.md` · **Date:** 2026-06-19 · **Prefix:** WA · **Version:** v1_0
- **Characteristic:** c7 — dismay / being shattered (fear named as collapse of composure). **Primary anchor:** Jer 1:17 — "Do not be dismayed by them, lest I dismay you before them."
- **Purpose:** consolidated grounding for prose on dismay, across all seven tiers. Foundation layer — not the essay.
- **Grounding source:** `WA-m01-findings-NEW-merged-bytier-v1-20260619.md`. **Discipline:** no-new-claims; tier refs and verse anchors retained; inferential/silence labels preserved.

## 1. Identity
Fear named as **collapse of composure** — the breaking of inner strength (T1.1.1). Terms: H0926 *ba.hal* "to dismay", H2865 *cha.tat* "to be shattered/dismayed", H0928 *be.ha.lah*, H1670 *de.a.vah*, + Aramaic H0927 *be.hal* (T1.1.2). An **event of collapse** — act-typed (action 79) but **passively undergone** (T1.2.1); **Niphal passive dominant** (37 — "one is *made* broken"), also causative Piel/Hiphil (God shatters) (T1.4.1). Name is **constitutional (inner strength broken)** (T1.1.3). A **compound** — couples collapse with **shame** (dismay + disgrace travel together) (T1.2.2).

## 2. God-relation, image, typology
**Agent** (20) — God **shatters/dismays** enemies — imaging God's **power to break** (T0.1.1). Never God's experiencer (T0.1.2); a creaturely analogue (T0.3.2). Expresses **creaturely finitude/vulnerability** — the image under collapse (T0.3.1); presence reveals the creature under threat (neutral) (T0.3.3). Typology: **silent** — no NT; eschat/covenant/christological markers absent (T0.4.3).

## 3. Created purpose / design-or-fall
Neutral 74 — **collapse of composure, not a design** (T0.2.1); **fallen-condition response** (T0.2.2). Immediate response: **composure failing, knees giving way, fleeing** — turn back, hasty word, "gave way knees" — consistent (collapse) (T1.5.1–1.5.2). Thin on sustained effect distinct from the collapse-event (T1.6).

## 4. Constitution
**Soul 5** is its leading location, with heart 3 — dismay reaches the **personal core**, the breaking of inner strength (T2.2.1–2.2.2). It carries the cluster's **second spirit-level case**: Ecc 7:9, "Be not quick in your spirit to become angry" (the *bahal* "hasty/dismayed" sense, located in the spirit) — touching the spirit's governing of disposition (T2.1.1/2.1.3). Flesh 1 (T2.6.1). **Silent on mind** (T2.4). Falls upon / seizes the person (downward-onto) (T2.10.1).

## 5. Faculties
Constitutively **affective**, single-faculty (T3.4). Lighter cognitive/memory co-terms (T3.2/T3.3). **Impairs agency** — knees give way, composure fails (T3.7). **Silent** on volition, moral evaluation, creativity, conscience at the faculty level (neutral-dominant) (T3.6/T3.8–3.10).

## 6. Relational interfaces
God object 6 (T4.2.1). At the human interface, **dismay is received from a powerful/self-disclosing party** — Gen 45:3, "his brothers could not answer him, for they were dismayed at his presence" (Joseph's self-disclosure) (T4.4.1); persons as the dismay-inspiring party (person 14) (T4.3.1). God's agent-mode is **responsive/judicial** — Jer 1:17, "Do not be dismayed by them, lest I dismay you before them" (dismay as consequence) (T4.1.2). 2 spiritual-being records (incl. Psa 104:29, creatures dismayed at God's hidden face) (T4.6.1).

## 7. Over time, suffering, eschatology
Silent on transformation/sequence/mechanism/sanctification (T5.1/5.2/5.3/5.5). **Concentrated in the suffering literature** — 10 Job/Lam refs; `cause` = "trouble coming upon him," "seeing disaster close upon them" (T5.4). **Silent** on eschatological trajectory (T5.6.3).

## 8. Within the cluster
Opposite: **rest / quiet** (*nu.ach*, *sha.an*, *sha.qat*) **and courage** (the "fear not, be not dismayed" formula) (T1.3.1); excludes composure (T1.3.2). Distinguished from **c6 (horror)** by direction (collapse-of vs recoil-from) and from **c8 (alarm)** by onset (shattering / Niphal passive vs abrupt startle) — the two share H0927 (T6.5.1). **Produced by fear** (the "fear not, neither be dismayed" pairing treats dismay as fear's collapse-product) (T6.3.1). The *chatat* root bridges **terror (c4) and dismay (c7)** (T6.4.2). Its **strongest cross-cluster partner is shame** (M07 — the shattering + the disgrace; co-term weight 41, the strongest other-characteristic partner in the cluster) — held → Session D (T6.1.1; cross-cluster register X2).

## 9. Interpretive lens
Genre: **prophecy 48 + wisdom 15** — dismay in prophetic judgement and Job (T7.2.2). Anchor **Jer 1:17** uniquely pairs **undergone and inflicted** dismay in one clause ("be not dismayed… lest I dismay you") (T7.2.6). Science lens: **psychophysiology** (the freeze/collapse register, alongside c4) (T7.3.1).

## 10. Inferential flags & silences
*Held → Session D:* the dismay↔shame pairing (X2, M07) — the strongest cross-cluster bond in M01; mark inferential where prose touches it. *Silences:* mind; typology; eschatology; sequence/mechanism; most moral/volitional faculties.

## 11. Essence
Dismay is fear as **collapse** — the shattering of inner strength, knees giving way, composure failing — undergone passively and, in God's hand, inflicted judicially ("lest I dismay you"). It reaches the soul, briefly touches the spirit, and travels with shame more than with any other characteristic.

# M01 c8 — Alarm / sudden fright: synthesis across all tiers

- **File:** `wa-m01-c08-alarm-synth-v1_0-20260619.md` · **Date:** 2026-06-19 · **Prefix:** WA · **Version:** v1_0
- **Characteristic:** c8 — alarm / sudden fright (fear named by its abruptness). **Primary anchor:** Dan 5:6 — "the king's color changed… his limbs gave way, and his knees knocked together."
- **Purpose:** consolidated grounding for prose on alarm, across all seven tiers. Foundation layer — not the essay.
- **Grounding source:** `WA-m01-findings-NEW-merged-bytier-v1-20260619.md`. **Discipline:** no-new-claims; tier refs and verse anchors retained; inferential/silence labels preserved. **Note:** small characteristic (action 14 / quality 5 / status 1); several tiers silent.

## 1. Identity
Fear named by its **abruptness** — a startle, sudden onset (T1.1.1). Terms: Aramaic **H0927 *be.hal*** (Daniel), H8429 *te.vah* "be startled" + Greek G4422/G4426 *ptoeō/pturomai* "to frighten", G1719 *emfobos* (T1.1.2). An **abrupt act** (T1.2.1), Aramaic Pael/Hithpeel + nominal — abrupt onset (T1.4.1). Name is **constitutional (limbs/colour)** and **temporal (sudden)** (T1.1.3). Appears **simple** (T1.2.2). Operates differently **by trigger** — dreams/visions (Daniel) vs sudden events (T1.4.2).

## 2. God-relation, image, typology
**Agent** (2) / **giver** (1) — God-sent alarming visions (Daniel) — imaging God as the **source of revelatory dread** (T0.1.1). Never God's experiencer (T0.1.2); a creaturely analogue (T0.3.2). Expresses **creaturely finitude** under sudden encounter (T0.3.1); presence reveals the startled creature (neutral) (T0.3.3). Typology: **christological candidate** — startle at sudden divine/uncanny manifestation (NT startle vocabulary) (T0.4.1).

## 3. Created purpose / design-or-fall
Neutral 18 — **startle, not a design** (T0.2.1); **fallen-condition response** (T0.2.2). Immediate response: **physical startle** — limbs giving way, colour changing, faces bowed (Dan 5:6 context) — consistent (somatic startle) (T1.5.1–1.5.2). Thin/near-silent on sustained effect (episodic) (T1.6.1).

## 4. Constitution
**Heart-silent** — its seat is the **body** (limbs/colour/knees, expressed in verse_text, not the location field) (T2.3.3; T2.6.1). Body-link is **indicative/expressive** — the body **registers** the sudden alarm (Dan 5:6) (T2.6.2); direction **inner startle → body** (T2.7.1). It surfaces **the thoughts** as the disturbed seat (Dan 7:28, "my thoughts greatly alarmed me") — the cognitive trigger more than a constitutional subset (T2.5.1). **Silent on spirit, soul, and mind-location** (T2.1; T2.2; T2.4).

## 5. Faculties
Constitutively **affective** (affect on all but one record, a field gap) (T3.4). Its "thoughts" are **trigger-content, not discernment** — minimal cognitive co-operation (T3.2). **Impairs agency** — limbs give way (Dan 5:6) (T3.7). **Silent** on volition, moral evaluation, perception-as-faculty, creativity, conscience (T3.6/T3.8–3.10).

## 6. Relational interfaces
**Silent** on a Godward-reverent object (T4.2.4). Startle **at a perceived spirit**: Luk 24:37, "they were startled and frightened and thought they saw a spirit" — its spiritual-beings interface (T4.6.1). The **"do not be alarmed" address** (calming) is its speech-mode (forbidden 2) (T1.4.3). Thin on giving/receiving interfaces (T4.3.4/T4.4.4); thin/silent on relational boundaries (T4.5.4).

## 7. Over time, suffering, eschatology
Silent on transformation/sequence/mechanism/sanctification (T5.1/5.2/5.3/5.5). **No Job/Lam presence** — silent on the suffering relationship (its context is the Daniel court) (T5.4.3). Present in **apocalyptic narrative** (Daniel's visions) but as **alarm at the vision**, not a trajectory toward fullness — apocalyptic-context, not eschatological-trajectory (T5.6.1).

## 8. Within the cluster
Opposite: **self-control / calm** (*enkrateia*; the "do not be alarmed" address) (T1.3.1). Distinguished from **c7 (dismay)** by onset (abrupt startle vs shattering; they share H0927) and from **c10 (astonishment)** by tone (fright vs stunned wonder; they share H8429) (T6.5.1). It is **vocabulary-bridged** to its neighbours via these two shared lemmas (T6.4.1) but shows **no productive/constitutive relation** to another characteristic (T6.3.4) and **no consistent sequence** (T6.2.3). Co-occurrence thin.

## 9. Interpretive lens
Genre: **prophecy 12 (Daniel) + gospel 6** — alarm in apocalyptic court-narrative (Daniel), requiring attention to the revelatory-vision form (T7.2.2). Anchor **Dan 5:6** uniquely renders the **somatic startle** in clinical detail (T7.2.6). Science lens: **affective neuroscience** (the startle/alarm response) (T7.3.1).

## 10. Inferential flags & silences
*Silences (extensive):* spirit, soul, heart-location, mind; suffering; sequence/mechanism; most moral/volitional faculties. A small, Daniel-centred, somatic-startle member.

## 11. Essence
Alarm is fear as **sudden somatic startle** — the king's colour changing and knees knocking (Dan 5:6) — most often triggered by a dream, vision, or uncanny appearance. It registers in the body, not the located heart, and its calming word is "do not be alarmed."

# M01 c9 — Anxiety / disquiet: synthesis across all tiers

- **File:** `wa-m01-c09-anxiety-synth-v1_0-20260619.md` · **Date:** 2026-06-19 · **Prefix:** WA · **Version:** v1_0
- **Characteristic:** c9 — anxiety / disquiet (fear as settled worried care). **Primary anchor:** Pro 12:25 — "Anxiety in a man's heart weighs him down, but a good word makes him glad."
- **Purpose:** consolidated grounding for prose on anxiety, across all seven tiers. Foundation layer — not the essay.
- **Grounding source:** `WA-m01-findings-NEW-merged-bytier-v1-20260619.md`. **Discipline:** no-new-claims; tier refs and verse anchors retained; inferential/silence labels preserved.

## 1. Identity
Fear as **settled worried care** — interior, gnawing unrest (T1.1.1). Terms: H1674 *de.a.gah* "anxiety", H8312 *sar.ap.pim* "disquieting thoughts", H7661 *sha.vats* "agony" + Aramaic H3735 *ke.ra*, Greek G0085 *ademoneo* "be distressed" (T1.1.2). A **state** of inner unrest (status 16), largely **nominal** (T1.2.1/T1.4.1). Name is **constitutional (interior)** (T1.1.3). A **cognitive compound** — couples affect with cognition: anxiety **"thinks"** (worried thought) (T1.2.2).

## 2. God-relation, image, typology
**Agent** (1) only — anxiety images **almost nothing** of God's nature; it is **near-wholly creaturely** (a significant near-silence) (T0.1.1). Never God's experiencer (T0.1.2). The silence here is **doubled**: not only is God not its experiencer, he is barely involved at all — anxiety sits **furthest from the divine image of any fear**, a purely creaturely disquiet (T0.1.3). Expresses the **limits of the finite, caring creature** (worried care), not an excellence (T0.3.1); valence-neutral (T0.3.3). Typology: NT present (Php 2, Paul's anxiety for Epaphroditus) but **no typological candidate** — silent (T0.4.3).

## 3. Created purpose / design-or-fall
Neutral 20 — its relief is **comfort/consolation** (Pro 12:25; Psa 94:19) — a condition to be relieved, not an equipping (T0.2.1). **Purely creaturely-internal, valence-neutral** — neither cultivated design nor framed as sin; the inner disquiet of the finite creature (T0.2.2). Immediate response: **the heart weighed down** — Pro 12:25, "Anxiety in a man's heart weighs him down" — consistent (weighing-down, relieved by a good word) (T1.5.1–1.5.2). Sustained, it establishes a **weighed-down, careworn** inner condition until relieved by consolation (Psa 94:19, "your consolations cheer my soul") (T1.6.1–1.6.2).

## 4. Constitution
Heart 3, soul 2, and — distinctively — the **inner parts / "entrails"** as a visceral soul-subset (the seat of churning care; heart → soul → gut) — the **most interiorly-located** fear (T2.5.1–2.5.2; T2.2). **Silent on spirit, mind, and body-part link** — it is interior (T2.1; T2.4; T2.6.3). Origin from **internal cares / external bad news** (field silent; effective source circumstantial) (T2.9.3). **Silent** on constitutional movement (T2.10.3).

## 5. Faculties
Constitutively **affective**, affect-dominant with a **cognition** blend (T3.4). **The cognitive fear** — affect+cognition (Psa 139:23, "Try me and know my thoughts!"; the "disquieting thoughts" sense): anxiety is the fear that **thinks** (worried rumination), engaging and arguably **impairing** cognition — the careworn heart weighed down (Pro 12:25) (*inferential*; T3.2). **Silent** on volition, agency, moral evaluation, perception-as-faculty, creativity, conscience (T3.6–3.10).

## 6. Relational interfaces
God object 1 — the **least God→human** of any fear (agent only 1) (T4.1.4/T4.2.1). **Thin/silent** on giving and receiving interfaces (T4.3.4/T4.4.4) and on the spiritual-beings interface (T4.6.4); thin on relational boundaries (T4.5.4). Its relief comes through a **word/consolation** extended by another (Pro 12:25; Psa 94:19).

## 7. Over time, suffering, eschatology
A genuine **relief-sequence**: anxiety **gives way to** gladness/consolation — Pro 12:25, "a good word makes him glad"; Psa 94:19, "your consolations cheer my soul" — revealing anxiety as a state **awaiting comfort**; mechanism = **encounter/intervention** (the good word) (*inferential*; T5.2.1–5.2.2/T5.3.1). **No Job/Lam presence** — silent on the suffering relationship (its context is wisdom/epistle) (T5.4.3). Silent on sanctification and on eschatological trajectory (T5.5/T5.6.3).

## 8. Within the cluster
Opposite: **comfort / consolation / gladness** (*tan.chum*, *sha.qat*) (T1.3.1); excludes gladness/comfort (T1.3.2). Distinguished from **c2 (ordinary fear)** by **tempo + faculty**: anxiety = settled, cognitive, interior (least divine involvement); ordinary fear = episodic, perceptual (T6.5.1/T1.3.3). **Vocabulary-isolated** — shares no lemma with the others (distinct root *deagah*); among the **thinnest** in co-occurrence (its partners are its consolation foils) (T6.4.4/T6.1.3); **no** productive/constitutive relation to another characteristic (T6.3.4). Cross-cluster, it borders **joy** (relief) and its consolation foils (held → Session D).

## 9. Interpretive lens
Genre: prophecy 9 + narrative 5 — anxiety across wisdom/prophecy/epistle (T7.2.2). Anchor **Pro 12:25** uniquely names anxiety's **relief by a word** (T7.2.6). Science lens: **clinical psychology — anxiety research** (Beck; Borkovec; Barlow) — the most apt lens; a flagged open question (Dugas' *intolerance of uncertainty*) on how the anxiety/perplexity register maps onto future-uncertainty, worth checking against the c9 verse evidence (T7.3.1/7.3.4).

## 10. Inferential flags & silences
*Inferential:* cognition-impairment; relief-sequence/mechanism. *Open question:* intolerance-of-uncertainty mapping (→ T7.2). *Silences:* spirit, mind, body-link; suffering(Job); sanctification; eschatology; most faculties. Its near-total **divine silence** is itself the load-bearing finding.

## 11. Essence
Anxiety is the cluster's **interior, cognitive, near-wholly creaturely** fear — the careworn, ruminating heart "weighed down," reaching even the gut, and **furthest from the divine image** of any fear. Its turn is not a virtue grown but a relief received: "a good word makes him glad."

# M01 c10 — Astonishment / being awe-struck: synthesis across all tiers

- **File:** `wa-m01-c10-astonishment-synth-v1_0-20260619.md` · **Date:** 2026-06-19 · **Prefix:** WA · **Version:** v1_0
- **Characteristic:** c10 — astonishment / being awe-struck (fear named as stunned arrest). **Primary anchor:** Hab 1:5 — "wonder and be astounded. For I am doing a work… that you would not believe" (+ Job 26:11).
- **Purpose:** consolidated grounding for prose on astonishment, across all seven tiers. Foundation layer — not the essay.
- **Grounding source:** `WA-m01-findings-NEW-merged-bytier-v1-20260619.md`. **Discipline:** no-new-claims; tier refs and verse anchors retained; inferential/silence labels preserved. **Note:** small characteristic (action 13 / status 1 / quality 1); several tiers silent or small-sample.

## 1. Identity
Fear named as **stunned arrest** — being dumbfounded; **borders awe** (T1.1.1). Terms: H8539 *ta.mah* "to be astounded" + Greek G2285 *thambos*, G1568 *ekthambeo*, G1569 *ekthambos*, Aramaic H8429 (T1.1.2). An **act/event** (a stunned reaction undergone — Qal + Greek passives) (T1.2.1/T1.4.1). **Relatively neutral as to direction** — the trigger varies (T1.1.3). Appears **simple** (T1.2.2).

## 2. God-relation, image, typology
**Agent** (1) — God's astonishing **work** as trigger: Hab 1:5 ("a work that you would not believe") — imaging God's **wonder-working** (T0.1.1). Never God's experiencer (T0.1.2); a creaturely analogue (T0.3.2). Expresses the creature **arrested before the overwhelming** — bordering the reverent acknowledgement of c1 but **stunned rather than honouring** (T0.3.1); valence-neutral (T0.3.3). Typology: **theophanic/christological** — astonishment at God's "unbelievable work" (Hab 1:5) and NT crowds astounded at Jesus' acts (T0.4.1).

## 3. Created purpose / design-or-fall
Neutral 13 — the stunned arrest before God's work; **borders wonder but not framed as equipping** (T0.2.1); **fallen-condition response** in the typology (T0.2.2). Immediate response: **being stunned / running** — panic-flight in the overwhelming case (Psa 48:5); small sample (IR n=2), consistent within the few cases but too narrow for a strong claim (T1.5.1/1.5.2).

## 4. Constitution
Heart 1; status 1 (T2.3.1). **Silent on spirit, soul, mind, and body-part link** (sparse) (T2.1; T2.2; T2.4; T2.6.3). **Silent** on constitutional movement (T2.10.3).

## 5. Faculties
Constitutively **affective** (affect on all but one record, a field gap) (T3.4). Minimal/no cognitive co-operation (T3.2). **Silent** across volition, agency, moral evaluation, perception-as-faculty, creativity, conscience (T3.5–3.10).

## 6. Relational interfaces
God object 1 — minority Godward reverence (T4.2.1). The **divine work** establishes the pattern; the human astonishment is the answering creaturely response (T0.4.2). **Thin/silent** on giving and receiving interfaces (T4.3.4/T4.4.4), relational boundaries (T4.5.4), and the spiritual-beings interface (T4.6.4).

## 7. Over time, suffering, eschatology
Silent on transformation/sequence/mechanism/sanctification (T5.1/5.2/5.3/5.5). A single Job datum (T5.4). Present in prophetic and Gospel-crowd settings; **silent** on eschatological trajectory (T5.6.3).

## 8. Within the cluster
Opposite: **composed comprehension** — the stunned arrest sits **between honour and collapse** (T1.3.1). Distinguished from **c1 (awe)** by orientation (awe **honours**; astonishment is **stunned**, not honouring — c10 ends where honouring begins) and from **c8 (alarm)** by tone (stunned wonder vs fright; they share H8429) (T6.5.1; T1.3.3). Among the **thinnest** in co-occurrence; **no** productive/constitutive relation, **no** consistent sequence (T6.2.3/T6.3.4).

## 9. Interpretive lens
Genre: prophecy 5 + gospel 6 — astonishment in prophetic and Gospel-crowd settings (T7.2.2). Anchor **Hab 1:5** uniquely ties astonishment to **God's unbelievable work** (T7.2.6). Science lens: **psychology of awe / religion** (Keltner & Haidt; Otto's *tremendum/fascinans*), alongside c1 (T7.3.1).

## 10. Inferential flags & silences
*Small-sample caveat:* immediate-response and several interfaces rest on very few records. *Silences:* spirit, soul, mind, body-link; sequence/mechanism; sanctification; eschatology; most faculties. A thin member sitting on the awe/wonder border.

## 11. Essence
Astonishment is fear as **stunned arrest** — the creature dumbfounded before God's unbelievable work (Hab 1:5). It borders awe but stops short of honouring: stunned rather than reverent, sitting between honour and collapse.

# M01 c11 — Cowardice / timidity: synthesis across all tiers

- **File:** `wa-m01-c11-cowardice-synth-v1_0-20260619.md` · **Date:** 2026-06-19 · **Prefix:** WA · **Version:** v1_0
- **Characteristic:** c11 — cowardice / timidity (fear as a moral fault). **Primary anchor:** 2Ti 1:7 — "God gave us a spirit not of fear but of power and love and self-control."
- **Purpose:** consolidated grounding for prose on cowardice, across all seven tiers. Foundation layer — not the essay.
- **Grounding source:** `WA-m01-findings-NEW-merged-bytier-v1-20260619.md`. **Discipline:** no-new-claims; tier refs and verse anchors retained; inferential/silence labels preserved. **Note:** small, NT-only characteristic (quality 3 / action 1 / status 1); the cluster's only trait/vice.

## 1. Identity
Fear named as a **moral fault** — culpable, defective fear (T1.1.1). Terms: **all NT Greek** — G1169 *deilos* "timid/cowardly", G1168 *deiliaō*, G1167 *deilia* "timidity" (T1.1.2). The cluster's **only quality-dominant member** — a **trait** (T1.2.1), nominal/adjectival, a settled disposition (T1.4.1). Name carries a **moral** implication from the outset (names a fault) (T1.1.3). Appears **simple** (T1.2.2).

## 2. God-relation, image, typology
**Giver (1) — but of its *opposite*:** 2Ti 1:7, "God gave us a spirit not of fear but of power and love and self-control." God's character is imaged **by contrast** — he is the giver of courage, not of cowardice (T0.1.1). Never God's experiencer (T0.1.2). The silence here carries a **moral edge**: the disposition God *gives* is its opposite, so the silence marks cowardice as a **disordered** creaturely state (T0.1.3). It expresses a **disordered image** (vice) (T0.3.1). Presence/absence reads **oppositely to c1**: its **presence is the disorder** — fear become vice and unbelief (sinful 4); answered by the gift of power/love/self-control; **absence** (replaced by courage) marks the rightly-ordered image (T0.3.3). Typology: **christological/redemptive by contrast** — the timidity rebuked by Christ ("Why are you afraid?", Mat 8:26) answered by his peace (Joh 14:27) and the Spirit's gift (2Ti 1:7); direction = the divine gift establishes the pattern the cowardice fails to meet (T0.4.1–0.4.2).

## 3. Created purpose / design-or-fall
**Sinful 4 / forbidden 1** — the **anti-purpose**: the failure of what the person is equipped to be, answered by the gift of "power and love and self-control" (T0.2.1). **Disordered/sinful (fall expressed as vice)** (T0.2.2). Immediate response: **failure of nerve/faith** — Mat 8:26, "Why are you afraid, O you of little faith?" (small sample, n=1) (T1.5.1/1.5.3). Sustained, it establishes **timidity as character** — a settled trait/defect; by contrast the gift establishes power/love/self-discipline (T1.6.1–1.6.2).

## 4. Constitution
Heart 1 (sparse) (T2.3.1). **Silent on spirit, soul, mind, and body-part link** (T2.1; T2.2; T2.4; T2.6.3). *(Note: 2Ti 1:7's "spirit" is read in the findings as the Spirit's gift, not a spirit-level constitutional location for cowardice — hence c11 is recorded silent on spirit-location; the second spirit-level case in the cluster is c7, Ecc 7:9.)* **Silent** on origin and on constitutional movement (T2.9/T2.10.3).

## 5. Faculties
Constitutively **affective**, single-faculty (T3.4). The **failure of volition** to act in faith (rebuked as "little faith"); its remedy is the Spirit of **self-control** (a volitional capacity) (T3.6). **Morally engaged as the negative pole** — the sinful fear, named a fault and listed among the disqualified (Rev 21:8) (T3.8). Impairs faithful relational standing (failure before Christ) (T3.11). Silent on perception, memory, creativity, conscience as faculties (T3.1–3.10).

## 6. Relational interfaces
**No Godward-reverent object** — its only God-relation is the **negative "little faith" rebuke** (T4.2.4). The one who does not overcome it remains in **little faith / faithlessness** (Mat 8:26; Rev 21:8 lists "the cowardly" with "the faithless") (T4.4.3). The disposition God did **not** give, set against the Spirit (2Ti 1:7); **Rom 8:15** names "the spirit of slavery to fall back into fear" — inferentially a vulnerability the adversary exploits (T4.6.1–4.6.2). **Thin/silent** on giving and receiving interfaces (T4.3.4/T4.4); thin on relational boundaries (T4.5.4).

## 7. Over time, suffering, eschatology
The **negative of formation** — answered by the Spirit-given power/love/self-control (2Ti 1:7), implying a sanctifying replacement (*inferential*; T5.5.1–5.5.2). **No Job/Lam presence** — silent on the suffering relationship (its context is NT moral exhortation) (T5.4.3). Its Rev 21:8 is a **judgement-verdict on the cowardly — a terminus, not a trajectory** (T5.6.1/5.6.3). Silent on transformation/sequence/mechanism in the fields (T5.1/5.2/5.3).

## 8. Within the cluster
Opposite: **power, love, self-discipline** and **peace** (*dunamis*, *sōfronismos*, *eirēnē*) — 2Ti 1:7; Joh 14:27, "Let not your hearts be troubled, neither let them be afraid" (T1.3.1). Explicitly **excludes faith** ("O you of little faith") and the Spirit-given power/love/self-discipline (T1.3.2). **c11 ≠ all** — the only one that is a **trait** and chiefly **sinful**; sharply set apart, needing no fine boundary-drawing (T1.3.3/T6.5.1/6.5.4). **Vocabulary-isolated** — distinct root (*deilia*), shares no lemma with the others; among the **thinnest** in co-occurrence (its partners are its power/love/self-discipline contrast); **no** productive/constitutive relation to another characteristic (T6.4.4/T6.1.3/6.3.4). Cross-cluster: the **fear-vs-faith/unbelief** node — cowardice as faithlessness is the key node (held → Session D; register X8).

## 9. Interpretive lens
Genre: **gospel 3 + epistle 1 + apocalyptic 1** — cowardice in NT moral exhortation, read against the Gospel rebukes and epistolary ethics (T7.2.2). Logical structure: the **contrast/antithesis** — "a spirit **not** of fear **but** of power and love and self-control" (2Ti 1:7) (T7.2.3). Anchor **2Ti 1:7** uniquely names fear's **divinely-given antidote** (T7.2.6). Science lens: bears on the **normativity divergence** (T7.3.3) — science has no category for fear-as-vice; cowardice is treated **categorically** as a moral fault, a theological, not clinical, framing.

## 10. Inferential flags & silences
*Inferential:* sanctifying-replacement reading; adversarial-vulnerability reading. *Silences:* spirit, soul, mind, body-link; suffering; sequence/mechanism; most faculties. *Boundary clarification carried:* 2Ti 1:7 "spirit" is the Spirit's gift, not a spirit-level location for cowardice (recorded divergence from the OLD findings, which read it as spirit-location).

## 11. Essence
Cowardice is the cluster's **single vice** — fear become moral fault and unbelief, the failure of nerve rebuked by Christ ("Why are you afraid, O you of little faith?") and listed among the disqualified (Rev 21:8). It is answered not by another fear but by a gift: "a spirit not of fear but of power and love and self-control."

# M02 · C5 — Indignation / Displeasure / Sullenness — Tier Catalogue Analysis

- **File:** wa-m02-c5-indignation-tieranalysis-v1_0-20260619.md · **Date:** 2026-06-19
- **Cluster / Characteristic:** M02 "Anger, Wrath and Indignation" · C5 Indignation / displeasure / sullenness
- **Version:** v1_0 · **Author:** le Roux Cilliers
- **Prior output (this session):** wa-m02-c4-jealousy-zeal-tieranalysis-v1_0-20260619.md
- **Catalogue answered:** WA-tier-catalogue-current-state-v2-20260619.md (126 questions, T0–T7) · **Science lens (T7.3):** wa-m02-anger-scienceextract-v1_0-20260513.md

**Change control (v1_0):** First issue. All 126 questions answered for C5. **valence is used** (CC-confirmed current 2026-06-19; the extract's PARKED marker is out of date).

**Evidence basis.** C5 = 49 focus-occurrences (OT 48 / NT 1): zaˈam (noun "indignation" 22; verb "be indignant" 11), zaˈaph (6+4), zalˈaˈphah "scorching" (3), zaˈeph "vexed/sullen" (2), aganaktēsis (1). Concentrated in Psalms (7), Isaiah (7), Proverbs (5), Daniel (4). valence: neutral 29, sinful 7, righteous 4, forbidden 2. Every observation cited; "Silent." where C5 verses do not speak. A consolidated Evidence Base follows the answers.

**Three strands (data-derived).** (i) **Human displeasure / sullenness** — Ahab "sullen and angry" (1Ki 20:43; 21:4), the cupbearer and baker "troubled/dejected" (Gen 40:6). (ii) **Denunciation / cursing** — Balaam summoned to "denounce" Israel (zaˈam, Num 23:7–8; senses "abhorred/accursed"). (iii) **Divine indignation** — God's "indignation" as judicial fury (Psa 69:24; 78:49 "wrath, indignation"; Isa 10:5,25 "the staff of my indignation"; Isa 13:5 "weapons of his indignation"; div_role possessor 13, agent 5). One **positive NT** case: "godly grief... what indignation!" (2Cor 7:11, aganaktēsis, righteous).

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**T0.1.1** — Relation to God: God is frequently the **possessor/agent** of indignation — "his wrath and indignation" (Psa 78:49); "the rod of my anger... the staff of my indignation" (Isa 10:5); "weapons of his indignation" (Isa 13:5). God is also the **object** of misdirected human rage — "a man's folly... his heart rages against the LORD" (Pro 19:3). Both relations occur; many human occurrences have no God-relation (1Ki 20:43).

**T0.1.2** — Across C5 indignation is **borne by God** (Psa 69:24; Isa 10:25; Mal 1:4) and by the **creature** (Ahab, 1Ki 21:4; Balaam, Num 23:7). *Interpretation:* indignation is a shared characteristic — God's settled judicial displeasure and the person's displeasure (rightly, 2Cor 7:11; or sullenly, 1Ki 21:4).

**T0.2.1** — Stated purpose/effect: God's indignation **executes judgment** — "let your burning anger / indignation overtake them" (Psa 69:24); it is the "staff" by which God strikes (Isa 10:5); it "ends" when its corrective work is done (Isa 10:25). Human sullen indignation produces **withdrawal** (Ahab "would eat no food," 1Ki 21:4). Godly indignation produces **earnest self-clearing** (2Cor 7:11). Record none where unstated.

**T0.2.2** — valence confirms **both**: neutral 29 (descriptive of God's judicial indignation, Isa 13:5) and a moral split — **righteous 4** (godly indignation, 2Cor 7:11; Psa 119:53 "hot indignation... because of the wicked"), **sinful 7 / forbidden 2** (sullen self-pity, 1Ki 21:4; rage against God, Pro 19:3). Divine indignation belongs to holy design; sullen human indignation to the fallen condition.

**T0.2.3** — Future-fullness orientation: yes — divine indignation is oriented to a **determined end / appointed time** ("the indignation... till the indignation is accomplished," Dan 11:36; Isa 10:25 "in a very little while my indignation will come to an end"; Zep 3:8 "the day when I rise up"). It points to an appointed consummation of judgment.

**T0.3.1** — Divine-likeness aspect: the aspect instantiated in the person is **righteous displeasure at evil** — "hot indignation... because of the wicked who forsake your law" (Psa 119:53), and the "indignation" of godly repentance (2Cor 7:11). Sullen self-pity (1Ki 21:4) images nothing of God.

**T0.3.2** — Shared: indignation is borne by God (Isa 10:5) and the person (2Cor 7:11) under related vocabulary; it is a divine judicial attribute the creature reflects rightly or distorts into sulking.

**T0.3.3** — Where right indignation is present it indicates **alignment with God's moral order** (Psa 119:53; 2Cor 7:11); where sullen indignation is present it indicates **wounded self-will** (1Ki 21:4 Ahab over a vineyard); where God's indignation rests on a person it indicates they stand **under judgment** (Mic 7:9 "I will bear the indignation of the LORD because I have sinned").

**T0.4.1** — Typological use: divine indignation is given an **eschatological-apocalyptic** register in Daniel — "what shall happen in the latter time of the indignation" (Dan 8:19; 11:36) — the divine instance establishing the pattern of the appointed end-time wrath. Direction: divine instance outward. Elsewhere none.

---

## T1 — Definition

**T1.1.1** — Programme name: **Indignation / displeasure / sullenness**. The name signals a **cooler, settled displeasure** — moral indignation, judicial fury, or sullen vexation — distinct from hot kindled rage. Senses: indignation 18, fury 5, sullen 2, "denounce."

**T1.1.2** — Primary terms: zaˈam (noun/verb, "indignation; to be indignant / to denounce, curse") — its root carries **to foam/be enraged** and **to denounce/curse**; zaˈaph ("rage, be vexed/sullen"); zalˈaˈphah ("scorching/burning heat"); aganaktēsis (Greek, "indignation"). Definitionally a **displeasure that condemns** — and at one edge **curses** (Num 23:7–8).

**T1.1.3** — Directional/relational: indignation is directed **against** wrongdoers (Psa 69:24; 119:53), expressed **toward** a denounced party (Num 23:7), or turned **inward** as sullenness (1Ki 21:4). It carries a condemnatory direction.

**T1.2.1** — Mainly a **condition/status** (noun forms, 32 — "the indignation of the LORD," Mic 7:9) with an **act** strand (verb forms, 15 — "denounce," Num 23:8; "be indignant") and a small **quality** (2 — "sullen," zaˈeph, 1Ki 20:43 as a descriptive state).

**T1.2.2** — **Compound**: indignation fuses with **wrath/anger** ("his wrath, indignation, and distress," Psa 78:49; "fury... indignation," Isa 30:27 context) and with **grief** in the godly case (2Cor 7:11 "godly grief... indignation"). The sullen form fuses displeasure with **dejection** (1Ki 21:4). Rarely simple.

**T1.3.1** — Structural opposite: **favour / good pleasure** — implied where indignation is the negative of God's favour ("his indignation" vs the restored "his hand... known to his servants," Isa 66:14 context). Contentment stands against sullenness.

**T1.3.2** — At its edge it excludes **acceptance/blessing**: Balaam cannot "denounce" (zaˈam) whom God has not denounced — "How can I denounce whom the LORD has not denounced?" (Num 23:8). Indignation resists where God has blessed.

**T1.3.3** — It ends where **hot rage** (C1/C2) begins (indignation is cooler, often moral or sulking) and where **grief** (M03) begins (the sullen/dejected edge, 1Ki 21:4; 2Cor 7:11 pairs it with grief). It is displeasure-with-condemnation, not mere heat.

**T1.4.1** — Modes: as **settled judicial fury** (a "staff/rod," Isa 10:5); as a **denouncing speech-act** (Num 23:7–8 "come, denounce"); as **scorching heat** (zalˈaˈphah, Psa 11:6 "scorching wind"); as **sullen withdrawal** (Ahab "vexed and sullen," 1Ki 20:43; 21:4); as **seizing affect** ("hot indignation seizes me," Psa 119:53). Multiple modes.

**T1.4.2** — Yes — mode varies: **divine** indignation as judicial instrument (Isa 10:5); **human moral** indignation as righteous heat (Psa 119:53); **human sullen** indignation as dejected withdrawal (1Ki 21:4); **denunciatory** indignation as curse-speech (Num 23:7). Distinct registers.

**T1.4.3** — Communicative/spoken mode: yes, prominently — indignation is exercised as **denunciation/cursing** (Num 23:7–8 "denounce"), and God **declares** his indignation (Eze 21:31 "I will pour out my indignation"; Mal 1:4). Recorded.

**T1.5.1** — Immediate response: Ahab's indignation issues in **lying down, turning his face away, refusing food** (1Ki 21:4); divine indignation issues in **judgment let loose** (Psa 78:49); godly indignation issues in **earnestness and self-clearing** (2Cor 7:11). Record none where unstated (Num 23:7).

**T1.5.2** — Varied: sullen withdrawal (1Ki 21:4), executed judgment (Psa 69:24), or zealous self-correction (2Cor 7:11). No single immediate response.

**T1.6.1** — Sustained effect: God's indignation, sustained, **devastates** ("the indignation of the LORD... his fury," Jer 50:25; Lam 2 context) and is bounded to an **appointed end** (Isa 10:25; Dan 11:36). Sullen human indignation, sustained, festers into **plotting** (Ahab's sullenness → Jezebel's plot, 1Ki 21:4–7). Record none where unstated.

**T1.6.3** — Immediate response is the flash (withdrawal/judgment); sustained effect is the **accumulated devastation or festering scheme** (Isa 10:25; 1Ki 21:7). Episode vs settled consequence.

**T1.7.1** — It "takes hold rightly" (valence righteous) where it is **moral indignation at evil** — "hot indignation... because of the wicked who forsake your law" (Psa 119:53) and the indignation of genuine repentance (2Cor 7:11). The condition is alignment with God's standard.

**T1.7.2** — It is **distorted** (valence sinful/forbidden) as **sullen self-pity** (Ahab over a denied vineyard, 1Ki 21:4) or **rage against God** for one's own folly (Pro 19:3 "his heart rages against the LORD"). The denunciation form is **blocked** where God has blessed — Balaam cannot curse Israel (Num 23:8). No verse attributes the indignation to another spirit — **silent** on that.

**T1.7.3** — Where indignation is present but does not take hold rightly, the person is shown **sullen, withdrawn, and self-harming** (Ahab, 1Ki 21:4) or **blaming God for self-caused ruin** (Pro 19:3).

---

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**T2.1.1** — Locations: **heart** — "his heart rages against the LORD" (Pro 19:3); the restored "hand of the LORD... his indignation against his enemies" set against the servants whose "heart shall rejoice" (Isa 66:14); **flesh** — "there is no soundness in my flesh because of your indignation" (Psa 38:3). 46/49 locate no seat (Num 23:7) — record none.

**T2.1.2** — The pattern: where located, indignation reaches the **heart** (its raging seat, Pro 19:3) and even the **flesh/body** under divine indignation ("no soundness in my flesh," Psa 38:3) — a notable somatic link. The body link is **expressive/indicative** of the inner displeasure or of judgment felt bodily.

**T2.10.1** — Movement: divine indignation moves **onto the person from God** — "let loose... his indignation" (Psa 78:49), "poured out" (Eze 21:31), and is **received-from-outside** (Dan 1:10 the official's fear of the king's displeasure). Sullen indignation arises **within** (1Ki 21:4). No angelic introduction. Record the onsets shown.

**T2.7.1** — Body direction: where a body link exists it runs **inner displeasure / divine indignation expressing into the body** — "no soundness in my flesh because of your indignation" (Psa 38:3), the heart that "rages" (Pro 19:3). Inner/divine-to-body. No body-to-soul feedback — **silent**.

**T2.9.1** — Origin: **within the person** for sullen/moral indignation (1Ki 21:4; Psa 119:53); **from God** for divine indignation (Psa 78:49 "his indignation"); and, in the godly case, produced **by godly grief** ("godly grief produces... what indignation," 2Cor 7:11). Multiple origins.

**T2.9.2** — Origin is **multiple** and context-dependent — within-person sullenness, divine bestowal of judicial indignation, and grief-produced righteous indignation (2Cor 7:11). It changes with context.

---

## T3 — The Inner Faculties

**T3.1.1** — Perception: indignation is triggered by what is **seen/heard** — Psalmist's hot indignation "because of the wicked" he observes (Psa 119:53); Ahab's sullenness on **hearing** Naboth's refusal (1Ki 21:4); the king's "displeasure" feared by sight (Dan 1:10). Perception is the gate.

**T3.1.2** — Effect on perception: sullen indignation **narrows** perception to the grievance (Ahab fixed on the vineyard, 1Ki 21:4). No verse states it distorting the senses generally — otherwise **silent**.

**T3.1.3** — Pattern: indignation is **perception-triggered** (a perceived wrong or denial), confirming its responsive, evaluative nature.

**T3.2.1** — Cognition: engaged as **moral appraisal** — the indignation "because of the wicked who forsake your law" is a judgment of their wrong (Psa 119:53); divine indignation follows God's reckoning of sin (Mic 7:9 "because I have sinned"). 

**T3.2.2** — Effect on cognition: sullen indignation **clouds** judgment toward self-pity and plotting (1Ki 21:4–7); godly indignation **sharpens** moral resolve (2Cor 7:11 "what earnestness... what indignation"). Both directions.

**T3.2.3** — Pattern: indignation is **appraisal-bound** — it rests on a judgment of wrong and reshapes the mind toward either festering or earnestness.

**T3.3.1** — Memory: thin — sullen indignation **holds** a grievance (Ahab, 1Ki 21:4); divine indignation recalls covenant sin (Mic 7:9). Direct memory-faculty engagement is limited — mostly **silent**.

**T3.3.2** — **Silent** on indignation acting on a memory faculty.

**T3.3.3** — The thinness indicates indignation is framed as **present displeasure**, with remembered grievance as backdrop.

**T3.4.1** — Affect: the core faculty (45/49 affect) — indignation is an **emotional state of condemnatory displeasure** (Num 23:7; 1Ki 21:4; Psa 119:53).

**T3.4.2** — Effect on affect: it can **darken** the affective field into sullenness (1Ki 21:4) or **intensify** moral feeling (Psa 119:53 "hot indignation"); paired with grief in 2Cor 7:11. 

**T3.4.3** — That affect dominates confirms indignation as a genuine **emotion**, distinct from hot rage by its cooler, often sulking or judicial register.

**T3.5.1** — Creativity: not engaged. **Silent.**

**T3.5.2** — **Silent.**

**T3.5.3** — Absence indicates no relation to the originative faculty.

**T3.6.1** — Volition: engaged where indignation **drives or withholds** action — Balaam is summoned to *choose* to denounce but cannot (Num 23:8); Ahab's sullen will **refuses** food and action (1Ki 21:4); godly indignation **mobilises** the will to set things right (2Cor 7:11). 

**T3.6.2** — Effect on volition: sullen indignation **paralyses/redirects** the will toward self-pity or scheming (1Ki 21:4–7); righteous indignation **energises** the will toward correction (2Cor 7:11).

**T3.6.3** — Pattern: indignation strongly engages the **will** at both poles — it must be governed lest it sour into sullen scheming.

**T3.7.1** — Agency: divine indignation is intensely **action-issuing** (the "staff" that strikes, Isa 10:5; "let loose" judgment, Psa 78:49); human indignation issues in **denunciation** (Num 23:7) or, sullenly, in **withdrawal/plotting** (1Ki 21:4–7).

**T3.7.2** — Effect on agency: it **drives** judgment (Isa 10:5), curse-speech (Num 23:7), corrective zeal (2Cor 7:11), or scheming injustice (1Ki 21:7).

**T3.7.3** — The indignation→act pattern marks it as **agency-generating**, for judgment, denunciation, or (sullenly) plotting.

**T3.8.1** — Moral evaluation: directly engaged — indignation *is* the affective form of a **condemnatory verdict** (Psa 119:53 against lawbreakers; God's indignation against sin, Mic 7:9; godly indignation, 2Cor 7:11). valence: righteous 4, sinful 7, forbidden 2.

**T3.8.2** — Effect: it **enacts** a moral verdict — righteous indignation condemns evil rightly (Psa 119:53; 2Cor 7:11); sullen indignation passes a **self-serving** false verdict (Ahab feels wronged over a just refusal, 1Ki 21:4).

**T3.8.3** — Pattern: indignation is **morally tri-valued** — God's righteous judicial indignation (Isa 10:5), the believer's righteous moral indignation (Psa 119:53; 2Cor 7:11), and sinful sullen self-pity (1Ki 21:4). Its morality depends on the justice of its grievance.

**T3.9.1** — Conscience: engaged where indignation is **borne as deserved judgment** under a guilty conscience — "I will bear the indignation of the LORD because I have sinned against him" (Mic 7:9). The acute witness of guilt accepts the indignation.

**T3.9.2** — Effect on conscience: the guilty conscience **submits** to the indignation as just (Mic 7:9). Recorded; elsewhere not stated.

**T3.9.3** — The Mic 7:9 case indicates indignation can engage conscience as **acknowledged just desert**, though this is a single clear instance.

**T3.10.1** — Conscientiousness: engaged in the godly case — indignation as part of the **integrated** repentant response ("godly grief produces... earnestness... indignation... zeal," 2Cor 7:11). Sullen indignation is the **failure** of integration (self-pity over a just denial, 1Ki 21:4).

**T3.10.2** — Effect: integrated righteous indignation **drives reform** (2Cor 7:11); unintegrated sullen indignation **drives injustice** (1Ki 21:7).

**T3.10.3** — The pattern marks indignation as a **moral test-site** — rightly integrated it is the indignation of repentance; wrongly, the sulk that schemes.

**T3.11.1** — Relational capacity: indignation is **relational** — directed against wrongdoers (Psa 119:53), expressed in denunciation of a people (Num 23:7), or souring a relationship (Ahab toward Naboth, 1Ki 21:4). It engages the bond.

**T3.11.2** — Effect on relational capacity: sullen indignation **damages** relationships (it leads to Naboth's judicial murder, 1Ki 21:4–13); righteous indignation **restores** community integrity (2Cor 7:11 the church's self-clearing). Both poles.

**T3.11.3** — The pattern shows indignation is **relationally embedded** — it arises against another and bears on the relationship for ill (sullen scheming) or good (corrective indignation).

---

## T4 — Relational Interfaces

**T4.1.1** — God-toward-human: yes — God's indignation operates from God toward persons/nations — "let your indignation overtake them" (Psa 69:24); the Assyrian "rod of my anger... staff of my indignation" sent against a godless nation (Isa 10:5–6); "weapons of his indignation" (Isa 13:5).

**T4.1.2** — Basis: **responsive/judicial** — extended in response to sin and covenant violation (Mic 7:9 "because I have sinned"; Isa 10:6 against "a godless nation"). Conditional on wrong; bounded to an appointed end (Isa 10:25).

**T4.1.3** — What it shows of God's disposition: God is **morally reactive to evil** — His indignation measures His opposition to sin, yet is **bounded and purposive** (Isa 10:25 "in a very little while... my indignation will come to an end"), showing restraint within judgment.

**T4.2.1** — Human-to-God: yes — the person **bears** God's indignation penitently (Mic 7:9), and (wrongly) **rages against** God for self-caused ruin (Pro 19:3 "his heart rages against the LORD"). The movement is the person's posture under or against God's displeasure.

**T4.2.2** — Inner posture required: **submission and confession** ("I will bear the indignation of the LORD... until he pleads my cause," Mic 7:9) — the right posture; the wrong posture is **blame-shifting rage** (Pro 19:3).

**T4.2.3** — What it shows: penitent bearing of indignation shows a **hope-filled, submissive** relationship (Mic 7:9 expects vindication); raging against God shows a **disordered** one (Pro 19:3).

**T4.3.1** — Person-to-person extension: yes — indignation/denunciation is extended toward another (Balaam hired to "denounce" Israel, Num 23:7); sullen indignation is "extended" as cold withdrawal/scheming toward Naboth (1Ki 21:4 ff.).

**T4.3.2** — Inner conditions accompanying it: **moral judgment** in the righteous case (Psa 119:53), **wounded entitlement** in the sullen case (1Ki 21:4), **hireling malice** in the denunciation case (Num 23:7 Balak's purpose).

**T4.3.3** — What the giver must have/become: the evidence states no required prior state for indignation; the denouncer's curse is **void unless God concurs** (Num 23:8 — one cannot denounce whom God has not denounced). Recorded.

**T4.4.1** — Receiving: the object of indignation **receives** judgment/denunciation — Israel is the intended object of Balaam's denunciation (Num 23:7), the wicked the object of divine indignation (Psa 69:24). Uptake is endured, not adopted.

**T4.4.2** — Conditions of uptake: **guilt** draws deserved indignation (Mic 7:9); **God's protection** blocks undeserved denunciation (Num 23:8 Israel cannot be cursed). 

**T4.4.3** — The person who meets indignation justly bears it **penitently and hopefully** (Mic 7:9); the one wrongly denounced is **shielded** (Num 23:8).

**T4.5.1** — Within bonds vs across distance: indignation operates **within bonds** (Ahab toward his subject Naboth, 1Ki 21:4; God toward His covenant people, Mic 7:9) and **across** them (God's indignation on the nations, Isa 13:5; 34:2 context). Both.

**T4.5.2** — Covenantal scope: divine indignation operates **within the covenant** (against His sinning people, Mic 7:9) and **crosses** to the nations (Isa 13:5; Mal 1:4 against Edom). Both.

**T4.5.3** — Relational scope: **wide** — God (Pro 19:3 as object), His people (Mic 7:9), the nations (Isa 13:5; Mal 1:4), a subject (1Ki 21:4), a hostile people (Num 23:7). Indignation reaches across the relational field.

**T4.6.1** — Spiritual beings: not shown operating toward angelic/adversarial beings. **Silent.**

**T4.6.2** — Adversarial site: not evidenced as a site of adversarial weaponising. **Silent** (recorded as not evidenced).

**T4.6.3** — Angelic mediation: divine indignation is at times executed **through a human instrument** (Assyria as the "staff of my indignation," Isa 10:5) — an instrumental mediation of judgment, though human, not angelic. Recorded; otherwise silent on angelic mediation.

---

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

**T5.1.1** — Transformation: indignation transforms **condition** — divine indignation lays a nation low (Isa 10:5–6); godly indignation transforms a repentant community ("at every point you have proved yourselves innocent," 2Cor 7:11). Record none where unstated.

**T5.1.2** — Reversible/irreversible: divine indignation is **bounded/reversible** ("in a very little while my indignation will come to an end," Isa 10:25; "until he pleads my cause," Mic 7:9); sullen indignation hardens into **executed** injustice once acted on (1Ki 21:13). Both.

**T5.2.1** — Sequence: **perceived wrong → sullen indignation → withdrawal → scheme/act** (Ahab, 1Ki 21:4–7,13); **godly grief → indignation → earnest reform** (2Cor 7:11); **sin → divine indignation → judgment → appointed end** (Isa 10:5–6,25). Record none where no sequence appears.

**T5.3.1** — Mechanism of change: **judgment** (divine indignation as the instrument, Isa 10:5) and **repentant grief** (the mechanism producing righteous indignation, 2Cor 7:11). Record none where unstated.

**T5.3.2** — Differs: divine indignation works change by **judicial striking** (Isa 10:5); godly indignation by **grief-driven self-correction** (2Cor 7:11); sullen indignation by **festering into scheme** (1Ki 21:7). Context-dependent.

**T5.4.1** — Relation to suffering: indignation **produces suffering** (divine indignation as affliction — "no soundness in my flesh because of your indignation," Psa 38:3) and is **produced by** suffering/grievance (Ahab's denied desire, 1Ki 21:4; the prophet "sat alone... filled with indignation," Jer 15:17 amid his affliction).

**T5.4.2** — What suffering does to it: affliction under God's indignation drives the sufferer to **confession and hope** (Mic 7:9; Psa 38:3–4,18 confession); the prophet's suffering-borne indignation drives him to **lament before God** (Jer 15:17–18). Suffering can turn indignation Godward.

**T5.5.1** — Sanctification arc: indignation participates — godly indignation is part of the **repentant transformation** that sanctifies a community (2Cor 7:11); the believer's hot indignation at lawlessness is a mark of **formed loyalty** to God's law (Psa 119:53). The sullen form is the anti-formative failure (1Ki 21:4).

**T5.6.1** — Eschatological orientation: yes — divine indignation is oriented to the **appointed "time of the indignation"** (Dan 8:19; 11:36) and the **day** of God's rising (Zep 3:8). Its present operation anticipates that consummation.

---

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics

**T6.1.1** — Co-occurring characteristics: **wrath/anger** ("his wrath, indignation, and distress," Psa 78:49; indignation beside fury, Isa 30:27 context — C1/C2), **grief** ("godly grief... indignation," 2Cor 7:11 — M03), and **denunciation/cursing** (Num 23:7–8). Strong pairing with wrath and, in the godly case, grief.

**T6.1.2** — Co-occurrence places C5 **adjacent to wrath** (as a cooler/judicial member) and bridging toward **grief** (the sullen/dejected and godly-grief edges) — it sits between hot anger and sorrow.

**T6.2.1** — Sequence: indignation **follows** a perceived/actual wrong and **precedes** judgment, withdrawal, or reform (Isa 10:5–6; 1Ki 21:4–7; 2Cor 7:11). It also **accompanies** wrath as a paired term (Psa 78:49).

**T6.2.2** — The relationship is **causal/developmental**: grievance causes indignation; indignation causes judgment/scheme/reform (Isa 10:6; 1Ki 21:7; 2Cor 7:11).

**T6.3.1** — Produces: indignation **produces** judgment (Isa 10:6), bodily affliction (Psa 38:3), corrective zeal (2Cor 7:11), or sullen scheming (1Ki 21:7).

**T6.3.2** — Produced by: indignation is **produced by** perceived wrong (Psa 119:53), denied desire (1Ki 21:4), godly grief (2Cor 7:11), and divine reckoning of sin (Mic 7:9).

**T6.3.3** — Constituent relation: indignation is a **constituent** of the wrath-complex (paired with wrath/distress, Psa 78:49) and of the godly-repentance complex (a constituent alongside earnestness and zeal, 2Cor 7:11).

**T6.4.1** — Shared vocabulary: the zaˈam/zaˈaph family is **distinct** from the burning-anger lemmas but is **collocated** with cheˈmah/aph/qeˈtseph (Psa 78:49; Isa 30:27 context) — shared collocation, not shared lemma. aganaktēsis is the NT indignation term, distinct from orgē.

**T6.4.2** — Root-level: the zaˈam and zaˈaph roots generate the indignation/rage/scorching senses within C5; they do **not** share a root with the burning-anger family — the link is conceptual/collocational.

**T6.4.3** — The vocabulary picture shows C5 is a **distinct, cooler displeasure** with its own roots, related to wrath by collocation and to grief by the sullen/dejected edge.

**T6.5.1** — Nearest neighbour: **C1/C2 anger/wrath** (indignation is paired with and shades into wrath, Psa 78:49). Distinction: indignation is **cooler and more judicial/moral or sullen** — "indignation" and "denounce" rather than "burning kindled."

**T6.5.2** — Apparent overlap: where zaˈam is rendered "fury/wrath" (senses fury 5, wrath 2) it overlaps C1/C2; the **precise boundary** is temperature and register — settled/judicial/sulking displeasure (C5) vs hot kindled heat (C1/C2). The **denunciation** sense (Num 23:7) and the **sullen** sense (1Ki 21:4) are distinctively C5.

**T6.5.3** — Distinction from C1/C2 is one of **degree/register** (cooler, judicial, or sulking vs hot), and from grief (M03) one of **direction** (condemnatory displeasure vs sorrow), though the sullen edge touches grief.

---

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**T7.1.1** — Primary terms/roots: **zaˈam** (H2194/H2195, "to be indignant; to denounce/curse"; noun "indignation") — root sense of **foaming/denouncing**; **zaˈaph** (H2196/H2197, "to rage, be vexed/sullen"); **zalˈaˈphah** (H2152, "scorching heat"); Greek **aganaktēsis** ("indignation"). Roots converge on **condemnatory displeasure**, with a denouncing/cursing edge.

**T7.1.2** — Grammatical range: **noun/status** dominant (32; "indignation," Mic 7:9), **verb/action** (15; "denounce," Num 23:8), **adjective/quality** (2; "sullen," zaˈeph, 1Ki 20:43). The range shows indignation as a settled **state**, a **denouncing act**, and a sullen **trait/mood**.

**T7.1.3** — Semantic range: from "indignation/fury" (Psa 78:49) through "denounce/abhor/accursed" (Num 23:7–8) and "scorching" (zalˈaˈphah, Psa 11:6) to "sullen/vexed" (1Ki 21:4) and the godly "indignation" of repentance (2Cor 7:11). Breadth: judicial fury → denunciation → scorching → sulking → righteous indignation.

**T7.1.4** — Distinguishing terms: **condition vs act** — zaˈam (the state of indignation) vs the verb "denounce"; **mood/quality** — zaˈeph "sullen" (1Ki 20:43). The denunciation sense is a distinct aspect within the same root.

**T7.1.5** — Opposite/absence term: not a single lexeme; the opposite is carried by **blessing/favour** (Num 23:8 — to "bless" vs "denounce"; Isa 66:14 indignation vs the servants' rejoicing). Idiomatic.

**T7.1.6** — Person-type term: the adjective **zaˈeph "sullen"** describes a person's state (1Ki 20:43; 21:4) — a quality/mood-term rather than a fixed person-type noun. Record: a mood-adjective, no settled person-type noun.

**T7.1.7** — Supplication/seeking term: none — no term for seeking indignation. Record none.

**T7.1.8** — OT→NT relationship: the Hebrew zaˈam/zaˈaph indignation family is represented in the NT by **aganaktēsis** (2Cor 7:11), where indignation appears in a **positive, sanctifying** light (the fruit of godly grief) — a notable development from the predominantly judicial/sullen OT range. Continuity of the concept; development toward a redeemable register.

**T7.1.9** — NT-coined term: **aganaktēsis** (and the verb aganakteō) is the NT indignation term; not newly coined but applied here to **righteous repentant indignation** (2Cor 7:11). Record the refined positive use.

**T7.1.10** — Full vocabulary arc: from OT **judicial/denunciatory/sullen** displeasure (zaˈam/zaˈaph) to NT **righteous repentant** indignation (aganaktēsis) — an arc from condemnation and sulking to sanctified moral indignation.

**T7.2.1** — Function of the primary term in its primary verse: in Num 23:7–8 zaˈam ("denounce") is the **verb Balaam is hired to perform and cannot** — the term carries the whole drama of the failed curse ("How can I denounce whom the LORD has not denounced?"). In Isa 10:5 "indignation" is the **noun defining the Assyrian's commission** as God's instrument.

**T7.2.2** — Literary forms: **narrative** (Gen 40:6; 1Ki 20:43; 21:4; Num 23), **psalm** (Psa 69:24; 78:49; 119:53), **wisdom** (Pro 19:3; 22:14), **prophecy** (Isa 10:5; 13:5; Mic 7:9; Mal 1:4), **apocalyptic** (Dan 8:19; 11:36), **NT epistle** (2Cor 7:11). Responsible reading distinguishes the judicial-prophetic texts, the sullen-narrative episodes, and the single NT repentance text (BOOK distribution: Psa 7, Isa 7, Pro 5, Dan 4).

**T7.2.3** — Logical structure: **judicial-consequential** in the divine texts — sin/godlessness → the staff of indignation → bounded judgment (Isa 10:5–6,25); **narrative-causal** in the sullen texts — denial → sullen indignation → scheme (1Ki 21:4–7); **fruit-structure** in the NT — godly grief → indignation among its fruits (2Cor 7:11).

**T7.2.4** — Contextual settings: **judicial/prophetic** (Isa 10:5; Mic 7:9), **royal-narrative** (1Ki 21:4), **liturgical-imprecatory** (Psa 69:24; 119:53), **apocalyptic** (Dan 11:36), **pastoral-epistolary** (2Cor 7:11). The settings show indignation as judicial instrument, sulking royal vice, imprecatory zeal, and repentant fruit.

**T7.2.5** — Primary anchor verse: **2 Corinthians 7:11** for the redeemed pole ("godly grief... what indignation, what fear, what longing, what zeal") and **Isaiah 10:5** for the divine-judicial pole ("the rod of my anger... the staff of my indignation"). Together they most fully express C5's range — righteous repentant indignation and God's bounded judicial indignation.

**T7.2.6** — These anchors show what no single verse shows alone: 2Cor 7:11 that indignation can be a **sanctifying fruit of grief**; Isa 10:5 that divine indignation is a **commissioned, bounded instrument of judgment** — the cooler, judicial-and-moral character that distinguishes C5 from hot rage.

**T7.3.1** — Most useful human-science lens: per the science extract, **moral psychology** — indignation is treated there as "moral anger... triggered by norm violation rather than personal frustration," a distinct moral emotion (Haidt; third-party punishment; justice sensitivity).

**T7.3.2** — Where the framework illuminates: the moral-anger account illuminates the **righteous** indignation texts — "hot indignation... because of the wicked who forsake your law" (Psa 119:53) and the repentant indignation of 2Cor 7:11 are precisely norm-violation-triggered moral anger; justice sensitivity illuminates why such indignation is commended. The trait-mood account illuminates the **sullen** disposition (Ahab, 1Ki 20:43).

**T7.3.3** — Where they diverge: science treats indignation as a human moral emotion only; the C5 evidence makes its primary register **divine judicial indignation** (Isa 10:5; Psa 78:49) — God's holy displeasure, a covenant/theological category science does not adjudicate (per the outside-science inventory). The **denunciation/curse** edge (Num 23:7) also has no clean scientific analogue.

**T7.3.4** — Gaps surfaced by science: moral-disengagement research (absence of indignation at genuine injustice = deactivated moral self-sanction) prompts examination of texts where indignation is **lacking** or **misdirected** (Ahab's sulking over a *just* refusal, 1Ki 21:4, is misdirected indignation) — a prompt for further verse work on disordered vs righteous indignation. Labelled inferential.

---

## Closing notes
- **Questions answered:** all 126. Silence recorded where C5 verses do not speak (T3.5 creativity; parts of T3.3 memory; T4.6.1/2 spiritual beings).
- **Key data feature:** three strands — human sullenness/displeasure (Ahab), denunciation/cursing (Balaam), divine judicial indignation (Isa 10:5; Psa 78:49) — plus one positive NT case, righteous repentant indignation (2Cor 7:11). valence (righteous 4 / sinful 7 / forbidden 2 / neutral 29) integrated.
- **Provenance:** read-resolved fields supporting; valence CC-confirmed current and used; T7.3 from the science extract.
