# M05 Characteristic F — Friendship: Tier-Catalogue Application (T0–T7)

- **Filename:** wa-m05-f-tier-answers-v1_0-20260620.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-20
- **Cluster:** M05 — "Love, Compassion and Kindness" · **Characteristic:** F — Friendship
- **What this is:** every active tier-catalogue question (126, T0–T7) applied to characteristic F, evidenced and quoted from the verse corpus, self-contained for prose development without reference to source.
- **Evidence basis:** the 32 distinct occurrences (Greek filos / filia, filofrōn; Hebrew re.eh, "the king's friend" — note: the *re.a* "companion" of Proverbs is not extracted into this band, so F's Hebrew evidence is the court-office "friend"), quoted verbatim from wa-ve-lexical-extract-M05-20260620.
- **Companion:** wa-m05-f-friendship-v1_0-20260620.md.
- **Standing scope flag (carried, for researcher review):** F may be a **relational category** (the peer-bond *between* persons) rather than an **inner-being characteristic** seated *within* a person. It is retained in the cluster on the felt-affect of the bond (affect-tagged) and on Joh 15. Several answers below register this flag where it bears.
- **Method note:** per-verse questions answered across the corpus with quoted exemplars; **"Silent"** = evidence does not speak (with reason).
- **Change note (v1_0):** first issue.

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**T0.1.1** — At the lexical-tag level, **no occurrence tags divine involvement** — friendship is the cluster's one wholly horizontal characteristic. At the verse level, two exceptions relate it to God: **God as the one befriended** — "Abraham believed God … and he was called a friend of God" (Jam 2:23); and **Christ befriending** — "No longer do I call you servants … but I have called you friends" (Joh 15:15). *(Observation: the tag is empty; interpretation: these two verses extend friendship to the God-relation.)*

**T0.1.2** — Friendship is **not predicated of God as a borne attribute** (God is not said to *be* friendship as he is said to be love or "the God of all comfort"); it appears as a **relation entered** — God befriends Abraham (Jam 2:23) and Christ befriends the disciples (Joh 15:14–15). The pattern indicates friendship is a creaturely-relational reality into which God graciously enters, rather than a divine attribute mirrored in the creature.

**T0.2.1** — Yes — friendship serves **loyal presence, disclosure, and rejoicing-together**: "David's friend" stands by him in crisis (2Sa 15:37); the friend "rejoices greatly" with the other (Joh 3:29); friends are called together to "Rejoice with me" (Luk 15:6). It binds persons in shared life.

**T0.2.2** — **Created design** as the good of human bonding, operating in the fallen world (friends in danger, betrayal, Luk 21:16) and capable of disorder ("friendship with the world is enmity with God", Jam 4:4). The bond itself is a creaturely good; its object can corrupt it.

**T0.2.3** — Yes, lightly — friendship is bound to a future welcome: "make friends for yourselves … so that when it fails they may receive you into the eternal dwellings" (Luk 16:9); and Christ's friends share in his disclosed purposes (Joh 15:15). It orients toward enduring fellowship.

**T0.3.1** — The likeness instantiated is **intimate disclosure and loyal love between persons** — Christ's "I have called you friends, for all that I have heard from my Father I have made known to you" (Joh 15:15) images a fellowship of shared knowledge and self-giving ("lay down his life for his friends", Joh 15:13).

**T0.3.2** — **An exclusively creaturely-relational good into which God enters** rather than a quality shared symmetrically — God is "friend *of*" Abraham (Jam 2:23) within a relation, not the bearer of a friendship-attribute. *(Interpretation, labelled — flows from the empty divine-bearer tag.)*

**T0.3.3** — Friendship's presence marks the person as bonded and known (Joh 15:15); its misdirection ("friend of the world", Jam 4:4) marks alienation from God. No image-doctrine is stated; **largely inferential**.

**T0.4.1** — Yes — **christological, divine establishing the pattern**: Christ's befriending of the disciples (Joh 15:14–15) and Abraham's friendship with God (Jam 2:23) set the pattern of divine-human friendship the human bond points toward.

---

## T1 — Definition

**T1.1.1** — Friendship. The name signals the **chosen peer-bond of mutual affection, loyalty, and shared life** — the standing relation between those who love one another as equals.

**T1.1.2** — Greek **filos** (friend), **filia** (friendship), **filofrōn** (friendly/of a friendly mind); Hebrew **re.eh** ("the king's friend", a court companion-office, 1Ki 4:5). Definitionally the *phil-* terms name the **affectionate bond** (shared root with love and brotherly-love).

**T1.1.3** — The name carries a **mutual, horizontal** implication — friendship runs between peers ("became friends with each other", Luk 23:12), marked by reciprocity and standing-with rather than the asymmetry of mercy or comfort.

**T1.2.1** — A **borne relational quality** — *quality* (28) far above *status* (4) and with no action tagging. Friendship is a standing bond one *has*, not a discrete act. **Scope-flag note:** this "quality" is the quality of a *relation between* persons, which is part of why F sits at the cluster's edge.

**T1.2.2** — **Compound**: friendship combines affection (the felt warmth, affect-tagged), loyalty (standing by — "David's friend", 2Sa 15:37), disclosure (shared knowledge — Joh 15:15), and shared rejoicing (Joh 3:29; Luk 15:6). It is a bond of feeling, fidelity, and mutual openness.

**T1.3.1** — Its structural opposite is **enmity** — "Herod and Pilate became friends … for before this they had been at enmity" (Luk 23:12); "friendship with the world is enmity with God" (Jam 4:4). Friendship and enmity are the named contraries.

**T1.3.2** — At its edge friendship excludes and resists **betrayal and divided loyalty**: friends may betray ("delivered up even by … friends", Luk 21:16), and friendship of the wrong object is forbidden ("a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God", Jam 4:4).

**T1.3.3** — Friendship is **not mere acquaintance and not the asymmetry of patronage**: it is mutual and disclosing — "No longer do I call you servants … but … friends" (Joh 15:15) marks the move from hierarchy to friendship. It ends where the bond is one-sided or its object displaces God (Jam 4:4).

**T1.4.1** — It operates as a **standing bond expressed in presence, request, disclosure, and shared joy** — standing by (2Sa 15:37), asking a friend's help ("Friend, lend me three loaves", Luk 11:5), being entrusted with knowledge (Joh 15:15), rejoicing together (Luk 15:6). Grammatically it is borne (noun/adjective), not a verb of doing.

**T1.4.2** — Yes — mode varies by **object and depth**: court loyalty ("the king's friend", 1Ki 4:5), intimate disclosure (Joh 15:15), mutual aid (Luk 11:5–8), and disordered alliance ("friendship with the world", Jam 4:4).

**T1.4.3** — Yes — friendship operates in **speech**: it is the form of address ("Friend, move up higher", Luk 14:10; "my friends, do not fear", Luk 12:4) and of mutual greeting ("The friends greet you. Greet the friends, each by name", 3Jo 15). One occurrence is commanded — the "friendly/humble mind" (filofrōn, 1Pe 3:8).

**T1.5.1** — The immediate response friendship shows is **loyal standing-with and shared rejoicing** — the friend who stands and "rejoices greatly" (Joh 3:29); friends called to "Rejoice with me" (Luk 15:6).

**T1.5.2** — Varied — loyalty in crisis (2Sa 15:37), aid in need (Luk 11:5), joy in finding (Luk 15:6), and, in betrayal, abandonment (Luk 21:16) — but consistent in expressing the bond's standing.

**T1.6.1** — Over time friendship **establishes loyal, disclosing fellowship** — the standing relation of those entrusted with one another ("I have called you friends, for all that I have heard from my Father I have made known to you", Joh 15:15).

**T1.6.3** — The immediate response is an act of loyalty or shared joy; the sustained effect is the **durable bond** itself — friends who stand by over time (2Sa 15:37) and are received "into the eternal dwellings" (Luk 16:9).

**T1.7.1** — It takes hold rightly in **mutual love, loyalty, and obedience to Christ** — "You are my friends if you do what I command you" (Joh 15:14) — and in a "friendly/humble mind" toward one another (1Pe 3:8).

**T1.7.2** — It is blocked or distorted by **enmity, betrayal, and misdirected alliance** — enmity (Luk 23:12), betrayal by friends (Luk 21:16), and friendship with the world that becomes "enmity with God" (Jam 4:4). **No adversarial spirit** is shown distorting it — **Silent**.

**T1.7.3** — The person in whom friendship is present but does not take hold is the **false or betraying friend** — those who "deliver up" their friends (Luk 21:16), and the elder brother who claims faithful service yet was never given "a young goat … to celebrate with my friends" (Luk 15:29), missing the fellowship offered.

---

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**T2.1.1** — **Soul** (1 — the only constitutional tag in the band): friendship reaches the soul in the deepest bonds, but the corpus rarely localises it constitutionally. **Largely unlocated** — consistent with the scope flag (a bond *between* persons is not easily seated *within* one).

**T2.1.2** — The near-absence of constitutional location is itself a finding: friendship is **the least interiorly-seated characteristic** in the cluster, engaging the affections (affect-tagged) but rarely named to heart, mind, or spirit. This supports the question whether F is an inner-being characteristic or a relational category.

**T2.10.1** — Yes, lightly — friendship is **received from outside** (received-from-outside, 3 occurrences) — entered through another's befriending: Christ "called you friends" (Joh 15:15); Herod and Pilate "became friends" (Luk 23:12). It comes upon the person through relation.

**T2.7.1** — **Silent.** No body link is evidenced.

**T2.9.1** — **Generated between persons and, in the key cases, initiated by another** — Christ initiates ("I have called you friends", Joh 15:15); God befriends Abraham (Jam 2:23). Origin is relational, often initiated by the greater party.

**T2.9.2** — **Single in kind** (relational origin) but varied in initiator — sometimes mutual ("became friends", Luk 23:12), sometimes graciously initiated (Joh 15:15).

---

## T3 — The Inner Faculties

**T3.1.1 / T3.1.2 / T3.1.3 · Perception** — **Silent.** No occurrence engages perception.

**T3.2.1 · Cognition (engage?)** — Yes, lightly — friendship involves **shared knowledge/disclosure**: "I have called you friends, for all that I have heard from my Father I have made known to you" (Joh 15:15). The friend is the one let into knowledge.

**T3.2.2 · Cognition (effect)** — It opens mutual understanding — the friend, unlike the servant, "knows what his master is doing" (Joh 15:15).

**T3.2.3 · Cognition (pattern)** — Cognition appears only at the bond's highest register (disclosure); it is not a general feature, marking friendship as chiefly affective with an apex of shared knowing.

**T3.3.1 / T3.3.2 / T3.3.3 · Memory** — **Silent.** No memorial engagement evidenced.

**T3.4.1 · Affect (engage?)** — Yes, dominantly (affect 28 of 32): friendship is the felt bond — warmth, loyalty, and shared joy ("rejoices greatly", Joh 3:29).

**T3.4.2 · Affect (effect)** — It produces the warmth of belonging and the joy of shared life (Luk 15:6) — and, in loss, the pain of betrayal (Luk 21:16).

**T3.4.3 · Affect (pattern)** — Affect dominance with almost no other faculty marks friendship as **a felt relational bond** more than a structured inner faculty — its whole register is affection-and-loyalty.

**T3.5.1 / T3.5.2 / T3.5.3 · Creativity** — **Silent.** No engagement with imagination or origination.

**T3.6.1 · Volition (engage?)** — Yes, lightly — friendship is **chosen and conditioned on will**: "You are my friends if you do what I command you" (Joh 15:14); one may "make friends" (Luk 16:9) or wrongly choose "friendship with the world" (Jam 4:4).

**T3.6.2 · Volition (effect)** — It directs the will toward loyalty and right alliance (Joh 15:14) or, disordered, toward the world (Jam 4:4).

**T3.6.3 · Volition (pattern)** — Volition appears at the points of *choosing* the bond and its object — friendship is entered and aimed by the will, though it is felt as affection.

**T3.7.1 · Agency (engage?)** — Lightly — friends act for one another: standing by (2Sa 15:37), aiding (Luk 11:5–8), interceding ("friends … urging him not to venture", Act 19:31), caring ("gave him leave to go to his friends and be cared for", Act 27:3).

**T3.7.2 · Agency (effect)** — The bond moves friends to mutual aid and protection.

**T3.7.3 · Agency (pattern)** — Agency is the bond's outworking, not its essence — friendship *is* a standing relation that *issues in* acts of loyalty.

**T3.8.1 · Moral evaluation (engage?)** — Yes, at the object: friendship is morally weighed by *whom* one befriends — "friendship with the world is enmity with God" (Jam 4:4, sinful); "a friend of God" (Jam 2:23, righteous); "a friend of tax collectors and sinners" (Luk 7:34, a charge Jesus bears in righteousness).

**T3.8.2 · Moral evaluation (effect)** — The bond is good or evil by its object — godly friendship is righteousness (Jam 2:23); worldly friendship is enmity with God (Jam 4:4).

**T3.8.3 · Moral evaluation (pattern)** — Mostly neutral-valenced (20 of 32) because friendship is a relational fact morally indifferent in itself; like love, its moral value **turns on its object** at the edges (the sinful and righteous cases).

**T3.9.1 / T3.9.2 / T3.9.3 · Conscience** — **Silent.** No occurrence engages the conscience.

**T3.10.1 · Conscientiousness (engage?)** — Lightly — friendship integrates loyal awareness and faithful action (standing by in danger, 2Sa 15:37; the "friendly mind", 1Pe 3:8) — but it is not a developed conscientiousness in the corpus.

**T3.10.2 · Conscientiousness (effect)** — Where present, it yields dependable loyalty between persons.

**T3.10.3 · Conscientiousness (pattern)** — Minimal — friendship's reliability is a feature of the *bond*, not a structured inner conscientiousness.

**T3.11.1 · Relational capacity (engage?)** — Yes, constitutively and pre-eminently — friendship **is** relational capacity in its purest form: the equipment for mutual, disclosing, loyal connection between persons (Joh 15:15).

**T3.11.2 · Relational capacity (effect)** — It binds persons as peers — standing by, sharing knowledge and joy, aiding in need — the most directly relational of all the cluster's characteristics.

**T3.11.3 · Relational capacity (pattern)** — Friendship is so wholly relational that it raises the **scope question** — it engages the relational capacity not as one faculty among others within a person but as the *bond itself between* persons.

---

## T4 — Relational Interfaces

**T4.1.1 · God→human** — Yes, lightly — Christ befriends and discloses to the disciples: "I have called you friends, for all that I have heard from my Father I have made known to you" (Joh 15:15).

**T4.1.2 · basis** — **Gracious initiative conditioned on faithful response** — "You are my friends if you do what I command you" (Joh 15:14): Christ initiates the friendship and it holds in obedience.

**T4.1.3 · what it shows of God** — That God in Christ **stoops to befriend** — moving the disciples from servants to friends and admitting them to his counsel (Joh 15:15), a friendship of disclosure and self-gift ("lay down his life for his friends", Joh 15:13).

**T4.2.1 · human→God** — Yes — Abraham's friendship with God: "Abraham believed God … and he was called a friend of God" (Jam 2:23) — friendship grounded in faith.

**T4.2.2 · inner posture required** — **Faith and obedience** — Abraham "believed God" (Jam 2:23); the disciples are friends "if you do what I command" (Joh 15:14).

**T4.2.3 · what it shows** — That the person may stand with God **as friend** — admitted to intimacy and counsel — the highest dignity of the bond, grounded in faith.

**T4.3.1 · human→human giving** — Yes, dominantly — friendship extended between persons: standing by (2Sa 15:37), aiding (Luk 11:5), interceding (Act 19:31), caring (Act 27:3), greeting (3Jo 15).

**T4.3.2 · giver's inner conditions** — A "friendly/humble mind" (filofrōn, 1Pe 3:8), loyalty, and shared love; and, supremely, willingness to "lay down his life for his friends" (Joh 15:13).

**T4.3.3 · what the giver must have received/become** — They must have **entered the mutual bond** — friendship presupposes reciprocity; Christ's friends first received his befriending and disclosure (Joh 15:15).

**T4.4.1 · human→human receiving** — Yes — friendship is received in being befriended ("I have called you friends", Joh 15:15) and welcomed ("Friend, move up higher", Luk 14:10; "received … into the eternal dwellings", Luk 16:9).

**T4.4.2 · conditions accompanying / blocking uptake** — Uptake accompanies mutual loyalty; it is blocked by enmity (Luk 23:12 before reconciliation), betrayal (Luk 21:16), or a heart set on the world (Jam 4:4).

**T4.4.3 · state of one who meets it but does not take it up** — The **elder brother**, who served faithfully yet never celebrated "with my friends" (Luk 15:29) — fellowship available but unentered; and the betrayer who turns friend to enemy (Luk 21:16).

**T4.5.1 · within bonds vs across distance** — Friendship **is** the existing bond, yet it can **cross distance and difference** — Jesus the "friend of tax collectors and sinners" (Luk 7:34) befriends across the moral boundary; former enemies "became friends" (Luk 23:12).

**T4.5.2 · within covenant only, or crossing** — It **crosses** — Jesus befriends sinners (Luk 7:34); friendship is extended to outsiders and former enemies (Luk 23:12) — though friendship "with the world" as a system is forbidden (Jam 4:4).

**T4.5.3 · relational scope** — Peers, kin, the powerful ("the king's friend", 1Ki 4:5; Asiarchs, Act 19:31), sinners (Luk 7:34), and the disciples whom Christ befriends; the one excluded bond is friendship *with the world* set against God (Jam 4:4).

**T4.6.1 / T4.6.2 / T4.6.3 · Spiritual beings** — **Silent.** No occurrence shows friendship operating toward, attacked by, or mediated through angelic or adversarial beings.

---

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

**T5.1.1 · Transformation** — Yes, lightly — friendship transforms **status**: from servant to friend (Joh 15:15), from enemies to friends (Luk 23:12) — a change in the relation between persons.

**T5.1.2 · reversible / irreversible** — **Shown reversible** — friends may become betrayers (Luk 21:16) and enemies may become friends (Luk 23:12); the bond can be entered and lost.

**T5.2.1 · Sequence of inner states** — Yes, lightly — **enmity → reconciliation → friendship** (Luk 23:12), and **servant → friend** (Joh 15:15) — relational sequences more than inner-state sequences.

**T5.3.1 · Mechanism of change** — By **befriending and disclosure** (Joh 15:15) and by **reconciliation** (Luk 23:12); friendship is formed through shared life, loyalty, and admitted intimacy.

**T5.3.2 · mechanism differ across contexts** — Yes: divine friendship by Christ's gracious disclosure (Joh 15:15); human friendship by reciprocal loyalty and shared experience (the aid and rejoicing texts); disordered friendship by alliance with the world (Jam 4:4).

**T5.4.1 · Suffering / affliction** — Yes — friendship operates **in danger and loss**: friends stand by in crisis (2Sa 15:37), are sources of care in trouble (Act 27:3), yet may betray under pressure (Luk 21:16); the greatest friendship is proven in death ("lay down his life for his friends", Joh 15:13).

**T5.4.2 · what suffering does to it** — Affliction **tests and proves** friendship — it is the arena in which loyalty is shown (2Sa 15:37; Joh 15:13) or fails (Luk 21:16).

**T5.5.1 · Formation and sanctification** — Lightly — friendship with Christ shapes the disciple toward obedience and shared purpose (Joh 15:14–15); the "friendly mind" is a commanded disposition (1Pe 3:8). Its formative role is real but thinner than the cluster's other characteristics. **Scope-flag note:** F's formation is largely the formation *of a relationship*, not of an inner virtue.

**T5.6.1 · Eschatological trajectory** — Yes, lightly — friendship is bound to a future welcome: "make friends for yourselves … so that … they may receive you into the eternal dwellings" (Luk 16:9). Present friendship anticipates eternal fellowship.

---

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics

**T6.1.1 · Co-occurrence** — Friendship co-occurs with **love** (agapē — supremely Joh 15:13, love laid down "for his friends"), **rejoicing-with** (sunchairō — "Rejoice with me", Luk 15:6, 9), **brotherly-love** (filadelfos) and **compassion/sympathy** (eusplanchnos, sumpathēs — the 1Pe 3:8 virtue-list), **like-mindedness** (homofrōn), **calling** (kaleō), and, by contrast, with **the sinful** (hamartōlos — "friend of … sinners", Luk 7:34).

**T6.1.2 · what co-occurrence shows** — Friendship sits within the **affectionate-bonding family** (love, brotherly-love, like-mindedness) and is the relational frame within which love is exercised ("for his friends", Joh 15:13) and joy is shared (Luk 15:6).

**T6.2.1 · Sequential relationship** — Yes — friendship is the **bond within which love is enacted**: "Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends" (Joh 15:13) — love is shown *to* friends; friendship is the standing context, love the act within it.

**T6.2.2 · what the sequence shows** — The relationship is **constitutive/contextual**: friendship is the relation; love is the movement that fills and proves it.

**T6.3.1 · does it produce another?** — Yes — friendship produces **shared joy** (sunchairō, Luk 15:6) and is the occasion of **sacrificial love** (Joh 15:13).

**T6.3.2 · is it produced by another?** — It is produced by **love and like-mindedness** — the affectionate, like-minded disposition that forms the bond (1Pe 3:8 virtue-list); Christ's love produces his friendship with the disciples (Joh 15).

**T6.3.3 · constituent of / constituted by another?** — Friendship is **constituted by** love, loyalty, and shared joy, and is itself the **relational frame** of which love (A) is the animating act. It is a *category* hosting the cluster's affections more than a discrete inner faculty — the scope flag again.

**T6.4.1 · shared vocabulary** — Friendship shares the **phil- root** with love (fileō), brotherly-love (filadelfia), benevolence (filanthrōpia), and good-loving (filagathos); filos, filia, and filofrōn are the friendship members of that family.

**T6.4.2 · shared root architecture** — The **phil-** root is the shared architecture generating love, friendship, brotherly-love, and benevolence — friendship is one branch of the single affectional root.

**T6.4.3 · what the sharing shows** — The phil-root sharing shows friendship is **a species of love's bonding** — the standing peer-relation within the wider family of affection.

**T6.5.1 · nearest neighbour and distinction** — The nearest neighbour is **love (A)**. The distinction: love is the **affection/act** (the movement of self-giving toward an object); friendship is the **standing mutual bond** (the relation between peers within which love lives). Love is what is given; friendship is the relationship that hosts it — "lay down his life [love] for his friends [friendship]" (Joh 15:13) holds both in one verse.

**T6.5.2 · precise boundary at overlap** — Where they overlap (Joh 15:13–15), the boundary is **act vs relation**: love names the self-giving; friendship names the mutual, disclosing bond between the parties.

**T6.5.3 · distinction of degree, kind, direction, or level?** — One of **kind** (act/affection vs standing relation) — and, at the deepest level, a **category** distinction that grounds the scope flag (F as relational category vs A as inner-being affection).

---

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**T7.1.1 · primary terms and root meanings** — Greek **filos** (friend), **filia** (friendship), **filofrōn** (friendly-minded) — all from the *phil-* root (affection); Hebrew **re.eh** ("the king's friend", a court office). Roots converge on **affectionate peer-bond**.

**T7.1.2 · grammatical range** — Noun (filos, filia), adjective (filofrōn "friendly"). The absence of an action-verb and the dominance of nouns confirm friendship operates as a **borne relation**, not an act.

**T7.1.3 · semantic range** — From court office ("the king's friend", 1Ki 4:5) through ordinary companionship (Luk 11:5; Act 10:24), intimate disclosure (Joh 15:15), and friendship with God (Jam 2:23) to disordered alliance ("friendship with the world", Jam 4:4). A range from social role to divine intimacy to forbidden alliance.

**T7.1.4 · terms distinguishing aspects** — Lightly — **filos** (the friend, person) is distinguished from **filia** (the friendship, relation) and **filofrōn** (the friendly disposition); the person/relation/disposition aspects are lexicalised within the small band.

**T7.1.5 · term for the opposite/absence** — The opposite is **enmity / enemy** (echthros, named in contrast — "enmity", Luk 23:12; "enemy of God", Jam 4:4); no dedicated antonym within the band, but enmity is its clear contrary.

**T7.1.6 · person-type term** — Yes — **filos** *is* the person-type ("the friend"), and Hebrew re.eh names the office-holder ("the king's friend", 1Ki 4:5).

**T7.1.7 · supplication / seeking term** — **None** dedicated; though one may "make friends" (Luk 16:9) and ask a friend's help ("Friend, lend me", Luk 11:5), there is no term for *seeking friendship* as such. **Silent.**

**T7.1.8 · OT↔NT continuity / development** — The OT friendship evidence in this band is the narrow court-office **re.eh** ("the king's friend"); the NT **filos/filia** carries the fuller relational and theological weight (friend of God, Jam 2:23; Christ's friends, Joh 15). The richer Hebrew *companion* term (re.a of Proverbs) is not in this band — a **data-coverage note**. Development runs toward the NT's elevated friendship.

**T7.1.9 · NT-coined term** — **None** coined, though Joh 15 **elevates** filos to name the disciples' relation to Christ — a theological elevation rather than a coinage. **Silent on coinage.**

**T7.1.10 · full vocabulary arc** — The arc spans **the king's friend (re.eh) → companion/friend (filos) → the friendship-bond (filia) → the friendly disposition (filofrōn) → friend of God / friends of Christ (Jam 2:23; Joh 15)** — from social office to divine intimacy.

**T7.2.1 · function of the primary term in its primary verse** — In **Joh 15:13–15** filos is the **term of the disciples' new standing** — Christ's "friends" rather than "servants", the relation that carries his self-disclosure and his self-giving love; the term bears the whole elevation of the passage.

**T7.2.2 · literary forms** — **Narrative** (1Ki 4; 2Sa 15; the Gospel scenes), **parable** (Luk 11:5–8 the friend at midnight; Luk 15 the lost-and-found celebrations), **discourse** (Joh 15), **epistle** (Jam 2; 4; 1Pe 3; 3Jo). Responsible reading honours the parable's illustrative aim distinctly from the discourse's theological claim.

**T7.2.3 · logical structure** — Joh 15:14–15: premise — friends, unlike servants, are admitted to the master's knowledge; conclusion — "I have called you friends, for all that I have heard from my Father I have made known to you." Jam 4:4: premise — friendship with the world is enmity with God; conclusion — therefore the would-be friend of the world makes himself God's enemy. Friendship is consistently defined by **whose** it is.

**T7.2.4 · contextual setting** — **Communal/social** (companionship, court, hospitality), **covenantal-theological** (friend of God, Jam 2:23; Christ's friends, Joh 15), and **antithetical** (friendship with the world vs God, Jam 4:4). The theological settings give the bond its weight.

**T7.2.5 · primary anchor verse** — **Joh 15:13** — "Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends" — most fully expresses friendship's essential character by binding it to supreme love; with Joh 15:15 ("I have called you friends") as the relational anchor and Jam 2:23 ("friend of God") as the theological one.

**T7.2.6 · what the anchor shows that no other shows** — Joh 15:13–15 alone **raises friendship to the highest dignity** — the bond for which life is laid down and into which Christ admits his own, disclosing the Father's counsel — showing friendship at its summit is divine-human intimacy, not mere human companionship.

**T7.3.1 · most useful human-science framework** — **Social psychology / positive psychology** — friendship and belonging research (Aristotle's utility/pleasure/virtue friendships; Baumeister and Leary's "need to belong"; Putnam's social capital; Eisenberger's social-pain findings).

**T7.3.2 · where the framework illuminates** — The "need to belong" research illuminates friendship as a **fundamental human motivation** whose frustration produces distress — matching the corpus's portrayal of friends as sources of care and standing-with (Act 27:3; 2Sa 15:37); Aristotle's virtue-friendship illuminates the highest biblical register (Joh 15, friendship grounded in shared good and disclosure rather than utility).

**T7.3.3 · where evidence and framework diverge** — Science explains friendship by proximity, similarity, and reciprocal benefit; the corpus presents friendship **with God** (Jam 2:23) and **Christ's befriending of sinners and servants** (Luk 7:34; Joh 15:15) — bonds grounded in grace and faith rather than affinity or exchange — and **forbids** "friendship with the world" (Jam 4:4) on theological, not social, grounds.

**T7.3.4 · aspect surfaced by the framework** — Belonging research frames friendship as an inner human *need*, which sharpens the **scope question** the band already carries: is F an inner-being characteristic (a constitutional capacity/need within the person) or a relational category (the bond between persons)? The science's framing of belonging as an inner motivation may favour retaining F, but on the *need/capacity* rather than the *bond*. **Flagged for researcher review — the standing scope flag.**

---

## Coverage summary

- **Answered substantively:** T0 (all, with the divine-bearer answers qualified by the empty tag), T1 (all), T2 (T2.1, T2.9, T2.10 substantive; T2.7 silent), T3 cognition(light)/affect/volition/agency/moral-evaluation/conscientiousness(light)/relational (substantive), T4.1–T4.5 (substantive), T5 (all), T6 (all), T7 (all bar T7.1.7 silent).
- **Silent:** T1.7.2 (adversarial branch), T2.7 body, T3.1 perception, T3.3 memory, T3.5 creativity, T3.9 conscience, T4.6 spiritual beings, T7.1.7.
- **Defining signals across the grid:** friendship is the **most horizontal** characteristic (no divine-bearer tag — T0.1.1), the **least interiorly-seated** (T2.1.2), and the one carrying a **standing scope flag** (relational category vs inner-being characteristic — T1.2.1, T3.11.3, T6.3.3, T7.3.4). Its summit (Joh 15) elevates it to divine-human intimacy; its corruption (Jam 4:4) is alliance with the world against God.

## §1 — Definition & scope of the characteristic

Friendship is the cluster's characteristic of the **bonded peer relationship** — the standing affectionate tie of friend to friend. It is the most horizontal and most descriptive band: "friend" names a relational *status* more than a felt act or an enacted disposition. The band gathers Greek **filos** (G5384, friend), **filia** (G5373, friendship), **filofrōn** (G5391, friendly); and Hebrew **re.eh** (H7463, friend / companion). Where love (A) is the affection itself, friendship is the *standing bond* within which such affection lives.

### filia (G5373, Greek) — “friendship” — 1 occ

**Jam 4:4** — sense=friendship · faculty=affect · type=status · valence=sinful · experiencer=other (addressed)
> Jam 4:4 You adulterous people ! Do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity with God ? Therefore whoever wishes to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God .

---

## §5 — Observation (grounded in the 32 distinct occurrences above)

- **A relational quality, not an act or a felt state.** Type is *quality* (28 of 32) with a little *status* (4) and no *action* — the only band so dominated by *quality*. "Friend" is a standing relational designation.
- **Predominantly neutral and descriptive.** Valence is *neutral* (20) with only *righteous* (2), *sinful* (2), *commanded* (1): "friend(s)" mostly names a relationship without moral charge, and the dominant sense is simply *friend / friends*.
- **The most horizontal band — no divine involvement.** *divine_involvement* is **empty**: friendship is the human-to-human tie. The single vertical reframing is Jesus' elevation of it — "Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends" and "I have called you friends" (Joh 15:13–15) — where the lone *soul* seat appears.
- **It takes moral colour from its object.** The two *sinful* occurrences are "friendship with the world is enmity with God" (Jam 4:4) — friendship, like love, coloured by what it is friendship *with*.
- **Affectional faculty.** *affect* (28) keeps the band within the inner-being field on the strength of the bond's affection, even where the surface use is descriptive.

## §6 — Interpretation (labelled; inferential where marked)

- **F is the cluster's peer-bond characteristic** — a symmetrical relationship between equals, distinct from love (affection toward an object), compassion (toward the weak), and kindness (loyal benevolence toward another).
- **SCOPE FLAG — INFERENTIAL.** The quality-dominant, neutral, divine-empty profile suggests friendship functions here more as a relational *category* than as an inner state. It is the band most open to the question whether "friend" is an *inner-being characteristic* or a *relationship label*. It is kept in scope on its *affect* faculty and the Joh 15 elevation, but the question is flagged for researcher review.
- **The Jam 4:4 case** shows friendship's worth, like love's, set by its object (world vs God).

## §7 — Reflection (cultural reach and tentative application — not prescriptive)

- **"Friend" is thin as an inner-being term in this corpus** — largely descriptive. The richer inner content of friendship (loyalty, affection) is carried by neighbouring bands: *philia*-love in A and chesed-loyalty in C. Reader-facing output should note that friendship's inner substance lives mainly next door.
- **"Friend of God", and Jesus calling disciples "friends",** reframe a horizontal category vertically — a significant but singular datum, flagged not developed.

## §8 — Boundary & data-quality notes

- **Flag 7 (dedup) applied:** 44 raw → 32 distinct (filos +11, re.eh +1). Counts distinct (raw in §2).
- **SCOPE FLAG (repeated for visibility):** F is the band most arguably a relational *category* rather than an inner-being characteristic — flagged for researcher scope review alongside the set-aside decision (Flag 6).
- **filofrōn** ("friendly"; one occurrence glossed "humble mind") is thin; retained.
- **re.eh** ("friend / companion") overlaps the neighbour / fellow sense; retained where the friendship reading holds.

# M06 · C-A Aversive affect — tier-question answers (T0–T7)

**File:** wa-m06-char-a-tieranswers-v1_0-20260620.md · **Date:** 2026-06-20
**Cluster:** M06 (Hate, Contempt and Hostility) · **Characteristic:** C-A Aversive affect — felt hatred / settled rejection
**Evidence base:** wa-m06-char-a-aversive-affect-v1_0-20260620.md (discovery) + wa-ve-lexical-extract-M06-20260620 (lexical) + wa-m06-hate-scienceextract-v1_0 §1 (T7.3 only)
**Terms (175 occ, all OT):** sa.ne (143), sin.ah (19), sa.tam (8), se.na [Aram.] (2), mas.te.mah (2), sa.ni (1)

> Convention: each question is answered from evidence (count/verse cited) or marked **SILENT** with the reason. Inferential reasoning is labelled. Science extract is used only at T7.3.

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**T0.1.1** — God-relation is present in 25 of 175 occurrences: God as **object** of hatred in 10 (Num 10:35; Deu 12:31; 2Ch 19:2; Psa 68:1; 81:15; 83:2; 139:21; Mal 2:16 — "those who hate the LORD"), and God as **agent** who hates in 15 (Deu 12:31; 16:22; Job 16:9; Psa 11:5; Pro 6:16; Isa 1:14; 61:8; Hos 9:15; Amo 6:8; Zec 8:17; Mal 1:3 "Esau I have hated"). So the relation runs both ways: God hates (evil, false worship) and God is hated.

**T0.1.2** — The characteristic **is borne by God himself**, not only by the creature: 15 agent-occurrences show divine hatred, directed at evil, injustice, and false worship (Pro 6:16 the things the LORD hates; Isa 1:14 "my soul hates" the corrupted feasts). This places aversive affect — specifically *hatred of evil* — within the divine nature, and so within what the image can reflect, while the bulk of human occurrences (sinful 83) show its fallen distortion.

**T0.2.1** — Aggregate (no single verse states a purpose universally). Where a role is shown, the **immediate-response** field gives effects: hate "works ruin" (Pro 26:28), "brings shame" (Pro 13:5), and aligns with loving violence (Psa 11:5). The commanded seam shows a positive role: hatred of evil as part of the fear of the LORD (Pro 8:13).

**T0.2.2** — **Both.** The commanded/righteous seam (22 occ: Exo 18:21; Psa 97:10; Amo 5:15; Psa 119:104,113,128,163; 139:21–22; Pro 8:13) reads as created design — rightly-ordered aversion to evil; the dominant sinful framing (83) reads as the fallen condition (causeless or self-serving hatred).

**T0.2.3** — **SILENT.** No eschatological/future-fullness orientation is tagged for any C-A occurrence (the eschatological abhorrence material sits in C-C, not here).

**T0.3.1** — Inferential, grounded in T0.1.2: the aspect of divine likeness instantiated is **holy aversion to evil** — the capacity to reject what is contrary to God's character (God hates evil; the righteous are commanded to hate evil, Psa 97:10).

**T0.3.2** — **Shared** between God and person, but valence-differentiated: God hates only evil/injustice (agent cases all object evil); the human capacity is the same affect, rightly or wrongly directed.

**T0.3.3** — Inferential: where a person hates *evil* (righteous seam) the image is rightly ordered; where a person hates *without cause* or hates *the good/God* (Psa 139:21 inverse; obj=God 10) the image is disordered. The evidence shows both states.

**T0.4.1** — **Mal 1:3** ("Esau I have hated, Jacob I have loved") carries election/covenant language; its typological extension (Rom 9:13) lies outside this OT extract and is **labelled inferential**. No other clearly typological use is tagged.

## T1 — Definition

**T1.1.1** — Programme name: *aversive affect* — felt, settled rejection of an object. The name signals an **emotion (affect)** that is also **directional** (it has an object) and **settled** (a standing orientation, not a momentary reaction).

**T1.1.2** — Primary Hebrew `sa.ne` (143) "to hate"; nominal `sin.ah` (19) "hatred"; `sa.tam` (8) the harboured grudge; Aramaic `se.na` (2). At the definitional level they show hatred as both an **act** (sa.ne, action 143) and a **standing state** (sin.ah, status).

**T1.1.3** — The name carries a **relational/directional** implication: hatred is always *of* something or someone (object_type person 75, abstract 27, God 10) — it is constitutively directed.

**T1.2.1** — Predominantly an **act** (type action 153) with a **condition/status** form (status 21, `sin.ah`); one quality occurrence (`sa.ni` "hated", adjectival). So: primarily act, secondarily standing condition.

**T1.2.2** — **Compound** on the evidence: every `sa.ne` occurrence is tagged **affect + cognition** (143) — hatred here fuses *feeling* with *appraisal* (one hates what one has judged). Constituent elements: an affective rejection and a cognitive evaluation.

**T1.3.1** — Structural opposite: **love** (`'ahav`, cluster M05). The evidence is direct — love is the stated *cause* of the contrasting hatred (Gen 29:31 Jacob's greater love for Rachel → Leah hated; Gen 37:4), and M05 co-occurs 12× in C-A verses; `ba.rakh` "to bless" appears as the partner term opposite hating (Gen 24:60).

**T1.3.2** — At its edge it excludes/resists love, blessing, and acceptance of its object (the love→hate contrast in Gen 29; the bless↔hate pairing).

**T1.3.3** — It is *not* mere anger (a reactive episode — see C/T7.3): the data shows it as a **settled** affect (status form `sin.ah`; harboured `sa.tam`), distinct from momentary reaction. It ends where appraisal-free reaction (anger, M02) or worth-judgement-only (contempt, C-B) begins.

**T1.4.1** — Mode per verse: realised grammatically as Qal verb (`sa.ne`, action) and as noun (`sin.ah`, status). The `mode` field is empty across the cluster, so finer mode data is not provided. The manner of functioning is **affective-cognitive rejection** of an object.

**T1.4.2** — Varies by **valence/direction**, not by constitutional level: the same root operates as condemned hatred (sinful 83) and as commanded hatred of evil (commanded/righteous 22). Direction (toward person / toward evil / toward God) is the main axis of variation.

**T1.4.3** — Yes, in part: the **commanded** occurrences (Exo 18:21; Psa 97:10; Amo 5:15) operate through a communicative/imperative mode — hatred of evil is *enjoined*. Otherwise mostly narrated, not spoken.

**T1.5.1** — Where shown (immediate_response, 9 occ): hate issues immediately in ruin (Pro 26:28), shame (Pro 13:5), pursuit (Eze 35:6), and loving violence (Psa 11:5). Most occurrences (166) tag no immediate response.

**T1.5.2** — **Varied** — the few tagged responses differ (ruin, shame, pursuit, violence); no single consistent immediate response.

**T1.6.1** — Over time it establishes a settled orientation of rejection (the `sin.ah`/`sa.tam` standing-state and harboured-grudge forms attest a durable condition); Pro 26:28 ties it to lasting "ruin."

**T1.6.3** — Distinct from the immediate response (T1.5) in that the sustained effect is the **standing disposition itself** (hatred as `sin.ah`), whereas the immediate response is its episodic output (ruin, shame).

**T1.7.1** — Operates *rightly* where its object is evil/falsehood (the righteous seam: Psa 97:10; 119:104; Pro 8:13) — i.e. under the inner condition of the fear of the LORD (Pro 8:13 explicitly).

**T1.7.2** — Operates *wrongly/distortedly* where it is causeless or self-interested (sinful 83); the data shows causes such as preference/jealousy (Gen 29:31; 37:4) and prior violation turning to revulsion (2Sa 13:15 Amnon). **SILENT** on adversarial-spirit interference (none tagged for C-A).

**T1.7.3** — **SILENT** — the lexical does not isolate a "present-but-not-taken-up" inner state for C-A.

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**T2.1.1** — Per verse, seat is named in 23 of 175: **soul 16, heart 8, flesh 1** (the rest unseated). Soul-engagement leads (e.g. Isa 1:14 "my soul hates").

**T2.1.2** — The pattern indicates aversive affect is **seated more in the soul than the heart**, with the body engaged only marginally (1 flesh). 152 unseated occurrences show the term often names the act without locating it. It never engages spirit, mind, or conscience explicitly.

**T2.10.1** — Movement: **received-from-outside** is tagged in 3 occurrences (origin), suggesting hatred can come *onto* a person; otherwise no constitutional-level movement (spirit→soul→body) is tagged. Mostly **none**.

**T2.7.1** — **SILENT** — with only 1 flesh-link and no direction tagged, body-direction is not evidenced for C-A.

**T2.9.1** — Origin: mostly **not stated** (172); **received-from-outside** in 3. Within-person generation is implied by cause cases (jealousy, Gen 29:31) but not tagged as an origin field — labelled inferential.

**T2.9.2** — Origin is **single where tagged** (received-from-outside) and otherwise unstated; it does not visibly change with context in the tagged data.

## T3 — The Inner Faculties

**T3.1 Perception — T3.1.1 / T3.1.2 / T3.1.3:** **SILENT** — no perceptive-faculty engagement tagged for any C-A occurrence.

**T3.2 Cognition — T3.2.1** — **Yes, strongly.** `cognition` is co-tagged on all 143 `sa.ne` occurrences: hatred here carries an appraisal of its object. **T3.2.2** — It organises judgement of the object (one hates what one has evaluated as bad/false; Psa 119:104 "I hate every false way"). **T3.2.3** — The pattern (cognition on 143 of 175) indicates aversive affect is **not raw feeling but feeling fused with judgement** — a defining trait of this characteristic.

**T3.3 Memory — all:** **SILENT** — no memory-faculty engagement tagged. (Inferential only: `sa.tam`'s harboured grudge implies retention; labelled inferential, not a finding.)

**T3.4 Affect — T3.4.1** — **Yes — definitive.** `affect` is tagged on **all 175** occurrences. **T3.4.2** — It is the affective faculty itself operating as rejection/aversion toward the object. **T3.4.3** — Universality of the affect tag confirms this characteristic **is** the affective core of the cluster.

**T3.5 Creativity — all:** **SILENT** — no creative-faculty engagement tagged.

**T3.6 Volition — T3.6.1** — **SILENT as a faculty tag**; inferential signal only: the **commanded** hatred of evil (Exo 18:21; Psa 97:10; Amo 5:15) implies a volitional/choice dimension (one is enjoined to hate evil). Labelled inferential. **T3.6.2 / T3.6.3** — SILENT (no volition tag).

**T3.7 Agency — all:** **SILENT** — no agency-faculty engagement tagged (the action-type is affective action, not agentive initiation in the tagged sense).

**T3.8 Moral Evaluation — T3.8.1** — **Yes, at the cluster level.** Though C-A's own faculty tag is affect+cognition (moral_evaluation is tagged on C-B terms), the **valence** data shows moral assessment operating *through* C-A: hatred is rated sinful/righteous/commanded/forbidden across its range. **T3.8.2** — Moral evaluation determines whether the hatred is rightly ordered (of evil) or disordered. **T3.8.3** — The bivalence pattern shows aversive affect is **morally evaluable in both directions** — the characteristic most directly carrying the "commanded hatred of evil" verdict.

**T3.9 Conscience — all:** **SILENT** — no conscience engagement tagged.

**T3.10 Conscientiousness — all:** **SILENT** — not tagged.

**T3.11 Relational Capacity — T3.11.1** — **SILENT as a faculty tag**; inferential: with object_type person in 75 occ, hatred operates against the relational bond (love→hate, Gen 29). Labelled inferential; no relational-capacity faculty tag. **T3.11.2 / T3.11.3** — SILENT.

## T4 — Relational Interfaces

**T4.1 God→Human — T4.1.1** — **Yes:** divine **agent** in 15 occ — God's hatred directed at evil, false worship, and (Mal 1:3) Esau. **T4.1.2** — Basis is **responsive/covenantal** where shown: God hates the corrupted worship his people bring (Isa 1:14), the things that are evil (Pro 6:16) — a response to evil, not arbitrary. **T4.1.3** — It shows God's disposition as **opposed to evil** — his hatred is the obverse of his holiness.

**T4.2 Human→God — T4.2.1** — **Yes (as its inverse):** 10 occ have God as object of human hatred ("those who hate the LORD/you", Psa 68:1; 81:15; 83:2; 139:21). This is the negative pole of the human-to-God interface — enmity rather than seeking. **T4.2.2** — The posture is rejection/opposition (no inner posture of seeking is shown). **T4.2.3** — It shows a relationship of **enmity** with God in those who hate him; Psa 139:21 shows the righteous counter-aligning with God *against* such haters.

**T4.3 Human→Giving — T4.3.1** — **Yes:** person-to-person hatred is the largest object class (person 75) — Esau/Jacob, Joseph's brothers (Gen 37:4), Amnon (2Sa 13:15). It operates as withdrawal of love/blessing toward the other. **T4.3.2 / T4.3.3** — **SILENT** — the lexical does not specify giver inner-conditions for hatred (these are framed for positive characteristics).

**T4.4 Human→Receiving — T4.4.1** — Inferential: the **received-from-outside** origin (3 occ) and the "hated wife/son" law (Deu 21:16) show hatred *landing on* a person from another. **T4.4.2 / T4.4.3** — **SILENT** (no uptake-condition data).

**T4.5 Boundaries — T4.5.1** — Evidence shows hatred operating **within existing bonds** (brothers: Gen 37:4; family: 2Sa 13; co-wives: Gen 29) and across them; the most acute cases are *within* kinship bonds. **T4.5.2** — Crosses covenantal boundaries (hatred of Israel's enemies and of God's enemies, Psa 83:2). **T4.5.3** — Relational scope is broad: kin, community, enemies, and God.

**T4.6 Spiritual Beings — all:** **SILENT** — no angelic/adversarial-being interface tagged for C-A (object_type spiritual-being appears once in the cluster, not in C-A).

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

**T5.1.1** — **SILENT** — no transformation of the person tagged. (Pro 26:28 shows hatred *causing* ruin to another, not transforming the hater — labelled inferential.) **T5.1.2** — SILENT.

**T5.2.1** — A **sequence** is shown in the cause data: love/preference → resulting hatred (Gen 29:31; 37:4), and prior violation → revulsion-hatred (2Sa 13:15 Amnon's love turning to hatred after the act). So a before→after sequence exists in narrative cases, though not as an inner-state progression of the hater.

**T5.3.1** — **SILENT** — no mechanism-of-change in the *person* tagged. **T5.3.2** — SILENT.

**T5.4.1** — Inferential: hatred operates as a **context for affliction** of its object (Eze 35:6 pursuit; Psa 83 enemies) — but not as response/product of suffering *in the hater*. Mostly **SILENT** on the hater's side. **T5.4.2** — SILENT.

**T5.5.1** — **SILENT** — no sanctification-arc participation tagged (the commanded-hatred-of-evil seam touches formation inferentially, but is not tagged as a developmental arc).

**T5.6.1** — **SILENT** — no eschatological trajectory tagged for C-A.

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics

**T6.1.1** — Adjacent characteristics co-occurring in C-A verses (non-M06 clusters): **M44 (17), M15 wisdom (16), M25 (16), M47 (15), M10b (12), M05 love (12), M10 (11), M14 (11), M26 (10), M23 (9)**, with M03 grief, M04 joy, M01 fear, M02 anger also present. Within M06, C-A co-occurs with C-C (3), C-B (2), C-F (1), C-D (1). **T6.1.2** — The strong co-occurrence with **love (M05)** and **wisdom (M15)** places aversive affect on the love↔hate axis and within the wisdom literature's moral evaluation of hatred.

**T6.2.1** — Sequence: love/preference reliably **precedes** the hatred in the narrative cases (Gen 29:31; 37:4). **T6.2.2** — The relationship reads as **causal** there (greater love for one produces hatred of the other).

**T6.3.1** — Produces: ruin/shame in the object (Pro 26:28; 13:5) — but these are effects on the *other*, not another inner characteristic of the hater; **largely SILENT** on producing another characteristic. **T6.3.2** — Produced by love-preference/jealousy in the cause cases (inferential link to M05 / jealousy). **T6.3.3** — Inferential: science (T7.3) treats contempt (C-B) as a *constituent* of hate (Sternberg) — so C-B may be a constituent of C-A; flagged as inferential, to test in consolidation.

**T6.4.1** — Vocabulary sharing: the `sa.ne` root generates the standard OT word for **enemy** ("the one who hates," `sone'`), shared with the enmity field (C-E) and with relational-opposition contexts across the programme. **T6.4.2** — Root-level: yes — `sa.ne` → both the verb "hate" and the participle "enemy/hater," a single root generating affect (C-A) and adversary (C-E) senses. **T6.4.3** — The sharing shows aversive affect and adversarial enmity are **etymologically linked** — the felt hatred and the relational opponent issue from one root.

**T6.5.1** — Nearest neighbour: **C-B (appraisive contempt).** Distinction: C-A is `affect`-led (felt rejection) while C-B is `moral_evaluation`-led (a verdict of worthlessness); C-A is **bivalent** (commanded hate of evil exists), C-B has **no righteous seam**. **T6.5.2** — The boundary: where the inner movement is *feeling-with-appraisal* it is C-A; where it is *appraisal-of-worth without the affective tag* it is C-B (na.ats/ba.zah are faculty-absent acts). **T6.5.3** — A distinction of **kind** (faculty: affect vs evaluation), reinforced by valence (bivalent vs uniformly sinful).

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**T7.1.1** — Primary terms: `sa.ne` "to hate" (143), `sin.ah` "hatred" (19), `sa.tam` "harbour animosity" (8), Aramaic `se.na` (2). Root sense: settled aversion/rejection of an object.

**T7.1.2** — Grammatical range: **verb** (Qal `sa.ne`, action 153), **noun** (`sin.ah`, status 19), **adjective/passive participle** (`sa.ni` "hated", 1). The range shows hatred as **act, standing condition, and ascribed status**.

**T7.1.3** — Semantic range: from interpersonal aversion (Gen 37:4) through harboured grudge (`sa.tam`) to morally-charged hatred of evil/falsehood (Psa 119) and divine hatred (Mal 1:3) — a breadth spanning private feeling to covenantal-theological judgement.

**T7.1.4** — Yes — the vocabulary distinguishes **act** (`sa.ne`) from **condition** (`sin.ah`) and from **harboured/persistent** animosity (`sa.tam`). Disposition-vs-act is lexically marked.

**T7.1.5** — Structural-opposite term: **love** (`'ahav`, M05) — not within the C-A set itself but its evidenced antonym (Gen 29:31 contrast; Mal 1:2–3 love/hate pairing). No dedicated "absence-of-hate" term in the set.

**T7.1.6** — Person-type term: **yes** — the `sa.ne` participle "the one who hates / enemy" (`sone'`), the standard OT word for a personal enemy (e.g. "those who hate him", Gen 24:60; "those who hate you", Psa 139:21).

**T7.1.7** — Supplication/seeking term: **none** — hatred is not sought from another; no such term in the set.

**T7.1.8** — OT↔NT: C-A is **OT-only** (all 175 OT); the Aramaic `se.na` (Daniel-era) is the only non-Hebrew form. NT continuity of the *affect* would be carried by Greek `miseō` (outside this M06 focus set) — **labelled inferential / outside-extract**.

**T7.1.9** — Newly-coined NT term: **none** in the C-A set (no NT terms).

**T7.1.10** — The full vocabulary arc shows aversive affect operating across **private emotion, persistent disposition, moral judgement, and divine attribute** — the widest valence range in the cluster.

**T7.2.1** — Function of the primary term: typically the **finite verb governing the clause** (Qal `sa.ne`), with the hater as subject and the hated as object (Gen 37:4 "his brothers… hated him").

**T7.2.2** — Literary form (by book): **psalm 49, wisdom 41, law/narrative 40, prophecy 24, narrative-history 19**, with 2 apocalyptic. Responsible interpretation must weight the **psalmic and wisdom** settings most — where hatred is morally evaluated (Psalms 119/139; Proverbs 8) rather than merely narrated.

**T7.2.3** — Logical structure (representative): in the wisdom/psalm material the argument runs *the fear of the LORD entails hatred of evil* (Pro 8:13), and *alignment with God entails hatred of his enemies* (Psa 139:21–22) — premise (love of God/good) → conclusion (hatred of evil).

**T7.2.4** — Contextual settings: **covenantal** (Mal 1:2–3; Deu), **liturgical/devotional** (Psalms), **judicial** (Exo 18:21 hating dishonest gain), and **familial-narrative** (Gen 29/37; 2Sa 13).

**T7.2.5** — Primary anchor (candidate, **authorial judgement**): **Psa 139:21–22** — "Do I not hate those who hate you, O LORD?… I hate them with complete hatred." It fuses affect (`sin.ah`), the cognitive-moral alignment, the God-interface (both human→God and counter-hatred), and the bivalence in a single text.

**T7.2.6** — That anchor shows what no other C-A verse shows together: **righteous hatred explicitly aligned to God's own**, naming the affect, its object, its moral warrant, and its directedness in one place.

**T7.3.1** — Human-science field (from science extract §1): **social psychology / affective science** — hatred as a sustained, dispositional negative orientation (distinct from reactive anger).

**T7.3.2** — Where science illuminates: **Sternberg's duplex theory** (negation of intimacy + passion + devaluation) coheres with the lexical finding that `sa.ne` fuses **affect + cognition** — the "devaluation/diminution" component matches the cognitive co-tag, and the affective component matches the universal affect tag. Hatred-as-stable-orientation matches the `sin.ah`/`sa.tam` standing-state forms.

**T7.3.3** — Divergence: science treats hatred as **pathological, to be reduced**; the biblical evidence includes a **commanded/righteous hatred of evil** (22 occ) and **divine hatred** (15 agent) that science has no normative framework to evaluate. This is the central divergence for C-A.

**T7.3.4** — Gap surfaced: science's reactive-vs-dispositional distinction prompts checking whether C-A's hatred is **situationally triggered or characterologically settled** — the lexical leans settled (status/grudge forms), which the per-verse cause data (Gen 29; 2Sa 13) only partly qualifies; worth a closer verse pass on the episodic cases.

# M06 · C-A — Aversive affect — felt hatred / settled rejection

**File:** wa-m06-char-a-aversive-affect-v1_0-20260620.md · **Date:** 2026-06-20 · **Cluster:** M06 (Hate, Contempt and Hostility)
**Source:** wa-ve-lexical-extract-M06-20260620 (b1–b3, extract v1_0) · **Prior:** wa-m06-ib-characteristics-v1_0-20260620.md

**Total occurrences gathered for this characteristic: 175** across 6 term(s).

**Defining signature (derived from aggregate evidence):** affect-dominant faculty; predominantly action/status; the felt, settled rejection of an object

**Scope note:** Candidate set from v1_0. mas.te.mah (H4895) flagged as overlapping C-E (enmity) — tested here.

## 2. Characteristic-level tallies (all occurrences)

- **Type:** action 153, status 21, quality 1
- **Seat:** (unseated) 152, soul 16, heart 8, flesh 1

- **Divine involvement:** agent 15, object 10

## 3. Evidence-grounded synthesis

> _Authored from the tallies above and the appendix below; see chat/obslog for the reading. Every claim ties to a count or a cited verse._

The faculty signal is unanimous: **all 175 occurrences tag `affect`**, and on `sa.ne` (143) `cognition` is co-tagged in *every single occurrence* — in this corpus hatred is not raw feeling but feeling fused with appraisal: one hates what one has judged. That fusion is the defining mark of this characteristic.

Grammatically it is predominantly an **action** (153) — something a person does toward an object — with a nominal **status** form (`sin.ah`, 19) naming the standing condition of hatred itself.

When a constitutional seat is named (23 of 175; 152 unseated), it leans to the **soul (16)** over the **heart (8)**, with a single flesh case. On the evidence here, settled hatred is seated in the soul more than the heart.

The object is most often a **person (75)**, with a substantial **abstract (27)** share and **ten God-as-object** cases — hatred is directed at persons, at qualities/things, and at God.

The decisive finding is **valence**: sinful (83) leads, but a coherent **righteous (19) / commanded (3)** seam — carried *entirely by `sa.ne`* — presents hatred of evil and falsehood as a rightly-ordered orientation of the inner being; a single forbidden case marks the inverse. Aversive affect is therefore **bivalent within one root**, not a uniformly negative passion.

The **divine interface runs both ways inside this one characteristic**: God as the agent who hates (15) and God as the object hated (10).

## 4. Membership validation (per term)

- **`sa.ne` (H8130, ×143) — CONFIRMED core.** affect+cognition on every occurrence; carries the entire righteous/commanded seam and both divine directions (agent 11 / object 10). The anchor term of the characteristic.
- **`sin.ah` (H8135, ×19) — CONFIRMED.** The nominal **status** of the same affect ("hatred" as a standing condition). affect ×19.
- **`sa.tam` (H7852, ×8) — CONFIRMED, with a nuance.** affect/action, **uniformly sinful (8/8)**; the sense leans to *harboured, persistent* animosity (a grudge) — a sub-nuance within aversive affect, not a separate characteristic.
- **`se.na` (H8131, Aramaic, ×2) — CONFIRMED.** affect/action; the Aramaic form of the `sa.ne` affect.
- **`mas.te.mah` (H4895, ×2) — RESOLVED to C-A on evidence, flag for dual-tag.** The lexical **faculty is `affect`** (both occurrences), which places it here, yet its sense ("animosity/enmity") is relational and would also read in **C-E**. Recommend dual-tag C-A↔C-E pending your IC2 decision.
- **`sa.ni` (H8146, ×1) — REVIEW (placement).** The single occurrence is a passive/adjectival "hated [one]"; faculty `affect` ties it to C-A, but its **function names the recipient's borne condition**, not the act of hating — overlapping the borne-disgrace layer (cf. C-D `cher.pah`). Flagged for your placement call; not silently moved.

# M06 · C-B Appraisive contempt — tier-question answers (T0–T7)

**File:** wa-m06-char-b-tieranswers-v1_0-20260620.md · **Date:** 2026-06-20
**Cluster:** M06 · **Characteristic:** C-B Appraisive contempt — judging-as-worthless / disdain
**Evidence base:** wa-m06-char-b-contempt-v1_0-20260620.md + lexical extract + science §2 (T7.3 only)
**Terms (69 occ, all OT):** na.ats (25), ba.zah (13), buz (11), ba.ash (8), ne.a.tsah (5), shut (3), she.at (3), biz.za.von (1)

> Each question is answered from evidence or marked **SILENT** with reason. Inferential reasoning labelled. Science used only at T7.3.

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**T0.1.1** — God-relation present in ~18 occ: God as **object** of contempt in 15 (Num 16:30; 2Sa 12:14; Psa 10:3,13; 74:10; Isa 1:4; Jer 23:17; Eze 28:24,26 — spurning/despising the LORD/the Holy One), God as **agent** in 3 (Deu 32:19; Lam 2:6; Mal 2:9 — God's judicial rejection).

**T0.1.2** — Predominantly **borne by the creature, not God**: contempt is overwhelmingly a human posture *toward* God (object 15) and only marginally something God does (agent 3, and there judicial). Unlike C-A (substantial divine hatred), appraisive contempt is **not a divine attribute** but a creaturely act — its rare divine cases are God *rejecting* the unfaithful, not devaluing worth.

**T0.2.1** — No created purpose stated. Where an effect appears (immediate_response 5): contempt issues in the servant being "despised" (Isa 53:3) and in disbelief (Num 14:11).

**T0.2.2** — Reads as the **fallen condition**: uniformly sinful (47) / neutral (16) with **no righteous or commanded seam at all** — there is no rightly-ordered contempt in the evidence.

**T0.2.3** — **SILENT** — no future-fullness orientation tagged.

**T0.3.1** — Inferential: contempt instantiates a **disordering** of the image — the devaluing of one made in God's image — rather than any divine likeness. Recorded as inferential.

**T0.3.2** — **Exclusively creaturely** in practice: the human despising of God/neighbour has no positive divine analogue here (God's 3 agent cases are judicial rejection, not worth-devaluation).

**T0.3.3** — Inferential: contempt directed at God (Psa 10:13 "the wicked renounces/spurns God") indicates a damaged image-relation in the contemnor; contempt suffered (Isa 53:3) indicates nothing defective in the *object*.

**T0.4.1** — **Isa 53:3** (`ba.zah`, the servant "despised and rejected") functions **typologically/christologically** — the human pointing toward the suffering of the Messiah; direction: human contempt establishes the pattern the servant bears. Labelled as the one tagged typological case.

## T1 — Definition

**T1.1.1** — Programme name: *appraisive contempt* — a downward judgement of worth, treating-as-worthless. The name signals an **evaluative** inner movement (a verdict), not primarily a felt emotion.

**T1.1.2** — Hebrew `na.ats` "spurn", `ba.zah` "despise" (acts); `buz` "contempt", `ne.a.tsah`, `she.at`, `biz.za.von` (the verdict-nouns); `ba.ash` "be/become odious" (the object-side). Definitionally: an **act of spurning** plus a **standing verdict of worthlessness**.

**T1.1.3** — The name carries a **hierarchical/relational** implication: contempt places its object *below* the contemnor on a scale of worth (cf. science §2, Gottman).

**T1.2.1** — A **condition/status verdict** (`buz`, status 20) expressed through **acts** (`na.ats`/`ba.zah`, action 49). Two-register: verdict + act.

**T1.2.2** — **Compound/two-register:** an interior `moral_evaluation` verdict (buz, ba.ash — 19) plus faculty-absent **acts** of spurning (na.ats, ba.zah — 47). `ba.ash` adds an **object-side** element ("becoming odious"), the converse pole of actively despising.

**T1.3.1** — Structural opposite: **honour / esteem** (`kabod`; the honour cluster). `ba.zah` "despise" is the standard antonym of `kabad` "to honour"; Isa 53:3 "we esteemed him not" names the absence of esteem.

**T1.3.2** — At its edge it excludes esteem, regard, and acknowledgement of worth.

**T1.3.3** — It is *not* felt hatred (C-A): contempt can be **cold** (no affect tag on na.ats/ba.zah/buz). It ends where the affective rejection (C-A) or the visceral repugnance (C-C, flesh-seated) begins.

**T1.4.1** — Mode: realised as Qal verbs of spurning/despising (action 49) and as verdict-nouns (status 20). The `mode` field is empty cluster-wide. Manner: an **evaluative downgrading** of the object.

**T1.4.2** — Varies by **object** more than by level: contempt of God (Num 16:30), of persons (Isa 53:3), of the offering/sacred (1Sa 2:17), and self-rendered-odious (`ba.ash`, 2Sa 16:21). No constitutional-level variation tagged.

**T1.4.3** — Inferential/partial: `na.ats` of the LORD's word (Num 15:31) operates against a *spoken* command (despising the commandment); not itself a speech-act of the contemnor in most cases. Mostly **none**.

**T1.5.1** — Immediate response (5 occ): "despised" outcome (Isa 53:3), disbelief (Num 14:11), war/escalation (1Ch 19:6). Most (64) tag none.

**T1.5.2** — **Varied** — no consistent immediate response.

**T1.6.1** — Sustained effect: the **standing verdict** itself (buz as a status); `ba.ash`'s "becoming a stench" (2Sa 10:6) is a durable spoiled standing. Otherwise sparse.

**T1.6.3** — The sustained effect is the **fixed low valuation / spoiled standing**; the immediate response is its episodic expression (an act of spurning, a refusal to believe).

**T1.7.1** — **SILENT** — no "right operation" conditions, since contempt has no righteous seam here.

**T1.7.2** — Distortion conditions: contempt is occasioned by sin and presumption — David's deed giving cause to despise the LORD (2Sa 12:14), breaking the commandment (Num 15:31), pride (Eze 28). No adversarial-spirit tag.

**T1.7.3** — **SILENT**.

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**T2.1.1** — Seat named in 13 of 69: **soul 7, heart 6** (rest unseated); `she.at` "scorn" notably soul-seated.

**T2.1.2** — Pattern: contempt, when seated, sits in **soul and heart roughly equally**, never in flesh — consistent with a cognitive/evaluative (not visceral) characteristic. 57 unseated.

**T2.10.1** — **SILENT/none** — no constitutional movement or external-source transfer tagged (origin all none).

**T2.7.1** — **SILENT** — no body link.

**T2.9.1** — Origin: **not stated** on any occurrence (origin all none). Cause data shows elicitors (sin, presumption) but not a tagged origin.

**T2.9.2** — **SILENT** — origin untagged throughout.

## T3 — The Inner Faculties

**T3.1 Perception — all:** **SILENT** — not tagged.

**T3.2 Cognition — T3.2.1** — Inferential/partial: contempt is an evaluative act bordering cognition, but the tagged faculty is `moral_evaluation`, not `cognition` (see T3.8). **SILENT** as a direct cognition tag; cross-ref T3.8. **T3.2.2/T3.2.3** — SILENT.

**T3.3 Memory — all:** **SILENT**.

**T3.4 Affect — T3.4.1** — Limited: `affect` tagged on only **3** occurrences (`shut` "despise"). **T3.4.2** — In those, contempt carries a scornful feeling. **T3.4.3** — The pattern (3 of 69) shows contempt is **predominantly NOT affective** — it is cold evaluation, distinguishing it from C-A. (The 3 affect cases are the `shut` flag noted in discovery.)

**T3.5 Creativity — all:** **SILENT**.

**T3.6 Volition — all:** **SILENT** — no volition tag.

**T3.7 Agency — T3.7.1** — Inferential: the spurning *acts* (na.ats/ba.zah, action 49) involve agentive doing, but agency-faculty is not tagged. **SILENT** as a tag; noted inferentially. **T3.7.2/3** — SILENT.

**T3.8 Moral Evaluation — T3.8.1** — **Yes — the defining faculty.** `moral_evaluation` tagged on 19 occ (`buz`, `ba.ash`): contempt is a verdict assessing the object against a worth-standard. **T3.8.2** — It renders the object as beneath worth/regard. **T3.8.3** — The pattern makes C-B the **evaluation-led** characteristic of the cluster — contempt *is* a moral-evaluative downgrade (uniformly negative here).

**T3.9 Conscience — all:** **SILENT**.

**T3.10 Conscientiousness — all:** **SILENT**.

**T3.11 Relational Capacity — T3.11.1** — Inferential: contempt is profoundly relational (object person 22; science §2 names it the most relationship-destructive emotion), but relational-capacity is not a tagged faculty. **SILENT** as a tag; cross-ref T4. **T3.11.2/3** — SILENT.

## T4 — Relational Interfaces

**T4.1 God→Human — T4.1.1** — Limited: God as agent of rejection in 3 (Deu 32:19; Lam 2:6; Mal 2:9). **T4.1.2** — Basis is **responsive/judicial** — God spurns in response to provocation/unfaithfulness. **T4.1.3** — Shows God's disposition to **reject the persistently unfaithful**, not to devalue worth arbitrarily.

**T4.2 Human→God — T4.2.1** — **Yes — the dominant vector:** 15 occ have God as object of human contempt (spurning the LORD, Num 16:30; renouncing God, Psa 10:13; despising the Holy One, Isa 1:4). **T4.2.2** — The posture is presumption/pride — the opposite of the seeking posture. **T4.2.3** — It shows a relationship of **disdainful rejection** of God — the gravest form in the data.

**T4.3 Human→Giving — T4.3.1** — **Yes:** person-directed contempt (person 22) — the servant despised (Isa 53:3), enemies' scorn (Psa 123). It operates as relational degradation. **T4.3.2/T4.3.3** — **SILENT** (no giver-condition data for a negative characteristic).

**T4.4 Human→Receiving — T4.4.1** — Inferential: contempt is *received/borne* by the despised (Isa 53:3 the servant; the object-side `ba.ash` "become odious to", 2Sa 10:6). **T4.4.2/3** — **SILENT**.

**T4.5 Boundaries — T4.5.1** — Operates both within bonds (David's house, 2Sa 12:14) and across (enemies' scorn). **T4.5.2** — Crosses covenantal boundaries (Gentile contempt of Israel; Israel's contempt of God). **T4.5.3** — Scope: God, covenant community, and outsiders.

**T4.6 Spiritual Beings — all:** **SILENT** — no angelic/adversarial interface tagged for C-B.

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

**T5.1.1 / T5.1.2** — **SILENT** — no transformation of the person tagged.

**T5.2.1** — Sequence (cause data): sin/presumption → contempt of the LORD (2Sa 12:14 deed → occasion to despise; Num 15:31 breaking command → despising the word). A before→after eliciting sequence, not an inner-state progression.

**T5.3.1 / T5.3.2** — **SILENT** — no mechanism-of-change in the person.

**T5.4.1** — Inferential: contempt is **suffered** in affliction (Isa 53:3 the servant; Psa 123 "we have had more than enough of contempt"). It is a *context for* affliction of the despised. **T5.4.2** — SILENT on what suffering does to the contempt itself.

**T5.5.1** — **SILENT**.

**T5.6.1** — **SILENT**.

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics

**T6.1.1** — Co-occurring non-M06 clusters: **M44 (7), M47 (7), M22 (7), M23 (6), M03 grief (6), M10 (5), M15 wisdom (5), M30 (5), M02 anger (4)**. Within M06, C-B co-occurs most with **C-D reproach (5)** — contempt and taunt travel together — then C-A (2), C-C (1).

**T6.1.2** — The C-B↔C-D co-occurrence (5) shows **contempt and verbal reproach as a working pair** — the inner verdict and its public expression; co-occurrence with grief (M03) reflects the despised one's suffering.

**T6.2.1** — Sequence: contempt **follows** an eliciting offence/sin in the cause cases; it often **precedes/accompanies** reproach (C-D). **T6.2.2** — The contempt→reproach relationship reads **causal/expressive** (the verdict issues in the taunt).

**T6.3.1** — Produces: **reproach/taunt (C-D)** as its outward expression — inferential from the co-occurrence + the verdict→act logic. **T6.3.2** — Produced by pride/presumption and by the object's perceived offence (Eze 28 pride; 2Sa 12:14). **T6.3.3** — Per science §2/Sternberg, **contempt (devaluation) is a constituent of hate (C-A)** — so C-B may be a *constituent element of C-A*. Flagged inferential for consolidation.

**T6.4.1** — Vocabulary sharing: `na.ats` and `ba.zah` recur in worship/covenant-violation contexts shared with the honour/worship fields; `ba.ash` "stink/odious" shares the somatic-disgust register with C-C's detestable vocabulary. **T6.4.2** — Root-level: `ba.ash` (odour) links to disgust/repugnance terms (C-C) at the sensory-metaphor level. **T6.4.3** — Shows contempt sits **between honour (its opposite) and loathing (C-C, via disgust)**.

**T6.5.1** — Nearest neighbour: **C-A (aversive affect).** Distinction: C-A is felt (affect), C-B is **cold evaluation** (moral_evaluation; only 3 of 69 affect-tagged) and **uniformly sinful** (no righteous seam). **T6.5.2** — Boundary: a verdict of *worthlessness without affect* = C-B; a *felt rejection* = C-A. **T6.5.3** — Distinction of **kind** (faculty) and **valence range**.

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**T7.1.1** — Primary terms: `na.ats` "spurn" (25), `ba.zah` "despise" (13), `buz` "contempt" (11). Root sense: to treat/regard as of no account.

**T7.1.2** — Grammatical range: **verb** (na.ats, ba.zah, ba.ash — action 49), **noun** (buz, ne.a.tsah, she.at, biz.za.von — status 20). The range shows contempt as **both the act of spurning and the standing verdict**.

**T7.1.3** — Semantic range: from spurning a command/sacred thing (Num 15:31; 1Sa 2:17), through despising a person (Isa 53:3), to becoming-odious (`ba.ash`, 2Sa 16:21) and nominal contempt/scorn (`buz`, Job 12:5).

**T7.1.4** — Yes — disposition/verdict (`buz` noun) vs act (`na.ats`/`ba.zah` verb) vs object-side condition (`ba.ash` "be odious"). Three aspects marked.

**T7.1.5** — Opposite/absence term: **honour/esteem** (`kabad`/`kabod`) — the standard antonym of `ba.zah`; "we esteemed him not" (Isa 53:3) names its absence.

**T7.1.6** — Person-type term: **partial** — `ba.zah`'s passive "the despised one" names the *object* (Isa 53:3); no dedicated agent-noun for "one who habitually despises" in the set.

**T7.1.7** — Supplication/seeking term: **none**.

**T7.1.8** — OT↔NT: C-B is **OT-only**; NT continuity of contempt (Gk `exoutheneō`, `kataphroneō`) is **outside this focus set** — labelled inferential.

**T7.1.9** — Newly-coined NT term: **none** in set.

**T7.1.10** — The vocabulary arc shows contempt operating across **cultic, royal, prophetic, and personal** registers — always a downward worth-verdict, never positively valued.

**T7.2.1** — Function: the primary verb governs the clause with the contemnor as subject and the despised as object (Isa 53:3 "he was despised", passive — the object foregrounded).

**T7.2.2** — Literary form: **prophecy 24, psalm 12, narrative-history 11, wisdom 11, law/narrative 9**. The prophetic and psalmic weighting requires reading contempt within **covenant-lawsuit and lament** settings (despising God / being despised before enemies).

**T7.2.3** — Logical structure (representative): *because* the offender has spurned the LORD's word/deed, judgement follows (Num 15:31; 2Sa 12:14) — offence (contempt of God) → consequence.

**T7.2.4** — Settings: **covenantal/judicial** (Num 15:31; Deu 32:19), **liturgical-lament** (Psa 10; 74; 123), **royal** (Eze 28), **servant-prophecy** (Isa 53).

**T7.2.5** — Primary anchor (candidate, **authorial judgement**): **Isa 53:3** — "He was despised and rejected by men… and we esteemed him not." It states contempt's essence (a worth-verdict, `ba.zah`), its relational and public character, its opposite (esteem), and its typological reach in one verse.

**T7.2.6** — That anchor shows what no other C-B verse shows: contempt **borne by the innocent/righteous one** — separating the verdict from any actual unworthiness in its object, and carrying the christological pattern.

**T7.3.1** — Field (science §2): **moral psychology / emotion research** — contempt and disgust.

**T7.3.2** — Where science illuminates: **Gottman** names contempt the most destructive relational emotion — communicating the other as fundamentally inferior — which matches C-B's `moral_evaluation` verdict and its relational object-class (person 22). **Haidt/Rozin** disgust illuminates the `ba.ash` "stink/odious" register as olfactory-disgust extended into the moral domain.

**T7.3.3** — Divergence: science treats contempt as **dysfunctional/to-be-reduced**; the biblical evidence frames the gravest cases as **contempt of God** (object 15) — a covenant-theological category science does not evaluate. (Note: unlike C-A, C-B has *no* "appropriate contempt" seam, so the divergence is narrower than for hatred.)

**T7.3.4** — Gap surfaced: science's **contempt-vs-disgust distinction** prompts disentangling C-B (cold contempt) from C-C (visceral loathing) — which the lexical already separates by faculty/seat; the `ba.ash` case sits on the seam and merits a verse-level check.
