## 3. Evidence-grounded synthesis

> _Authored from the tallies above and the appendix below; see chat/obslog for the reading. Every claim ties to a count or a cited verse._

This characteristic splits cleanly by faculty into **two registers**:

1. A nominal **verdict of worthlessness** carrying `moral_evaluation` — `buz` "contempt" (11) and `ba.ash` "be/become odious" (8), 19 occurrences. This is the interior appraisal: a judgement that something is of no worth.
2. A set of **acts of spurning/despising** that carry **no interior faculty at all** — `na.ats` (25), `ba.zah` (13), `ne.a.tsah` (5) — 47 faculty-absent occurrences. These name the outward act that *expresses* contempt rather than the appraisal itself.

So C-B straddles the inner/outer boundary in its own right: contempt is part inner verdict, part outward act of spurning.

**Grammar:** action 49 (spurn/despise) versus status 20 (the "contempt/scorn" nouns).

**The dominant relational vector is toward God.** Object_type God appears 10 times, and divine involvement is **object 15** against agent 3 — in this corpus contempt is markedly *directed at God or the holy* (the spurning of the Holy One), far more than it is something God does. This is the opposite skew to C-A, where God was as often agent as object.

**Valence is the clean contrast with C-A:** contempt is **overwhelmingly sinful (47) with no righteous or commanded seam at all**. Where aversive affect (C-A) was bivalent within a single root, appraisive contempt has no rightly-ordered use in this corpus.

**Seat:** when seated (12 of 69), soul (7) and heart (6) are near-even; `she.at` "scorn" notably seats in the soul.

## 4. Membership validation (per term)

- **`na.ats` (H5006, ×25) — CONFIRMED.** The act of *spurning*; faculty-absent (outward expression). Heavily God-directed (object 12 of 25). A core member, but on the expression side of contempt.
- **`ba.zah` (H0959, ×13) — CONFIRMED.** The act of *despising*; faculty-absent, action, predominantly sinful.
- **`buz` (H0937, ×11) — CONFIRMED core.** `moral_evaluation` / status — the **nominal verdict** of worthlessness. The interior anchor of the characteristic.
- **`ba.ash` (H0887, ×8) — RESOLVED into C-B (resolves the v1_0 omission).** Faculty `moral_evaluation` matches C-B's signature; it is unseated, so it does **not** fit C-C (loathing, which seats in flesh). Directional nuance: `ba.ash` is "to *become* odious / be held in contempt" — the **object-side** of the contempt relation (making oneself contemptible), the converse of actively despising. Flagged as a sub-sense, placed here on faculty evidence.
- **`ne.a.tsah` (H5007A/B, ×5) — CONFIRMED.** Nominal "contempt"; faculty-absent, status, sinful.
- **`she.at` (H7589, ×3) — CONFIRMED.** Nominal "scorn"; soul-seated (3) — one of the few seated contempt terms.
- **`biz.za.von` (H0963, ×1) — CONFIRMED.** Nominal "contempt"; status.
- **`shut` (H7590, ×3) — REVIEW (faculty mismatch).** Sense "despise" fits contempt, but the lexical faculty is **`affect`**, not `moral_evaluation` — which would pull it toward C-A. Flagged for your placement / dual-tag call (IC2); not silently moved.

# M06 · C-C Loathing — tier-question answers (T0–T7)

**File:** wa-m06-char-c-tieranswers-v1_0-20260620.md · **Date:** 2026-06-20
**Cluster:** M06 · **Characteristic:** C-C Loathing — visceral repugnance / detestation
**Evidence base:** wa-m06-char-c-loathing-v1_0-20260620.md + lexical extract + science §2 (disgust; T7.3 only)
**Terms (29 occ; OT 27 / NT 2):** ta.av (H8581 20 + H8374 1), she.qets (4), de.ra.on (2), bdelussomai (2)

> Answered from evidence or marked **SILENT** with reason. Inferential labelled. Science used only at T7.3. NB: discovery established C-C is **faculty-absent throughout**; the interior signal is the 3 flesh-seated cases.

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**T0.1.1** — God-relation present in 3 occ, all as **agent**: God abhors (Psa 5:6 the bloodthirsty; Psa 106:40 his own heritage in judgement; Amo 6:8 "the LORD abhors the pride of Jacob"). No God-as-object cases.

**T0.1.2** — **Borne by God himself** in the abhorrence-of-evil sense: divine abhorrence (agent 3) targets bloodshed, pride, and corruption. So loathing-of-evil, like hatred-of-evil (C-A), has a **divine instance** — it is not exclusively creaturely.

**T0.2.1** — Where shown: the commanded detestation serves to **separate the person from the abominable** (Deu 7:26 "you shall utterly detest it… it is devoted to destruction"). Effect at Rev 21:8: the detestable share the fiery judgement.

**T0.2.2** — **Both.** A created-design role appears in the commanded/righteous seam (Deu 7:26 detest the devoted thing; Psa 119:163 abhor falsehood; Rom 2:22 abhor idols); a fallen instance appears in the forbidden case (Deu 23:7 "you shall not abhor" the brother-nation — wrongful loathing).

**T0.2.3** — Partial: the **eschatological** abhorrence (de.ra.on, Isa 66:24 / Dan 12:2 "everlasting abhorrence"; Rev 21:8) orients toward a final state — the only characteristic in M06 with a tagged eschatological reach.

**T0.3.1** — Inferential: rightly-directed loathing instantiates **God's repudiation of evil/uncleanness** (God abhors pride, Amo 6:8); wrongly-directed loathing (Deu 23:7) disorders it.

**T0.3.2** — **Shared** between God and person (God abhors evil; the person is commanded to detest the abominable), valence-differentiated as in C-A.

**T0.3.3** — Inferential: a person who abhors falsehood/idols (Psa 119:163; Rom 2:22) shows a rightly-ordered repudiation faculty; one who abhors the brother (Deu 23:7) shows it disordered.

**T0.4.1** — **de.ra.on** (Isa 66:24; Dan 12:2 "shame and everlasting abhorrence") is used **eschatologically** — the final state of the rejected; direction: pointing beyond the immediate to the last judgement. Tagged typological/eschatological.

## T1 — Definition

**T1.1.1** — Programme name: *loathing* — visceral repugnance / detestation. The name signals a **repudiating revulsion** (treating as abominable), with a bodily/ritual colouring.

**T1.1.2** — `ta.av` "abhor/detest/loathe" (the act, 21); `she.qets` "detestation", `de.ra.on` "abhorrence" (the object/condition nouns); Greek `bdelussomai` "abhor". Definitionally: to **recoil from as abominable**.

**T1.1.3** — Carries a **separation** implication — to abhor is to set apart from oneself as unclean/abominable (Deu 7:26).

**T1.2.1** — Predominantly an **act** (action 23) with a **status/object** form (`she.qets`/`de.ra.on`, status 6) naming the detestable thing/condition.

**T1.2.2** — On the evidence, **simple at the faculty level** (no faculty tag), but bears a **dual register**: a **ritual/somatic** mode (flesh-seated `she.qets`/`de.ra.on`) and a **moral** mode (`ta.av` of falsehood/idols).

**T1.3.1** — Structural opposite: **delight / desire** (to long-for, the homonymic counter-sense) and, on the ritual axis, **clean/holy** vs detestable (Lev 11). No opposite term inside the C-C set.

**T1.3.2** — At its edge it excludes acceptance, desire, and contact — it pushes the abominable away (Deu 7:26 separation).

**T1.3.3** — It is *not* cold contempt (C-B, evaluation/unseated): loathing carries a **visceral/somatic** edge (the only flesh-seated set) and a **ritual** register C-B lacks.

**T1.4.1** — Mode: Qal/Piel verbs of abhorring (action 23) and object-nouns (status 6). `mode` field empty. Manner: **repudiating recoil**.

**T1.4.2** — Varies by **register**: ritual/dietary (Lev 11 `she.qets`, flesh-seated) vs moral (Psa 119:163 abhor falsehood) vs eschatological (Isa 66:24 `de.ra.on`).

**T1.4.3** — Partial: the **commanded** detestation (Deu 7:26) operates through an imperative/communicative mode. Otherwise none.

**T1.5.1** — Immediate response (1 occ): the detestable are cast into the fire (Rev 21:8). Otherwise none tagged.

**T1.5.2** — **SILENT** — too few tagged (1) to assess consistency.

**T1.6.1** — Sustained effect: a durable condition of **being-abominable / everlasting abhorrence** (de.ra.on, Dan 12:2) — a permanent repudiated state.

**T1.6.3** — The sustained effect (everlasting abhorrence) is a **fixed final condition**; the immediate response (consigned to fire) is its episodic enactment.

**T1.7.1** — Operates rightly where its object is the abominable/false (Deu 7:26; Psa 119:163; Rom 2:22) — under a condition of covenant fidelity.

**T1.7.2** — Distorted where directed at the brother (Deu 23:7 forbidden). No adversarial-spirit tag.

**T1.7.3** — **SILENT**.

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**T2.1.1** — Seat named in 8 of 29: **flesh 3, soul 3, heart 2**. The **flesh-seating is unique to C-C** (`she.qets` ×2, `de.ra.on` ×1).

**T2.1.2** — Pattern: loathing is the **only M06 characteristic with a body seat** — its detestation register touches the flesh (the ritually unclean/abominable), while its moral register reaches soul/heart. The body link is **indicative** (marking the abominable) rather than expressive.

**T2.10.1** — **received-from-outside** tagged once (origin); otherwise no movement. Mostly none.

**T2.7.1** — Body link (3 flesh): direction is **soul/person repudiating outward toward** the abominable object — the body marks the boundary of the clean/unclean rather than feeding back inward. Inferential reading of the 3 cases.

**T2.9.1** — Origin: **not stated** (28); received-from-outside once.

**T2.9.2** — **SILENT** — too sparse.

## T3 — The Inner Faculties

**T3.1 Perception — all:** **SILENT** (no tag). *Inferential note:* the disgust register implies an olfactory/sensory basis (cf. science §2), but no perception faculty is tagged.

**T3.2 Cognition — all:** **SILENT**.

**T3.3 Memory — all:** **SILENT**.

**T3.4 Affect — all:** **SILENT as a tag** — `faculty` is absent on all 29. *Inferential:* the repugnance has an affective/visceral quality, but the extract does not tag it `affect` (unlike C-A). Recorded as inferential, not a finding.

**T3.5 Creativity — all:** **SILENT**.

**T3.6 Volition — T3.6.1** — Inferential: commanded detestation (Deu 7:26) implies a volitional/choice element. **SILENT** as a tag. **T3.6.2/3** — SILENT.

**T3.7 Agency — all:** **SILENT** (the abhorring acts are repudiations, agency untagged).

**T3.8 Moral Evaluation — T3.8.1** — Inferential: the valence spread (commanded/righteous/forbidden/sinful) shows moral assessment operating through loathing, but `moral_evaluation` is **not** a tagged faculty here (unlike C-B). **SILENT** as a direct tag; cross-ref valence. **T3.8.2/3** — SILENT-with-inferential.

**T3.9 Conscience — all:** **SILENT**.

**T3.10 Conscientiousness — all:** **SILENT**.

**T3.11 Relational Capacity — all:** **SILENT**.

> **C-C faculty note:** with no faculty tagged on any occurrence, every T3 sub-question is silent at the tag level. This is the strongest evidence that C-C is, lexically, an **act of repudiation + a category of the abominable** rather than a tagged interior faculty.

## T4 — Relational Interfaces

**T4.1 God→Human — T4.1.1** — **Yes:** God as agent abhorring (Psa 5:6; 106:40; Amo 6:8). **T4.1.2** — Basis **responsive/judicial** — God abhors evil, bloodshed, and pride. **T4.1.3** — Shows God's disposition to **repudiate corruption** within his own people (Psa 106:40).

**T4.2 Human→God — T4.2.1** — **SILENT/none** — no God-as-object cases (obj=God empty). Loathing is not directed at God in the evidence (unlike C-A/C-B). **T4.2.2/3** — SILENT.

**T4.3 Human→Giving — T4.3.1** — **Yes (object-directed):** detestation of persons/things (person 7) — Edom/Egypt (Deu 23:7, forbidden), the devoted thing (Deu 7:26). **T4.3.2/3** — **SILENT**.

**T4.4 Human→Receiving — T4.4.1** — Inferential: the abominable are *made* detestable / everlastingly abhorred (de.ra.on, Dan 12:2) — a borne condition. **T4.4.2/3** — **SILENT**.

**T4.5 Boundaries — T4.5.1** — Operates strongly across **covenantal/ritual boundaries** (clean vs unclean; Israel vs the abominable). **T4.5.2** — Crosses covenant lines (the forbidden Deu 23:7 case concerns near-kin nations). **T4.5.3** — Scope: the abominable/unclean, evil, and the eschatologically rejected.

**T4.6 Spiritual Beings — T4.6.1** — **Partial:** object_type **spiritual-being** is tagged once in C-C (the cluster's only such case) — loathing touching idols/false-worship objects (cf. Rom 2:22 abhor idols). **T4.6.2/3** — SILENT.

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

**T5.1.1 / T5.1.2** — **SILENT** — no transformation tagged.

**T5.2.1** — **SILENT** — no inner sequence (only 2 cause cases, both elicitors not progressions).

**T5.3.1 / T5.3.2** — **SILENT**.

**T5.4.1** — **SILENT** — no suffering relation tagged on the experiencer side.

**T5.5.1** — **SILENT**.

**T5.6.1** — **Yes — uniquely for M06:** loathing is **eschatologically oriented** — `de.ra.on` "everlasting abhorrence" (Dan 12:2; Isa 66:24) and the detestable in the fire (Rev 21:8) point to a final state. C-C is the only M06 characteristic carrying this.

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics

**T6.1.1** — Co-occurring non-M06 clusters: **M10 (4), M27 (4), M47 (3), M14 (2), M23 (2), M13 (2), M12 (2), M26 (2)**. Within M06: C-A (3), C-B (1), C-D (1). Sparse co-occurrence overall (small corpus).

**T6.1.2** — The thin co-occurrence reflects C-C's **specialised ritual/eschatological register** — it sits somewhat apart from the interpersonal mass of the cluster.

**T6.2.1 / T6.2.2** — **SILENT** — no consistent sequence (corpus too small).

**T6.3.1** — **SILENT** — no production of another characteristic tagged. **T6.3.2** — Produced by encounter with the abominable/unclean (Deu 7:26 the devoted thing as cause). **T6.3.3** — Per science §2, loathing/disgust may be a **constituent of contempt-and-hate** (the revulsion component of Sternberg's model) — so C-C may be a constituent of C-A. Inferential; flagged.

**T6.4.1** — Vocabulary sharing: `ta.av` "abhor" shares the **disgust register** with C-B's `ba.ash` "stink/odious"; both root in sensory revulsion. **T6.4.2** — Root-level: the abhorrence/stench vocabulary links C-C and C-B at the **somatic-disgust** level. **T6.4.3** — Shows loathing (C-C) and the disgust-edge of contempt (`ba.ash`, C-B) are **the two halves of one disgust phenomenon** that the cluster's vocabulary conflates (science §2 flags exactly this).

**T6.5.1** — Nearest neighbour: **C-A (aversion)** by sense, **C-B (`ba.ash`)** by disgust-register. Distinction from C-A: C-C is **faculty-absent + flesh-seated + ritual**, C-A is **affect-tagged + soul-seated**. **T6.5.2** — Boundary: visceral/ritual repudiation = C-C; felt rejection = C-A; cold worth-verdict = C-B. **T6.5.3** — Distinction of **constitutional level** (flesh vs soul) and **register** (ritual/somatic vs affective vs evaluative).

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**T7.1.1** — Primary terms: `ta.av` "abhor/detest/loathe" (21); `she.qets` "detestation" (4); `de.ra.on` "abhorrence" (2); Gk `bdelussomai` (2). Root sense: to recoil from as abominable/unclean.

**T7.1.2** — Grammatical range: **verb** (ta.av, bdelussomai — action 23), **noun** (she.qets, de.ra.on — status 6). Range shows loathing as **the act of abhorring and the category of the abominable**.

**T7.1.3** — Semantic range: ritual/dietary detestable (Lev 11), moral abhorrence of falsehood/idols (Psa 119:163; Rom 2:22), divine abhorrence of evil (Amo 6:8), eschatological abhorrence (Dan 12:2). Narrow root, broad register.

**T7.1.4** — Yes — act (`ta.av`) vs object/condition (`she.qets`/`de.ra.on`). Act vs condition marked.

**T7.1.5** — Opposite/absence term: **delight/desire** (conceptual) and **clean/holy** (ritual axis); none inside the set.

**T7.1.6** — Person-type term: **none** — `she.qets`/`de.ra.on` name the abominable *thing/condition*, not a person-type.

**T7.1.7** — Supplication/seeking term: **none**.

**T7.1.8** — OT↔NT: **the only M06 characteristic with NT continuity** — Hebrew `ta.av` → Greek `bdelussomai` (Rom 2:22 abhor idols; Rev 21:8 the detestable). Continuity of the **abhorrence act** across Testaments, carrying the ritual→moral→eschatological arc.

**T7.1.9** — Newly-coined NT term: **none**; `bdelussomai` is the LXX/NT counterpart, not a coinage.

**T7.1.10** — The vocabulary arc shows loathing operating from **bodily/ritual detestation through moral abhorrence to eschatological repudiation** — uniquely spanning flesh, soul, and last things.

**T7.2.1** — Function: the primary verb governs the clause with the abhorrer as subject (Amo 6:8 "the LORD abhors…"); the object-nouns function as predicate categories ("they are detestable", Lev 11:11).

**T7.2.2** — Literary form: **prophecy 10, psalm 6, law 4, wisdom 4**, plus **epistle 1 (Rom 2:22)** and **apocalyptic 1 (Rev 21:8)**. The legal (Levitical) and apocalyptic forms require reading loathing within **purity law** and **final-judgement** frames.

**T7.2.3** — Logical structure: *because* the thing is devoted/abominable, the person must utterly detest and separate from it (Deu 7:26) — abomination → mandated repudiation.

**T7.2.4** — Settings: **liturgical/purity-legal** (Lev 11), **covenantal** (Deu 7; 23), **prophetic-judicial** (Amo 6:8), **eschatological** (Dan 12; Rev 21).

**T7.2.5** — Primary anchor (candidate, **authorial judgement**): **Deu 7:26** — "you shall utterly detest it and abhor it, for it is devoted to destruction." It states the act (`ta.av`), the object (the abominable), the separation purpose, and the commanded valence together. (Lev 11:11 is the ritual-category anchor; Amo 6:8 the divine-abhorrence anchor.)

**T7.2.6** — That anchor shows what others do not together: loathing as **a commanded inner posture of separation** from the abominable — the design role of the faculty made explicit.

**T7.3.1** — Field (science §2): **moral psychology / disgust research** (Haidt, Rozin).

**T7.3.2** — Where science illuminates: the **bodily-disgust → moral-disgust** model maps C-C's dual register precisely — the flesh-seated ritual detestable (`she.qets`, contamination aversion) and the moral abhorrence of falsehood/idols. The `ba.ash`/`ta.av` stink-and-abhor vocabulary reflects the olfactory-contamination basis science identifies.

**T7.3.3** — Divergence: science treats disgust as **contamination-avoidance to be habituated**; the biblical evidence includes **commanded and divine** abhorrence of evil (Deu 7:26; Amo 6:8) as normative — a category science evaluates only as adaptive/maladaptive.

**T7.3.4** — Gap surfaced: science's contempt/disgust split prompts confirming whether the cluster's "abhorrence" vocabulary is doing **disgust-work (C-C)** or **contempt-work (C-B `ba.ash`)** verse-by-verse — the seam case the discovery already flagged.

---

### Answer coverage (C-C)
Substantive: T0 (9/9 — incl. eschatology) · T1 (16/18) · T6 (~10/13) · T7 (20/20) · T4 (~9/18, incl. the spiritual-being case). **Distinctively, every T3 sub-question is SILENT at the tag level** (faculty absent on all 29) — itself the key finding. T5 mostly silent except T5.6.1 (eschatological — unique to C-C). All silents carry a reason.

**Defining signature (derived from aggregate evidence):** repugnance sense; the only sub-set seating in FLESH; ritual forbidden/commanded valence present

**Scope note:** Candidate set from v1_0. ba.ash (H0887) also tested for fit here in §4.

## 3. Evidence-grounded synthesis

> _Authored from the tallies above and the appendix below; see chat/obslog for the reading. Every claim ties to a count or a cited verse._

**Evidence correction to the v1_0 label.** `faculty` is **absent on all 29 occurrences**. This characteristic is *not* a distinctly-tagged interior faculty in the extract. Lexically it is two things:

1. the **act of treating-as-detestable** — `ta.av` "abhor/detest" (21) and `bdelussomai` "abhor" (2), action 23; and
2. the **ritual/category noun for a detestable thing** — `she.qets` "detestation" (4) and `de.ra.on` "abhorrence" (2), status 6.

The "visceral repugnance (interior)" framing from v1_0 is only partly supported. The **only somatic signal is the flesh seat on 3 occurrences** (`she.qets` ×2, `de.ra.on` ×1), and these sit with the **forbidden** ritual valence (the Levitical unclean categories, e.g. unclean creatures that "are detestable"). The interior/visceral reading rests on those 3 flesh cases, not on a faculty tag.

Like C-A, it carries a **small bivalent seam**: `ta.av` abhorring *evil* reads commanded/righteous (1 each), while the detestable *thing* reads forbidden (3).

**Distinctness from C-B is real on the evidence:** C-B's `ba.ash` is `moral_evaluation` + unseated (an appraisal); C-C is faculty-absent + the **only flesh-seating set** in the cluster (the ritual/somatic detestable). Seat and faculty keep them apart, so `ba.ash` stays in C-B, not here.

## 4. Membership validation (per term)

- **`ta.av` (H8581, ×20) — CONFIRMED.** The act of detesting; faculty-absent, action; carries the small bivalent seam (commanded/forbidden/righteous singletons).
- **`she.qets` (H8263, ×4) — CONFIRMED; the somatic/ritual anchor.** flesh-seated (2) + forbidden (2) — the Levitical detestable category.
- **`de.ra.on` (H1860, ×2) — CONFIRMED.** flesh-seated abhorrence (the eschatological "abhorrence to all flesh" register).
- **`bdelussomai` (G0948, ×2) — CONFIRMED.** NT continuity of the detesting *act* (`ta.av`).
- **`ta.av` (H8374, ×1) — CONFIRMED.** Second Strong's of the same translit; soul-seated, divine-agent.
- **`ba.ash` re-test:** does **not** belong here — `moral_evaluation` + unseated places it in C-B, not in this flesh-seated/faculty-absent set.

**Characteristic-status flag (evidence-based, escalates IC1):** because faculty is absent throughout and the interior signal is only 3 flesh cases, the data leaves open whether C-C should stand as a **separate characteristic** or be folded as the **somatic/ritual sub-mode** of aversion under C-A, distinguished solely by the flesh-seat. Presented for your decision; not decided here.

# M06 · C-D Reproach / taunt / derision — tier-question answers (T0–T7)

**File:** wa-m06-char-d-tieranswers-v1_0-20260620.md · **Date:** 2026-06-20
**Cluster:** M06 · **Characteristic:** C-D Reproach / taunt / derision — verbal hostility & borne disgrace
**Evidence base:** wa-m06-char-d-reproach-v1_0-20260620.md + lexical extract + science §4 (social rejection; T7.3 only)
**Terms (111 occ, all OT):** cher.pah (72), cha.raph (38), shim.tsah (1)

> Answered from evidence or marked **SILENT** with reason. Inferential labelled. Science used only at T7.3. NB: discovery established two poles — `cher.pah` (affect-tagged, borne disgrace = interior) and `cha.raph` (faculty-absent, outward act).

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**T0.1.1** — God-relation present in ~22 occ: God as **object** of taunt in 18 (1Sa 17:26,36 Goliath defying "the armies of the living God"; 2Ki 19:4,16,23; 2Ch 32:17; Isa 37; Psa 74:10,18,22; 79:12; 89:51 — reproaching/defying God), God as **agent** in 9 (Jos 5:9 "I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt"; Psa 119:22; Jer 23:40; Joe 2:19; Zep 3:18 — God imposing or removing reproach), and **addressee** in 2.

**T0.1.2** — God is **the object reproached** (his name defied — Goliath, Rabshakeh) and **the agent who removes or imposes reproach** (Jos 5:9; Zep 3:18 removal; Jer 23:40 imposition). The **borne affective disgrace** (`cher.pah`, affect 72) is creaturely; what is divine is being the *target* of reproach and the *one who lifts* it. So reproach engages God relationally without the felt-disgrace being a divine attribute.

**T0.2.1** — Where shown (immediate_response 13): reproach issues in flight (Psa 31:11), being covered with shame (Psa 71:13), the enemy reviling God's name (Psa 74:18), and — positively — its **removal** upon keeping God's testimonies (Psa 119:22) and at restoration (Joe 2:19; Zep 3:18).

**T0.2.2** — Reads as the **fallen condition** in its act-pole (sinful 67 taunting) and as a **borne affliction** in its condition-pole (neutral 30, the narrated state of disgrace). Its *removal* is a redemptive act of God (Jos 5:9; Zep 3:18).

**T0.2.3** — **Yes:** an eschatological orientation toward the **removal of reproach/shame** at restoration (Joe 2:19 "never again… a reproach"; Zep 3:18–20). The future fullness is the lifting of disgrace.

**T0.3.1** — Inferential: in the act-pole, taunting **disorders** the image (defying God, degrading a neighbour); in the condition-pole, borne reproach for God's sake (Psa 69) participates in a **righteous suffering** pattern. Recorded inferential.

**T0.3.2** — The felt-disgrace is **creaturely**; God's role (reproached / remover-of-reproach) is the divine side. Not a shared attribute but a relational interface.

**T0.3.3** — Inferential: reproach borne *for God's sake* (Psa 69:7,9) indicates a rightly-aligned image bearing affliction; reproach *of God* (Goliath) indicates the reviler's disordered relation to God.

**T0.4.1** — **Psa 69** (the reproach borne for God's sake — "the reproaches of those who reproach you have fallen on me", v.9) is used **typologically/christologically** (the human pointing toward the Messiah who bears reproach; cf. its NT use). Direction: the human bearer establishes the pattern fulfilled in Christ. Labelled the principal typological case.

## T1 — Definition

**T1.1.1** — Programme name: *reproach / taunt / derision* — verbal hostility and the borne disgrace it inflicts. The name signals a **two-sided** reality: an outward act of degrading speech and an inward/social condition of shame.

**T1.1.2** — `cher.pah` "reproach" (the borne condition, 72); `cha.raph` "to taunt/defy" (the verbal act, 38); `shim.tsah` "derision" (1). Definitionally: the **act of degrading by speech** and the **state of being disgraced**.

**T1.1.3** — Carries a **public/relational** implication — reproach exists in the space between persons and communities (science §4), and a **directional** one (taunt is aimed *at* a target, often God).

**T1.2.1** — A **condition/status** (`cher.pah`, status 73 — the borne disgrace) *and* an **act** (`cha.raph`, action 38 — the taunt). The cluster's clearest condition+act pairing.

**T1.2.2** — **Compound:** an interior **affective condition** (cher.pah, affect 72 — felt disgrace) plus a faculty-absent **outward act** (cha.raph). The two poles are nearly disjoint in the data.

**T1.3.1** — Structural opposite: **honour / glory** (`kabod`). Reproach is the removal/inverse of honour; its *lifting* restores honour (Jos 5:9; Zep 3:19–20).

**T1.3.2** — At its edge it excludes honour, vindication, and good name — it degrades standing.

**T1.3.3** — It is *not* the inner worth-verdict of contempt (C-B): reproach is **expressed and borne** (verbal act + social condition), whereas contempt can remain an unexpressed evaluation. C-D begins where the verdict goes public.

**T1.4.1** — Mode per verse: `cher.pah` realised as a noun naming the condition (status 73); `cha.raph` as a Piel verb of taunting/defying (action 38). Manner: **degradation by speech** and **the bearing of disgrace**.

**T1.4.2** — Varies by **pole and target**: the act-pole targets God (18), persons (Nabal, 1Sa 25:39), and communities; the condition-pole is borne by the self (self 17) and others (44).

**T1.4.3** — **Yes — strongly communicative:** `cha.raph` is intrinsically a **speech-act** (taunting, defying, reviling — 1Sa 17:26; Psa 74:18 "reviles your name"). This is the cluster's most speech-based characteristic.

**T1.5.1** — Immediate response (13 occ): flight (Psa 31:11), being covered/shamed (Psa 71:13), the enemy's reviling (Psa 74:18); and removal of reproach on covenant fidelity (Psa 119:22).

**T1.5.2** — **Varied** — responses range from flight/shame (in the reproached) to defiant reviling (in the taunter) to removal (in restoration).

**T1.6.1** — Sustained effect: a durable **state of disgrace** — "everlasting reproach" (Jer 23:40), reproach "among the nations" (Psa 44:13) — a standing social condition.

**T1.6.3** — The sustained effect is the **lasting borne disgrace**; the immediate response is its episodic enactment (a taunt uttered, a flight, a shaming).

**T1.7.1** — In the condition-pole, reproach is rightly **borne** when suffered for God's sake (Psa 69:7; 119:22 reproach removed through fidelity).

**T1.7.2** — In the act-pole, taunting arises from defiance/pride (Goliath, 1Sa 17:26; Rabshakeh, 2Ki 19). No adversarial-spirit tag.

**T1.7.3** — **SILENT**.

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**T2.1.1** — Seat named in 8 of 111: **heart 5, soul 3** (rest unseated). Borne disgrace, when seated, sits in heart/soul.

**T2.1.2** — Pattern: reproach is **largely unseated (103)** — fitting its **social/relational** location (science §4: it exists "between persons", not as an individual inner state). The few seated cases (heart/soul) are the *felt* disgrace pole (cher.pah). Never flesh.

**T2.10.1** — **received-from-outside** tagged twice — reproach comes *onto* the person from another (consistent with its relational nature). Otherwise none.

**T2.7.1** — **SILENT** — no body link.

**T2.9.1** — Origin: **mostly not stated** (109); **received-from-outside** (2) — reproach is sourced in another's speech/action.

**T2.9.2** — Origin is **external where tagged** (from the reproacher); single, not multiple.

## T3 — The Inner Faculties

**T3.1 Perception — all:** **SILENT**.

**T3.2 Cognition — all:** **SILENT** (cha.raph is faculty-absent; cher.pah is affect, not cognition).

**T3.3 Memory — all:** **SILENT** — *inferential note:* "everlasting reproach" (Jer 23:40) implies remembered disgrace; not tagged.

**T3.4 Affect — T3.4.1** — **Yes — for the condition-pole:** `affect` tagged on all 72 `cher.pah` occurrences. **T3.4.2** — Borne reproach registers as **felt disgrace/shame** — an interior affective state. **T3.4.3** — The pattern shows that, in this corpus, **social disgrace is internalised as affect** (a key inner-being finding): reproach is not merely a social fact but a felt condition. The act-pole (cha.raph) is, by contrast, affect-absent.

**T3.5 Creativity — all:** **SILENT**.

**T3.6 Volition — all:** **SILENT**.

**T3.7 Agency — T3.7.1** — Inferential: `cha.raph` (the taunt) is an agentive speech-act; agency-faculty not tagged. **SILENT** as a tag. **T3.7.2/3** — SILENT.

**T3.8 Moral Evaluation — all:** **SILENT as a tag** — *inferential:* taunting carries a moral charge (sinful 67), but `moral_evaluation` is not the tagged faculty.

**T3.9 Conscience — all:** **SILENT**.

**T3.10 Conscientiousness — all:** **SILENT**.

**T3.11 Relational Capacity — T3.11.1** — Inferential/strong: reproach is **constitutively relational/social** (science §4) — it operates in the relational space and inflicts social pain — but relational-capacity is not a tagged faculty. **SILENT** as a tag; the relational nature is captured at T4. **T3.11.2/3** — SILENT.

## T4 — Relational Interfaces

**T4.1 God→Human — T4.1.1** — **Yes:** God as agent **removing** reproach (Jos 5:9; Joe 2:19; Zep 3:18) and **imposing** it in judgement (Jer 23:40; Eze 22:4). **T4.1.2** — Basis **covenantal/responsive** — removal at restoration, imposition at unfaithfulness. **T4.1.3** — Shows God as the **vindicator who lifts disgrace** from his people and the judge who imposes it.

**T4.2 Human→God — T4.2.1** — **Yes — the dominant act-vector:** God as object of taunt in 18 (defying the living God — Goliath, Rabshakeh; reviling God's name — Psa 74:18). **T4.2.2** — The posture is **defiance/blasphemy** — the inverse of worship. **T4.2.3** — It shows reproach-of-God as **the gravest provocation**, which God himself answers (Psa 74:22 "arise, plead your cause").

**T4.3 Human→Giving — T4.3.1** — **Yes:** person-to-person taunting (person 27) — Nabal (1Sa 25:39), the mocking of the afflicted (Pro 17:5 "whoever mocks the poor insults his Maker"). **T4.3.2/3** — **SILENT** (no giver-condition data).

**T4.4 Human→Receiving — T4.4.1** — **Yes — strongly:** reproach is **borne/received** (self 17; received-from-outside 2) — the reproached bears disgrace from others (Neh 1:3; Psa 69; Lam 3:61). **T4.4.2/3** — The uptake is involuntary suffering; **SILENT** on conditions of refusal.

**T4.5 Boundaries — T4.5.1** — Operates within bonds (covenant community shamed before nations, Psa 44:13) and across (enemy nations taunting Israel/God). **T4.5.2** — Crosses covenantal boundaries (Gentile reproach of Israel and God; Pro 17:5 crosses to the Maker). **T4.5.3** — Scope: God, the covenant people, the afflicted, and enemies.

**T4.6 Spiritual Beings — all:** **SILENT** — no angelic/adversarial interface tagged for C-D.

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

**T5.1.1** — Inferential: borne reproach is a **context for** affliction that the Psalter shows being **transformed into vindication** (Psa 119:22 reproach removed; Zep 3:19–20) — but transformation of the *person* is not directly tagged. **T5.1.2** — SILENT.

**T5.2.1** — Sequence (cause→state): an offence/defiance → reproach inflicted (1Sa 17:26 defiance → taunt; Gen 34:14 → reproach). A relational before→after.

**T5.3.1** — Mechanism (where shown): **divine intervention** removes reproach (Jos 5:9; Joe 2:19) — change by encounter/restoration rather than gradual formation. **T5.3.2** — SILENT.

**T5.4.1** — **Yes:** reproach operates as **a form of affliction/suffering** — it *is* social pain borne by the afflicted (Psa 69; Lam 3:61; Neh 1:3). **T5.4.2** — The evidence shows the reproached crying out and being vindicated; suffering does not strengthen the reproach but occasions appeal to God.

**T5.5.1** — Inferential: bearing reproach for God's sake (Psa 69) participates in a **formation-through-suffering** arc; not tagged as such. Labelled inferential.

**T5.6.1** — **Yes:** an eschatological orientation toward the **final removal of reproach** (Joe 2:19; Zep 3:18–20) — restoration replaces disgrace.

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics

**T6.1.1** — Co-occurring non-M06 clusters: **M44 (11), M07 (11), M41 (10), M02 anger (7), M25 (6), M03 grief (6), M01 fear (6), M08 (5), M22 (5), M04 joy (5), M05 love (4)**. Within M06: **C-B contempt (5)**, C-A (1), C-C (1).

**T6.1.2** — The C-B↔C-D pairing (5) confirms **contempt (verdict) and reproach (its public voicing)** as a working unit; co-occurrence with anger (M02), grief (M03), and fear (M01) reflects the *reproached person's* emotional context.

**T6.2.1** — Sequence: contempt (C-B) often **precedes/accompanies** reproach (the verdict issuing in the taunt); defiance precedes the taunt of God (1Sa 17). **T6.2.2** — The relationship reads **causal/expressive**.

**T6.3.1** — Produces: grief/shame in the reproached (co-occurrence with M03), and provokes God's vindication (Psa 74:22). **T6.3.2** — Produced by **contempt (C-B)** and by defiance/pride. **T6.3.3** — Reproach is the **outward act that expresses** the contempt-verdict — so C-D may be the *expression-constituent* paired with C-B. Flagged for consolidation.

**T6.4.1** — Vocabulary sharing: `cher.pah` shares the **honour/shame** field with the honour cluster (reproach as inverse of honour); `cha.raph` the **defiance** register with enmity (C-E). **T6.4.2** — Root-level: limited; the sharing is conceptual (shame↔honour) more than root-level. **T6.4.3** — Shows reproach sits on the **honour–shame axis**, linking M06 to the honour/glory characteristics.

**T6.5.1** — Nearest neighbour: **C-B (contempt).** Distinction: C-B is the **inner worth-verdict** (moral_evaluation, often unexpressed); C-D is the **voiced/borne disgrace** (the taunt + the felt shame, affect-tagged). **T6.5.2** — Boundary: an unexpressed devaluation = C-B; a degrading speech-act or a borne social shame = C-D. **T6.5.3** — Distinction of **mode** (inner verdict vs outward expression / borne condition).

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**T7.1.1** — Primary terms: `cher.pah` "reproach" (72), `cha.raph` "to taunt/defy/revile" (38). Root sense: to expose to shame / cast a taunt.

**T7.1.2** — Grammatical range: **noun** (cher.pah — the condition, status 73), **verb** (cha.raph — the act, Piel, action 38). The split itself shows the **condition vs act** structure.

**T7.1.3** — Semantic range: from personal insult (1Sa 25:39) through national disgrace (Psa 44:13; Neh 1:3) to the defiance of God himself (1Sa 17:26; 2Ki 19) — private to cosmic-covenantal.

**T7.1.4** — Yes — **condition** (`cher.pah`) vs **act** (`cha.raph`) is the defining lexical distinction (status vs action).

**T7.1.5** — Opposite/absence term: **honour/glory** (`kabod`) — reproach is its removal; vindication (Jos 5:9; Zep 3:19) names the reversal.

**T7.1.6** — Person-type term: **partial** — `cha.raph`'s participle "the reviler/taunter" names the agent; `cher.pah` names the borne condition, not a person-type.

**T7.1.7** — Supplication/seeking term: **none** (reproach is not sought; though appeal *against* reproach is frequent — Psa 119:22).

**T7.1.8** — OT↔NT: C-D is **OT-only**; its NT continuity runs through Greek `oneidismos`/`oneidizō` (reproach borne by Christ, Rom 15:3; Heb 13:13) — **outside this focus set**, labelled inferential. Psa 69's NT use is the bridge.

**T7.1.9** — Newly-coined NT term: **none** in set.

**T7.1.10** — The vocabulary arc shows reproach operating across **insult, disgrace, defiance-of-God, and (in restoration) its removal** — the cluster's most public, honour–shame-bound characteristic.

**T7.2.1** — Function: `cher.pah` typically the **predicate/object naming the state** ("we have become a reproach", Psa 44:13); `cha.raph` the **finite verb of defiance** ("he has defied the armies of the living God", 1Sa 17:36).

**T7.2.2** — Literary form: **prophecy 38, psalm 31, narrative-history 25, wisdom 8, lament 3**. The **psalmic/lament** weighting is decisive — reproach is overwhelmingly the cry of the afflicted before God.

**T7.2.3** — Logical structure: in the lament material, *because* the enemy reproaches God's name and people, God is appealed to *to act* (Psa 74:18–22) — reproach (premise) → plea for vindication (conclusion).

**T7.2.4** — Settings: **liturgical-lament** (Psa 69; 74; 79), **military-covenantal** (1Sa 17; 2Ki 19 — defiance of the living God), **restoration-prophetic** (Joe 2; Zep 3).

**T7.2.5** — Primary anchor (candidate, **authorial judgement**): **Psa 69** (esp. v.7,9,19–20) — the reproach borne *for God's sake* ("for your sake I have borne reproach… the reproaches of those who reproach you have fallen on me"). It unites the felt-disgrace (`cher.pah`), the God-relation, the bearing-for-God, and the typological reach.

**T7.2.6** — That anchor shows what no other C-D verse shows together: **reproach borne vicariously for God**, fusing the interior affective disgrace with the covenant/christological pattern.

**T7.3.1** — Field (science §4): **social psychology — ostracism and rejection research** (Leary, Baumeister, Williams).

**T7.3.2** — Where science illuminates: **Eisenberger's** finding that social rejection activates physical-pain circuitry coheres with the lexical result that borne reproach (`cher.pah`) is tagged **affect** — social disgrace registered as felt pain. Reproach/taunt as **instruments of social degradation** (combining devaluation with public humiliation) matches the C-B→C-D verdict→voicing pairing.

**T7.3.3** — Divergence: science locates reproach **purely "between persons", not as an inner state** (§4); the biblical evidence **internalises** it (affect-tagged) *and* makes God a party to it (object 18 / agent 9) — reproach of and from God, which science's interpersonal frame does not contain.

**T7.3.4** — Gap surfaced: science's honour–shame-culture findings prompt reading C-D within an **honour–shame frame** explicitly, and checking whether the cluster includes **restoration/removal-of-reproach** strategies — which the data does (Jos 5:9; Zep 3), a point worth foregrounding.

## 3. Evidence-grounded synthesis

> _Authored from the tallies above and the appendix below; see chat/obslog for the reading. Every claim ties to a count or a cited verse._

The faculty tags split this characteristic into **two poles with almost no overlap**:

1. **An inner affective condition** — `cher.pah` "reproach" (72), tagged `affect` + `status` on *every* occurrence. This is the **borne, felt disgrace** of being reproached. That a status-noun is affect-tagged throughout is significant for the programme's question: in this corpus, **borne disgrace is registered as an interior affective state**, not merely a social fact.
2. **An outward verbal act** — `cha.raph` "to taunt" (38, faculty-absent, action) plus `shim.tsah` "derision" (1). This is the **speech that inflicts** the disgrace.

The split is near-total (every `cher.pah` = affect/status; every `cha.raph` = faculty-absent/action), making C-D the **clearest "inner condition + outward expression" pairing** in the whole cluster.

**The act-side is strongly God-directed:** `cha.raph` has God as object (10) or addressee (2) in 12 of 38 — the taunting/defying of God (the Goliath / Rabshakeh / imprecatory-lament register). On the condition-side, `cher.pah` shows divine **agent** in 9 — reproach borne in relation to God.

**Seat** is almost entirely absent (103 of 111); the handful seated split heart/soul.

**Valence:** sinful (67) leads, but a large **neutral (30)** share reflects that much "reproach" is simply the *narrated condition* of disgrace, not itself a moral act.

## 4. Membership validation (per term)

- **`cher.pah` (H2781, ×72) — CONFIRMED core; the inner-condition pole.** `affect` + `status` on every occurrence — the felt, borne disgrace. The cluster's second-largest term after `sa.ne`.
- **`cha.raph` (H2778A, ×38) — CONFIRMED; the outward-act pole.** faculty-absent, action, near-uniformly sinful (35/38); markedly God-directed (object 10 / addressee 2).
- **`shim.tsah` (H8103, ×1) — CONFIRMED.** Nominal "derision"; faculty-absent, aligns with the expression pole.

**Inner/outer-layer flag (evidence-based, bears on IC3):** C-D is *not* a purely outward set. Its dominant member `cher.pah` is affect-tagged — the felt disgrace is genuinely interior. So if the faculty-absent terms are pushed into a separate "expression/boundary" layer, `cher.pah` is the counter-example that must stay on the interior side. Presented for your IC3 decision.

**Cluster:** M06 · **Characteristic:** C-E Adversarial enmity — settled relational opposition
**Evidence base:** wa-m06-char-e-enmity-v1_0-20260620.md + lexical extract + science §3 + outside-inventory (T7.3 only)
**Terms (9 occ; OT 5 / NT 4):** antidikos (4), ya.riv (3), a.yav (1), qim (1)

> Answered from evidence or marked **SILENT** with reason. NB: discovery established C-E as the **weakest interior engagement** — all faculty-absent, all unseated, mostly neutral; it names a relational *role*. Most inner-faculty questions are therefore silent at the tag level.

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**T0.1.1** — **SILENT/none** — no divine_involvement tagged on any C-E occurrence (God neither agent nor object here). *Outside-inventory note (science):* `antidikos`/`qim` carry a covenant-lawsuit register (the adversary before God's court) that the lexical does not tag — flagged inferential.

**T0.1.2** — **Not borne by God** in the tagged data: enmity here is a creaturely relational stance. (The covenant-adversary / "the satan" register sits outside this extract.)

**T0.2.1** — Where shown: as the opponent in a dispute one is urged to settle quickly (the legal-adversary sense — Matt-type setting in the NT terms). Effect at Job 22:20 ("our adversaries are cut off / consumed").

**T0.2.2** — Reads as belonging to the **fallen/relational order** — opposition between parties; mostly **neutral** valence (5), i.e. a described relational fact rather than a moral state.

**T0.2.3** — **SILENT** — no future orientation tagged.

**T0.3.1 / T0.3.2 / T0.3.3** — **SILENT** — with no God-relation and no faculty tag, no image-bearer aspect is evidenced.

**T0.4.1** — **SILENT** in the lexical; *inferential (outside-inventory):* the divine-court adversary register could carry typological weight (the accuser), but it is not tagged here.

## T1 — Definition

**T1.1.1** — Programme name: *adversarial enmity* — a settled relational opposition (standing-against). The name signals a **relation/position**, not a feeling.

**T1.1.2** — `ya.riv` "opponent/one who contends", `antidikos` "opponent/adversary", `a.yav` "be hostile", `qim` "adversary/those who rise up". Definitionally: **the party that stands against another**.

**T1.1.3** — Carries a **purely relational/directional** implication — enmity is constituted by the *against*-relation.

**T1.2.1** — A **condition/status** (status 8 — the standing of being an opponent), with one **act** form (`a.yav` "be hostile", action 1).

**T1.2.2** — **Simple** — a single relational stance; no compound interior structure evidenced.

**T1.3.1** — Structural opposite: **alliance / friendship / peace** (the covenant-friend vs adversary contrast). No opposite term in the set.

**T1.3.2** — At its edge it excludes alliance, peace, and shared cause.

**T1.3.3** — It is *not* the felt hatred of C-A (no affect) nor the dispositional cruelty of C-F (no quality of character) — it is **only the relation of opposition**.

**T1.4.1** — Mode: realised as opponent-nouns (status 8) and one verb of being-hostile. Manner: **standing against**.

**T1.4.2** — Varies by **setting**: legal (the courtroom `antidikos`, the NT terms), military/national (Exo 23:22 enemies of Israel), and personal dispute (`ya.riv`, Job).

**T1.4.3** — Partial: the legal-adversary sense operates in a **judicial/communicative** setting (a case argued); not a speech-act of the term itself.

**T1.5.1** — Immediate response (1 occ): the adversaries are "cut off / consumed" (Job 22:20). **T1.5.2** — **SILENT** — too few to assess.

**T1.6.1 / T1.6.3** — **SILENT** — no sustained inner effect tagged.

**T1.7.1 / T1.7.2 / T1.7.3** — **SILENT** — no conditions-of-reception data (the term names a relation, not an inner uptake). One **received-from-outside** origin tag (enmity arriving from another).

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**T2.1.1** — **None** — no constitutional seat tagged on any occurrence (all 9 unseated).

**T2.1.2** — Pattern: enmity is **entirely unseated** — consistent with a relational position rather than an inner-being state. This is itself the finding (its non-engagement of any seat).

**T2.10.1** — **received-from-outside** tagged once (enmity coming onto the person from an opponent); otherwise none.

**T2.7.1** — **SILENT** — no body link.

**T2.9.1** — Origin: **not stated** (8); received-from-outside (1). **T2.9.2** — **SILENT**.

## T3 — The Inner Faculties

**T3.1–T3.11 (all 33 sub-questions):** **SILENT at the tag level** — `faculty` is absent on all 9 occurrences. C-E engages no inner faculty in the tagged data; it names a relational role. *Inferential only:* the role presupposes hostility (an affective/volitional ground), but nothing is tagged. This blanket silence is the key evidential finding for C-E and bears directly on its status (see consolidation).

## T4 — Relational Interfaces

**T4.1 God→Human — all:** **SILENT** — no divine involvement tagged.

**T4.2 Human→God — all:** **SILENT** — God not an object here. *(Outside-inventory: the adversary-before-God register exists but is untagged.)*

**T4.3 Human→Giving — T4.3.1** — **Yes (by nature):** enmity is a stance *toward* another (person 3; the opponent in dispute/court/war). It operates as the **against-relation** itself. **T4.3.2/3** — **SILENT**.

**T4.4 Human→Receiving — T4.4.1** — Inferential: one *has* an adversary (the adversary is met, Exo 23:22; the legal opponent confronts). received-from-outside (1). **T4.4.2/3** — **SILENT**.

**T4.5 Boundaries — T4.5.1** — Operates **across relational distance** by definition (the adversary is the other party); the covenant frame (Exo 23:22 "I will be an enemy to your enemies") sets it within God's covenant. **T4.5.2** — Crosses covenantal lines (national enemies). **T4.5.3** — Scope: opponents in law, war, and dispute.

**T4.6 Spiritual Beings — T4.6.1** — **Inferential (flag):** `antidikos` is the term used in the NT for **the cosmic adversary** ("your adversary the devil", 1Pe 5:8) — an adversarial-being interface — but in this M06 extract the C-E occurrences tag object as person/none, not spiritual-being. Flagged for verse-level confirmation; not asserted from the tags. **T4.6.2/3** — **SILENT**.

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

**T5.1–T5.6 (all):** **SILENT** — no transformation, sequence, mechanism, suffering-relation, sanctification, or eschatology tagged (Job 22:20 shows the adversary *consumed*, an outcome, not a formation). C-E carries no developmental dimension in the data.

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics

**T6.1.1** — Co-occurring non-M06 clusters: **M44 (3), M41 (2), M26 (1), M33 (1)** — sparse. Within M06: **C-F (1)** only.

**T6.1.2** — The sparse co-occurrence reflects C-E's **specialised legal/relational register** and small corpus; it sits at the cluster's relational edge.

**T6.2.1 / T6.2.2** — **SILENT** — no sequence (corpus too small).

**T6.3.1** — **SILENT**. **T6.3.2** — Inferential: enmity may be *produced by* aversive affect (C-A) — the `sa.ne` root generates "enemy"; the relation follows the feeling. **T6.3.3** — Inferential: C-E may be the **relational outworking of C-A** (felt hatred → standing opposition). Flagged.

**T6.4.1** — Vocabulary sharing: the **enemy** field overlaps `sa.ne`-derived "enemy" (C-A) and `tsar`/adversary vocabulary across the programme. **T6.4.2** — Root-level: `sa.ne` → "enemy" links C-A and the enmity field; `mas.te.mah` (kept in C-A) is the affect-bearing bridge term. **T6.4.3** — Shows C-E is the **relational pole** of which C-A is the **affective pole** — one phenomenon (hatred → enmity) across two characteristics.

**T6.5.1** — Nearest neighbour: **C-A** (by the shared enemy-concept) and **C-F** (by hostile stance). Distinction: C-A is felt (affect), C-F is a character-quality, **C-E is only the relation** (no affect, no quality, no seat). **T6.5.2** — Boundary: where there is a *standing-against another* with no tagged inner content, it is C-E. **T6.5.3** — Distinction of **kind** — relation vs feeling (C-A) vs disposition (C-F).

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**T7.1.1** — Primary terms: `ya.riv` "opponent", `antidikos` "adversary/opponent", `a.yav` "be hostile", `qim` "adversary". Root sense: one who contends/stands against.

**T7.1.2** — Grammatical range: **noun** (the opponent — status 8) and **verb** (`a.yav` be hostile — action 1). The range shows enmity as **chiefly a named relation**, only marginally an act.

**T7.1.3** — Semantic range: legal opponent (`antidikos`), military/national enemy (Exo 23:22), personal contender (`ya.riv`, Job) — narrow, all within the *opposition* field.

**T7.1.4** — Partial: `ya.riv`/`antidikos` (the opponent as person) vs `a.yav` (to be hostile, the act). Person vs act marked; disposition-vs-condition not differentiated.

**T7.1.5** — Opposite term: **friend/ally / peace** — none inside the set.

**T7.1.6** — Person-type term: **yes — definitionally** — `ya.riv`, `antidikos`, `qim` *are* person-type terms (the opponent/adversary). C-E is almost entirely person-type vocabulary.

**T7.1.7** — Supplication/seeking term: **none**.

**T7.1.8** — OT↔NT: C-E is the **most NT-weighted** characteristic relative to its size (4 of 9 NT) — Greek `antidikos` continues the adversary concept (legal and cosmic). Continuity of the **opponent role** across Testaments.

**T7.1.9** — Newly-coined NT term: **none** (`antidikos` is classical Greek, not a coinage).

**T7.1.10** — The vocabulary arc shows enmity as a **stable relational position** spanning court, battlefield, and dispute — with little interior content.

**T7.2.1** — Function: the term functions as **subject/object naming a party** ("your adversary", Matt 5:25; "my adversary", Job 31:35) — a role in the sentence, not a predicate of inner state.

**T7.2.2** — Literary form: **gospel 3, prophecy 2, law 1, wisdom 1, psalm 1, epistle 1** — spread thin; the **gospel/legal** settings (the courtroom adversary) dominate the NT cases.

**T7.2.3** — Logical structure: in the legal setting, *settle with your adversary quickly lest judgement follow* (the NT `antidikos` material) — opposition → counsel to reconcile before judgement.

**T7.2.4** — Settings: **judicial** (the `antidikos` court), **covenantal-military** (Exo 23:22), **dispute** (Job).

**T7.2.5** — Primary anchor (candidate, **authorial judgement**): **Exo 23:22** — "I will be an enemy to your enemies and an adversary to your adversaries" — the clearest statement, placing human enmity within God's covenant defence of his people. (Job 31:35 anchors the personal/legal sense.)

**T7.2.6** — That anchor shows what others do not: enmity **framed by God's covenant alignment** — God himself taking the adversary's side against his people's adversaries.

**T7.3.1** — Field (science §3 + outside-inventory): **clinical/social psychology** for human hostility/opposition; **outside science** for the legal-covenantal adversary register (per the science extract's outside-inventory).

**T7.3.2** — Where science illuminates: hostility-as-stable-orientation (Type-A cognitive hostility) coheres with C-E's status-type, unseated, settled character — opposition as a standing posture rather than an episode.

**T7.3.3** — Divergence: science treats the adversary relation sociologically; the biblical material adds the **covenant-lawsuit / divine-court** register (God as defender; the cosmic accuser) that science does not address — the principal divergence for C-E (flagged in the science outside-inventory).

**T7.3.4** — Gap surfaced: science's reactive/proactive distinction and the legal-adversary register together prompt a **verse-level check of `antidikos`** to confirm whether any C-E case carries the cosmic-adversary (spiritual-being) sense the tags did not capture.

---

### Answer coverage (C-E)
Substantive: T1 (~12/18) · T6 (~8/13) · T7 (18/20) · T4 (partial). **Blanket SILENT across all of T3 (33 questions) and all of T5 (9)** — the defining evidential fact for C-E: it engages no inner faculty and carries no developmental dimension. This silence is the finding that puts C-E's status as a standalone *inner-being characteristic* in question (carried to consolidation).

**Defining signature (derived from aggregate evidence):** faculty typically absent; status type; a relational standing-against (opponent/adversary)

**Scope note:** Candidate set from v1_0. mas.te.mah (H4895) tested here for pull from C-A.

## 3. Evidence-grounded synthesis

> _Authored from the tallies above and the appendix below; see chat/obslog for the reading. Every claim ties to a count or a cited verse._

This is the **smallest and most relational/outer** characteristic in the cluster: 9 occurrences, **all faculty-absent, all unseated**, and predominantly **neutral** in valence (5 of 9; only 1 sinful). These terms name a **relational role or position** — the opponent (`antidikos`, `ya.riv`), one who is hostile (`a.yav`), the adversary who rises against (`qim`) — rather than an inner state or a moral act.

Because faculty is absent throughout and valence is mostly neutral, C-E engages the inner being only **by implication**: the role of "adversary" presupposes hostility, but the term itself names the standing-against, not the feeling behind it.

This is the converse of C-A: where `mas.te.mah` (kept in C-A) carried the *affect* of animosity, C-E carries the *relation* of opposition with no affect tag.

## 4. Membership validation (per term)

- **`antidikos` (G0476, ×4) — CONFIRMED member.** Role-noun "opponent/adversary"; faculty-absent, status, neutral. Weak interior engagement.
- **`ya.riv` (H3401, ×3) — CONFIRMED.** "Opponent / one who contends"; status, faculty-absent.
- **`a.yav` (H0340, ×1) — CONFIRMED.** The single action ("be hostile / be an enemy").
- **`qim` (H7009, ×1) — CONFIRMED.** "Adversary / those who rise up"; status, sinful.
- **`mas.te.mah` note:** its *enmity* sense belongs to this relational field, but its lexical faculty `affect` kept it in C-A. Candidate dual-tag C-A↔C-E (IC2).

**Characteristic-status flag (GR-PROG-007, escalates IC1/IC3):** with faculty absent on all 9, neutral valence, and no seat, C-E shows the **weakest inner-being engagement of the six**. The terms pass the relevance filter only on branch (b) — implication. The data leaves open whether C-E is a standalone *interior characteristic* or a **relational-interface layer** beneath the cluster. Presented for your decision; not decided here.

# M06 · C-F Cruelty / ruthlessness — tier-question answers (T0–T7)

**File:** wa-m06-char-f-tieranswers-v1_0-20260620.md · **Date:** 2026-06-20
**Cluster:** M06 · **Characteristic:** C-F Cruelty / ruthlessness — dispositional character quality
**Evidence base:** wa-m06-char-f-cruelty-v1_0-20260620.md + lexical extract + science §3 (T7.3 only)
**Terms (38 occ; OT 32 / NT 6):** a.rits (20), akh.za.ri (8), hubrizō (5), akh.zar (2), sho.tet (1), akh.ze.riy.yut (1), afilagathos (1)

> Answered from evidence or marked **SILENT** with reason. NB: discovery established C-F as a **dispositional quality** (quality 31), with `a.rits` affect-tagged (inner ferocity) and the `akhzar`-family faculty-absent; `hubrizō` (action) and `sho.tet` flagged as pulling elsewhere.

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**T0.1.1** — **SILENT/none** — **no divine_involvement tagged on any of the 38 occurrences.** God is neither agent nor object of cruelty anywhere in the evidence.

**T0.1.2** — **Never borne by God.** This is the sharpest T0 finding in the cluster: cruelty/ruthlessness has **zero divine instance** — unlike aversion (C-A) and loathing (C-C), where divine hatred/abhorrence of evil exists. Cruelty is exclusively creaturely and, in valence, almost entirely sinful (33 of 38).

**T0.2.1** — Where shown (immediate_response 8): cruelty issues in destruction — perishing from the land (Jos 23:13), seeking the life (Psa 86:14), making the land desolate (Isa 13:9), spitting/stoning/mistreating (Luk 18:32; Act 14:5; 1Th 2:2).

**T0.2.2** — Reads as the **fallen condition** — a corrupted character trait (sinful 33). No created-design instance.

**T0.2.3** — **SILENT** — no future-fullness orientation.

**T0.3.1** — Inferential: cruelty is a **defacing of the image** — the trait directly opposite to the divine mercy/compassion; its presence marks the image disordered. Recorded inferential. **T0.3.2** — **Exclusively creaturely** — no divine analogue (the only M06 characteristic with no divine side at all). **T0.3.3** — Inferential: the cruel person (`a.rits`/`akhzari`) displays a settled disposition contrary to God's character (Pro 12:10 "the mercy of the wicked is cruel").

**T0.4.1** — **SILENT** — no typological use tagged (the ruthless enemy-from-the-north imagery is judgement-instrument, not typology, in the tags).

## T1 — Definition

**T1.1.1** — Programme name: *cruelty / ruthlessness* — a dispositional character quality. The name signals a **settled trait of character**, not an episode or relation.

**T1.1.2** — `a.rits` "ruthless", `akh.zar`/`akh.za.ri`/`akh.ze.riy.yut` "cruel/cruelty", `hubrizō` "mistreat/insult", `sho.tet` "scourge", `afilagathos` "hating good". Definitionally: **the disposition to inflict harm unmoved by the victim's suffering**.

**T1.1.3** — Carries a **characterological** implication — it describes *what a person is* (a quality), engaging the relational direction only as the trait acts outward.

**T1.2.1** — A **quality** (quality 31 — the dominant type), with marginal **act** (`hubrizō`, action 5) and **status** (`sho.tet`/`akh.ze.riy.yut`, 2) forms.

**T1.2.2** — Mixed at the faculty level: `a.rits` "ruthless" is **affect**-tagged (an inner ferocity, 20), while the `akhzar`-family is **faculty-absent** (the trait named from outside). So: a quality with a partial affective core.

**T1.3.1** — Structural opposite: **mercy / compassion** (`rachamim`; the compassion cluster) — Pro 12:10 sets "tender mercies" against the cruelty of the wicked; `afilagathos` "hating good" inverts `philagathos` "loving good".

**T1.3.2** — At its edge it excludes mercy, tenderness, and being-moved by another's suffering.

**T1.3.3** — It is *not* a relational role (C-E) nor a felt episode (C-A): cruelty is a **standing character trait** (quality), the disposition behind hostile acts.

**T1.4.1** — Mode: realised chiefly as **adjective/quality** ("the ruthless", "a cruel man" — quality 31), with NT verb `hubrizō` (to mistreat). Manner: **a fixed disposition expressed in harm**.

**T1.4.2** — Varies by **register**: the OT "ruthless/cruel" enemy or person (a trait — Pro 12:10; Isa 13:11; Jer 6:23) vs the NT **act** of insolent mistreatment (`hubrizō` — Luk 18:32; 1Th 2:2). Trait (OT) vs act (NT).

**T1.4.3** — Partial: `hubrizō` includes **insolent speech/mistreatment** (a communicative-aggressive mode). `afilagathos` appears in a vice-list (2Ti 3:3). Otherwise none.

**T1.5.1** — Immediate response (8 occ): destruction, seeking-life, desolation, spitting/stoning/mistreatment (refs above). **T1.5.2** — **Consistent in kind** — the responses uniformly involve **infliction of harm/destruction**.

**T1.6.1** — Sustained effect: the **enduring trait itself** (a quality), and the lasting devastation it works (Jos 23:13 "until you perish"; Isa 13:9 desolation).

**T1.6.3** — The sustained effect is the **settled cruel character**; the immediate response is its episodic act (a stoning, a desolation).

**T1.7.1** — **SILENT** — no "right operation" conditions (cruelty has no righteous use; valence sinful 33 / neutral 5).

**T1.7.2** — Distortion conditions: cruelty arises where mercy is absent (Pro 12:10) and in judgement-instrument enemies (Jer 6:23; Isa 13). No adversarial-spirit tag (though `sho.tet` "scourge" names an affliction-instrument).

**T1.7.3** — **SILENT**.

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**T2.1.1** — Seat named in 5 of 38: **soul 4, flesh 1** (rest unseated).

**T2.1.2** — Pattern: cruelty is **largely unseated (34)**, consistent with a character-quality rather than a located state; the few seated cases touch **soul** (the disposition's depth) and one **flesh**. Never heart/spirit/mind.

**T2.10.1** — **SILENT/none** — no constitutional movement or external transfer tagged (origin all none).

**T2.7.1** — **SILENT** — single flesh case, no direction.

(Secondary neighbour: C-D, via `hubrizō`'s insolent-mistreatment overlap — the review flag.)

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**T7.1.1** — Primary terms: `a.rits` "ruthless" (20), `akh.za.ri`/`akh.zar`/`akh.ze.riy.yut` "cruel/cruelty" (11), `hubrizō` "mistreat" (5). Root sense: violent/ruthless disposition; merciless infliction of harm.

**T7.1.2** — Grammatical range: chiefly **adjective/quality** (the ruthless/cruel — quality 31), an abstract **noun** (`akh.ze.riy.yut` "cruelty"), and a **verb** (`hubrizō`). The dominance of the adjectival/quality form shows cruelty is named primarily as **a property of persons**.

**T7.1.3** — Semantic range: from the ruthless conqueror/enemy (Isa 13:11; Jer 6:23) through the cruel individual (Pro 12:10) to insolent mistreatment (`hubrizō`, NT) and the vice "hating good" (`afilagathos`).

**T7.1.4** — Yes — **quality/disposition** (`a.rits`, `akhzar`) vs **act** (`hubrizō`) vs **abstract condition** (`akh.ze.riy.yut` "cruelty"). Disposition / act / condition distinguished.

**T7.1.5** — Opposite term: **mercy/compassion** (`rachamim`) — Pro 12:10 explicitly contrasts; `philagathos` "loving good" inverts `afilagathos`.

**T7.1.6** — Person-type term: **yes — clearly** — `a.rits` "the ruthless one" and `akh.za.ri` "the cruel one" *are* person-type terms naming the habitual possessor of the trait. C-F is the M06 characteristic with the strongest person-type vocabulary.

**T7.1.7** — Supplication/seeking term: **none**.

**T7.1.8** — OT↔NT: the trait (`a.rits`/`akhzar`, OT) continues as the **act** (`hubrizō`, NT) and the **vice** (`afilagathos`, NT) — a shift from naming the *character* to naming the *behaviour/vice* across Testaments. 6 of 38 NT.

**T7.1.9** — Newly-coined NT term: **`afilagathos`** ("hating/without love of good", 2Ti 3:3) is a rare compound vice-term — its coinage shows cruelty conceptualised in the NT as the **privation of love-of-good**.

**T7.1.10** — The vocabulary arc shows cruelty operating from **ruthless character → cruel act → vice of hating-good** — consistently a property/behaviour opposed to mercy.

**T7.2.1** — Function: typically an **adjective qualifying a subject** ("the ruthless", "a cruel messenger", Pro 17:11) — predicating the trait of a person/nation.

**T7.2.2** — Literary form: **prophecy 17, wisdom 10, psalm 3, gospel 3, narrative-history 2, epistle 2, lament 1**. The **prophetic** (the ruthless enemy/instrument of judgement) and **wisdom** (the cruel vs the merciful) forms dominate and frame interpretation.

**T7.2.3** — Logical structure: in wisdom, *the wicked's "mercy" is itself cruel* (Pro 12:10) — a moral contrast premise; in prophecy, *because* of sin, a ruthless nation is brought as judgement (Isa 13; Jer 6).

**T7.2.4** — Settings: **wisdom-moral** (Pro 11:17; 12:10), **prophetic-judgement** (Isa 13; Jer 6; 50), **persecution-narrative** (Luk 18:32; Act 14:5; 1Th 2:2).

**T7.2.5** — Primary anchor (candidate, **authorial judgement**): **Pro 12:10** — "the mercy of the wicked is cruel" (`akhzari`) — it names cruelty as a **character trait**, sets it against mercy (its opposite), and exposes it as the wicked's defining disposition, all in one wisdom saying. (Jer 6:23 anchors the ruthless-enemy image.)

**T7.2.6** — That anchor shows what no other C-F verse shows: cruelty as the **inner character of the wicked**, contrasted directly with mercy — locating it as a disposition, not merely an act.

**T7.3.1** — Field (science §3): **clinical / social psychology** — hostility, aggression, and cruelty.

**T7.3.2** — Where science illuminates: the **trait-vs-act** distinction (dispositional hostility; reactive vs proactive aggression — Berkowitz) maps C-F's quality-dominant form with its NT act-form (`hubrizō`); **Bandura's moral disengagement** illuminates how cruelty is sustained "unmoved by suffering" — matching the discovery's reading of the trait. **Baumeister** (perpetrator/victim gap) frames the cluster's persecution narratives.

**T7.3.3** — Divergence: science treats cruelty as a **disorder/dysfunction** (dark triad, psychopathy); the biblical material frames it **morally** as the privation of mercy and (uniquely) provides **no divine instance** — cruelty is the one M06 trait with no holy analogue, a categorical theological point science does not make.

**T7.3.4** — Gap surfaced: the **reactive/proactive** distinction prompts checking whether C-F's cruelty is situationally triggered or characterologically rooted — the data leans **characterological** (quality-dominant), with the NT `hubrizō` cases the more act-like; the `hubrizō`/`sho.tet` placement flags from discovery are the verse-level items to resolve.

## 3. Evidence-grounded synthesis

> _Authored from the tallies above and the appendix below; see chat/obslog for the reading. Every claim ties to a count or a cited verse._

This characteristic is dominantly a **quality / disposition** (quality 31 of 38) — a settled *trait* of a person (ruthless, cruel), not an episodic state — and is near-uniformly **sinful** (33 of 38).

The faculty signal splits: `a.rits` "ruthless" (20) is **affect**-tagged — the cluster's main cruelty term carries an *inner ferocity* — while the `akhzar`-family "cruel / cruelty" (11) is **faculty-absent**, naming the trait from outside.

**Seat** is mostly absent; a few soul (4) and one flesh case.

Two candidate members **pull elsewhere on the evidence** rather than confirming as dispositional cruelty:
- `hubrizō` (5) is an **action** ("mistreat / insult / treat insolently"), which sits closer to the insolent-speech register of **C-D** than to a character trait.
- `sho.tet` "scourge" (1) is a **status** noun naming an *instrument of affliction* (neutral valence), fitting neither the dispositional-cruelty pole nor C-D's derision cleanly.

These two are the evidence's answer to the v1_0 `sho.tet` overlap flag: it does not fit C-F well, and `hubrizō` only partly does.

## 4. Membership validation (per term)

- **`a.rits` (H6184, ×20) — CONFIRMED core.** `affect` + `quality` — the ruthless/violent person, with inner ferocity. Anchor of the characteristic.
- **`akh.za.ri` (H0394, ×8) — CONFIRMED.** "Cruel"; quality, faculty-absent; one soul and one flesh seating.
- **`akh.zar` (H0393, ×2) — CONFIRMED.** "Cruel"; quality.
- **`akh.ze.riy.yut` (H0395, ×1) — CONFIRMED.** The noun "cruelty" (the trait abstracted).
- **`afilagathos` (G0865, ×1) — CONFIRMED.** NT vice-list trait "hating good"; affect/quality.
- **`hubrizō` (G5195, ×5) — REVIEW (pulls to C-D).** An *action* of insolent mistreatment, not a dispositional quality; closer to C-D's verbal-hostility/insolence register. Flagged for placement (IC2).
- **`sho.tet` (H7850, ×1) — REVIEW (fits neither pole; resolves the v1_0 overlap).** "Scourge" names an instrument of affliction; status/neutral. Does not fit C-F (disposition) or C-D (derision) cleanly — candidate for re-placement or exclusion. Flagged.
