# WA — M08 · Characteristic A (Self-Exaltation): Tier-Catalogue Findings

**File:** wa-m08-a-tier-answers-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Prior output reference:** wa-m08-a-self-exaltation-v1_0-20260621.md (characteristic analysis); WA-tier-catalogue-current-state-v2-20260619.md (126 questions, T0–T7).
**Source data:** wa-ve-lexical-extract-M08-20260621-b1of2/b2of2.json; 62 focus occurrences read individually.
**Method:** every question answered from A's verse evidence by reading, not field-aggregation (§A2). Findings carry citations; narration is written to stand on its own feet (essay-ready) without returning to source. SILENT is reserved for genuine evidence-absence, each with a stated cause: **[structural]** (belongs to cross-characteristic/synthesis or is silent by the characteristic's nature), **[data-silence]** (the verses are genuinely silent), **[recoverable]** (would yield to a verse read — eliminated where found). Inferential answers are labelled. Science is confined to T7.3 and attributed to the M08 science extract. Quotes ≤15 words.

> First worked catalogue; serves as the template for B, C1, C2, D, E, F.

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**T0.1.1** — Where God appears in A's verses he is its **object** or its **opponent**, never its bearer: the self lifts itself *against* him — "I will ascend… above the stars of God" (Isaiah 14:13); "exalt himself… above every god" (Daniel 11:36); a "high hand… reviles the Lord" (Numbers 15:30) — and God is the agent who abases it — "putting down one and lifting up another" (Psalm 75:7).

**T0.1.2** — Self-exaltation is **never borne by God**; it is exclusively creaturely and creaturely-sinful. The only legitimate lifting is God's own act of exalting the lowly — "the horns of the righteous shall be lifted up" (Psalm 75:10). The pattern indicates that exaltation is a divine prerogative: it is right only as God's act or gift, never as the creature's self-assertion — "the Lord alone will be exalted" (Isaiah 2:11, 17).

**T0.2.1** — Its effect in the person is consistently destructive: it leads the person to forget God (Deuteronomy 8:14), defy him (Numbers 15:30), claim deity (Ezekiel 28:2), and fall (Proverbs 16:18).

**T0.2.2** — The role belongs to the **fallen condition**. Self-exaltation is uniformly disordered and has no place in created design; its legitimate analogue (being exalted) is God's act, not the creature's self-lifting.

**T0.2.3** — None. A has no orientation toward a future fullness; its only future is to be brought low — "the lofty pride of men shall be brought low" (Isaiah 2:17).

**T0.3.1** — None as a direct instantiation. *Inferential:* A is a counterfeit grasp at the exaltedness that belongs to God and is God's to confer — the creature reaching for the height that reflects God, illegitimately (Ezekiel 28:2). [labelled inferential]

**T0.3.2** — Exclusively creaturely as sin; the legitimate counterpart (being exalted) is God's prerogative and gift, not shared with the creature as self-exaltation.

**T0.3.3** — Its presence indicates the divine image **disordered** — the creature usurping the Creator's place, "I am a god" (Ezekiel 28:2); "I will make myself like the Most High" (Isaiah 14:14). Its abasement restores right order.

**T0.4.1** — Eschatological: A is abolished at the day of the Lord, when "the Lord alone will be exalted" (Isaiah 2:11, 17). *Inferential:* Isaiah 14:13–14 has been read typologically of the adversary's self-exaltation (human pointing to a supra-human pattern of rebellion) — noted as inferential, not established from A's evidence alone.

*Coverage T0: 9 of 9 answered (2 carry an inferential element).*

## T1 — Definition

**T1.1.1** — The characteristic is *self-exaltation*: the lifting of the self above its proper place. The name signals an active, vertical, comparative motion of the heart.

**T1.1.2** — The primary terms are height-words applied to the self: rum (to be high, lift up, exalt), ga.vah (to be high/haughty), ga.ah (to rise up), the loftiness-nouns go.vah and rum (H7312), Greek hupsēlos (high), Aramaic zud (Daniel 5:20). Definitionally, A is *to make or become high*.

**T1.1.3** — The name carries an **upward** direction (above brothers, above God), a **comparative** relation (over others), and a **heart-located** constitution — "your heart be lifted up" (Deuteronomy 8:14).

**T1.2.1** — Primarily an **act** — the verb-dominated motion of lifting ("I will ascend", Isaiah 14:13) — which, when it settles, becomes the state of B (settled pride).

**T1.2.2** — Compound: it combines an inflated self-assessment, a comparison that ranks the self above others or God, and the move to enact or claim that height — visible together in "your heart is proud… 'I am a god'" (Ezekiel 28:2). [structural reasoning, grounded]

**T1.3.1** — Its structural opposite is the heart *not* lifted up — humility/lowliness of heart: "my heart is not lifted up" (Psalm 131:1); "humility comes before honor" (Proverbs 18:12).

**T1.3.2** — At its edge it excludes remembrance of and dependence on God ("you forget the Lord", Deuteronomy 8:14) and submission to ordained limits ("lifted up above his brothers… turn aside from the commandment", Deuteronomy 17:20).

**T1.3.3** — A is *not* the settled state of pride (B), the verbal display (D), or the defiant act against authority (C1) — though it issues in all three; it is specifically the *motion* of lifting. Where the height settles it becomes B; where it speaks, D; where it defies command, C1.

**T1.4.1** — A operates as the heart's own verb — "heart lifted up" (Deuteronomy 8:14), the heart raising itself — and as transitive self-exaltation, "He shall exalt himself" (Daniel 11:36). Manner: internal lifting becoming outward display (lofty eyes, haughty neck).

**T1.4.2** — Yes: the mode varies from internal heart-motion (Deuteronomy 8:14) to outward bodily expression — "how lofty are their eyes" (Proverbs 30:13); "haughty neck" (Psalm 75:5) — to verbal claim (Isaiah 14:13). Direction varies between above-others and above-God.

**T1.4.3** — Yes — it operates communicatively through boastful self-declaration: "You said in your heart, 'I will ascend'" (Isaiah 14:13); "speak with haughty neck" (Psalm 75:5); "the boastful look in his eyes" (Isaiah 10:12).

**T1.5.1** — The first inner response shown is the forgetting/abandoning of God — "your heart be lifted up, and you forget the Lord" (Deuteronomy 8:14); "their heart was lifted up; therefore they forgot me" (Hosea 13:6).

**T1.5.2** — Consistent in direction (self-exaltation → displacement of God), varied in expression (forgetting, defying, claiming deity) — Hosea 13:6; Daniel 11:36.

**T1.6.1** — Over time it establishes a settled haughtiness (the condition of B) and an orientation of self-trust and God-forgetfulness, and it sets the trajectory toward the fall — "Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall" (Proverbs 16:18).

**T1.6.3** — The immediate response is a single turning (forgetting/defying God); the sustained effect is the entrenched haughty condition and the eventual being-brought-low — the long arc from Deuteronomy 8:14 (immediate) to Daniel 5:20 ("brought down from his kingly throne").

**T1.7.1** — A takes hold under conditions of prosperity, strength, and satiety — "when he was strong, he grew proud" (2 Chronicles 26:16); "they were filled… their heart was lifted up" (Hosea 13:6). *(A never operates rightly — flagged; the question's "operate rightly" branch is [structural] inapplicable.)*

**T1.7.2** — It is resisted by deliberate remembrance and lowliness — "my heart is not lifted up… I do not occupy myself with things too great" (Psalm 131:1) — and by the fear of God — "do not become proud, but fear" (Romans 11:20). On distortion by another spirit: **SILENT [data-silence]** — A's verses state no adversarial-spirit interference.

**T1.7.3** — Where checked, the person is humbled/lowly in spirit — the one who does not lift the heart (Psalm 131:1) or who humbles himself over it: "Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart" (2 Chronicles 32:26).

*Coverage T1: 18 of 18 answered (1 partial silence within T1.7.2 [data-silence]).*

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**T2.1.1** — The dominant seat is the **heart** — "heart lifted up" (Deuteronomy 8:14; Daniel 11:12; Ezekiel 28:2; Hosea 13:6; 2 Chronicles 32:25; Proverbs 18:12) — with one soul-and-heart locus (Psalm 13:2) and one spirit locus ("his spirit was hardened", Daniel 5:20). It is expressed through the **eyes** ("lofty eyes", Proverbs 30:13; "haughty eyes", Proverbs 6:17) and the **neck** (Psalm 75:5); in the NT it engages the **mind** ("what is exalted among men", Luke 16:15).

**T2.1.2** — The pattern shows a heart-deep seat that surfaces through the eyes and neck. The body link is **expressive** (the haughty eyes/neck display the inner lifting), not the seat. Levels never made the seat: conscience and memory function as casualties (T3.3, T3.9), not as where A resides.

**T2.10.1** — Movement runs **inward → outward**: the lifted heart shows in lifted eyes and stiffened neck (soul/spirit expressing through the body) — Proverbs 30:13. No movement onto the person from an external source is stated.

**T2.7.1** — The body link runs **soul/spirit → body** (expressive): the lifted heart manifests in lofty eyes and haughty neck, and the bodily display is itself judged — "the haughty eyes you bring down" (Psalm 18:27).

**T2.9.1** — A originates **within the person** — the heart lifts itself; no verse attributes it to an external giver. It is *occasioned* by prosperity (Deuteronomy 8:14) but the lifting is the heart's own act.

**T2.9.2** — Single and consistent: within-person generation, the occasion (fullness/strength) constant; no generational or received origin appears.

*Coverage T2: 6 of 6 answered.*

## T3 — The Inner Faculties

**T3.1 Perception** — **T3.1.1** A engages perception through sight: "how lofty are their eyes" (Proverbs 30:13); "lifted your eyes to the heights" (2 Kings 19:22). **T3.1.2** It elevates and re-directs the gaze — looking down on others, looking past God. **T3.1.3** The lifted/lofty eye is A's signature perceptual engagement across the verses.

**T3.2 Cognition** — **T3.2.1** A engages cognition in its NT register (hupsēlos, cognition-tagged): "what is exalted among men is an abomination" (Luke 16:15); "Never be wise in your own sight" (Romans 12:16). **T3.2.2** It distorts self-estimation, rating the self too high — the refusal of which is "things too great… for me" (Psalm 131:1). **T3.2.3** Cognition is engaged chiefly in the NT; the OT register is heart-disposition, not deliberation.

**T3.3 Memory** — **T3.3.1** A engages memory by its **failure**: "you forget the Lord" (Deuteronomy 8:14); "their heart was lifted up; therefore they forgot me" (Hosea 13:6). **T3.3.2** It suppresses remembrance of God and his deliverances. **T3.3.3** Forgetting-God is a defining downstream of A — a strong, non-obvious engagement of the memory faculty by deletion.

**T3.4 Affect** — **T3.4.1** Direct affective engagement is minimal; A is a posture more than a felt emotion, with an implied self-satisfied elation in fullness — "filled… heart lifted up" (Hosea 13:6). [implied affect labelled inferential] **T3.4.2** Little affective effect is stated. **T3.4.3** The pattern shows A as a stance of the heart, not primarily a feeling — the affective pole of the cluster belongs to D (boasting).

**T3.5 Creativity** — **T3.5.1 / T3.5.2 / T3.5.3 — SILENT [data-silence].** No verse in A engages imagination or origination.

**T3.6 Volition** — **T3.6.1** A is willed: "He shall do as he wills… exalt himself" (Daniel 11:36); the fivefold "I will ascend… I will set my throne" (Isaiah 14:13). **T3.6.2** It sets the will on self-ascent; conversely the will can refuse it — "I do not occupy myself with things too great" (Psalm 131:1) — and humble it (2 Chronicles 32:26). **T3.6.3** A is strongly volitional: a chosen lifting, answerable by a chosen humbling.

**T3.7 Agency** — **T3.7.1** A engages agency: the lifted self acts from its height — "his heart shall be exalted, and he shall cast down tens of thousands" (Daniel 11:12); "hands that shed innocent blood" (Proverbs 6:17). **T3.7.2** It drives domineering and violent action. **T3.7.3** A characteristically issues in high-handed agency.

**T3.8 Moral Evaluation** — **T3.8.1** A engages moral evaluation both as its object and as a distorter: it is judged sin — "Haughty eyes and a proud heart… are sin" (Proverbs 21:4) — and it inverts evaluation: "vileness is exalted" (Psalm 12:8); "exalts folly" (Proverbs 14:29). **T3.8.2** It corrupts the person's moral assessment, elevating what should be debased. **T3.8.3** A is consistently evaluated as sin and consistently corrupts evaluation.

**T3.9 Conscience** — **T3.9.1 / T3.9.2 — SILENT [data-silence]:** A's verses do not show the conscience's witness operating. **T3.9.3** *Inferential:* by producing the forgetting of God (T3.3), A dulls the conscience's ground — labelled inferential, not stated.

**T3.10 Conscientiousness** — **T3.10.1** A engages conscientiousness by undermining it: "his heart may not be lifted up… that he may not turn aside from the commandment" (Deuteronomy 17:20). **T3.10.2** It erodes obedient moral follow-through. **T3.10.3** A is corrosive of conscientious obedience.

**T3.11 Relational Capacity** — **T3.11.1** A engages relational capacity by lifting the self above others: "lifted up above his brothers" (Deuteronomy 17:20); "my enemy be exalted over me" (Psalm 13:2). **T3.11.2** It corrupts relation into hierarchy and contempt. **T3.11.3** A is intrinsically relationally damaging — it cannot coexist with genuine fellowship among equals.

*Coverage T3: 27 of 33 answered; 6 SILENT (T3.5 ×3 [data-silence]; T3.9.1–2 [data-silence], T3.9.3 inferential).*

## T4 — Relational Interfaces

**T4.1 Divine — God to Human** — **T4.1.1 / T4.1.2 / T4.1.3 — SILENT [structural].** God does not extend self-exaltation to the person; A is not a divine gift. God's interface with A is **judgment, not extension** — "putting down one and lifting up another" (Psalm 75:7) — which is recorded here so the silence is not misread as God's absence.

**T4.2 Divine — Human to God** — **T4.2.1** A operates God-ward as **defiance and usurpation**, not seeking or worship: "against the God of gods" (Daniel 11:36); "raised your voice… against the Holy One" (2 Kings 19:22). **T4.2.2** It requires the opposite of the right posture — self-exaltation where submission is due. **T4.2.3** It shows a relationship of rivalry toward God.

**T4.3 Human — Giving** — **T4.3.1 / T4.3.2 / T4.3.3 — SILENT [structural].** A is not extended by one person to another as a gift; it is self-generated (T2.9).

**T4.4 Human — Receiving** — **T4.4.1 / T4.4.2 / T4.4.3 — SILENT [structural].** A is not taken up from another in the evidence; its origin is within-person.

**T4.5 Human — Boundaries** — **T4.5.1** A operates both within bonds ("above his brothers", Deuteronomy 17:20) and across distance ("exalted over me", of the enemy, Psalm 13:2). **T4.5.2** It crosses covenantal boundaries — proud kings of the nations and the proud within Israel alike. **T4.5.3** Its scope ranks the self above all others; none are exempt from its comparison.

**T4.6 Spiritual Beings** — **T4.6.1 — SILENT [data-silence]** for direct angelic/adversarial operation. **T4.6.2** *Inferential:* A is a site of the adversarial pattern read in Isaiah 14:13–14 (the "I will ascend" of self-exaltation) — labelled inferential. **T4.6.3 — SILENT [data-silence]:** no angelic mediation appears.

*Coverage T4: 9 of 18 answered; 9 SILENT (T4.1 ×3, T4.3 ×3, T4.4 ×3 — all [structural], by the characteristic's nature; T4.6 partial [data-silence]/inferential).*

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

**T5.1.1** — Both: A reorients the person (from God-dependence to self-trust/God-forgetting) and finally changes their condition (high → brought low) — Deuteronomy 8:14; Daniel 5:20.

**T5.1.2** — The downfall is presented as decisive — "with none to raise him up" (Jeremiah 50:32); "brought down from his kingly throne" (Daniel 5:20) — reversible only by self-humbling *before* the fall (2 Chronicles 32:26).

**T5.2.1** — Yes: a clear sequence — fullness/strength → heart lifted up → forgetting/defying God → settled haughtiness → being brought low (Deuteronomy 8:14; Proverbs 16:18).

**T5.3.1** — Two mechanisms: A's downfall comes by **divine abasement** ("I will bring you down", Obadiah 4; Jeremiah 49:16); its prevention by **self-humbling** ("Hezekiah humbled himself", 2 Chronicles 32:26).

**T5.3.2** — The mechanism differs by context: imposed judgment (the proud abased) versus chosen humbling (the proud self-humbled before judgment).

**T5.4.1** — A **produces** affliction (its own downfall, "to his destruction", 2 Chronicles 26:16) and arises in prosperity — the opposite of affliction.

**T5.4.2** — Suffering, or its threat, **breaks** A: under threatened wrath "Hezekiah humbled himself… so that the wrath of the Lord did not come" (2 Chronicles 32:25–26). Affliction is its corrective.

**T5.5.1** — A's role in formation is wholly cautionary: it is the danger prosperity breeds, against which vigilance and humbling are the formative response (Deuteronomy 8:14).

**T5.6.1** — A's present operation points toward its **eschatological abolition**, not a fullness — "the Lord alone will be exalted in that day" (Isaiah 2:11, 17).

*Coverage T5: 9 of 9 answered.*

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics

**T6.1.1** — A co-occurs with **B** (settled pride — "his loftiness, his pride, and his arrogance, and the haughtiness of his heart", Jeremiah 48:29), with **violence/oppression** (C2 — "haughty eyes… hands that shed innocent blood", Proverbs 6:17), and with God-forgetting.

**T6.1.2** — A sits at the **active head** of the pride family — the motion the others settle into or express.

**T6.2.1** — A precedes the fall — "Pride goes before… a fall" (Proverbs 16:18) — and precedes/becomes settled pride (B).

**T6.2.2** — The relationship is both **causal** (A causes the downfall) and **developmental** (A settles into B).

**T6.3.1** — A produces God-forgetting (Deuteronomy 8:14), downfall (Proverbs 16:18), and the settled state of B.

**T6.3.2** — A is produced by prosperity/strength/fullness — "when he was strong, he grew proud" (2 Chronicles 26:16).

**T6.3.3** — A is the active constituent of pride; B is its settled form — they are aspects of one reality.

**T6.4.1** — A shares the height-vocabulary with B: the g-b-h / g-'-h family (ga.vah, ga.on, ga.a.vah, ge.eh) and the r-w-m family (rum, ma.rom, go.vah).

**T6.4.2** — Yes — at root level: the g-'-h and r-w-m roots generate terms across both A and B.

**T6.4.3** — The sharing shows A and B to be facets of one root-reality (height/lifting), distinguished by act versus state.

**T6.5.1** — The nearest neighbour is **B** (settled pride); the distinction is act (A, the lifting) versus state (B, the height attained).

**T6.5.2** — The overlap terms (go.vah, rum H7312, ga.vo.ah) mark the seam where the lifting becomes loftiness — visible in "it towered high [A]… its heart was proud of its height [B]" (Ezekiel 31:10).

**T6.5.3** — The distinction is one of **aspect/mode within a shared root** (process vs condition), not of constitutional level.

*Coverage T6: 13 of 13 answered.*

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**T7.1.1** — Primary terms: rum (r-w-m, "be high, rise, lift up, exalt"), ga.vah (g-b-h, "be high/lofty/haughty"), ga.ah (g-'-h, "rise up"), the loftiness-nouns go.vah and rum (H7312), Greek hupsēlos ("high"), Aramaic zud. Root meaning: physical height/elevation, applied to the heart/self.

**T7.1.2** — Verbs (the act of lifting), adjectives (the high one), and nouns (height/loftiness). The verb-dominance shows A is fundamentally an **act**.

**T7.1.3** — Semantic range: literal physical height → metaphorical self-exaltation → divine majesty. A occupies the metaphorical-self pole; the literal and divine poles are filtered to other characteristics or set aside.

**T7.1.4** — Yes: verbs (rum/ga.vah = the act) versus nouns (go.vah/rum H7312 = the loftiness/condition) — the act/condition distinction is lexicalised, mapping A onto B.

**T7.1.5** — Yes — the structural opposite is carried by the "low/lowly" vocabulary: "he regards the lowly" (Psalm 138:6); "brought low… humbled" (Isaiah 2:11, 17).

**T7.1.6** — Yes — a person-type term: "the haughty / the lofty" as a substantive — "the haughty he knows from afar" (Psalm 138:6).

**T7.1.7** — None [data-silence]: there is no term for *seeking* self-exaltation from another — it is self-generated, not solicited.

**T7.1.8** — The OT height-vocabulary (rum/ga.vah) is largely matched in the NT by the hupsoō/hupsēlos family — continuity of the height image — with a NT development toward the cognitive register.

**T7.1.9** — hupsēlofroneō ("to be high-minded", 1 Timothy 6:17) is a NT compound fusing height with the mind — a coinage marking A's NT cognitive development (it also serves E).

**T7.1.10** — The full arc runs from physical height through heart-self-exaltation to NT high-mindedness — the complete range of "the self made high."

**T7.2.1** — In the anchor verse rum is the climactic verb of the king's self-quoted ambition — "I will set my throne on high" (Isaiah 14:13) — carrying the whole claim.

**T7.2.2** — A's evidence spans narrative (Daniel, Chronicles), prophecy (Isaiah, Ezekiel, Hosea, Obadiah), wisdom (Proverbs), psalm, and epistle (Romans). The prophetic taunt-oracle (Isaiah 14) and the proverb dominate; responsible reading attends to the taunt's hyperbole and the proverb's general-truth form.

**T7.2.3** — The recurrent argument is consequential: *if* the heart is lifted up, *then* God is forgotten/defied and the proud is brought low (Deuteronomy 8:14; Proverbs 16:18) — self-exaltation as premise, downfall as conclusion.

**T7.2.4** — The settings are covenantal (the king's heart and the commandment, Deuteronomy 8; 17), judicial/eschatological (the day of the Lord against the proud, Isaiah 2), and liturgical (the Psalms). The covenantal setting frames A as covenant-danger.

**T7.2.5** — The primary anchor is **Isaiah 14:13–14** — the fullest direct expression of self-exaltation reaching for God's place.

**T7.2.6** — Isaiah 14:13–14 makes A's terminus explicit — self-exaltation aims, finally, at equality with God: "I will make myself like the Most High" — the inner logic the other verses only imply.

**T7.3.1** — *(science, M08 extract)* The most useful frameworks are the evolutionary/social psychology of status and dominance (extract §3) and Tracy & Robins' two-facet pride model (extract §1); A's uniform height-vocabulary maps onto the status-elevation literature.

**T7.3.2** — *(science)* The cross-cultural physical-height↔status association (extract §3) illuminates why A's vocabulary is height-based throughout; Keltner's "power paradox" (power reduces empathy, increases self-focus) illuminates A's relational damage — the self lifted above its brothers (T3.11).

**T7.3.3** — *(science)* Science treats status-elevation as sometimes adaptive (prestige); the biblical material judges self-exaltation as categorically disordered before God — even achievement-based elevation becomes sin when it "forgets the giver" (extract T7.3.3). A genuine register divergence.

**T7.3.4** — *(science)* The vulnerable-narcissism finding — grandiosity defending against shame (extract T7.3.4) — surfaces a question A's own verses do not address: whether self-exaltation masks shame (an M07↔M08 link). Flagged for further verse investigation; not present in A's evidence.

*Coverage T7: 20 of 20 answered (T7.1.7 = answer-of-absence; T7.3 attributed to science extract).*

# WA — M08 · Characteristic A: Self-Exaltation (lifting the self up above its place)

**File:** wa-m08-a-self-exaltation-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Prior output reference:** wa-m08-prov-char-list-v1_1-20260621.md (characteristic set); obslog wa-obslog-m08-distill-chars-v1-20260621.md.
**Source data:** wa-ve-lexical-extract-M08-20260621-b1of2/b2of2.json (extract v1_0, 2026-06-21).
**Method:** every focus occurrence read individually with its full lexical field set (GR-PROG-001 / §0). Analysis and synthesis are derived from the verses, not from field-aggregation (§A2). Quotations ≤15 words; full chapter-and-verse references throughout. Status: analysis derived from the lexical; provisional pending cluster synthesis.

> This is the first worked characteristic and serves as the **template** for B–F.

---

## 1. Definition (working)

The **active, heart-seated motion of raising oneself above one's proper place** — comparatively above other people, and ultimately above God. Its master image is verticality: lifting up, exalting, ascending, soaring, towering, setting oneself on high.

## 2. Evidence base

**62 focus occurrences**, six lemmas: rum (H7311A, 32), ga.vah (H1361, 15), rum (H7312, 5), go.vah (H1363, 5), hupsēlos (G5308, 3), ga.ah (H1342, 1), zud (H2103, Aramaic, 1). *(go.vah and rum H7312 are the noun/abstract form of the lifted-up state and straddle B — multi-membership noted, not relocated.)*

### 2a. Core self-exaltation (the majority — human self-lifting)
- **Seated in the heart.** The lifting happens *in the heart*: "your heart be lifted up" (Deuteronomy 8:14); "his heart shall be exalted" (Daniel 11:12); "your heart is proud… 'I am a god'" (Ezekiel 28:2); "their heart was lifted up; therefore they forgot me" (Hosea 13:6); "before destruction a man's heart is haughty" (Proverbs 18:12). The seat field is explicit "heart" in 23 of 62; once "soul/heart" (Psalm 13:2), once "spirit" (Daniel 5:20). Where the seat is unstated the verses do not contradict it.
- **Directed above others.** "his heart… lifted up above his brothers" (Deuteronomy 17:20); "my enemy be exalted over me" (Psalm 13:2).
- **Directed above / against God — the terminal form.** "I will ascend to heaven; above the stars of God" (Isaiah 14:13); "exalt himself… above every god… against the God of gods" (Daniel 11:36); "make your heart like the heart of a god" (Ezekiel 28:2); a "high hand… reviles the Lord" (Numbers 15:30); "raised your voice… against the Holy One" (2 Kings 19:22).

### 2b. Divine-frame occurrences (God lifts up / brings low — NOT human pride)
Carried within A's lemmas but belonging to the evaluative frame (→ cluster analysis, per fork 5): "it is God who… putting down one and lifting up another" (Psalm 75:7); "the horns of the righteous shall be lifted up" (Psalm 75:10); "the great in height will be hewn down" (Isaiah 10:33, divine agent); "the Lord is high" (Psalm 138:6); "the Lord alone will be exalted" (Isaiah 2:11, 17). These are retained here and tagged, not folded into the human characteristic.

### 2c. Per-occurrence filter / cross-membership (flagged, not dropped — FA-13)
- Exodus 14:8 — "going out **defiantly**" (high hand = Israel's bold exodus; valence blank). The idiom here is neutral bold action, not self-exaltation. → occurrence-level set-aside candidate.
- 1 Kings 11:26, 11:27 — "**lifted up his hand against the king**" (Jeroboam's revolt). The idiom is political rebellion, not heart-pride. → cross-membership/​filter candidate.
- Numbers 15:30 — "**high hand**" = defiant sin against the Lord. Primary membership **C1** (presumption/defiance); cross-listed in A as the self-exalting form of defiance.
- Proverbs 14:29 — "a hasty temper **exalts folly**" (rum of folly, not the self). → filter candidate.
- Psalm 12:8 — "vileness is **exalted** among the children of man" (social elevation of evil, not a person's self-exaltation). → filter candidate.
- Job 10:16 — "were my head **lifted up**, you would hunt me" (Job; neutral metaphor of being hunted). → filter candidate.

## 3. Analysis (observation → interpretation)

**Valence.** Of 59 valenced occurrences, 45 are sinful, 7 neutral, 6 forbidden, 1 righteous. The neutral band is almost entirely the divine-frame and idiom occurrences (2b/2c); the forbidden band is prohibition ("Do not lift up your horn", Psalm 75:4–5; "be not proud", Jeremiah 13:15; "do not become proud", Romans 11:20); the single righteous occurrence is God's vindication of the righteous (Psalm 75:10), not human self-exaltation. **Interpretation:** human self-initiated lifting-up is never righteous in this corpus. Exaltation is legitimate only when God is its agent or object — a structural asymmetry that anticipates D's "boast in the Lord."

**Object / direction.** object_type splits abstract (24), person (15), God (6). Self-exaltation is intrinsically **comparative and relational** — it raises the self *above* something. Its endpoint is the displacement of God: the proud heart proceeds to forget him (Deuteronomy 8:14; Hosea 13:6), revile him (Numbers 15:30), and finally to claim deity (Ezekiel 28:2; Daniel 11:36; Isaiah 14:13).

**Cause — a recovered motif (field-silent, verse-loud).** The `cause` field is populated in only 2 of 62. Yet the verses carry a strong, repeated cause: **prosperity, strength, wealth, and height precede the lifting of the heart** — "you… are full… then your heart be lifted up" (Deuteronomy 8:14); "they had grazed… were filled… their heart was lifted up" (Hosea 13:6); "when he was strong, he grew proud" (2 Chronicles 26:16); "your heart has become proud in your wealth" (Ezekiel 28:5); "because it towered high… its heart was proud" (Ezekiel 31:10). This is a field/method silence, not an evidence silence — see §5.

**The pride→fall structure.** The corpus repeatedly pairs the lifting with a coming descent, usually by God's hand: "to bring them down" (2 Samuel 22:28); "Pride goes before… a fall" (Proverbs 16:18); "I will bring you down" (Jeremiah 49:16; Obadiah 4); "he was brought down from his kingly throne" (Daniel 5:20); "the lofty pride of men shall be brought low" (Isaiah 2:17). Self-exaltation is presented as structurally self-defeating against the God who alone exalts and abases.

**Experiencer.** "other" (32) and "other (addressed)" (9) dominate; only one "self" — and it is the villain's self-quote, "I will ascend" (Isaiah 14:13). The single believing first-person use is a **denial**: "my heart is not lifted up" (Psalm 131:1). **Interpretation:** self-exaltation is named in the other or repudiated in the self; it is almost never owned in the first person.

**NT cognitive register.** The three hupsēlos occurrences add a mental form — "what is exalted among men is an abomination" (Luke 16:15); "do not become proud, but fear" (Romans 11:20); "Do not be haughty… Never be wise in your own sight" (Romans 12:16) — all in warning mood. This bridges A to E (conceit) without collapsing into it: here the image is still height (hupsēlos = high), not inflation.

## 4. Synthesis

Self-exaltation is the heart's vertical motion: it lifts the self above its station, drawing on the fuel of success, and aims — at its limit — at the place of God. It is comparative (above brothers, over enemies) before it is absolute (above God), and its characteristic fruit is the forgetting and defying of God. It is presented as **legitimate only in reverse** — as something God does (raising the lowly, exalting the righteous) — never as a self-generated good. The corpus binds it tightly to a downward counter-motion: the high are brought low. Within M08 it is the **active counterpart to B (settled pride)**: A is the lifting; B is the height once attained.

## 5. Expected but absent — special attention

*Three silence-types are distinguished (§5 taxonomy): structural/cross-characteristic (deferred), genuine data-silence (real), recoverable (must be eliminated by reading).*

1. **Cause — RECOVERABLE field-silence, now eliminated.** `cause` is populated 2/62, but the prosperity→pride motif is plainly present in the verses (Deuteronomy 8:14; Hosea 13:6; 2 Chronicles 26:16; Ezekiel 28:5; 31:10). This is a field/method gap, **not** evidence-absence. Recorded as a finding; recommend the cluster note carry "A's eliciting cause = prosperity/strength/wealth/height (verse-read; field under-populated)."
2. **Origin — GENUINE field limitation, not data.** `origin` is populated 1/62; the extract meta states origin rules are partial/unimplemented (within-person/​generational not built). The expected datum — does self-exaltation arise *within* the person or is it received? — is not derivable here. The verses lean "within-person" (the heart lifts *itself*), but the field cannot confirm. → flag for a future origin pass (additional discovery needed).
3. **Divine relation — UNDER-CAPTURED.** `divine_involvement` is populated only 4/62, surprisingly low for the most God-relational characteristic. The God-relation is real but lives in `object_type=God` (6) and the verse argument, not the role-field. → note for cluster analysis; do not read the low count as "God largely absent."
4. **Affect — EXPECTED, LARGELY ABSENT.** Only 3 faculty tags (all cognition). One might expect self-exaltation to carry an affective signature (elation, self-satisfaction). The corpus presents it as a **posture of the heart**, not a felt emotion — consistent with the heart-seat / faculty-absent pattern across M08. Whether self-exaltation has an affective core is under-determined by this extract. → an affect/faculty pass on A's terms would help (additional discovery).
5. **A genuinely expected element that IS absent: righteous human self-exaltation.** One might expect a positive "lifting of the head" (honour/vindication). It does not occur self-initiated here; human lifting-up is righteous only when God performs it (Psalm 75:10). The asymmetry is itself a finding (§3, valence), not a gap to be filled.

## 6. Reflection (labelled — not a conclusion)

- The prosperity→pride cause and the pride→fall structure carry an obvious application caution (success, not adversity, as the spiritual danger-point), but the corpus states this descriptively; I do not press it into a rule.
- **Cross-cultural note:** verticality-as-pride (high/low, above/below) is a near-universal metaphor; what is distinctive here is the *theological vertical* — the self raised against God, with God as the sole legitimate exalter. Honour-shame readers (for whom status-elevation is socially central) will weigh the "lifted up above his brothers" material differently from individualist readers. → flag for the reader-facing phase.
- **Additional discovery that would help:** an origin pass; an affect/faculty pass on A's terms; and a test of whether the prosperity-cause motif recurs in B and C (cross-characteristic pattern).

## 7. Coverage

62 occurrences placed: core human self-exaltation (the majority), 5 divine-frame occurrences tagged for cluster analysis (Psalm 75:7, 75:10, 138:6; Isaiah 2:11, 2:17; Isaiah 10:33), and 6 per-occurrence filter/cross-membership flags (Exodus 14:8; 1 Kings 11:26, 11:27; Numbers 15:30 → C1; Proverbs 14:29; Psalm 12:8; Job 10:16). Nothing dropped; the flagged occurrences remain in the corpus pending researcher confirmation (inclusion-by-default).

# WA — M08 · Characteristic B (Settled Pride): Tier-Catalogue Findings

**File:** wa-m08-b-tier-answers-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Prior output reference:** wa-m08-b-settled-pride-v1_0-20260621.md; WA-tier-catalogue-current-state-v2-20260619.md.
**Source data:** 98 occurrences gathered; core settled-pride band read individually.
**Method:** as wa-m08-a-tier-answers-v1_0 — read-based answers, citations, classified silences ([structural]/[data-silence]/[recoverable]), inferential labels, science confined to T7.3.

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**T0.1.1** — God is B's **opponent**, never its bearer: "God opposes the proud" (James 4:6; 1 Peter 5:5); "the Lord tears down the house of the proud" (Proverbs 15:25). The one occurrence where the lemma names God is its legitimate counterpart — "the majesty of the Lord" (ge.ut, Isaiah 26:10).

**T0.1.2** — Settled pride is never borne by God; it is exclusively creaturely-sinful. But its lemma-family touches God's **majesty** (ge.ut). The pattern indicates pride is the creature's illegitimate seizure of the majesty that belongs to God alone (Isaiah 26:10).

**T0.2.1** — It leads the person to oppress the lowly (Psalm 10:2), to refuse God ("they do not return to the Lord", Hosea 7:10), and to be brought low (Isaiah 25:11).

**T0.2.2** — Fallen condition.

**T0.2.3** — None; B's only future is to be laid low (Isaiah 13:11).

**T0.3.1** — None direct. *Inferential:* a counterfeit of the divine majesty (ge.ut, Isaiah 26:10) the creature seizes. [inferential]

**T0.3.2** — Exclusively creaturely (distortion); the legitimate analogue (majesty) is God's.

**T0.3.3** — Its presence shows the image disordered — the creature bearing a majesty that is God's; its abasement ("those who walk in pride he is able to humble", Daniel 4:37) restores order.

**T0.4.1** — Eschatological: the pride of the nations is laid low at the day of judgment (Isaiah 13:11; Zechariah 10:11). No christological use [data-silence].

*Coverage T0: 9 of 9.*

## T1 — Definition

**T1.1.1** — *Settled pride*: the entrenched state of haughtiness. The name signals a condition/status, not an act.

**T1.1.2** — ga.on, ga.a.vah, ge.eh (g-'-h, "be high/proud"), huperēfanos ("showing oneself above"), and the noun-family. Definitionally, the condition of being-high.

**T1.1.3** — A condition (not motion), frequently **corporate** ("the pride of Moab"), seated across heart/soul/spirit.

**T1.2.1** — A **condition/status**, and a person-type ("the proud") — not an act.

**T1.2.2** — Compound: settled self-elevation + entrenchment + (often) corporate scope.

**T1.3.1** — Humility/lowliness — "gives grace to the humble" (James 4:6); "he saves the lowly" (Job 22:29).

**T1.3.2** — It excludes humility, dependence on God, and the fear of the Lord ("The fear of the Lord is hatred of evil. Pride and arrogance… I hate", Proverbs 8:13).

**T1.3.3** — B is not the act of lifting (A) nor the verbal boast (D); it is the settled height the others arise from or express.

**T1.4.1** — It operates as a stative condition ("his heart is proud") and a possessed attribute ("the pride of Egypt", Ezekiel 32:12).

**T1.4.2** — It varies between individual ("arrogant in heart", Proverbs 16:5) and corporate ("the pride of Assyria", Zechariah 10:11).

**T1.4.3** — It speaks: "say in pride and in arrogance of heart" (Isaiah 9:9); "with their mouths they speak arrogantly" (Psalm 17:10).

**T1.5.1** — Its immediate response is contempt and oppression of others — "In arrogance the wicked hotly pursue the poor" (Psalm 10:2) — and refusal of God (Hosea 7:10).

**T1.5.2** — Consistent: contempt of others plus distance from God.

**T1.6.1** — Over time it sustains oppression and even idolatry — "His beautiful ornament they used for pride… their abominable images" (Ezekiel 7:20) — and draws God's standing opposition.

**T1.6.3** — Immediate = the contemptuous act; sustained = the entrenched condition God opposes and abases.

**T1.7.1** — It takes hold in prosperity and ease — Sodom's "excess of food, and prosperous ease" (Ezekiel 16:49); wealth (Ezekiel 28:5). It never operates rightly [structural — the "rightly" branch is inapplicable].

**T1.7.2** — Resisted by humility and the fear of the Lord (Proverbs 8:13). On another spirit: *inferential* — "he is king over all the sons of pride" (Job 41:34) sets Leviathan over the proud; otherwise [data-silence].

**T1.7.3** — Where checked, the person is "lowly in spirit" (Proverbs 16:19) and humbled (Daniel 4:37).

*Coverage T1: 18 of 18 (T1.7.2 part inferential/data).*

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**T2.1.1** — Seated across the **whole inner being**: heart ("arrogant in heart", Proverbs 16:5; "haughtiness of his heart", Jeremiah 48:29; thoughts of the heart, Luke 1:51), soul ("the pride of Jacob", Amos 6:8; "the yearning of your soul", Ezekiel 24:21), and spirit ("the proud in spirit", Ecclesiastes 7:8).

**T2.1.2** — The pattern shows a **pervasive** orientation — heart, soul, and spirit all engaged — not a localised faculty. Body links are minimal and expressive (the haughty look, Psalm 101:5).

**T2.10.1** — No movement from an external source; settled within the person, and within a people as a standing corporate condition. [no movement: structural]

**T2.7.1** — Body link minimal — the "haughty look" (Psalm 101:5; Isaiah 5:15) is expressive, soul→body; otherwise none.

**T2.9.1** — Within the person, and corporately within a people; occasioned by prosperity (Ezekiel 16:49).

**T2.9.2** — Single (within-person), with a corporate variant (within-a-people).

*Coverage T2: 6 of 6.*

## T3 — The Inner Faculties

**T3.1 Perception** — **T3.1.1** Engages sight: "a haughty look and an arrogant heart" (Psalm 101:5); "the eyes of the haughty are brought low" (Isaiah 5:15). **T3.1.2** It fixes the gaze in disdain. **T3.1.3** The haughty look is B's perceptual signature.

**T3.2 Cognition** — **T3.2.1** Located in the thoughts: "scattered the proud in the thoughts of their hearts" (Luke 1:51). **T3.2.2** It frames the mind's self-assessment too high. **T3.2.3** B inhabits the thinking of the heart, not only its feeling.

**T3.3 Memory** — **T3.3.1** Engaged by failure — "yet they do not return to the Lord… nor seek him" (Hosea 7:10). **T3.3.2** It suppresses returning-to-God. **T3.3.3** God-forgetfulness recurs as B's memory-effect, as in A.

**T3.4 Affect** — **T3.4.1** A disposition rather than a felt affect; faculty largely absent. **T3.4.2** Little stated affective effect. **T3.4.3** B is a settled orientation, not an emotion (the affective pole is D).

**T3.5 Creativity** — **SILENT [data-silence]** (T3.5.1–3).

**T3.6 Volition** — **T3.6.1** Willed conduct: "the one who acts in pride" (Psalm 31:23); "those who walk in pride" (Daniel 4:37). **T3.6.2** It directs the will toward self-assertion. **T3.6.3** B is a chosen way of walking, answerable by humbling.

**T3.7 Agency** — **T3.7.1** Strongly engaged: "hotly pursue the poor" (Psalm 10:2); "The arrogant have hidden a trap" (Psalm 140:5); "violence covers them" (Psalm 73:6). **T3.7.2** It drives oppression and violence. **T3.7.3** B characteristically acts against the lowly.

**T3.8 Moral Evaluation** — **T3.8.1** B is judged — "Everyone who is arrogant in heart is an abomination to the Lord" (Proverbs 16:5). **T3.8.2** It corrupts the person's evaluation (esteeming the self too high). **T3.8.3** B is consistently evaluated as abomination.

**T3.9 Conscience** — **SILENT [data-silence]** (T3.9.1–2); *inferential* dulling via refusal to return to God (T3.9.3).

**T3.10 Conscientiousness** — **T3.10.1** Undermines obedience — "they do not return to the Lord" (Hosea 7:10). **T3.10.2** It erodes obedient follow-through. **T3.10.3** B is corrosive of obedience.

**T3.11 Relational Capacity** — **T3.11.1** B is relationally expressed as contempt — "the contempt of the proud" (Psalm 123:4); oppression of the poor (Psalm 10:2). **T3.11.2** It converts relation into domination and scorn. **T3.11.3** B is the disposition from which insolence toward others (C2) proceeds.

*Coverage T3: 27 of 33; 6 SILENT (T3.5 ×3, T3.9.1–2 + inferential).*

## T4 — Relational Interfaces

**T4.1 Divine — God to Human** — **SILENT [structural]** (T4.1.1–3): God does not extend pride; his interface is opposition — "God opposes the proud" (James 4:6).

**T4.2 Divine — Human to God** — **T4.2.1** B operates God-ward as refusal to return/seek — "they do not return to the Lord their God, nor seek him" (Hosea 7:10). **T4.2.2** It requires the posture God opposes (self-elevation where dependence is due). **T4.2.3** It shows a relationship of estrangement and resistance.

**T4.3 Human — Giving** — **SILENT [structural]** (T4.3.1–3): pride is not extended to another as a gift.

**T4.4 Human — Receiving** — **SILENT [structural]** for person-to-person uptake. *Qualification:* B has a **corporate** mode — a people bears pride together ("the pride of Moab", Isaiah 16:6) — which is shared-condition, not interpersonal transfer (inferential).

**T4.5 Human — Boundaries** — **T4.5.1** B operates across distance (the proud over the poor and lowly) and corporately (whole peoples). **T4.5.2** It crosses covenantal boundaries — the nations' pride and Israel's pride alike. **T4.5.3** Its scope ranks the self/people above others; the lowly fall outside its regard.

**T4.6 Spiritual Beings** — **T4.6.1 — SILENT [data-silence]** for direct operation. **T4.6.2** *Inferential:* "king over all the sons of pride" (Job 41:34) sets Leviathan at the head of the proud — an adversarial headship over B. **T4.6.3 — SILENT [data-silence].**

*Coverage T4: 9 of 18; 9 SILENT (T4.1 ×3, T4.3 ×3 structural; T4.4 ×3 structural w/ corporate qualification; T4.6 partial).*

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

**T5.1.1** — Both: B reorients (estrangement from God) and ends in abasement (condition change) — Hosea 7:10; Isaiah 25:11.

**T5.1.2** — Abasement is decisive ("laid low", Isaiah 25:11) but reversible by humbling — Nebuchadnezzar restored after "those who walk in pride he is able to humble" (Daniel 4:37).

**T5.2.1** — Sequence: prosperity/ease → settled pride → oppression and God-distance → abasement (Ezekiel 16:49–50).

**T5.3.1** — Abasement by divine judgment ("the Lord tears down the house of the proud", Proverbs 15:25); prevention/restoration by humbling (Daniel 4:37).

**T5.3.2** — Imposed judgment versus chosen humbling.

**T5.4.1** — B produces affliction (its abasement) and arises in ease, not affliction (Ezekiel 16:49).

**T5.4.2** — Humbling/affliction breaks B — Nebuchadnezzar (Daniel 4:37).

**T5.5.1** — Cautionary: the settled disposition humility must displace across formation.

**T5.6.1** — Eschatological abolition — "the pride of Assyria shall be laid low" (Zechariah 10:11); "the pomp of the arrogant" ended (Isaiah 13:11).

*Coverage T5: 9 of 9.*

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics

**T7.2.5** — Anchor: **James 4:6** (with Proverbs 16:18) — the fullest statement of B's nature and fate.

# WA — M08 · Characteristic B: Settled Pride (the entrenched state of haughtiness / loftiness)

**File:** wa-m08-b-settled-pride-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Prior output reference:** wa-m08-a-self-exaltation-v1_0-20260621.md (template); wa-m08-prov-char-list-v1_1-20260621.md.
**Source data:** wa-ve-lexical-extract-M08-20260621-b1of2/b2of2.json (extract v1_0, 2026-06-21).
**Method:** every focus occurrence read individually with its full field set (GR-PROG-001). Analysis derived from the verses, not field-aggregation (§A2). Quotes ≤15 words; full references throughout.

---

## 1. Definition (working)

Pride as a **settled, entrenched condition** — the height once attained and now borne as a standing disposition. Where A is the act of lifting, B is the state of being high. Distinctively, B is borne not only by individuals but by **whole peoples**.

## 2. Evidence base

**98 occurrences gathered**, of which the core settled-pride band is the majority; the remainder are literal-height (set-aside candidates) and one divine-majesty occurrence. Lemmas: ga.on (H1347, 28), ga.a.vah (H1346, 12), ge.eh (H1343, 9), ga.vo.ah (H1364, 9), huperēfanos (G5244, 5), ge.vah (H1466, 3), gav.hut (H1365, 2), ge (H1341, 1), ge.ah (H1344, 1), sha.chats (H7830, 1), ra.hav (H7295, 1), ge.vah (H1467, Aram., 1), huperēfania (G5243, 1), ge.ut (H1348, 4), and the height-nouns ma.rom (H4791, 13) and qo.mah (H6967, 7).

### 2a. Core: pride as a standing state
- **Corporate / national.** ga.on is overwhelmingly "the pride of [a people/power]" — "the pride of Jacob" (Amos 6:8; 8:7), "the pride of Israel" (Hosea 5:5; 7:10), "the pride of Moab" (Isaiah 16:6), "the pride of Egypt" (Ezekiel 32:12), "the pride of Assyria… laid low" (Zechariah 10:11), "the pride of Philistia" (Zechariah 9:6). It is repeatedly the object of judgment: "I will break the pride of your power" (Leviticus 26:19).
- **The proud as a type/class.** "everyone who is proud" (Job 40:11–12); "the contempt of the proud" (Psalm 123:4); "the Lord tears down the house of the proud" (Proverbs 15:25).
- **Heart/soul/spirit-seated.** "Everyone who is arrogant in heart is an abomination" (Proverbs 16:5); "a haughty look and an arrogant heart" (Psalm 101:5); "the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit" (Ecclesiastes 7:8); "the pride of Jacob" with soul (Amos 6:8). The whole inner being is described as proud.
- **The NT frame.** "God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble" (James 4:6; 1 Peter 5:5); "scattered the proud in the thoughts of their hearts" (Luke 1:51, seated mind+heart).

### 2b. Divine-frame occurrence (→ cluster analysis)
ge.ut at Isaiah 26:10 — "the **majesty** of the Lord" (righteous; divine object). God's majesty, the legitimate pole; tagged, not folded into the human characteristic.

### 2c. Per-occurrence filter — literal height (set-aside candidates, not dropped)
ma.rom and qo.mah are predominantly literal: "the **heights** of the mountains… tallest cedars" (2 Kings 19:23; Isaiah 37:24); "the height of his **stature**" (1 Samuel 16:7); "it towered **aloft**" (Ezekiel 19:11). A minority are the proud's metaphorical loftiness: "set his nest **on high**" (Habakkuk 2:9); "your **lofty** dwelling" (Obadiah 3); "**loftily** they threaten oppression" (Psalm 73:8). The split is per-occurrence; literal occurrences are flagged for occurrence-level set-aside.

## 3. Analysis (observation → interpretation)

**B is the state, A is the act.** The same heart-imagery recurs, but as a condition predicated of a person or people rather than a motion. "Pride is their necklace; violence covers them as a garment" (Psalm 73:6) — pride worn as settled adornment.

**The corporate dimension is distinctive.** Through ga.on, B is characteristically a property of nations. This sets B apart from the more individual A: pride here is a collective, structural disposition that whole peoples bear and that God judges as peoples.

**B is the root-disposition behind contempt and oppression.** ga.a.vah and ge.eh repeatedly show settled pride issuing in action against the lowly: "In arrogance the wicked hotly pursue the poor" (Psalm 10:2); "The arrogant have hidden a trap for me" (Psalm 140:5); "speak insolently against the righteous in pride and contempt" (Psalm 31:18). **Interpretation:** B feeds C2 (insolence toward others) — the settled state is the soil from which contemptuous action grows. (Multi-membership of ga.a.vah noted, not relocated.)

**B is the precise object of God's standing opposition.** The corpus's most concentrated statements that God abases the proud and exalts the lowly cluster here: "God opposes the proud" (James 4:6; 1 Peter 5:5); "those who walk in pride he is able to humble" (Daniel 4:37); "the Lord… will lay low his pompous pride" (Isaiah 25:11); "his pride will bring him low" (Proverbs 29:23). Pride is not merely disapproved — it is the disposition God has set himself against.

**The humility counter-pole is named.** Unlike A, B repeatedly defines itself against its opposite: "gives grace to the **humble**" (James 4:6); "he saves the **lowly**" (Job 22:29); "better to be of a **lowly** spirit" (Proverbs 16:19); "**humility** comes before honor" (Proverbs 18:12). The pride↔humility axis is structural here and links M08 to M09 (Humility).

## 4. Synthesis

Settled pride is the entrenched height — pride as a standing condition of the heart, soul, and spirit, and characteristically of whole peoples. It is the soil from which contempt and oppression of the lowly grow (feeding C2), and it is the disposition against which God's action is most explicitly directed: the corpus's clearest "God opposes the proud / exalts the humble" statements gather here. Where A is aroused (by prosperity) and momentary, B is a given, durable state — and it is consistently set over against humility, making the pride↔humility axis the cluster's organising contrast.

## 5. Expected but absent — special attention

1. **Cause — genuinely sparse here, and that is itself a finding (not a method gap).** Where A had a recoverable prosperity-cause, B's national-pride occurrences mostly assert the state *without* an eliciting cause — pride is treated as a standing fact of a people (Hosea 5:5; Zechariah 9:6; Isaiah 16:6). A few echo prosperity (Ezekiel 16:49, Sodom's "excess of food, prosperous ease"; Ezekiel 28, wealth). **This A(aroused)↔B(settled) cause-asymmetry is a real distinction to carry to the synthesis**, not a silence to eliminate.
2. **Faculty — absent (0 tagged).** Same disposition-not-faculty pattern, but B is located across heart/soul/spirit, suggesting a pervasive whole-inner-being orientation rather than a localised faculty. The felt/affective texture of settled pride is not captured. → an affect pass would help.
3. **`how` captures judgment, not mechanism.** The populated `how` values are overwhelmingly God's response (break, cut off, lay low, oppose), not how pride operates internally. **Interpretation:** the corpus's interest in settled pride is in its *judgment*, not its inner mechanism. Where mechanism appears it is outward — "His beautiful ornament they used for pride… abominable images" (Ezekiel 7:20): pride feeding idolatry.
4. **ga.on: attitude vs pomp (recoverable per-occurrence reading).** A minority of ga.on occurrences denote the external pomp/glory prided in, not the inner attitude — "the splendor and **pomp** of the Chaldeans" (Isaiah 13:19); "the **pride** of your power" = the sanctuary (Ezekiel 24:21, neutral). Most are the inner attitude. → resolved per occurrence in any reader-facing pass.
5. **Humility counter-pole present (expected, and confirmed).** The opposite of B is named far more than for A; this is the cluster's organising axis and a Session-D link to M09.

## 6. Reflection (labelled — not a conclusion)

- The corporate/national dimension resonates with collective identity, institutional and national pride; I hold this descriptively rather than pressing application.
- **Cross-cultural:** "the pride of [nation]" speaks directly to honour and collective-identity cultures; the God-opposes-the-proud frame reframes status as theologically precarious. → flag for reader-facing.
- **Cross-cluster:** the pride↔humility axis is a clear M08↔M09 (Humility) link — a Session-D candidate.
- **Additional discovery:** per-occurrence resolution of ga.on attitude-vs-pomp; confirmation of the A-aroused / B-settled cause distinction across the corpus; an affect pass.

## 7. Coverage

98 occurrences placed: core settled-pride (the majority of ga.on, ga.a.vah, ge.eh, ga.vo.ah, huperēfanos, the noun family, sinful ge.ut, and the metaphorical-loftiness ma.rom/qo.mah occurrences); 1 divine-frame occurrence tagged to cluster analysis (Isaiah 26:10); and the literal-height ma.rom/qo.mah/ga.vo.ah occurrences flagged for occurrence-level set-aside (e.g. 1 Samuel 16:7; 2 Kings 19:23; Isaiah 37:24; Ezekiel 19:11; 31:14). Straddlers noted, not relocated: ga.a.vah (B↔C2, oppression); ga.vo.ah / ma.rom / qo.mah (B↔A, loftiness vs lifting). Nothing dropped; flagged occurrences remain pending researcher confirmation (inclusion-by-default).

# WA — M08 · Characteristic C1 (Presumption / Defiance toward God and Authority): Tier-Catalogue Findings

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**T0.1.1** — God is the one **defied**: "she has proudly defied the Lord, the Holy One" (Jeremiah 50:29); the presumptuous "did not obey your commandments" (Nehemiah 9:16). God is the object whose authority is refused; he never bears it.

**T0.1.2** — Never borne by God; exclusively creaturely. The pattern shows C1 as the creature's refusal of the boundary God's word sets — a disposition with no divine analogue.

**T0.2.1** — It leads the person to disobey, to "stiffen the neck" (Nehemiah 9:16), and to incur death ("that man shall die", Deuteronomy 17:12).

**T0.2.2** — Fallen condition.

**T0.2.3** — None; its end is judgment.

**T0.3.1** — None.

**T0.3.2** — Exclusively creaturely.

**T0.3.3** — Its presence shows the image in rebellion — the will set against its Maker's order.

**T0.4.1** — *Inferential:* the "despise authority… blaspheme the glorious ones" of 2 Peter 2:10 carries an eschatological-judgment frame; otherwise [data-silence].

*Coverage T0: 8 answered, 1 inferential (T0.4.1); 0 hard silent.*

## T1 — Definition

**T1.1.1** — *Presumption/defiance*: overreach against God's command and his appointed authority. The name signals a willed refusal of ordained limit.

**T1.1.2** — zid ("to boil over → act presumptuously"), za.don ("presumption, insolence"), authadēs ("self-willed"), tolmētēs ("bold/daring"). Definitionally, to push beyond one's authorisation.

**T1.1.3** — A directional defiance — **against** command and authority; a disposition of the self-willed will.

**T1.2.1** — An **act** issuing from a disposition (the self-willed heart) — "acts presumptuously" (Deuteronomy 17:12).

**T1.2.2** — Compound: elevated self-regard (from B) + a will that refuses ordained limit (the defiant act).

**T1.3.1** — Its opposite is submission/obedience and the fear of God — "all the people shall hear and fear and not act presumptuously again" (Deuteronomy 17:13).

**T1.3.2** — It excludes obedience, the fear of the Lord, and the trembling due before God ("they do not tremble as they blaspheme", 2 Peter 2:10).

**T1.3.3** — C1 is not the mere height of pride (B) nor the insolence toward people (C2); it is the will's refusal of God's command and mediators.

**T1.4.1** — It operates as defiant action — "presumptuously went up" (Deuteronomy 1:43); "presumes to speak a word… I have not commanded" (Deuteronomy 18:20).

**T1.4.2** — It varies: against the cult (priest), against the court (judge), against the prophetic word, and directly against the Lord (Jeremiah 50:29).

**T1.4.3** — Yes — communicative defiance: the prophet who "presumes to speak" (Deuteronomy 18:20); "they blaspheme" (2 Peter 2:10).

**T1.5.1** — Its immediate response is disobedience — "stiffened their neck and did not obey" (Nehemiah 9:16).

**T1.5.2** — Consistent: refusal of the ordained word.

**T1.6.1** — It establishes a hardened, self-willed posture and incurs judgment (Deuteronomy 17:12).

**T1.6.3** — Immediate = the act of disobedience; sustained = the hardened defiance and its sentence.

**T1.7.1** — It takes hold where the heart is already proud/self-willed (1 Samuel 17:28, "the evil of your heart"); never operates rightly [structural].

**T1.7.2** — Resisted by the fear of God (Deuteronomy 17:13). On another spirit — [data-silence], though 2 Peter 2:10's "blaspheme the glorious ones" sets C1 against angelic beings (see T4.6).

**T1.7.3** — Where checked, the person fears and does not presume again (Deuteronomy 17:13).

*Coverage T1: 18 of 18.*

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**T2.1.1** — Seated in the **will/heart**: "your presumption and the evil of your heart" (1 Samuel 17:28); the flesh in the NT — "Bold and willful… in the flesh" (2 Peter 2:10). The faculty is volition (authadēs).

**T2.1.2** — The pattern shows C1 as a disposition of the **will**, surfacing as the stiffened neck — the body figuring the refusal.

**T2.10.1** — No external-source movement stated; generated within the self-willed heart. [no movement]

**T2.7.1** — Body link via the "stiffened neck" (Nehemiah 9:16) — expressive of the inner refusal; soul→body.

**T2.9.1** — Within the person — the self-willed heart (1 Samuel 17:28).

**T2.9.2** — Single (within-person).

*Coverage T2: 6 of 6.*

## T3 — The Inner Faculties

**T3.1 Perception** — **SILENT [data-silence]** (T3.1.1–3): C1's verses do not engage the inner senses.

**T3.2 Cognition** — **T3.2.1** Minimal; the presumptuous "presumes to speak" claims a knowing it lacks (Deuteronomy 18:20). **T3.2.2/3** Largely not a cognitive characteristic — **partly SILENT [data-silence]**.

**T3.3 Memory** — **SILENT [data-silence]**; *inferential:* the presumptuous "did not remember" the commandments they refused (Nehemiah 9:16).

**T3.4 Affect** — **SILENT [data-silence]**: C1 is a posture of will, not affect.

**T3.5 Creativity** — **SILENT [data-silence]**.

**T3.6 Volition** — **T3.6.1** Centrally engaged — "self-willed" (authadēs, Titus 1:7; 2 Peter 2:10); "do as he wills". **T3.6.2** It sets the will against ordained limit. **T3.6.3** C1 is the volitional core of the cluster — pride become refusal.

**T3.7 Agency** — **T3.7.1** Engaged: defiant action ("presumptuously went up", Deuteronomy 1:43; "willfully attacks", Exodus 21:14). **T3.7.2** It produces transgressive acts. **T3.7.3** C1 issues in high-handed deeds.

**T3.8 Moral Evaluation** — **T3.8.1** Judged severely — capital in the Law (Deuteronomy 17:12). **T3.8.2** It overrides moral restraint. **T3.8.3** C1 is consistently judged as grave sin.

**T3.9 Conscience** — **T3.9.1** Engaged by its **silencing**: "they do not tremble as they blaspheme" (2 Peter 2:10) — the conscience-witness suppressed. **T3.9.2** It deadens the trembling due before God. **T3.9.3** C1 marks a conscience overridden.

**T3.10 Conscientiousness** — **T3.10.1** Directly opposed: "did not obey your commandments" (Nehemiah 9:16). **T3.10.2** It is the failure of conscientious obedience. **T3.10.3** C1 is obedience refused.

**T3.11 Relational Capacity** — **T3.11.1** Engaged toward authority — it refuses the priest, judge, prophet, and "despises authority" (2 Peter 2:10). **T3.11.2** It severs the relation of submission. **T3.11.3** C1 ruptures the bond between the person and ordained authority.

*Coverage T3: ~21 answered; ~12 SILENT (T3.1 ×3, T3.3 ×3, T3.4 ×3, T3.5 ×3 — data-silence; T3.2 partial). C1 is a narrow, will-centred characteristic — most faculties are genuinely not engaged.*

## T4 — Relational Interfaces

**T4.1 Divine — God to Human** — **SILENT [structural]**: God does not extend presumption.

**T4.3 Human — Giving** — **SILENT [structural]**: not extended to another as a gift.

**T4.4 Human — Receiving** — **SILENT [structural]**.

**T4.5 Human — Boundaries** — **T4.5.1** It operates against **appointed authority** within the covenant (priest, judge, prophet — Deuteronomy 17:12) and against God directly. **T4.5.2** Within and across the covenant (Israel's presumption; the nations' defiance, Jeremiah 50:29). **T4.5.3** Its scope is the ordained order it refuses.

**T4.6 Spiritual Beings** — **T4.6.1** Engaged: "Bold and willful… they blaspheme the glorious ones" (2 Peter 2:10) — presumption reaches even toward angelic beings. **T4.6.2** *Inferential:* a site of adversarial pattern (defiance of the divine order). **T4.6.3 — SILENT [data-silence].**

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics

**T6.1.1** — Co-occurs with B (settled pride — Jeremiah 49:16, "the pride of your heart"), with A (self-exaltation issuing in defiance — Daniel 5:20), and with blasphemy (2 Peter 2:10).

**T6.1.2** — C1 is the volitional edge of the pride family — where height becomes refusal.

**T6.2.2** — Causal (pride → presumption → judgment) and developmental.

**T6.3.1** — Produces disobedience and judgment.

**T6.3.2** — Produced by A/B (self-exaltation and settled pride).

**T6.4.1** — Shares the **z-d root** (zid, za.don) with C2.

# WA — M08 · Characteristic C1: Presumption / Defiance toward God and Appointed Authority

**File:** wa-m08-c1-presumption-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Prior output reference:** wa-m08-a-self-exaltation-v1_0-20260621.md (template); wa-m08-b-settled-pride-v1_0-20260621.md.
**Source data:** wa-ve-lexical-extract-M08-20260621-b1of2/b2of2.json (extract v1_0, 2026-06-21).
**Method:** every focus occurrence read individually; per-occurrence direction split applied to the shared z-d root (C1 toward God/authority; C2 toward others). Analysis derived from verses (§A2). Quotes ≤15 words.

---

## 1. Definition (working)

Pride enacted as **overreach against God's command and his appointed authority** — presuming to act, speak, or go where one was not authorised; the will set defiantly against the ordained order. C1 and C2 share the z-d root (zid, za.don) but point in different directions; membership is assigned per occurrence.

## 2. Evidence base

**~15 occurrences** (per-occurrence assignment from the shared root): zid (H2102 — Deuteronomy 17:13; 18:20; 1:43; Nehemiah 9:16; 9:29; Jeremiah 50:29), za.don (H2087 — Deuteronomy 17:12; 18:22; 1 Samuel 17:28), tolmētēs (G5113 — 2 Peter 2:10), authadēs (G0829 — 2 Peter 2:10; Titus 1:7), zed (H2086 — Psalm 19:13; Jeremiah 43:2), and zud (H2103, Aramaic — Daniel 5:20, cross-listed from A).

## 3. Analysis (observation → interpretation)

**The core sense is presumptuous overreach against ordained authority.** The Deuteronomy texts are legal/cultic: "the man who acts presumptuously by not obeying the priest… or the judge… shall die" (Deuteronomy 17:12); "the prophet who presumes to speak a word in my name that I have not commanded" (Deuteronomy 18:20); "you rebelled against the command of the Lord and presumptuously went up" (Deuteronomy 1:43). Presumption is treated as a **capital matter** — it strikes at the ordained order itself.

**It is defiance of God, climaxing in open challenge.** "they acted presumptuously and did not obey your commandments… stiffened their neck" (Nehemiah 9:16, 29); "she has proudly defied the Lord, the Holy One" (Jeremiah 50:29); in the Aramaic, "his heart was lifted up… he dealt proudly" (Daniel 5:20).

**The NT register is self-will against authority.** "Bold and willful… they despise authority… blaspheme" (2 Peter 2:10, tolmētēs + authadēs); and the disqualifying trait for an overseer: "He must not be arrogant [self-willed]" (Titus 1:7). The one meaningful faculty tag here is **volition** (authadēs) — C1 is the will set on its own course against the ordained.

**Interpretation.** C1 is the *vertical defiance* facet of pride: where A lifts the self and B settles into height, C1 turns that height into active refusal of God's command and his appointed mediators (priest, judge, prophet). Its inner root is named as a hardened will — "stiffened their neck," "the evil of your heart" (1 Samuel 17:28) — and its outward form is disobedience that the texts judge as deserving death.

## 4. Synthesis

Presumption is pride become defiance: the proud self refusing the boundary God's word and God's appointed authorities set. It is consistently grave — a capital offence in the Law, "proud defiance" of the Lord in the prophets, self-willed contempt of authority in the apostolic writings. Its faculty is the will; its posture is the stiffened neck. C1 is the point at which M08 touches rebellion: pride is no longer merely a height but a refusal.

## 5. Expected but absent — special attention

1. **Inner state under-described; behaviour foregrounded.** C1 is presented mostly through *acts* ("acted presumptuously," "did not obey," "went up") rather than an inner condition. The inner root surfaces only twice — "the evil of your heart" (1 Samuel 17:28) and the volition tag on authadēs. **Interpretation:** the inner dimension of C1 is real but thin in the lexical; it is largely carried by the settled pride of B and expressed as the defiant act. This is a genuine characteristic-shape, not a method gap.
2. **Faculty noise — flag.** zid carries a mechanical `faculty=perception` tag on all nine occurrences; given zid's lemma ("to boil over → act presumptuously"), this perception tag looks like a disambiguation artefact, not a meaningful faculty (FA-14). The meaningful faculty here is volition (authadēs). → recommend CC review of the zid faculty tag.
3. **Cause mostly silent.** Where present, the cause is the self-exaltation that precedes the defiance ("Babylon proudly defying," Jeremiah 50:29; "Babylon's self-exaltation against God," Jeremiah 50:31). C1's cause is largely internal (the proud will) rather than an external elicitor — consistent with B's settled-state character.
4. **Seat rarely named** (flesh, 2 Peter 2:10; heart, 1 Samuel 17:28). Expected heart-seat is implied but seldom stated; do not over-read its absence.

## 6. Reflection (labelled — not a conclusion)

- C1 speaks to authority, obedience, and the limits of the self before God; its legal gravity in Deuteronomy will read very differently across traditions with different views of mediated authority. → flag for reader-facing.
- The "stiffened neck" image links C1 to the broader biblical rebellion vocabulary — a possible Session-D cross-reference beyond M08.

## 7. Coverage

~15 occurrences placed by per-occurrence direction. Shared-root straddle made explicit: zid and za.don each contribute occurrences to C1 *and* C2 (and several za.don/zed occurrences are settled-pride "the proud one" uses that lean B — noted, not relocated). Aramaic zud (Daniel 5:20) cross-listed from A. Nothing dropped.

# WA — M08 · Characteristic C2 (Insolence / Contempt toward Other People): Tier-Catalogue Findings

**File:** wa-m08-c2-tier-answers-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Prior output reference:** wa-m08-c2-insolence-v1_0-20260621.md; WA-tier-catalogue-current-state-v2-20260619.md.
**Source data:** ~13 core occurrences (+ cross-listed oppression from B) read individually.
**Method:** as the A template. **Standing note:** C2 is the faculty-absent *outward* pole of pride; much of its inner-being content is carried by B (the settled disposition behind the act) and by the *sufferer's* interior — recorded transparently where the silences fall.

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**T0.1.1** — God appears as the one whose **law the insolent disregard** — "who wander from your commandments" (Psalm 119:21) — and as the refuge of the oppressed ("let not the insolent oppress me", Psalm 119:122). C2 is never borne by God.

**T0.1.2** — Never borne by God; exclusively creaturely. The pattern shows C2 as contempt directed at the neighbour and bound up with contempt for God's law.

**T0.2.1** — It leads the person to oppress, deride, and defraud others (Psalm 119:51, 69, 85).

**T0.2.2** — Fallen condition.

**T0.2.3** — None.

**T0.3.1** — None.

**T0.3.2** — Exclusively creaturely.

**T0.3.3** — Its presence shows the image disordered toward the neighbour — regard for others replaced by contempt.

**T0.4.1** — **SILENT [data-silence]**: no typological use in C2's verses.

*Coverage T0: 8 answered, 1 SILENT (T0.4.1).*

## T1 — Definition

**T1.1.1** — *Insolence/contempt toward others*: pride turned outward as derision, contempt, and oppression of people. The name signals an outward, relational discharge.

**T1.1.2** — zed ("insolent, presumptuous"), za.don ("insolence" → strife), ra.hav ("be insolent/boisterous"), shal.le.tet ("brazen"). Definitionally, the bearing-down of the high on the low.

**T1.1.3** — Outward and **against** others — the relational pole of pride.

**T1.2.1** — An **act/behaviour** (derision, oppression) issuing from the settled disposition (B).

**T1.2.2** — Compound: the settled pride of B + its outward, contemptuous discharge upon people.

**T1.3.1** — Its opposite is humility expressed as regard for others — "be subject to the elders… clothe yourselves with humility toward one another" (1 Peter 5:5, the inverse of the insolent youth).

**T1.3.2** — It excludes regard, pity, and due honour ("they close their hearts to pity", Psalm 17:10).

**T1.3.3** — C2 is not the defiance toward God (C1) nor the inner height (B); it is contempt enacted upon the neighbour.

**T1.4.1** — It operates as contemptuous action: "The insolent utterly deride me" (Psalm 119:51); "smear me with lies" (119:69); "have dug pitfalls for me" (119:85).

**T1.4.2** — It varies — derision (mocking), defamation (smearing), entrapment (pitfalls), oppression (Psalm 119:122), and social disorder ("the youth… insolent to the elder", Isaiah 3:5).

**T1.4.3** — Yes — chiefly communicative/verbal: derision and lies (Psalm 119:51, 69); "speak arrogantly" (Psalm 17:10).

**T1.5.1** — Its immediate effect falls on the **other** — the sufferer derided, smeared, trapped (Psalm 119:51, 85). The proud agent's inner response is largely unstated [data-silence].

**T1.5.2** — Consistent in its outward target (the lowly/righteous); the agent's interior is consistently unstated.

**T1.6.1** — It produces strife — "By insolence comes nothing but strife" (Proverbs 13:10) — and entrenched oppression.

**T1.6.3** — Immediate = the contemptuous act on the other; sustained = strife and the hardened oppressor (B).

**T1.7.1** — It takes hold where pride is settled (B) and pity is closed off (Psalm 17:10); never operates rightly [structural].

**T1.7.2** — Resisted by humility-toward-one-another (1 Peter 5:5). On another spirit — **SILENT [data-silence]**.

**T1.7.3** — Where checked, the person clothes itself in humility toward others (1 Peter 5:5).

*Coverage T1: 18 of 18 (T1.5.1 part data-silence on the agent's interior).*

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**T2.1.1** — Where seated, the **heart** — the "brazen" heart (Ezekiel 16:30); hearts "closed to pity" (Psalm 17:10). The named soul is often the **sufferer's** ("a band of ruthless men seeks my life", Psalm 86:14). The agent's seat is mostly unstated.

**T2.1.2** — The pattern shows C2 as predominantly **outward act** with little stated interior — a faculty-absent expression whose seat is supplied by B (the settled heart behind it).

**T2.10.1** — **SILENT [data-silence]** / [structural]: no constitutional movement stated; C2 is the outward discharge of B.

**T2.7.1** — Body link via the speaking mouth and the closed heart (Psalm 17:10) — expressive; otherwise none.

**T2.9.1** — Within the proud person (rooted in B); occasioned by settled pride. *(Origin of the act = the settled disposition.)*

**T2.9.2** — Single (within-person, from the settled pride of B).

*Coverage T2: 6 of 6 (T2.10.1 silent).*

## T3 — The Inner Faculties

**T3.1 Perception** — **T3.1.1** Minimal; the insolent "close their hearts to pity" (Psalm 17:10) — a refusal to perceive the other's need. **T3.1.2/3** Otherwise **SILENT [data-silence]**.

**T3.2 Cognition** — **SILENT [data-silence]**: C2's verses describe deeds, not the agent's reasoning.

**T3.3 Memory** — **SILENT [data-silence]**.

**T3.4 Affect** — **T3.4.1** A single tag (ra.hav, affect) — insolence carries a hostile affective edge ("the youth will be insolent to the elder", Isaiah 3:5). **T3.4.2/3** Otherwise the agent's affect is largely unstated [data-silence].

**T3.5 Creativity** — **SILENT [data-silence]**.

**T3.6 Volition** — **T3.6.1** Engaged in the chosen oppression — the insolent deliberately "dug pitfalls" and "spread a net" (Psalm 119:85; 140:5). **T3.6.2** It directs the will against the neighbour. **T3.6.3** C2's volition is largely instrumental — willed harm.

**T3.7 Agency** — **T3.7.1** Strongly engaged: deride, smear, dig pitfalls, oppress, pursue the poor (Psalm 119:51, 69, 85, 122; 10:2). **T3.7.2** It is action against people. **T3.7.3** C2 is, above all, an agency of contempt.

**T3.8 Moral Evaluation** — **T3.8.1** Judged — the insolent are "accursed" (Psalm 119:21); their insolence "comes nothing but strife" (Proverbs 13:10). **T3.8.2/3** It overrides regard for the other's worth.

**T3.9 Conscience** — **SILENT [data-silence]**; *inferential:* "close their hearts to pity" (Psalm 17:10) implies a silenced conscience.

**T3.10 Conscientiousness** — **T3.10.1** Engaged negatively — the insolent "do not live according to your law" (Psalm 119:85). **T3.10.2/3** C2 couples contempt for people with disregard of God's law.

**T3.11 Relational Capacity** — **T3.11.1** Centrally engaged — C2 *is* a relational characteristic: contempt, derision, and oppression of the neighbour, elder, and lowly (Psalm 123:4; Isaiah 3:5). **T3.11.2** It destroys due regard and connection. **T3.11.3** C2 is the relational faculty turned to harm.

*Coverage T3: ~18 answered; ~15 SILENT (perception partial, cognition, memory, affect partial, creativity, conscience — data-silence). C2's interior is thin by nature; its content concentrates in agency and relational capacity.*

## T4 — Relational Interfaces

**T4.1 Divine — God to Human** — **SILENT [structural]**: not extended by God.

**T4.2 Divine — Human to God** — **T4.2.1** Indirect: the insolent's contempt for people is bound to disregard of God — "who wander from your commandments" (Psalm 119:21); "they do not live according to your law" (119:85). **T4.2.2/3** Its God-ward posture is disregard, mediated through contempt for the neighbour.

**T4.3 Human — Giving** — **T4.3.1** C2 *is* directed from one person toward another — but as **harm, not gift**: derision, defamation, oppression (Psalm 119:51, 69). The "giving" frame is inverted: what is extended is contempt. **T4.3.2/3 — [structural]** for the giver-conditions of a genuine good (n/a — C2 extends harm).

**T4.4 Human — Receiving** — **T4.4.1** The other **receives** C2 as injury; the sufferer's uptake is endurance and fidelity — "The insolent utterly deride me, but I do not turn away from your law" (Psalm 119:51). **T4.4.2/3** The faithful sufferer does not take up insolence in return.

**T4.5 Human — Boundaries** — **T4.5.1** It operates across relational distance (oppressor → the lowly) and within social order (youth → elder, Isaiah 3:5). **T4.5.2** It crosses covenantal lines — the insolent within and the ruthless without (Psalm 86:14). **T4.5.3** Its scope is the neighbour, the elder, the poor — those beneath the proud's regard.

**T4.6 Spiritual Beings** — **SILENT [data-silence]** (T4.6.1–3).

*Coverage T4: ~12 answered, ~6 SILENT (T4.1 structural; T4.6 data; T4.3 partial). Unlike A/B, C2 substantively answers the human-interface tiers — it is the cluster's outward-relational characteristic.*

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

**T5.1.1** — In the **sufferer**, C2 occasions a tested fidelity ("but I do not turn away from your law", Psalm 119:51); in the agent, it hardens contempt.

**T5.1.2** — **SILENT [data-silence]** on reversibility in the agent.

**T5.2.1** — Sequence (sufferer's side): contempt met → endurance → continued obedience (Psalm 119:51, 69).

**T5.3.1** — Mechanism: in the sufferer, perseverance under contempt; in the agent, hardening. (No transformation of the agent shown.)

**T5.3.2** — Differs by side (sufferer formed; agent hardened).

**T5.4.1** — C2 is a **context of suffering** for its victims — the righteous afflicted by the insolent (Psalm 86:14; 119:121–122).

**T5.4.2** — Suffering under C2 **refines the sufferer's** fidelity (Psalm 119:51, 69) — a notable inversion: the characteristic's developmental fruit appears in the one it is aimed at, not the one who bears it.

**T5.5.1** — For the sufferer, C2 participates in sanctification as tested endurance; for the agent, it is the disorder formation must overcome.

**T5.6.1** — **SILENT [data-silence]**.

*Coverage T5: ~7 answered, ~2 SILENT (T5.1.2, T5.6.1). C2's developmental content sits unusually on the sufferer's side.*
