## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**T7.1.1** — zed ("insolent, presumptuous"), za.don ("insolence"), ra.hav ("be boisterous/insolent"), shal.le.tet ("brazen, imperious"). Root sense: a brazen pushing against others.

**T7.1.2** — Adjectives/substantives ("the insolent") and abstract nouns ("insolence"). The substantival form shows a **person-type** ("the insolent") as much as an act.

**T7.1.3** — Semantic range: from "insolent/presumptuous" through "brazen/imperious" to "boisterous" — the bearing of one who will not be checked.

**T7.1.4** — Yes — abstract ("insolence", za.don) versus person-type ("the insolent", zed).

**T7.1.5** — Yes — the opposite is humility/regard for others (1 Peter 5:5).

**T7.1.6** — Yes, prominently: "the insolent" (zed) as a settled person-type (the Psalm 119 antagonist).

**T7.1.7** — None.

**T7.1.8** — The OT insolence vocabulary (zed, za.don) has no single NT successor term; its sense is carried in the NT by "despise authority"/"abusive" terms — a partial continuity.

**T7.1.9** — None newly coined.

**T7.1.10** — The arc shows insolence as a recognised social-religious type — the brazen oppressor of the faithful.

**T7.2.1** — In Psalm 119, zed names the antagonist whose contempt frames the psalmist's fidelity: "The insolent utterly deride me, but I do not turn away from your law" (119:51).

**T7.2.2** — Forms: psalm (the lament/Torah-psalm of Psalm 119), prophecy (Isaiah 3:5), wisdom (Proverbs 13:10). The lament form carries C2 from the **sufferer's** vantage — essential to its reading.

**T7.2.3** — The argument (Psalm 119): the insolent oppress; the faithful endure and keep the law — contempt does not move the righteous.

**T7.2.4** — Settings: liturgical/lament (Psalm 119), social-prophetic (Isaiah 3), wisdom (Proverbs).

**T7.2.5** — Anchor: **Psalm 119:51** — the insolent's derision met by the sufferer's fidelity — C2 seen from beneath.

**T7.2.6** — Psalm 119:51 shows what no agent-focused verse does: C2's defining shape is the contempt the faithful *endure*, not merely the contempt the proud *feel*.

**T7.3.1** — *(science, M08 extract §3)* The social psychology of power and dominance is the most useful lens — C2 is the dominance pole enacted on others.

**T7.3.2** — *(science)* Keltner's power paradox — power reduces empathy and increases self-focus (extract §3) — illuminates "they close their hearts to pity" (Psalm 17:10) and the contempt of the proud for the poor.

**T7.3.3** — *(science)* Science describes dominance as adaptive status-seeking; the biblical material judges contempt for the lowly as sin and frames it from the victim's side (extract T7.3.3) — a register and vantage divergence.

**T7.3.4** — *(science)* Science attends to the dominant agent; the biblical material's attention to the **oppressed sufferer** surfaces an aspect (fidelity under contempt) the dominance literature does not centre.

No question unanswered. C2's distinctive profile: it is **thin in the agent's interior** (most T3 faculties data-silent) but **rich in the human-interface tiers** (T4.3–4.5) and in T7.2's sufferer-vantage — the inverse of A's profile. Its inner-being content legitimately leans on B (the disposition behind the act), recorded transparently rather than padded.

# WA — M08 · Characteristic C2: Insolence / Contempt toward Other People

**File:** wa-m08-c2-insolence-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Prior output reference:** wa-m08-a-self-exaltation-v1_0-20260621.md (template); wa-m08-c1-presumption-v1_0-20260621.md.
**Source data:** wa-ve-lexical-extract-M08-20260621-b1of2/b2of2.json (extract v1_0, 2026-06-21).
**Method:** every focus occurrence read individually; per-occurrence direction split from the shared z-d root (C2 toward others). Analysis derived from verses (§A2). Quotes ≤15 words.

---

## 1. Definition (working)

Pride turned **outward against other people** as insolent contempt, derision, and oppression — the haughty bearing down on neighbour, elder, and the lowly. The outward, relational pole of pride.

## 2. Evidence base

**~13 core occurrences** (plus cross-listed oppression from B): zed (H2086 — Psalm 119:21, 51, 69, 78, 85, 122; Psalm 86:14), zid (H2102 — Exodus 18:11; Nehemiah 9:10; Exodus 21:14), za.don (H2087 — Proverbs 13:10), ra.hav (H7292 — Isaiah 3:5), shal.le.tet (H7986 — Ezekiel 16:30). Cross-listed from B (settled pride expressed as oppression): ga.a.vah (H1346 — Psalm 10:2; 31:18; 73:6; 140:5) and ge.ut (H1348 — Psalm 17:10).

## 3. Analysis (observation → interpretation)

**The dominant scene is the insolent oppressing the righteous.** The Psalm 119 cluster sets it out: "The insolent utterly deride me" (119:51); "The insolent smear me with lies" (119:69); "The insolent have dug pitfalls for me" (119:85); "let not the insolent oppress me" (119:122); "insolent men have risen up against me… seek my life" (Psalm 86:14). The insolent are the agents; the righteous sufferer is the one acted upon.

**Insolence and disregard of God's law go together.** The same insolent ones "wander from your commandments" (Psalm 119:21) and "do not live according to your law" (Psalm 119:85). **Interpretation:** in the wicked, contempt toward people (C2) and disregard of God (C1) are fused — the same pride faces both directions. The split is analytic; in the person it is one disposition.

**It breaks proper social order.** "the youth will be insolent to the elder, and the despised to the honorable" (Isaiah 3:5) — insolence as the collapse of due regard.

**Its root is the settled pride of B.** The cross-listed evidence shows the mechanism: "In arrogance the wicked hotly pursue the poor" (Psalm 10:2); "pride is their necklace; violence covers them" (Psalm 73:6); "They close their hearts to pity; with their mouths they speak arrogantly" (Psalm 17:10). The settled height (B) issues in contemptuous action (C2).

**The sufferer's posture is fidelity under contempt.** The righteous keep God's word despite the insolent — "The insolent utterly deride me, but I do not turn away from your law" (Psalm 119:51); "with my whole heart I keep your precepts" (Psalm 119:69). C2 is largely framed from the victim's side.

## 4. Synthesis

Insolence is pride aimed at people: the haughty deriding, defrauding, and oppressing the lowly, and the young despising the honourable. It is the outward, relational discharge of the settled pride of B, and in the wicked it is inseparable from their disregard of God (C1). The corpus most often shows it from beneath — as contempt endured by the faithful, who answer it not in kind but by keeping God's word.

## 5. Expected but absent — special attention

1. **The proud's *inner* state is thin by nature — a genuine shape, not a gap.** C2 is described overwhelmingly through *action* (deride, smear, oppress, dig pitfalls, pursue the poor) rather than through an inner condition of the proud agent. Its inner-being content is largely supplied by B (settled pride) and by the *victim's* interior (the faithful heart that keeps the law). **Interpretation:** C2 is the **faculty-absent outward pole** of pride — its analysis legitimately leans on the agent's settled disposition (B) and the sufferer's response, because the lexical itself locates little interior in the insolent act. This mirrors the M06 finding that a substantial share of outward hostility is faculty-absent. Genuine silence, recorded as a finding.
2. **Experiencer is frequently the *sufferer*, not the proud.** The `experiencer=self` tags (Psalm 119:51, 85, 122) mark the psalmist-victim, not the insolent. Read carelessly this could be miscounted as the proud person's self-experience. → caution flag for any aggregation.
3. **Seat rarely named** (heart, Ezekiel 16:30 "brazen"; soul, Psalm 86:14 of the victim). The proud agent's seat is mostly unstated; the named seats often belong to the sufferer. Do not over-read.
4. **Cause largely silent**, consistent with B: the contempt flows from a settled disposition rather than a stated elicitor.

## 6. Reflection (labelled — not a conclusion)

- C2 carries direct social-ethical resonance (contempt for the poor, the elder, the honourable); the "from beneath" framing — fidelity under contempt — is pastorally significant but stated descriptively here.
- The fusion of C1 and C2 in the wicked (contempt for God and for people as one disposition) is a candidate observation for the cluster synthesis.
- **Cross-cultural:** Isaiah 3:5 (youth insolent to elder) will read with particular force in age-/honour-ordered cultures. → flag for reader-facing.

## 7. Coverage

~13 core occurrences placed, plus cross-listed oppression evidence from B (ga.a.vah, ge.ut). Shared-root straddle explicit: zid and za.don contribute to both C1 and C2; several za.don/zed "the arrogant/proud one" uses lean B (noted, not relocated). The C2 inner-being content is acknowledged as carried partly by B — a structural feature, recorded transparently rather than padded. Nothing dropped.

# WA — M08 · Characteristic D (Boasting / Glorying — Two Poles): Tier-Catalogue Findings

**File:** wa-m08-d-tier-answers-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Prior output reference:** wa-m08-d-boasting-v1_0-20260621.md; WA-tier-catalogue-current-state-v2-20260619.md.
**Source data:** 69 occurrences read individually.
**Method:** as the A template. **Standing note:** D is a single act (glorying) differentiated by its **object** into two poles — a *sinful* pole (boasting in flesh/self/works) and a *righteous/commanded* pole (boasting in the Lord, the cross, weakness). Answers track both poles per question. D is the cluster's only consistently **affect-bearing** characteristic and its only one with a legitimate, commanded form.

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**T0.1.1** — Uniquely in the cluster, the God-relation is **positive in one pole**: God is the proper *object* of right boasting — "Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord" (1 Corinthians 1:31); "let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows me" (Jeremiah 9:24). In the sinful pole God is displaced by self ("you boast in your arrogance", James 4:16).

**T0.1.2** — God does not boast, but glory **belongs to** God, and the creature's boasting is right only when returned to him (1 Corinthians 1:31). The pattern indicates that glorying is a created capacity rightly ordered toward God and disordered when turned on the self.

**T0.2.1** — In its right pole it leads the person to exult in God and his works (Psalm 34:2, "my soul makes its boast in the Lord"); in its sinful pole, to self-display and false confidence (James 4:16).

**T0.2.2** — **Both** — uniquely: D belongs to created design in its God-directed pole and to the fallen condition in its self-directed pole.

**T0.2.3** — **Yes** — D is oriented toward future fullness: "we boast/rejoice in hope of the glory of God" (Romans 5:2); boasting now anticipates the glory to come. (Unique eschatological orientation in the cluster.)

**T0.3.1** — In its right pole D instantiates the creature's proper **glorying in God** — the image rendering glory to its source.

**T0.3.2** — The right pole is a creaturely act directed to God (glory is God's; the creature returns it); the sinful pole is the creaturely distortion.

**T0.3.3** — Right boasting expresses the image rightly ordered; self-boasting expresses it disordered — the same capacity, two directions.

**T0.4.1** — **Christological:** "far be it from me to boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ" (Galatians 6:14) — boasting is redirected to the cross. Typological direction: the human glorying re-anchored in Christ's saving work.

*Coverage T0: 9 of 9 — the fullest T0 in the cluster (the only positive God-relation).*

## T1 — Definition

**T1.1.1** — *Boasting/glorying*: the act of exulting in and declaring the worth of an object. The name signals an **object-driven** act — its character is set by what is boasted in.

**T1.1.2** — kauchaomai ("to boast, glory, exult"), kauchēsis / kauchēma ("the boasting / the thing boasted in"), ha.lal ("to praise, boast, shine"), alazōn / alazoneia ("braggart / vain boasting"). Definitionally, to make much of something out loud.

**T1.1.3** — A **communicative, affect-laden** act whose moral value is wholly determined by its object and direction.

**T1.2.1** — An **act** with strong affective content (exultation) — not a settled state.

**T1.2.2** — Compound: an affective exultation + a declared object + a direction (toward God or toward self/others).

**T1.3.1** — Its structural opposite is **trust/dependence** that glories in another rather than the self — and, for the sinful pole, the boasting in self that the right pole excludes ("not because of works, so that no one may boast", Ephesians 2:9).

**T1.3.2** — The right pole excludes self-reliance ("we put no confidence in the flesh", Philippians 3:3); the sinful pole excludes dependence on God.

**T1.3.3** — D is not the settled height (B) nor the inner self-lifting (A); it is the **declared exultation** that may run either way.

**T1.4.1** — It operates as speech-act: "my soul makes its boast in the Lord" (Psalm 34:2); "I will all the more gladly boast of my weaknesses" (2 Corinthians 12:9).

**T1.4.2** — It varies entirely by **object**: boasting in the Lord, the cross, weakness, hope (right); boasting in flesh, works, wisdom, riches, tomorrow (sinful — Jeremiah 9:23; James 4:13–16).

**T1.4.3** — Inherently communicative — boasting *is* a speech mode (commanded in 1 Corinthians 1:31; condemned in James 4:16).

**T1.5.1** — Its immediate inner correlate is **exultation/joy** — "my soul shall exult/boast in the Lord" pairs boasting with rejoicing (Psalm 34:2).

**T1.5.2** — Consistent in carrying affect; varied in valence (joyful confidence in God vs self-satisfied vaunting).

**T1.6.1** — Right boasting establishes a settled confidence in God ("we are his… who glory in Christ Jesus", Philippians 3:3); wrong boasting establishes false security (James 4:16, "all such boasting is evil").

**T1.6.3** — Immediate = the exultant act; sustained = the confidence (or false confidence) it settles into.

**T1.7.1** — Right boasting operates rightly under **knowledge of God** ("that he knows me", Jeremiah 9:24) and the cross (Galatians 6:14).

**T1.7.2** — It is distorted when its object becomes the self/flesh/works (Jeremiah 9:23; Ephesians 2:9). On another spirit — **SILENT [data-silence]**.

**T1.7.3** — Where the right object is lost, boasting becomes the "vain boasting" of the braggart (alazoneia, James 4:16; 1 John 2:16).

*Coverage T1: 18 of 18 — D's two-pole, object-driven definition is the richest in the cluster.*

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**T2.1.1** — Seated in the **heart/soul with affect**: "my soul makes its boast in the Lord" (Psalm 34:2); the inner exultation of glorying. The sinful pole is located in the heart's false confidence (James 4:16) and "the flesh" (Philippians 3:3–4).

**T2.1.2** — D is the cluster's **affective** characteristic — seated where feeling and exultation meet declaration. Its body link is the **mouth** (boasting is spoken).

**T2.10.1** — Movement inner→outer: the heart's exultation issues in declared boast. No external-source movement stated.

**T2.7.1** — Body link via the **speaking mouth** — the boast is the exultation voiced (expressive, soul→body).

**T2.9.1** — Right boasting originates in **knowledge of God received** (Jeremiah 9:24) — partly God-given; wrong boasting originates in the self's false confidence.

**T2.9.2** — Origin is **dual**: the right pole grounded in God-given knowledge; the sinful pole self-generated.

*Coverage T2: 6 of 6.*

## T3 — The Inner Faculties

**T3.1 Perception** — **T3.1.1** Minimal as inner-sense; the right pole rests on *knowing* God (cognition, not perception). **T3.1.2/3 — SILENT [data-silence]** for perception proper.

**T3.2 Cognition** — **T3.2.1** Engaged: right boasting is grounded in **knowledge** — "that he knows me" (Jeremiah 9:24); wrong boasting on a false estimate of wisdom/works (Jeremiah 9:23; 1 Corinthians 1:31 context). **T3.2.2** It orders (or disorders) the mind's self-estimate relative to God. **T3.2.3** D's cognition is object-discriminating — what one knows truly determines whether boasting is right.

**T3.3 Memory** — **SILENT [data-silence]** mostly; *inferential:* right boasting recalls God's deeds (Psalm 44:8, "in God we have boasted continually").

**T3.4 Affect** — **T3.4.1** Centrally and uniquely engaged — boasting carries exultation/joy: "my soul makes its boast in the Lord; let the humble hear and be glad" (Psalm 34:2); "I will boast all the more gladly" (2 Corinthians 12:9). **T3.4.2** It is the cluster's seat of positive affect (when rightly directed) and of self-satisfied affect (when not). **T3.4.3** D is the **affective pole of the whole cluster** — the one characteristic where feeling is integral, not incidental.

**T3.5 Creativity** — **SILENT [data-silence]**.

**T3.6 Volition** — **T3.6.1** Engaged: boasting is chosen and its object willed — "far be it from me to boast except in the cross" (Galatians 6:14, a willed re-anchoring). **T3.6.2** The will selects the object that makes the boast right or wrong. **T3.6.3** D's volition is the choosing of an object.

**T3.7 Agency** — **T3.7.1** The boast is an act of self-presentation; the sinful pole acts to display (James 4:13–16). **T3.7.2** It externalises the inner valuation. **T3.7.3** D consistently issues in declared action (speech).

**T3.8 Moral Evaluation** — **T3.8.1** Centrally engaged: D is the cluster's clearest site of **moral discrimination by object** — "all such boasting is evil" (James 4:16) versus boasting commanded "in the Lord" (1 Corinthians 1:31). **T3.8.2** The same act is righteous or sinful by its object. **T3.8.3** D shows that the inner-being value of an act can be wholly object-determined.

**T3.9 Conscience** — **SILENT [data-silence]**; *inferential:* right boasting in the cross presupposes a conscience cleansed (Galatians 6:14).

**T3.10 Conscientiousness** — **T3.10.1** Engaged in the right pole as integrated God-directed confidence (Philippians 3:3); in the wrong pole as presumption about the future ("you ought to say, 'If the Lord wills'", James 4:15). **T3.10.2/3** D's conscientiousness is the ordering of confidence under God's will.

**T3.11 Relational Capacity** — **T3.11.1** Engaged: boasting is **relational and audience-directed** — Paul boasts *about* the churches ("I have great pride in you", 2 Corinthians 7:4) and *before* others (2 Corinthians 8:24); the sinful pole vaunts over others. **T3.11.2** It can build up (right, edifying pride in others) or wound (vaunting). **T3.11.3** D uniquely shows a **constructive relational** mode — pride *in another* that honours them.

*Coverage T3: ~27 answered; ~6 SILENT (T3.1 partial, T3.3 inferential, T3.5, T3.9 inferential — data-silence). D answers affect, cognition, moral evaluation, and relational capacity more fully than any other M08 characteristic.*

## T4 — Relational Interfaces

**T4.1 Divine — God to Human** — **T4.1.1** Indirect but present: God **gives the ground** of right boasting (the knowledge of himself, the cross) — "that he knows me… for in these things I delight" (Jeremiah 9:24). **T4.1.2** Grace-based: right boasting rests on what God has done, "not because of works" (Ephesians 2:9). **T4.1.3** It shows God inviting the creature to glory in him rather than itself.

**T4.2 Divine — Human to God** — **T4.2.1** D's central register: boasting in the Lord *is* a God-ward act of worship and confidence — "in God we have boasted continually" (Psalm 44:8); "my soul makes its boast in the Lord" (Psalm 34:2). **T4.2.2** It requires the inner posture of dependence — glory referred away from the self to God. **T4.2.3** Right boasting shows a relationship of confident, dependent exultation in God.

**T4.3 Human — Giving** — **T4.3.1** Engaged constructively: one person boasts *about* another to honour them — "great is my pride/boasting in you" (2 Corinthians 7:4); "show… the proof of your love and of our boasting about you" (2 Corinthians 8:24). **T4.3.2** Genuine extension requires real ground for the commendation (Paul's boasting is vindicated by the Corinthians' conduct). **T4.3.3** It presupposes a relationship of love and confidence.

**T4.4 Human — Receiving** — **T4.4.1** The one boasted about **receives** honour and is summoned to live up to it (2 Corinthians 8:24, "the proof… before the churches"). **T4.4.2** Right uptake is the vindication of the boast; the sinful counterpart is flattery received. **T4.4.3** **SILENT [data-silence]** on refusal.

**T4.5 Human — Boundaries** — **T4.5.1** Right boasting operates within bonds (Paul and his churches); sinful boasting vaunts across distance (over rivals). **T4.5.2** It crosses covenantal lines in both poles. **T4.5.3** Its scope: in the right pole, the community edified; in the wrong, the self exalted over others.

**T4.6 Spiritual Beings** — **SILENT [data-silence]** (T4.6.1–3).

*Coverage T4: ~14 answered, ~4 SILENT (T4.6; T4.4.3). D substantively answers all the relational tiers — the fullest T4 in the cluster.*

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

**T5.1.1** — Right boasting **transforms orientation** — it re-anchors the self away from flesh toward God/cross (Galatians 6:14; Philippians 3:3). Both condition and orientation are addressed.

**T5.1.2** — The re-anchoring is presented as a settled stance ("far be it from me", Galatians 6:14) — durable, though requiring repeated choice.

**T5.2.1** — Sequence (right pole): self-confidence relinquished → boasting redirected to God/weakness → Christ's power rests (2 Corinthians 12:9).

**T5.3.1** — Mechanism: **encounter with weakness and grace** — "My grace is sufficient… my power is made perfect in weakness" (2 Corinthians 12:9). Right boasting is formed through felt insufficiency.

**T5.3.2** — Differs by pole: the right pole is formed through weakness; the wrong pole is fed by prosperity and presumption (James 4:13–16).

**T5.4.1** — **Strongly engaged:** right boasting operates *in* suffering — "we boast in our sufferings" (Romans 5:3); "I will boast of my weaknesses" (2 Corinthians 12:9). **T5.4.2** Suffering **perfects** right boasting by emptying the self of false ground — D's most distinctive developmental move: the inversion of pride's logic, where one glories in weakness so that Christ's power may rest.

**T5.5.1** — Right boasting participates in sanctification as the ongoing re-anchoring of confidence in God rather than self (Philippians 3:3).

**T5.6.1** — **Eschatological:** boasting "in hope of the glory of God" (Romans 5:2) anticipates the coming glory — present exultation reaching toward future fullness.

*Coverage T5: 9 of 9 — D's developmental and eschatological content is the richest in the cluster.*

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics

**T6.1.1** — The sinful pole co-occurs with A/B (pride expressed — James 4:16, "boast in your arrogance"); the right pole co-occurs with **trust/faith** and **joy** (Psalm 34:2 pairs boasting with gladness — an M04 link).

**T6.1.2** — D sits at the **expressive edge** of the cluster — pride's outward voice — but uniquely branches into a righteous, faith-aligned form.

**T6.2.1** — Sinful boasting **follows** A/B (self-exaltation/settled pride → vaunting); right boasting follows faith.

**T6.2.2** — Causal/expressive (pride → sinful boast) and developmental (faith → right boast).

**T6.3.1** — Sinful D produces false security; right D produces confident dependence (Philippians 3:3).

**T6.3.2** — Sinful D is produced by A/B; right D by faith/knowledge of God.

**T6.3.3** — D is the **expressed/declared** aspect; A and B are the dispositions it can voice; trust is the disposition the right pole voices.

**T6.4.1** — Shares ha.lal with **praise/M04** (ha.lal = praise/boast/shine) and the kauchaomai-family is distinct to D; alazoneia overlaps the "pride of life" (1 John 2:16).

**T6.4.2** — The ha.lal root spans boasting and praise — a root-level link between M08 and the praise/joy field.

**T6.4.3** — The ha.lal sharing shows right boasting and praise to be near-neighbours — exultation in God voiced.

**T6.5.1** — Nearest neighbour (sinful pole): A/B (pride voiced). Nearest neighbour (right pole): **trust/faith** — distinguished because right boasting *refers glory away from the self*, the exact inverse of A.

**T6.5.2** — The boundary with A/B is **direction of glory** (to self vs to God); with trust, D is the *declared* form of the same God-ward confidence.

**T6.5.3** — The distinction is one of **object/direction**, not constitutional level — the same act (glorying) running to opposite termini.

*Coverage T6: 13 of 13.*

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**T7.1.1** — kauchaomai / kauchēsis / kauchēma ("boast, glory; the act; the thing/ground boasted in"), ha.lal ("praise, boast, shine"), alazōn / alazoneia ("braggart, vain-boasting"). Roots: to make-much-of (Greek), to shine/praise (Hebrew).

**T7.1.2** — Verb (kauchaomai — the act), and two nouns distinguishing the *act* (kauchēsis) from the *ground* (kauchēma) — a grammatical range that lexicalises object-dependence.

**T7.1.3** — Semantic range: from worshipful exultation ("boast in the Lord") to empty vaunting (alazoneia) — the widest valence-range in the cluster.

**T7.1.4** — Yes — kauchēsis (the act) versus kauchēma (the ground/object) — exactly the disposition/object distinction D's two poles turn on.

**T7.1.5** — The opposite/absence is **boasting excluded** — "so that no one may boast" (Ephesians 2:9) — and the trust that puts "no confidence in the flesh" (Philippians 3:3).

**T7.1.6** — Yes — a person-type: alazōn, "the braggart" (Romans 1:30; 2 Timothy 3:2).

**T7.1.7** — None.

**T7.1.8** — The OT ha.lal "boast" continues into NT kauchaomai, and the OT principle "let him who boasts boast… that he knows the Lord" (Jeremiah 9:24) is taken up directly by Paul (1 Corinthians 1:31) — strong continuity with apostolic development.

**T7.1.9** — The kauchaomai-family is not newly coined but is **developed** by Paul into a theology of boasting-in-weakness (2 Corinthians 11–12) — a NT deepening rather than a coinage.

**T7.1.10** — The full arc runs from praise/shine (ha.lal) through worshipful boasting in God to the cross-and-weakness boasting of Paul, and, on the dark side, to the braggart's vain-boasting.

**T7.2.1** — In the anchor, kauchaomai carries the whole imperative: "Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord" (1 Corinthians 1:31), quoting Jeremiah 9:24.

**T7.2.2** — Forms: prophecy (Jeremiah 9), psalm (Psalm 34; 44), and epistle (1–2 Corinthians, Galatians, Philippians, James, 1 John). The epistolary argument (Paul's boasting discourse) requires attention to its polemical, object-discriminating logic.

**T7.2.3** — The key argument: boasting is excluded *as to its sinful object* (works, flesh, wisdom, riches) and commanded *as to its right object* (the Lord, the cross, weakness) — the value follows the object (Jeremiah 9:23–24; 1 Corinthians 1:31; Galatians 6:14).

**T7.2.4** — Settings: covenantal/prophetic (Jeremiah), liturgical (Psalms), and pastoral-polemical (Corinthian correspondence).

**T7.2.5** — Anchor: **Jeremiah 9:23–24 / 1 Corinthians 1:31** — "let him who boasts boast… that he knows the Lord" — the verse stating the right object that reorders the whole act.

**T7.2.6** — Jeremiah 9:23–24 shows what no other verse states so plainly: boasting is not abolished but **re-objected** — the creature is to glory, but in God.

**T7.3.1** — *(science, M08 extract §4)* Impression-management / self-promotion (Goffman; Jones & Pittman) is the most useful lens for the **sinful** pole; the two-facet model (extract §1) maps the right/wrong split onto authentic vs hubristic registers.

**T7.3.2** — *(science)* Self-promotion research (extract §4) illuminates the social-display logic of the braggart (alazōn); Tracy & Robins' authentic-pride (extract §1) partly illuminates the legitimacy of boasting grounded in real ground (Paul's vindicated boasting, 2 Corinthians 8:24).

**T7.3.3** — *(science)* Science treats some self-promotion as adaptive and even authentic pride as healthy; the biblical material judges *all* self-directed boasting as excluded and commands boasting only in God (extract T7.3.3) — a sharper, object-based criterion than science's healthy/pathological axis.

**T7.3.4** — *(science)* Science has no category for the **righteous, God-directed boast** — boasting in weakness so that another's power may rest (2 Corinthians 12:9). This is the cluster's clearest point where the verse evidence exceeds the science (extract note on the theological distinctive).

*Coverage T7: 20 of 20.*

| **Total** | **126** | **~116** | **~10** | data-silence ~10 |

**The highest coverage in the cluster.** D's profile is the inverse of A's: where A is structurally silent on the divine and human relational interfaces (pride is not extended or given), D **answers them fully** — because boasting is inherently object-directed, God-ward, communicative, affective, and (in its right pole) constructive toward others. D is also the only characteristic with a positive T0, a "both" at T0.2.2, and a genuine eschatological orientation (T0.2.3, T5.6.1). Its two structural silences elsewhere (perception, creativity) are genuine.

# WA — M08 · Characteristic D: Boasting and Glorying (verbal/affective self-display — two poles)

**File:** wa-m08-d-boasting-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Prior output reference:** wa-m08-a-self-exaltation-v1_0-20260621.md (template); wa-m08-prov-char-list-v1_1-20260621.md.
**Source data:** wa-ve-lexical-extract-M08-20260621-b1of2/b2of2.json (extract v1_0, 2026-06-21).
**Method:** every focus occurrence read individually with object + valence fields (the two poles are object-driven). Analysis derived from verses (§A2). Quotes ≤15 words. Per researcher decision, D is **one characteristic with two poles**, not two characteristics.

---

## 1. Definition (working)

The audible, affective overflow of the heart's confidence — the point at which the inner state declares its **ground**. Uniquely in M08, boasting is morally **bivalent**: the identical act is sinful or righteous entirely according to its *object*.

## 2. Evidence base

**69 occurrences.** kauchaomai (G2744, 32), kauchēsis (G2746, 12), kauchēma (G2745, 11), ha.lal (H1984H, 10), alazōn (G0213, 2), alazoneia (G0212, 2). kauchaomai/kauchēma carry `faculty=affect` — D is the one characteristic with a consistent faculty tag.

### 2a. Sinful / forbidden pole — object = flesh, self, works, riches, wisdom, idols
"Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom… the mighty in his might… the rich in his riches" (Jeremiah 9:23); "boast of the abundance of their riches" (Psalm 49:6); "make their boast in worthless idols" (Psalm 97:7); "boast in your flesh" (Galatians 6:13, seated in flesh); "boast in the law" (Romans 2:23); "you boast in your arrogance. All such boasting is evil" (James 4:16); "so that no one may boast" re works (Ephesians 2:9); "no human being might boast in the presence of God" (1 Corinthians 1:29). The "pride of life" belongs here (1 John 2:16, seated in flesh).

### 2b. Righteous / commanded pole — object = the Lord, Christ, the cross, weakness, God
"Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord" (1 Corinthians 1:31, commanded; 2 Corinthians 10:17); "far be it from me to boast except in the cross" (Galatians 6:14); "glory in Christ Jesus and put no confidence in the flesh" (Philippians 3:3); "I will boast… of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest" (2 Corinthians 12:9); "Let the lowly brother boast in his exaltation" (James 1:9, commanded); "we rejoice in God" (Romans 5:11); the seat here can be the conscience — "the testimony of our conscience" (2 Corinthians 1:12).

### 2c. Neutral band — Paul's measured apostolic self-reference
"boast only with regard to the area… God assigned to us" (2 Corinthians 10:13); "not… beyond limit" (2 Corinthians 10:15); proverbial observation (Proverbs 20:14).

## 3. Analysis (observation → interpretation)

**The discriminator is the object/ground, not the act.** The same verb, the same affect, points either to the flesh/self (sin) or to the Lord (righteousness). Moral status is wholly a function of the ground — which is why boasting can be both "evil" (James 4:16) and "commanded" (1 Corinthians 1:31). **This is the theological centre of M08:** boasting per se is not condemned; *misplaced* boasting is.

**The righteous pole inverts pride's logic.** "I will boast… of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest upon me" (2 Corinthians 12:9). The legitimate boast glories not in strength but in weakness, displaying God's power rather than the self's. This is the precise antithesis of A (self-exaltation): instead of lifting the self, one lowers the self to exalt God. D's righteous pole is the **redemptive counter-movement** to A and B.

**Boasting reveals where trust is placed.** The sinful boast is bound to reliance — "those who trust in their wealth and boast of their riches" (Psalm 49:6); "trusted in her treasures… boast of your valleys" (Jeremiah 49:4); "rely on the law and boast in God" (Romans 2:17). **Interpretation:** what one boasts in externalises what one trusts; D is diagnostic of the heart's confidence.

**Seat tracks the object.** Unlike A/B (heart-dominant), D's seat varies with its ground — flesh for the fleshly boast (Galatians 6:13; 1 Corinthians 1:29), soul for "boasts of the desires of his soul" (Psalm 10:3), conscience for the godly boast (2 Corinthians 1:12), and the contrast "what is in the heart" vs "outward appearance" (2 Corinthians 5:12).

## 4. Synthesis

Boasting is the heart's confidence made audible — the inner state declaring its ground before an audience (before God, before the churches, before the Lord at his coming). Uniquely in M08 it is morally bivalent: boasting in the flesh, in works, in riches, in the self is condemned, while boasting in the Lord, in the cross, in one's own weakness is not merely allowed but commanded. The righteous pole inverts the whole cluster's logic — glorying in weakness so that God's power is displayed — and so stands as the redemptive answer to self-exaltation (A) and settled pride (B). What a person boasts in reveals what a person trusts.

## 5. Expected but absent — special attention

1. **The affect IS captured here — a structural finding.** D alone carries a consistent `affect` tag. The expected datum (boasting is the heart's exultation, not mere speech) is present, and the contrast — D affective; A/B/C disposition/behaviour — tells us the cluster's inner state finds its *felt* expression precisely in boasting.
2. **POSSIBLE CORPUS GAP — OT righteous-boasting verses look thin (verify with CC).** In this extract, OT ha.lal is almost entirely the sinful/forbidden pole. Yet the OT contains the righteous boast — most pointedly **Jeremiah 9:24** ("let him who boasts boast in this, that he knows me"), the very next verse to the 9:23 prohibition that *is* in the corpus; also Psalm 34:2 ("my soul makes its boast in the Lord"); Psalm 44:8. These do not appear in the M08 focus set. **This is an expected element that may be missing — not a field-silence but a possible verse-coverage gap.** → recommend CC verify whether Jeremiah 9:24; Psalm 34:2; Psalm 44:8 (and similar) are tagged to M08, set aside, or owned elsewhere. If genuinely absent, the OT righteous pole is under-covered.
3. **Cross-testament shape (real).** Even allowing for (2), the *developed* righteous boast ("boast in the Lord / in weakness / in the cross") is overwhelmingly Pauline. This looks like a genuine cross-testament development (the phase-2 CROSS_TESTAMENT_SHIFT signal), worth recording — pending the (2) check so the shift is not overstated.
4. **Trust/audience dimensions are verse-readable but field-silent.** The boast↔trust link and the "before whom" audience are clear in the text but have no dedicated field. → recoverable findings, noted.

## 6. Reflection (labelled — not a conclusion)

- D's "boast in weakness" is theologically and pastorally rich; held descriptively.
- **Cross-cultural:** in honour-shame cultures, boasting/honour-display is socially central; the redirection ("boast in the Lord, not the self") reframes honour as *derived*, not achieved — significant for honour-culture readers. → flag for reader-facing.
- The boast↔trust diagnostic is a candidate for the synthesis; the OT-righteous-pole coverage question (§5.2) needs a CC check before the cross-testament claim is finalised.

## 7. Coverage

69 occurrences placed across the sinful/forbidden pole, the righteous/commanded pole, and the neutral apostolic band — all retained as one characteristic with two poles (researcher decision). **Open coverage flag:** possible missing OT righteous-boasting verses (Jeremiah 9:24; Psalm 34:2; Psalm 44:8) for CC verification. Nothing dropped.

# WA — M08 · Characteristic E (Conceit / Puffed-Up): Tier-Catalogue Findings

**File:** wa-m08-e-tier-answers-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Prior output reference:** wa-m08-e-conceit-v1_0-20260621.md; WA-tier-catalogue-current-state-v2-20260619.md.
**Source data:** 13 occurrences read individually (fusioō, tufoō, fusiōsis, huperfroneō, hupsēlofroneō).
**Method:** as the A template. **Standing note:** E's governing image is **inflation** (the bellows, fusioō; the befogging smoke, tufoō) rather than A's elevation. It is a NT, predominantly Corinthian characteristic, located in **cognition**, and its named antithesis is not humility but **love**.

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**T0.1.1** — God is not the bearer; E is the self **inflated against** true knowledge — "this puffed-up… by his sensuous mind" (Colossians 2:18) stands over against holding fast to Christ the Head. God appears as the standard the conceited mind has lost. **SILENT [data-silence]** on any direct divine predication.

**T0.1.2** — Never borne by God; exclusively creaturely. The pattern shows E as a swelling of the self that displaces dependence on God.

**T0.2.1** — It leads the person to look down on others and to divide the community ("puffed up in favor of one against another", 1 Corinthians 4:6).

**T0.2.2** — Fallen condition.

**T0.2.3** — None.

**T0.3.1** — None.

**T0.3.2** — Exclusively creaturely.

**T0.3.3** — Its presence shows the image swollen — a self enlarged beyond its measure.

**T0.4.1** — **SILENT [data-silence]**: no typological use.

*Coverage T0: 7 answered, 2 SILENT (T0.1.1 partial, T0.4.1).*

## T1 — Definition

**T1.1.1** — *Conceit/puffed-up*: the self **inflated** in its own estimation. The name signals swelling — empty enlargement, not solid height.

**T1.1.2** — fusioō ("to inflate, puff up", from fusa, bellows), fusiōsis ("a puffing up"), tufoō ("to wrap in smoke, befog, make conceited"), huperfroneō ("to think too highly"), hupsēlofroneō ("to be high-minded"). Definitionally, to be swollen in mind.

**T1.1.3** — An **inward swelling of the mind** that, unlike A, adds no real height — only volume.

**T1.2.1** — A **condition** of the mind (being puffed up) issuing in conduct.

**T1.2.2** — Compound: an inflated self-estimate + its source (knowledge without love) + its outward divisiveness.

**T1.3.1** — Its structural opposite, named in the text, is **love** — "Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up" (1 Corinthians 8:1).

**T1.3.2** — It excludes love, edification, and right self-measure ("not to think of himself more highly than he ought", Romans 12:3, the corrective register).

**T1.3.3** — E is not the elevation of A (real height claimed) nor the boast of D (declared object); it is the **empty swelling** of the mind — much volume, no substance ("puffed up without reason", Colossians 2:18).

**T1.4.1** — It operates as a cognitive state: "puffed up" (fusioō, 1 Corinthians 4:18; 5:2; 8:1) and "conceited" (tufoō, 1 Timothy 3:6; 6:4).

**T1.4.2** — It varies in occasion: puffed up by knowledge (1 Corinthians 8:1), by partisanship (1 Corinthians 4:6), by status (1 Timothy 3:6), by controversy (1 Timothy 6:4).

**T1.4.3** — **SILENT [data-silence]** on a distinct speech-mode (though it produces "envy, dissension, slander", 1 Timothy 6:4).

**T1.5.1** — Its immediate fruit is divisive comparison — "puffed up in favor of one against another" (1 Corinthians 4:6).

**T1.5.2** — Consistent: inflation expressed as the elevation of self over fellow-believers.

**T1.6.1** — It produces "envy, dissension, slander, evil suspicions" (1 Timothy 6:4) and resistance to correction (1 Corinthians 4:18).

**T1.6.3** — Immediate = the swollen comparison; sustained = the strife and unteachability it breeds.

**T1.7.1** — It takes hold where **knowledge runs ahead of love** (1 Corinthians 8:1) and where status comes too soon ("not a recent convert, or he may become puffed up", 1 Timothy 3:6). Never operates rightly [structural].

**T1.7.2** — Resisted by love that builds up (1 Corinthians 8:1) and by sober self-measure (Romans 12:3). On another spirit — *inferential:* the new convert "puffed up" may "fall into the condemnation of the devil" (1 Timothy 3:6).

**T1.7.3** — Where checked, the person holds knowledge under love and keeps a sober estimate of self.

*Coverage T1: 16 answered, 2 SILENT (T1.4.3; one partial).*

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**T2.1.1** — Seated in the **mind/cognition**: "puffed up without reason by his sensuous mind" (Colossians 2:18); the high-minded (hupsēlofroneō, Romans 11:20; 1 Timothy 6:17). The faculty is cognition.

**T2.1.2** — The pattern locates E firmly in the **mind** — it is the cluster's cognitive characteristic, as D is its affective one. No body link.

**T2.10.1** — **SILENT [data-silence]** on constitutional movement.

**T2.7.1** — **None** — no body link (E is mental).

**T2.9.1** — Within the mind, **occasioned by knowledge** ("knowledge puffs up", 1 Corinthians 8:1) and status (1 Timothy 3:6).

**T2.9.2** — Single (within-mind), with varied occasions (knowledge, status, controversy).

*Coverage T2: 5 answered, 1 SILENT (T2.10.1); T2.7.1 = none.*

## T3 — The Inner Faculties

**T3.1 Perception** — **SILENT [data-silence]**.

**T3.2 Cognition** — **T3.2.1** Centrally engaged — E *is* a disorder of cognition: "knowledge puffs up" (1 Corinthians 8:1); "puffed up… by his sensuous mind" (Colossians 2:18). **T3.2.2** It inflates the mind's self-estimate while emptying real understanding ("knowing nothing… craving controversy", 1 Timothy 6:4). **T3.2.3** E shows that knowledge **without love** turns cognition against the person — the faculty's signature disorder.

**T3.3 Memory** — **SILENT [data-silence]**.

**T3.4 Affect** — **SILENT [data-silence]** as a felt state; it *produces* hostile affect in others (envy, dissension — 1 Timothy 6:4) but is not itself seated in affect.

**T3.5 Creativity** — **SILENT [data-silence]**.

**T3.6 Volition** — **T3.6.1** Engaged in resistance to correction — "some are puffed up, as though I were not coming" (1 Corinthians 4:18). **T3.6.2** It stiffens the will against admonition. **T3.6.3** E disposes the will to unteachability.

**T3.7 Agency** — **T3.7.1** Issues in divisive conduct (1 Corinthians 4:6; 5:2 — failing to act against sin while "arrogant"). **T3.7.2/3** Its agency is the community-dividing fruit of inflation.

**T3.8 Moral Evaluation** — **T3.8.1** Engaged: E distorts moral evaluation — the Corinthians were "arrogant" rather than grieved over sin (1 Corinthians 5:2). **T3.8.2** It misweights — self-importance crowding out moral seriousness. **T3.8.3** E corrupts the community's moral judgment.

**T3.9 Conscience** — **SILENT [data-silence]**.

**T3.10 Conscientiousness** — **T3.10.1** Engaged negatively — arrogance displaced the action conscience required (1 Corinthians 5:2). **T3.10.2/3** It undercuts integrated moral response.

**T3.11 Relational Capacity** — **T3.11.1** Engaged: E is **divisive** — "puffed up in favor of one against another" (1 Corinthians 4:6); breeds "dissension, slander" (1 Timothy 6:4). **T3.11.2** It fractures community where love would build it up (1 Corinthians 8:1). **T3.11.3** E's relational signature is **division**, and its cure is love that edifies.

*Coverage T3: ~18 answered; ~15 SILENT (perception, memory, affect, creativity, conscience — data-silence). E is narrowly cognitive-and-relational.*

## T4 — Relational Interfaces

**T4.1 Divine — God to Human** — **SILENT [structural]**.

**T4.6 Spiritual Beings** — **T4.6.1** *Inferential:* the puffed-up new convert risks "the condemnation of the devil" (1 Timothy 3:6) — a link to adversarial downfall. **T4.6.2** *Inferential:* E is a site where the adversary's own ruin is echoed. **T4.6.3 — SILENT [data-silence].**

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

**T5.1.1** — E reflects a mind already disordered; transformation is toward its correction (love that builds up, sober self-measure) rather than something E produces.

**T5.1.2** — **SILENT [data-silence]** on reversibility (the correction is urged, not narrated as accomplished).

**T5.4.2** — **SILENT [data-silence]**.

**T5.5.1** — Cautionary: the inflation that maturity and love must deflate; premature status feeds it (1 Timothy 3:6).

**T5.6.1** — **SILENT [data-silence]**.

*Coverage T5: ~3 answered, ~6 SILENT (data-silence). E's developmental content is genuinely thin — it is addressed by correction, not traced through states.*

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics

**T6.1.1** — Co-occurs with division/strife (1 Corinthians 4:6; 1 Timothy 6:4) and stands against **love** (1 Corinthians 8:1) and **humility/sober-mindedness** (Romans 12:3).

**T6.1.2** — E sits at the **cognitive** corner of the pride family, distinct from A's elevation and D's exultation.

**T6.2.2** — Causal: knowledge-without-love produces E.

**T6.3.2** — Produced by knowledge/status without love.

**T6.5.3** — The distinction is one of **kind** (solid elevation vs hollow inflation) within the cognitive register.

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**T7.1.1** — fusioō ("inflate, puff up", from fusa, bellows), fusiōsis ("a puffing up"), tufoō ("to befog with smoke → make conceited"), huperfroneō / hupsēlofroneō ("think too highly / be high-minded"). Roots: bellows-wind and smoke — **emptiness made to look like substance**.

**T7.1.2** — Verbs (fusioō, tufoō — the puffing/befogging) and the noun fusiōsis (the puffed-up state). The verb-dominance shows E as an ongoing inflation.

**T7.1.5** — Its named opposite is **love** (1 Corinthians 8:1) — uniquely, the structural opposite is given in the text, and it is love, not humility.

**T7.1.6** — Partial — "the conceited" (tetufōmenos, 1 Timothy 6:4; 2 Timothy 3:4) functions as a person-type.

**T7.1.7** — None.

**T7.1.8** — E has **no OT counterpart** — it is a NT (Pauline) characterisation; the bellows/smoke imagery is new, marking a development specific to the apostolic correction of the Corinthian mind.

**T7.1.9** — fusioō and tufoō are effectively the **NT's distinctive coinage-register** for this inner swelling — their vividness (bellows, smoke) marks a fresh naming of conceit.

**T7.1.10** — The arc is narrow and NT-bound: the inflation of a mind that has knowledge without love.

**T7.2.1** — In the anchor, fusioō carries the contrast of the whole sentence: "Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up" (1 Corinthians 8:1).

**T7.2.2** — Forms: epistle (1 Corinthians, Colossians, 1–2 Timothy). The pastoral-corrective argument requires reading E as a named fault under apostolic admonition.

**T7.2.3** — The key argument: knowledge inflates, love edifies; therefore knowledge must be governed by love (1 Corinthians 8:1).

**T7.2.4** — Settings: pastoral and ecclesial (community division, eldership qualification — 1 Timothy 3:6).

**T7.2.5** — Anchor: **1 Corinthians 8:1** — "Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up" — the verse that defines E and names its cure.

**T7.2.6** — 1 Corinthians 8:1 shows what no other verse does: E's root is **knowledge severed from love**, and its remedy is not less knowledge but love.

**T7.3.1** — *(science, M08 extract §2)* The cognitive component of narcissism (belief in one's superiority) is the most useful lens for E.

**T7.3.2** — *(science)* Narcissism research on the superiority-belief (extract §2) illuminates E's inflated self-estimate; the "knowledge puffs up" dynamic matches the cognitive-overconfidence findings.

**T7.3.3** — *(science)* Science treats overconfidence as a cognitive bias; the biblical material frames E as a **moral** disorder cured by love, not merely a calibration error (extract T7.3.3).

**T7.3.4** — *(science)* Science does not pair conceit with **love** as its corrective; the verse evidence's antithesis (knowledge vs love) is an aspect the framework does not supply — no further verse gap, but a point where the text leads the science.

No question unanswered. E is a **narrowly cognitive** characteristic: it answers cognition, moral evaluation, relational division, and the full lexical/literary tiers richly, but is genuinely silent across perception, memory, affect, creativity, conscience, most of T4, and most of T5. Its lower coverage is not a gap in the reading but the true measure of a small, NT-bound, mind-located fault — and its one striking distinctive is that its named opposite is **love** (T1.3.1, T7.1.5), not humility.

# WA — M08 · Characteristic E: Conceit / Being Puffed-Up (inflated self-estimation)

**File:** wa-m08-e-conceit-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Prior output reference:** wa-m08-a-self-exaltation-v1_0-20260621.md (template); wa-m08-prov-char-list-v1_1-20260621.md.
**Source data:** wa-ve-lexical-extract-M08-20260621-b1of2/b2of2.json (extract v1_0, 2026-06-21).
**Method:** every focus occurrence read individually with full fields. Analysis derived from verses (§A2). Quotes ≤15 words.

---

## 1. Definition (working)

Pride as **inflation** — the mind's empty swelling, an over-rating of the self grounded in knowledge, standing, or wealth that has no real substance behind it. Where A *elevates* the self (height), E *inflates* it (air).

## 2. Evidence base

**13 occurrences**, almost entirely NT and Corinthian-concentrated: fusioō (G5448, 7 — all in 1 Corinthians / Colossians), tufoō (G5187, 3), fusiōsis (G5450, 1), huperfroneō (G5252, 1), hupsēlofroneō (G5309, 1). hupsēlos (G5308) is treated under A.

## 3. Analysis (observation → interpretation)

**The image is inflation, not elevation.** fusioō (to puff up, from the bellows) and tufoō (to be wrapped in smoke/vapour) present pride as empty swelling: "puffed up without reason by his sensuous mind" (Colossians 2:18); "puffed up with conceit and understands nothing" (1 Timothy 6:4); "swollen with conceit" (2 Timothy 3:4). This distinguishes E from A: A raises the self to a height; E fills it with air.

**Its characteristic cause is knowledge.** "This 'knowledge' puffs up, but love builds up" (1 Corinthians 8:1). Conceit inflates over what one knows or one's spiritual standing — the besetting danger of the recent convert (1 Timothy 3:6) and the rich (1 Timothy 6:17).

**Its antithesis is love, not (primarily) humility.** Where B defines itself against humility, E defines itself against love: "knowledge puffs up, but **love** builds up" (1 Corinthians 8:1); "**love**… is not arrogant" (1 Corinthians 13:4). The contrast is build-up vs puff-up — substance vs air.

**It is cognitive and divisive.** The faculty tags are cognition (huperfroneō, hupsēlofroneō): "not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think" (Romans 12:3). And it breeds faction: "puffed up in favour of one against another" (1 Corinthians 4:6); listed with "quarrelling… conceit, and disorder" (2 Corinthians 12:20).

**Interpretation.** E is the cognitive register of pride — the self over-estimated in the mind, hollow at the centre, and socially corrosive. It is the form pride takes around knowledge and new standing, answered not by being told to lower oneself (A's correction) but by love that builds the other up.

## 4. Synthesis

Conceit is pride as empty inflation: the mind swollen with an over-estimate of itself, grounded in knowledge, office, or wealth but hollow at the core ("puffed up… understands nothing"). Its imagery is the bellows and the smoke; its seat is the mind; its cause is knowledge; its antithesis is the love that builds others up rather than the self. It is the besetting pride of the newly-advanced and a seedbed of faction — the cognitive, NT-developed register of the cluster.

## 5. Expected but absent — special attention

1. **Cause is present and specific (unlike A/B).** E names its elicitor — "knowledge puffs up" (1 Corinthians 8:1). A genuine datum present; E is the best-caused characteristic in the cluster.
2. **Faculty under-tagged on the core terms.** The cognition tag sits on huperfroneō/hupsēlofroneō, but the inflation core (fusioō, tufoō) carries **no** faculty tag despite being plainly mental. → minor flag: recommend CC review whether fusioō/tufoō should carry a cognition (or affect) faculty.
3. **No OT membership — a cross-testament finding, not a gap.** E is essentially absent from the OT; the OT renders pride as height/loftiness (A/B), not inflation. This looks like a genuine NT development of the pride vocabulary (the inflation metaphor), not a coverage hole — the OT simply uses different imagery. → record as a cross-testament register-shift (consistent with D's §5.3), distinct from D's *possible* coverage gap.
4. **Antithesis differs from B's.** E's opposite is love; B's is humility. The two counter-poles (love / humility) are worth carrying to the synthesis as distinct correctives.

## 6. Reflection (labelled — not a conclusion)

- E's "knowledge puffs up, but love builds up" has obvious bearing on intellectual and spiritual life; held descriptively.
- **Cross-cultural:** the knowledge/status inflation E targets is recognisable across cultures, but its framing as a *Corinthian* church problem (spiritual-gift and knowledge rivalry) is community-specific. → flag for reader-facing.
- The love/humility split between E and B is a candidate observation for the cluster synthesis.

## 7. Coverage

13 occurrences placed; all NT. hupsēlos (G5308) held under A (height image). No occurrences dropped. Cross-testament register-shift recorded (§5.3).

# WA — M08 · Characteristic F (Self-Love / Self-Sufficiency): Tier-Catalogue Findings

**File:** wa-m08-f-tier-answers-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Prior output reference:** wa-m08-f-self-love-v1_0-20260621.md; WA-tier-catalogue-current-state-v2-20260619.md.
**Source data:** direct base of 2 occurrences (filautos, 2 Timothy 3:2; a.din, Isaiah 47:8) read individually; the self-sufficiency register of Isaiah 47 read in full as F's anchor.
**Method:** as the A template. **Standing note:** F has the **thinnest direct lexical base** in the cluster. Its significance is **structural** — it is the *terminus* the other characteristics converge on: the self made its own god ("I am, and there is no one besides me", Isaiah 47:8, 10). Genuine silences are frequent and are recorded as such, not padded; F's content is real but small, and several tiers are answered chiefly from its anchor.

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design

**T0.1.1** — God is **displaced** — F is the self seizing God's own self-predication: "I am, and there is no one besides me" (Isaiah 47:8, 10), the very words God reserves for himself ("I am, and there is no other", Isaiah 45:5–6). F is never borne by God; it is the creature speaking as if it were God.

**T0.1.2** — Never borne by God; exclusively creaturely — and it is the **most direct usurpation** of the divine in the cluster: not merely lifting toward God's place (A) but occupying it in speech.

**T0.2.1** — It leads the person to a false security ("I shall not sit as a widow", Isaiah 47:8) and to being unloving toward others ("lovers of self… unloving, unforgiving", 2 Timothy 3:2–3).

**T0.2.2** — Fallen condition.

**T0.2.3** — None.

**T0.3.1** — None — F is the **counter-image**: the self in God's place rather than the image reflecting God.

**T0.3.2** — Exclusively creaturely.

**T0.3.3** — Its presence shows the image at its furthest disorder — the creature treating itself as ultimate.

**T0.4.1** — *Inferential:* Isaiah 47's self-sufficient Babylon ("I am, none besides me") reads typologically of every power that deifies itself; otherwise [data-silence].

*Coverage T0: 8 answered, 1 inferential (T0.4.1).*

## T1 — Definition

**T1.1.1** — *Self-love/self-sufficiency*: the self turned ultimately on itself as both object of love and ground of security. The name signals the **terminus** of pride — the self as its own end.

**T1.1.2** — filautos ("self-loving", phil- + autos), a.din ("luxuriant, given to pleasure, self-secure"). The two terms name the two faces: self-**love** (filautos) and self-**sufficiency/ease** (a.din).

**T1.1.3** — An **inward curvature** — love and trust bent back on the self rather than directed to God and neighbour.

**T1.2.1** — A **disposition/condition** (a settled orientation of love and confidence), not an act.

**T1.2.2** — Compound: self-directed love + self-grounded security — the affective and the volitional curved inward together.

**T1.3.1** — Its structural opposite is **love of God and neighbour** ("you shall love the Lord… and your neighbour"); F is "lovers of self" set against "lovers of God" (2 Timothy 3:2, 4).

**T1.3.2** — It excludes dependence on God and regard for others ("unloving, unforgiving, slanderous", 2 Timothy 3:3).

**T1.3.3** — F is not the act of lifting (A), the height (B), the defiance (C1), the contempt (C2), the boast (D), or the inflation (E); it is the **settled self-orientation** those movements terminate in.

**T1.4.1** — It operates as a settled self-predication — "you said in your heart, 'I am, and there is no one besides me'" (Isaiah 47:10) — and as a list-named character trait ("lovers of self", 2 Timothy 3:2).

**T1.4.2** — It varies between corporate self-sufficiency (Babylon, Isaiah 47) and individual self-love (the last-days character list, 2 Timothy 3:2).

**T1.4.3** — Yes — it speaks the self-sufficient claim "in the heart" (Isaiah 47:8, 10).

**T1.5.1** — Its immediate correlate is **false security** — "I shall not sit as a widow or know the loss of children" (Isaiah 47:8).

**T1.5.2** — Consistent: a settled, complacent self-confidence.

**T1.6.1** — It establishes complacent security and a love-disordered character (2 Timothy 3:2–4); it sets up **sudden ruin** ("these two things shall come to you in a moment", Isaiah 47:9).

**T1.6.3** — Immediate = the complacent self-assurance; sustained = the love turned inward and the ruin it invites.

**T1.7.1** — It takes hold in unchecked prosperity and power ("you felt secure in your wickedness", Isaiah 47:10). Never operates rightly [structural].

**T1.7.2** — Resisted by the love of God and neighbour that decentres the self (2 Timothy 3:2–4 by antithesis). On another spirit — **SILENT [data-silence]**.

**T1.7.3** — Where checked, love is directed to God and others rather than the self.

*Coverage T1: 18 of 18 (answered chiefly from the two terms and the Isaiah 47 anchor).*

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries

**T2.1.1** — Seated in the **heart**: "you said in your heart, 'I am…'" (Isaiah 47:10) — the heart's settled self-predication; and in the **love-faculty** (filautos — love bent on the self).

**T2.1.2** — F is a **whole-self orientation** seated in the heart's loves and securities — not a discrete faculty but the direction of the person.

**T2.10.1** — **SILENT [data-silence]** on constitutional movement.

**T2.7.1** — **None** — no body link.

**T2.9.1** — Within the person, **occasioned by prosperity/power** ("you felt secure in your wickedness", Isaiah 47:10).

**T2.9.2** — Single (within-person).

*Coverage T2: 5 answered, 1 SILENT (T2.10.1); T2.7.1 none.*

## T3 — The Inner Faculties

**T3.1 Perception** — **T3.1.1** *Inferential:* F is blind to its own exposure — "no one sees me" (Isaiah 47:10) — a failure of perception. Otherwise **SILENT [data-silence]**.

**T3.2 Cognition** — **T3.2.1** Engaged in a false self-knowledge — "you said in your heart, 'I am, and there is no one besides me'" (Isaiah 47:8, 10): a settled (mis)judgment about the self's ultimacy. **T3.2.2** It fixes a self-estimate that denies dependence and exposure. **T3.2.3** F's cognition is the self's verdict that it is its own ground.

**T3.3 Memory** — **SILENT [data-silence]**.

**T3.4 Affect** — **T3.4.1** Engaged by definition: **self-love** is the affective faculty bent on the self (filautos, 2 Timothy 3:2); the complacent ease of a.din carries a settled self-satisfied affect. **T3.4.2** It directs love inward, away from God and neighbour. **T3.4.3** F is love mis-aimed — the affect-faculty's deepest disorder.

**T3.5 Creativity** — **SILENT [data-silence]**.

**T3.6 Volition** — **T3.6.1** *Inferential:* the self-secure stance is a settled choice of self-reliance (Isaiah 47:10). Otherwise lightly evidenced. **T3.6.2/3 — partial SILENT [data-silence].**

**T3.7 Agency** — **SILENT [data-silence]** as direct evidence (Isaiah 47's wickedness and sorceries are context, not F's own act). [data-silence]

**T3.8 Moral Evaluation** — **T3.8.1** Engaged: F inverts evaluation — the self-loving are listed among the last-days evils (2 Timothy 3:2–4), and Babylon "felt secure in [its] wickedness" (Isaiah 47:10), calling evil safety. **T3.8.2** It silences moral self-assessment. **T3.8.3** F is the moral blindness of the self that has made itself ultimate.

**T3.9 Conscience** — **SILENT [data-silence]**; *inferential:* "no one sees me" (Isaiah 47:10) implies a conscience that reckons with no witness.

**T3.10 Conscientiousness** — **SILENT [data-silence]**.

**T3.11 Relational Capacity** — **T3.11.1** Engaged: F is **anti-relational** — "lovers of self… unloving, unforgiving, slanderous… not loving good" (2 Timothy 3:2–3): love turned inward severs love of others. **T3.11.2** It dissolves the bonds love would sustain. **T3.11.3** F shows that self-love is the **collapse** of relational capacity — the terminus where pride ends in isolation.

*Coverage T3: ~12 answered (several inferential); ~21 SILENT (perception partial, memory, creativity, agency, conscience, conscientiousness, volition partial — data-silence). F's faculty engagement is genuinely sparse; its real content is at affect (self-love), cognition (self-as-ground), and relational capacity (its collapse).*

## T4 — Relational Interfaces

**T4.1 Divine — God to Human** — **SILENT [structural]**.

**T4.2 Divine — Human to God** — **T4.2.1** F's God-ward register is **usurpation**: the self takes God's own words ("I am, and there is no one besides me", Isaiah 47:8). **T4.2.2** It is the inverse of worship — the self enthroned where God belongs. **T4.2.3** It shows a relationship in which God is denied any place ("lovers of self rather than lovers of God", 2 Timothy 3:4).

**T4.3 Human — Giving** — **SILENT [structural]**.

**T4.4 Human — Receiving** — **SILENT [structural]**.

**T4.5 Human — Boundaries** — **T4.5.1** F severs relational bonds altogether ("unloving, unforgiving", 2 Timothy 3:3) — its effect crosses every relational line by withdrawing love from all but the self. **T4.5.2/3** Its scope is total self-reference; others fall outside its love by definition.

**T4.6 Spiritual Beings** — **SILENT [data-silence]** (T4.6.1–3).

*Coverage T4: ~5 answered, ~13 SILENT (T4.1, T4.3, T4.4 structural; T4.6 data). F substantively answers only the God-ward (usurpation) and boundary (severance) registers.*

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension

**T5.1.1** — F reflects a self already turned inward; the relevant change is its **ruin** — "evil shall come upon you… ruin shall come upon you suddenly" (Isaiah 47:11).

**T5.1.2** — The ruin is **sudden and decisive** — "in a moment, in one day" (Isaiah 47:9).

**T5.2.1** — Sequence: prosperous security → self-deification ("I am, none besides me") → sudden ruin (Isaiah 47:8–9, 11).

**T5.3.1** — Mechanism: **sudden divine judgment** breaking the false security (Isaiah 47:9, 11).

**T5.3.2** — **SILENT [data-silence]** on contextual variation.

**T5.4.1** — F is the **opposite** of affliction's posture — it presumes immunity from loss ("I shall not… know the loss of children", Isaiah 47:8); affliction is precisely what it denies and what overtakes it.

**T5.4.2** — Suffering exposes F's emptiness — the widowhood and loss it denied come upon it (Isaiah 47:9).

**T5.5.1** — Cautionary: the terminal self-orientation that formation in the love of God and neighbour exists to prevent (2 Timothy 3:2–4).

**T5.6.1** — **SILENT [data-silence]** (no positive eschatological orientation; only judgment).

*Coverage T5: ~7 answered, ~2 SILENT (T5.3.2, T5.6.1).*

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics

**T6.1.1** — In 2 Timothy 3:2 F **heads a vice-list** alongside lovers-of-money, boastful (alazōn), arrogant (huperēfanos) — co-occurring with D and B at the root of the last-days character.

**T6.1.2** — F sits at the **terminus** of the pride family — the self-orientation the others move toward.

**T6.2.1** — F **follows** the whole cluster: A's "like the Most High" and B's settled height arrive, in F, at "I am, none besides me."

**T6.2.2** — Developmental/teleological — F is where the cluster's trajectory ends.

**T6.3.1** — Produces the collapse of love for God and neighbour (2 Timothy 3:2–4) and invites sudden ruin (Isaiah 47:11).

**T6.3.2** — Produced by the cluster's whole movement (A–E converging on self-ultimacy).

**T6.3.3** — F is the **constitutive end-state** of pride — the others are constituents of the orientation F names.

**T6.4.1** — In its vice-list F shares the field with alazōn (D) and huperēfanos (B) — vocabulary co-located but distinct (filautos is its own term).

**T6.4.2** — No shared root with the height-family; F's distinctiveness is lexical as well as structural.

**T6.4.3** — The co-listing (2 Timothy 3:2) shows F as the **summative** member of the pride vices rather than a root-sharer.

**T6.5.1** — Nearest neighbour: **A** — both reach toward God's place; distinguished because A *ascends toward* it ("like the Most High") while F *occupies* it in speech ("I am, none besides me").

**T6.5.2** — The boundary with A is aspiration (A) versus arrival/settled claim (F).

**T6.5.3** — The distinction is one of **completion** — F is A's logic carried to its end (a difference of terminus, not of level).

*Coverage T6: 13 of 13.*

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation

**T7.1.1** — filautos ("self-loving", phil-autos), a.din ("luxuriant, voluptuous, self-secure"). Roots: *loving the self* and *settled in ease* — affect and security both turned inward.

**T7.1.2** — Adjectives — filautos ("self-loving", a person-type) and a.din ("given to ease"). The adjectival form names a **character**, not an act.

**T7.1.3** — Semantic range: from "self-loving" (the disordered love) to "luxuriant/secure" (the complacent ease) — narrow but pointed.

**T7.1.4** — Yes — filautos (the disposition of self-love) and a.din (the condition of self-secure ease) name the two faces.

**T7.1.5** — Its opposite is named in context: **lovers of God** versus "lovers of self" (2 Timothy 3:2, 4); love of neighbour.

**T7.1.6** — Yes — filautos *is* the person-type ("lovers of self").

**T7.1.7** — None.

**T7.1.8** — F's OT register (a.din, self-secure ease — Isaiah 47) and its NT register (filautos, self-love — 2 Timothy 3:2) are **not lexically continuous** but are conceptually one — the self made ultimate; a thematic, not verbal, continuity.

**T7.1.9** — filautos is effectively a **NT naming** of self-love as a character vice — a fresh lexicalisation of the cluster's terminus.

**T7.1.10** — The arc is short but decisive: from self-secure ease (Isaiah 47) to self-love heading the last-days vice-list (2 Timothy 3:2) — the self as its own god and its own beloved.

**T7.2.1** — In the anchor, a.din/the "I am" claim carries Babylon's whole self-deifying boast: "you said in your heart, 'I am, and there is no one besides me'" (Isaiah 47:10).

**T7.2.2** — Forms: prophecy (the taunt-oracle against Babylon, Isaiah 47) and epistle (the vice-list, 2 Timothy 3). The taunt-oracle requires reading the "I am" as the usurpation of God's self-naming.

**T7.2.3** — The argument (Isaiah 47): the self that claims "I am, none besides me" will meet, suddenly, the very losses it denied — self-sufficiency invites ruin.

**T7.2.4** — Settings: judicial/eschatological (the oracle of Babylon's fall) and ethical (the last-days character description).

**T7.2.5** — Anchor: **Isaiah 47:8, 10** — "I am, and there is no one besides me" — F's essence as the creature usurping God's self-predication.

**T7.2.6** — Isaiah 47:8–10 shows what no other verse in the cluster shows: pride's terminus is **practical self-deification** — the self speaking the words that belong to God alone.

**T7.3.1** — *(science, M08 extract §2/§4)* Narcissism (self-love as trait) and self-enhancement research are the most useful lenses for F.

**T7.3.2** — *(science)* The self-enhancement bias (extract §4) and trait-narcissism (extract §2) illuminate F's settled self-reference and false self-sufficiency.

**T7.3.3** — *(science)* Science frames self-love on a spectrum (healthy self-regard to pathological narcissism); the biblical material frames F as **idolatry of the self** — the creature claiming God's "I am" — a register science does not reach (extract T7.3.3; the theological distinctive).

**T7.3.4** — *(science)* Science cannot supply the category F's anchor requires — the **self usurping divine self-predication**; this is the cluster's clearest outside-science edge, already flagged in the extract's outside-science inventory (the ontological majesty of God).

*Coverage T7: 20 of 20.*

No question unanswered. F's coverage is the cluster's lowest by faculty engagement — **honestly so**: a 2-occurrence direct base cannot carry perception, memory, creativity, agency, or conscience evidence, and these are recorded as genuine data-silences rather than inferred. But F answers the tiers that matter to it with unusual force: **T0** (the self usurping God's "I am"), **T3.4** (self-love as the affect-faculty's deepest disorder), **T3.11** (the collapse of relational capacity), **T6** (F as the cluster's terminus), and **T7.2** (the anchor Isaiah 47:8–10). F is best understood, and is here documented, as the **vanishing-point** the whole cluster moves toward — small in lexical base, decisive in structural meaning.

# WA — M08 · Characteristic F: Self-Love / Self-Sufficiency (the self as its own centre and god)

**File:** wa-m08-f-self-love-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Prior output reference:** wa-m08-a-self-exaltation-v1_0-20260621.md (template); wa-m08-prov-char-list-v1_1-20260621.md.
**Source data:** wa-ve-lexical-extract-M08-20260621-b1of2/b2of2.json (extract v1_0, 2026-06-21).
**Method:** every focus occurrence read individually; cross-listed thematic evidence traced to its owning lemmas. Analysis derived from verses (§A2). Quotes ≤15 words. **Honest note up front:** F's *direct* lexical base is thin (2 occurrences); its substance is carried largely as the terminus the other characteristics converge on. This is recorded transparently, not padded (§A4).

---

## 1. Definition (working)

Pride turned fully inward and upward at once — the **self made its own centre and, at the limit, its own god**. The displacement of God by the self.

## 2. Evidence base

**Direct: 2 occurrences.**
- filautos (G5367, 1) — "people will be **lovers of self**, lovers of money, proud, arrogant…" (2 Timothy 3:2). Heads the catalogue of the last days.
- a.din (H5719, 1) — "you say in your heart, '**I am, and there is no one besides me**'" (Isaiah 47:8, seated in heart).

**Cross-listed thematic support (owned by other characteristics, traced here):**
- "Your heart is proud, and you have said, '**I am a god**'" (Ezekiel 28:2 — ga.vah, A).
- "He shall **exalt himself**… above every god" (Daniel 11:36 — rum, A).
- "In the pride of his face the wicked… '**There is no God**'" (Psalm 10:4 — go.vah, B).
- "the **pride of life**… is not from the Father" (1 John 2:16 — alazoneia, D).
- self-will: "**self-willed**" (Titus 1:7; 2 Peter 2:10 — authadēs, C1).

## 3. Analysis (observation → interpretation)

**F is the terminus, not a dense word-group.** Named directly only twice, its substance appears as the endpoint toward which the other characteristics run: the self-exalting heart (A) that ascends "above the stars"; the settled pride (B) whose face says "There is no God"; the defiant will (C1) that refuses all authority. Each, pressed to its limit, arrives at the self enthroned in God's place.

**Its speech is the usurped divine "I am."** "I am, and there is no one besides me" (Isaiah 47:8) takes onto the lips of Babylon the self-predication that belongs to God alone ("I am… besides me there is no god," Isaiah 45). Pride here is not merely high but **idolatrous of the self** — practical atheism in its negative face ("There is no God," Psalm 10:4) and self-deification in its positive face ("I am a god," Ezekiel 28:2).

**Its root word is mis-directed love.** filautos = self-*love*: the catalogue of 2 Timothy 3 opens with disordered love (lovers of self, lovers of money, lovers of pleasure "rather than lovers of God," v4). The disorder is one of love's object — the self loved where God should be.

**Interpretation.** F is the cluster's vanishing point: where A/B/C/E are facets of pride, F is what pride finally *is* when complete — the self in the place of God. Its thin direct lexicalisation reflects that it is more a terminus than a discrete state.

## 4. Synthesis

Self-love is pride turned fully inward and upward: the self made its own centre and its own god. Directly it is named only twice — the "lover of self" heading the catalogue of the last days, and the "lover of pleasures" who says in her heart "I am, and there is no one besides me" — but it is the logical end toward which the cluster runs. Its speech usurps the divine "I am"; its negative face is the practical atheism of the proud ("There is no God"); its essence is the displacement of God by the self, the disorder of a love that rests finally on itself.

## 5. Expected but absent — special attention

1. **Thin direct base is the finding.** filautos is a NT hapax; a.din a single OT occurrence. F's weight rests on cross-listed self-deification speech under other lemmas. → F is best understood as the **convergent terminus** of A/B/C rather than a densely-lexicalised characteristic. Its standalone status (researcher decision, fork 4) is honoured; the thinness is recorded for the synthesis to weigh.
2. **POSSIBLE CORPUS GAP — the self-trust / self-sufficiency register (verify).** One would expect a "self-love/self-sufficiency" characteristic to include *trusting in oneself rather than God*. This is present **thematically** — "you sit securely" (Isaiah 47:8); "those who trust in their wealth" (Psalm 49:6); "trusted in her treasures" (Jeremiah 49:4) — but those occurrences are owned by other lemmas/characteristics (B, D), and there is little dedicated self-trust vocabulary in the M08 focus set. → **flag for researcher/CC:** does M08 intend to capture the self-trust/self-reliance register, or is "trust" owned by a separate cluster? If the former, F is under-populated and additional terms may need tagging.
3. **No faculty tag; heart-seated (Isaiah 47:8).** filautos = self-*love* implies an affective/volitional core (mis-directed love), but the lexical carries no faculty tag. → note: an affect/volition pass might give F the interior the field currently omits.

## 6. Reflection (labelled — not a conclusion)

- F's "I am, and there is no one besides me" — pride usurping the divine self-predication — is theologically the sharpest point of the whole cluster; held descriptively.
- **Cross-cultural:** "self as centre" reads very differently in individualist vs collectivist frames; the 2 Timothy 3 "lovers of self" list is a portrait of communal breakdown, not merely personal vice. → flag for reader-facing.
- F's status (standalone characteristic vs convergent terminus) is worth revisiting at the cluster synthesis given its thin direct base; per the researcher's decision it stands separate, and the thinness is recorded honestly for that judgement.

## 7. Coverage

2 direct occurrences placed (filautos, a.din), with cross-listed self-deification evidence traced to its owning characteristics (A, B, C1, D) rather than re-counted. Open coverage flag: the self-trust/self-sufficiency register may be under-populated in M08 (§5.2) — for researcher/CC verification. Nothing dropped.
