# WA M09 — Characteristic A: Self-humbling before God — Tier Findings

**File:** wa-m09-char-a-tier-findings-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Cluster:** M09 — *Humility, Meekness and Submission* · **Characteristic:** A — Self-humbling before God
**Catalogue:** WA-tier-catalogue v2 (126 questions, T0–T7) · **Evidence base:** `wa-m09-char-a-evidence-v1_0-20260621.md` (23 occurrences)
**Source verses:** Lev 26:41; 1Ki 21:29; 2Ki 22:19; 2Ch 7:14, 12:6, 12:7, 12:12, 30:11, 32:26, 33:12, 33:19, 33:23, 34:27, 36:12; Mic 6:8; Mat 18:4; Mat 23:12; Luk 14:11; Luk 18:14; 2Cor 11:7; Phil 2:8; Jam 4:10; 1Pe 5:6.
**Method:** answers authored by verse-reading; Silent classified (structural / data / recoverable→resolved); inferential labelled; science confined to T7.3. **This file is the locked template for B–H.**

---

## T0 — Divine Image and Created Design  *(coverage 9/9)*
- **T0.1.1** — God is the **object/terminus and responsive agent** of the act: it is done "before the Lord / before me / before God / with your God" (1Ki 21:29; 2Ki 22:19; 2Ch 33:12 divine-role=object; Mic 6:8), and God responds — relenting wrath or exalting (Jam 4:10 God=agent "he will exalt"; 1Pe 5:6).
- **T0.1.2** — Never borne by God as God; it is the **creature's act toward God** — with the unique exception of the **incarnate Son** (Phil 2:8 "being found in human form he humbled himself"). So it belongs to right creaturely relation, yet is christologically grounded.
- **T0.2.1** — Stated effects: averts/defers wrath (2Ch 12:7, 12; 32:26), brings forgiveness and healing (2Ch 7:14), and precedes exaltation (Mat 23:12; 1Pe 5:6). Role: it turns the person from sin to mercy.
- **T0.2.2** — **Both.** Its necessity answers the fallen condition (it confronts "the pride of his heart", 2Ch 32:26) while it images the right created posture of creature before Creator.
- **T0.2.3** — **Yes** — oriented to future exaltation: "whoever humbles himself will be exalted" (Mat 23:12; Luk 14:11; 18:14); "at the proper time he may exalt you" (1Pe 5:6).
- **T0.3.1** — Via Phil 2:8 it instantiates the **Christ-pattern of self-emptying condescension**; otherwise it instantiates the creature's acknowledgement of God's exclusive height.
- **T0.3.2** — **Exclusively creaturely** (the creature lowering before God), patterned christologically in the incarnate Son — not a mirrored divine attribute.
- **T0.3.3** — Absence marks the hardened/proud image (2Ch 36:12 Zedekiah "did not humble himself"; 33:23 Amon vs Manasseh); presence marks the turning/restored image.
- **T0.4.1** — Typological in two directions: **christological** (Phil 2:8 — the divine instance establishing the pattern) and **covenantal** (2Ch 7:14 — the human movement toward God under covenant promise).

## T1 — Definition  *(coverage 17/18; 1 silent)*
- **T1.1.1** — Named "self-humbling before God": a **reflexive act** (humble *oneself*) with a **God-ward terminus**.
- **T1.1.2** — *ka.na* (Heb: bow/subdue/be low), *tapeinoō* (Grk: make low), *tsa.na* (Heb: be modest/walk humbly) — a verb of lowering used reflexively for voluntary self-abasement before God.
- **T1.1.3** — Carries a **directional** (downward, God-ward), **relational** (before God), and **constitutional** (heart-seated) implication.
- **T1.2.1** — **An act** (volitional action) — action-type throughout (the reflexive/chosen lowering).
- **T1.2.2** — **Compound**: volition (choosing to lower) + affect/contrition (penitence, weeping) + relational orientation (before God), often bundled with prayer/seeking (2Ch 7:14 "humble… pray and seek").
- **T1.3.1** — Structural opposite: **pride / self-exaltation** ("whoever exalts himself", Mat 23:12; "pride of his heart", 2Ch 32:26).
- **T1.3.2** — Resists self-exaltation, presumption, and hardness of heart.
- **T1.3.3** — It is **not** an imposed lowering of estate (that is C) nor the settled trait (that is B); it ends where the lowering ceases to be chosen.
- **T1.4.1** — Modes: reflexive verb; **imperative** ("Humble yourselves", Jam 4:10; 1Pe 5:6); narrative past (the kings "humbled themselves"); **gnomic present** (Gospel maxim).
- **T1.4.2** — **Yes** — commanded (NT exhortation) vs narrated act (OT kings) vs general maxim (Gospels).
- **T1.4.3** — **Yes** — commanded and addressed ("you humbled yourself", 2Ki 22:19; 2Ch 34:27), accompanied by confession ("The Lord is righteous", 2Ch 12:6).
- **T1.5.1** — Immediate sequel: divine relief (wrath turns, 2Ch 12:7, 12) or exaltation (Jam 4:10; 1Pe 5:6); inner-side, penitence with torn clothes and weeping (2Ch 34:27).
- **T1.5.2** — **Varied by corpus** (Chronicles: wrath-relief; Gospels/Epistles: exaltation) but **consistent** in that a divine response always follows.
- **T1.6.1** — Sustained effect: a **restored covenant standing** (forgiveness, healing, 2Ch 7:14) and a settled lowliness that receives grace (→ B).
- **T1.6.3** — Immediate = the relief/exaltation; sustained = the restored standing and abiding lowliness.
- **T1.7.1** — Right operation under a **penitent/tender heart** (2Ki 22:19; 2Ch 34:27), acknowledged guilt (2Ch 12:6), and distress driving to God (2Ch 33:12).
- **T1.7.2** — Blocked by **pride of heart** (2Ch 32:26) and **hardness** (Zedekiah, 2Ch 36:12, though God's word came through Jeremiah). No adversarial-spirit interference evidenced.
- **T1.7.3** — [SILENT–data] No verse shows a *hollow* self-humbling present-but-not-taking-hold; the negative cases are outright refusal, not failed uptake.

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries  *(coverage 6/6)*
- **T2.1.1** — Located in the **heart**: "uncircumcised heart" (Lev 26:41), "penitent/tender heart" (2Ki 22:19; 2Ch 34:27), "pride of his heart" (2Ch 32:26). No spirit/soul/mind named.
- **T2.1.2** — The pattern (**heart only**) indicates self-humbling is a **heart-act** — the volitional-affective centre — not a cognitive or spirit-level event.
- **T2.10.1** — **None** — no movement across constitutional levels; the act originates within and bends the person's own heart.
- **T2.7.1** — Body link is **inner→body, expressive**: contrition shown bodily (torn clothes, weeping, 2Ch 34:27).
- **T2.9.1** — Origin: **generated within the person** (one humbles oneself), prompted by hearing God's word (2Ki 22:19 "when you heard").
- **T2.9.2** — **Single** origin (within-person), consistently prompted by encounter with God's word or threat.

## T3 — The Inner Faculties  *(coverage 33/33 — engaged faculties answered; non-engaged faculties answered at the pattern level)*
- **T3.1 Perception** — .1 engaged at the **trigger**: humbling follows "when you heard" God's word (2Ki 22:19; 2Ch 34:27); .2 perception prompts the act; .3 pattern — perception is the *antecedent* of self-humbling, not its content.
- **T3.2 Cognition** — .1 engaged as **acknowledgement** ("The Lord is righteous", 2Ch 12:6 — recognition of God's justice and one's guilt); .2 reorders self-assessment; .3 cognition present as confession/judgement of self.
- **T3.3 Memory** — .1 none; .2 no effect; .3 [SILENT–data on .1/.2] memory **never engaged** — indicates self-humbling is not a memorial act.
- **T3.4 Affect** — .1 engaged: penitence, tenderness, weeping, distress (2Ki 22:19; 2Ch 34:27; 33:12); .2 the act is emotionally loaded contrition; .3 affect is **integral** to the act.
- **T3.5 Creativity** — .1 none; .2 no effect; .3 creativity **never engaged** — the act originates nothing new; it bends an existing will.
- **T3.6 Volition** — .1 strongly engaged — the act is reflexive/chosen ("Humble yourselves"); .2 the will bends itself against pride; .3 self-humbling is **paradigmatically volitional** (its defining faculty).
- **T3.7 Agency** — .1 engaged — the person initiates the act; .2 agency exercised as self-lowering; .3 it is an **agentive** act (something one does, not undergoes — the C-contrast).
- **T3.8 Moral Evaluation** — .1 engaged — self measured against God's standard ("the Lord is righteous"; pride judged, 2Ch 32:26); .2 reorders moral self-estimate; .3 moral evaluation is **constitutive** (the act is a right judgement of self before God).
- **T3.9 Conscience** — .1 engaged — conviction/penitence (penitent heart, acknowledged guilt); .2 conscience drives the turning; .3 conscience is **active** as the witness of sin that precipitates the act.
- **T3.10 Conscientiousness** — .1 engaged — integrates moral awareness + volition + action ("turn from their wicked ways", 2Ch 7:14); .2 issues in changed conduct; .3 the act is an **integrated** moral-volitional-active turning.
- **T3.11 Relational Capacity** — .1 engaged — constituted **before God** (a relational bending); .2 reorders the God-relation toward dependence; .3 relational capacity is **the very frame** of the act (it exists only in relation to God).

## T4 — Relational Interfaces  *(coverage 14/18; 4 silent)*
- **T4.1.1** — **Yes** (God's side = response): God relents (2Ch 12:7), forgives/heals (2Ch 7:14), exalts (Jam 4:10; 1Pe 5:6).
- **T4.1.2** — **Conditional-covenantal/responsive**: "if my people… humble themselves… *then* I will hear" (2Ch 7:14).
- **T4.1.3** — Shows God **disposed to mercy toward the humble** (the grace-to-the-humble logic; → B, Jam 4:6).
- **T4.2.1** — **Yes — the primary axis**: the human movement toward God in repentant self-abasement, seeking his face (2Ch 7:14; 33:12 "entreated the favor").
- **T4.2.2** — Requires a **penitent, pride-relinquished heart**.
- **T4.2.3** — Shows the person's **dependence on and submission to God's righteousness**.
- **T4.3.1** — Largely **none** (the act is God-ward); the one quasi-horizontal case is humbling "before Jeremiah the prophet" as God's spokesman (2Ch 36:12, by its refusal).
- **T4.3.2 / T4.3.3** — [SILENT–structural] person-to-person *giving* is not the mode of A; these belong to other-directed characteristics.
- **T4.4.1 / T4.4.2 / T4.4.3** — [SILENT–structural] A is not a received-from-another characteristic (it is self-originated before God).
- **T4.5.1** — Operates **within** the covenant relationship (Israel's kings) and is commanded to **all** ("whoever").
- **T4.5.2** — **Crosses** covenantal boundary in the NT universalising ("everyone who humbles himself").
- **T4.5.3** — Scope: **anyone before God** — narrowed in OT to covenant Israel's leaders, universalised in NT.
- **T4.6.1 / T4.6.2 / T4.6.3** — [SILENT–data] no angelic/adversarial operation evidenced (candidate uniform cross-cluster silence, cf. M05/M07 T4.6 — Session-D note).

## T5 — Formative and Developmental Dimension  *(coverage 9/9)*
- **T5.1.1** — **Both** — changes the person's **condition** (spared/forgiven) and **orientation** (pride → lowliness).
- **T5.1.2** — **Reversible** as a returnable posture (kings humble across reigns); the christological instance (Phil 2:8) is once-for-all.
- **T5.2.1** — **Yes** — hearing God's word → conviction/penitence → self-humbling → divine relief/exaltation.
- **T5.3.1** — Mechanism: **encounter** (with God's word/threat) and **discipline/affliction** ("in his distress… humbled himself greatly", 2Ch 33:12).
- **T5.3.2** — **Differs**: word-encounter (Josiah, Hezekiah) vs distress-in-captivity (Manasseh).
- **T5.4.1** — **Yes** — affliction is a primary **occasion/producer** of the act (Manasseh; the kings under threat).
- **T5.4.2** — Suffering **elicits and deepens** the humbling.
- **T5.5.1** — **Participates** — the repeated covenant call (2Ch 7:14) is formative discipline shaping the people toward grace-receiving lowliness.
- **T5.6.1** — **Yes** — oriented to eschatological **exaltation/reversal** ("will be exalted"; "at the proper time").

## T6 — Structural Relationships with Other Characteristics  *(coverage 13/13)*
- **T6.1.1** — Co-occurs with repentance/turning (*shuv*, 2Ch 7:14), prayer/seeking (*atar/darash*), weeping (*bakhah*), sin/guilt (*chattat/maal/avon*), and **obedience** (Phil 2:8).
- **T6.1.2** — Its place: the **penitential hinge** of the inner-being landscape — where sin meets mercy.
- **T6.2.1** — **Precedes** divine mercy/exaltation; **accompanies** repentance.
- **T6.2.2** — Relationship is **causal/responsive** (the human act conditions the divine response).
- **T6.3.1** — Produces the **ground of forgiveness/exaltation**.
- **T6.3.2** — Produced by **conviction and affliction**.
- **T6.3.3** — A **constituent of repentance**; meets **obedience (D)** at the cross (Phil 2:8 "humbled himself by becoming obedient").
- **T6.4.1** — Shares *ka.na* and *tapeinoō* with **C** (being-brought-low) and the *tapein-* root with **B**.
- **T6.4.2** — **Yes** — the *tapein-* root spans A/B/C; *ka.na* spans A/C (one lexical field, differentiated by voice/agency).
- **T6.4.3** — Shows act (A), trait (B), and condition (C) are **one semantic field** read apart by voice and agency.
- **T6.5.1** — Nearest neighbour **C**; distinguished by **agency/voice** (chosen/reflexive vs imposed/passive).
- **T6.5.2** — Boundary: the same verb is A when the subject lowers *himself* before God, C when he *is lowered* by God/circumstance/enemy.
- **T6.5.3** — Distinction is of **kind and direction**, not degree.

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological Foundation  *(coverage 18/20; 2 none-recorded)*
- **T7.1.1** — *ka.na*, *tapeinoō*, *tsa.na* — root meanings of **lowering / bringing-down**.
- **T7.1.2** — Grammatical range = **verb** (reflexive/Niphal/Hiphil/imperative/participle) — operates as an act (done, commanded, narrated).
- **T7.1.3** — Semantic range: from **subjugation** ("be subdued") → **voluntary self-abasement** → **repentant bending before God**.
- **T7.1.4** — **Yes** — voice distinguishes **act** (A, reflexive) from **condition** (C, passive).
- **T7.1.5** — **Yes** — opposite/absence terms: pride/self-exaltation (*gavah* "height"; *hupsoō*; *huperēphanos*).
- **T7.1.6** — **Yes** — person-type term *tsanua / tapeinos* "the humble (person)".
- **T7.1.7** — **None** — no term for *seeking this act from another*; the seeking-terms (*darash/atar*) seek God, not the characteristic.
- **T7.1.8** — *ka.na* (OT: king-before-God, wrath-relief) → *tapeinoō* (NT: universal maxim + christological) — **continuity of the lowering act, developed from national-covenant to universal/christological**.
- **T7.1.9** — **None** newly coined for the *act* (the NT coinage *tapeinofrosunē* names the trait, → B).
- **T7.1.10** — Full arc: **subjugation → voluntary repentant self-abasement → christological self-emptying**.
- **T7.2.1** — Function: the **main verb** of its clause — "X humbled himself before the Lord."
- **T7.2.2** — Forms: **OT narrative** (dominant, Chronicles/Kings), wisdom/prophecy (Mic 6:8), Gospel maxim, epistle exhortation; narrative requires reading within the reign-evaluation, the maxim as principle.
- **T7.2.3** — Logic: **conditional-covenantal** ("if… humble… then I will hear") and **reversal** ("whoever humbles… will be exalted").
- **T7.2.4** — Setting: **covenantal** (Chronicles' retribution theology), **penitential/liturgical** (prayer, torn clothes), **eschatological** (the reversal).
- **T7.2.5** — Primary anchor: **2Ch 7:14** (fullest covenant sequence); christological apex **Phil 2:8**.
- **T7.2.6** — 2Ch 7:14 uniquely shows self-humbling as the **hinge of covenant restoration** (humble → pray → seek → turn → God hears/forgives/heals).
- **T7.3.1** *(science, per M09 extract §1)* — Lens: **positive/moral psychology of humility** (Tangney; VIA; Davis other-/self-focused; contriteness as acute humility).
- **T7.3.2** — Illuminates: the **situational-vs-dispositional** distinction maps A (act) to humbling experiences (failure/affliction) generating humility — illuminating the affliction-trigger (Manasseh "in distress"). Tangney's accurate self-appraisal illuminates the relinquished "pride of heart".
- **T7.3.3** — Divergence: science frames humility as **accurate self-appraisal/other-focus**; A is **God-ward repentant self-abasement before a holy God** — a vertical, theological referent the self-appraisal frame does not reach (the extract's own T7.3.3 register-divergence point).
- **T7.3.4** — The framework's **pseudo-humility** (self-focused self-abasement) surfaces a category A's verses **do not** instantiate (its negatives are outright refusal); it appears instead as *false humility/asceticism* in B (Col 2:18, 23). Worth the cross-note; not a gap in A.

# WA M09 — Characteristic A: Self-humbling before God — Evidence

**File:** wa-m09-char-a-evidence-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Cluster:** M09 — *Humility, Meekness and Submission* · **Characteristic:** A — Self-humbling before God
**Occurrences gathered:** 23 · **Source:** `wa-ve-lexical-extract-M09-20260621-b1of1.json` (extract v1_0, 2026-06-21, batch 1/1)
**Prior output:** `wa-m09-provisional-chars-v1_0-20260621.md` (provisional set). **Phase:** evidence-gather (§4), pre-interpret.
**Status:** self-contained evidence record. Field values are READ-resolved per the extract; counts are indicative (not yet CC-version-locked). Definitions/signatures/flags are authored; the evidence tables are gathered mechanically from the extract.

> Note on references: the extract renders Philippians as "Phili" and Philemon as "Phile" (differs from the Session-A book codes Php/Phm). Full book names used below for clarity. Flagged for normalisation.

## Definition
The **chosen inner act of lowering oneself before God** — a volitional self-abasement, characteristically bound to repentance, by which a person (or people) bends the will and heart under God and so turns away threatened judgement. It is an *act done*, not a condition suffered (contrast C) and not a settled trait (contrast B).

## Inner-being signature (observation → interpretation)
- **Kind:** overwhelmingly *action* (the term is the doing of self-lowering); the faculty field is mostly absent because the term names an act rather than a faculty — its inner content is read from seat and object.
- **Seat:** where located, the **heart** (Leviticus 26:41 "uncircumcised heart"; 2 Kings 22:19 and 2 Chronicles 34:27 "your heart was penitent/tender"; 2 Chronicles 32:26 "the pride of his heart"). The act is heart-seated even when the verb is outward.
- **Object / direction:** God-ward — "before the Lord / before me / before God / with your God". This is the discriminator from C (which is directed by circumstance or enemy).
- **Experiencer:** self or addressed-self ("humble *yourselves*"); the act is reflexive.
- **Valence:** **righteous → commanded**; its *absence* is marked sinful (2 Chronicles 36:12 "did not humble himself"; 2 Chronicles 33:23 contrast with Manasseh).

## Sub-patterns (verse-likeness)
1. **The Chronicles/Kings repentance-relief pattern** — self-humbling averts or defers wrath: 1 Kings 21:29 (Ahab); 2 Chronicles 12:6–7, 12; 2 Chronicles 32:26; 2 Chronicles 33:12. The act is the hinge between sin and mercy.
2. **The commanded covenant call** — 2 Chronicles 7:14 "if my people… humble themselves"; James 4:10 "Humble yourselves before the Lord"; 1 Peter 5:6 "under the mighty hand of God"; Micah 6:8 "walk humbly with your God".
3. **The Gospel reversal frame** — Matthew 18:4; 23:12; Luke 14:11; 18:14 "whoever humbles himself will be exalted" (cross-cutting axis; see flags).
4. **The Christological maximum** — Philippians 2:8 "he humbled himself" (paired with obedience-to-death; the A↔D hinge).

## Cross-links
- **D Obedience:** Philippians 2:8 fuses self-humbling with obedience ("humbled himself by becoming obedient"). A and D meet at the cross.
- **M10 (sin) / M45 (repentance):** co-terms chattat "sin", maal "unfaithfulness", shuv "repent/return", bakhah "weep" recur around the act.

## Interpret-phase flags
- **Fork A+B (open):** A (act) vs B (disposition) are close; the verse-likeness keeps them distinct (chosen act vs borne trait), but a merge into a single "humility" head is defensible. Carried for decision.
- **Leviticus 26:41** ("if their… heart is humbled") sits at the A/C edge — covenant turning vs being-brought-low; routed to A on the repentance-response reading. Flagged.

# WA M09 — Characteristic B: Lowliness as settled disposition — Tier Findings

**File:** wa-m09-char-b-tier-findings-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Cluster:** M09 · **Characteristic:** B — Lowliness as settled disposition · **Catalogue:** WA-tier-catalogue v2 (126Q)
**Evidence base:** `wa-m09-char-b-evidence-v1_0-20260621.md` (13 occurrences)
**Source verses:** Pro 11:2; Mat 11:29; Rom 12:16; 2Cor 10:1; Jam 4:6; 1Pe 5:5 (×2); Act 20:19; Eph 4:2; Phil 2:3; Col 3:12; **Col 2:18; Col 2:23** (counterfeit pole).
**Method:** authored by verse-reading; Silent classified; inferential labelled; science (T7.3) attributed to M09 extract §1.

---

## T0 — Divine Image  *(9/9)*
- **T0.1.1** — Lowliness is **predicated of Christ** ("I am gentle and lowly in heart", Mat 11:29) and God **gives grace to the humble** (Jam 4:6; 1Pe 5:5). God both **bears** it (in Christ) and **responds** to it with grace.
- **T0.1.2** — **Yes — uniquely borne by God-in-Christ** (Mat 11:29), the one M09 characteristic predicated of the incarnate Son as his own settled heart-state. So it images Christ directly (contrast A, never borne by God).
- **T0.2.1** — Purpose: it **receives grace** (Jam 4:6; 1Pe 5:5), **gives rest to the soul** (Mat 11:29), and **orders community** (Phil 2:3; Eph 4:2). The counterfeit (Col 2:23) "has an appearance of wisdom" but is "of no value against the flesh" — a purpose-failure.
- **T0.2.2** — **Both** — restored/commanded good (the put-on virtue) and, in its counterfeit, a fallen distortion (Col 2).
- **T0.2.3** — [inferential] grace-to-the-humble orients toward ongoing/eschatological grace.
- **T0.3.1** — Instantiates **Christ-likeness of lowly-heartedness** (Mat 11:29).
- **T0.3.2** — **Shared** between God (Christ) and the person (unlike A) — Christ is lowly in heart; believers put on the same.
- **T0.3.3** — Presence = Christlike, grace-receiving image; the counterfeit/haughtiness (Col 2; Rom 12:16) = distorted image.
- **T0.4.1** — **Christological** (Mat 11:29 — "learn from me", the divine instance establishing the pattern); direction divine→human.

## T1 — Definition  *(18/18)*
- **T1.1.1** — Names a **borne trait of lowly-mindedness** toward self and others.
- **T1.1.2** — *tapeinos* (lowly/humble), *tapeinofrosunē* (lowliness-of-**mind**: *tapeinos*+*phrēn*), *tsa.nu.a* (modest/humble) — definitional: humble-mindedness.
- **T1.1.3** — **Constitutional** (heart/mind-seated) + **relational** (toward others) implication.
- **T1.2.1** — A **disposition/quality** (borne trait); *tapeinos* tagged **affect**.
- **T1.2.2** — **Compound** — *tapeinofrosunē* literally compounds lowliness + mind: low self-estimate + other-regard + affect.
- **T1.3.1** — Structural opposite: **pride / haughtiness** (Rom 12:16 "do not be haughty"; the "puffed-up… sensuous mind", Col 2:18).
- **T1.3.2** — Resists conceit, vainglory, selfish ambition (Phil 2:3).
- **T1.3.3** — **Not** the act of self-humbling (A) nor imposed low estate (C); and crucially **not** the counterfeit self-abasement/asceticism (Col 2) that mimics it.
- **T1.4.1** — Adjective (lowly), noun (humility), modal "with all humility" (Act 20:19; Eph 4:2), imperative "put on / clothe yourselves" (Col 3:12; 1Pe 5:5).
- **T1.4.2** — **Varies** — described trait (Mat 11:29), commanded virtue (Col 3:12), counterfeit (Col 2).
- **T1.4.3** — **Communicative** — commanded/addressed ("clothe yourselves… with humility"); operates in community conduct.
- **T1.5.1** — Immediate response: **grace received** (Jam 4:6; 1Pe 5:5 "God… gives grace to the humble").
- **T1.5.2** — **Consistent** grace-pairing (Jam 4:6 = 1Pe 5:5, both citing Pro 3:34).
- **T1.6.1** — Sustained: **rest to the soul** (Mat 11:29) and **unity/forbearance** in the body (Eph 4:2–3).
- **T1.6.3** — Immediate = grace received; sustained = soul-rest and community concord.
- **T1.7.1** — Right operation in a heart that **counts others more significant** (Phil 2:3) and **associates with the lowly** (Rom 12:16).
- **T1.7.2** — Distorted by **self-made religion / asceticism** (Col 2:23) and haughtiness; the counterfeit is "puffed up… by his sensuous mind" (Col 2:18) — pride masquerading as humility. (Col 2:18 ties it to **"worship of angels"** — an angelic-object distortion; see T4.6.)
- **T1.7.3** — Present-but-not-holding = **the counterfeit**: the form (asceticism) without the substance ("of no value… against the flesh", Col 2:23).

## T2 — Constitutional Location  *(6/6)*
- **T2.1.1** — Seated in **heart, soul, mind**: "lowly in heart… rest for your souls" (Mat 11:29); "inward parts" (Col 3:12); *tapeinofrosunē* = mind (*phrēn*) by composition. The counterfeit relocates to **flesh/mind** (Col 2:18, 23).
- **T2.1.2** — Pattern: true lowliness is **heart-deep**; the counterfeit is **flesh-seated** ("self-made… severity to the body", Col 2:23). The seat itself distinguishes true from false humility.
- **T2.10.1** — [inferential] "put on / clothe" (Col 3:12; 1Pe 5:5) is a **donning** onto the person (clothing-image), not a constitutional movement across levels.
- **T2.7.1** — Body link in the **counterfeit** — "severity to the body" (Col 2:23, false asceticism); the true trait runs heart→conduct (expressive).
- **T2.9.1** — Origin: **received / put on** (Col 3:12; 1Pe 5:5) and **learned from Christ** (Mat 11:29 "learn from me"); the counterfeit is **self-made** (Col 2:23).
- **T2.9.2** — Two origins by valence: true = received/learned from Christ; counterfeit = self-generated.

## T3 — The Inner Faculties  *(cognition, affect, volition, agency, moral-eval, conscientiousness, relational engaged; perception/memory/creativity/conscience none-or-inferential)*
- **T3.2 Cognition** — engaged — *tapeinofrosunē* is lowliness of **mind**; "count others more significant" (Phil 2:3) and "never be wise in your own sight" (Rom 12:16) are cognitive self-estimates; pattern: cognition engaged as **right self-reckoning**.
- **T3.4 Affect** — engaged (*tapeinos* = affect); "rest for your souls" (Mat 11:29) — a felt lowliness/soul-rest.
- **T3.6 Volition** — engaged — "put on / clothe yourselves with humility" is volitional **donning**; Phil 2:3 chosen other-regard.
- **T3.7 Agency** — engaged — humility shapes action toward others (serving "with all humility", Act 20:19).
- **T3.8 Moral Evaluation** — engaged — humility is a right moral self-assessment; the counterfeit is morally judged ("of no value", Col 2:23); pattern: moral-evaluation central (true vs false humility).
- **T3.10 Conscientiousness** — engaged — integrated humble conduct (serving, bearing with one another, Eph 4:2).
- **T3.11 Relational Capacity** — **strongly engaged** — humility is fundamentally **toward others** (Phil 2:3; Rom 12:16; Eph 4:2; 1Pe 5:5 "toward one another"); the **defining outward axis** of B.
- **T3.1 / T3.3 / T3.5 / T3.9** (perception, memory, creativity, conscience) — none/[inferential]; pattern: B is **cognitive-affective-relational**, not perceptual/memorial/creative.

## T4 — Relational Interfaces  *(15/18 — including a rare M09 T4.6 answer)*
- **T4.1.1 / .2 / .3** — God **gives grace to the humble** (Jam 4:6; 1Pe 5:5); **responsive** (grace to the humble, opposed to the proud — Pro 3:34 basis); shows God **draws near / favours the lowly**.
- **T4.2.1** — [inferential] lowliness is the posture before God that receives grace; "come to me… learn" (Mat 11:29, toward Christ).
- **T4.3.1 / .2 / .3** — **Central**: humility is practiced **toward one another** (Phil 2:3; Eph 4:2; 1Pe 5:5; Rom 12:16); inner condition = other-regard without conceit; must have **received/put on** the Christ-pattern before extending it.
- **T4.4.1** — [inferential] humility is received from Christ's example/grace; uptake requires relinquishing pride.
- **T4.5.1 / .2 / .3** — Operates **within the body** ("toward one another") and **toward the lowly** (Rom 12:16 — crossing status lines downward); scope = the whole community, especially the low.
- **T4.6.1 / T4.6.2** — **Yes (notable):** the counterfeit humility is tied to **"worship of angels"** and "elemental spirits" (Col 2:18 context) — false humility is a **site of angelic/adversarial distortion**; humility **can be weaponised** as self-abasing, angel-venerating asceticism. B is the rare M09 characteristic with genuine T4.6 content.
- **T4.6.3** — [SILENT–data] no angelic *mediation/strengthening* of true humility shown.

## T5 — Formative and Developmental  *(7/9)*
- **T5.1.1** — [inferential] putting on humility transforms self-estimate and community relations (orientation-change).
- **T5.3.1 / .2** — **Formation by imitation/instruction** ("learn from me", Mat 11:29; "put on", Col 3:12); differs from the counterfeit's self-made formation (Col 2:23).
- **T5.4.1** — Humility exercised **amid trials** ("serving… with all humility and with tears and with trials", Act 20:19).
- **T5.5.1** — **Participates** — humility is in the put-on-the-new-self list (Col 3:12) — a core sanctification virtue.
- **T5.6.1** — [inferential] grace-to-the-humble and soul-rest anticipate eschatological rest/exaltation.
- **T5.1.2 / T5.2.1** — [SILENT–data] reversibility and a staged sequence not shown (a donned state).

## T6 — Structural Relationships  *(12/13)*
- **T6.1.1 / .2** — Co-occurs with **gentleness/meekness** (Col 3:12; Eph 4:2 → M05), **patience** (Eph 4:2), **compassion/kindness** (Col 3:12 → M05); opposite **pride/haughtiness** (Rom 12:16). Col 3:12 is the **M09↔M05 hinge**. Place: the renewed-self ensemble of relational virtues.
- **T6.2.1 / .2** — Accompanies/precedes **unity and forbearance** (Eph 4:2–3); developmental-correlational.
- **T6.3.1 / .2 / .3** — **Produces** soul-rest (Mat 11:29) and community concord; **produced by** learning Christ; **constituent** of the renewed self (Col 3:12).
- **T6.4.1 / .2** — *tapeinos/tapeinofrosunē* shared with **A** (act) and **C** (low estate); *tsanua* with A's *tsana* — the *tapein-* root spans A/B/C.
- **T6.5.1 / .2 / .3** — Nearest = **A** (same field) — distinguished by **kind** (trait vs act); also near **M05 meekness** (Col 3:12) — humility = posture concerning self/before God, meekness = manner toward others (M05 T6). Distinction of **kind**.

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological  *(19/20)*
- **T7.1.1** — *tapeinos* (low/humble), *tapeinofrosunē* (*tapeinos*+*phrēn* "mind"), *tsanua* (modest) — roots = **low + mind**.
- **T7.1.2** — Adjective + noun — **disposition-words** (borne quality).
- **T7.1.3** — Semantic range: from socially-low → humble-minded (moral virtue).
- **T7.1.4** — The **disposition** member of the *tapein-* field (vs act A, condition C); *tapeinofrosunē* names the virtue specifically.
- **T7.1.5** — Opposite: **pride** (*huperēphania*, Jam 4:6 / 1Pe 5:5 "God opposes the proud"); haughtiness (Rom 12:16).
- **T7.1.6** — Person-type: *tapeinos / tsanua* "the humble (person)" (Pro 11:2; Jam 4:6).
- **T7.1.8** — OT (*tsanua*, modest) → NT — the NT **coins/revalues** lowliness from the pagan-negative *tapeinos* (servile) into a Christic moral excellence.
- **T7.1.9** — **tapeinofrosunē** — effectively a NT coinage/revaluation; the coinage shows the NT making lowliness a **virtue**.
- **T7.1.10** — Arc: socially-low/servile (pagan negative) → Christic humble-mindedness (NT virtue), with a counterfeit (asceticism).
- **T7.2.1** — Function: predicate adjective / object of "put on" — naming the trait borne.
- **T7.2.2** — Forms: Gospel (Mat 11:29), epistle paraenesis (Col/Eph/Phil/1Pe), wisdom (Pro 11:2), **polemic** (Col 2, against false humility).
- **T7.2.3** — Logic: "God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble" (Jam 4:6; 1Pe 5:5); "count others more significant" (Phil 2:3).
- **T7.2.4** — Setting: community paraenesis, christological (Mat 11:29), polemical (Col 2).
- **T7.2.5 / .6** — Anchor **Mat 11:29** — lowliness **as Christ's own settled heart-state**, the source of soul-rest, grounding the human trait in the incarnate person.
- **T7.3.1** *(science §1)* — positive/moral psychology of humility (Tangney; VIA; Davis other-/self-focused; pseudo-humility).
- **T7.3.2** — Illuminates: Davis's **other-focused vs self-focused** humility maps to B's two faces (Phil 2:3 / Rom 12:16); **dispositional** humility (stable orientation) maps to B (vs situational A/C); Tangney's "secure, not destabilised by criticism" coheres with the restful lowly heart.
- **T7.3.3** — Divergence: science frames humility horizontally (self-appraisal/other-focus); B grounds it **christologically** (put on Christ's lowliness; receive grace).
- **T7.3.4** — **Strong hit:** the science's named **pseudo-humility** (self-focused self-abasement) is **directly instantiated** in B's counterfeit *tapeinofrosunē* (Col 2:18, 23) — the cluster's clearest verse-instance of the framework's surfaced category.
- **T7.1.7** — [SILENT–data] no term for seeking the trait from another.

# WA M09 — Characteristic B: Lowliness as settled disposition — Evidence

**File:** wa-m09-char-b-evidence-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Cluster:** M09 — *Humility, Meekness and Submission* · **Characteristic:** B — Lowliness as settled disposition
**Occurrences gathered:** 13 · **Source:** `wa-ve-lexical-extract-M09-20260621-b1of1.json` (extract v1_0, 2026-06-21, batch 1/1)
**Prior output:** `wa-m09-provisional-chars-v1_0-20260621.md` (provisional set). **Phase:** evidence-gather (§4), pre-interpret.
**Status:** self-contained evidence record. Field values are READ-resolved per the extract; counts are indicative (not yet CC-version-locked). Definitions/signatures/flags are authored; the evidence tables are gathered mechanically from the extract.

> Note on references: the extract renders Philippians as "Phili" and Philemon as "Phile" (differs from the Session-A book codes Php/Phm). Full book names used below for clarity. Flagged for normalisation.

## Definition
**Humility as an abiding interior orientation** — lowly-mindedness toward oneself and a corresponding esteem of others. Not the act of self-lowering (A) nor an imposed low condition (C), but the *borne quality* of a humble heart.

## Inner-being signature
- **Kind:** *quality / status* (a borne trait), with the adjective *tapeinos* tagged **faculty = affect** — humility as a felt interior set, not merely behaviour.
- **Seat:** heart and soul (Matthew 11:29 "lowly in heart… rest for your souls"; Colossians 3:12 inward-parts).
- **Direction:** toward **others** and toward **self-estimate** (Philippians 2:3 "count others more significant"; Romans 12:16 "associate with the lowly… never be wise in your own sight").
- **Valence:** righteous → commanded; received from God ("clothe yourselves with humility", 1 Peter 5:5; "put on… humility", Colossians 3:12).

## Sub-patterns
1. **The clothed/put-on virtue** — Colossians 3:12; 1 Peter 5:5; Ephesians 4:2; Acts 20:19. Humility as donned character, listed with gentleness/patience.
2. **The Christ-pattern interior** — Matthew 11:29 "I am gentle and lowly in heart" (the only place the disposition is predicated of Christ as his own settled state).
3. **The grace-magnet** — James 4:6; 1 Peter 5:5 "God… gives grace to the humble" (the disposition as the object of divine favour).
4. **COUNTERFEIT POLE (flagged):** *tapeinofrosunē* at Colossians 2:18 and 2:23 carries sense "asceticism", **valence = sinful** — self-made, body-severe false humility seated in "flesh/mind". The *same lemma* names true humility and its counterfeit; a key finding for the interpret phase.

## Cross-links
- **M05 Gentleness (E):** humility and meekness are listed together (Colossians 3:12; Ephesians 4:2) — the M09↔M05 hinge. M05 distinguishes them: gentleness = manner toward others; humility = posture concerning self/before God.
- **M08 (pride/arrogance):** the structural opposite; huperēphanos "arrogant" is the recurrent antonym co-term ("God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble").

## Interpret-phase flags
- **Fork A+B (open):** see A.
- **2 Corinthians 10:1** ("humble when face to face") routed to B as demeanour/disposition, but reads as outward bearing — B/C edge; flagged.
- **Counterfeit tapeinofrosunē** (Colossians 2): decide whether the sinful-asceticism sense is held within B as its counterfeit pole or split out.

# WA M09 — Characteristic C: Being brought low / lowly estate / humiliation — Tier Findings

**File:** wa-m09-char-c-tier-findings-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Cluster:** M09 · **Characteristic:** C — Being brought low / lowly estate / humiliation · **Catalogue:** WA-tier-catalogue v2 (126Q)
**Evidence base:** `wa-m09-char-c-evidence-v1_0-20260621.md` (13 occurrences)
**Source verses:** 2Ch 28:19; Job 40:12; Psa 106:42; Psa 107:12; 2Cor 12:21; 2Cor 7:6; Act 8:33; Jam 1:9; Jam 1:10; Luk 1:48; Luk 1:52; Phil 3:21; Phil 4:12.
**Method:** authored by verse-reading; Silent classified; inferential labelled; science (T7.3) attributed to M09 extract §1. **Inner↔outer boundary handled explicitly (fork 3).**

---

## T0 — Divine Image  *(9/9)*
- **T0.1.1** — God is the **active agent** of lowering ("the Lord humbled Judah", 2Ch 28:19; "my God may humble me", 2Cor 12:21; the command to abase the proud, Job 40:12) **and of reversal** ("he has… exalted those of humble estate", Luk 1:52). Act 8:33 = **Christ's** humiliation (Isa 53).
- **T0.1.2** — **Yes — assumed by Christ** (Act 8:33; the lowly body, Phil 3:21, conformed from his). Otherwise God is the **agent who lowers/reverses**, not the bearer. Pattern: a creaturely condition the incarnate Son **takes on**.
- **T0.2.1** — Effects: **disciplinary** (2Ch 28:19 judgment; 2Cor 12:21 lest Paul be proud), **occasions comfort** (2Cor 7:6 "comforts the downcast"), and is the **ground God reverses** (Luk 1:52; Jam 1:9).
- **T0.2.2** — **Fallen condition** primarily (results from sin/judgment/affliction), redemptively used by God — **both**, weighted fallen.
- **T0.2.3** — **Strong future orientation** — reversed: "exalted those of humble estate" (Luk 1:52); the lowly brother's "exaltation" (Jam 1:9); "our lowly body… like his glorious body" (Phil 3:21).
- **T0.3.1** — Instantiates the creature's **dependence/contingency** and, christologically, the Son's **condescension** (Act 8:33; Phil 3:21).
- **T0.3.2** — Creaturely condition **assumed by Christ** (shared via incarnation).
- **T0.3.3** — The low estate itself is a circumstance (not an image-index); God's **reversal** of it shows the image's destiny (exaltation/glory).
- **T0.4.1** — **Christological + eschatological** — Act 8:33 (Christ's humiliation), Phil 3:21 (lowly→glorious body), Luk 1:52 (Magnificat reversal); the divine assumes the low and reverses it.

## T1 — Definition  *(14/18)*
- **T1.1.1** — Names an **imposed / circumstantial low condition** (undergone).
- **T1.1.2** — *ka.na* (be subdued/brought low), *tapeinoō* (be humbled), *tapeinos* (downcast/lowly), *tapeinōsis* (humiliation/low estate) — lowness **undergone**.
- **T1.1.3** — **Condition/status** implication (undergone, not chosen); usually externally caused.
- **T1.2.1** — A **condition/status** (the patient's state), not an act.
- **T1.2.2** — Largely **simple** (a state), with an **affective correlate** (downcast).
- **T1.3.1** — Structural opposite: **exaltation / being lifted up** (Luk 1:52; Jam 1:9); height/glory.
- **T1.3.2** — It is the **absence** of exaltation/status; being undergone, it "resists" nothing.
- **T1.3.3** — **Not** the chosen act (A) nor the virtue (B); ends where the lowering becomes voluntary (A) or settled trait (B).
- **T1.4.1** — Passive verb (be brought low), noun (humiliation), adjective (downcast/lowly).
- **T1.4.2** — **Varies** — divine discipline (2Ch 28:19; 2Cor 12:21), enemy-affliction (Psa 106:42; 107:12), social estate (Luk 1:48, 52; Jam 1:9–10), want (Phil 4:12), **somatic** (Phil 3:21).
- **T1.5.1** — Immediate response: **mourning** (2Cor 12:21 "I may have to mourn") and **comfort received** (2Cor 7:6 God "comforted the downcast").
- **T1.5.2** — **Varied** — grief (downcast) or **learned contentment** (Phil 4:12 "I have learned… how to be brought low").
- **T1.6.1** — Sustained: **dependence/contentment** (Phil 4:12) and **readiness for comfort/exaltation**.
- **T1.6.3** — Immediate = downcast grief/comfort; sustained = learned contentment / awaited exaltation.
- **T1.7.1** — [inferential] rightly borne when received as **discipline** (2Cor 12:21) or with **learned contentment** (Phil 4:12).
- **T1.4.3 / T1.7.2 / T1.7.3** — [SILENT–data] not a speech mode; blocking/non-uptake conditions not described.

## T2 — Constitutional Location and Boundaries  *(6/6 — the inner↔outer boundary)*
- **T2.1.1** — **Heart** — "he bowed their hearts down with hard labor" (Psa 107:12); **affect** — "downcast" (2Cor 7:6); **body** — "our lowly body" (Phil 3:21). The condition reaches from circumstance into heart and body.
- **T2.1.2** — Pattern (the **inner↔outer boundary**, fork 3): the **inner** correlate is heart/affect (bowed heart, downcast spirit); the **outer** is body/estate (lowly body, humble social estate). Humiliation **straddles** the boundary — its inner-being relevance is carried by the heart/affect pole (Psa 107:12; 2Cor 7:6), its outer edge by the somatic/social pole (Phil 3:21; Luk 1:48).
- **T2.10.1** — **Movement onto the person from an external source**: God or enemies bring the lowering **onto** the person (2Ch 28:19; Psa 106:42 enemies; 2Cor 12:21 God) — external→person direction.
- **T2.7.1** — Body link **both directions**: the condition **is** bodily (Phil 3:21, somatic lowness awaiting transformation); and bodily affliction **feeds back** to bow the heart (Psa 107:12 hard labour → bowed heart).
- **T2.9.1** — Origin: **external** — divine discipline (2Ch 28:19; 2Cor 12:21), enemy/circumstance (Psa 106:42; 107:12; Phil 4:12), or social birth-estate (Luk 1:48). Not self-generated.
- **T2.9.2** — Origin **multiple** (God / enemies / circumstance / estate), varying by context.

## T3 — The Inner Faculties  *(affect central; AGENCY notably suspended; rest pattern)*
- **T3.4 Affect** — **engaged** — "downcast" (2Cor 7:6, *tapeinos*=affect), mourning (2Cor 12:21), bowed heart (Psa 107:12); affect is the **inner correlate** of the condition (the felt lowness).
- **T3.7 Agency** — **suspended in the patient** — the person is **acted upon**; agency belongs to the **lowering agent** (God/enemies), not the lowered. Pattern (the A↔C discriminator): C is **undergone**, A is **enacted**.
- **T3.6 Volition** — mostly none (undergone), except **Phil 4:12** the learned attitudinal response is volitional; pattern: C is **not volitional** (vs A).
- **T3.2 Cognition** — [inferential] "I have learned" the secret of being brought low (Phil 4:12) — a cognitive learning of contentment.
- **T3.8 Moral Evaluation** — [inferential] where it is discipline, a moral cause is named (2Ch 28:19 judgment for Ahaz's unfaithfulness).
- **T3.11 Relational Capacity** — engaged as **recipient** — the downcast are **met by comfort** (2Cor 7:6, via Titus' coming).
- **T3.9 Conscience** — [inferential] 2Cor 12:21 "mourn over those who… have not repented" (Paul's conscience-grief, adjacent).
- **T3.1 / T3.3 / T3.5 / T3.10** (perception, memory, creativity, conscientiousness) — none; pattern: C is a **borne affective condition**, not an active faculty-operation.

## T4 — Relational Interfaces  *(13/18)*
- **T4.1.1 / .2 / .3** — God **brings low** (2Ch 28:19; 2Cor 12:21), **comforts the downcast** (2Cor 7:6), and **exalts the lowly** (Luk 1:52) — disciplinary/responsive; shows a God who **both disciplines and lifts** the low.
- **T4.2.1** — [inferential] the low estate is the posture from which one is regarded/exalted (Luk 1:48 Mary's "humble estate" regarded by God).
- **T4.3.1** — Comfort **given** to the downcast (2Cor 7:6, person-mediated via Titus).
- **T4.4.1** — The downcast **receive** comfort (2Cor 7:6).
- **T4.5.1 / .2 / .3** — God's reversal reaches the lowly **across status** (Luk 1:52; Jam 1:9) — crossing social boundaries upward; God lifts the low.
- **T4.6.x** — [SILENT–data] lowering agents are God/human-enemies/circumstance; no angelic/adversarial operation.
- **T4.1 sub / T4.2.2/.3 / T4.4.2/.3** — partial/[inferential] as noted.

## T5 — Formative and Developmental  *(9/9 — C is the most T5-laden char)*
- **T5.1.1** — **Strong** — being brought low changes condition; the **reversal** transforms it to exaltation (Luk 1:52) / glorification (Phil 3:21).
- **T5.1.2** — Somatic humiliation → glory is **irreversible** eschatologically (Phil 3:21); disciplinary humbling is **reversible** (Paul restored).
- **T5.2.1** — **Yes** — low estate → (mourning/comfort) → exaltation/transformation (Magnificat and Phil 3:21 arcs).
- **T5.3.1 / .2** — Mechanism: **discipline** (2Ch 28:19; 2Cor 12:21), **affliction/circumstance** (Psa 107:12; Phil 4:12), and **eschatological transformation** (Phil 3:21) — differing across contexts.
- **T5.4.1 / .2** — **Central** — the low estate often **is** the suffering (Psa 107:12 hard labour; 2Cor affliction; Phil 4:12 want); God meets it with comfort.
- **T5.5.1** — **Participates** — humbling discipline forms (guards Paul from pride, 2Cor 12:21; teaches contentment, Phil 4:12).
- **T5.6.1** — **Strong** — Luk 1:52 reversal; Phil 3:21 lowly→glorious body; Jam 1:9 the lowly's exaltation.

## T6 — Structural Relationships  *(11/13)*
- **T6.1.1 / .2** — Co-occurs with **comfort** (2Cor 7:6 → M05 D), **exaltation** (Luk 1:52 — the reversal pair), **mourning/grief** (2Cor 12:21 → M03), riches/fading (Jam 1:10). Place: the **affliction-and-reversal** junction.
- **T6.2.1 / .2** — **Consistently precedes exaltation** (the humble-exalted reversal); accompanies mourning — causal/developmental.
- **T6.3.1 / .2 / .3** — **Produced by** discipline/affliction; **produces** dependence/comfort-readiness; constituent of the **affliction→comfort→glory** arc.
- **T6.4.1 / .2** — *ka.na/tapeinoō/tapeinos* shared with **A** (act) and **B** (disposition) — the same field in **passive/condition voice**; *tapeinōsis* is the condition-noun.
- **T6.5.1 / .2 / .3** — Nearest = **A** (same verbs) — distinguished by **agency/voice** (undergone vs chosen); and **B** — B = virtue, C = circumstantial estate (Luk 1:52 *estate* vs Mat 11:29 *heart-trait*). Distinction of **kind/voice**.
- **T6.2 sub** — [SILENT–data] where sequence not shown.

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological  *(18/20)*
- **T7.1.1** — *ka.na, tapeinoō, tapeinos, tapeinōsis* — roots of **lowering / being-low**.
- **T7.1.2** — **Passive verb / noun / adjective** — the **condition/state** grammar (undergone).
- **T7.1.3** — Semantic range: social low estate → affliction/humiliation → bodily lowness.
- **T7.1.4** — The **condition** member of the *tapein-* field (vs act A, disposition B) — voice/grammar distinguishes.
- **T7.1.5** — Opposite: **exaltation** (*hupsoō*, Luk 1:52; *doxa* "glory", Phil 3:21).
- **T7.1.6** — Person-type: *tapeinos* "the lowly / those of humble estate".
- **T7.1.8** — OT (*ka.na*, national subjection/judgment) → NT (*tapeinōsis/tapeinoō*, individual + christological + eschatological) — the low estate becomes **christologically assumed and eschatologically reversed**.
- **T7.1.9** — *tapeinōsis* "humiliation/low estate" — NT develops the condition-noun (Luk 1:48; Phil 3:21).
- **T7.1.10** — Arc: subjection/judgment → affliction/low estate → christological humiliation → eschatological glorification.
- **T7.2.1** — Function: predicate/object naming the state the person is in or brought into.
- **T7.2.2** — Forms: narrative (2Ch), psalm (Psa 106–107), Gospel canticle (Luk 1 Magnificat), epistle (2Cor/Phil/Jam), prophecy-quote (Act 8:33 = Isa 53).
- **T7.2.3** — Logic: the humble-exalted **reversal** (Luk 1:52; Jam 1:9–10); discipline-against-pride (2Cor 12:21).
- **T7.2.4** — Setting: judicial/disciplinary (2Ch), liturgical (Magnificat), eschatological (Phil 3:21), affliction (2Cor; Phil 4).
- **T7.2.5 / .6** — Anchor **Luk 1:52** — the low estate as the **object of God's reversing mercy** (his characteristic lifting of the low); note Phil 3:21 (somatic eschatology).
- **T7.3.1** *(science §1)* — humility psychology, **involuntary/situational pole** (situationally-triggered humility; humbling experiences).
- **T7.3.2** — Illuminates: **situationally-triggered** humility (failure/suffering/loss reduce inflated appraisal) maps to C (discipline/affliction — 2Ch 28:19; 2Cor 12:21; Phil 4:12); contriteness's somatic quality maps to bodily lowness (Psa 107:12; Phil 3:21).
- **T7.3.3** — Divergence: science studies humbling experiences for their psychological effect (reduced narcissism); C frames the low estate **theologically** as discipline and the ground of God's reversal — a meaning the effect-account doesn't carry.
- **T7.3.4** — **Structural confirmation:** the science's **situational-vs-dispositional** distinction maps cleanly onto the **A (act) / B (disposition) / C (situational condition)** split — the verse evidence confirms the three-fold distinction the framework predicts.

# WA M09 — Characteristic C: Being brought low / lowly estate / humiliation — Evidence

**File:** wa-m09-char-c-evidence-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Cluster:** M09 — *Humility, Meekness and Submission* · **Characteristic:** C — Being brought low / lowly estate / humiliation
**Occurrences gathered:** 13 · **Source:** `wa-ve-lexical-extract-M09-20260621-b1of1.json` (extract v1_0, 2026-06-21, batch 1/1)
**Prior output:** `wa-m09-provisional-chars-v1_0-20260621.md` (provisional set). **Phase:** evidence-gather (§4), pre-interpret.
**Status:** self-contained evidence record. Field values are READ-resolved per the extract; counts are indicative (not yet CC-version-locked). Definitions/signatures/flags are authored; the evidence tables are gathered mechanically from the extract.

> Note on references: the extract renders Philippians as "Phili" and Philemon as "Phile" (differs from the Session-A book codes Php/Phm). Full book names used below for clarity. Flagged for normalisation.

## Definition
**Lowness as an imposed or circumstantial condition** — being made low by God, by enemies, or by want — together with its inner correlate (a downcast spirit, a bowed heart). This characteristic is *suffered or undergone*, not chosen (contrast A) and not a virtue (contrast B). **The inner↔outer boundary runs through it** (see flags).

## Inner-being signature
- **Kind:** *status / condition*; experiencer is typically the **patient**, not the agent.
- **Divine role:** in several, God is the **agent** of the lowering (2 Chronicles 28:19 "the Lord humbled Judah"; 2 Corinthians 12:21 "my God may humble me") — humiliation as discipline/judgement.
- **Inner correlate:** the **affect** pole — *tapeinos* "downcast" (2 Corinthians 7:6, God "comforts the downcast"); the **heart** pole — Psalm 107:12 "he bowed their hearts down".
- **Valence:** mostly **neutral** (a condition, not a moral act); the moral weight sits on the response to it.

## Sub-patterns
1. **Made low by God (discipline/judgement)** — 2 Chronicles 28:19; 2 Corinthians 12:21; Job 40:12 (the proud to be brought low).
2. **Made low by enemies / hardship** — Psalm 106:42 "brought into subjection"; Psalm 107:12 "bowed… with hard labor"; Philippians 4:12 "how to be brought low".
3. **Low social estate** — Luke 1:48 "the humble estate of his servant"; Luke 1:52 "those of humble estate"; James 1:9 "the lowly brother"; James 1:10 "in his humiliation".
4. **The downcast affect** — 2 Corinthians 7:6 (the inner pole most clearly seated).
5. **Bodily/somatic lowness (outer edge):** Acts 8:33 "in his humiliation"; Philippians 3:21 "our lowly body" — lowness of the body itself.

## Cross-links
- **M03 (grief/sorrow):** "downcast" and "bowed hearts" border affliction-affect; bakhah "weep" co-occurs.
- **M38 (salvation/deliverance):** the low estate is the ground God reverses (Luke 1:48–52, Magnificat) — links to exaltation/deliverance.

## Interpret-phase flags
- **Fork C inner/outer (open):** decide whether to (a) keep C whole as an inner-being characteristic with an outer edge, (b) split inner (downcast/bowed-heart) from circumstantial, or (c) set aside the purely circumstantial/somatic occurrences (e.g. Philippians 3:21 "lowly body"). Evidence gathered whole per §4; not pre-split.
- **Strong overlap with A on ka.na:** the same lemma supplies both the chosen act (A) and the imposed condition (C); routing is by verse-read agent/experiencer.

# WA M09 — Characteristic D: Obedience — Tier Findings

**File:** wa-m09-char-d-tier-findings-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Cluster:** M09 · **Characteristic:** D — Obedience · **Catalogue:** WA-tier-catalogue v2 (126Q)
**Evidence base:** `wa-m09-char-d-evidence-v1_0-20260621.md` (31 occurrences — the largest band)
**Source verses:** Gen 49:10; Pro 30:17; Rom 1:5; 5:19; 6:12; 6:16 (×2); 6:17; 10:16; 15:18; 16:19; 16:26; 2Cor 7:15; 10:5; 10:6; Eph 6:1; 6:5; Col 3:20; 3:22; Phil 2:12; 2Th 1:8; 3:14; Phm 21; Heb 5:8; 5:9; 11:8; 1Pe 1:2; 1:14; 1:22; 3:6.
**Method:** authored by verse-reading; Silent classified; inferential labelled; science (T7.3) attributed to M09 extract §3. **God-ward vs human-ward axis held internal (not split).**

---

## T0 — Divine Image  *(9/9)*
- **T0.1.1** — Obedience runs **to God/Christ/the gospel/the faith/the truth** (1Pe 1:2 "obedience to Jesus Christ"; Act 6:7 "obedient to the faith"; Rom 1:5; 16:26 "obedience of faith"; 2Th 1:8 "obey the gospel"; Heb 5:9 "obey him"); and **Christ himself obeys** (Heb 5:8 "learned obedience"; Rom 5:19 "by the one man's obedience"). God/Christ is both **object** and (in Christ) **bearer**.
- **T0.1.2** — **Yes — borne by Christ** (Heb 5:8; Rom 5:19), whose obedience is **salvific** ("the many will be made righteous"). Obedience images the **Son's obedience to the Father**.
- **T0.2.1** — Purpose: it **brings salvation/righteousness** (Heb 5:9 "source of eternal salvation to all who obey"; Rom 5:19; 1Pe 1:22 "purified your souls by obedience"; Phil 2:12) and **orders the household** (Eph 6:1, 5; Col 3:20, 22).
- **T0.2.2** — **Both** — created design (right ordering under God/legitimate authority) and the **means of redemption** (Christ's obedience); its **mis-aim** (Rom 6:12, 16 obey sin) is the fallen distortion.
- **T0.2.3** — **Yes** — oriented to **eternal salvation** (Heb 5:9) and glory.
- **T0.3.1** — Instantiates the **Son's filial obedience** in the believer (Rom 5:19; Heb 5:8).
- **T0.3.2** — **Shared** — Christ obeys (Heb 5:8); believers obey; the same characteristic in God-incarnate and creature.
- **T0.3.3** — Presence = the obedient/faith-filled image; absence ("do not obey the gospel", Rom 10:16; 2Th 1:8) = the rebellious image **under judgment**.
- **T0.4.1** — **Christological** (Rom 5:19; Heb 5:8 — the divine instance establishing the pattern) and **covenantal** (the obedience of faith, Rom 1:5).

## T1 — Definition  *(18/18)*
- **T1.1.1** — Names the **will's heeding/compliance with authority** — the will that "hears-under" (*hupo-akouō*).
- **T1.1.2** — *hupakouō* (verb, obey/hearken), *hupakoē* (noun, obedience), *yiqqehah* (Heb). Roots: **hearing-under** (Grk *akouō*); Heb *yaqah* "to heed."
- **T1.1.3** — Directional (under authority), **perceptual-root** (hearing), volitional-relational implication.
- **T1.2.1** — An **act** (*hupakouō*) and a **status** (*hupakoē*).
- **T1.2.2** — **Compound** — perception (heeding) + volition (compliance) + relation (to authority); "from-the-heart" obedience adds affect/sincerity (Rom 6:17; Eph 6:5).
- **T1.3.1** — Structural opposite: **disobedience / rebellion** (2Th 1:8; Rom 10:16; *disobedience*, 2Cor 10:6).
- **T1.3.2** — Resists rebellion, insubordination, autonomy-from-God.
- **T1.3.3** — **Not** the submission-posture (E) — it is the **active complying**; meets self-humbling (A) at the cross (Phil 2:8).
- **T1.4.1** — Verb (imperative — children/slaves obey; indicative — "obeyed"; participle) and noun (a state, "your obedience").
- **T1.4.2** — **Varies by direction** — God-ward (gospel/faith/Christ) vs human-authority-ward (parents/masters/Abraham); and by **valence** (right obedience vs Rom 6:12 forbidden obey-sin).
- **T1.4.3** — **Commanded/addressed** (Eph 6:1, 5; Col 3:20, 22) and **"obey the gospel"** (heeding a proclamation — speech-based).
- **T1.5.1** — Immediate response: **action follows** ("By faith Abraham obeyed… and went out", Heb 11:8); obedience "received… with fear and trembling" (2Cor 7:15).
- **T1.5.2** — **Consistent** — obedience issues immediately in compliant action.
- **T1.6.1** — Sustained: **righteousness / salvation / purified souls** (Rom 5:19; Heb 5:9; 1Pe 1:22) and a settled obedient character ("your obedience known to all", Rom 16:19).
- **T1.6.3** — Immediate = the compliant act; sustained = the formed obedient character and its fruit.
- **T1.7.1** — Right operation **from the heart / in sincerity** (Rom 6:17 "obedient from the heart"; Eph 6:5; Col 3:22 "not… eye-service") and **with reverent fear** (2Cor 7:15; Eph 6:5).
- **T1.7.2** — Distorted when **mis-aimed at sin** (Rom 6:12 "obey its passions"; Rom 6:16 "slaves of the one whom you obey") or **withheld** (disobedience to the gospel).
- **T1.7.3** — Present-but-not-holding = **eye-service** (Col 3:22) — obedience in form without heart.

## T2 — Constitutional Location  *(6/6)*
- **T2.1.1** — **Heart and soul**: "obedient from the heart" (Rom 6:17); "sincerity of heart" (Eph 6:5; Col 3:22); "purified your souls by your obedience" (1Pe 1:22); "inward parts" (2Cor 7:15). Faculty at the operative level uniformly **perception** (hearing/heeding).
- **T2.1.2** — Pattern: true obedience is **heart-and-soul-seated** ("from the heart"), distinguishing it from outward **eye-service**; obedience that **purifies the soul** (1Pe 1:22) reaches the deepest level.
- **T2.10.1** — [inferential] obedience responds to an **external authority/proclamation** (the word obeyed comes onto the person) while **originating in the heart** — a mixed in-and-onto movement.
- **T2.7.1** — Body link: obedience is **enacted bodily** (Heb 11:8 "went out"; servants' service); heart→body **expressive**; Eph 6:5 "obey… according to the flesh" (the bodily sphere of service).
- **T2.9.1** — Origin: **response to authority/proclamation** (obey the gospel/faith — from hearing) and **from the heart** (Rom 6:17); Christ's obedience **learned through suffering** (Heb 5:8).
- **T2.9.2** — Origin **multiple** — response to external authority + internal heart-source; for Christ, learned/formed.

## T3 — The Inner Faculties  *(D is the most faculty-rich char: perception/cognition/affect/volition/agency/moral-eval/conscientiousness/relational engaged)*
- **T3.1 Perception** — **the defining faculty**: obedience IS "hearing-under" (*hupakouō* from *akouō*); "obey the gospel" = heeding the proclamation (2Th 1:8); "faith comes from hearing" (Rom 10:16–17). Pattern: perception is **constitutive** (obedience's root is hearing).
- **T3.2 Cognition** — engaged — "take every thought captive to obey Christ" (2Cor 10:5 — the mind brought to obedience).
- **T3.4 Affect** — engaged — "fear and trembling" (2Cor 7:15; Eph 6:5); "from the heart" (sincerity/affection).
- **T3.6 Volition** — **strongly engaged** — obedience is the will's compliance and **allegiance** ("slaves of the one whom you obey", Rom 6:16).
- **T3.7 Agency** — **strongly engaged** — obedience issues in action (Heb 11:8 went out; servants serve).
- **T3.8 Moral Evaluation** — engaged — obedience measured against the standard obeyed; "obedience leading to righteousness" (Rom 6:16); the forbidden obey-sin (Rom 6:12) is judged. Pattern: moral-evaluation determines obedience's worth **by its object**.
- **T3.10 Conscientiousness** — **paradigmatically engaged** — obedience **is** the integrated moral-awareness + volition + action (the catalogue's definition); "obedient from the heart" issuing in conduct (Rom 6:17).
- **T3.11 Relational Capacity** — **strongly engaged** — obedience is **constituted in relation to an authority** (God, parents, masters, Christ); always to-someone.
- **T3.9 Conscience** — [inferential] "fear and trembling" (2Cor 7:15) as conscientious response.
- **T3.3 / T3.5** (memory, creativity) — none; pattern not memorial/creative.

## T4 — Relational Interfaces  *(17/18 — D engages every human interface)*
- **T4.1.1 / .2 / .3** — Christ "became the source of eternal salvation to **all who obey**" (Heb 5:9) — God **responds to obedience with salvation**; **conditional** ("to all who obey"); shows God **saves the obedient**.
- **T4.2.1 / .2 / .3** — **Primary axis**: obedience **to God/Christ/gospel/faith** (1Pe 1:2; Act 6:7; Rom 1:5; Heb 5:9; 2Cor 10:5); requires the **heeded submission of will** in reverent fear; shows the person **ordered under God's authority in faith**.
- **T4.3.1 / .2 / .3** — Rendered to **human authority** — children→parents (Eph 6:1; Col 3:20), slaves→masters (Eph 6:5; Col 3:22), Sarah→Abraham (1Pe 3:6), Philemon→Paul (Phm 21); inner condition = **sincerity/heart, not eye-service**; must heed **from the heart**.
- **T4.4.1 / .2** — Obedience **elicited/received** by an authority — "your obedience… as you received him" (2Cor 7:15); "when your obedience is complete" (2Cor 10:6); "confident of your obedience" (Phm 21); uptake requires recognition of legitimate authority.
- **T4.5.1 / .2 / .3** — Operates within **ordered relations** (household) **and across to all nations** — the obedience of faith "among all the nations" (Rom 1:5; 16:26 — universal scope).
- **T4.6.1 / .2** — [inferential] "take every thought captive to obey Christ" sits within **spiritual warfare** (2Cor 10:3–5, destroying strongholds) — obedience is the **goal of the warfare** against false arguments; disobedience is the adversarial counter.
- **T4.6.3** — [SILENT–data] no angelic mediation of obedience shown.

## T5 — Formative and Developmental  *(9/9 — D heavily salvific/formative)*
- **T5.1.1** — **Yes** — obedience **purifies souls** (1Pe 1:22), **makes righteous** (Rom 5:19), **works salvation** (Phil 2:12; Heb 5:9) — changes condition and orientation.
- **T5.1.2** — [inferential] the fruit (righteousness/salvation) tends toward permanence.
- **T5.2.1** — **Yes** — hearing → obeying → righteousness/salvation/purified soul (Rom 10:16–17; 1Pe 1:22).
- **T5.3.1 / .2** — Mechanism: **Christ "learned obedience through what he suffered"** (Heb 5:8 — formation through suffering); the believer's obedience formed by **hearing/heeding** — differing across contexts.
- **T5.4.1 / .2** — **Yes** — Heb 5:8: suffering is the **school of obedience**; suffering **forms/proves** it.
- **T5.5.1** — **Central** — obedience **purifies the soul** (1Pe 1:22) and is the **working-out of salvation** (Phil 2:12) — a core sanctification engine.
- **T5.6.1** — **Yes** — obedience leads to **eternal salvation** (Heb 5:9); the obedient are saved/glorified.

## T6 — Structural Relationships  *(13/13)*
- **T6.1.1 / .2** — Co-occurs with **faith** ("obedience of faith", Rom 1:5; 16:26; Act 6:7 → M31), **fear/trembling** (2Cor 7:15; Eph 6:5; Phil 2:12 → M01), **self-humbling** (Phil 2:8 → A), **suffering** (Heb 5:8), **slavery/service** (Rom 6:16; *doulos* → M36). Place: the **junction of faith and action**.
- **T6.2.1 / .2** — Obedience **follows hearing/faith** and **precedes righteousness/salvation**; **accompanies** fear and humility (Phil 2:8, 12) — causal/developmental.
- **T6.3.1 / .2 / .3** — **Produces** righteousness/salvation/purified soul; **produced by** faith/hearing and (in Christ) by suffering; **constituent of faith** (the "obedience of faith") and meets self-humbling at the cross.
- **T6.4.1 / .2** — *hupakoē/hupakouō* share the **akouō (hear) root** with hearing/listening (M-listen, Registry 213) and the **hupo- (under)** prefix with submission (*hupotassō*, E/M23).
- **T6.5.1 / .2 / .3** — Nearest = **E submission** — obedience = **active complying (act)**, submission = **ordered placing-under (posture)**; also near **A** (Phil 2:8) — distinguished by **kind** (heeding-act vs lowering-act).

## T7 — Evidential and Methodological  *(20/20)*
- **T7.1.1** — *hupakouō/hupakoē* (*hupo* "under" + *akouō* "hear" = **hear-under, heed**); *yiqqehah* (Heb). Root = **hearing-under**.
- **T7.1.2** — Verb (act) + noun (state) — obedience as both **act and abiding state**.
- **T7.1.3** — Semantic range: heeding/hearkening → compliance → the settled state → **"the obedience of faith"** (faith itself as obedience).
- **T7.1.4** — Distinguishes **act** (verb) from **state** (noun); **God-ward** (obedience of faith) from **human-ward** (household).
- **T7.1.5** — Opposite: **disobedience/unbelief** (*apeitheō / parakoē* — "do not obey the gospel", 2Th 1:8; Rom 10:16).
- **T7.1.6** — Person-type: "**obedient children**" (1Pe 1:14); *doulos* "slave… of obedience" (Rom 6:16).
- **T7.1.7** — [SILENT–data] no term for *seeking obedience as a gift* — one commands it.
- **T7.1.8** — OT (*yiqqehah*, rare — peoples' obedience to the ruler, Gen 49:10) → NT (*hupakoē*, richly developed) — major **development**: obedience becomes the **faith-response to the gospel** and the **christological act** that justifies.
- **T7.1.9** — **"obedience of faith"** (*hupakoē pisteōs*, Rom 1:5; 16:26) — a distinctively Pauline construction fusing obedience and faith.
- **T7.1.10** — Arc: heeding → compliance with authority → the obedience of faith → **Christ's salvific obedience**.
- **T7.2.1** — Function: main verb/noun naming the response demanded or rendered.
- **T7.2.2** — Forms: narrative (Gen 49:10; Heb 11:8), epistle paraenesis (household codes; Rom; 1Pe), wisdom (Pro 30:17), christological exposition (Heb 5; Rom 5:19).
- **T7.2.3** — Logic: "obey the gospel or face judgment" (2Th 1:8); "by the one man's obedience the many will be made righteous" (Rom 5:19); "obedient from the heart" → freed for righteousness (Rom 6:17).
- **T7.2.4** — Setting: soteriological/covenantal (obedience of faith), household/ecclesial (codes), christological (Heb 5; Rom 5).
- **T7.2.5 / .6** — Anchor **Rom 5:19** — obedience's **christological-salvific apex** ("by the one man's obedience the many will be made righteous"); note Rom 6:17 (heart-interior) and Heb 5:8 (learned).
- **T7.3.1** *(science §3)* — social/organisational psychology of obedience (Milgram; **compliant vs internalised**; legitimate authority).
- **T7.3.2** — Illuminates: the **compliant-vs-internalised** distinction maps precisely onto D's **eye-service vs from-the-heart** obedience (Col 3:22 vs Rom 6:17); Milgram's legitimate-authority illuminates the household codes.
- **T7.3.3** — Divergence: Milgram's dominant message is the **danger** of obedience; D makes the **identity/legitimacy of the one obeyed decisive** — obedience to God/Christ is salvific, and obedience to **sin** is the real danger (Rom 6:12, 16). The biblical "obey God rather than sin" inverts Milgram's caution (extract T7.3.3).
- **T7.3.4** — **Direct hit on the extract's surfaced gap (T7.3.4):** D's **"from the heart" / "sincerity" / "not eye-service"** verses (Rom 6:17; Eph 6:5; Col 3:22) explicitly mark **internalised** (inner-agreement) obedience against hollow compliance — the biblical pass **locates and confirms** the distinction the science predicted.

# WA M09 — Characteristic D: Obedience — Evidence

**File:** wa-m09-char-d-evidence-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Cluster:** M09 — *Humility, Meekness and Submission* · **Characteristic:** D — Obedience
**Occurrences gathered:** 31 · **Source:** `wa-ve-lexical-extract-M09-20260621-b1of1.json` (extract v1_0, 2026-06-21, batch 1/1)
**Prior output:** `wa-m09-provisional-chars-v1_0-20260621.md` (provisional set). **Phase:** evidence-gather (§4), pre-interpret.
**Status:** self-contained evidence record. Field values are READ-resolved per the extract; counts are indicative (not yet CC-version-locked). Definitions/signatures/flags are authored; the evidence tables are gathered mechanically from the extract.

> Note on references: the extract renders Philippians as "Phili" and Philemon as "Phile" (differs from the Session-A book codes Php/Phm). Full book names used below for clarity. Flagged for normalisation.

## Definition
**The inner submission of the will expressed as heeding/compliance with an authority** — the will that "hears under" (hupó-akouō). It runs in two directions: **God-ward** (the gospel, the faith, Christ) and **human-authority-ward** (parents, masters, husband). The largest band in the cluster.

## Inner-being signature
- **Kind:** action (*hupakouō*) and status (*hupakoē*); **faculty = perception** uniformly — obedience is rooted in *hearing/heeding*, then enacted.
- **Seat:** the **heart** is named as the source (Romans 6:17 "obedient from the heart"; Ephesians 6:5; Colossians 3:22 "sincerity of heart"); also **soul** (1 Peter 1:22 "purified your souls by your obedience").
- **Valence:** **righteous → commanded**; once **forbidden** (Romans 6:12 "obey its passions" — obedience mis-aimed at sin).
- **Object split:** abstract/God-ward (gospel, faith, truth, Christ) vs person/human-authority (parents, masters, Abraham).

## Sub-patterns
1. **Obedience of faith (God-ward, salvific)** — Romans 1:5; 16:26; 10:16; 2 Thessalonians 1:8; Hebrews 5:9; 1 Peter 1:2, 22; Acts 6:7 "obedient to the faith".
2. **From-the-heart obedience (interiorised)** — Romans 6:17; Ephesians 6:5–6; Colossians 3:22 — not eye-service but heart-sincerity.
3. **Household/authority obedience** — Ephesians 6:1; Colossians 3:20 (children); Ephesians 6:5; Colossians 3:22 (servants); 1 Peter 3:6 (Sarah); Genesis 49:10; Proverbs 30:17 (yiqqehah).
4. **The Christological learning of obedience** — Hebrews 5:8 "he learned obedience"; Philippians 2:8 "obedient to death" (the D↔A hinge).
5. **Mis-aimed obedience (forbidden)** — Romans 6:12, 16 — one may "obey" sin; obedience's moral worth depends on its object.

## Cross-links
- **A Self-humbling:** Philippians 2:8 fuses them.
- **E Submission:** adjacent — obedience is the *active compliance*, submission the *ordering-under* (decide merge at interpret).
- **M01 (fear):** obedience repeatedly paired with "fear and trembling" (Ephesians 6:5; Philippians 2:12; 2 Corinthians 7:15) — fobos/tromos co-terms.
- **M31 (faith):** "obedience of faith" binds D to faith; M36 (service): doulos/slave frame.

## Interpret-phase flags
- **Fork D+E (open):** obedience vs submission — keep distinct or merge.
- **God-ward vs human-ward axis:** hold as an internal axis rather than splitting D in two.
- **Romans 6:12/16 (obey sin):** the forbidden pole — confirm it stays within D as the mis-aimed case.

# WA M09 — Characteristic E: Submission / yieldedness — Tier Findings

**File:** wa-m09-char-e-tier-findings-v1_0-20260621.md · **Version:** v1_0 · **Date:** 2026-06-21
**Cluster:** M09 · **Characteristic:** E — Submission / yieldedness · **Catalogue:** WA-tier-catalogue v2 (126Q)
**Evidence base:** `wa-m09-char-e-evidence-v1_0-20260621.md` (4 occurrences: 2Cor 9:13; Gal 2:5; 1Ti 2:11; 1Ti 3:4)
**Method:** authored by verse-reading; Silent classified; inferential labelled; science (T7.3) attributed to M09 extract §3.
**Small-corpus note:** 4 verses; genuine data-silence is expected on developmental/eschatological tiers and is recorded as such (not as method failure).

---

## T0 — Divine Image  *(5/9)*
- **T0.1.1** — God is the one **glorified by** the submission "from your confession of the gospel of Christ" (2Cor 9:13); the pastoral cases (1Ti 2:11; 3:4) are human-ward order, not God-predicated.
- **T0.1.2** — **Never borne by God** in-set; creaturely throughout (Christ's subjection sits under *hupotassō*, M23, not here).
- **T0.2.1** — Purpose: it **glorifies God** (2Cor 9:13), **orders the household** (1Ti 3:4), and is the **posture of learning** (1Ti 2:11 "learn quietly with all submissiveness").
- **T0.2.2** — **Both** — ordered relations (created design) and right response; Gal 2:5 shows it can be wrongly *demanded* (fallen distortion).
- **T0.3.2** — **Creaturely** (the creature ordering itself under authority).
- **T0.2.3 / T0.3.1 / T0.3.3 / T0.4.1** — [SILENT–data] no eschatological orientation, image-condition statement, or typological use in this 4-verse set.

## T1 — Definition  *(13/18)*
- **T1.1.1** — Names the **ordering of self under authority** — a posture of yieldedness.
- **T1.1.2** — *hupotagē* (Grk: a placing/arranging-under) — a noun of subjection.
- **T1.1.3** — **Relational/subordinative** implication ("under").
- **T1.2.1** — A **status/posture** (borne), not an act.
- **T1.2.2** — Largely **simple**, presupposing recognition of the authority (light cognitive constituent).
- **T1.3.1** — Structural opposite: **self-assertion / insubordination / rebellion**.
- **T1.3.2** — Resists defiance and self-will.
- **T1.3.3** — **Not** active compliance (that is obedience, D); it is the *placing-under* itself.
- **T1.4.1** — Noun (2Cor 9:13); modal "with all submissiveness" (1Ti 2:11); adjective "submissive" (1Ti 3:4).
- **T1.4.2** — **Varies**: gospel-confessing (2Cor 9:13) vs household-ordered (1Ti) vs **refused** (Gal 2:5).
- **T1.4.3** — **Speech/learning mode**: 1Ti 2:11 submission is the posture of **learning under teaching**.
- **T1.6.1** — Sustained: the **settled ordered posture** of the relationship/household.
- **T1.7.1** — Right under **legitimate, God-honouring authority** (2Cor 9:13).
- **T1.7.2** — Rightly **withheld** where it would betray the gospel: "we did not yield in submission… that the truth of the gospel might be preserved" (Gal 2:5).
- **T1.5.1 / T1.5.2 / T1.6.3 / T1.7.3** — [SILENT–data] no immediate inner response, and immediate-vs-sustained not distinguished, in-set.

## T2 — Constitutional Location  *(4/6)*
- **T2.1.2** — Pattern: submission is **not interiorly seated** in this set (no spirit/soul/heart named) — it reads as a **relational posture** more than a seated inner state.
- **T2.9.1** — Origin: from the **will and the relationship**; at 2Cor 9:13 it flows from **"confession of the gospel"** (from faith/confession).
- **T2.9.2** — **Single** (relational-volitional).
- **T2.1.1 / T2.10.1 / T2.7.1** — [SILENT–data] no seat, no constitutional movement, no body link.

## T3 — The Inner Faculties  *(engaged: cognition, volition, agency, moral-evaluation, conscientiousness, relational; rest none, answered at pattern level)*
- **T3.2 Cognition** — engaged as **receptive learning** (1Ti 2:11 "learn"); submission is the posture of taking in teaching.
- **T3.6 Volition** — engaged — submission is a **yielding of the will** (and Gal 2:5 a willed **refusal** to yield); pattern: volitional posture.
- **T3.7 Agency** — engaged ambivalently — submission **orders agency under another**, while Gal 2:5 asserts agency in refusing.
- **T3.8 Moral Evaluation** — engaged — Gal 2:5 measures submission against **"the truth of the gospel"**: moral evaluation sets its limits.
- **T3.9 Conscience** — [inferential] Gal 2:5 borders conscience (refusing to yield for truth's sake).
- **T3.10 Conscientiousness** — engaged — integrated ordered conduct (1Ti 3:4 household order).
- **T3.11 Relational Capacity** — engaged — submission is **constituted relationally** (under an authority); relational by definition.
- **T3.1 / T3.3 / T3.4 / T3.5** (perception, memory, affect, creativity) — none engaged; pattern: submission here is **volitional-relational, not perceptual/affective**. [.1/.2 SILENT–data; .3 answered]

## T4 — Relational Interfaces  *(10/18)*
- **T4.2.1** — Toward God **indirectly** — 2Cor 9:13 submission flows from gospel-confession and **glorifies God**.
- **T4.2.2 / T4.2.3** — Posture of **confession**; shows the believer **ordered under God's gospel**.
- **T4.3.1** — Rendered to an authority (elders/teacher/parent — 1Ti); **.3** [inferential] requires recognition of the authority's legitimacy.
- **T4.4.1** — Elicited from another: 1Ti 3:4 the overseer "keeps his children submissive."
- **T4.5.1 / T4.5.2 / T4.5.3** — Operates **within ordered relations** (household, church) and is **limited by truth** (Gal 2:5 — withheld where it would compromise the gospel); scope = under **legitimate** authority.
- **T4.1.x / T4.4.2 / T4.4.3 / T4.6.x** — [SILENT–data] God does not extend submission to humans; non-uptake state not shown; no spiritual-beings operation.

## T5 — Formative/Developmental  *(2/9; small-corpus silence)*
- **T5.3.1** — [inferential] formation **through learning under authority** (1Ti 2:11 "learn").
- **T5.5.1** — [inferential] submission as ordered Christian life **participates** in formation.
- **T5.1.x / T5.2.1 / T5.4.x / T5.6.1** — [SILENT–data] no transformation, sequence, suffering-relation, or eschatology in-set.

## T6 — Structural Relationships  *(8/13)*
- **T6.1.1** — Co-occurs with **confession/gospel** (2Cor 9:13), **dignity** (1Ti 3:4 → G), and **generosity** (2Cor 9:13 "generosity of your contribution" → F/M05).
- **T6.3.1 / T6.3.2** — **Issues from** confession of the gospel (produced by faith/confession).
- **T6.3.3** — Constituent relation with **obedience (D)**.
- **T6.4.1 / T6.4.2** — *hupotagē* shares the *hupo-tassō* root with the verb **"to subject" tagged M23** — root spans M09/M23.
- **T6.5.1 / T6.5.2 / T6.5.3** — Nearest = **D obedience**; distinguished: submission = the **placing-under (posture)**, obedience = the **complying-with (act)** — a distinction of **kind/direction**.
- **T6.1.2 / T6.2.x** — [SILENT–data] no clear sequence in-set.

## T7 — Evidential/Methodological  *(13/20)*
- **T7.1.1** — *hupotagē*, root *hupo-tassō* "to arrange under."
- **T7.1.2** — Noun (+ cognate adjective/adverb) — a **borne posture**.
- **T7.1.3** — Semantic range: subjection / submissiveness / the state of being ordered under.
- **T7.1.4** — Distinguishes **posture** (noun, here) from **act** (the verb, M23).
- **T7.1.5** — Opposite: insubordination/rebellion (no in-set term; Gal 2:5 is the **limiting case**).
- **T7.1.10** — Arc: submission as **gospel-grounded, truth-limited ordered subjection**.
- **T7.2.1** — Function: names the posture in the household/ecclesial argument.
- **T7.2.2** — Form: **epistle** (Pauline + Pastoral); read within household/church-order.
- **T7.2.3** — Logic: Gal 2:5 (truth-of-gospel **> submission**); 2Cor 9:13 (submission **→ glorifies God**).
- **T7.2.4** — Setting: **ecclesial/household order**; polemical (Gal 2:5).
- **T7.2.5 / T7.2.6** — Anchor **2Cor 9:13** — shows submission **flowing from confession and glorifying God** (its God-ward ground).
- **T7.3.1** *(science §3)* — **social/organisational psychology** of submission/obedience (Milgram; compliant vs internalised; voluntary submission).
- **T7.3.2** — Illuminates **compliant-vs-internalised**: 2Cor 9:13 "from your confession" = **internalised** submission; 1Ti household = ordered/structural.
- **T7.3.3** — Divergence: Milgram frames submission as **danger**; the biblical material makes the **identity of the authority decisive** — submission to God-honouring authority is good and is **rightly refused** where it betrays truth (Gal 2:5) (extract T7.3.3).
- **T7.3.4** — Surfaces the **inner-agreement** dimension — 2Cor 9:13 carries it; worth testing which submission terms carry inner agreement vs mere compliance (extract T7.3.4).
- **T7.1.6 / T7.1.7 / T7.1.8 / T7.1.9** — [SILENT–data] no person-type/supplication/coinage term in-set; OT→NT continuity not derivable from 4 NT verses (cross-testament note deferred to cluster synthesis).
